# Process Repository

The main end-to-end business processes are often called **value streams** or **cross-functional process chains**. They cut across departments and describe how the organisation creates, sells, delivers, supports, and manages value.

## A Common Set

| End-to-end process | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| **Order to Cash** | Customer order → fulfilment → delivery → invoicing → payment collection |
| **Lead to Order / Lead to Cash** | Marketing lead → sales opportunity → quote → contract/order. If extended through payment, it becomes Lead to Cash |
| **Quote to Order** | Customer request → quotation → negotiation → accepted order |
| **Procure to Pay** | Purchase need → requisition → purchase order → goods/services receipt → supplier invoice → payment |
| **Plan to Produce / Plan to Make** | Demand planning → production planning → manufacturing → quality control → finished goods |
| **Forecast to Stock** | Forecast demand → plan inventory → procure/manufacture → hold stock ready for sale |
| **Design to Launch / Idea to Market** | Product idea → design → development → testing → launch |
| **Issue to Resolution / Request to Resolve** | Customer issue/request → triage → investigation → resolution → closure |
| **Hire to Retire** | Workforce planning → recruitment → onboarding → payroll/HR management → performance → offboarding/retirement |
| **Record to Report** | Financial transactions → journals → reconciliations → close → financial/statutory reporting |
| **Acquire to Retire** | Asset need → acquisition → deployment → maintenance → depreciation → disposal |
| **Source to Contract** | Supplier identification → RFQ/RFP → negotiation → contract award |
| **Contract to Renewal** | Contract setup → obligation management → performance monitoring → renewal/termination |
| **Service Request to Fulfilment** | Internal or customer service request → approval → fulfilment → confirmation |
| **Concept to Customer** | Broad product/service lifecycle from concept through development, launch, sale, delivery, and support |

## A Useful Way to Group Them

### 1. Customer-facing / revenue processes

These are the processes most directly tied to revenue and customer value.

- **Lead to Order** — Find potential customers, qualify them, develop opportunities, quote, negotiate, and win the sale.
- **Order to Cash** — Receive the order, deliver the goods or services, invoice the customer, and collect payment.
- **Issue to Resolution** — Handle complaints, faults, warranty claims, service tickets, returns, and customer support.

### 2. Supply chain and operations processes

These are about planning, sourcing, making, moving, and delivering.

- **Plan to Produce** — Plan demand, schedule production, manufacture goods, test quality, and release finished product.
- **Procure to Pay** — Buy goods and services, receive them, match invoices, and pay suppliers.
- **Forecast to Stock** — Forecast demand and maintain inventory so products are available when needed.
- **Warehouse to Deliver** — Pick, pack, ship, deliver, and confirm receipt.

### 3. Product and service lifecycle processes

These are about creating or improving what the business sells.

- **Idea to Market** — Identify opportunity, develop a product/service, test it, price it, launch it, and manage adoption.
- **Design to Launch** — More product-development focused: design, build, validate, release.
- **Change to Release** — Common in IT/software: request change, assess, build, test, approve, deploy.

### 4. Finance and corporate management processes

These keep the organisation controlled and compliant.

- **Record to Report** — Capture accounting transactions, reconcile accounts, close periods, and produce reports.
- **Budget to Forecast** — Set budgets, track actuals, revise forecasts, and manage financial performance.
- **Risk to Compliance** — Identify risks, define controls, monitor compliance, manage audits and remediation.

### 5. People and asset processes

These manage key organisational resources.

- **Hire to Retire** — Recruit, onboard, manage, develop, pay, and offboard employees.
- **Acquire to Retire** — Acquire assets, maintain them, depreciate them, and dispose of them.
- **Request to Fulfilment** — An employee or department asks for something — equipment, access, travel, software — and the organisation approves and provides it.

## The Numbered Catalogue

Twenty-six end-to-end chains, grouped by what they are for. V01–V09 are the
original nine; V10–V26 extend the set into areas the first pass left uncovered —
demand generation before a lead exists, what happens after the sale, reverse
logistics, running maintenance, security and privacy response, governance,
decisioning, and analytics.

### Customer-facing

- **V01** Order to Cash — order through fulfilment, delivery, invoicing, payment
- **V07** Issue to Resolution — complaints, faults, warranty claims, support
- **V10** Market to Lead — campaigns and demand generation, before a lead exists
- **V11** Sign to Onboard — contract signed through to a customer in service
- **V12** Renew to Retain — renewal, retention, cancellation and win-back

### Supply chain and operations

- **V02** Procure to Pay — buy, receive, match, pay
- **V05** Plan to Produce — plan demand, schedule, manufacture, release
- **V09** Source to Contract — identify suppliers, tender, negotiate, award
- **V13** Return to Refund — reverse logistics, disposition and refunds
- **V14** Dock to Stock — inbound receipt, inspection and putaway
- **V15** Detect to Repair — running maintenance, from fault to return to service

### Product and service lifecycle

- **V06** Idea to Market — opportunity through development, launch and adoption
- **V26** Concept to Commissioning — capital projects, concept to asset in service

### Risk, governance and security

- **V16** Detect to Respond — security and privacy incident response
- **V17** Audit to Action — audit planning through to remediated findings
- **V18** Draft to Publish — policy and procedure lifecycle
- **V19** Request to Access — access requests, review and revocation
- **V20** Matter to Resolution — legal matters, disputes and litigation

### Decisioning

- **V21** Application to Decision — applications for credit, cover, grants, licences
- **V22** Claim to Settlement — claim notification through to settlement

### Finance and information

- **V03** Record to Report — transactions, reconciliation, close, reporting
- **V04** Hire to Retire — recruit, onboard, pay, develop, offboard
- **V08** Acquire to Retire — asset acquisition through to disposal
- **V23** Meter to Cash — measured consumption through to collected revenue
- **V24** Transaction to Return — tax determination, lodgement and audit
- **V25** Data to Insight — a business question through to a published, monitored result

The External Participants that would initiate the process and be the main external participant during the end-to-end process (e.g. Customer, Applicant, Interviewee, Inventor, Complainant, Seller, Buyer, Owner, etc.). 3. The small number of high-level Subprocesses that would be carried out during the end-to-end Value Chain. 4. The typical IT Systems that would support these processes. 5. The high-level flow of information to and from the Processes and the IT Systems.

# Enterprise Value Chains Catalogue

## V01 — Order to Cash

**Teams and roles involved.**
Order to Cash usually involves Sales, Customer Service, Order Management, Credit Control, Warehouse/Logistics, Billing, Accounts Receivable, Finance, and sometimes Legal or Contracts. Key roles include account manager, sales operations analyst, order processor, credit officer, fulfilment coordinator, warehouse picker/packer, delivery coordinator, billing officer, collections officer, and customer support agent.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Customer or Buyer. The process is normally initiated when a customer places an order, accepts a quote, signs a contract, or triggers a recurring purchase/subscription. Other external parties may include freight carriers, payment providers, distributors, resellers, or customer procurement teams.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive order, validate customer/order, check credit and pricing, confirm availability, fulfil goods or services, deliver to customer, issue invoice, receive payment, reconcile payment, manage disputes or deductions, and close the order.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, ERP, order management, eCommerce platform, customer portal, warehouse management system, transport management system, billing system, accounts receivable system, payment gateway, document management, and customer service/ticketing platform.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include pricing policy, credit policy, customer master data policy, order acceptance procedure, fulfilment procedure, delivery terms, billing policy, tax rules, revenue recognition policy, returns policy, dispute management procedure, and debt collection policy.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides order details, purchase orders, delivery instructions, contact details, payment details, and dispute or return requests. The process provides the customer with quotes, order confirmations, availability updates, shipment notifications, invoices, statements, payment receipts, credit notes, and service updates.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates customer master data, sales orders, inventory reservations, shipment records, delivery confirmations, invoices, receivables, payment records, and financial postings. IT systems provide pricing, credit status, inventory availability, order status, invoice status, payment status, and reporting information.

```text
Context Diagram: V01 — Order to Cash (O2C).

1. Central system (process-system)
A single central process/system ellipse named "Order Processing Company"
representing the whole organisation that runs the Order to Cash process. It is

2. External entities (external-entity)

- Freight Carrier
- Payment Gateway
- Bank

3. Layout
"Order Processing Company" sits in the centre. The Customer sits to the LEFT

This Context Diagram frames the Order Processing Company as a single system in
```

```text
- Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP)
- ERP / Credit System
- Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)
- Transport Management System (TMS)
- Billing / ERP System
- Payment Gateway / Bank Interface
- ERP / General Ledger System
- Case / Ticketing System

- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
```

### V01.01 — Receive Order

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.01 Receive Order — first subprocess of the Order to Cash value
chain, capturing an inbound customer order and recording it in the Order
Management System before passing it to validation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the company receiving and processing the order,
  with lanes for Customer Service and Order Processing.
Pool "Customer" — the external buyer placing the order.
Pool "Order Management System (OMS)" — the system of record for sales orders.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer": black-box, single instance.
Pool "Order Management System (OMS)": black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Order Management System (OMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Order received from Customer"
  User task "Log initial order contact"
  User task "Capture order channel and details"
  Exclusive gateway "Order information complete?"
  - branch "No — information missing":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: Send task "Request missing information from
        Customer", Intermediate message catch event "Customer responds",
        User task "Update order details"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Order information complete")
  - branch "Yes — details sufficient":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Order information complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Order information complete"
  User task "Confirm order receipt with Customer"
  Send task "Send order acknowledgement to Customer"

Order Processing lane:
  User task "Review captured order details"
  User task "Assign order type and priority"
  Service task "Create sales order record in OMS"
  User task "Verify order record created"
  End event "Order record confirmed — ready for Validate Customer / Order"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Details Complete", labelled "48-hour response deadline exceeded", leading
  to End event "Order abandoned — customer unresponsive".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Customer Service lane with the message
  start event, moves through order capture and the completeness gateway loop,
  then passes via sequence flow into the Order Processing lane for review,
  order creation in the OMS, and verification before reaching the end event.
  The "No" branch of the completeness gateway enters the standard-loop
  subprocess and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway "Order information
  complete"; the "Yes" branch bypasses the subprocess and also rejoins at
  that same merge gateway, continuing to the acknowledgement send task.

Message flows:
  Customer → Customer Service lane (inbound order details, purchase order,
    or subscription trigger)
  Send task "Request missing information from Customer" → Customer (request
    for clarification or missing order data)
  Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Customer responds" (customer
    reply with missing information)
  Send task "Send order acknowledgement to Customer" → Customer (order
    acknowledgement with reference number)
  Service task "Create sales order record in OMS" → Order Management System
    (OMS) (new sales order record)
  Order Management System (OMS) → User task "Verify order record created"
    (confirmation of record creation and assigned order number)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inbound Order" — written by User task "Capture order channel
  and details"; read by User task "Review captured order details".
Data Object "Order Acknowledgement" — written by User task "Confirm order
  receipt with Customer"; read by Send task "Send order acknowledgement to
  Customer".
Data Object "Sales Order Record" — written by Service task "Create sales
  order record in OMS"; read by User task "Verify order record created".

This subprocess receives the customer's order through any channel, gathers
all necessary order details through an iterative clarification loop if needed,
and registers a confirmed sales order record in the Order Management System.
It hands a complete, system-recorded order to the Validate Customer / Order
subprocess, which checks the customer's standing and the order's correctness
before credit and pricing review begins.
```

### V01.02 — Validate Customer / Order

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.02 Validate Customer / Order — validates customer master data
and order details before credit and pricing checks in the Order to Cash chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the company running the Order to Cash process,
  with Order Processing and Customer Service lanes.
Pool "Customer" — the external buyer who submitted the order.
Pool "Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP)" — IT system holding customer
  master data, credit standing, and order history.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Order Processing lane:
  Message start event "Order received from Receive Order"
  User task "Review order details for completeness"
  Service task "Retrieve customer record from CRM/ERP"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer record found?"
  - branch "No — new customer": User task "Create new customer record"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer record found")
  - branch "Yes — existing customer": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Customer record found")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer record found"
  Service task "Validate customer master data"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer data valid?"
  - branch "No — data issues": User task "Flag customer data discrepancy"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer data valid")
  - branch "Yes — data confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Customer data valid")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer data valid"
  User task "Validate order line items, quantities, and pricing references"
  Exclusive gateway "Order details complete and valid?"
  - branch "Yes — valid": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Order
    details complete and valid")
  - branch "No — incomplete or invalid": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "Order details complete and valid")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Order details complete and valid"

Customer Service lane:
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Order Confirmed by Customer" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Contact customer to clarify or
    correct order details", Intermediate message catch event "Customer
    response received", User task "Update order details with customer
    corrections"
  Exclusive gateway "Order valid after clarification?"
  - branch "Yes — proceed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Order
    valid after clarification")
  - branch "No — cancel order": User task "Notify customer of order
    rejection", End event "Order rejected — process ends"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Order valid after clarification"
  User task "Confirm validated order to customer"
  End event "Customer and order validated — ready for Check Credit and
    Pricing"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Order Confirmed by Customer" — label "Clarification overdue (48 hours)" —
  triggers User task "Escalate unresolved order to senior customer service
  agent", then flows to end of subprocess.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Order Processing lane with the message
start event, proceeds through customer record retrieval, the "Customer record
found?" gateway (branches for new and existing customer rejoining at the
merge), customer data validation, the "Customer data valid?" gateway (branches
for data issues and confirmed data rejoining at the merge), and order line
item validation. The "Order details complete and valid?" gateway branches:
the "Yes" branch proceeds directly to the merge; the "No" branch passes to
the Customer Service lane and enters the "Repeat Until Order Confirmed by
Customer" loop subprocess. On exit from the loop, the "Order valid after
clarification?" gateway branches to either order rejection (ending at the
rejection end event) or the merge. The merge leads to confirmation of the
validated order and the final end event, both in the Customer Service lane.

Message flows:
Customer → Order Processing lane (incoming order details triggering the
  message start event)
Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP) → Order Processing lane (customer
  record data, returned in response to retrieval service task)
Order Processing lane → Customer Master Data System (CRM/ERP) (new or
  updated customer record written during create/validate tasks)
Customer Service lane → Customer (clarification request sent during contact
  task)
Customer → Customer Service lane (customer response received at intermediate
  message catch event)
Customer Service lane → Customer (validated order confirmation sent at
  confirm task)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incoming Order" — read by "Review order details for
  completeness"; read by "Validate order line items, quantities, and pricing
  references".
Data Object "Customer Record" — written by "Create new customer record";
  read by "Validate customer master data"; written by "Update order details
  with customer corrections".
Data Object "Validated Order" — written by "Validate order line items,
  quantities, and pricing references"; written by "Update order details with
  customer corrections"; read by "Confirm validated order to customer".

This subprocess takes the raw order handed off from Receive Order and
confirms that both the customer master data and the order itself are accurate,
complete, and consistent. Any gaps are resolved with the customer through a
structured clarification loop before the order is formally accepted. The
output — a fully validated customer record and a clean, confirmed order — is
passed to Check Credit and Pricing, which uses it to assess creditworthiness
and apply correct pricing.
```

### V01.03 — Check Credit & Pricing

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.03 Check Credit & Pricing — the third subprocess in the Order to
Cash value chain, sitting between Validate Customer / Order and Confirm
Availability.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the internal organisation running the credit and
pricing check.
  Lane "Sales / Pricing" — sales operations analyst and pricing analyst who
  retrieve and confirm pricing for the validated order.
  Lane "Credit Control" — credit officer who assesses the customer's credit
  status and approves or declines the order.

Pool "Customer" — external buyer who receives the outcome of the credit and
pricing check.

Pool "ERP / Credit System" — IT system that holds pricing rules, credit limits,
credit status, and financial master data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / Credit System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation (lanes top to bottom: Sales / Pricing, Credit Control)
3. ERP / Credit System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Sales / Pricing lane:
  Message start event "Validated order received from Validate Customer / Order"
  Service task "Retrieve pricing rules and discounts from ERP / Credit System"
  User task "Apply pricing to order lines"
  Data-based exclusive gateway "Pricing complete?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pricing complete")
  - branch "No — pricing exception":
      Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Pricing Exception Until Resolved"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Identify pricing discrepancy",
        User task "Escalate to pricing analyst for correction"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pricing complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Pricing complete"
  Send task "Forward priced order to Credit Control"

Credit Control lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Priced order received from Sales / Pricing"
  Service task "Retrieve customer credit status from ERP / Credit System"
  User task "Assess credit limit and exposure"
  Exclusive gateway "Credit assessment outcome?"
  - branch "Credit approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Credit assessment resolved")
  - branch "Credit limit exceeded — manual review":
      User task "Perform manual credit review"
      User task "Record credit decision"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Credit assessment resolved")
  - branch "Credit declined":
      User task "Record credit decline reason"
      Send task "Notify customer of credit decline"
      End event "Order declined — credit refused"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Credit assessment resolved"
  Service task "Record credit approval and confirmed pricing in ERP / Credit
  System"
  Send task "Send credit and pricing confirmation to customer"
  End event "Credit and pricing confirmed — ready for Confirm Availability"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Pricing
Exception Until Resolved" — label "Pricing resolution deadline exceeded" —
flow continues to: User task "Escalate pricing exception to sales manager" then
to End event "Order on hold — pricing unresolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Sales / Pricing lane with the message start
event, passes through pricing retrieval, application, and the loop subprocess
where needed, then merges at "Pricing complete" and crosses via the intermediate
catch event into the Credit Control lane. In Credit Control the flow runs through
credit retrieval, assessment, and the three-way gateway; the manual-review and
approved branches merge at "Credit assessment resolved" before the credit
approval is recorded and the confirmation is sent; the declined branch ends
independently.

Message flows:
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Retrieve pricing rules and discounts from
  ERP / Credit System") → ERP / Credit System (pricing rules and discount
  schedules)
  ERP / Credit System → Sales Organisation (Service task "Retrieve pricing
  rules and discounts from ERP / Credit System") (pricing rules and discount
  schedules returned)
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Retrieve customer credit status from ERP /
  Credit System") → ERP / Credit System (credit status request)
  ERP / Credit System → Sales Organisation (Service task "Retrieve customer
  credit status from ERP / Credit System") (credit limit, exposure, and status
  returned)
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Record credit approval and confirmed pricing
  in ERP / Credit System") → ERP / Credit System (credit approval and pricing
  record written)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Send credit and pricing confirmation to
  customer") → Customer (credit approval and confirmed pricing notification)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Notify customer of credit decline") → Customer
  (credit decline notification)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Priced Order" — written by User task "Apply pricing to order
lines"; read by User task "Assess credit limit and exposure".
Data Object "Credit Assessment Record" — written by User task "Record credit
decision"; read by Service task "Record credit approval and confirmed pricing in
ERP / Credit System".
Data Object "Credit Decline Notice" — written by User task "Record credit
decline reason"; read by Send task "Notify customer of credit decline".

This subprocess takes the validated order from Validate Customer / Order,
applies the correct pricing and discounts, and subjects the customer account to
a credit assessment against limits held in the ERP / Credit System. Orders that
pass both checks are stamped with confirmed pricing and an approved credit
status, ready to be handed to Confirm Availability. Orders that fail the credit
check are declined, the customer is notified, and the flow ends without
progressing further.
```

### V01.04 — Confirm Availability

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.04 Confirm Availability — fourth subprocess in the Order to Cash
value chain, sitting between Check Credit & Pricing and Fulfil Goods or
Services.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the internal organisation running the availability
  confirmation process, with two lanes:
  - Order Processing (order processor)
  - Planning / Inventory (inventory controller, planner)
Pool "Customer" — the external buyer who receives the availability outcome.
Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)" — the warehouse management system
  that provides inventory availability and accepts reservations.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Order Processing lane:
  Message start event "Credit and pricing confirmed — received from Check
    Credit & Pricing"
  User task "Review confirmed order and prepare availability check request"
  Send task "Submit availability check to WMS"
  Intermediate message catch event "Availability result received from WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "Stock available for full order?"
    - branch "Yes — full quantity available":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock available for full order?")
    - branch "Partial — insufficient stock for full order":
        User task "Assess partial availability options"
        Exclusive gateway "Partial fulfilment acceptable?"
          - branch "Yes — customer accepts partial":
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway
                "Partial fulfilment acceptable?")
          - branch "No — back-order or alternative required":
              User task "Identify back-order date or alternative source"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway
                "Partial fulfilment acceptable?")
        Exclusive merge gateway "Partial fulfilment acceptable?"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock available for full order?")
    - branch "No — stock unavailable":
        User task "Identify back-order date or alternative source"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock available for full order?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock available for full order?"
  User task "Confirm reservation and update order with availability details"
  Send task "Send availability confirmation or back-order notification to
    Customer"
  End event "Availability confirmed — ready for Fulfil Goods or Services"

Planning / Inventory lane:
  User task "Review WMS availability result and validate reservation
    feasibility"
  Service task "Record inventory reservation in WMS"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit availability check to WMS" —
  label "WMS response overdue (24 hours)" — triggers User task "Escalate
  WMS non-response to Planning / Inventory team" in Order Processing lane,
  followed by End event "Availability check escalated — process on hold".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Order Processing lane at the message start
  event, moves through the availability check request and the message catch
  event for the WMS result, then enters the "Stock available for full order?"
  exclusive gateway. The "Yes" branch, the resolved partial and no-stock
  branches all converge at the exclusive merge gateway of the same name. Flow
  then passes to the Order Processing task "Confirm reservation and update
  order with availability details", crossing into the Planning / Inventory
  lane for "Review WMS availability result and validate reservation
  feasibility" and "Record inventory reservation in WMS" before returning to
  Order Processing for the send task and end event.

Message flows:
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Submit availability check to WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (availability check request)
  Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) → Sales Organisation (Intermediate
    message catch event "Availability result received from WMS")
    (availability status and stock quantities)
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Record inventory reservation in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (inventory reservation request)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Send availability confirmation or back-order
    notification to Customer") → Customer (availability confirmation or
    back-order notification)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Availability Check Request" — written by User task "Review
  confirmed order and prepare availability check request"; read by Send task
  "Submit availability check to WMS".
Data Object "WMS Availability Result" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Availability result received from WMS"; read by User task "Review
  WMS availability result and validate reservation feasibility" and Exclusive
  gateway "Stock available for full order?".
Data Object "Updated Sales Order" — written by User task "Confirm reservation
  and update order with availability details"; read by Send task "Send
  availability confirmation or back-order notification to Customer".
Data Object "Inventory Reservation Record" — written by Service task "Record
  inventory reservation in WMS"; read by User task "Confirm reservation and
  update order with availability details".

This subprocess confirms whether the ordered goods can be fulfilled from
current stock, establishes a reservation against available inventory, and
determines back-order dates or alternatives where stock is insufficient. It
concludes by notifying the customer of the confirmed availability position and
hands a reserved, fully updated sales order to Fulfil Goods or Services so
that physical picking and packing can begin without delay.
```

### V01.05 — Fulfil Goods or Services

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.05 Fulfil Goods or Services — the internal fulfilment subprocess
that picks, packs, inspects and releases goods or services for handover to
Deliver to Customer.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the organisation fulfilling the order, with lanes
for Warehouse / Operations and Quality Assurance.
Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)" — warehouse management system
that records picks, packs and inventory movements.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sales Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Warehouse / Operations lane:
  Message start event "Confirmed availability received from Confirm
      Availability"
  User task "Review pick list and allocate stock"
  Service task "Record pick instruction in WMS"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Pick Complete" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Pick items from warehouse location",
      Service task "Update pick progress in WMS"
  User task "Pack items and apply shipping labels"
  Service task "Record packed order in WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "Fulfilment type?"
  - branch "Goods": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Fulfilment type resolved")
  - branch "Service": User task "Confirm service delivery readiness"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment type resolved"
  Send task "Transfer packed order to Quality Assurance"

Quality Assurance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Packed order received from Warehouse /
      Operations"
  User task "Inspect goods against order and quality standards"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection passed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome
      resolved")
  - branch "No": User task "Record defect and raise rejection notice"
      Service task "Update rejection in WMS"
      Exclusive gateway "Rework possible?"
      - branch "Yes — rework": User task "Return items to Warehouse /
          Operations for rework"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Rework or scrap resolved")
      - branch "No — scrap": User task "Quarantine and write off defective
          stock"
          Service task "Record write-off in WMS"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Rework or scrap resolved")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Rework or scrap resolved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome resolved"
  Exclusive gateway "All items fulfilled?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment
      completeness resolved")
  - branch "No — partial": User task "Flag partial fulfilment and notify
      Order Processing"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment completeness
      resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment completeness resolved"
  User task "Approve release of order for dispatch"
  Service task "Record fulfilment confirmation in WMS"
  End event "Fulfilled order released — ready for Deliver to Customer"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Pick
Complete", labelled "Pick overdue", triggers: User task "Escalate pick delay
to fulfilment coordinator" leading to End event "Pick escalation raised —
ready for Deliver to Customer".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow begins in the Warehouse / Operations lane, moves
through pick list review, the looping pick subprocess, packing, and the
fulfilment-type gateway (merging at "Fulfilment type resolved"), then passes
to the Quality Assurance lane via a send and a message catch event.
Inspection results diverge at "Inspection passed?"; the No branch diverges
again at "Rework possible?", with both rework and scrap branches merging at
"Rework or scrap resolved" before rejoining the main path at "Inspection
outcome resolved". The completeness gateway diverges and merges at
"Fulfilment completeness resolved" before the flow ends at release.

Message flows:
Sales Organisation (Service task "Record pick instruction in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (pick instruction)
Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) → Sales Organisation (Service task
    "Update pick progress in WMS") (pick progress confirmation)
Sales Organisation (Service task "Record packed order in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (packed order record)
Sales Organisation (Service task "Update rejection in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (rejection notice)
Sales Organisation (Service task "Record write-off in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (stock write-off record)
Sales Organisation (Service task "Record fulfilment confirmation in WMS") →
    Inventory / Warehouse System (WMS) (fulfilment confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Pick List" — written by User task "Review pick list and
    allocate stock"; read by User task "Pick items from warehouse location".
Data Object "Packed Order Record" — written by User task "Pack items and
    apply shipping labels"; read by User task "Inspect goods against order
    and quality standards".
Data Object "Inspection Report" — written by User task "Inspect goods
    against order and quality standards"; read by User task "Record defect
    and raise rejection notice" and User task "Approve release of order for
    dispatch".
Data Object "Fulfilment Confirmation" — written by User task "Approve
    release of order for dispatch"; read by Service task "Record fulfilment
    confirmation in WMS".

This subprocess takes the confirmed, available order from Confirm
Availability and executes all internal work needed to make goods or services
physically ready for dispatch: stock is allocated, picked, packed, quality-
inspected and formally released. Partial or defective outcomes are flagged
before the handover point. The end event delivers a release-approved
fulfilment record to Deliver to Customer, which will arrange carrier
collection and onward shipment.
```

### V01.06 — Deliver to Customer

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.06 Deliver to Customer — the sixth subprocess of the Order to
Cash value chain, covering dispatch, carrier handover, transit tracking,
and proof-of-delivery confirmation before invoicing begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the company executing the delivery process,
  containing the Logistics / Dispatch lane.
Pool "Customer" — the external buyer receiving the shipment.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — the external carrier transporting the goods.
Pool "Transport Management System (TMS)" — the IT system managing
  shipment records, carrier bookings, and delivery confirmations.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Transport Management System (TMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Freight Carrier
4. Transport Management System (TMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Logistics / Dispatch lane:
  Message start event "Fulfilment confirmed — ready for delivery from
    Fulfil Goods or Services"
  User task "Review shipment details and delivery instructions"
  Service task "Create shipment record in TMS"
  User task "Book freight carrier and confirm pickup slot"
  Send task "Send dispatch notification to Customer"
  Send task "Send pickup instruction to Freight Carrier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Carrier confirms pickup and
    collection"
  User task "Record carrier handover and update shipment status in TMS"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Transit period elapses"
  Exclusive gateway "Delivery outcome received?"
    - branch "Delivered successfully": User task "Record proof of
        delivery in TMS"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery outcome received")
    - branch "Delivery exception reported": User task "Investigate
        delivery exception"
      Exclusive gateway "Exception resolved?"
        - branch "Re-attempt delivery": Send task "Instruct Freight
            Carrier to reattempt delivery"
          Intermediate message catch event "Carrier confirms reattempt
            outcome"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception resolved")
        - branch "Return to sender": User task "Initiate return and
            update TMS"
          Send task "Notify Customer of delivery failure"
          End event "Delivery failed — order returned, no further
            delivery"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Exception resolved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery outcome received")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery outcome received"
  Send task "Send delivery confirmation and shipment notification to
    Customer"
  Service task "Post delivery confirmation to TMS"
  End event "Delivery confirmed — ready for Issue Invoice"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Investigate delivery
  exception" — label "Exception investigation timeout (48 hours)" —
  flows to Send task "Notify Customer of delivery failure", then to
  End event "Delivery failed — order returned, no further delivery".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Logistics / Dispatch lane carries the full
  flow from start to end. After "Delivery outcome received?" the
  "Delivered successfully" branch and the resolved path from "Exception
  resolved" both converge at the exclusive merge gateway "Delivery
  outcome received", continuing to the send and post tasks before the
  end event.

Message flows:
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Send dispatch notification to
    Customer") → Customer (dispatch notification)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Send pickup instruction to Freight
    Carrier") → Freight Carrier (pickup instruction)
  Freight Carrier → Sales Organisation (Intermediate message catch
    event "Carrier confirms pickup and collection") (pickup
    confirmation)
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Create shipment record in TMS") →
    Transport Management System (TMS) (shipment record creation)
  Sales Organisation (User task "Record carrier handover and update
    shipment status in TMS") → Transport Management System (TMS)
    (handover status update)
  Freight Carrier → Sales Organisation (Intermediate message catch
    event "Transit period elapses" context — delivery outcome message)
    (proof of delivery or exception report)
  Sales Organisation (User task "Record proof of delivery in TMS") →
    Transport Management System (TMS) (proof-of-delivery record)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Instruct Freight Carrier to reattempt
    delivery") → Freight Carrier (reattempt instruction)
  Freight Carrier → Sales Organisation (Intermediate message catch
    event "Carrier confirms reattempt outcome") (reattempt outcome)
  Sales Organisation (User task "Initiate return and update TMS") →
    Transport Management System (TMS) (return record update)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Notify Customer of delivery failure")
    → Customer (delivery failure notification)
  Sales Organisation (Send task "Send delivery confirmation and
    shipment notification to Customer") → Customer (delivery
    confirmation and shipment notification)
  Sales Organisation (Service task "Post delivery confirmation to
    TMS") → Transport Management System (TMS) (delivery confirmation
    posting)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Shipment Record" — written by User task "Review shipment
  details and delivery instructions"; read by Service task "Create
  shipment record in TMS"; read by User task "Book freight carrier and
  confirm pickup slot".
Data Object "Pickup Confirmation" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Carrier confirms pickup and collection"; read by User
  task "Record carrier handover and update shipment status in TMS".
Data Object "Proof of Delivery" — written by User task "Record proof
  of delivery in TMS"; read by Service task "Post delivery
  confirmation to TMS".
Data Object "Delivery Exception Report" — written by User task
  "Investigate delivery exception"; read by Exclusive gateway
  "Exception resolved?".

This subprocess takes a fulfilled order from the warehouse and manages
the end-to-end delivery journey: booking the carrier, handing over
goods, tracking transit, and resolving any delivery exceptions. On
successful delivery it captures proof of delivery in the TMS and sends
a confirmation to the customer. It hands a confirmed delivery record to
the Issue Invoice subprocess so that billing can proceed on the correct
delivery date and terms.
```

```text
  - branch "Yes — approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Invoice approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice approved?"
  Exclusive gateway "Correction required?"
  - branch "Yes — corrections needed":
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected invoice received from
      Billing"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Correction required?")
  - branch "No — proceed to post":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Correction required?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Correction required?"
  Service task "Post invoice to Billing / ERP System"
  User task "Release invoice to customer"
  Send task "Send invoice to Customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer acknowledgement or query
  received"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer requests correction?"
  - branch "Yes — correction requested":
      User task "Log correction request and notify Billing"
      End event "Correction request raised — returned to Billing lane
      for revision"
  - branch "No — invoice accepted":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer requests
      correction?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer requests correction?"
  End event "Invoice issued and accepted — ready for Receive Payment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Invoice
Draft Correct" — label "Draft overdue (24 hours)" — triggers an escalation
task "Escalate draft delay to Finance controller" in the Billing lane, then
flows to a local End event "Escalation raised".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review invoice for compliance
and accuracy" — label "Review overdue (4 business hours)" — triggers Send task
"Send review overdue alert to finance controller" in the Finance lane, then
flows to a local End event "Review escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Billing lane at the message start event,
passes through retrieval, draft preparation, and the completeness gateway
(with the correction subprocess on the No branch, rejoining at the merge
gateway), then moves to the Finance lane for review and the approval gateway;
the No-approval branch returns a correction note and catches the corrected
invoice before rejoining at the "Correction required?" merge gateway; after
posting, control returns to the Finance lane for release, then a send task
dispatches the invoice, an intermediate catch event awaits customer response,
and the customer-correction gateway either raises a correction end event or
merges and continues to the final accepted end event.

Message flows:
Customer → Sales Organisation / Finance lane, Send task "Send invoice to
Customer" (delivery confirmation trigger at start).
Sales Organisation / Finance lane, Send task "Send invoice to Customer" →
Customer (tax invoice document).
Customer → Sales Organisation / Finance lane, Intermediate message catch
event "Customer acknowledgement or query received" (acknowledgement or
correction query).
Sales Organisation / Billing lane, Service task "Pull pricing, tax, and
billing data from Billing / ERP System" → Billing / ERP System (data
request for pricing, tax, and order details).
Billing / ERP System → Sales Organisation / Billing lane, Service task
"Pull pricing, tax, and billing data from Billing / ERP System" (pricing,
tax rules, and order data response).
Sales Organisation / Finance lane, Service task "Post invoice to Billing /
ERP System" → Billing / ERP System (approved invoice for posting to
accounts receivable ledger).
Billing / ERP System → Sales Organisation / Finance lane, Service task
"Post invoice to Billing / ERP System" (posting confirmation and invoice
reference number).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Delivery Confirmation" — read by User task "Retrieve delivery
and order details".
Data Object "Invoice Draft" — written by User task "Prepare invoice draft";
read by User task "Submit invoice for Finance approval"; updated by User task
"Revise invoice draft".
Data Object "Correction Notes" — written by Send task "Return invoice to
Billing with correction notes"; read by User task "Identify and correct
invoice data errors".
Data Object "Approved Invoice" — written by Service task "Post invoice to
Billing / ERP System"; read by User task "Release invoice to customer".
Data Object "Customer Correction Request" — written by Intermediate message
catch event "Customer acknowledgement or query received"; read by Exclusive
gateway "Customer requests correction?".

This subprocess takes the delivery confirmation handed off by Deliver to
Customer, constructs a tax-compliant invoice, obtains Finance approval, posts
it to the Billing / ERP System, and transmits it to the Customer. Any data
errors are resolved in a controlled correction loop before approval, and
customer-raised queries are logged before the process closes. The verified,
accepted invoice record is then ready for the Receive Payment subprocess to
match against incoming funds.
```

### V01.08 — Receive Payment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.08 Receive Payment — captures and records incoming customer
payments within the Order to Cash value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the company processing and recording payment.
  Lane "Accounts Receivable" (collections officer)
  Lane "Finance" (finance controller)
Pool "Customer" — the external buyer making payment.
Pool "Payment Gateway / Bank" — external payment processing and banking system.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Gateway / Bank" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Payment Gateway / Bank

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Accounts Receivable lane:
  Message start event "Invoice received from Issue Invoice"
  User task "Review open invoice and expected payment details"
  Send task "Send payment request to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment received from customer"
  User task "Confirm payment receipt and check amount"
  Exclusive gateway "Payment amount correct?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount
    correct")
  - branch "No — short payment or discrepancy":
      User task "Log payment discrepancy and contact customer"
      Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolved?"
      - branch "Yes — corrected payment received":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolved")
      - branch "No — unresolved after review":
          End event "Discrepancy unresolved — escalated to Manage Disputes
          and Deductions"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount correct")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount correct"
  Service task "Submit payment record to Payment Gateway / Bank for
  processing"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received from
  Payment Gateway / Bank"
  User task "Apply payment to open invoice in accounts receivable ledger"
  Send task "Send payment receipt to customer"

Finance lane:
  User task "Review and approve payment posting"
  Service task "Post payment to general ledger"
  End event "Payment posted — ready for Reconcile Payment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
Payment received from customer" — label "Payment overdue (payment terms
elapsed)"; triggers User task "Issue payment reminder to customer" in
Accounts Receivable lane, which loops back to the intermediate message
catch event.
Interrupting error boundary event on "Submit payment record to Payment
Gateway / Bank for processing" — label "Payment processing error"; triggers
User task "Investigate processing failure and retry or escalate" in
Accounts Receivable lane, ending at End event "Processing failure escalated
to Finance".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom through the Accounts Receivable lane
from the message start event through invoice review, payment request, receipt
confirmation, and amount checking. The "Payment amount correct?" gateway
branches to the discrepancy path or continues to the merge; after the merge,
flow continues to Payment Gateway / Bank submission and confirmation, then
to invoice application and customer receipt. Control then passes to the
Finance lane for approval and general ledger posting before reaching the
end event.

Message flows:
Customer → Send task "Send payment request to customer" (payment request
  notification)
Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Payment received from customer"
  (incoming payment)
Customer → User task "Log payment discrepancy and contact customer"
  (corrected payment or response)
Send task "Send payment receipt to customer" → Customer (payment receipt)
Service task "Submit payment record to Payment Gateway / Bank for
  processing" → Payment Gateway / Bank (payment submission)
Payment Gateway / Bank → Intermediate message catch event "Payment
  confirmation received from Payment Gateway / Bank" (payment confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Open Invoice" — read by "Review open invoice and expected
  payment details"; read by "Apply payment to open invoice in accounts
  receivable ledger".
Data Object "Payment Record" — written by "Confirm payment receipt and check
  amount"; read by "Submit payment record to Payment Gateway / Bank for
  processing"; read by "Review and approve payment posting".
Data Object "Payment Discrepancy Log" — written by "Log payment discrepancy
  and contact customer"; read by "Review and approve payment posting".
Data Object "Payment Receipt" — written by "Send payment receipt to
  customer"; read by "Review and approve payment posting".
Data Object "General Ledger Posting" — written by "Post payment to general
  ledger".

This subprocess captures the incoming customer payment against an open
invoice, validates the amount, processes it through the Payment Gateway /
Bank, and applies it to the accounts receivable ledger. Finance approves and
posts the transaction to the general ledger, producing a confirmed payment
record and a customer receipt. The completed posting is handed to Reconcile
Payment, where the ledger entry is matched against bank statements and
cleared.
```

### V01.09 — Reconcile Payment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V01.09 Reconcile Payment — the subprocess that matches incoming
payments to open receivables and posts the results to the general ledger,
sitting between Receive Payment and Manage Disputes & Deductions in the
Order to Cash chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sales Organisation" — the company executing the reconciliation process,
  containing the Accounts Receivable and Finance lanes.
Pool "Bank" — external financial institution that supplies the bank statement
  and transaction data.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — IT system that holds the receivables
  ledger and accepts financial postings.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Bank" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Bank
2. Sales Organisation
3. ERP / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Accounts Receivable lane (reconciliations analyst):

Message start event "Bank statement received from Receive Payment"
Service task "Import bank statement and transaction data"
User task "Match payments to open receivables"
Exclusive gateway "All payments matched?"
- branch "Yes — fully matched":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All payments matched")
- branch "No — unmatched items remain":
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Items Resolved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Identify unmatched or short-paid items",
    User task "Investigate discrepancy",
    Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy type?"
    - branch "Timing difference": User task "Flag item for next-cycle
      carry-forward" (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Overpayment or underpayment": User task "Raise adjustment
      request" (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Requires dispute": User task "Escalate to dispute management"
      (exits subprocess)
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All payments matched")
Exclusive merge gateway "All payments matched"
User task "Post matched receipts to accounts receivable ledger"
Service task "Send posting request to ERP / General Ledger System"
Intermediate message catch event "Posting confirmation received"

Finance lane (finance controller):

User task "Review reconciliation report"
Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation approved?"
- branch "Approved":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved")
- branch "Rejected — corrections required":
  User task "Return reconciliation to Accounts Receivable for correction"
  Intermediate message catch event "Corrected reconciliation received"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved"
User task "Confirm period close and archive reconciliation record"
End event "Reconciliation complete — ready for Manage Disputes & Deductions"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
Items Resolved" — label "Investigation deadline exceeded (5 business days)";
on trigger: End event "Unresolved items escalated to Finance for manual
review".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Accounts Receivable lane with the import
and matching tasks, passes through the "All payments matched?" gateway whose
unmatched branch enters the standard-loop subprocess before both branches
rejoin at the "All payments matched" merge gateway; the posting tasks follow,
then the flow passes to the Finance lane for review through the
"Reconciliation approved?" gateway, whose rejection branch loops via the
corrected-reconciliation catch event before rejoining the "Reconciliation
approved" merge gateway, leading to the close and archive task and the end
event.

Message flows:
Bank → Service task "Import bank statement and transaction data"
  (bank statement and payment transaction data)
Service task "Send posting request to ERP / General Ledger System" →
  ERP / General Ledger System (matched receipt posting request)
ERP / General Ledger System → Intermediate message catch event "Posting
  confirmation received" (general ledger posting confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Bank Statement" — read by Service task "Import bank statement
  and transaction data".
Data Object "Payment Matching Report" — written by User task "Match payments
  to open receivables"; read by User task "Review reconciliation report".
Data Object "Adjustment Request" — written by User task "Raise adjustment
  request".
Data Object "Reconciliation Record" — written by User task "Confirm period
  close and archive reconciliation record".

V01.09 Reconcile Payment takes the confirmed receipts handed over by Receive
Payment, systematically matches each incoming bank transaction to an open
receivable, resolves timing differences and short payments through a
controlled investigation loop, and posts the agreed figures to the ERP /
General Ledger System once Finance approves the reconciliation report. Any
items that cannot be resolved internally are flagged and passed to Manage
Disputes & Deductions, ensuring the ledger remains accurate and the order
cycle can be formally closed.
```

```text
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Customer Service (case manager)
  - Accounts Receivable (collections officer)
  - Finance (finance controller)

Pool "Customer" — the external buyer raising a dispute or deduction.

dispute cases.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sales Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case / Ticketing System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Sales Organisation
3. Case / Ticketing System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sales Organisation)

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Dispute or deduction request received
    from Customer"
  User task "Log and categorise dispute"
  Service task "Open dispute case in Case / Ticketing System"
  User task "Review dispute documentation and claim details"
  Exclusive gateway "Dispute type?"
  - branch "Pricing or billing error": User task
      "Escalate to Accounts Receivable for billing review"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Dispute type")
  - branch "Delivery or fulfilment claim": User task

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Dispute type")
  - branch "Contract or terms dispute": User task
      "Escalate to Finance for contract review"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Dispute type")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Dispute type"

Accounts Receivable lane:

  Exclusive gateway "Investigation outcome?"
  - branch "Additional information required": Send task
      "Request additional information from Customer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Customer responds with
        additional information"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Investigation outcome")
  - branch "Ready to resolve": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Investigation outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Investigation outcome"
  User task "Prepare resolution recommendation"
  Exclusive gateway "Resolution type?"
  - branch "Credit note to be issued": User task
      "Raise credit note for approval"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type")
  - branch "Deduction accepted": User task
      "Approve deduction and adjust receivable balance"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type")
  - branch "Dispute rejected": User task
      "Prepare rejection rationale and notify Customer"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type"

Finance lane:
  User task "Review and approve resolution"
  Exclusive gateway "Approved?"
  - branch "Not approved": User task "Return case to Accounts
      Receivable with comments"
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised recommendation
        received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approved")
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approved"
  Service task "Post financial adjustment to ERP / General Ledger"
  User task "Update dispute case status to resolved"
  Service task "Close case in Case / Ticketing System"
  Send task "Send resolution notification to Customer"
  End event "Dispute resolved — ready for Close Order"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Investigate dispute
and gather supporting evidence" — label "Investigation deadline
exceeded" — triggers escalation User task "Escalate overdue
investigation to Finance" in Finance lane, ending at End event
"Escalated dispute unresolved — ready for Close Order".

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Customer responds with additional information" — label "Customer
response deadline exceeded" — triggers User task "Mark dispute as
unresolved due to no customer response" in Accounts Receivable lane,
ending at End event "Dispute closed no response — ready for
Close Order".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Customer Service lane where the
dispute is logged and categorised before branching by dispute type;
each type branch escalates to Accounts Receivable or Finance and
rejoins at the "Dispute type" merge gateway; the Accounts Receivable
lane then investigates, requesting further information from the
Customer if needed and merging back at "Investigation outcome", then
prepares a resolution and branches by resolution type — credit note,
deduction acceptance, or rejection — all rejoining at "Resolution
type"; control passes to the Finance lane for approval, looping back
to Accounts Receivable via an intermediate catch event if not approved
and merging at "Approved"; once approved, Finance posts the financial
adjustment, closes the case, and sends the resolution notification
before the end event.

Message flows:
Customer → Customer Service lane (dispute or deduction request with
  supporting documentation)
Accounts Receivable lane → Customer (request for additional
  information)
Customer → Accounts Receivable lane (additional information response)
Customer Service lane → Case / Ticketing System (open new dispute
  case)
Finance lane → Case / Ticketing System (update and close dispute case)
Finance lane → Customer (resolution notification — credit note,
  rejection, or deduction confirmation)

7. Data objects

  documentation and claim details".

  User task "Prepare resolution recommendation".
Data Object "Resolution Recommendation" — written by User task
  "Prepare resolution recommendation"; read by User task "Review
  and approve resolution".
Data Object "Credit Note" — written by User task "Raise credit note
  for approval"; read by Service task "Post financial adjustment
  to ERP / General Ledger".
Data Object "Financial Adjustment Posting" — written by Service task
  "Post financial adjustment to ERP / General Ledger"; read by
  User task "Update dispute case status to resolved".

This subprocess takes a customer-raised dispute or deduction from
initial logging through investigation, resolution determination, and
financial adjustment, ensuring every claim is reviewed, approved, and
posted correctly before the case is closed. It hands a fully resolved
and financially posted dispute record to Close Order, where the order
can be confirmed complete and the books finalised.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
  - branch "Yes — order complete":

    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disputes or deductions

  Exclusive merge gateway "Disputes or deductions open"

Finance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Order closure notification
    received from Order Processing"
  User task "Verify all financial postings complete"

  - branch "No — postings missing": User task "Raise and post
    missing journal entries in ERP"

  - branch "Yes — all postings complete":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Financial postings
    complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Financial postings complete"
  User task "Confirm revenue recognised in line with policy"
  Service task "Post final revenue recognition entry to General Ledger"
  User task "Archive order documentation"
  End event "Order formally closed and all records archived"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Flag outstanding items
  for resolution" — label "Resolution overdue (5 business days)" —
  flows to End event "Order closure escalated — unresolved items
  outstanding".
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Confirm dispute or
  deduction resolved" — label "Dispute resolution overdue (10 business
  days)" — flows to End event "Order closure escalated — dispute
  unresolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Order Processing lane, passing
through completeness and dispute checks before the order status is
updated and a closure notification is sent to Finance; the Finance lane
picks up the notification, verifies and corrects postings where needed,
confirms revenue recognition, and posts the final General Ledger entry
before archiving and ending. The "All items fulfilled and invoiced"
gateway branches on an outstanding-items path that loops back via the
merge before progressing; the "Disputes or deductions open" gateway
holds progress until resolution is confirmed before reaching the same
merge.

Message flows:
Sales Organisation (Service task "Update order status to closed in
  OMS") → Order Management System (OMS) (updated order status record).
Order Management System (OMS) → Sales Organisation (User task "Review

Sales Organisation (Service task "Record corrected postings in ERP /
  General Ledger") → ERP / General Ledger System (corrected journal
  entries).
Sales Organisation (Service task "Post final revenue recognition entry
  to General Ledger") → ERP / General Ledger System (revenue

Data Object "Order Completion Checklist" — written by User task
  "Review order for completeness"; read by User task "Confirm delivery
  and fulfilment obligations met".
Data Object "Outstanding Items Record" — written by User task "Flag
  outstanding items for resolution"; read by Exclusive gateway "All
  items fulfilled and invoiced?".
Data Object "Financial Postings Summary" — written by User task
  "Verify all financial postings complete"; read by User task "Confirm
  revenue recognised in line with policy".
Data Object "Revenue Recognition Entry" — written by User task
  "Confirm revenue recognised in line with policy"; read by Service
  task "Post final revenue recognition entry to General Ledger".
Data Object "Archived Order Record" — written by User task "Archive
  order documentation".

Close Order confirms that every fulfilment, invoicing, and payment
obligation has been met and that all financial entries are correctly
posted and recognised. It formally sets the sales order to closed in
the Order Management System and posts the final revenue recognition
entry to the General Ledger, leaving a complete and auditable record.
Because this is the last subprocess in the Order to Cash chain, the end
event marks the conclusion of the entire cycle with no handoff to a
successor process.
```

## V02 — Procure to Pay

**Teams and roles involved.**
Procure to Pay involves Procurement, Requesting Departments, Finance, Accounts Payable, Receiving/Warehouse, Legal, Contract Management, and sometimes Risk or Compliance. Key roles include requisitioner, procurement officer, category manager, buyer, approver, goods receipting officer, accounts payable officer, contract manager, and finance controller.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Supplier or Seller. The process may be initiated by an internal purchase need, but the external interaction begins when suppliers respond to purchase orders, provide goods or services, submit invoices, or resolve payment queries.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: identify need, create requisition, approve purchase, issue purchase order, receive goods or confirm services, match purchase order/goods receipt/invoice, approve invoice, pay supplier, handle exceptions, and close the procurement transaction.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ERP procurement modules, supplier portal, purchase requisition system, contract management system, inventory or warehouse system, accounts payable system, electronic invoicing system, payment platform, document management, and workflow/approval tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include procurement policy, delegation of authority, purchase approval procedure, supplier onboarding policy, conflict of interest policy, contract management procedure, goods receipting procedure, invoice matching rules, payment terms policy, and anti-bribery/corruption controls.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Suppliers receive purchase orders, delivery instructions, contract terms, remittance advice, and payment status. Suppliers provide quotes, order acknowledgements, delivery notices, goods/services, invoices, credit notes, tax documents, and bank/payment details.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process records supplier master data, requisitions, approvals, purchase orders, goods receipts, service confirmations, invoices, payment runs, and accounting entries. IT systems provide approved supplier lists, contract pricing, budget availability, approval status, open purchase orders, invoice exceptions, and payment status.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V02 - Procure to Pay (P2P)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V02.01. Identify Need
V02.02. Create Requisition
V02.03. Approve Purchase
V02.04. Issue Purchase Order
V02.05. Receive Goods / Confirm Services
V02.06. Match PO / GR / Invoice
V02.07. Approve Invoice
V02.08. Pay Supplier
V02.09. Handle Exceptions
V02.10. Close Procurement Transaction

This is the supply-side, spend-management end-to-end process: an internal
purchase need flows through requisition, approval, ordering, receipt,
three-way matching, invoice approval and payment. The main external
participant is the Supplier (Seller); the process is triggered by an
internal need (a reorder point, a project requirement or a replenishment),
and the external interaction begins when the purchase order is issued to
the supplier.
```

**Context diagram prompt.**

```text
Context Diagram: V02 — Procure to Pay (P2P).

1. Central system (process-system)
A single central process/system ellipse named "Procurement Company"
representing the whole organisation that runs the Procure to Pay process. It
is the system in context: everything inside it — requesting departments,
procurement, receiving, accounts payable, finance and the supporting IT
systems (ERP procurement, requisition, supplier portal, contract, warehouse,
accounts payable and general ledger) — is treated as one black box.

2. External entities (external-entity)
The parties OUTSIDE the company that exchange information with it, one
rectangle each:
- Supplier
- Freight Carrier
- Payment Platform
- Bank

3. Layout
"Procurement Company" sits in the centre. The Supplier sits to the RIGHT
(the supply side that receives orders and is paid). Freight Carrier sits to
the RIGHT (delivery). Payment Platform and Bank sit to the RIGHT (settlement).
The demand originates INSIDE the company (an internal need), so no external
demand actor sits on the left. Every external entity connects directly to the
central system with labelled information flows; entities never connect to one
another.

4. Information flows (each a labelled connector between an external entity and
   the central system; show both directions where information flows both ways)
- Procurement Company → Supplier: request for quote, purchase order, delivery
  instructions, contract terms, remittance advice, payment status.
- Supplier → Procurement Company: quote, order acknowledgement, delivery
  notice, goods / services, invoice, credit note, tax documents, bank details.
- Procurement Company → Freight Carrier: inbound collection / delivery
  booking (where the buyer arranges carriage).
- Freight Carrier → Procurement Company: delivery notification & proof of
  delivery.
- Procurement Company → Payment Platform: payment instruction / payment run.
- Payment Platform → Procurement Company: payment confirmation & settlement
  advice.
- Bank → Procurement Company: bank statement & cleared payments.
- Procurement Company → Bank: payment file & remittance details.

This Context Diagram frames the Procurement Company as a single system in
context: an internal need drives the Procure to Pay process, the Supplier
provides the goods or services and is paid, the Freight Carrier delivers, and
the Payment Platform and Bank settle payment. The four external entities are
exactly the external actors of the Process Context diagram below, so the two
views stay consistent.
```

```text
This Process Context diagram frames the whole Procure to Pay value chain: the
```

A single high-level ArchiMate view of the Procure to Pay service area. It shows

```text
ArchiMate: V02 — Procure to Pay — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: show how the organisation provides the Purchasing Service and the
related services (to the internal requesters and to the Supplier) across the ten

PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS — with the internal Requesting Department on the far
left and the Supplier / settlement actors on the far right. Read top-to-bottom
as service → process → application (ArchiMate service realisation).

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)
- Requesting Department — the internal party the purchasing service is provided
  to (far left, the originator of every need).

  The Supplier ACCESSES this interface; the interface SERVES the business

- Application Interfaces (optional, only the few the portal calls): "Ordering
```
