```text
3. Business Services (Business Service) — the services provided, top band,
   left-to-right in procurement-journey order:
- Requisition & Approval Service — capture the need, requisition and approve.
- Purchasing Service — issue the purchase order to the supplier.
- Goods & Service Receipt Service — receive goods, confirm services.
- Invoice Matching & Approval Service — match and approve supplier invoices.
- Payment & Settlement Service — pay the supplier and settle.
- Exception & Closure Service — resolve exceptions and close the transaction.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — the ten V02 processes, middle band in
   V02.01 → V02.10 order. Each REALISES the business service shown and is the
   link anchor to its BPMN diagram:
- V02.01 Identify Need                    -> realises Requisition & Approval Service
- V02.02 Create Requisition               -> realises Requisition & Approval Service
- V02.03 Approve Purchase                 -> realises Requisition & Approval Service
- V02.04 Issue Purchase Order             -> realises Purchasing Service
- V02.05 Receive Goods / Confirm Services -> realises Goods & Service Receipt Service
- V02.06 Match PO / GR / Invoice          -> realises Invoice Matching & Approval Service
- V02.07 Approve Invoice                  -> realises Invoice Matching & Approval Service
- V02.08 Pay Supplier                     -> realises Payment & Settlement Service
- V02.09 Handle Exceptions                -> realises Exception & Closure Service
- V02.10 Close Procurement Transaction    -> realises Exception & Closure Service

5. Applications (Application Component) — the IT systems that support the
   processes, bottom band:
- ERP / Catalogue System
- Purchase Requisition System
- ERP / Budgeting System
- ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal
- Inventory / Warehouse System (GRN)
- Accounts Payable / Invoice System
- Payment Platform / Banking System
- Case / Workflow System
- ERP / General Ledger System

6. Relationships
- Supplier -accesses-> Supplier Portal / Purchasing Channel.
- Supplier Portal / Purchasing Channel -serving-> the Purchasing, Receipt,
  Invoice and Payment services.
- Each Business Process -realisation-> its Business Service (section 4).
- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
  (serving, application -> process):
    V02.01 <- ERP / Catalogue System;      V02.02 <- Purchase Requisition System;
    V02.03 <- ERP / Budgeting System;       V02.04 <- ERP Procurement / Supplier Portal;
    V02.05 <- Inventory / Warehouse (GRN);  V02.06 <- Accounts Payable / Invoice System;
    V02.07 <- Accounts Payable / Invoice System; V02.08 <- Payment Platform / Banking;
    V02.09 <- Case / Workflow System;       V02.10 <- ERP Procurement + ERP / General Ledger.
- Freight Carrier -serving-> V02.05 Receive Goods / Confirm Services.
- Payment Platform and Bank -serving-> V02.08 Pay Supplier.

7. Intent
The Purchasing Service sits top-centre as the headline service. The ten Business
Processes form the backbone in V02.01 -> V02.10 order so the reader can trace
the procurement journey and drill from any process straight into its detailed

diagrams. The mapping of process -> actors/teams/applications is the Process
<-> Actors / Teams / IT Systems matrix above.
```

**BPMN prompt conventions (V02 onward).**

The per-process BPMN prompts below follow three modelling conventions that
differ from V01, applied consistently across every stage:

1. **Rework / retry = Expanded Subprocess with a loop marker.** Any place a step
   may need to be repeated until it succeeds (correct a document, resolve a
   mismatch, chase a supplier response) is modelled as an **Expanded Subprocess**
   carrying a **standard loop marker (⟳)**. Its internals show a single attempt
   (try → optional wait → an exclusive gateway "«resolved?»" whose "Yes" reaches
   the subprocess end); the loop marker repeats the attempt while the condition
   is unmet — so no loop-back sequence flow is drawn inside the subprocess.
2. **Timeouts = interrupting timer boundary event on the Expanded Subprocess.**
   Each retry subprocess carries one **interrupting timer boundary event** on its
   boundary ("«deadline»"). When it fires it cancels the subprocess (all retries)
   and routes to an "Escalate to «manager»" task followed by an **escalation end
   event** — this stage ends abnormally and the parent value chain decides what
   happens next. **No non-interrupting boundary events are used anywhere.**
3. **Consistent numbering.** Stages are numbered V02.01 … V02.10 exactly as the
   high-level subprocess list and every other V02 diagram above.

### V02.01 — Identify Need

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.01 Identify Need — first subprocess of the Procure to Pay
value chain, capturing how an internal purchase need is recognised and
documented before a formal requisition is raised.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams that identify and
validate the purchase need.
  Lane "Requesting Department" — requisitioner who identifies and
  documents the need.
  Lane "Procurement" — procurement officer who reviews, validates,
  and decides how to proceed.
Pool "ERP / Catalogue System" — IT system providing catalogue data,
budget availability, and approved supplier lists.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / Catalogue System": black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Buying Organisation (white-box, contains all sequence flow)
2. ERP / Catalogue System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Requesting Department lane:
  Start event "Internal purchase need arises"
  User task "Describe and document the need"
  User task "Estimate quantity and required delivery date"
  Send task "Submit need details to Procurement"

Procurement lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Need details received from
  Requesting Department"
  Service task "Check catalogue for existing items and contracts"
  Service task "Check budget availability"
  Exclusive gateway "Need valid and funded?"
  - branch "No — budget or scope issue": User task "Return need to
    requisitioner with comments"
    Intermediate message catch event "Revised need details received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Need valid and funded?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Need valid
    and funded?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Need valid and funded?"
  Exclusive gateway "Sourcing route?"
  - branch "Existing contract or catalogue item": User task
    "Record need against existing contract or catalogue item"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sourcing route?")
  - branch "New or spot purchase required": User task
    "Classify need and determine procurement category"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sourcing route?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sourcing route?"
  User task "Confirm need is approved to proceed to requisition"
  End event "Need identified and confirmed — ready for
  Create Requisition"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Return need to
requisitioner with comments": label "Requisitioner non-response
deadline", triggers User task "Escalate unresolved need to
Procurement manager", followed by Escalation end event "Need
identification timed out — escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Requesting Department lane,
passes through documenting and submitting the need, then crosses
into the Procurement lane where the two exclusive gateways
("Need valid and funded?" and "Sourcing route?") each diverge into
their respective branches before converging at their named merge
gateways, and the flow ends at the confirmed-need end event.
The "No" branch of "Need valid and funded?" loops back into the
merge gateway after the revised need is received; the timer
boundary event on the return task exits to the escalation path
without rejoining the main flow.

Message flows:
ERP / Catalogue System → Service task "Check catalogue for
existing items and contracts" (catalogue items, approved supplier
list, contract pricing).
ERP / Catalogue System → Service task "Check budget availability"
(budget availability data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Purchase Need Record" — written by User task "Describe
and document the need"; read by User task "Estimate quantity and
required delivery date"; read by Service task "Check catalogue for
existing items and contracts"; read by User task "Classify need and
determine procurement category"; read by User task "Confirm need is
approved to proceed to requisition".
Data Object "Budget Check Result" — written by Service task "Check
budget availability"; read by Exclusive gateway "Need valid and
funded?".

This subprocess captures an internal purchase need, validates it
against available budget and existing catalogue items or contracts,
and routes it down the correct sourcing path. It hands a confirmed,
classified, and approved-to-proceed need record to the Create
Requisition subprocess, ensuring only legitimate and funded needs
advance in the Procure to Pay value chain.
```

### V02.02 — Create Requisition

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.02 Create Requisition — second subprocess in the Procure to Pay
value chain, converting an identified need into a formally recorded and
categorised purchase requisition ready for approval.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams that create and validate
the purchase requisition.
  Lane "Requesting Department" — requisitioner who drafts the requisition.
  Lane "Procurement" — buyer who reviews and completes the requisition.
Pool "Purchase Requisition System" — system that stores and routes
requisitions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Purchase Requisition System": black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Buying Organisation (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Requesting
   Department, Procurement)
2. Purchase Requisition System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Requesting Department lane:
  Message start event "Need confirmed — received from Identify Need"
  User task "Draft requisition details"
  User task "Attach supporting documentation"
  Exclusive gateway "Requisition details complete?"
  - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Correct requisition
    details", Intermediate message catch event "Corrections reviewed",
    Exclusive gateway "Details now complete?" whose "Yes" branch exits
    subprocess and whose "No" branch loops repeats.
    Interrupting timer boundary event "48-hour correction deadline" on
    the subprocess — fires to: User task "Escalate incomplete requisition
    to Procurement lead", then Escalation end event "Requisition
    abandoned — escalated to Procurement lead"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Requisition
    details complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Requisition details complete"
  Service task "Submit requisition to Purchase Requisition System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Requisition reference number
  received"
  User task "Confirm submission to requester"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Review requisition for policy compliance"
  User task "Classify spend category and assign supplier type"
  Exclusive gateway "Requisition acceptable?"
  - branch "No": User task "Return requisition to requester with
    comments" (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Requisition
    acceptable")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Requisition
    acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Requisition acceptable"
  Exclusive gateway "Returned to requester?"
  - branch "Yes": Intermediate message catch event "Corrected
    requisition received", (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Returned to requester")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Returned to
    requester")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Returned to requester"
  User task "Record spend classification in Purchase Requisition System"
  User task "Confirm requisition ready for approval"
  End event "Requisition complete — ready for Approve Purchase"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "48-hour correction deadline" — mounted
on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete" in the Requesting
Department lane — fires when the 48-hour deadline expires, cancels the
subprocess, routes to User task "Escalate incomplete requisition to
Procurement lead", then Escalation end event "Requisition abandoned —
escalated to Procurement lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Requesting Department lane with the
message start event, passes through drafting and documentation tasks, then
the completeness gateway — the "No" branch enters the correction
subprocess (looping until complete or timing out to escalation); the "Yes"
branch and the subprocess exit both merge at the exclusive merge gateway
"Requisition details complete", then the requisition is submitted and
acknowledged. Control passes to the Procurement lane for compliance review
and classification; the "No" branch of "Requisition acceptable" returns
the requisition with comments and the "Yes" branch rejoins at the merge
gateway; both branches then test whether the requisition was returned,
waiting on the corrected version if so, before flowing to spend
classification, system recording, and the end event.

Message flows:
  Service task "Submit requisition to Purchase Requisition System" →
    Purchase Requisition System (requisition record submitted for
    storage and routing)
  Purchase Requisition System → Intermediate message catch event
    "Requisition reference number received" (system-assigned reference
    number returned to Requesting Department lane)
  User task "Record spend classification in Purchase Requisition System"
    → Purchase Requisition System (spend category and supplier type
    classification written to requisition record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Purchase Requisition" — written by User task "Draft
requisition details"; read by User task "Attach supporting documentation";
read by User task "Review requisition for policy compliance"; read/written
by User task "Classify spend category and assign supplier type"; read by
User task "Record spend classification in Purchase Requisition System".

Data Object "Supporting Documentation" — written by User task "Attach
supporting documentation"; read by User task "Review requisition for
policy compliance".

This subprocess takes a confirmed internal need and produces a formally
drafted, documented, and classified purchase requisition that has passed a
Procurement compliance review. All requisition details, spend categories,
and supplier type assignments are recorded in the Purchase Requisition
System. The completed requisition is handed to Approve Purchase, where
budget holders and finance will authorise or reject it before a purchase
order can be raised.
```

### V02.03 — Approve Purchase

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.03 Approve Purchase — third subprocess in the Procure to Pay
value chain, receiving a submitted requisition and returning a budget-confirmed
approval decision ready for purchase order issue.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams that approve the purchase
  requisition against budget and policy.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
    - Procurement (buyer)
    - Budget Holder / Approver (approver)
    - Finance / Treasury (finance controller)
Pool "ERP / Budgeting System" — IT system that holds budget data, approval
  workflow, and records approval decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / Budgeting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. Buying Organisation
  2. ERP / Budgeting System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Procurement (buyer) lane:
  Message start event "Approved requisition received from Create Requisition"
  Service task "Retrieve requisition details from ERP / Budgeting System"
  User task "Review requisition for policy and category compliance"
  Exclusive gateway "Policy compliant?"
  - branch "No": User task "Return requisition to requestor with comments"
      End event "Requisition returned — non-compliant, exits subprocess"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Policy compliant")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Policy compliant"
  Send task "Forward requisition for budget holder approval"

Budget Holder / Approver (approver) lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Requisition forwarded for approval"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Budget Holder Decision Received"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review requisition and supporting documentation"
    Exclusive gateway "Decision made?"
    - branch "Approved": (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Rejected": (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Information required": Send task
        "Request additional information from buyer"
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received"
        (loop repeats)
  Interrupting timer boundary event on "Repeat Until Budget Holder Decision
    Received" labelled "Approval deadline exceeded":
    User task "Escalate to finance controller"
    Escalation end event "Approval escalated — exits subprocess"
  Exclusive gateway "Budget holder decision?"
  - branch "Rejected": User task "Notify buyer of rejection with reason"
      End event "Requisition rejected by budget holder — exits subprocess"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Budget holder decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Budget holder decision"
  Service task "Record budget holder approval in ERP / Budgeting System"

Finance / Treasury (finance controller) lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Budget holder approval recorded"
  User task "Verify budget availability and financial authority"
  Exclusive gateway "Budget available and authority confirmed?"
  - branch "No — insufficient budget": User task
      "Notify procurement of budget shortfall"
      End event "Approval failed — budget insufficient, exits subprocess"
  - branch "No — authority exceeded": User task
      "Escalate to senior finance authority"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Senior Authority Decision Received"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Submit for senior authority review"
        Exclusive gateway "Senior authority decision made?"
        - branch "Approved": (exits subprocess)
        - branch "More information required": (loop repeats)
      Interrupting timer boundary event on "Repeat Until Senior Authority
        Decision Received" labelled "Senior authority deadline exceeded":
        User task "Escalate to finance director"
        Escalation end event "Senior authority escalated — exits subprocess"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Budget available and authority confirmed")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Budget available and authority confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Budget available and authority confirmed"
  Service task "Record financial approval and commit budget in ERP /
    Budgeting System"
  User task "Confirm purchase approval and notify buyer"
  End event "Purchase approved — ready for Issue Purchase Order"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess "Repeat Until Budget
  Holder Decision Received", labelled "Approval deadline exceeded" —
  interrupting; cancels the subprocess; routes to User task "Escalate to
  finance controller" then Escalation end event "Approval escalated —
  exits subprocess".
Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess "Repeat Until Senior
  Authority Decision Received", labelled "Senior authority deadline exceeded" —
  interrupting; cancels the subprocess; routes to User task "Escalate to
  finance director" then Escalation end event "Senior authority escalated —
  exits subprocess".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Procurement lane with the message start
  event, passes through the policy compliance gateway (non-compliant branch
  ends there; compliant branch merges and continues), then crosses to the
  Budget Holder / Approver lane via send task and intermediate catch event.
  The budget holder approval loop subprocess runs with the timer boundary
  as its escape route; on rejection the flow ends in the Budget Holder lane;
  on approval the flow continues via the decision gateway and merge, then
  a service task records the decision before crossing to the Finance / Treasury
  lane via an intermediate catch event. The finance lane runs the budget and
  authority check; insufficient budget and escalation paths end in that lane;
  the confirmed path merges, commits budget, notifies the buyer, and reaches
  the normal end event.

Message flows:
  Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve requisition details from ERP /
    Budgeting System") → ERP / Budgeting System (requisition record request).
  ERP / Budgeting System → Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve
    requisition details from ERP / Budgeting System") (requisition details
    and budget data).
  Buying Organisation (Service task "Record budget holder approval in ERP /
    Budgeting System") → ERP / Budgeting System (approval record).
  Buying Organisation (Service task "Record financial approval and commit
    budget in ERP / Budgeting System") → ERP / Budgeting System
    (financial approval and budget commitment).
  ERP / Budgeting System → Buying Organisation (Service task "Record financial
    approval and commit budget in ERP / Budgeting System")
    (budget commitment confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Purchase Requisition" — read by "Review requisition for policy
  and category compliance"; read by "Review requisition and supporting
  documentation"; read by "Verify budget availability and financial authority".
Data Object "Approval Decision Record" — written by "Record budget holder
  approval in ERP / Budgeting System"; written by "Record financial approval
  and commit budget in ERP / Budgeting System".
Data Object "Budget Availability Report" — read by "Verify budget availability
  and financial authority"; written by "Record financial approval and commit
  budget in ERP / Budgeting System".

V02.03 Approve Purchase takes the validated requisition from Create Requisition
and routes it through a two-stage approval: first a policy and category review
by the buyer, then budget holder sign-off, and finally a financial authority and
budget availability check by Finance / Treasury. Timed escalation paths handle
stalled approvals, and rejections at any stage close the subprocess abnormally.
The normal outcome — a committed budget entry and a confirmed approval — is
handed to Issue Purchase Order so a purchase order can be raised against a
funded, authorised requisition.
```

### V02.04 — Issue Purchase Order

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

Procure to Pay value chain, covering the preparation, approval, and
dispatch of the purchase order to the supplier, following approved
purchase requisition.

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams that create and issue
the purchase order.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Procurement (buyer)
  - Contract Management (contract manager)
Pool "Supplier" — external party that receives and acknowledges the
purchase order.

the purchase order and transmits it to the supplier.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal" — black-box,
System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Buying Organisation
3. ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Approved purchase requisition received from
  Approve Purchase"
  User task "Review approved requisition and confirm supplier selection"
  Exclusive gateway "Existing contract in place?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract check
    complete")
  - branch "No": User task "Identify and engage suitable supplier"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract check complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Contract check complete"
  User task "Draft purchase order details"
  Send task "Send draft PO to Contract Management for review"

Contract Management lane:
  User task "Review draft purchase order against contract terms"
  Exclusive gateway "PO aligned with contract?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Return approved PO to Procurement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PO review outcome")
  - branch "No": User task "Mark discrepancies and return to Procurement"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until PO Revised and Approved" (standard
    loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Revise purchase order to address discrepancies",
      Send task "Resubmit revised PO to Contract Management",
      User task "Re-review revised purchase order",
      Exclusive gateway "PO now aligned?"
      - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
      - branch "No": (loop repeats)
    Interrupting timer boundary event "Revision deadline exceeded" on
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until PO Revised and Approved" → User
    task "Escalate PO revision failure to category manager" → Escalation
    end event "PO revision escalated — contract manager notified"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PO review outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "PO review outcome"
  Send task "Forward finalised PO to Procurement for issuance"

Procurement lane (continued):
  User task "Finalise and authorise purchase order"
  Service task "Record authorised purchase order in ERP Procurement
  System"
  Send task "Issue purchase order to supplier via Supplier Portal"
  Intermediate message catch event "Order acknowledgement received from
  supplier"
  Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement
    check")
  - branch "No":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Acknowledgement Resolved"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
      Send task "Contact supplier to resolve acknowledgement query",
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received",
      Exclusive gateway "Issue resolved?"
      - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
      - branch "No": (loop repeats)
    Interrupting timer boundary event "Acknowledgement resolution
    deadline exceeded" on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
    Acknowledgement Resolved" → User task "Escalate unresolved
    acknowledgement to procurement manager" → Escalation end event "PO
    acknowledgement escalated — unresolved"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement check")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement check"
  User task "Confirm purchase order status and update records"
  Service task "Update purchase order status in ERP Procurement System"
  End event "Purchase order issued and confirmed — ready for Receive
  Goods / Confirm Services"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "Revision deadline exceeded" —
attached to Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until PO Revised and Approved"
— fires when the revision cycle exceeds its permitted duration, cancels
the subprocess, routes to User task "Escalate PO revision failure to
category manager", then to Escalation end event "PO revision escalated
— contract manager notified".

Interrupting timer boundary event "Acknowledgement resolution deadline
exceeded" — attached to Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Acknowledgement Resolved" — fires when the resolution cycle exceeds its
permitted duration, cancels the subprocess, routes to User task
"Escalate unresolved acknowledgement to procurement manager", then to
Escalation end event "PO acknowledgement escalated — unresolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Procurement lane with the message
start event, passes through supplier selection and the "Contract check
complete" merge, then draft PO creation and handoff to Contract
Management. The Contract Management lane handles review; the "PO
aligned with contract?" gateway branches to direct approval or the
revision loop, both rejoining at "PO review outcome", before returning
to Procurement. Procurement finalises, records, and issues the PO; the
"Acknowledgement acceptable?" gateway branches to direct confirmation or
the acknowledgement resolution loop, both rejoining at "Acknowledgement
check", leading to the update tasks and the end event. Escalation
branches from both boundary events terminate at their own escalation end
events and do not rejoin the main flow.

Message flows:
ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal → Procurement lane
  (authorised purchase order recorded and confirmation returned)
Procurement lane → ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal
  (purchase order transmitted via Supplier Portal)
Procurement lane → Supplier (purchase order issued)
Supplier → Procurement lane (order acknowledgement)
Procurement lane → Supplier (query to resolve acknowledgement)
Supplier → Procurement lane (response to acknowledgement query)
Procurement lane → ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal
  (purchase order status update)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Purchase Requisition" — read by User task "Review
approved requisition and confirm supplier selection".
Data Object "Draft Purchase Order" — written by User task "Draft
purchase order details"; read by User task "Review draft purchase order
against contract terms".
Data Object "Reviewed Purchase Order" — written by User task "Review
draft purchase order against contract terms"; read by User task
"Finalise and authorise purchase order".
Data Object "Authorised Purchase Order" — written by User task "Finalise
and authorise purchase order"; read by Service task "Record authorised
purchase order in ERP Procurement System" and Send task "Issue purchase
order to supplier via Supplier Portal".
Data Object "Order Acknowledgement" — written by Intermediate message
catch event "Order acknowledgement received from supplier"; read by
Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement acceptable?".

V02.04 Issue Purchase Order transforms an approved requisition into a
formally issued and supplier-confirmed purchase order. It ensures the PO
aligns with existing contract terms, is authorised under the delegation
of authority policy, is transmitted to the supplier through the ERP
Procurement System and Supplier Portal, and that a valid acknowledgement
is received. The confirmed purchase order record is then handed to
V02.05 Receive Goods / Confirm Services, which uses it to validate
incoming deliveries or service completions.
```

### V02.05 — Receive Goods / Confirm Services

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.05 Receive Goods / Confirm Services — sits between Issue
Purchase Order and Match PO / GR / Invoice in the Procure to Pay chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams that receive goods and
confirm services.

  records physical deliveries.
  Lane "Requesting Department" — requisitioner who confirms services or

Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System" — warehouse and goods-receipt system
that records GRNs.

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / Warehouse System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Freight Carrier
3. Buying Organisation
4. Inventory / Warehouse System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Receiving / Warehouse lane:
  Message start event "Purchase order issued — delivery expected from
  Issue Purchase Order"
  Exclusive gateway "Delivery type?"
  - branch "Physical goods": Intermediate message catch event "Delivery
    notice received from Freight Carrier"
    User task "Book delivery slot and prepare receiving dock"
    Intermediate message catch event "Shipment arrives at dock"
    User task "Inspect goods against purchase order"
    Exclusive gateway "Goods acceptable?"
    - branch "Yes — fully acceptable":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Goods acceptable?")
    - branch "Partial or damaged":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Discrepancy Resolved" (standard
      loop) containing, in order: User task "Record discrepancy and
      contact supplier", Intermediate message catch event "Supplier
      response received", Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolved?"
      whose "Yes" branch exits the subprocess and whose "No" branch
      loops.
      Timer boundary event "72-hour resolution deadline" interrupting,
      attached to "Repeat Until Discrepancy Resolved" — on fire: User
      task "Escalate unresolved goods discrepancy to category manager",
      Escalation end event "Goods discrepancy escalated — exception
      raised"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Goods acceptable?")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Goods acceptable?"
    Service task "Record goods receipt and create GRN in Inventory /
    Warehouse System"
    User task "Sign and file proof of delivery"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery type?")
  - branch "Services or intangible delivery":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery type?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery type?"

Requesting Department lane:
  User task "Review service delivery evidence or completion report"
  Exclusive gateway "Service delivery acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Service delivery
    acceptable?")
  - branch "No — shortfall identified":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Service Confirmed" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Raise service shortfall with
    supplier", Intermediate message catch event "Supplier clarification
    received", Exclusive gateway "Shortfall resolved?" whose "Yes"
    branch exits the subprocess and whose "No" branch loops.
    Timer boundary event "5-day confirmation deadline" interrupting,
    attached to "Repeat Until Service Confirmed" — on fire: User task
    "Escalate unresolved service shortfall to finance controller",
    Escalation end event "Service confirmation escalated — exception
    raised"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Service delivery
    acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Service delivery acceptable?"
  User task "Record service confirmation"
  Service task "Post service confirmation to Inventory / Warehouse
  System"
  End event "Goods receipt or service confirmation complete — ready
  for Match PO / GR / Invoice"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "72-hour resolution deadline" —
attached to Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Discrepancy Resolved" in
the Receiving / Warehouse lane; on fire, cancels the subprocess and
routes to User task "Escalate unresolved goods discrepancy to category
manager" then Escalation end event "Goods discrepancy escalated —
exception raised".

Interrupting timer boundary event "5-day confirmation deadline" —
attached to Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Service Confirmed" in the

to User task "Escalate unresolved service shortfall to finance

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Receiving / Warehouse lane at the
message start event and immediately diverges at the "Delivery type?"
exclusive gateway; the physical-goods branch passes through the
Freight Carrier message catch events, inspection, the "Goods
acceptable?" gateway (whose partial-or-damaged branch enters the loop
subprocess and returns to the merge, and whose escalation path ends at
an escalation end event), then GRN creation, and rejoins at the
"Delivery type?" exclusive merge gateway; the services branch passes
directly to that same merge gateway; flow then continues into the
Requesting Department lane, through service-delivery review, the
"Service delivery acceptable?" gateway (whose shortfall branch enters
the loop subprocess and returns to the merge, and whose escalation path
ends at an escalation end event), then service confirmation posting,
and closes at the end event.

Message flows:
Supplier → Receiving / Warehouse lane, "Book delivery slot and prepare
receiving dock" (advance shipment notice / delivery notice).
Freight Carrier → Receiving / Warehouse lane, Intermediate message
catch event "Shipment arrives at dock" (physical shipment handover).
Receiving / Warehouse lane, "Record discrepancy and contact supplier"
→ Supplier (discrepancy notification).
Supplier → Receiving / Warehouse lane, Intermediate message catch event

Warehouse System" → Inventory / Warehouse System (service confirmation

order".
Data Object "Delivery Notice" — read by "Book delivery slot and prepare

notice received from Freight Carrier".
Data Object "Discrepancy Report" — written by "Record discrepancy and

Data Object "Service Completion Report" — read by "Review service
delivery evidence or completion report"; written by "Record service
confirmation".
Data Object "Service Shortfall Record" — written by "Raise service
shortfall with supplier"; read by "Escalate unresolved service
shortfall to finance controller".

This subprocess receives the purchase order signal from Issue Purchase
Order and manages the two parallel receipt paths — physical goods
inspection and receipting at the warehouse, and intangible service
confirmation by the requesting department. It produces either a signed
Goods Receipt Note recorded in the Inventory / Warehouse System or a
posted service confirmation, and hands a completed receipt record to
Match PO / GR / Invoice so that three-way matching can begin.
```

### V02.06 — Match PO / GR / Invoice

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.06 Match PO / GR / Invoice — the accounts payable stage that
reconciles the purchase order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice before
approving the liability for payment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal teams performing three-way matching
  Lane "Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer)"
Pool "Supplier" — external party whose invoice triggers the match process
Pool "Accounts Payable / Invoice System" — records invoices, match results,
  and exception flags

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Accounts Payable / Invoice System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance

3. Layout

Top: Supplier
Middle: Buying Organisation
Bottom: Accounts Payable / Invoice System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane:
  Message start event "Supplier invoice received from Issue Purchase Order"
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from system"
  Service task "Retrieve goods receipt / service confirmation from system"
  User task "Register invoice against PO and GR"
  Service task "Record invoice in Accounts Payable / Invoice System"
  Exclusive gateway "Invoice matches PO and GR?"
  - branch "Yes — full match":
      Service task "Mark invoice as matched in system"
      End event "Invoice matched — ready for Approve Invoice"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found":
      Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Invoice Discrepancy" (standard loop)
        containing, in order:
        User task "Identify and categorise discrepancy"
        Send task "Request clarification or credit note from supplier"
        Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
        User task "Review supplier response and updated documents"
        Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolved?"
        - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
        - branch "No": (loop repeats)
      Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice matches PO and GR?"
      Service task "Mark invoice as matched in system"
      End event "Invoice matched — ready for Approve Invoice"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve Invoice Discrepancy",
  label "Resolution deadline exceeded", routes to:
  User task "Escalate unresolved discrepancy to Finance Controller"
  followed by Escalation end event "Discrepancy unresolved — escalated to
  Handle Exceptions"

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Accounts Payable lane with the message
start event, proceeds through retrieval and registration tasks, then enters
the "Invoice matches PO and GR?" gateway; the "Yes" branch flows directly
to "Mark invoice as matched in system" and the matched end event; the "No"
branch enters the "Resolve Invoice Discrepancy" expanded subprocess, whose
normal exit rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway "Invoice matches PO and
GR?" and then flows to "Mark invoice as matched in system" and the same
matched end event; the timer boundary on the subprocess routes to the
escalation task and escalation end event outside the subprocess.

Message flows:
Supplier → Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane (supplier
  invoice document triggering the start event)
Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane → Supplier (clarification
  request or credit note request during discrepancy resolution)
Supplier → Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane (supplier
  response or revised invoice during discrepancy resolution)
Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane →
  Accounts Payable / Invoice System (invoice registration, match status
  update, and exception flag writes)
Accounts Payable / Invoice System →
  Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) lane (open PO data, GR
  confirmation data, and current invoice status reads)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Supplier Invoice" — written by "Register invoice against PO
  and GR"; read by "Identify and categorise discrepancy"
Data Object "Purchase Order" — read by "Retrieve open purchase order from
  system"; read by "Register invoice against PO and GR"
Data Object "Goods Receipt / Service Confirmation" — read by "Retrieve
  goods receipt / service confirmation from system"; read by "Register
  invoice against PO and GR"
Data Object "Match Result Record" — written by "Mark invoice as matched in
  system"; read by downstream Approve Invoice subprocess

This subprocess takes the supplier invoice produced in Issue Purchase Order
and reconciles it against the open purchase order and goods receipt or
service confirmation on file. When all three documents agree the invoice is
marked as matched and handed to Approve Invoice for final liability sign-off.
Discrepancies trigger a structured retry loop that contacts the supplier for
correction; if resolution is not achieved within the deadline the matter
escalates abnormally to Handle Exceptions, keeping the payment cycle on track
without leaving unresolved liabilities dormant.
```

### V02.07 — Approve Invoice

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

to Pay value chain, receiving a matched invoice from Match PO / GR /
Invoice and forwarding an approved invoice to Pay Supplier.

  Lane "Accounts Payable" — accounts payable officer who routes the

  Lane "Budget Holder / Approver" — approver who reviews and approves

may be contacted if the invoice requires correction.
Pool "Accounts Payable / Invoice System" — IT system that records
invoice status, routes approval tasks, and stores the approved invoice.

Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Accounts Payable / Invoice System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Buying Organisation (white-box, subdivided into lanes top to bottom:
   Accounts Payable, Budget Holder / Approver, Finance / Treasury)
3. Accounts Payable / Invoice System

Accounts Payable lane:
  Message start event "Matched invoice received from Match PO / GR /
  Invoice"

  Invoice System"
  User task "Review matched invoice for completeness"

  - branch "No — invoice incomplete or outside tolerance":
      Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Invoice Discrepancy Before Routing"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
        Send task "Request invoice correction from Supplier"
        Intermediate message catch event "Corrected invoice received"
        User task "Re-check corrected invoice"
        Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolved?"
        - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
        - branch "No": (loop repeats)
      Interrupting timer boundary event "Correction deadline exceeded"
      attached to subprocess → User task "Escalate unresolved invoice
      discrepancy to Finance Controller" → Escalation end event
      "Invoice discrepancy unresolved — escalated"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Invoice complete and
      within tolerance")
  - branch "Yes — invoice acceptable":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Invoice complete and
      within tolerance")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice complete and within tolerance"
  Service task "Submit invoice for approval in Accounts Payable /
  Invoice System"
  Exclusive gateway "Approval tier required?"
  - branch "Budget holder approval sufficient":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approval tier resolved")
  - branch "Finance / Treasury authorisation required":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approval tier resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approval tier resolved"

Budget Holder / Approver lane:
  User task "Review invoice against budget and purchase order"
  Exclusive gateway "Invoice approved by budget holder?"
  - branch "Approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Budget holder decision")
  - branch "Rejected — return to Accounts Payable":
      User task "Record rejection reason and return invoice"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Budget holder decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Budget holder decision"

Finance / Treasury lane:
  Exclusive gateway "Finance / Treasury review required?"
  - branch "Yes — high-value or policy-mandated":
      User task "Perform financial and compliance review of invoice"
      Exclusive gateway "Invoice authorised by Finance / Treasury?"
      - branch "Authorised":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance review
          outcome")
      - branch "Not authorised — return for correction":
          User task "Record non-authorisation and instruct Accounts
          Payable"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance review
          outcome")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Finance review outcome"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance / Treasury
      review resolved")
  - branch "No — budget holder approval sufficient":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance / Treasury
      review resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Finance / Treasury review resolved"
  Service task "Record final approval status in Accounts Payable /
  Invoice System"
  Exclusive gateway "Invoice fully approved?"
  - branch "Yes":
      Send task "Notify Accounts Payable of approval"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Final approval outcome")
  - branch "No — rejected or returned":
      Send task "Notify Accounts Payable of rejection outcome"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Final approval outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Final approval outcome"

Accounts Payable lane (continued):
  Exclusive gateway "Outcome of approval?"
  - branch "Approved — proceed to payment":
      Service task "Mark invoice as approved in Accounts Payable /

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event "Correction deadline exceeded" —
attached to Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Invoice Discrepancy Before
Routing"; fires when the supplier correction window expires; routes to

Controller", then Escalation end event "Invoice discrepancy
unresolved — escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Accounts Payable lane with the
message start event, passing through invoice completeness checking
and the loop subprocess (with its timer boundary escalation path),

passes to the Finance / Treasury lane. The Finance / Treasury lane

"Re-check corrected invoice".
Data Object "Approval Decision Record" — written by User task
"Review invoice against budget and purchase order"; read by Service
task "Record final approval status in Accounts Payable / Invoice
System".

This subprocess takes a three-way matched invoice from V02.06 and
routes it through the appropriate approval tier — budget holder alone
or budget holder plus Finance / Treasury — resolving any remaining
discrepancies with the Supplier before sign-off. Invoices that pass
all approval steps are marked approved and handed to V02.08 Pay
Supplier with a confirmed payment instruction; invoices that cannot
be resolved or are rejected are returned to the Supplier or escalated,
ending this stage abnormally.
```

### V02.08 — Pay Supplier

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.08 Pay Supplier — executes payment to the supplier following
approved invoice, within the Procure to Pay value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the organisation executing the payment process,
  with lanes for Accounts Payable and Finance / Treasury.
Pool "Supplier" — the external party receiving payment and remittance advice.
Pool "Payment Platform" — the external payment intermediary processing the
  payment instruction.
Pool "Bank" — the external financial institution executing the funds transfer.
Pool "Payment Platform / Banking System" — the IT system recording payment
  runs and banking transactions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Platform" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Bank" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Platform / Banking System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Buying Organisation
3. Payment Platform
4. Bank
5. Payment Platform / Banking System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Accounts Payable lane:
  Message start event "Approved invoice received from Approve Invoice"
  User task "Select invoices for payment run"
  Service task "Generate payment run proposal"
  User task "Review and confirm payment run"
  Exclusive gateway "Payment run approved?"
  - branch "No": User task "Adjust payment run"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment run approved?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Payment run approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Payment run approved?"
  Send task "Submit payment instruction to Payment Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received"
  User task "Reconcile payments against open invoices"
  Service task "Mark invoices as paid in Accounts Payable system"
  Send task "Send remittance advice to Supplier"

Finance / Treasury lane:
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Payment Authorised" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Review payment run for treasury sign-off"
    Exclusive gateway "Authorised?"
    - branch "No": User task "Return payment run with comments"
      (loop repeats)
    - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
  Timer boundary event (interrupting) on "Repeat Until Payment Authorised"
    labelled "Authorisation deadline exceeded" — cancels subprocess, routes
    to User task "Escalate to Finance Controller", then Escalation end event
    "Payment authorisation escalated — abnormal end"
  Service task "Record payment accounting entries in Payment Platform /
    Banking System"
  End event "Payment complete — ready for Close Procurement Transaction"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Payment Authorised", labelled "Authorisation deadline exceeded"; fires
  when the treasury authorisation deadline is exceeded; cancels the
  subprocess and routes to User task "Escalate to Finance Controller",
  then Escalation end event "Payment authorisation escalated — abnormal
  end".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Accounts Payable lane with the message
start event, proceeds through invoice selection, payment run generation,
review, and the "Payment run approved?" exclusive gateway; the "No" branch
loops to "Adjust payment run" then rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway;
the "Yes" branch also rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway; flow then
passes to the Finance / Treasury lane for the "Repeat Until Payment
Authorised" expanded subprocess; on successful authorisation, flow returns
to the Accounts Payable lane for submission of the payment instruction,
the intermediate message catch event awaiting payment confirmation,
reconciliation, marking invoices paid, and sending remittance advice;
the Finance / Treasury lane then records accounting entries and reaches
the end event.

Message flows:
  Send task "Submit payment instruction to Payment Platform" →
    Pool "Payment Platform" (payment instruction).
  Pool "Payment Platform" → Intermediate message catch event
    "Payment confirmation received" (payment confirmation).
  Pool "Payment Platform" → Pool "Bank" (funds transfer instruction).
  Pool "Bank" → Pool "Payment Platform" (settlement confirmation).
  Send task "Send remittance advice to Supplier" → Pool "Supplier"
    (remittance advice).
  Service task "Record payment accounting entries in Payment Platform /
    Banking System" → Pool "Payment Platform / Banking System"
    (payment run and accounting entries).
  Pool "Payment Platform / Banking System" → Service task "Generate
    payment run proposal" (open approved invoices and payment terms).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Payment Run Proposal" — written by Service task "Generate
  payment run proposal"; read by User task "Review and confirm payment
  run"; read by User task "Review payment run for treasury sign-off".
Data Object "Payment Instruction" — written by Send task "Submit payment
  instruction to Payment Platform"; read by Pool "Payment Platform".
Data Object "Payment Confirmation" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Payment confirmation received"; read by User task "Reconcile
  payments against open invoices".
Data Object "Remittance Advice" — written by Send task "Send remittance
  advice to Supplier"; read by Pool "Supplier".
Data Object "Accounting Entry" — written by Service task "Record payment
  accounting entries in Payment Platform / Banking System".

V02.08 Pay Supplier takes an approved invoice and executes the end-to-end
payment cycle: selecting invoices for a payment run, obtaining treasury
authorisation, submitting the instruction to the Payment Platform, awaiting
bank settlement confirmation, reconciling payments, and closing open
invoice balances. On normal completion it marks all invoices as paid,
dispatches remittance advice to the Supplier, and posts the accounting
entries, handing a fully settled and recorded payment to V02.10 Close
Procurement Transaction.
```

### V02.09 — Handle Exceptions

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.09 Handle Exceptions — the exception-resolution subprocess within
the Procure to Pay value chain, triggered when a matching, approval, or payment
failure requires cross-functional investigation and resolution before the
transaction can proceed to Close Procurement Transaction.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — the internal organisation resolving the exception,
  with lanes for Accounts Payable, Procurement, and Finance / Treasury.
Pool "Supplier" — the external supplier involved in the disputed transaction.
Pool "Case / Workflow System" — the IT system used to log, track, and route
  exception cases.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case / Workflow System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Buying Organisation
3. Case / Workflow System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Accounts Payable lane:
  Message start event "Exception identified — received from Approve Invoice or
    Match PO / GR / Invoice"
  User task "Log exception case"
  Service task "Record exception in Case / Workflow System"
  User task "Classify exception type"
  Exclusive gateway "Exception type?"
  - branch "Invoice dispute":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type routed")
  - branch "Delivery or quantity discrepancy":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type routed")
  - branch "Pricing or contract mismatch":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type routed")
  - branch "Duplicate or erroneous invoice":
      User task "Reject and request corrected invoice"
      Send task "Send rejection notice to Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected invoice received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type routed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exception type routed"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Investigate discrepancy against purchase order and contract"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Supplier Response Confirmed"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    Send task "Request clarification or credit note from Supplier",
    Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received",
    Exclusive gateway "Response acceptable?"
    - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
    - branch "No": (loop repeats)
  Timer boundary event on "Repeat Until Supplier Response Confirmed" —
    interrupting, label "Supplier response deadline exceeded" — routes to:
    User task "Escalate unresolved exception to category manager"
    Escalation end event "Exception escalated — unresolved supplier response"
  User task "Agree resolution action with Accounts Payable"

Finance / Treasury lane:
  User task "Review financial impact of exception"
  Exclusive gateway "Financial adjustment required?"
  - branch "Yes":
      User task "Raise adjustment journal or credit note entry"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Adjustment assessed")
  - branch "No":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Adjustment assessed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Adjustment assessed"
  User task "Authorise resolution and update case status"
  Service task "Update exception status in Case / Workflow System"
  Exclusive gateway "Exception fully resolved?"
  - branch "Yes":
      End event "Exception resolved — ready for Close Procurement Transaction"
  - branch "No":
      User task "Escalate to finance controller"
      Escalation end event "Exception escalated — unresolved financial
        discrepancy"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Repeat Until Supplier Response Confirmed"
  — label "Supplier response deadline exceeded" — cancels the subprocess and
  routes to User task "Escalate unresolved exception to category manager"
  followed by Escalation end event "Exception escalated — unresolved supplier
  response" in the Procurement lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work enters the Accounts Payable lane at the message start
event, proceeds through logging, classification, and the exception-type gateway,
merging at "Exception type routed"; the duplicate-invoice branch completes its
own rejection and corrected-invoice receipt cycle before merging. Control passes
to the Procurement lane for investigation and supplier clarification via the
expanded subprocess loop; on successful resolution, Procurement hands off to the
Finance / Treasury lane for financial review, the adjustment gateway merges at
"Adjustment assessed", and the final gateway routes either to the normal end
event or the escalation end event.

Message flows:
Accounts Payable lane "Send rejection notice to Supplier" → Supplier (invoice
  rejection notice).
Supplier → Accounts Payable lane "Corrected invoice received" (corrected invoice
  or credit note).
Procurement lane "Request clarification or credit note from Supplier" → Supplier
  (clarification request or credit note request).
Supplier → Procurement lane "Supplier response received" (supplier response,
  credit note, or supporting documentation).
Accounts Payable lane "Record exception in Case / Workflow System" →
  Case / Workflow System (exception case record).
Finance / Treasury lane "Update exception status in Case / Workflow System" →
  Case / Workflow System (updated case status and resolution outcome).
Case / Workflow System → Accounts Payable lane "Log exception case" (case
  reference and routing instructions).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Exception Case Record" — written by "Log exception case"; read by
  "Classify exception type"; read by "Investigate discrepancy against purchase
  order and contract"; read by "Authorise resolution and update case status".
Data Object "Supplier Response" — written by intermediate message catch event
  "Supplier response received"; read by exclusive gateway "Response acceptable?";
  read by "Agree resolution action with Accounts Payable".
Data Object "Corrected Invoice" — written by intermediate message catch event
  "Corrected invoice received"; read by exclusive merge gateway "Exception type
  routed".
Data Object "Adjustment Journal Entry" — written by "Raise adjustment journal or
  credit note entry"; read by "Authorise resolution and update case status".

This subprocess receives exceptions surfaced by Match PO / GR / Invoice or
Approve Invoice and provides a structured, auditable path to resolve them through
cross-functional collaboration across Accounts Payable, Procurement, and Finance
/ Treasury. Supplier discrepancies are challenged directly, financial impacts are
assessed and journalled, and unresolved cases are formally escalated rather than
left pending. When an exception is fully resolved and the case is closed, the
transaction is handed forward to Close Procurement Transaction for final ledger
reconciliation and record closure.
```

### V02.10 — Close Procurement Transaction

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V02.10 Close Procurement Transaction — final subprocess of the
Procure to Pay value chain, reconciling and archiving all procurement
records after payment has been made.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Buying Organisation" — internal teams that close and archive the
procurement transaction.
  Lane "Procurement" — procurement officer who reviews PO completion
  and archives procurement records.
  Lane "Finance / Treasury" — finance controller who reconciles
  accounts and posts final accounting entries.

Pool "ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal" — system that holds
open purchase orders and supplier-facing records.

Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — system that holds accounting
entries and the general ledger.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Buying Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal" — black-box,
System = true, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Buying Organisation
2. ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal
3. ERP / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Buying Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Payment confirmed — received from Pay Supplier"
  User task "Review PO and goods receipt for completeness"
  Service task "Retrieve final PO and GR records from ERP Procurement
    System / Supplier Portal"
  Exclusive gateway "PO fully delivered and receipted?"
  - branch "No — outstanding items remain":
      Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Outstanding Items Until Complete"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Identify and document outstanding items",
        Send task "Notify relevant parties of outstanding items",
        Intermediate message catch event "Resolution response received",
        Exclusive gateway "Items resolved?" — branch "Yes": exits
        subprocess; branch "No": loop repeats.
      Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve Outstanding Items
        Until Complete" labelled "Resolution deadline exceeded" —
        fires, cancels subprocess, routes to task "Escalate
        unresolved items to category manager" then
        Escalation end event "Outstanding items escalated — close
        attempt abandoned"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PO fully delivered and
        receipted")
  - branch "Yes — all items complete":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PO fully delivered and
        receipted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "PO fully delivered and receipted"
  User task "Mark purchase order as closed in ERP Procurement System
    / Supplier Portal"
  Service task "Archive procurement documentation"
  End event "Procurement records closed and archived — hand to
    Finance / Treasury for final reconciliation"

Finance / Treasury lane:
  Message start event "Procurement records closed — received from
    Procurement"
  Service task "Retrieve payment and invoice records from ERP /
    General Ledger System"
  User task "Reconcile invoices, payments, and purchase orders"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation complete and balanced?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found":
      Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Reconciliation Discrepancy Until
        Balanced" (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Investigate and correct reconciliation discrepancy",
        Service task "Update accounting entries in ERP / General
          Ledger System",
        Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy cleared?" — branch "Yes":
        exits subprocess; branch "No": loop repeats.
      Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve Reconciliation
        Discrepancy Until Balanced" labelled "Reconciliation deadline
        exceeded" — fires, cancels subprocess, routes to task
        "Escalate reconciliation failure to finance controller" then
        Escalation end event "Reconciliation escalated — transaction
        cannot be closed"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation complete
        and balanced")
  - branch "Yes — balanced":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation complete
        and balanced")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation complete and balanced"
  Service task "Post final accounting entries to ERP / General
    Ledger System"
  User task "Confirm transaction closure and update procurement
    register"
  End event "Procurement transaction closed — Procure to Pay cycle
    complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve Outstanding Items Until
Complete" — label "Resolution deadline exceeded" — cancels subprocess,
routes to "Escalate unresolved items to category manager", ends with
Escalation end event "Outstanding items escalated — close attempt
abandoned".

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve Reconciliation
Discrepancy Until Balanced" — label "Reconciliation deadline exceeded"
— cancels subprocess, routes to "Escalate reconciliation failure to
finance controller", ends with Escalation end event "Reconciliation
escalated — transaction cannot be closed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Procurement lane, flow passes from the
message start event through PO completeness review and ERP record
retrieval to the exclusive gateway "PO fully delivered and receipted?";
the "No" branch enters the loop subprocess and, if unresolved before
the timer fires, exits to escalation; the "Yes" branch and the resolved
branch of the loop both rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway, then
flow continues to mark the PO closed and archive documentation, ending
with the hand-off end event. In the Finance / Treasury lane, flow
passes from its message start event through record retrieval and
reconciliation to the exclusive gateway "Reconciliation complete and
balanced?"; the "No" branch enters the reconciliation loop subprocess
and, if unresolved before the timer fires, exits to escalation; the
"Yes" branch and the resolved branch of the loop both rejoin at the
exclusive merge gateway, then flow continues to post accounting entries
and confirm closure, ending at the final end event.

Message flows:
Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve final PO and GR records
  from ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal") →
  ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal (open PO and GR data
  requested).
ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal →
  Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve final PO and GR
  records from ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal")
  (final PO and GR records returned).
Buying Organisation (Service task "Mark purchase order as closed in
  ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal") →
  ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal (PO closure instruction).
Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve payment and invoice
  records from ERP / General Ledger System") →
  ERP / General Ledger System (payment and invoice records
  requested).
ERP / General Ledger System →
  Buying Organisation (Service task "Retrieve payment and invoice
  records from ERP / General Ledger System")
  (payment and invoice records returned).
Buying Organisation (Service task "Update accounting entries in ERP /
  General Ledger System") →
  ERP / General Ledger System (corrected accounting entries).
Buying Organisation (Service task "Post final accounting entries to
  ERP / General Ledger System") →
  ERP / General Ledger System (final accounting entries).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Purchase Order Record" — read by "Review PO and goods
  receipt for completeness"; read by "Retrieve final PO and GR
  records from ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal"; written by
  "Mark purchase order as closed in ERP Procurement System /
  Supplier Portal".
Data Object "Goods Receipt Record" — read by "Review PO and goods
  receipt for completeness"; read by "Retrieve final PO and GR
  records from ERP Procurement System / Supplier Portal".
Data Object "Invoice and Payment Record" — read by "Retrieve payment
  and invoice records from ERP / General Ledger System"; read by
  "Reconcile invoices, payments, and purchase orders".
Data Object "Reconciliation Report" — written by "Reconcile invoices,
  payments, and purchase orders"; read by "Post final accounting
  entries to ERP / General Ledger System".
Data Object "Procurement Archive Package" — written by "Archive
  procurement documentation"; read by "Confirm transaction closure
  and update procurement register".

Close Procurement Transaction verifies that every purchase order is
fully receipted and closes it in the ERP, archives all procurement
documentation, then reconciles invoices and payments against the
general ledger and posts the final accounting entries. Successful
completion confirms that the Procure to Pay cycle is fully concluded,
with all records balanced, closed, and available for audit; any
unresolvable discrepancy or outstanding item is escalated before the
cycle can be declared complete.
```

## V03 — Record to Report

**Teams and roles involved.**
Record to Report involves Finance, Financial Accounting, Management Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Payroll Finance, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Internal Audit, External Reporting, and senior executives. Key roles include financial accountant, management accountant, tax accountant, finance controller, CFO, reconciliations analyst, reporting analyst, and auditor.

**External participants.**
This process is usually cycle-driven rather than initiated by a single external participant. Important external participants include Regulators, Tax Authorities, External Auditors, Shareholders, Banks, Owners, and Board Members. They consume or review the financial outputs of the process.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: capture financial transactions, post journals, maintain chart of accounts, reconcile accounts, manage accruals and provisions, close accounting periods, consolidate entities, prepare management reports, prepare statutory reports, submit tax/regulatory returns, and support audit.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ERP general ledger, sub-ledgers, consolidation system, financial close system, tax system, treasury system, payroll system, fixed asset register, reporting/BI platform, document management system, and audit management tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include accounting policy, chart of accounts governance, journal posting procedure, month-end close procedure, reconciliation policy, accruals policy, tax compliance policy, financial delegation policy, audit procedure, and statutory reporting requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
External auditors, regulators, tax authorities, banks, and owners may request financial statements, reconciliations, supporting schedules, tax returns, compliance reports, or audit evidence. The process provides financial statements, management reports, statutory returns, audit responses, covenant reporting, and tax submissions.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process consumes transactions from sales, procurement, payroll, assets, inventory, banking, and other operational systems. It creates journals, reconciliations, close tasks, consolidation entries, tax calculations, reporting packs, audit evidence, and final financial statements.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V03 - Record to Report (R2R)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V03.01. Capture Financial Transactions
V03.02. Post Journals
V03.03. Maintain Chart of Accounts
V03.04. Reconcile Accounts
V03.05. Manage Accruals and Provisions
V03.06. Close Accounting Periods
V03.07. Consolidate Entities
V03.08. Prepare Management Reports
V03.09. Prepare Statutory Reports
V03.10. Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns
V03.11. Support Audit

This is the finance close-and-report end-to-end process: operational
transactions flow into the ledger, are posted, reconciled, accrued,
closed, consolidated and reported, then filed with the tax and
regulatory authorities and supported through the external audit. It is
cycle-driven rather than triggered by a single external party — each
accounting period drives the cycle. The external participants
(Regulators, Tax Authorities, External Auditors, Shareholders / Owners,
Banks and Board Members) are consumers of the financial outputs, and the
source of the transactions is the organisation's own operational
systems.
```

```text
This Context Diagram frames the Financial Reporting Company as a single
system in context: an internal accounting cycle drives the Record to
Report process, the operational systems feed the transactions, and the
tax and regulatory authorities, the external auditor, the bank and the
owners and board consume or review the financial outputs. The six
external entities are exactly the external actors of the Process Context
diagram below, so the two views stay consistent.
```

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN

teams are the lanes of the "Finance Organisation" pool (key role in
brackets), and IT systems are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V03.01** Capture Financial Transactions | — | Accounts Payable / Receivable (sub-ledger accountant), Financial Accounting (financial accountant) | Sub-Ledger / Source Systems |
| **V03.02** Post Journals | — | Financial Accounting (financial accountant), Finance Controller (finance controller) | ERP / General Ledger System |
| **V03.03** Maintain Chart of Accounts | — | Financial Accounting (financial accountant), Finance Controller (finance controller) | ERP / General Ledger System |
| **V03.04** Reconcile Accounts | Bank | Financial Accounting (reconciliations analyst) | Reconciliation System |
| **V03.05** Manage Accruals and Provisions | — | Financial Accounting (financial accountant), Management Accounting (management accountant) | ERP / General Ledger System |
| **V03.06** Close Accounting Periods | — | Financial Accounting (financial accountant), Finance Controller (finance controller) | Financial Close System |
| **V03.07** Consolidate Entities | — | External Reporting (reporting analyst), Finance Controller (finance controller) | Consolidation System |
| **V03.08** Prepare Management Reports | Board Members | Management Accounting (management accountant), Finance Controller (finance controller) | Reporting / BI Platform |
| **V03.09** Prepare Statutory Reports | Regulator, Shareholders / Owners | External Reporting (reporting analyst), Finance Controller (finance controller), CFO (CFO) | Disclosure Management System |
| **V03.10** Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns | Tax Authority, Regulator | Tax (tax accountant), Treasury (treasury accountant) | Tax System |
