**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V03):

- **External actors:** Bank (V03.04); Board Members (V03.08); Regulator (V03.09, V03.10); Shareholders / Owners (V03.09); Tax Authority (V03.10); External Auditor (V03.11).
- **Teams:** Accounts Payable / Receivable (V03.01); Financial Accounting (V03.01, V03.02, V03.03, V03.05, V03.06, V03.11); Finance Controller (V03.02, V03.03, V03.06, V03.07, V03.08, V03.09, V03.11); Management Accounting (V03.05, V03.08); External Reporting (V03.07, V03.09); CFO (V03.09); Tax (V03.10); Treasury (V03.10); Internal Audit (V03.11).
- **IT systems:** Sub-Ledger / Source Systems (V03.01); ERP / General Ledger System (V03.02, V03.03, V03.05); Reconciliation System (V03.04); Financial Close System (V03.06); Consolidation System (V03.07); Reporting / BI Platform (V03.08); Disclosure Management System (V03.09); Tax System (V03.10); Audit Management System (V03.11); Document Management System (V03.11).

**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

A single high-level ArchiMate view of the Record to Report service area.
It shows the **Actors**, **Services**, **Processes**, **Interfaces** and
**Applications** that provide the Financial Reporting Service and the
related assurance and filing services across the eleven V03 processes.
Each Business Process is a drill-down anchor: link it to the matching
V03.nn BPMN diagram and its marker turns green.

```text
ArchiMate: V03 — Record to Report — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: show how the organisation provides the Financial Reporting
Service and the related services (to the internal board / executives and
to the external regulators, auditor, bank and owners) across the eleven
V03 Record to Report processes, and the applications that support them.
Lay it out in three horizontal bands, top to bottom — BUSINESS SERVICES
→ BUSINESS PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS — with the internal Board /
Executives on the far left and the external consumers on the far right.
Read top-to-bottom as service → process → application (ArchiMate service
realisation).

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)
- Board / Executives — the internal party the reporting service is
  provided to (far left, the primary consumer of management reporting).
- Regulator, Tax Authority — external parties that receive statutory and
  tax filings (far right).
- External Auditor — the external party that reviews and gives the audit
  opinion (far right).
- Bank, Shareholders / Owners — external actors that receive statements,
  covenant reporting and financial results (far right).

2. Interfaces
- Business Interface "Regulatory & Audit Portal / Reporting Channel" —
  the channel the external auditor, regulator and tax authority use to
  receive statements, returns and audit evidence, and through which the
  bank and owners receive reporting. The external actors ACCESS this
  interface; the interface SERVES the business services below.
- Application Interfaces (optional, only the few the portal calls):
  "Filing API" on the Tax System, "Disclosure API" on the Disclosure
  Management System.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — the services provided, top
   band, left-to-right in reporting-journey order:
- Transaction & Ledger Service — capture transactions, post journals and
  maintain the chart of accounts.
- Reconciliation & Provisions Service — reconcile accounts and manage
  accruals and provisions.
- Period Close & Consolidation Service — close periods and consolidate
  entities.
- Management Reporting Service — prepare and issue management reports.
- Statutory & Regulatory Reporting Service — prepare statutory reports
  and submit tax and regulatory returns.
- Assurance & Audit Service — support the external audit and sign off.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — the eleven V03 processes,
   middle band in V03.01 → V03.11 order. Each REALISES the business
   service shown and is the link anchor to its BPMN diagram:
- V03.01 Capture Financial Transactions   -> realises Transaction & Ledger Service
- V03.02 Post Journals                     -> realises Transaction & Ledger Service
- V03.03 Maintain Chart of Accounts        -> realises Transaction & Ledger Service
- V03.04 Reconcile Accounts                -> realises Reconciliation & Provisions Service
- V03.05 Manage Accruals and Provisions    -> realises Reconciliation & Provisions Service
- V03.06 Close Accounting Periods          -> realises Period Close & Consolidation Service
- V03.07 Consolidate Entities              -> realises Period Close & Consolidation Service
- V03.08 Prepare Management Reports         -> realises Management Reporting Service
- V03.09 Prepare Statutory Reports          -> realises Statutory & Regulatory Reporting Service
- V03.10 Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns    -> realises Statutory & Regulatory Reporting Service
- V03.11 Support Audit                      -> realises Assurance & Audit Service

5. Applications (Application Component) — the IT systems that support the
   processes, bottom band:
- Sub-Ledger / Source Systems
- ERP / General Ledger System
- Reconciliation System
- Financial Close System
- Consolidation System
- Reporting / BI Platform
- Disclosure Management System
- Tax System
- Audit Management System
- Document Management System

6. Relationships
- External Auditor, Regulator, Tax Authority -accesses-> Regulatory &
  Audit Portal / Reporting Channel.
- Regulatory & Audit Portal / Reporting Channel -serving-> the
  Statutory & Regulatory Reporting and Assurance & Audit services.
- Each Business Process -realisation-> its Business Service (section 4).
- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
  (serving, application -> process):
    V03.01 <- Sub-Ledger / Source Systems;   V03.02 <- ERP / General Ledger System;
    V03.03 <- ERP / General Ledger System;    V03.04 <- Reconciliation System;
    V03.05 <- ERP / General Ledger System;    V03.06 <- Financial Close System;
    V03.07 <- Consolidation System;           V03.08 <- Reporting / BI Platform;
    V03.09 <- Disclosure Management System;    V03.10 <- Tax System;
    V03.11 <- Audit Management System + Document Management System.
- Bank -serving-> V03.04 Reconcile Accounts.
- V03.08 Prepare Management Reports -serving-> Board / Executives.
- V03.09 Prepare Statutory Reports -serving-> Regulator and Shareholders
  / Owners.
- V03.10 Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns -serving-> Tax Authority and
  Regulator.
- V03.11 Support Audit -serving-> External Auditor.

7. Intent
The Financial Reporting Service sits top-centre as the headline service.
The eleven Business Processes form the backbone in V03.01 -> V03.11
order so the reader can trace the record-to-report cycle and drill from
any process straight into its detailed BPMN model. This one ArchiMate
view therefore links to all eleven V03 BPMN process diagrams. The
mapping of process -> actors/teams/applications is the Process <->
```

### V03.01 — Capture Financial Transactions

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.01 Capture Financial Transactions — the opening subprocess of the
Record to Report value chain, in which raw financial transactions from
operational sources are captured and recorded into sub-ledgers ready for
journal posting.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal finance teams that capture and
  validate financial transactions.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - "Accounts Payable / Receivable" (sub-ledger accountant)
  - "Financial Accounting" (financial accountant)
Pool "Sub-Ledger / Source Systems" — the ERP sub-ledgers and operational
  source systems that receive and store transaction data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Sub-Ledger / Source Systems" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Finance Organisation (white-box; contains all process flow)
2. Sub-Ledger / Source Systems (black-box; IT system at the bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Accounts Payable / Receivable lane:
  Message start event "Transaction source data received from operational
    systems"
  User task "Review incoming transaction data"
  Exclusive gateway "Transaction type recognised?"
  - branch "No — unrecognised type": User task "Refer transaction for
    classification guidance"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transaction type recognised")
  - branch "Yes — recognised type": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Transaction type recognised")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Transaction type recognised"
  User task "Code transaction to appropriate account"
  User task "Enter transaction details into sub-ledger"
  Service task "Submit transaction record to Sub-Ledger / Source Systems"
  Intermediate message catch event "Transaction acknowledgement received"
  Exclusive gateway "Transaction accepted by system?"
  - branch "No — rejected": User task "Correct transaction data"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transaction accepted by system")
  - branch "Yes — accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Transaction accepted by system")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Transaction accepted by system"

Financial Accounting lane:
  User task "Review sub-ledger transaction for completeness and accuracy"
  Exclusive gateway "Transaction complete and accurate?"
  - branch "No — incomplete or inaccurate": User task "Return transaction
    to Accounts Payable / Receivable for correction"
    End event "Transaction returned for correction — review restarts"
  - branch "Yes — complete and accurate": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "Transaction complete and accurate")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Transaction complete and accurate"
  User task "Authorise transaction entry"
  User task "Confirm transaction captured in sub-ledger"
  End event "Transaction captured and authorised — ready for Post Journals"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Correct transaction data"
  — label "Correction deadline exceeded" — triggers End event "Transaction
  escalated to financial accountant for manual resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Accounts Payable / Receivable lane with
the message start event, proceeds through transaction review, the
"Transaction type recognised?" gateway (unrecognised branch loops through
the referral task back to the merge; recognised branch passes straight
through), then coding, entry, submission to the system, the acknowledgement
catch event, and the "Transaction accepted by system?" gateway (rejected
branch passes through correction task back to the merge; accepted branch
passes straight through), then control passes to the Financial Accounting
lane for completeness review, the "Transaction complete and accurate?"
gateway (inaccurate branch ends at its own end event; accurate branch
passes to the merge), then authorisation and confirmation, ending at the
subprocess end event.

Message flows:
Sub-Ledger / Source Systems → Accounts Payable / Receivable lane
  (incoming transaction source data — triggers message start event)
Accounts Payable / Receivable lane → Sub-Ledger / Source Systems
  (transaction record submitted for posting — from Service task "Submit
  transaction record to Sub-Ledger / Source Systems")
Sub-Ledger / Source Systems → Accounts Payable / Receivable lane
  (transaction acknowledgement — received by intermediate message catch
  event "Transaction acknowledgement received")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incoming Transaction Data" — written by User task "Review
  incoming transaction data"; read by User task "Code transaction to
  appropriate account".
Data Object "Coded Transaction Record" — written by User task "Code
  transaction to appropriate account"; read by User task "Enter transaction
  details into sub-ledger".
Data Object "Sub-Ledger Entry" — written by User task "Enter transaction
  details into sub-ledger"; read by User task "Review sub-ledger transaction
  for completeness and accuracy".
Data Object "Authorised Transaction Confirmation" — written by User task
  "Authorise transaction entry"; read by User task "Confirm transaction
  captured in sub-ledger".

This subprocess receives raw transaction data generated by operational
activities — purchasing, sales, payroll, and banking — and ensures each
transaction is correctly classified, coded, and entered into the appropriate
sub-ledger with formal authorisation. It hands a complete set of
authorised, system-confirmed sub-ledger entries to the Post Journals
subprocess, providing the verified foundation on which journal entries will
be created and posted to the general ledger.
```

### V03.02 — Post Journals

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.02 Post Journals — second subprocess in the Record to Report
value chain, converting captured financial transactions into approved
general ledger journal entries.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal team that prepares, reviews,
and posts journal entries to the general ledger.
  Lane "Financial Accounting" — financial accountant who prepares and
  submits journals.
  Lane "Finance Controller" — finance controller who reviews and approves
  journals.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — the system that receives, validates,
and records approved journal entries.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Finance Organisation (white-box, two lanes top to bottom:
   Financial Accounting, Finance Controller)
2. ERP / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  Message start event "Captured transaction data received from
  Capture Financial Transactions"
  User task "Prepare journal entry"
  User task "Attach supporting documentation"
  Service task "Submit journal entry for approval"
  Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received"
  Exclusive gateway "Journal approved?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Post journal entry to general ledger"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?")
  - branch "No": User task "Correct and resubmit journal entry"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?"
  Exclusive gateway "Further journals to post?"
  - branch "Yes": (loop repeats)
  - branch "No": (exits subprocess)
  End event "All journals posted — ready for Maintain Chart of Accounts"

Finance Controller lane:
  User task "Review journal entry"
  Exclusive gateway "Entry acceptable?"
  - branch "Approved": Send task "Send approval notification"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?")
  - branch "Rejected": User task "Record rejection reason"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?"

Note: The "Further journals to post?" gateway is modelled as an
expanded subprocess to represent the repeating cycle.

Corrected Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  Message start event "Captured transaction data received from
  Capture Financial Transactions"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Journals Posted"
  (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Prepare journal entry",
    User task "Attach supporting documentation",
    Service task "Submit journal entry for approval",
    Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received",
    Exclusive gateway "Journal approved?"
      - branch "Yes": Service task "Post journal entry to general
        ledger"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?")
      - branch "No": User task "Correct and resubmit journal entry"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Journal approved?"
  End event "All journals posted — ready for Maintain Chart of Accounts"

Finance Controller lane:
  User task "Review journal entry"
  Exclusive gateway "Entry acceptable?"
  - branch "Approved": Send task "Send approval notification"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?")
  - branch "Rejected": User task "Record rejection reason"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Entry acceptable?"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Journals Posted" — label "Period close deadline reached" — triggers
End event "Journal posting halted — escalate to Finance Controller".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Financial Accounting lane the flow moves from
the message start event into the expanded subprocess loop. Inside the
loop, each iteration begins with preparing and documenting the journal,
proceeds to submission, waits for the approval decision, then routes
through the "Journal approved?" exclusive gateway: the approved branch
posts the entry to the general ledger and the rejected branch corrects
and resubmits, both rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway "Journal
approved?" before the next loop iteration. When all journals are posted
the loop exits to the end event. In the Finance Controller lane, the
"Review journal entry" task leads to the "Entry acceptable?" gateway,
whose approved branch sends a notification and whose rejected branch
records the reason, both rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway
"Entry acceptable?" before control returns to Financial Accounting
via a message flow.

Message flows:
  Financial Accounting "Submit journal entry for approval" →
    Finance Controller "Review journal entry" (journal entry package
    with supporting documentation)
  Finance Controller "Send approval notification" →
    Financial Accounting Intermediate message catch event "Approval
    decision received" (approval or rejection decision)
  Finance Controller "Record rejection reason" →
    Financial Accounting Intermediate message catch event "Approval
    decision received" (rejection reason and instruction to correct)
  Financial Accounting "Post journal entry to general ledger" →
    ERP / General Ledger System (approved journal entry for posting)
  ERP / General Ledger System →
    Financial Accounting "Post journal entry to general ledger"
    (posting confirmation and journal reference number)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Journal Entry" — written by "Prepare journal entry",
read by "Attach supporting documentation", read by "Review journal
entry", read by "Post journal entry to general ledger".
Data Object "Supporting Documentation" — written by "Attach supporting
documentation", read by "Review journal entry".
Data Object "Rejection Reason" — written by "Record rejection reason",
read by "Correct and resubmit journal entry".
Data Object "Posting Confirmation" — written by "Post journal entry
to general ledger", read by "Post journal entry to general ledger"
(on receipt of confirmation from ERP).

V03.02 Post Journals takes the captured transaction data produced by
Capture Financial Transactions and converts it into reviewed, approved,
and system-recorded general ledger entries. The financial accountant
prepares each journal and attaches evidence; the finance controller
reviews and either approves or rejects it; approved journals are posted
to the ERP general ledger in a repeating cycle until all period journals
are complete. The subprocess hands a fully posted general ledger to
Maintain Chart of Accounts, ensuring the ledger structure and balances
are aligned before period-end close activities begin.
```

### V03.03 — Maintain Chart of Accounts

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.03 Maintain Chart of Accounts — the subprocess within Record
to Report that governs the creation, amendment, and retirement of account
codes in the chart of accounts, ensuring the general ledger structure
remains current, controlled, and compliant with accounting policy.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal finance function carrying out
chart of accounts governance.
  Lane "Financial Accounting" — financial accountant who initiates and
  prepares chart of accounts change requests.
  Lane "Finance Controller" — finance controller who reviews, approves or
  rejects changes and authorises updates to the live chart of accounts.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — the system of record in which the
chart of accounts is maintained and from which updates are published.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Finance Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Financial Accounting above,
   Finance Controller below)
2. ERP / General Ledger System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  None start event "Chart of accounts change required — continuing from
  periodic close planning or ad-hoc business request"
  User task "Identify requirement for account change"
  User task "Prepare chart of accounts change request"
  User task "Classify change type and assign account attributes"
  Send task "Submit change request for controller review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Controller decision received"
  Exclusive gateway "Change approved?"
  - branch "Rejected — minor clarification needed": User task
    "Revise and resubmit change request"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Change approved?")
  - branch "Rejected — request withdrawn": End event "Change request
    withdrawn — no update made to chart of accounts"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Change approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Change approved?"
  User task "Apply approved change in ERP / General Ledger System"
  User task "Validate account code structure and attributes in system"
  Exclusive gateway "Validation passed?"
  - branch "No — correction required": User task "Correct account
    entry in ERP / General Ledger System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Validation passed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed?"
  User task "Update chart of accounts documentation and register"
  Send task "Notify affected teams of chart of accounts change"

Finance Controller lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Change request received from
  Financial Accounting"
  User task "Review chart of accounts change request"
  User task "Assess compliance with accounting policy and CoA governance"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision on change request?"
  - branch "Approve": Send task "Issue approval to Financial Accounting"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision on change request?")
  - branch "Reject — revise": Send task "Return request with revision
    comments to Financial Accounting"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision on change request?")
  - branch "Reject — withdraw": Send task "Issue rejection and closure
    to Financial Accounting"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision on change request?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision on change request?"
  End event "Chart of accounts updated and documented — ready for
  Post Journals and Close Accounting Periods"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review chart of accounts
change request" — label "Review overdue (3 business days)" — on expiry,
escalates to an End event "Escalation raised — controller review timeout".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Financial Accounting lane with the
identification and preparation of a change request, which is submitted
to the Finance Controller lane for review and a three-way approval
decision (approve, reject-revise, reject-withdraw). An approval loops
back through the merge gateway and passes control back to Financial
Accounting to apply the change in the ERP system, validate it, and
complete documentation. A reject-revise decision returns to Financial
Accounting for revision before resubmission; a reject-withdraw terminates
at its own End event. The Finance Controller lane closes with its own End
event once the decision is issued.

Message flows:
Financial Accounting (Send task "Submit change request for controller
review") → ERP / General Ledger System (change request logged for
audit trail).
Finance Controller (Send task "Issue approval to Financial Accounting")
→ Financial Accounting (Intermediate message catch event "Controller
decision received") (approval notification).
Finance Controller (Send task "Return request with revision comments to
Financial Accounting") → Financial Accounting (Intermediate message catch
event "Controller decision received") (revision comments).
Finance Controller (Send task "Issue rejection and closure to Financial
Accounting") → Financial Accounting (Intermediate message catch event
"Controller decision received") (withdrawal notification).
Financial Accounting (User task "Apply approved change in ERP / General
Ledger System") → ERP / General Ledger System (new or amended account
code payload).
ERP / General Ledger System → Financial Accounting (User task "Validate
account code structure and attributes in system") (validation response).
Financial Accounting (User task "Correct account entry in ERP / General
Ledger System") → ERP / General Ledger System (corrected account entry).
Financial Accounting (Send task "Notify affected teams of chart of
accounts change") → ERP / General Ledger System (change notification
broadcast to downstream users).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Chart of Accounts Change Request" — written by User task
"Prepare chart of accounts change request"; read by User task "Review
chart of accounts change request".
Data Object "Account Attributes Record" — written by User task "Classify
change type and assign account attributes"; read by User task "Apply
approved change in ERP / General Ledger System".
Data Object "Controller Review Decision" — written by User task "Assess
compliance with accounting policy and CoA governance"; read by
Intermediate message catch event "Controller decision received".
Data Object "Chart of Accounts Documentation" — written by User task
"Update chart of accounts documentation and register"; read by Send task
"Notify affected teams of chart of accounts change".

This subprocess governs the full lifecycle of a chart of accounts change,
from initial identification of a need through controller-approved creation
or amendment in the ERP general ledger to documentation and notification.
Its output — a validated, policy-compliant account structure — is the
reference frame that Post Journals (V03.02) depends on for correct coding
and that Close Accounting Periods (V03.06) relies on for a complete and
accurate period-end ledger.
```

### V03.04 — Reconcile Accounts

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.04 Reconcile Accounts — the subprocess within Record to Report
that matches internal account balances against external bank statements,
identifies and resolves discrepancies, and produces a signed-off bank
reconciliation ready for period close.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal finance function that owns and
executes the reconciliation process.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Financial Accounting (reconciliations analyst)
Pool "Bank" — external bank providing statements and responding to
queries.
Pool "Reconciliation System" — IT system used to match transactions,
record differences, and store completed reconciliations.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Bank" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Reconciliation System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Bank
2. Finance Organisation
3. Reconciliation System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  Message start event "Bank statement received from Bank"
  Service task "Import bank statement into Reconciliation System"
  Service task "Extract general ledger balances from Reconciliation System"
  User task "Match transactions against general ledger entries"
  Exclusive gateway "All transactions matched?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "All transactions matched")
    - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Discrepancies Resolved"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Investigate unmatched items"
        User task "Contact Bank to clarify outstanding items"
        Intermediate message catch event "Bank clarification received"
        User task "Post correcting entries or mark item as reconciling"
      (exits subprocess, continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "All transactions matched")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All transactions matched"
  User task "Prepare reconciliation statement"
  User task "Review and approve reconciliation statement"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation approved?"
    - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Reconciliation approved")
    - branch "Rejected — requires correction": User task
      "Rework reconciliation and address reviewer comments"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation approved"
  Service task "Store signed-off reconciliation in Reconciliation System"
  End event "Reconciliation complete — ready for Close Accounting Periods"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Discrepancies Resolved" — label "Escalation deadline exceeded" — triggers
User task "Escalate unresolved discrepancy to Finance Controller" followed
by an End event "Reconciliation escalated — pending Finance Controller
resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Financial Accounting lane when the bank
statement arrives and proceeds linearly through import, extraction, and
matching. The "All transactions matched?" gateway branches to either the
merge directly (Yes) or through the loop subprocess (No), both rejoining
at the exclusive merge gateway "All transactions matched". Flow then moves
through preparation and approval; the "Reconciliation approved?" gateway
branches to either the merge directly (Approved) or through rework
(Rejected), both rejoining at "Reconciliation approved". Flow concludes
with storage and the end event.

Message flows:
Bank → Financial Accounting lane (bank statement)
Financial Accounting lane → Bank (query on outstanding items, sent during
  User task "Contact Bank to clarify outstanding items")
Bank → Financial Accounting lane (clarification response, received at
  Intermediate message catch event "Bank clarification received")
Financial Accounting lane → Reconciliation System (bank statement import,
  at Service task "Import bank statement into Reconciliation System")
Reconciliation System → Financial Accounting lane (general ledger
  balances, at Service task "Extract general ledger balances from
  Reconciliation System")
Financial Accounting lane → Reconciliation System (matched results and
  reconciliation statement, at Service task "Store signed-off
  reconciliation in Reconciliation System")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Bank Statement" — written by Message start event "Bank
  statement received from Bank"; read by Service task "Import bank
  statement into Reconciliation System".
Data Object "General Ledger Extract" — written by Service task "Extract
  general ledger balances from Reconciliation System"; read by User task
  "Match transactions against general ledger entries".
Data Object "Unmatched Items List" — written by User task "Match
  transactions against general ledger entries"; read by User task
  "Investigate unmatched items".
Data Object "Reconciliation Statement" — written by User task "Prepare
  reconciliation statement"; read by User task "Review and approve
  reconciliation statement"; read by Service task "Store signed-off
  reconciliation in Reconciliation System".

V03.04 Reconcile Accounts matches the organisation's internal general
ledger balances against externally supplied bank statements, investigates
and resolves any unmatched items through a structured loop that can
escalate to the Finance Controller if unresolved within the deadline, and
produces a reviewed and approved reconciliation statement. The signed-off
statement is stored in the Reconciliation System and handed to Close
Accounting Periods as evidence that account balances are substantiated
before the period is locked.
```

### V03.05 — Manage Accruals and Provisions

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.05 Manage Accruals and Provisions — subprocess within the
Record to Report value chain, sitting between Reconcile Accounts and
Close Accounting Periods.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal finance teams carrying out
accruals and provisions management.
  Lane "Financial Accounting" — financial accountant who identifies,
  prepares, and posts accruals and provisions entries.
  Lane "Management Accounting" — management accountant who reviews
  estimates, challenges assumptions, and approves accrual values.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — system of record that receives
accrual and provision journal entries and stores posted balances.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Finance Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Financial Accounting
   above, Management Accounting below)
2. ERP / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  Timer start event "Period-end accruals cycle triggered"
  User task "Identify accruals and provisions required"
  User task "Gather supporting data and estimates"
  User task "Prepare accrual and provision schedules"
  Send task "Submit schedules for management review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Review outcome received"
  Exclusive gateway "Schedules approved?"
    - branch "No — revisions required": User task "Revise accrual
      and provision schedules"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Schedules approved")
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Schedules approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Schedules approved"
  User task "Prepare accrual journal entries"
  Service task "Post accrual and provision journals to ERP"
  User task "Confirm postings and update accruals register"
  Exclusive gateway "Reversal required in next period?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Schedule reversal entries in ERP"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reversal check")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Reversal check")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reversal check"
  End event "Accruals and provisions posted — ready for Close
  Accounting Periods"

Management Accounting lane:
  User task "Review accrual and provision schedules"
  User task "Validate estimates against business activity"
  Exclusive gateway "Estimates acceptable?"
    - branch "Yes — approve": Send task "Return approval to
      Financial Accounting"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Estimates acceptable")
    - branch "No — reject with comments": Send task "Return
      schedules with revision comments"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Estimates acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Estimates acceptable"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Prepare accrual and
provision schedules" — label "Schedule preparation deadline exceeded"
— triggers End event "Escalate overdue accruals to Finance Controller".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Financial Accounting lane with the
timer start, moves through identification and preparation tasks, then
crosses to the Management Accounting lane for review. The approval
gateway in Management Accounting sends either an approval or a
rejection back to Financial Accounting; the rejection branch loops
through "Revise accrual and provision schedules" before returning to
the exclusive merge gateway "Schedules approved". Once approved,
Financial Accounting prepares and posts journal entries, confirms
postings, checks whether reversals are needed, and reaches the end
event.

Message flows:
  Financial Accounting "Submit schedules for management review" →
  Management Accounting "Review accrual and provision schedules"
  (accrual and provision schedules)
  Management Accounting "Return approval to Financial Accounting" →
  Financial Accounting Intermediate message catch event "Review
  outcome received" (approval confirmation)
  Management Accounting "Return schedules with revision comments" →
  Financial Accounting Intermediate message catch event "Review
  outcome received" (revision comments)
  Financial Accounting "Post accrual and provision journals to ERP" →
  ERP / General Ledger System (accrual and provision journal entries)
  ERP / General Ledger System → Financial Accounting "Confirm
  postings and update accruals register" (posting confirmation and
  balance update)
  Financial Accounting "Schedule reversal entries in ERP" →
  ERP / General Ledger System (scheduled reversal journal entries)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Accrual and Provision Schedules" — written by "Prepare
accrual and provision schedules"; read by "Review accrual and
provision schedules"; updated by "Revise accrual and provision
schedules".
Data Object "Supporting Data and Estimates" — written by "Gather
supporting data and estimates"; read by "Prepare accrual and
provision schedules".
Data Object "Accrual Journal Entries" — written by "Prepare accrual
journal entries"; read by "Post accrual and provision journals to ERP".
Data Object "Accruals Register" — read by "Identify accruals and
provisions required"; written by "Confirm postings and update accruals
register".
Data Object "Reversal Schedule" — written by "Schedule reversal
entries in ERP"; read by ERP / General Ledger System at the start of
the next period.

This subprocess collects all period-end accruals and provisions,
secures management accounting approval of the underlying estimates,
and posts the agreed journal entries to the ERP general ledger. Where
entries must be unwound in the following period, reversal instructions
are lodged in the system before the period is sealed. The confirmed,
posted accrual and provision balances are handed to Close Accounting
Periods, where they become part of the complete trial balance used to
seal the period.
```

### V03.06 — Close Accounting Periods

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.06 Close Accounting Periods — executes the month-end close
sequence within the Record to Report value chain, locking the accounting
period once all tasks are verified complete.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal team executing the period-close
process, with lanes for Financial Accounting and Finance Controller.
Pool "Financial Close System" — the IT system managing close task
checklists, period status, and lock controls.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Financial Close System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Finance Organisation (white-box, with lanes)
2. Financial Close System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Financial Accounting lane:
  Timer start event "Period-end date reached"
  User task "Initiate close checklist"
  Service task "Load open close tasks from Financial Close System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Tasks Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Work through close task",
    User task "Mark task complete in Financial Close System",
    Service task "Retrieve updated task status from Financial Close
    System"
  Exclusive gateway "All close tasks complete?"
  - branch "No": User task "Escalate outstanding tasks to Finance
    Controller" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "All close tasks complete?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "All close tasks complete?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All close tasks complete?"
  User task "Run trial balance"
  Service task "Retrieve trial balance from Financial Close System"
  User task "Review trial balance for errors or omissions"
  Exclusive gateway "Trial balance acceptable?"
  - branch "No": User task "Investigate and correct trial balance
    errors" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Trial balance acceptable?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Trial balance acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Trial balance acceptable?"
  Send task "Submit period-close pack to Finance Controller for sign-off"

Finance Controller lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Period-close pack received"
  User task "Review period-close pack"
  Exclusive gateway "Close pack approved?"
  - branch "No": Send task "Return pack with issues to Financial
    Accounting" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Close pack approved?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Close pack approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Close pack approved?"
  User task "Approve period close"
  Service task "Instruct Financial Close System to lock period"
  Intermediate message catch event "Period lock confirmed"
  End event "Period closed — ready for Consolidate Entities"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Tasks Complete" — label "Close deadline exceeded" — triggers User
task "Escalate unresolved tasks to Finance Controller for forced close
decision", then flow rejoins at exclusive gateway "All close tasks
complete?".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Financial Accounting lane with the
timer start event, proceeds through checklist loading, the standard-loop
subprocess, the task-completion gateway and its merge, then through trial
balance steps and the acceptability gateway and its merge, before the
send task hands the pack to the Finance Controller lane; the Finance
Controller lane flows through review, the approval gateway and its merge,
period approval, and the system lock instruction, ending at the end event.
The "No" branch of "All close tasks complete?" routes to escalation before
rejoining the merge gateway. The "No" branch of "Trial balance
acceptable?" routes to error correction before rejoining its merge
gateway. The "No" branch of "Close pack approved?" returns the pack to
Financial Accounting before rejoining its merge gateway.

Message flows:
Financial Accounting → Financial Close System (load close task list
request)
Financial Close System → Financial Accounting (close task list and
current status)
Financial Accounting → Financial Close System (task completion updates)
Financial Close System → Financial Accounting (updated task status)
Financial Accounting → Financial Close System (trial balance run request)
Financial Close System → Financial Accounting (trial balance data)
Financial Accounting → Finance Controller (period-close pack)
Finance Controller → Financial Close System (period lock instruction)
Financial Close System → Finance Controller (period lock confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Close Checklist" — written by User task "Initiate close
checklist"; read by User task "Work through close task".
Data Object "Task Status Record" — written by User task "Mark task
complete in Financial Close System"; read by Exclusive gateway
"All close tasks complete?".
Data Object "Trial Balance" — written by Service task "Retrieve trial
balance from Financial Close System"; read by User task "Review trial
balance for errors or omissions".
Data Object "Period-Close Pack" — written by User task "Run trial
balance"; read by User task "Review period-close pack".
Data Object "Period Lock Confirmation" — written by Service task
"Instruct Financial Close System to lock period"; read by Intermediate
message catch event "Period lock confirmed".

This subprocess enforces the structured close of an accounting period by
driving all checklist tasks to completion, validating the trial balance,
and obtaining Finance Controller sign-off before instructing the Financial
Close System to lock the period. Once the period lock is confirmed, a
clean, closed period is handed forward to the Consolidate Entities
subprocess, where inter-company eliminations and group-level aggregation
can proceed on a stable ledger.
```

```text
Sequence flows: flow begins in the External Reporting lane with the start

eliminates intercompany transactions and balances, applies currency
translation adjustments, and assembles a reviewed and signed-off
consolidated reporting pack. The approved consolidated group accounts are
then handed to Prepare Management Reports and Prepare Statutory Reports,
where they form the foundation for both internal performance reporting and
external statutory disclosure.
```

```text
External Reporting → Disclosure Management System (finalised statutory
  report submitted for archiving)
Disclosure Management System → External Reporting (finalisation
  confirmation)
External Reporting → Regulator (signed statutory report lodged)
Regulator → External Reporting (filing acknowledgement)
External Reporting → Shareholders / Owners (statutory financial
  statements distributed)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Statutory Reporting Pack" — written by User task "Compile
  statutory reporting pack"; read by User task "Map financial statements
  to statutory disclosure requirements".
Data Object "Draft Statutory Report" — written by Service task "Load
  draft statutory pack into Disclosure Management System"; read by
  User task "Perform disclosure checklist review".
Data Object "Disclosure Checklist" — written by User task "Perform
  disclosure checklist review"; read by Exclusive gateway "Disclosure
  checklist passed?".
Data Object "Notes to Financial Statements" — written by User task
  "Prepare notes to financial statements"; read by User task "Review
  statutory financial statements".
Data Object "Review Comments" — written by User task "Review statutory
  financial statements"; read by User task "Revise statutory report per
  Finance Controller comments".
Data Object "Signed Statutory Financial Statements" — written by User
  task "Review and sign statutory financial statements"; read by Service
  task "Finalise statutory report in Disclosure Management System".

This subprocess takes the consolidated financial data produced by
Consolidate Entities and transforms it into signed, disclosure-compliant
statutory financial statements. It moves the output through external
reporting compilation, Finance Controller review, and CFO sign-off
before lodging the finalised report with the Regulator and distributing
it to Shareholders and Owners. The filed and acknowledged report hands
directly to Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns, which will use the same
approved financial base for tax and regulatory compliance filings.
```

### V03.10 — Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.10 Submit Tax / Regulatory Returns — the subprocess in which
the Tax and Treasury teams calculate, review, and file tax and regulatory
returns with the Tax Authority and Regulator, drawing on the Tax System
to prepare submissions and capture confirmations.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal teams that prepare and submit
tax and regulatory returns.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Tax lane (tax accountant)
  - Treasury lane (treasury accountant)

Pool "Tax Authority" — external body that receives and acknowledges tax
returns.
Pool "Regulator" — external body that receives and acknowledges
regulatory returns.
Pool "Tax System" — IT system used to calculate tax, prepare return
packages, and record submissions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax Authority" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Tax System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Tax Authority
2. Regulator
3. Finance Organisation
4. Tax System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Tax lane:
  Message start event "Period close confirmed — ready for Submit Tax /
    Regulatory Returns"
  User task "Identify filing obligations and deadlines"
  Service task "Extract financial data for tax calculation"
  User task "Calculate current and deferred tax"
  Service task "Send financial data to Tax System for return preparation"
  Intermediate message catch event "Prepared tax return received from
    Tax System"
  User task "Review and validate tax return"
  Exclusive gateway "Tax return approved?"
    - branch "corrections required": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Tax Return Approved" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify and correct tax return errors",
      Service task "Send corrected data to Tax System",
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised tax return received from
        Tax System",
      User task "Re-review revised tax return"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Tax
      return approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Tax return approved"
  User task "Obtain authorisation to lodge tax return"
  Send task "Submit tax return to Tax Authority"
  Intermediate message catch event "Tax return acknowledgement received
    from Tax Authority"
  User task "Record tax return submission and acknowledgement"
  Exclusive gateway "Regulatory return required?"
    - branch "yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory
      return required")
    - branch "no": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory
      return required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory return required"

Treasury lane:
  User task "Identify regulatory filing obligations"
  User task "Prepare regulatory return package"
  User task "Review and validate regulatory return"
  Exclusive gateway "Regulatory return approved?"
    - branch "corrections required": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Regulatory Return Approved" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify and correct regulatory return errors",
      User task "Re-review corrected regulatory return"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Regulatory return approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Regulatory return approved"
  User task "Obtain authorisation to lodge regulatory return"
  Send task "Submit regulatory return to Regulator"
  Intermediate message catch event "Regulatory return acknowledgement
    received from Regulator"
  User task "Record regulatory return submission and acknowledgement"
  User task "Update tax and regulatory obligations register"
  End event "All returns filed — record to report cycle complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Obtain authorisation to
lodge tax return" — labelled "Authorisation deadline exceeded" — flows
to End event "Tax return filing escalated — deadline missed".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Obtain authorisation to
lodge regulatory return" — labelled "Authorisation deadline exceeded" —
flows to End event "Regulatory return filing escalated — deadline
missed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Tax lane with identification of
obligations, moves through calculation, Tax System preparation, review,
and the correction loop if needed, then through authorisation and
submission to the Tax Authority, before passing control to the Treasury
lane at the "Regulatory return required" merge gateway; Treasury
prepares, reviews (with its own correction loop if needed), authorises,
submits to the Regulator, and closes the process at the final end event.
Each correction loop rejoins its respective merge gateway before
proceeding to authorisation.

Message flows:
Tax System → Tax lane (prepared tax return / revised tax return)
Tax lane → Tax System (financial data for return preparation / corrected
  data for return preparation)
Tax lane → Tax Authority (tax return submission)
Tax Authority → Tax lane (tax return acknowledgement)
Treasury lane → Regulator (regulatory return submission)
Regulator → Treasury lane (regulatory return acknowledgement)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Filing Obligations Schedule" — written by User task
"Identify filing obligations and deadlines"; read by User task "Obtain
authorisation to lodge tax return".

Data Object "Tax Return Package" — written by Intermediate message catch
event "Prepared tax return received from Tax System"; read by User task
"Review and validate tax return".

Data Object "Authorised Tax Return" — written by User task "Obtain
authorisation to lodge tax return"; read by Send task "Submit tax return
to Tax Authority".

Data Object "Tax Submission Record" — written by User task "Record tax
return submission and acknowledgement"; read by User task "Update tax
and regulatory obligations register".

Data Object "Regulatory Return Package" — written by User task "Prepare
regulatory return package"; read by User task "Review and validate
regulatory return".

Data Object "Authorised Regulatory Return" — written by User task
"Obtain authorisation to lodge regulatory return"; read by Send task
"Submit regulatory return to Regulator".

Data Object "Regulatory Submission Record" — written by User task
"Record regulatory return submission and acknowledgement"; read by User
task "Update tax and regulatory obligations register".

This subprocess takes the closed-period financial data produced by
Close Accounting Periods and translates it into filed tax returns and
regulatory submissions. The Tax team calculates and lodges the tax
return with the Tax Authority, while the Treasury team prepares and
submits the regulatory return to the Regulator; both flows include
review, correction loops, and formal authorisation before submission.
Acknowledgements from both external bodies are captured, the obligations
register is updated, and the Record to Report cycle concludes — with
fully evidenced submissions available to support the Support Audit
subprocess if required.
```

### V03.11 — Support Audit

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V03.11 Support Audit — the final subprocess of Record to Report,
in which the Finance Organisation responds to external audit requests,
provides evidence and explanations, and resolves findings to close the
audit.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Finance Organisation" — the internal teams that support the audit
  Lane "Internal Audit" — auditor coordinating the audit support process
  Lane "Financial Accounting" — financial accountant supplying evidence
  Lane "Finance Controller" — finance controller reviewing and approving
    responses
Pool "External Auditor" — external audit firm requesting evidence and
  issuing findings
Pool "Audit Management System" — IT system managing audit requests,
  findings and status
Pool "Document Management System" — IT system storing and retrieving
  audit evidence documents

2. Pool properties

Pool "Finance Organisation" — white-box, single instance
Pool "External Auditor" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Auditor
2. Finance Organisation
3. Audit Management System
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Finance Organisation)

Internal Audit lane:
  Message start event "Audit engagement notification received from
    External Auditor"
  User task "Register audit engagement and assign audit support team"
  Service task "Log audit engagement in Audit Management System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Audit request list received from
    External Auditor"
  User task "Triage and assign audit requests to Financial Accounting"

Financial Accounting lane:
  User task "Retrieve supporting documents from Document Management
    System"
  User task "Compile evidence package for audit request"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence complete and accurate?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
    complete and accurate")
  - branch "No":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Package Complete"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify gaps or errors in evidence",
      User task "Obtain additional supporting documents from Document
        Management System",
      User task "Update evidence package"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence complete and
      accurate")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence complete and accurate"
  Service task "Upload evidence package to Document Management System"
  Send task "Submit evidence package to Internal Audit for review"

Internal Audit lane (continued):
  User task "Review evidence package for completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Package approved?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Package
    approved")
  - branch "No, rework required":
    User task "Return evidence package to Financial Accounting with
      review notes"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Package approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Package approved"
  Send task "Transmit evidence package to External Auditor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Audit findings or queries received
    from External Auditor"
  User task "Log findings and queries in Audit Management System"
  User task "Distribute findings to Financial Accounting and Finance
    Controller"

Financial Accounting lane (continued):
  User task "Prepare draft responses to audit findings"
  Send task "Submit draft responses to Finance Controller for approval"

Finance Controller lane:
  User task "Review draft responses to audit findings"
  Exclusive gateway "Responses approved?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Responses
    approved")
  - branch "No, revisions required":
    User task "Return draft responses to Financial Accounting with
      comments"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Responses approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Responses approved"
  User task "Approve final audit responses"
  Send task "Submit approved responses to Internal Audit"

Internal Audit lane (continued):
  Service task "Record approved responses in Audit Management System"
  Send task "Transmit final responses to External Auditor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Audit clearance or outstanding items
    received from External Auditor"
  Exclusive gateway "All findings cleared?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All findings
    cleared")
  - branch "No, items remain open":
    User task "Escalate unresolved findings to Finance Controller"
    User task "Coordinate resolution of outstanding items"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All findings cleared")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All findings cleared"
  User task "Confirm audit completion and archive audit file in Document
    Management System"
  End event "Audit support concluded — audit file archived and findings
    resolved"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Package Complete" — label "Evidence deadline exceeded" —
  flows to End event "Audit support escalated — evidence deadline missed"
  in the Financial Accounting lane.
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Coordinate resolution of
  outstanding items" — label "Resolution deadline exceeded" — flows to
  End event "Audit support escalated — outstanding items unresolved" in
  the Internal Audit lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Internal Audit lane with the message
start event, passes to Financial Accounting for evidence gathering and
compilation, returns to Internal Audit for review, then to Financial
Accounting for response drafting, then to Finance Controller for
approval, and back to Internal Audit for final transmission and closure.
The "Evidence complete and accurate?" gateway branches to an expanded
subprocess for rework or directly to the merge; the "Package approved?"
gateway loops back through Internal Audit before merging; the "Responses
approved?" gateway loops back through Financial Accounting before
merging; the "All findings cleared?" gateway escalates to resolution
steps or merges directly to archive and close.

Message flows:
External Auditor → Internal Audit lane (audit engagement notification)
External Auditor → Internal Audit lane (audit request list)
Internal Audit lane → External Auditor (evidence package transmitted)
External Auditor → Internal Audit lane (audit findings and queries)
Internal Audit lane → External Auditor (approved responses)
External Auditor → Internal Audit lane (audit clearance or outstanding
  items)
Internal Audit lane → Audit Management System (log audit engagement)
Internal Audit lane → Audit Management System (log findings and queries)
Internal Audit lane → Audit Management System (record approved
  responses)
Financial Accounting lane → Document Management System (upload evidence
  package)
Financial Accounting lane → Document Management System (retrieve
  supporting documents)
Internal Audit lane → Document Management System (archive audit file)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Audit Engagement Record" — written by User task "Register
  audit engagement and assign audit support team"; read by User task
  "Triage and assign audit requests to Financial Accounting"
Data Object "Audit Request List" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Audit request list received from External Auditor"; read by
  User task "Triage and assign audit requests to Financial Accounting"
Data Object "Evidence Package" — written by User task "Compile evidence
  package for audit request"; read by User task "Review evidence package
  for completeness"; updated by User task "Update evidence package"
Data Object "Audit Findings and Queries" — written by User task "Log
  findings and queries in Audit Management System"; read by User task
  "Prepare draft responses to audit findings"
Data Object "Draft Audit Responses" — written by User task "Prepare
  draft responses to audit findings"; read by User task "Review draft
  responses to audit findings"
Data Object "Approved Audit Responses" — written by User task "Approve
  final audit responses"; read by Service task "Record approved
  responses in Audit Management System"

V03.11 Support Audit receives an external audit engagement, coordinates
the retrieval and compilation of evidence across Financial Accounting,
routes packages and responses through Internal Audit and Finance
Controller review, and transmits approved materials to the External
Auditor until all findings are cleared. It closes with the audit file
archived in the Document Management System and all findings resolved,
completing the Record to Report value chain.
```

## V04 — Hire to Retire

**Teams and roles involved.**
Hire to Retire involves Human Resources, Recruitment, Hiring Managers, Payroll, IT, Facilities, Learning and Development, Legal, Finance, and sometimes Security or Compliance. Key roles include recruiter, HR business partner, hiring manager, payroll officer, onboarding coordinator, training manager, employee relations adviser, IT provisioning officer, and people manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participant at the start is the Applicant or Candidate. Once hired, the main participant becomes the Employee. Other external participants may include recruitment agencies, referees, background check providers, training providers, benefits providers, and superannuation/pension funds.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: workforce planning, create vacancy, attract candidates, assess and interview candidates, make offer, onboard employee, provision access/equipment, manage payroll and benefits, manage performance, develop employee, manage changes, handle leave/absence, and offboard/retire employee.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include HRIS/HCM, applicant tracking system, payroll system, learning management system, identity and access management system, workforce management system, performance management system, employee self-service portal, document management, and case management system.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include recruitment policy, equal opportunity policy, background check procedure, employment contract policy, onboarding procedure, remuneration policy, leave policy, performance management procedure, workplace conduct policy, health and safety policy, disciplinary procedure, and termination/offboarding procedure.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Applicants provide resumes, applications, interview availability, identity documents, references, and employment history. The process provides job advertisements, interview invitations, assessment instructions, offer letters, contracts, onboarding instructions, employment communications, payslips, performance feedback, and exit documentation.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates and updates candidate records, employee master data, contracts, payroll details, tax information, benefits records, leave balances, training records, performance reviews, access requests, equipment allocations, and termination records. Systems provide vacancy status, candidate status, employee lifecycle status, payroll calculations, compliance alerts, and workforce reporting.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V04 - Hire to Retire (H2R)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V04.01. Workforce Planning
V04.02. Create Vacancy
V04.03. Attract Candidates
V04.04. Assess and Interview Candidates
V04.05. Make Offer
V04.06. Onboard Employee
V04.07. Provision Access / Equipment
V04.08. Manage Payroll and Benefits
V04.09. Manage Performance
V04.10. Develop Employee
V04.11. Manage Changes
V04.12. Handle Leave / Absence
V04.13. Offboard / Retire Employee

This is the people, or workforce, end-to-end process: the employee
lifecycle flows from workforce planning through recruitment, selection,
offer and onboarding, into ongoing pay, performance, development and
change, and finally to offboarding and retirement. The main external
participant at the start is the Applicant / Candidate, who becomes the
Employee once hired; the process is triggered by an internal workforce
need (a new or vacant role identified in workforce planning), and the
external interaction begins when the vacancy is advertised and candidates
apply.
```

**Context diagram prompt.**

```text
Context Diagram: V04 — Hire to Retire (H2R).

1. Central system (process-system)
A single central process/system ellipse named "Employer Company"
representing the whole organisation that runs the Hire to Retire process. It
is the system in context: everything inside it — human resources,
recruitment, hiring and people managers, payroll, IT, facilities, learning
and development, legal and finance, together with the supporting IT systems
(HRIS / HCM, applicant tracking, payroll, learning, identity and access,
workforce, and performance management) — is treated as one black box.

2. External entities (external-entity)
The parties OUTSIDE the company that exchange information with it, one
rectangle each:
- Applicant / Candidate
- Employee
- Recruitment Agency
- Referee
- Background Check Provider
- Training Provider
- Benefits Provider
- Superannuation / Pension Fund

3. Layout
"Employer Company" sits in the centre. The Applicant / Candidate sits to the
LEFT (the labour-market party who responds to job adverts and applies), with
the Recruitment Agency and Referee also to the LEFT (candidate sourcing and
vetting). The Employee sits to the RIGHT (the ongoing employment
relationship once hired). Background Check Provider, Training Provider,
Benefits Provider and Superannuation / Pension Fund sit to the RIGHT (the
service providers in the employment relationship). The workforce need
originates INSIDE the company (an internal need), so no external demand
actor drives it. Every external entity connects directly to the central
system with labelled information flows; entities never connect to one
another.

4. Information flows (each a labelled connector between an external entity and
   the central system; show both directions where information flows both ways)
- Employer Company → Applicant / Candidate: job advertisements, interview
  invitations, assessment instructions, offer letters, contracts, onboarding
  instructions.
- Applicant / Candidate → Employer Company: resumes, applications, interview
  availability, identity documents, references, employment history.
- Employer Company → Employee: employment communications, payslips,
  performance feedback, exit documentation.
- Employee → Employer Company: personal / bank / tax details, leave and
  absence requests, timesheets, acknowledgements.
- Employer Company → Recruitment Agency: vacancy briefs and candidate
  requirements.
- Recruitment Agency → Employer Company: sourced candidates and shortlists.
- Employer Company → Referee: reference requests.
- Referee → Employer Company: reference responses.
- Employer Company → Background Check Provider: check requests (identity,
  right-to-work, criminal record, credentials).
- Background Check Provider → Employer Company: check results and clearance.
- Employer Company → Training Provider: course bookings and enrolments.
- Training Provider → Employer Company: course completions and certifications.
- Employer Company → Benefits Provider: benefit enrolments and elections.
- Benefits Provider → Employer Company: benefit confirmations and statements.
- Employer Company → Superannuation / Pension Fund: contributions and member
  registrations.
- Superannuation / Pension Fund → Employer Company: membership confirmations
  and statements.

This Context Diagram frames the Employer Company as a single system in
context: an internal workforce need drives the Hire to Retire process, the
Applicant / Candidate applies and becomes the Employee once hired, and the
recruitment, background, training, benefit and superannuation providers
support recruitment and the ongoing employment relationship. The eight
external entities are exactly the external actors of the Process Context
diagram below, so the two views stay consistent.
```
