```text
3. Performance Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Employing Organisation)

Hiring Manager / People Manager lane:
  Message start event "Performance cycle initiated — employee active
    following Onboard Employee"
  User task "Set performance objectives with employee"
  Service task "Record objectives in Performance Management System"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Review period elapsed"
  User task "Conduct performance review meeting with employee"
  Service task "Record review outcome in Performance Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Review outcome?"
  - branch "Satisfactory or above": User task "Provide positive
    feedback and agree next-cycle objectives"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Review outcome resolved")
  - branch "Performance concern identified": User task "Document
    performance concern and notify HR"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Review outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Review outcome resolved"
  Exclusive gateway "Further action required?"
  - branch "No further action": End event "Performance cycle
    complete — record available for Develop Employee"
  - branch "Formal performance management required":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Action determination resolved")

Human Resources lane:
  Exclusive merge gateway "Action determination resolved"
  User task "Open formal performance improvement case"
  Service task "Log formal case in Performance Management System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Performance Improvement Plan
    Concluded" (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Review PIP progress with people manager",
    User task "Hold formal PIP meeting with employee",
    Service task "Update PIP progress in Performance Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "PIP outcome?"
  - branch "Performance improved": User task "Close formal case and
    record improvement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PIP outcome resolved")
  - branch "Performance not improved": User task "Escalate to
    disciplinary or exit procedure"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "PIP outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "PIP outcome resolved"
  End event "Formal performance case closed — outcome recorded in
    Performance Management System"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Performance Improvement Plan Concluded" — label "PIP deadline
exceeded" — triggers User task "Escalate overdue PIP to HR leadership"
in the Human Resources lane, leading to End event "PIP escalated —
awaiting further instruction".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Hiring Manager / People Manager lane
with objective-setting and progresses through review and outcome
assessment. The "Satisfactory or above" and "Performance concern
identified" branches of the "Review outcome?" gateway both rejoin at
the exclusive merge gateway "Review outcome resolved", then proceed to
the "Further action required?" gateway. The "No further action" branch
ends in the first end event. The "Formal performance management
required" branch crosses to the Human Resources lane at the exclusive
merge gateway "Action determination resolved", continuing through case
opening, the PIP subprocess, and concluding at the "PIP outcome
resolved" merge gateway before the second end event.

Message flows:
Employee → Hiring Manager / People Manager lane (employee
  self-assessment and availability for review meeting)
Hiring Manager / People Manager lane → Employee (performance
  objectives and review feedback)
Human Resources lane → Employee (formal performance improvement plan
  documentation and meeting notices)
Employee → Human Resources lane (acknowledgement of PIP and
  progress updates)
Service task "Record objectives in Performance Management System" →
  Performance Management System (objectives data)
Performance Management System → Service task "Record objectives in
  Performance Management System" (confirmation of record created)
Service task "Record review outcome in Performance Management System" →
  Performance Management System (review outcome data)
Performance Management System → Service task "Record review outcome
  in Performance Management System" (compliance alerts and review
  status)
Service task "Log formal case in Performance Management System" →
  Performance Management System (formal case record)
Service task "Update PIP progress in Performance Management System" →
  Performance Management System (PIP progress update)
Performance Management System → Service task "Update PIP progress in
  Performance Management System" (current PIP status and alerts)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Performance Objectives" — written by User task "Set
  performance objectives with employee"; read by User task "Conduct
  performance review meeting with employee".
Data Object "Performance Review Record" — written by Service task
  "Record review outcome in Performance Management System"; read by
  User task "Review PIP progress with people manager".
Data Object "Performance Improvement Plan" — written by User task
  "Open formal performance improvement case"; read by User task "Hold
  formal PIP meeting with employee" and User task "Review PIP progress
  with people manager".
Data Object "Formal Case Outcome" — written by User task "Close
  formal case and record improvement" or User task "Escalate to
  disciplinary or exit procedure"; read by Service task "Update PIP
  progress in Performance Management System".

This subprocess manages the full employee performance cycle from
objective-setting through periodic review to formal improvement action
where needed. Satisfactory outcomes are recorded and feed into the
Develop Employee subprocess, which uses the review record to target
learning and development activities. Formal cases that reach resolution
leave a closed case record in the Performance Management System for
audit and compliance purposes.
```

### V04.10 — Develop Employee

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V04.10 Develop Employee — the subprocess in the Hire to Retire
value chain that identifies employee learning needs, enrols the employee
in training, tracks completion, and records development outcomes.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Employing Organisation" — the organisation running the development
process, containing Learning & Development and its training manager.
Pool "Employee" — the employee who requests, confirms, and completes
training.
Pool "Training Provider" — the external organisation delivering training
programmes.
Pool "Learning Management System" — the LMS that records enrolments,
tracks completion, and stores development history.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Employing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Employee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Training Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Learning Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Employee
2. Employing Organisation
3. Training Provider
4. Learning Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Employing Organisation)

Learning & Development lane:

Message start event "Development need received from Manage Performance"
User task "Review development need and confirm learning objectives"
User task "Identify suitable training programmes or providers"
Exclusive gateway "Training available internally or externally?"
  - branch "internal": Service task "Create internal training enrolment
    in LMS"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Enrolment route resolved")
  - branch "external": Send task "Request programme availability and
    cost from Training Provider"
    Intermediate message catch event "Programme details received from
    Training Provider"
    User task "Evaluate programme details and select provider"
    Service task "Create external training enrolment in LMS"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Enrolment route resolved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Enrolment route resolved"
Send task "Send enrolment confirmation and joining instructions to
Employee"
Intermediate message catch event "Training completion confirmed by
Training Provider"
User task "Record training outcome and update development record in LMS"
Exclusive gateway "Development objective met?"
  - branch "yes": User task "Close development activity and notify
    Employee"
    End event "Development record updated — ready for Manage Changes"
  - branch "no": User task "Discuss further development options with
    Employee"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Development Objective Met"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify revised or additional training programme",
      Send task "Request updated programme details from Training Provider",
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised programme details
      received",
      User task "Enrol employee in revised programme in LMS",
      Send task "Send updated enrolment confirmation to Employee",
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised training completion
      confirmed"
    End event "Development objective not met — escalate to Manage
    Performance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on expanded subprocess "Repeat Until
Development Objective Met" — label "Maximum development cycle elapsed
(90 days)" — triggers End event "Development cycle timed out — escalate
to HR".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Learning & Development lane carries all flow
from the message start event through the internal/external gateway, which
branches to the internal enrolment service task or to the external send
task and its intermediate catch event, both branches merging at the
exclusive merge gateway "Enrolment route resolved", continuing to
confirmation, completion catch event, outcome recording, and the met/not
met gateway; the "yes" branch closes and ends, while the "no" branch
enters the standard-loop subprocess before ending in escalation.

Message flows:
Employing Organisation → Training Provider (request for programme
availability and cost)
Training Provider → Employing Organisation (programme details and
confirmation)
Employing Organisation → Employee (enrolment confirmation and joining
instructions)
Training Provider → Employing Organisation (training completion
confirmation)
Employee → Employing Organisation (acknowledgement of enrolment, where
needed)
Employing Organisation → Learning Management System (enrolment creation
and outcome recording requests)
Learning Management System → Employing Organisation (enrolment status,
completion status, and development record updates)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Development Need" — read by "Review development need and
confirm learning objectives".
Data Object "Learning Objectives" — written by "Review development need
and confirm learning objectives"; read by "Identify suitable training
programmes or providers".
Data Object "Training Programme Details" — written by "Evaluate programme
details and select provider"; read by "Create external training enrolment
in LMS".
Data Object "Enrolment Record" — written by "Create internal training
enrolment in LMS" and "Create external training enrolment in LMS"; read
by "Send enrolment confirmation and joining instructions to Employee".
Data Object "Training Outcome" — written by "Record training outcome and
update development record in LMS"; read by "Close development activity
and notify Employee".

This subprocess takes a development need surfaced during performance
management, matches the employee to appropriate internal or external
training, manages enrolment and completion with the Training Provider and
the Learning Management System, and records the outcome against the
employee's development record. Where the development objective is met the
record is closed and the outcome is available to Manage Changes; where it
is not met a further development cycle is initiated or the case is
escalated back to performance management.
```

### V04.11 — Manage Changes

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V04.11 Manage Changes — handles employee lifecycle change requests
within the Hire to Retire value chain, updating employment records and payroll
after an approved change takes effect.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Employing Organisation" — the organisation processing the change.
  Lane "Human Resources (HR Business Partner)" — receives and assesses the
    change request, communicates outcomes.
  Lane "Hiring Manager / People Manager (People Manager)" — initiates and
    endorses the change request, notifies the employee.
  Lane "Payroll (Payroll Officer)" — updates payroll details where the change
    has a pay or benefits impact.

Pool "Employee" — the employee whose employment record is being changed.
Pool "HRIS / HCM System" — records and maintains employee master data and
  change history.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Employing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Employee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "HRIS / HCM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Employee
2. Employing Organisation
3. HRIS / HCM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Employing Organisation)

Hiring Manager / People Manager lane:
  Message start event "Employee change request received from Employee"
  User task "Review and validate change request"
  Exclusive gateway "Change request valid?"
  - branch "No — invalid or incomplete":
      Send task "Return request to employee for correction"
      End event "Invalid request returned to Employee"
  - branch "Yes — valid":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Change request valid")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Change request valid"
  User task "Endorse change request and document rationale"

Human Resources (HR Business Partner) lane:
  User task "Assess change against policy and employment conditions"
  Exclusive gateway "Authorisation required?"
  - branch "Yes — senior or cross-functional sign-off needed":
      User task "Escalate for additional authorisation"
      Intermediate message catch event "Authorisation decision received"
  - branch "No — HR can approve directly":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation required"
  Exclusive gateway "Change approved?"
  - branch "No — rejected":
      Send task "Notify hiring manager and employee of rejection"
      End event "Change request rejected — hiring manager and employee notified"
  - branch "Yes — approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Change approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Change approved"
  Service task "Update employee record in HRIS / HCM System"
  User task "Issue change confirmation letter or contract amendment"
  Send task "Send change confirmation to employee"

Hiring Manager / People Manager lane:
  User task "Notify employee of effective date and any operational impacts"
  Exclusive gateway "Does change affect pay or benefits?"
  - branch "No":
      End event "Change recorded — no payroll action required"
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Does change affect pay or benefits")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Does change affect pay or benefits"

Payroll (Payroll Officer) lane:
  User task "Update payroll details to reflect approved change"
  Service task "Submit updated payroll record to HRIS / HCM System"
  User task "Verify next payroll run includes the change"
  End event "Change complete — payroll updated, ready for Manage Payroll
    and Benefits"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Escalate for additional authorisation"
  — label "Authorisation overdue (5 business days)" — triggers User task
  "Escalate reminder to HR Business Partner and senior approver" then returns
  to Intermediate message catch event "Authorisation decision received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Hiring Manager / People Manager lane,
passes to the Human Resources lane for policy assessment and approval, returns
briefly to the Hiring Manager / People Manager lane for employee notification,
and concludes in the Payroll lane when a pay or benefits impact exists. The
"Change request valid?" gateway branches either to a rejection end event or
merges and continues to endorsement. The "Authorisation required?" gateway
branches to escalation with a message catch or directly to the merge. The
"Change approved?" gateway branches to a rejection end event or merges and
continues to record update and confirmation. The "Does change affect pay or
benefits?" gateway branches to a no-payroll end event or merges into the
Payroll lane to conclude.

Message flows:
Employee → "Review and validate change request" (change request form with
  details of requested change)
"Return request to employee for correction" → Employee (request returned with
  reason for correction)
"Send change confirmation to employee" → Employee (change confirmation letter
  or contract amendment)
"Update employee record in HRIS / HCM System" → HRIS / HCM System (approved
  change details written to employee master record)
"Submit updated payroll record to HRIS / HCM System" → HRIS / HCM System
  (updated payroll fields for next pay run)
HRIS / HCM System → "Verify next payroll run includes the change" (payroll
  run confirmation showing updated record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Change Request Form" — written by Employee (at initiation,
  external); read by "Review and validate change request".
Data Object "Change Rationale Document" — written by "Endorse change request
  and document rationale"; read by "Assess change against policy and employment
  conditions".
Data Object "Policy Assessment Record" — written by "Assess change against
  policy and employment conditions"; read by "Escalate for additional
  authorisation".
Data Object "Authorisation Decision" — written by external approver via
  "Authorisation decision received"; read by "Change approved?" gateway.
Data Object "Change Confirmation Letter / Contract Amendment" — written by
  "Issue change confirmation letter or contract amendment"; read by "Send change
  confirmation to employee".
Data Object "Updated Payroll Record" — written by "Update payroll details to
  reflect approved change"; read by "Submit updated payroll record to HRIS /
  HCM System".

Manage Changes validates, endorses, and gains approval for an employee
lifecycle change — such as a promotion, role transfer, working-pattern
adjustment, or salary revision — updates the employee master record in the
HRIS / HCM System, and where a pay or benefits impact exists hands an updated
payroll record to Manage Payroll and Benefits to be reflected in the next pay
run.
```

### V04.12 — Handle Leave / Absence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V04.12 Handle Leave / Absence — subprocess within the Hire to Retire
value chain in which a leave or absence request is received, reviewed,
approved or declined, recorded, and payroll is notified, sitting between
Manage Changes and Offboard / Retire Employee.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Employing Organisation" — the internal teams that receive, assess,
  and record leave and absence requests.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - "Hiring Manager / People Manager" (people manager)
  - "Human Resources" (employee relations adviser)
  - "Payroll" (payroll officer)
Pool "Employee" — the employee submitting the leave or absence request
  and receiving outcomes.
Pool "Workforce Management System" — the system that records leave
  balances, absence entries, and produces compliance alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Employing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Employee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Workforce Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Employee
2. Employing Organisation (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Hiring
   Manager / People Manager, Human Resources, Payroll)
3. Workforce Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Employing Organisation)

Hiring Manager / People Manager lane:
  Message start event "Leave or absence request received from Employee"
  User task "Review leave request and check team coverage"
  Exclusive gateway "Request type?"
  - branch "Planned leave": User task "Verify leave balance and
    entitlement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved")
  - branch "Unplanned absence": User task "Record initial absence
    notification and expected duration"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved"
  Exclusive gateway "Manager decision?"
  - branch "Approved": Send task "Notify Employee of approval"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision communicated")
  - branch "Declined": Send task "Notify Employee of decline with reason"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision communicated")
  - branch "More information needed":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Information Sufficient"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
      Send task "Request additional information from Employee",
      Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received
        from Employee",
      User task "Re-assess leave request with new information",
      Exclusive gateway "Information now sufficient?",
      - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
      - branch "No": (loop repeats)
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision communicated")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision communicated"
  Exclusive gateway "Leave approved?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Submit approved leave record to Workforce
      Management System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Leave recorded")
  - branch "No": End event "Leave request declined — no further action"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Leave recorded"
  Intermediate message catch event "Leave balance confirmation received
    from Workforce Management System"
  User task "Confirm leave dates and coverage arrangement finalised"
  Send task "Forward leave details to Payroll for pay adjustment"

Human Resources lane:
  User task "Review for policy compliance and entitlement verification"
  Exclusive gateway "Compliance check outcome?"
  - branch "Compliant": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Compliance outcome resolved")
  - branch "Non-compliant or escalation required": User task
      "Advise people manager and document compliance concern"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Compliance outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Compliance outcome resolved"
  User task "Update employee absence record in Workforce Management
    System"

Payroll lane:
  User task "Receive leave details and determine pay impact"
  Exclusive gateway "Pay adjustment required?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Calculate adjusted pay and update payroll
      run"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pay impact resolved")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Pay impact resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Pay impact resolved"
  Service task "Confirm payroll update to Workforce Management System"
  End event "Leave handled and payroll updated — ready for
    Offboard / Retire Employee"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Information Sufficient", labelled "5 business days elapsed without
  sufficient information", triggering User task "Escalate unresolved
  leave request to HR adviser" in the Human Resources lane, followed
  by End event "Leave request escalated and closed pending resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Hiring Manager / People Manager lane
with the message start event, passes through request-type and decision
gateways (with the loop subprocess handling requests needing more
information, all branches rejoining at their respective merge gateways),
then flows to the Human Resources lane for compliance review and absence
recording, then to the Payroll lane for pay impact assessment and payroll
confirmation, ending at the end event in the Payroll lane.

Message flows:
Employee → Hiring Manager / People Manager lane (leave or absence
  request submission).
Hiring Manager / People Manager lane → Employee (approval or decline
  notification via send tasks).
Hiring Manager / People Manager lane → Employee (request for additional
  information).
Employee → Hiring Manager / People Manager lane (additional information
  provided).
Hiring Manager / People Manager lane → Workforce Management System
  (approved leave record submission).
Workforce Management System → Hiring Manager / People Manager lane
  (leave balance and confirmation response).
Human Resources lane → Workforce Management System (absence record
  update).
Payroll lane → Workforce Management System (payroll update
  confirmation).
Workforce Management System → Payroll lane (updated leave balance and
  compliance alerts).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Leave Request" — written by Message start event "Leave or
  absence request received from Employee"; read by User task "Review
  leave request and check team coverage"; read by User task "Review for
  policy compliance and entitlement verification".
Data Object "Leave Balance Report" — read by User task "Verify leave
  balance and entitlement"; written by Service task "Submit approved
  leave record to Workforce Management System".
Data Object "Absence Notification" — written by User task "Record
  initial absence notification and expected duration"; read by User task
  "Review for policy compliance and entitlement verification".
Data Object "Compliance Check Record" — written by User task "Review
  for policy compliance and entitlement verification"; read by User task
  "Advise people manager and document compliance concern".
Data Object "Approved Leave Record" — written by Service task "Submit
  approved leave record to Workforce Management System"; read by User
  task "Receive leave details and determine pay impact".
Data Object "Payroll Adjustment Detail" — written by User task
  "Calculate adjusted pay and update payroll run"; read by Service task
  "Confirm payroll update to Workforce Management System".

Handle Leave / Absence captures an employee's planned or unplanned
absence from the moment the request arrives, routes it through manager
review and HR compliance checking, and records the outcome in the
Workforce Management System. Payroll is notified of any pay impact and
confirms the adjustment before closing the case. The subprocess hands
a fully recorded and pay-adjusted absence record forward to
Offboard / Retire Employee, ensuring the employee's leave history and
final entitlements are accurate at the point of separation.
```

### V04.13 — Offboard / Retire Employee

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V04.13 Offboard / Retire Employee — the final subprocess of the
Hire to Retire value chain, closing the employee lifecycle by managing
all exit activities and handing final obligations to external parties.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Employing Organisation" — the internal teams managing the
offboarding and retirement process.
  Lane "Human Resources" — employee relations adviser leading the
  offboarding case.
  Lane "Payroll" — payroll officer processing final pay and fund
  notifications.
  Lane "IT" — IT provisioning officer revoking access and recovering
  equipment.
Pool "Employee" — the departing employee providing information and
returning assets.
Pool "Superannuation / Pension Fund" — external fund receiving final
contribution and member transfer details.
Pool "Benefits Provider" — external provider notified of benefit
cessation.
Pool "HRIS / HCM System" — HR system of record for the employee
lifecycle.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Employing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Employee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Superannuation / Pension Fund" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Benefits Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "HRIS / HCM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Employee
2. Employing Organisation
3. Superannuation / Pension Fund
4. Benefits Provider
5. HRIS / HCM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Employing Organisation)

Human Resources lane:
  Message start event "Offboarding trigger received from Manage Changes
  or employee resignation / retirement notification"
  User task "Open offboarding case and confirm exit details"
  Service task "Record exit reason and expected last day in HRIS / HCM
  System"
  User task "Issue offboarding checklist to employee"
  Intermediate message catch event "Signed offboarding acknowledgement
  received from employee"
  User task "Schedule exit interview"
  Intermediate message catch event "Exit interview completed by
  employee"
  User task "Conduct exit interview and record feedback"
  User task "Verify all HR obligations met (references, certificates of
  service, statutory notices)"
  Exclusive gateway "Disciplinary or legal hold applies?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate to Legal and pause offboarding
    until cleared"
    Intermediate message catch event "Legal clearance received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disciplinary or legal hold
    applies")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disciplinary or
    legal hold applies")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Disciplinary or legal hold applies"
  User task "Prepare and issue certificate of service and reference
  letter"
  Send task "Send exit documentation package to employee"
  End event "HR offboarding obligations complete"

Payroll lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Last working day confirmed from
  Human Resources"
  User task "Calculate final pay, unused leave, and termination
  entitlements"
  Exclusive gateway "Redundancy or retirement payment applicable?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Calculate redundancy or retirement
    payment in accordance with remuneration policy"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Redundancy or retirement
    payment applicable")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Redundancy or
    retirement payment applicable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Redundancy or retirement payment applicable"
  User task "Process final payroll run"
  Service task "Record final pay and termination details in HRIS / HCM
  System"
  Send task "Issue final payslip to employee"
  User task "Notify Superannuation / Pension Fund of final contribution
  and member cessation"
  User task "Notify Benefits Provider of benefit cessation"
  User task "File tax and statutory cessation declarations"
  End event "Final pay and fund notifications complete"

IT lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Offboarding task list received from
  Human Resources"
  User task "Identify all active system accounts and access rights"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Access Revoked" (standard loop)
  containing, in order: User task "Revoke system account or access
  right", Service task "Update revocation in IAM System", User task
  "Confirm revocation and mark item complete in checklist"
  Service task "Disable employee record in HRIS / HCM System"
  User task "Coordinate equipment return with employee"
  Intermediate message catch event "Equipment return confirmed"
  User task "Record returned equipment and update asset register"
  User task "Decommission or reallocate equipment as required"
  End event "Access revoked and equipment recovered — offboarding
  complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Open offboarding case
and confirm exit details" — label "Trigger overdue (2 business days)"
— flows to User task "Escalate delayed offboarding start to HR manager".

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Access Revoked" — label "Access revocation deadline exceeded
(last working day)" — flows to User task "Raise urgent access
revocation incident".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Human Resources lane the flow runs from the
message start event through case opening, HRIS recording, checklist
issuance, acknowledgement catch, exit interview scheduling, interview
completion catch, interview conduct, obligations verification, the
legal-hold gateway and its merge, certificate preparation, and the send
task to the HR end event. The Payroll lane begins from the last-day
confirmation catch event, runs through final-pay calculation, the
redundancy gateway and its merge, the final payroll run, HRIS recording,
final payslip send, fund and benefits notifications, and tax declarations
to the payroll end event. The IT lane begins from the offboarding task
list catch event, runs through account identification, the access
revocation subprocess, HRIS disable, equipment coordination, the
equipment return catch event, asset recording, and decommission to the
IT end event. The legal-hold "Yes" branch flows through the escalation
task and legal-clearance catch event before rejoining the exclusive merge
gateway. The redundancy "Yes" branch flows through the redundancy
calculation task before rejoining its merge gateway.

Message flows:
Employee → Human Resources lane (signed offboarding acknowledgement).
Employee → Human Resources lane (exit interview completed notification).
Human Resources lane → Employee (offboarding checklist).
Human Resources lane → Employee (exit documentation package including
certificate of service and reference letter).
Human Resources lane → Payroll lane (last working day confirmation).
Human Resources lane → IT lane (offboarding task list).
Payroll lane → Employee (final payslip).
Payroll lane → Superannuation / Pension Fund (final contribution and
member cessation notification).
Payroll lane → Benefits Provider (benefit cessation notification).
Human Resources lane → HRIS / HCM System (exit reason, last day, and
case data).
Payroll lane → HRIS / HCM System (final pay and termination record).
IT lane → HRIS / HCM System (employee record disable request).
HRIS / HCM System → Human Resources lane (confirmation of record
updated).
Employee → IT lane (equipment return confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Offboarding Checklist" — written by User task "Open
offboarding case and confirm exit details"; read by User task "Verify
all HR obligations met (references, certificates of service, statutory
notices)".
Data Object "Exit Interview Record" — written by User task "Conduct
exit interview and record feedback"; read by User task "Verify all HR
obligations met (references, certificates of service, statutory notices)".
Data Object "Certificate of Service" — written by User task "Prepare
and issue certificate of service and reference letter"; read by Send
task "Send exit documentation package to employee".
Data Object "Final Pay Calculation" — written by User task "Calculate
final pay, unused leave, and termination entitlements"; read by User
task "Process final payroll run".
Data Object "Termination Record" — written by Service task "Record
final pay and termination details in HRIS / HCM System"; read by User
task "File tax and statutory cessation declarations".
Data Object "Access Revocation Checklist" — written by User task
"Identify all active system accounts and access rights"; read by
Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Access Revoked".
Data Object "Asset Return Record" — written by User task "Record
returned equipment and update asset register"; read by User task
"Decommission or reallocate equipment as required".

V04.13 Offboard / Retire Employee closes the Hire to Retire lifecycle
by executing all exit obligations across Human Resources, Payroll, and
IT in parallel. Human Resources manages the case, exit interview, and
statutory documentation; Payroll calculates and issues final entitlements
and notifies the superannuation fund and benefits provider; IT revokes
all access and recovers equipment. Once all three lanes reach their end
events, the organisation has fulfilled its legal, financial, and security
obligations, and the employee record is closed — completing the
Hire to Retire value chain.
```

## V05 — Plan to Produce

**Teams and roles involved.**
Plan to Produce involves Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Production Planning, Manufacturing Operations, Procurement, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Maintenance, Engineering, Finance, and Logistics. Key roles include demand planner, production planner, plant manager, production supervisor, machine operator, quality inspector, maintenance technician, inventory controller, and supply chain manager.

**External participants.**
The external participants are usually indirect. The main external trigger may be Customer Demand, a Distributor, a Retailer, or a forecast from the market. Suppliers and contract manufacturers may also participate during production planning and execution.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: forecast demand, plan supply, create production plan, check capacity and materials, schedule production, issue materials, manufacture product, inspect quality, manage exceptions, record production output, move finished goods to inventory, and close production orders.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ERP manufacturing modules, material requirements planning system, advanced planning and scheduling system, manufacturing execution system, warehouse management system, quality management system, maintenance management system, product lifecycle management system, and reporting/BI tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include production planning policy, inventory policy, quality policy, safety procedure, bill of materials governance, production scheduling procedure, material handling procedure, maintenance procedure, batch/lot traceability procedure, and non-conformance procedure.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Customers, distributors, and market channels provide demand signals, orders, forecasts, service-level expectations, and product requirements. Suppliers provide material availability, lead times, substitutions, and delivery confirmations. The process may provide production availability, delivery promise dates, shortage notices, and fulfilment commitments.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process consumes demand forecasts, sales orders, inventory levels, bills of materials, routings, supplier lead times, capacity data, and quality specifications. It creates production plans, work orders, material reservations, shop-floor instructions, quality results, production confirmations, inventory movements, and cost postings.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V05 - Plan to Produce (Make)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V05.01. Forecast Demand
V05.02. Plan Supply
V05.03. Create Production Plan
V05.04. Check Capacity and Materials
V05.05. Schedule Production
V05.06. Issue Materials
V05.07. Manufacture Product
V05.08. Inspect Quality
V05.09. Manage Exceptions
V05.10. Record Production Output
V05.11. Move Finished Goods to Inventory
V05.12. Close Production Orders

This is the make / produce end-to-end process: a demand forecast flows
through supply and production planning, capacity and material checks,
scheduling, material issue, manufacture, quality inspection, output
recording and finished-goods put-away before the production orders are
closed. The external participants are mostly indirect — demand comes from
Customers, Distributors and Retailers as the market signal, and materials
from Suppliers and Contract Manufacturers; the process is triggered by a
demand signal or a forecast rather than a single external order.
```

### V05.01 — Forecast Demand

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.01 Forecast Demand — opens the Plan to Produce value chain by
gathering demand signals from external parties and producing a validated
demand forecast ready for supply planning.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the company running the forecasting
process, containing all internal lanes.
  Lane "Demand Planning" — demand planner who collects, models, and
  validates the forecast.
  Lane "Supply Planning" — supply chain manager who reviews and approves
  the consensus forecast.
Pool "Customer" — external customer providing demand signals and orders.
Pool "Distributor" — external distributor providing sell-through data and
forecasts.
Pool "Retailer" — external retailer providing point-of-sale data and
replenishment requirements.
Pool "Reporting / BI Tools" — IT system supplying historical sales data and
publishing the approved forecast.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Distributor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Retailer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Reporting / BI Tools" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Distributor
3. Retailer
4. Manufacturing Organisation
5. Reporting / BI Tools

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Demand Planning lane:
  Message start event "Demand signals received from Customer, Distributor,
  and Retailer"
  Service task "Retrieve historical sales data from Reporting / BI Tools"
  User task "Consolidate demand signals and historical data"
  User task "Build statistical demand forecast"
  User task "Apply market intelligence and adjustments"
  Exclusive gateway "Forecast data sufficient?"
  - branch "No — data gaps identified": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
    Data Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Request
    additional demand data from external parties", Intermediate message
    catch event "Additional data received", User task "Incorporate
    additional data into forecast"
    (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Yes — data sufficient": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Forecast data sufficient")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Forecast data sufficient"
  User task "Finalise draft demand forecast"
  Send task "Submit draft forecast to Supply Planning for review"

Supply Planning lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Draft forecast received from Demand
  Planning"
  User task "Review draft demand forecast"
  User task "Facilitate consensus forecasting meeting"
  Exclusive gateway "Forecast approved?"
  - branch "No — revisions required": Send task "Return forecast with
    revision comments to Demand Planning"
    Intermediate message catch event "Revised forecast received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Forecast approved")
  - branch "Yes — approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Forecast approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Forecast approved"
  User task "Record approved consensus forecast"
  Service task "Publish approved forecast to Reporting / BI Tools"
  End event "Approved demand forecast published — ready for Plan Supply"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Data
Complete" — labelled "Data collection deadline exceeded" — triggers End event
"Forecast abandoned due to insufficient data".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Demand Planning lane with the message
start event, proceeds through data retrieval, consolidation, statistical
modelling, and adjustment tasks, then reaches the "Forecast data sufficient"
gateway; the "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and exits back
to the merge gateway, while the "Yes" branch flows directly to the merge
gateway; both branches rejoin and continue to forecast finalisation and
submission to Supply Planning. The flow crosses to the Supply Planning lane
via an internal message catch event, proceeds through review and consensus
tasks, reaches the "Forecast approved" gateway; the "No" branch sends
revision comments back to Demand Planning and waits for the revised forecast
before rejoining the merge gateway, and the "Yes" branch flows directly to
the merge gateway; both branches rejoin at the merge gateway and continue to
recording and publishing the approved forecast.

Message flows:
Customer → Demand Planning lane (demand signals and order data)
Distributor → Demand Planning lane (sell-through data and distribution
forecasts)
Retailer → Demand Planning lane (point-of-sale data and replenishment
requirements)
Reporting / BI Tools → Demand Planning lane (historical sales data and
trend reports)
Supply Planning lane → Demand Planning lane (revision comments on draft
forecast)
Demand Planning lane → Supply Planning lane (draft demand forecast for
review)
Supply Planning lane → Reporting / BI Tools (approved consensus forecast
for publication)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Demand Signals" — written by Message start event "Demand
signals received from Customer, Distributor, and Retailer"; read by User
task "Consolidate demand signals and historical data".
Data Object "Historical Sales Data" — written by Service task "Retrieve
historical sales data from Reporting / BI Tools"; read by User task
"Consolidate demand signals and historical data".
Data Object "Statistical Demand Forecast" — written by User task "Build
statistical demand forecast"; read by User task "Apply market intelligence
and adjustments".
Data Object "Draft Demand Forecast" — written by User task "Finalise draft
demand forecast"; read by User task "Review draft demand forecast".
Data Object "Revision Comments" — written by Send task "Return forecast
with revision comments to Demand Planning"; read by User task "Incorporate
additional data into forecast".
Data Object "Approved Consensus Forecast" — written by User task "Record
approved consensus forecast"; read by Service task "Publish approved
forecast to Reporting / BI Tools".

V05.01 Forecast Demand captures demand signals from customers, distributors,
and retailers, enriches them with historical data from the Reporting / BI
Tools system, and produces a statistically grounded, consensus-approved
demand forecast. The approved forecast is published to the BI platform and
handed to V05.02 Plan Supply, where it becomes the primary input for
determining how supply capacity and procurement commitments should be shaped
to meet anticipated demand.
```

### V05.02 — Plan Supply

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.02 Plan Supply — second subprocess in the Plan to Produce value
chain, translating demand forecasts into confirmed supply commitments.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the internal organisation running the
  supply planning process, with lanes for Supply Planning and Procurement.
Pool "Supplier" — external supplier providing material availability,
  lead times, and delivery confirmations.
Pool "Contract Manufacturer" — external contract manufacturer providing
  capacity and production commitments.
Pool "Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System" — IT system used to
  generate and process material requirements and supply recommendations.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Manufacturer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Contract Manufacturer
3. Manufacturing Organisation
4. Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Supply Planning lane:
  Message start event "Validated demand forecast received from
    Forecast Demand"
  Service task "Load demand forecast into MRP System"
  Service task "Run MRP to generate supply requirements"
  Intermediate message catch event "MRP supply recommendations received"
  User task "Review MRP supply recommendations"
  Exclusive gateway "Recommendations acceptable?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Recommendations acceptable")
    - branch "No": User task "Adjust parameters and resubmit to MRP"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Recommendations acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Recommendations acceptable"
  User task "Identify sourcing options for each requirement"
  Exclusive gateway "In-house or outsource?"
    - branch "In-house — procure materials": User task
        "Prepare purchase requisitions for materials"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "In-house or outsource")
    - branch "Outsource — contract manufacturer": Send task
        "Send production request to Contract Manufacturer"
        Intermediate message catch event
        "Contract Manufacturer capacity confirmation received"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "In-house or outsource")
  Exclusive merge gateway "In-house or outsource"
  User task "Consolidate supply plan"
  User task "Validate supply plan against demand"
  Exclusive gateway "Supply plan balanced?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Supply plan balanced")
    - branch "No — gaps or excess": User task
        "Resolve gaps or excess supply"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supply plan balanced")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supply plan balanced"
  User task "Approve supply plan"
  End event "Supply plan approved — ready for Create Production Plan"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Raise and issue purchase orders to Suppliers"
  Intermediate message catch event
    "Supplier delivery confirmation received"
  User task "Record supplier commitments in MRP System"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  'Supplier delivery confirmation received'" — if no confirmation is
  received within the expected lead-time window, label "Supplier response
  overdue"; flow continues to User task "Escalate overdue supplier
  commitment" in the Procurement lane, ending at End event "Supplier
  escalation raised".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  'Contract Manufacturer capacity confirmation received'" — label
  "Contract Manufacturer response overdue"; flow continues to User task
  "Escalate contract manufacturer delay" in the Supply Planning lane,
  ending at End event "Contract Manufacturer escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Supply Planning lane with the message
  start event, moves through MRP loading and review, through the
  "Recommendations acceptable" gateway and merge, then to sourcing
  identification and the "In-house or outsource" gateway; the in-house
  branch passes to the Procurement lane for purchase order creation and
  returns after supplier commitment recording; the outsource branch stays
  in Supply Planning for contract manufacturer coordination; both branches
  rejoin at the "In-house or outsource" merge, continuing through supply
  plan consolidation, validation, the "Supply plan balanced" gateway and
  merge, approval, and the end event.

Message flows:
  Supply Planning lane "Service task: Load demand forecast into MRP
    System" → Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System (demand
    forecast data).
  Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System → Supply Planning lane
    "Intermediate message catch event: MRP supply recommendations
    received" (supply recommendations and material requirements).
  Supply Planning lane "User task: Adjust parameters and resubmit to
    MRP" → Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System (revised
    planning parameters).
  Procurement lane "User task: Raise and issue purchase orders to
    Suppliers" → Supplier (purchase orders).
  Supplier → Procurement lane "Intermediate message catch event: Supplier
    delivery confirmation received" (material availability, lead times,
    and delivery confirmations).
  Procurement lane "User task: Record supplier commitments in MRP
    System" → Material Requirements Planning (MRP) System (confirmed
    supplier commitments).
  Supply Planning lane "Send task: Send production request to Contract
    Manufacturer" → Contract Manufacturer (production request and
    specifications).
  Contract Manufacturer → Supply Planning lane "Intermediate message
    catch event: Contract Manufacturer capacity confirmation received"
    (capacity confirmation and production commitment).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Demand Forecast" — read by "Load demand forecast into MRP
  System".
Data Object "MRP Supply Recommendations" — written by Material
  Requirements Planning (MRP) System; read by "Review MRP supply
  recommendations".
Data Object "Purchase Requisition" — written by "Prepare purchase
  requisitions for materials"; read by "Raise and issue purchase orders
  to Suppliers".
Data Object "Purchase Order" — written by "Raise and issue purchase
  orders to Suppliers"; read by "Record supplier commitments in MRP
  System".
Data Object "Supplier Delivery Confirmation" — written by Supplier;
  read by "Record supplier commitments in MRP System".
Data Object "Contract Manufacturer Commitment" — written by Contract
  Manufacturer; read by "Consolidate supply plan".
Data Object "Supply Plan" — written by "Consolidate supply plan"; read
  by "Validate supply plan against demand" and "Approve supply plan".

Plan Supply translates the validated demand forecast into a balanced,
approved supply plan by running MRP, reviewing recommendations, sourcing
materials through purchase orders to Suppliers, and securing capacity
from Contract Manufacturers where needed. The approved supply plan, with
confirmed purchase orders and external commitments in place, is handed
to Create Production Plan as the authoritative basis for scheduling
production.
```

### V05.03 — Create Production Plan

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.03 Create Production Plan — the subprocess in which Production
Planning and Engineering translate the approved supply plan into a validated
production plan, drawing on bill-of-materials and routing data from the PLM
System, ready for capacity and materials checking.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the internal teams that create and
validate the production plan.
  Lane "Production Planning" — production planner who owns plan creation.
  Lane "Engineering" — engineer who validates BOM and routing data.
Pool "Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System" — IT system holding bill
of materials, routings, and product specifications.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Organisation (white-box, with Production Planning lane
   above Engineering lane)
2. Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Production Planning lane:
  Message start event "Approved supply plan received from Plan Supply"
  User task "Review approved supply plan"
  Service task "Request BOM and routing data from PLM System"
  Intermediate message catch event "BOM and routing data received"
  User task "Draft production plan"
  User task "Define production quantities and sequences"
  Send task "Send draft production plan for engineering review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Engineering review outcome received"
  Exclusive gateway "Engineering review passed?"
  - branch "No — revisions required":
      Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until Engineering Approved"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Revise draft production plan",
        Send task "Resubmit revised plan to Engineering",
        Intermediate message catch event "Re-review outcome received"
      (exits subprocess — continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Engineering review passed")
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Engineering review passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Engineering review passed"
  User task "Finalise production plan"
  Service task "Record finalised plan in PLM System"
  End event "Production plan created — ready for Check Capacity and
    Materials"

Engineering lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Draft production plan received"
  User task "Validate BOM completeness and accuracy"
  User task "Validate routings and work centre assignments"
  Exclusive gateway "BOM and routing data valid?"
  - branch "No — data issues found":
      Service task "Request BOM or routing correction from PLM System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected data received from
        PLM System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "BOM and routing data valid")
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "BOM and routing data valid")
  Exclusive merge gateway "BOM and routing data valid"
  User task "Approve engineering review"
  Send task "Send engineering review outcome to Production Planning"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until
Engineering Approved" — label "Revision deadline exceeded" — triggers
End event "Plan revision timed out — escalate to production planner".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within Production Planning lane, flow runs from the
message start event through review, BOM request, drafting, sequencing,
and the send task to Engineering, then waits for the review outcome,
passes through the "Engineering review passed?" gateway — the "No"
branch enters the revision subprocess and exits to the merge gateway;
the "Yes" branch goes directly to the merge gateway — after which flow
continues through finalisation and recording to the end event. Within
Engineering lane, flow runs from the incoming message catch event
through BOM and routing validation to the "BOM and routing data valid?"
gateway — the "No" branch requests corrected data from PLM, catches the
correction, and continues to the merge gateway; the "Yes" branch goes
directly to the merge gateway — after which flow continues through
approval and the send task back to Production Planning.

Message flows:
  Manufacturing Organisation (Service task "Request BOM and routing data
    from PLM System") → Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System
    (BOM and routing data request)
  Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System → Manufacturing Organisation
    (Intermediate message catch event "BOM and routing data received")
    (BOM, routings, and product specifications)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Send task "Send draft production plan for
    engineering review") → Manufacturing Organisation Engineering lane
    (Intermediate message catch event "Draft production plan received")
    (draft production plan)
  Manufacturing Organisation Engineering lane (Send task "Send
    engineering review outcome to Production Planning") →
    Manufacturing Organisation Production Planning lane
    (Intermediate message catch event "Engineering review outcome
    received") (engineering review result and comments)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Expanded Subprocess revision — Send task
    "Resubmit revised plan to Engineering") → Manufacturing Organisation
    Engineering lane (re-review cycle) (revised production plan)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Service task "Request BOM or routing
    correction from PLM System") → Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
    System (correction request)
  Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System → Manufacturing Organisation
    Engineering lane (Intermediate message catch event "Corrected data
    received from PLM System") (corrected BOM or routing records)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Service task "Record finalised plan in PLM
    System") → Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) System
    (finalised production plan)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Supply Plan" — read by User task "Review approved
  supply plan".
Data Object "BOM and Routing Data" — read by User task "Validate BOM
  completeness and accuracy"; read by User task "Validate routings and
  work centre assignments".
Data Object "Draft Production Plan" — written by User task "Draft
  production plan"; read by User task "Validate BOM completeness and
  accuracy".
Data Object "Engineering Review Report" — written by User task "Approve
  engineering review"; read by Production Planning lane (Intermediate
  message catch event "Engineering review outcome received").
Data Object "Finalised Production Plan" — written by User task
  "Finalise production plan"; read by Service task "Record finalised
  plan in PLM System".

Create Production Plan takes the approved supply plan and, in
collaboration with Engineering, builds a validated production plan
complete with confirmed quantities, sequences, BOMs, and routings. It
ensures all product data is accurate before handing a fully approved,
recorded production plan to Check Capacity and Materials, where resource
availability and stock levels will be verified against that plan.
```

### V05.04 — Check Capacity and Materials

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.04 Check Capacity and Materials — confirms that production
capacity and required materials are available before scheduling begins
in the Plan to Produce value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the internal teams that verify
capacity and material availability.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Production Planning (production planner)
  - Warehouse (inventory controller)

Pool "Supplier" — external party that confirms material availability
and lead times when stock is short.

Pool "ERP Manufacturing Module" — system that holds capacity data,
inventory records, material reservations, and shortage reports.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Manufacturing Module" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Organisation (white-box, with two lanes)
2. Supplier
3. ERP Manufacturing Module

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Production Planning lane:
  Message start event "Production plan received from Create
    Production Plan"
  Service task "Retrieve capacity data from ERP"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient capacity available?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Sufficient capacity available")
  - branch "No": User task "Identify capacity shortfall and
      resolution options"
    Exclusive gateway "Shortfall resolvable internally?"
    - branch "Yes — adjust schedule or overtime":
        User task "Adjust planned capacity allocation"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Shortfall resolvable internally")
    - branch "No — escalate":
        End event "Capacity shortfall unresolvable — escalate
          to Manage Exceptions"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Shortfall resolvable internally"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Sufficient capacity available")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient capacity available"
  User task "Request material availability check from Warehouse"
  Intermediate message catch event "Material availability
    confirmed received from Warehouse"
  Exclusive gateway "All materials available?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "All materials available")
  - branch "No — shortage identified":
      User task "Log material shortage and initiate supplier
        inquiry"
      Send task "Send material shortage inquiry to Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplier availability
        response received"
      Exclusive gateway "Supplier can fulfil on time?"
      - branch "Yes": User task "Record supplier commitment
          in ERP"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway
          "Supplier can fulfil on time")
      - branch "No": End event "Material shortage unresolvable
          — escalate to Manage Exceptions"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier can fulfil on time"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "All materials available")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All materials available"
  Service task "Confirm capacity and material status in ERP"
  End event "Capacity and materials confirmed — ready for
    Schedule Production"

Warehouse lane:
  User task "Check stock levels and material reservations in ERP"
  Service task "Record material availability result in ERP"
  Send task "Send material availability confirmation to
    Production Planning"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on "Intermediate message catch
  event Supplier availability response received" — label "Supplier
  response overdue (48 hours)" — triggers End event "Supplier
  non-response — escalate to Manage Exceptions".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Production Planning lane, flow moves
from the start event through capacity retrieval and the capacity
gateway; the "No" branch resolves at the internal-shortfall merge
before rejoining the capacity merge; flow continues to the material
availability request, waits for Warehouse confirmation, then
traverses the materials gateway; the "No" branch contacts the
Supplier and resolves at the supplier-fulfilment merge before
rejoining the materials merge; flow ends at ERP confirmation and
the end event. The Warehouse lane runs its own internal sequence
from stock check through recording to the send task.

Message flows:
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning — Service task
    "Retrieve capacity data from ERP") → ERP Manufacturing Module
    (capacity and routing data request).
  ERP Manufacturing Module → Manufacturing Organisation
    (Production Planning — Service task "Retrieve capacity data
    from ERP") (capacity data and routings).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning — User task
    "Request material availability check from Warehouse") →
    Manufacturing Organisation (Warehouse — User task "Check stock
    levels and material reservations in ERP") (material check
    request).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Warehouse — Service task "Record
    material availability result in ERP") → ERP Manufacturing
    Module (material availability and reservation update).
  ERP Manufacturing Module → Manufacturing Organisation (Warehouse
    — Service task "Record material availability result in ERP")
    (confirmed reservation or shortage flag).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Warehouse — Send task "Send material
    availability confirmation to Production Planning") →
    Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning —
    Intermediate message catch event "Material availability
    confirmed received from Warehouse") (material availability
    confirmation).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning — Send task
    "Send material shortage inquiry to Supplier") → Supplier
    (material shortage inquiry).
  Supplier → Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning —
    Intermediate message catch event "Supplier availability
    response received") (availability and lead-time response).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning — Service task
    "Confirm capacity and material status in ERP") →
    ERP Manufacturing Module (capacity and material confirmation
    record).
  ERP Manufacturing Module → Manufacturing Organisation
    (Production Planning — Service task "Confirm capacity and
    material status in ERP") (write confirmation acknowledgement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Capacity Check Report" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve capacity data from ERP"; read by Exclusive gateway
  "Sufficient capacity available?".
Data Object "Material Availability Report" — written by User task
  "Check stock levels and material reservations in ERP"; read by
  Exclusive gateway "All materials available?".
Data Object "Supplier Availability Response" — written by
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier availability response
  received"; read by Exclusive gateway "Supplier can fulfil on
  time?".
Data Object "Material Reservation Record" — written by Service
  task "Record material availability result in ERP"; read by
  Service task "Confirm capacity and material status in ERP".

Check Capacity and Materials verifies that the manufacturing
organisation has both the production capacity and the physical
materials required to execute the incoming production plan. It
resolves capacity shortfalls through internal reallocation and
material shortfalls through supplier inquiry, escalating
unresolvable cases to Manage Exceptions. A confirmed capacity-and-
materials status, recorded in the ERP Manufacturing Module, is
handed to Schedule Production so that work orders can be timed and
sequenced with confidence.
```

### V05.05 — Schedule Production

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.05 Schedule Production — converts the approved production plan
into a time-sequenced shop-floor schedule within the Plan to Produce value
chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the internal teams that build and
approve the production schedule.
  Lane "Production Planning" — production planner who drives scheduling
  activity and resolves conflicts.
  Lane "Manufacturing Operations" — plant manager who reviews, adjusts,
  and approves the finalised schedule.

Pool "Advanced Planning & Scheduling (APS) System" — IT system that
optimises and stores the production schedule.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Advanced Planning & Scheduling (APS) System" — black-box,
System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Organisation (white-box, two lanes top to bottom:
   Production Planning, Manufacturing Operations)
2. Advanced Planning & Scheduling (APS) System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Production Planning lane:
  Message start event "Approved production plan received from Create
    Production Plan"
  User task "Review approved production plan and constraints"
  Service task "Load plan and capacity data into APS System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Optimised schedule returned from
    APS System"
  User task "Review optimised schedule for conflicts"
  Exclusive gateway "Scheduling conflicts identified?"
    - branch "Yes — conflicts found":
        Expanded Subprocess "Resolve Scheduling Conflicts Until
          Schedule is Feasible" (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Identify conflict root cause",
          User task "Adjust resource or timing parameters",
          Service task "Resubmit adjusted parameters to APS System",
          Intermediate message catch event "Revised schedule returned
            from APS System",
          User task "Evaluate revised schedule"
        (exits subprocess)
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scheduling conflicts
          identified")
    - branch "No — schedule is feasible":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scheduling conflicts
          identified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scheduling conflicts identified"
  User task "Prepare schedule documentation for handover"
  Send task "Submit finalised schedule to Manufacturing Operations
    for approval"

Manufacturing Operations lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Finalised schedule received for
    approval"
  User task "Review finalised production schedule"
  Exclusive gateway "Schedule approved by plant manager?"
    - branch "No — revisions required":
        User task "Document required revisions and return to
          Production Planning"
        Send task "Send revision instructions to Production Planning"
        Intermediate message catch event "Revised schedule received
          from Production Planning"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved by
          plant manager")
    - branch "Yes — approved":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved by
          plant manager")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved by plant manager"
  User task "Confirm schedule acceptance"
  Service task "Publish approved schedule to APS System"
  End event "Approved production schedule published — ready for
    Issue Materials"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Resolve
Scheduling Conflicts Until Schedule is Feasible" — label "Conflict
resolution time limit exceeded" — triggers End event "Schedule
escalated to supply chain manager — exception raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Production Planning lane, moving
from plan review through APS loading, conflict resolution (looping
inside the subprocess until the schedule is feasible), and schedule
preparation, then crossing to the Manufacturing Operations lane for
plant-manager review and approval; the approval gateway branches to
a revision loop that returns a revised schedule message to Production
Planning and re-enters the approval gateway merge, or to the
confirmed-acceptance path that publishes to the APS System and ends.

Message flows:
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning) → Advanced
    Planning & Scheduling (APS) System (capacity and plan data
    loaded for optimisation).
  Advanced Planning & Scheduling (APS) System → Manufacturing
    Organisation (Production Planning) (optimised schedule
    returned).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Production Planning) → Advanced
    Planning & Scheduling (APS) System (adjusted parameters
    resubmitted during conflict resolution).
  Advanced Planning & Scheduling (APS) System → Manufacturing
    Organisation (Production Planning) (revised schedule returned
    during conflict resolution loop).
  Manufacturing Organisation (Manufacturing Operations) → Advanced
    Planning & Scheduling (APS) System (approved schedule
    published for shop-floor use).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Production Plan" — read by User task "Review
  approved production plan and constraints".
Data Object "Capacity and Constraint Data" — read by Service task
  "Load plan and capacity data into APS System".
Data Object "Optimised Schedule" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Optimised schedule returned from APS System"; read
  by User task "Review optimised schedule for conflicts".
Data Object "Revised Schedule" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Revised schedule returned from APS System"; read by
  User task "Evaluate revised schedule".
Data Object "Schedule Documentation" — written by User task "Prepare
  schedule documentation for handover"; read by User task "Review
  finalised production schedule".
Data Object "Revision Instructions" — written by User task "Document
  required revisions and return to Production Planning"; read by
  User task "Review optimised schedule for conflicts".
Data Object "Approved Production Schedule" — written by Service task
  "Publish approved schedule to APS System".

This subprocess transforms the capacity-checked production plan into a
time-sequenced, conflict-free shop-floor schedule endorsed by the plant
manager. Scheduling conflicts are resolved iteratively inside a bounded
loop, and the plant manager's approval gate ensures operational
feasibility before commitment. The published approved schedule is handed
to Issue Materials, which uses it to trigger the release of raw materials
to the shop floor.
```

### V05.06 — Issue Materials

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.06 Issue Materials — the subprocess that picks, stages, and

within the Plan to Produce value chain.

  - Warehouse (inventory controller)

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Organisation (white-box, two lanes)
2. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

Warehouse lane:

    Production"
  User task "Review material requirements and pick list"

Manufacturing Operations lane:

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Materials acceptable")
  - branch "No — materials rejected":

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Materials acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Materials acceptable"
  User task "Confirm material receipt on shop floor"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Raise material shortage

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Warehouse lane with the message start
  event and proceeds through stock checking, the "Materials available"
  gateway and its merge, picking, verification, the "Quantities correct"
  gateway and its merge, staging, WMS recording, and the send task. The

  continues through inspection, the "Materials acceptable" gateway and
  its merge, and concludes at the end event. The shortage-resolution

Message flows:
  Manufacturing Organisation (Warehouse lane — Service task "Check stock
    availability in WMS") → Warehouse Management System (WMS) (stock

  Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Manufacturing Organisation

7. Data objects

Issue Materials picks stock against the production schedule, verifies
quantities and lot traceability, stages materials, and posts the issue
transaction in the WMS. It hands confirmed, receipted materials to the
Manufacture Product subprocess, giving the shop floor a complete and
documented material set ready for production to begin.
```

```text
  Exclusive merge gateway "In-process check outcome"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract manufacturing required?"

        Manufacturer", Intermediate message catch event "Production

        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Manufacturing route
```
