```text
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Manufacturing route resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Manufacturing route resolved"
  User task "Complete batch and record output quantities in MES"
  Send task "Send completed batch notification to MES"
  End event "Batch manufactured — ready for Inspect Quality"

Maintenance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Deviation escalation received"
  User task "Assess equipment condition"
  Exclusive gateway "Maintenance required?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Perform corrective maintenance",
        Send task "Confirm equipment restored to Manufacturing
        Operations", (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Maintenance outcome")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Maintenance outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Maintenance outcome"
  End event "Maintenance resolved — production may resume"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Batch Complete", labelled "Batch cycle time limit exceeded", triggers
  Send task "Escalate batch overrun to production supervisor".
Interrupting error boundary event on User task "Perform corrective
  maintenance", labelled "Equipment failure cannot be resolved",
  triggers End event "Unresolvable equipment failure — escalate to
  Manage Exceptions".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Manufacturing Operations lane the flow runs
  from the message start event through machine set-up, MES notification,
  the standard-loop subprocess, in-process checks, the in-process check
  gateway and its merge, then the contract-manufacturing gateway and its
  merge, batch completion, and the end event. The Maintenance lane runs
  independently from its message catch event through assessment and the
  maintenance gateway to its merge and end event. The in-process check
  "No — major deviation" branch sends an escalation before rejoining the
  merge gateway.

Message flows:
  Manufacturing Organisation (Send task "Notify MES of production start")
    → Manufacturing Execution System (MES) (production start signal)
  Manufacturing Execution System (MES) → Manufacturing Organisation
    (Manufacturing Operations lane, Service task "Retrieve work order
    and shop-floor instructions from MES") (work order and routing
    instructions)
  Manufacturing Organisation (User task "Record step completion in MES")
    → Manufacturing Execution System (MES) (step completion records)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Send task "Send completed batch
    notification to MES") → Manufacturing Execution System (MES)
    (batch completion confirmation)
  Manufacturing Organisation (Send task "Dispatch job pack to Contract
    Manufacturer") → Contract Manufacturer (job pack and specifications)
  Contract Manufacturer → Manufacturing Organisation (Intermediate
    message catch event "Production confirmation received from Contract
    Manufacturer") (production confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Work Order" — read by User task "Retrieve work order and
  shop-floor instructions from MES"; read by User task "Execute
  production step per routing".
Data Object "Shop-Floor Instructions" — read by User task "Set up
  machines and tooling"; read by User task "Execute production step
  per routing".
Data Object "In-Process Check Record" — written by User task "Perform
  in-process checks"; read by Exclusive gateway "In-process check
  passed?".
Data Object "Batch Production Record" — written by User task "Complete
  batch and record output quantities in MES"; read by Send task "Send
  completed batch notification to MES".
Data Object "Job Pack" — written by Send task "Dispatch job pack to
  Contract Manufacturer"; read by Intermediate message catch event
  "Production confirmation received from Contract Manufacturer".
Data Object "Maintenance Report" — written by User task "Perform
  corrective maintenance"; read by Send task "Confirm equipment restored
  to Manufacturing Operations".

This subprocess covers the full shop-floor execution of a production
order, from retrieving MES instructions and setting up equipment through
iterative step execution and in-process checking to finalising the batch.
It handles both internal manufacture and contract-manufacturer
co-ordination, and routes equipment deviations to Maintenance before
closing the batch. The completed batch record and output quantities are
handed to Inspect Quality for conformance verification.
```

### V05.08 — Inspect Quality

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.08 Inspect Quality — the quality assurance gate that
verifies manufactured output against specifications before production
output is recorded.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the organisation running the
inspection process, with lanes for Quality Assurance and Manufacturing
Operations.
Pool "Quality Management System (QMS)" — IT system that records
inspection criteria, results, and non-conformance reports.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Quality Management System (QMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom:
   Quality Assurance, Manufacturing Operations)
2. Quality Management System (QMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Quality Assurance lane:
  Message start event "Manufactured batch received from Manufacture
  Product"
  Service task "Retrieve quality specifications and inspection plan"
  User task "Perform incoming inspection of manufactured batch"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection result?"
    - branch "Pass": Service task "Record inspection pass in QMS"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection result")
    - branch "Fail — minor non-conformance": User task "Raise
      non-conformance report"
      Service task "Log non-conformance in QMS"
      Exclusive gateway "Disposition decision?"
        - branch "Rework authorised": Send task "Issue rework
          instruction to Manufacturing Operations"
          Intermediate message catch event "Rework complete
          confirmation received"
          User task "Re-inspect reworked batch"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition decision")
        - branch "Reject batch": User task "Approve batch rejection"
          Service task "Record batch rejection in QMS"
          End event "Batch rejected — escalated to Manage Exceptions"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Disposition decision"
      Service task "Record disposition outcome in QMS"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection result")
    - branch "Fail — critical non-conformance": User task "Approve
      batch quarantine"
      Service task "Record quarantine and critical non-conformance
      in QMS"
      End event "Critical non-conformance — escalated to Manage
      Exceptions"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection result"
  User task "Release batch and sign off inspection record"
  Service task "Update QMS with batch release status"
  End event "Batch released — ready for Record Production Output"

Manufacturing Operations lane:
  User task "Receive rework instruction from Quality Assurance"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Rework Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Execute rework on batch",
    User task "Confirm rework steps completed"
  Send task "Send rework complete confirmation to Quality Assurance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Rework Complete", labelled "Rework deadline exceeded", triggering
End event "Rework timed out — escalated to Manage Exceptions" in the
Manufacturing Operations lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Quality Assurance lane with the
message start event, proceeds through inspection and the three-branch
exclusive gateway "Inspection result?". The pass branch and the
minor-fail disposition branch rejoin at exclusive merge gateway
"Inspection result" and continue to batch release and the end event.
The minor-fail branch first resolves through exclusive gateway
"Disposition decision?" whose rework branch loops via Manufacturing
Operations and returns on rework confirmation, rejoining at exclusive
merge gateway "Disposition decision" before continuing to merge gateway
"Inspection result". The reject and critical branches each end at their
own end events without rejoining. The Manufacturing Operations lane
receives the rework instruction, executes the standard-loop subprocess,
and sends the confirmation back to the Quality Assurance lane.

Message flows:
Quality Management System (QMS) → Quality Assurance lane, "Retrieve
quality specifications and inspection plan" (inspection criteria and
test plan).
Quality Assurance lane, "Record inspection pass in QMS" → Quality
Management System (QMS) (inspection pass result).
Quality Assurance lane, "Log non-conformance in QMS" → Quality
Management System (QMS) (non-conformance report).
Quality Assurance lane, "Record batch rejection in QMS" → Quality
Management System (QMS) (batch rejection record).
Quality Assurance lane, "Record quarantine and critical non-conformance
in QMS" → Quality Management System (QMS) (quarantine and critical
non-conformance record).
Quality Assurance lane, "Record disposition outcome in QMS" → Quality
Management System (QMS) (disposition outcome).
Quality Assurance lane, "Update QMS with batch release status" →
Quality Management System (QMS) (batch release confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inspection Plan" — read by "Retrieve quality
specifications and inspection plan"; written by "Retrieve quality
specifications and inspection plan".
Data Object "Inspection Record" — written by "Perform incoming
inspection of manufactured batch"; read by "Release batch and sign off
inspection record".
Data Object "Non-Conformance Report" — written by "Raise
non-conformance report"; read by "Approve batch rejection" and "Approve
batch quarantine".
Data Object "Rework Instruction" — written by "Issue rework instruction
to Manufacturing Operations"; read by "Receive rework instruction from
Quality Assurance".
Data Object "Batch Release Record" — written by "Release batch and sign
off inspection record"; read by "Update QMS with batch release status".

This subprocess verifies that every manufactured batch meets the
organisation's quality specifications before it progresses further in
the production value chain. Passed and reworked batches are formally
released with a signed inspection record, while batches with critical
or unresolvable non-conformances are quarantined and escalated. The
released batch record and any open non-conformance items are handed to
Record Production Output and, where exceptions persist, to Manage
Exceptions.
```

### V05.09 — Manage Exceptions

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.09 Manage Exceptions — handles deviation, breakdown, and
non-conformance events that arise during production execution, sitting
between Inspect Quality and Record Production Output in the Plan to
Produce value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the internal teams that detect,
escalate, resolve, and close production exceptions.
  Lane "Manufacturing Operations" — production supervisor who logs
  exceptions and coordinates resolution.
  Lane "Maintenance" — maintenance technician who responds to equipment
  breakdowns and performs repairs.
  Lane "Quality Assurance" — quality inspector who dispositions
  non-conforming material and raises corrective actions.

Pool "Supplier" — external supplier who provides replacement or
substitute materials.
Pool "Contract Manufacturer" — external contract manufacturer who
receives rework or overflow instructions.
Pool "Maintenance Management System (CMMS)" — records work orders,
breakdown events, and maintenance resolutions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Manufacturer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Maintenance Management System (CMMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Contract Manufacturer
3. Manufacturing Organisation
4. Maintenance Management System (CMMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Manufacturing Operations lane:
  Message start event "Quality non-conformance or production exception
  received from Inspect Quality"
  User task "Log exception details and classify exception type"
  Exclusive gateway "Exception type?"
  - branch "Equipment breakdown": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Exception type resolved")
  - branch "Material non-conformance": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "Exception type resolved")
  - branch "Process deviation": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Exception type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exception type resolved"
  User task "Confirm resolution and update exception record"
  Exclusive gateway "Production can continue?"
  - branch "Yes": End event "Exception resolved — ready for Record
    Production Output"
  - branch "No — escalate": User task "Escalate exception to plant
    manager and notify stakeholders"
    End event "Exception escalated and production halted"

Maintenance lane:
  User task "Receive breakdown notification and assess equipment fault"
  Service task "Log breakdown work order in CMMS"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repair Until Equipment Cleared" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Perform repair or preventive
    action", User task "Test equipment and verify restoration"
  Intermediate message catch event "Clearance confirmation received"
  User task "Close work order and record maintenance outcome in CMMS"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type resolved")

Quality Assurance lane:
  User task "Review non-conforming material and apply disposition
  decision"
  Exclusive gateway "Disposition decision?"
  - branch "Rework": Send task "Issue rework instruction to Contract
    Manufacturer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Rework completion confirmed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition complete")
  - branch "Return to Supplier": Send task "Issue return notice to
    Supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Replacement material confirmed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition complete")
  - branch "Scrap": User task "Authorise scrap and record quantity"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Disposition complete"
  User task "Raise corrective action report"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception type resolved")

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repair Until
Equipment Cleared" — label "Repair deadline exceeded (shift limit)" —
flow continues to User task "Escalate exception to plant manager and
notify stakeholders" in the Manufacturing Operations lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Manufacturing Operations lane where
the exception is logged and classified; the Equipment breakdown branch
routes to the Maintenance lane, the Material non-conformance branch
routes to the Quality Assurance lane, and the Process deviation branch
is handled within Manufacturing Operations; all three branches rejoin
at the exclusive merge gateway "Exception type resolved" in
Manufacturing Operations, continuing to confirmation and the production
continuity gateway, whose Yes branch ends the subprocess and whose No
branch escalates and ends at a separate end event.

Message flows:
  Maintenance Management System (CMMS) → Maintenance lane "Breakdown
  work order created and stored"
  Maintenance lane → Maintenance Management System (CMMS) "Work order
  closure and maintenance outcome posted"
  Quality Assurance lane → Contract Manufacturer "Rework instruction"
  Contract Manufacturer → Quality Assurance lane "Rework completion
  confirmation"
  Quality Assurance lane → Supplier "Return and replacement notice"
  Supplier → Quality Assurance lane "Replacement material confirmation"

7. Data objects

Data Object "Exception Log" — written by User task "Log exception
details and classify exception type"; read by User task "Confirm
resolution and update exception record".
Data Object "Breakdown Work Order" — written by Service task "Log
breakdown work order in CMMS"; read by User task "Close work order and
record maintenance outcome in CMMS".
Data Object "Disposition Decision Record" — written by User task
"Review non-conforming material and apply disposition decision"; read
by User task "Raise corrective action report".
Data Object "Corrective Action Report" — written by User task "Raise
corrective action report"; read by User task "Confirm resolution and
update exception record".

Manage Exceptions detects and classifies production deviations —
equipment breakdowns, material non-conformances, and process
departures — and drives each to a documented resolution through
coordinated action across Maintenance, Quality Assurance, and
Manufacturing Operations. Resolved exceptions, corrective action
reports, and updated work records are handed forward to Record
Production Output, which captures the final quantities and costs
against the production order.
```

### V05.10 — Record Production Output

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V05.10 Record Production Output — captures confirmed production
quantities, costs, and consumption data and hands a closed production
record to Close Production Orders.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — the organisation running the process,
  with lanes for Manufacturing Operations and Finance.
Pool "Manufacturing Execution System (MES)" — shop-floor execution system
  that holds work-order confirmations and production actuals.
Pool "ERP Manufacturing Module" — enterprise system that receives cost
  postings and production confirmations (referenced here for completeness
  but primary in V05.12; included because Finance posts cost data to it).

2. Pool properties

Pool "Manufacturing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Manufacturing Execution System (MES)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "ERP Manufacturing Module" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Manufacturing Execution System (MES)
2. Manufacturing Organisation
3. ERP Manufacturing Module

4. Lane contents in flow order (Manufacturing Organisation)

Manufacturing Operations lane:
  Message start event "Production completion confirmed — received from
    Manufacture Product"
  User task "Review work-order completion data"
  Service task "Retrieve production actuals from MES"
  User task "Verify quantities produced against work order"
  Exclusive gateway "Quantities match work order?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quantities
        Verified")
    - branch "No — variance found":
        User task "Investigate and resolve production variance"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quantities Verified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quantities Verified"
  User task "Confirm material consumption against bill of materials"
  Exclusive gateway "Consumption data complete?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Consumption
        Data Confirmed")
    - branch "No — data missing":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Consumption Data Complete"
          (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Request
          missing consumption data from shop floor", Intermediate
          message catch event "Consumption data received"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Consumption Data
          Confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Consumption Data Confirmed"
  User task "Record batch and lot traceability data"
  User task "Post production confirmation to MES"
  Send task "Send production output record to Finance"

Finance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Production output record received"
  User task "Review production actuals for cost posting"
  User task "Post labour, material, and overhead costs"
  Service task "Send cost posting to ERP Manufacturing Module"
  User task "Confirm production order cost settlement"
  End event "Production output recorded and costs posted — ready for
    Close Production Orders"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Consumption Data Complete" — label "48-hour data deadline exceeded" —
  flow continues to End event "Production output incomplete — escalated
  to exception handling".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Manufacturing Operations lane with the
  message start event, proceeds through work-order review, MES data
  retrieval, and quantity verification, with the exclusive gateway
  branching to variance investigation or directly to the merge; after the
  merge, material consumption confirmation follows, with its own exclusive
  gateway branching to the loop subprocess or directly to the second
  merge; after the second merge, batch traceability recording, MES
  confirmation posting, and send task complete the Manufacturing
  Operations lane; a send task passes the output record to the Finance
  lane, where cost review, cost posting, ERP submission, and settlement
  confirmation lead to the end event.
Message flows:
  Manufacturing Execution System (MES) → Manufacturing Operations lane,
    Service task "Retrieve production actuals from MES" (production
    actuals, work-order completion data).
  Manufacturing Operations lane, User task "Post production confirmation
    to MES" → Manufacturing Execution System (MES) (confirmed production
    quantities and traceability data).
  Finance lane, Service task "Send cost posting to ERP Manufacturing
    Module" → ERP Manufacturing Module (labour, material, and overhead
    cost postings).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Work Order Completion Record" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve production actuals from MES"; read by User task "Verify
  quantities produced against work order".
Data Object "Production Variance Report" — written by User task
  "Investigate and resolve production variance"; read by User task
  "Confirm material consumption against bill of materials".
Data Object "Material Consumption Record" — written by User task "Confirm
  material consumption against bill of materials"; read by User task
  "Record batch and lot traceability data".
Data Object "Batch and Lot Traceability Record" — written by User task
  "Record batch and lot traceability data"; read by User task "Post
  production confirmation to MES".
Data Object "Production Output Record" — written by Send task "Send
  production output record to Finance"; read by User task "Review
  production actuals for cost posting".
Data Object "Cost Posting Document" — written by User task "Post labour,
  material, and overhead costs"; read by Service task "Send cost posting
  to ERP Manufacturing Module".

Record Production Output collects confirmed quantities, material
consumption, and batch traceability from the shop floor, resolves any
variances, and posts a full production confirmation to the MES. Finance
then settles all associated labour, material, and overhead costs against
the ERP Manufacturing Module, producing a fully costed and traceable
production output record that is handed to Close Production Orders for
final order settlement and financial closure.
```

```text
  actual production costs from ERP" (actual material, labour,
  and overhead cost data).
Finance lane, Service task "Post cost variance entries to ERP"
  → ERP Manufacturing Module (variance journal entries and
  cost postings).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Open Production Order List" — read by "Review open
  production orders for closure" / written by "Set production
  order status to closed in ERP".
Data Object "Production Order Completion Record" — written by
  "Verify production order quantities and completions" / read by
  "Confirm work order closure to Finance".
Data Object "Actual vs Standard Cost Report" — written by
  "Compare actual costs to standard costs" / read by
  "Investigate and document cost variance".
Data Object "Cost Variance Analysis" — written by "Revise
  variance analysis" / read by "Post cost variance entries
  to ERP".
Data Object "Production Order Close-out Report" — written by
  "Generate production order close-out report".

Close Production Orders reconciles all open work orders against
confirmed output quantities, resolves any discrepancies, and
triggers a full cost-variance analysis in Finance. Actual
production costs are compared to standard costs, variances are
investigated and documented within period-end constraints, and
journal entries are posted to the ERP. The subprocess delivers
closed work orders, reconciled financial records, and a
close-out report, bringing the Plan to Produce value chain to
a controlled and auditable conclusion.
```

## V06 — Idea to Market

**Teams and roles involved.**
Idea to Market involves Strategy, Product Management, Research and Development, Innovation, Marketing, Sales, Customer Experience, Engineering, Finance, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Operations, and sometimes external partners. Key roles include product manager, product owner, innovation lead, business analyst, designer, engineer, market researcher, compliance adviser, pricing analyst, and launch manager.

**External participants.**
External participants may include Customers, Inventors, Research Partners, Design Partners, Regulators, Beta Users, Distributors, or Investors. The process may be initiated by a market opportunity, customer need, internal idea, invention, regulatory change, or competitive pressure.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: identify opportunity, capture ideas, assess feasibility, define business case, design solution, develop prototype, test with users, validate commercial model, prepare launch, release to market, monitor adoption, and refine product/service.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include idea management platform, product lifecycle management system, project portfolio management system, CRM, market research tools, design/prototyping tools, requirements management tools, collaboration tools, document management, analytics/BI, and marketing automation.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include innovation governance, product development methodology, business case approval procedure, intellectual property policy, customer research policy, privacy policy, regulatory compliance procedure, product safety policy, pricing policy, launch readiness checklist, and change control procedure.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Customers and market participants provide needs, feedback, complaints, survey responses, test results, buying signals, and usage data. Inventors or partners provide concepts, prototypes, technical details, or research findings. The process provides concept descriptions, prototypes, trial invitations, product information, launch communications, and post-launch updates.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process records ideas, opportunity assessments, requirements, designs, business cases, approvals, test results, launch plans, product data, pricing data, campaign assets, and performance metrics. Systems provide market insights, customer data, portfolio status, development progress, risk/compliance status, and launch performance reporting.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V06 - Idea to Market (I2M)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V06.01. Identify Opportunity
V06.02. Capture Ideas
V06.03. Assess Feasibility
V06.04. Define Business Case
V06.05. Design Solution
V06.06. Develop Prototype
V06.07. Test with Users
V06.08. Validate Commercial Model
V06.09. Prepare Launch
V06.10. Release to Market
V06.11. Monitor Adoption
V06.12. Refine Product / Service

This is the innovation and commercialisation end-to-end process: a market
opportunity, customer need or internal idea flows through feasibility, a
business case, design, prototyping, user testing and commercial validation,
into launch, release, adoption monitoring and refinement. The main external
participant is the Customer; the process may be triggered by a market
opportunity, a customer need or an internal idea, and the external
interaction begins when concept descriptions, trial invitations and launch
communications reach the market.
```

### V06.01 — Identify Opportunity

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.01 Identify Opportunity — first subprocess of the Idea to Market
value chain, in which the organisation scans its environment, collects market
signals, and confirms a validated opportunity ready for idea capture.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the internal teams that run the process.
  Lane "Strategy" — market researcher who scans for and interprets signals.
  Lane "Product Management" — product manager who evaluates and confirms the
    opportunity.
Pool "Customer" — external customers who provide needs, feedback, and
  market signals.
Pool "Market Research Tools" — IT system that stores market insights and
  surfaces customer data for analysis.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Product Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Market Research Tools" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Product Organisation
3. Market Research Tools

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Strategy lane:
  Message start event "Market signal or customer need received from Customer"
  User task "Gather and document market signals"
  Service task "Retrieve market insights from Market Research Tools"
  User task "Analyse market trends and competitive landscape"
  User task "Identify and describe candidate opportunities"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient data to assess opportunity?"
  - branch "No — data gaps remain":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Data Is Sufficient" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Request additional market research",
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional data received from Market
        Research Tools", User task "Supplement opportunity description"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient data to assess
        opportunity")
  - branch "Yes — data is adequate":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient data to assess
        opportunity")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient data to assess opportunity"
  User task "Draft opportunity statement"
  Service task "Record opportunity statement in Market Research Tools"

Product Management lane:
  User task "Review opportunity statement"
  Exclusive gateway "Opportunity validated?"
  - branch "No — return for rework":
      User task "Document reasons for rejection and guidance"
      End event "Opportunity rejected — process closed"
  - branch "Yes — opportunity confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity validated")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity validated"
  User task "Prioritise and endorse validated opportunity"
  End event "Validated opportunity confirmed — ready for Capture Ideas"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Data
  Is Sufficient" — label "Research deadline exceeded" — triggers End event
  "Opportunity closed — insufficient data obtained".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Strategy lane with the message start
  event, proceeds through signal gathering, system retrieval, analysis, and
  opportunity description, then reaches the "Sufficient data" gateway; the
  "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess before rejoining the merge
  gateway, while the "Yes" branch rejoins directly; flow continues to the
  draft and record steps, then crosses to the Product Management lane for
  review and the "Opportunity validated" gateway; the "No" branch ends at
  the rejection end event while the "Yes" branch rejoins the merge gateway
  and proceeds to prioritisation and the final end event.

Message flows:
  Customer → Strategy lane, message start event (market signals, customer
    needs, feedback)
  Strategy lane, Service task "Retrieve market insights from Market Research
    Tools" → Market Research Tools (query for market and customer data)
  Market Research Tools → Strategy lane, Service task "Retrieve market
    insights from Market Research Tools" (market insights and customer data)
  Strategy lane, Service task "Record opportunity statement in Market
    Research Tools" → Market Research Tools (opportunity statement record)
  Market Research Tools → Strategy lane, Intermediate message catch event
    "Additional data received from Market Research Tools" (supplementary
    research data)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Market Signal Log" — written by User task "Gather and document
  market signals"; read by User task "Analyse market trends and competitive
  landscape".
Data Object "Opportunity Statement" — written by User task "Draft opportunity
  statement"; read by User task "Review opportunity statement".
Data Object "Validation Decision" — written by User task "Document reasons
  for rejection and guidance"; read by End event "Opportunity rejected —
  process closed". Also written by User task "Prioritise and endorse
  validated opportunity"; read by End event "Validated opportunity confirmed
  — ready for Capture Ideas".

This subprocess establishes a confirmed, prioritised opportunity statement
grounded in market signals, customer needs, and competitive analysis. The
Strategy lane provides the evidence base and the Product Management lane
applies commercial judgement to endorse or reject it. A validated opportunity
statement is handed to Capture Ideas, where the Innovation and Product
Management teams will solicit and log ideas that respond to the confirmed
opportunity.
```

```text
BPMN: V06.02 Capture Ideas — second subprocess in the Idea to Market
value chain, receiving identified opportunities and collecting ideas from

1. Pools & Lanes

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Research / Design Partner
3. Product Organisation
4. Idea Management Platform

Message start event "Opportunity identified — received from Identify

User task "Open idea submission campaign"

- branch "No — all ideas rejected": User task "Document rejection

User task "Prepare idea shortlist for feasibility assessment"

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Innovation lane with the message

Message flows:

Customer → Innovation lane, Intermediate message catch event "Ideas

Research / Design Partner → Innovation lane, Intermediate message catch

Innovation lane, Send task "Invite customers and partners to submit

Innovation lane, Send task "Invite customers and partners to submit

Innovation lane, Send task "Send additional call for ideas to customers

Idea Management Platform → Product Management lane, Service task

Product Management lane, Send task "Notify submitters of outcome" →

Product Management lane, Send task "Notify submitters of outcome" →

7. Data objects

Data Object "Idea Submission" — written by User task "Collect and log
internal ideas"; written by User task "Log and categorise additional
ideas"; read by User task "Review and categorise submitted ideas".
Data Object "Idea Long-list" — written by User task "Consolidate idea
long-list"; read by User task "Screen ideas against strategic criteria".
Data Object "Idea Shortlist" — written by User task "Prepare idea
shortlist for feasibility assessment"; read by End event "Idea shortlist
confirmed — ready for Assess Feasibility".
Data Object "Rejection Rationale" — written by User task "Document
rejection rationale"; read by Send task "Notify submitters of outcome".

V06.02 Capture Ideas opens a structured submission campaign, draws ideas
from customers, research and design partners, and internal staff, and
logs everything in the Idea Management Platform. The Product Management
team screens and prioritises the resulting pool against strategic
criteria, producing a ranked shortlist. That shortlist is handed to
V06.03 Assess Feasibility, where each viable idea is evaluated for
technical and commercial viability.
```

### V06.03 — Assess Feasibility

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.03 Assess Feasibility — third subprocess in the Idea to
Market value chain, receiving captured ideas from Capture Ideas and
handing a feasibility outcome to Define Business Case.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out feasibility
assessment.
  Lane "Research and Development" — engineer leads technical evaluation.
  Lane "Product Management" — business analyst coordinates assessment
  and makes the go/no-go recommendation.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — external partner providing specialist
input into feasibility analysis.
Pool "Collaboration Tools" — platform used to record assessments,
share findings, and track tasks.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Product Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Collaboration Tools" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Research / Design Partner
2. Product Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom:
   Research and Development, Product Management)
3. Collaboration Tools

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Research and Development lane:
  Message start event "Captured idea received from Capture Ideas"
  User task "Review idea and scope technical evaluation"
  Service task "Log feasibility study in Collaboration Tools"
  User task "Conduct technical feasibility analysis"
  User task "Engage Research / Design Partner for specialist input"
  Intermediate message catch event "Partner specialist input received"
  User task "Consolidate technical findings"
  User task "Document technical feasibility outcome"
  Send task "Share technical findings with Product Management"

Product Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Technical findings received"
  User task "Review technical findings and assess business feasibility"
  User task "Assess strategic fit and resource requirements"
  Exclusive gateway "Feasibility assessment complete?"
  - branch "Information gaps remain": Expanded Subprocess
    "Repeat Until Assessment Complete" (standard loop) containing,
    in order: User task "Identify missing information",
    Send task "Request additional input from Research and Development",
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional findings received",
    User task "Update feasibility assessment"
    (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Assessment complete": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "Feasibility assessment complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Feasibility assessment complete"
  Service task "Record completed assessment in Collaboration Tools"
  Exclusive gateway "Feasibility outcome?"
  - branch "Not feasible": User task "Document rationale and
    close idea"
    End event "Idea closed — no further action"
  - branch "Feasible": User task "Prepare feasibility summary
    for business case"
    Service task "Submit feasibility summary to Collaboration Tools"
    End event "Feasibility confirmed — ready for Define Business Case"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Assessment Complete" — label "Assessment overdue (10 business days)" —
triggers Send task "Escalate assessment delay to Product Management
lead", then End event "Assessment escalated — process paused".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in Research and Development with the message
start event and proceeds through technical scoping, logging, analysis,
partner engagement, and consolidation before passing findings to Product
Management via a send task. Product Management receives findings, reviews
them, and enters the feasibility-complete gateway; the loop branch
re-enters Research and Development for additional input before rejoining
at the exclusive merge gateway; the outcome gateway then branches to
either closure or summary preparation, each ending at its own end event.

Message flows:
Research / Design Partner → User task "Engage Research / Design Partner
for specialist input" (specialist feasibility input requested).
Intermediate message catch event "Partner specialist input received" ←
Research / Design Partner (specialist findings and technical data).
Service task "Log feasibility study in Collaboration Tools" →
Collaboration Tools (new feasibility study record).
Service task "Record completed assessment in Collaboration Tools" →
Collaboration Tools (completed assessment details).
Service task "Submit feasibility summary to Collaboration Tools" →
Collaboration Tools (feasibility summary document).
Collaboration Tools → User task "Review idea and scope technical
evaluation" (captured idea details and prior assessment context).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Feasibility Study Record" — written by User task "Review
idea and scope technical evaluation"; read by User task "Conduct
technical feasibility analysis".
Data Object "Technical Feasibility Findings" — written by User task
"Document technical feasibility outcome"; read by User task "Review
technical findings and assess business feasibility".
Data Object "Feasibility Summary" — written by User task "Prepare
feasibility summary for business case"; read by Service task "Submit
feasibility summary to Collaboration Tools".

Assess Feasibility takes the captured idea handed over by Capture Ideas,
subjects it to technical analysis by Research and Development — drawing
on specialist input from the Research / Design Partner — and then has
Product Management weigh strategic fit and resource viability. Ideas that
do not clear the feasibility bar are closed with documented rationale;
those that do are packaged as a feasibility summary and passed to Define
Business Case, where the commercial and financial case is built out.
```

### V06.04 — Define Business Case

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.04 Define Business Case — fourth subprocess in the Idea to
Market value chain, converting a feasibility-assessed concept into a
structured business case approved for solution design.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the internal teams that define, price,
and approve the business case.
  Lane "Product Management" — product manager leads business case
  definition and coordinates approval.
  Lane "Finance" — pricing analyst develops financial model and
  validates assumptions.
Pool "Investor" — external party that reviews and endorses investment
decisions.
Pool "Project Portfolio Management System" — IT system that records
business cases, tracks approval status, and provides portfolio data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Product Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Investor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Project Portfolio Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Investor
2. Product Organisation
3. Project Portfolio Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Product Management lane:
  Message start event "Feasibility assessment received from Assess
  Feasibility"
  User task "Define business case scope and objectives"
  User task "Document market opportunity and strategic fit"
  Service task "Retrieve portfolio status from Project Portfolio
  Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient market data available?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
    market data available")
  - branch "No": User task "Commission supplementary market research"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient market data
    available")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient market data available"
  User task "Hand financial assumptions to Finance"

Finance lane:
  User task "Develop financial model and pricing scenarios"
  User task "Validate cost, revenue, and margin assumptions"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Financial Model Accepted" (standard
  loop) containing, in order: User task "Revise financial model",
  User task "Revalidate assumptions"
  User task "Produce investment summary"
  Service task "Record financial model in Project Portfolio Management
  System"

Product Management lane:
  User task "Compile full business case document"
  User task "Submit business case for internal governance review"
  Exclusive gateway "Internal governance approved?"
  - branch "No — rework required": User task "Revise business case
    to address feedback" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Internal governance approved")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Internal
    governance approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Internal governance approved"
  Send task "Send business case to Investor for endorsement"
  Intermediate message catch event "Investor endorsement received"
  Exclusive gateway "Investor endorsement granted?"
  - branch "Endorsed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Investor
    endorsement granted")
  - branch "Not endorsed — revision requested": User task "Revise
    business case in response to Investor feedback" (continues to
    exclusive merge gateway "Investor endorsement granted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Investor endorsement granted"
  Service task "Record approved business case in Project Portfolio
  Management System"
  End event "Business case approved — ready for Design Solution"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
Until Financial Model Accepted" — label "Financial modelling deadline
exceeded" — triggers End event "Business case withdrawn — financial
model could not be finalised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Product Management lane with the
message start event, proceeds through scope definition and market
documentation, retrieves portfolio data, then branches at the market
data gateway before merging and handing off to Finance. Finance
develops, validates, and loops on the financial model until accepted,
then produces the investment summary and records it, before returning
to Product Management to compile and submit the business case.
The internal governance gateway branches to rework or continues; both
rejoin at the internal governance merge gateway. The send task
dispatches the business case to Investor, the process waits at the
message catch event, then the endorsement gateway branches to revision
or continues; both rejoin at the endorsement merge gateway. The flow
concludes with recording the approved business case and the end event.

Message flows:
Product Management "Send business case to Investor for endorsement"
  → Investor (business case document for endorsement).
Investor → Product Management "Investor endorsement received"
  (endorsement decision and conditions).
Product Organisation "Retrieve portfolio status from Project Portfolio
  Management System" → Project Portfolio Management System (portfolio
  status request).
Project Portfolio Management System → Product Organisation "Retrieve
  portfolio status from Project Portfolio Management System" (portfolio
  status and capacity data).
Finance "Record financial model in Project Portfolio Management System"
  → Project Portfolio Management System (financial model and pricing
  scenarios).
Product Management "Record approved business case in Project Portfolio
  Management System" → Project Portfolio Management System (approved
  business case record).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Case Document" — written by User task "Compile
full business case document"; read by User task "Submit business case
for internal governance review"; read by Send task "Send business case
to Investor for endorsement".
Data Object "Financial Model" — written by User task "Develop financial
model and pricing scenarios"; read by User task "Validate cost, revenue,
and margin assumptions"; read by User task "Produce investment summary".
Data Object "Market Opportunity Assessment" — written by User task
"Document market opportunity and strategic fit"; read by User task
"Compile full business case document".
Data Object "Investor Endorsement Decision" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Investor endorsement received"; read by Exclusive
gateway "Investor endorsement granted?".

Define Business Case translates the approved feasibility assessment into
a fully costed, governance-reviewed, and investor-endorsed business case.
It produces a formally recorded business case document that confirms
strategic fit, financial viability, and investment commitment. This
approved artefact is handed to Design Solution, which uses it as the
authoritative brief for defining the solution architecture and
requirements.
```

### V06.05 — Design Solution

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.05 Design Solution — the subprocess in which Research and
Development and Engineering translate an approved business case into a
validated solution design, working with a Research / Design Partner and
supported by Design / Prototyping Tools.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the organisation running the Design Solution
process, containing the teams directly involved.
  Lane "Research and Development" — led by the designer; owns
    conceptual design, design review, and iteration.
  Lane "Engineering" — led by the engineer; owns technical
    architecture, feasibility confirmation, and design
    specification sign-off.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — external design or research partner
  who co-creates and reviews design artefacts.
Pool "Design / Prototyping Tools" — the design and prototyping platform
  that stores, versions, and renders design assets.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Product Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Design / Prototyping Tools" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Research / Design Partner
2. Product Organisation
3. Design / Prototyping Tools

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Research and Development lane:
  Message start event "Approved business case received from Define
    Business Case"
  User task "Review business case and define design brief"
  Send task "Share design brief with Research / Design Partner"
  Intermediate message catch event "Partner design input received"
  User task "Develop initial solution concepts"
  Service task "Upload initial concepts to Design / Prototyping Tools"
  Intermediate message catch event "Concepts stored and versioned
    confirmed"
  User task "Facilitate design workshop with Engineering and Partner"
  Exclusive gateway "Concept direction agreed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Concept direction agreed")
  - branch "No": User task "Revise concepts based on workshop feedback"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Concept direction agreed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Concept direction agreed"
  User task "Produce detailed design artefacts"
  Service task "Publish design artefacts to Design / Prototyping Tools"
  Intermediate message catch event "Artefacts published and accessible
    confirmed"
  User task "Conduct design review"
  Exclusive gateway "Design review passed?"
  - branch "No — rework required": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Design Review Passed" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Revise design artefacts",
      Service task "Update design artefacts in Design / Prototyping
        Tools",
      User task "Conduct design review"
      (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Design review passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Design review passed"
  User task "Document design rationale and decisions"

Engineering lane:
  User task "Assess technical feasibility of solution concepts"
  Send task "Provide feasibility input to design workshop"
  User task "Define technical architecture"
  Service task "Record technical architecture in Design / Prototyping
    Tools"
  User task "Review detailed design artefacts for engineering
    completeness"
  User task "Sign off design specification"
  End event "Validated solution design complete — ready for Develop
    Prototype"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Design Review Passed", labelled "Review cycle limit reached",
  leading to End event "Design escalated — review cycle limit
  exceeded".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Research and Development lane with
the message start event and proceeds through brief definition, partner
engagement, concept development, and upload to tooling. After the
intermediate message catch event confirming storage, flow moves to the
design workshop task. The "Concept direction agreed?" gateway branches
to a revision task or directly to the merge; both paths rejoin at the
merge before detailed artefact production. After publication and the
tooling confirmation event, the design review gateway branches to the
loop subprocess on the "No" branch and directly to the merge on the
"Yes" branch; both rejoin at the "Design review passed" merge. Final
documentation of design rationale concludes the Research and
Development lane. Engineering lane tasks interleave: feasibility
assessment and workshop input feed the shared workshop task in Research
and Development; technical architecture recording and artefact review
follow the publication step; sign-off concludes in the Engineering lane
at the end event.

Message flows:
  Research and Development (Send task "Share design brief") →
    Research / Design Partner (design brief)
  Research / Design Partner → Research and Development (Intermediate
    message catch event "Partner design input received")
    (design input and co-design materials)
  Research and Development (Service task "Upload initial concepts") →
    Design / Prototyping Tools (initial concept assets)
  Design / Prototyping Tools → Research and Development (Intermediate
    message catch event "Concepts stored and versioned confirmed")
    (storage confirmation)
  Research and Development (Service task "Publish design artefacts") →
    Design / Prototyping Tools (detailed design artefacts)
  Design / Prototyping Tools → Research and Development (Intermediate
    message catch event "Artefacts published and accessible confirmed")
    (publication confirmation)
  Engineering (Service task "Record technical architecture") →
    Design / Prototyping Tools (technical architecture records)
  Engineering (Service task "Update design artefacts in Design /
    Prototyping Tools") → Design / Prototyping Tools
    (revised artefact versions)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Design Brief" — written by User task "Review business case
  and define design brief"; read by Send task "Share design brief with
  Research / Design Partner" and User task "Develop initial solution
  concepts".
Data Object "Solution Concepts" — written by User task "Develop initial
  solution concepts"; read by User task "Facilitate design workshop
  with Engineering and Partner" and User task "Assess technical
  feasibility of solution concepts".
Data Object "Detailed Design Artefacts" — written by User task "Produce
  detailed design artefacts"; read by User task "Review detailed design
  artefacts for engineering completeness" and User task "Conduct design
  review".
Data Object "Technical Architecture" — written by User task "Define
  technical architecture"; read by User task "Review detailed design
  artefacts for engineering completeness" and User task "Sign off
  design specification".
Data Object "Design Rationale" — written by User task "Document design
  rationale and decisions"; read by End event "Validated solution
  design complete — ready for Develop Prototype".

Design Solution takes an approved business case and transforms it into
a fully specified, technically validated solution design. Working
collaboratively with the Research / Design Partner and Engineering,
the Research and Development team iterates on concepts, resolves
feasibility constraints, and publishes signed-off design artefacts
and rationale in the Design / Prototyping Tools. The subprocess hands
a complete, approved design specification to Develop Prototype, where
Engineering will build the first working version.
```

### V06.06 — Develop Prototype

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.06 Develop Prototype — the subprocess in which Engineering and
Research and Development build a working prototype from the approved solution
design, coordinating with a Research / Design Partner, and hand the prototype
to user testing.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the internal teams that develop the prototype.
  Lane "Engineering" — engineer who leads prototype build and integration work.
  Lane "Research and Development" — designer who contributes design assets and
    reviews prototype fidelity.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — external partner supplying specialist
  components, materials, or technical expertise.
Pool "Product Lifecycle Management System" — PLM system that stores design
  specifications, prototype records, and build artefacts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Product Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Research / Design Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Product Lifecycle Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Research / Design Partner
2. Product Organisation (Engineering lane above Research and Development lane)
3. Product Lifecycle Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Approved solution design received from Design Solution"
  Service task "Retrieve design specifications from PLM System"
  User task "Plan prototype build activities"
  User task "Assign components and resources"
  User task "Build prototype components"
  User task "Integrate prototype components"
  Exclusive gateway "Integration successful?"
    - branch "No — integration issues found": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
      Until Integration Issues Resolved" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Log integration defects", User task "Rework components",
      User task "Re-test integration"; then (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Integration successful?")
    - branch "Yes — integration complete": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Integration successful?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Integration successful?"
  Send task "Notify Research / Design Partner that prototype is ready for
    joint review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Partner review feedback received"
  Exclusive gateway "Partner feedback acceptable?"
    - branch "No — rework required": User task "Action partner feedback on
      prototype"; (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Partner feedback
      acceptable?")
    - branch "Yes — prototype accepted": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Partner feedback acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Partner feedback acceptable?"
  Service task "Record finalised prototype in PLM System"
  User task "Prepare prototype handover documentation"
  End event "Prototype finalised — ready for Test with Users"

Research and Development lane:
  User task "Review design specifications for prototype fidelity"
  User task "Produce design assets and reference materials"
  User task "Conduct prototype fidelity review"
  User task "Approve prototype design quality"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Integration Issues Resolved" — label "Build deadline exceeded" — triggers
  End event "Prototype build failed — escalate to Engineering lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in Engineering with retrieval of specifications,
moves through planning, build, and integration, loops internally via the
expanded subprocess until integration succeeds, then proceeds to partner
notification and the intermediate catch event awaiting feedback; the partner
feedback gateway either routes back to rework or continues to merge and
finalisation. Research and Development tasks run in parallel after design
specifications are retrieved: "Review design specifications" leads to
"Produce design assets", then "Conduct prototype fidelity review", then
"Approve prototype design quality", rejoining the Engineering flow at the
point where the finalised prototype is recorded.

Message flows:
Product Organisation (Engineering — Send task "Notify Research / Design
  Partner that prototype is ready for joint review") →
  Research / Design Partner (joint review request).
Research / Design Partner → Product Organisation (Engineering —
  Intermediate message catch event "Partner review feedback received")
  (prototype review feedback).
Product Organisation (Engineering — Service task "Retrieve design
  specifications from PLM System") →
  Product Lifecycle Management System (design specification retrieval
  request).
Product Lifecycle Management System → Product Organisation (Engineering —
  Service task "Retrieve design specifications from PLM System")
  (design specifications returned).
Product Organisation (Engineering — Service task "Record finalised prototype
  in PLM System") →
  Product Lifecycle Management System (finalised prototype record and build
  artefacts).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Design Specifications" — read by Engineering task "Retrieve
  design specifications from PLM System"; read by Research and Development
  task "Review design specifications for prototype fidelity".
Data Object "Prototype Build Plan" — written by Engineering task "Plan
  prototype build activities"; read by Engineering task "Assign components
  and resources".
Data Object "Design Assets" — written by Research and Development task
  "Produce design assets and reference materials"; read by Engineering task
  "Build prototype components".
Data Object "Integration Defect Log" — written by Expanded Subprocess task

  components".
Data Object "Partner Review Feedback" — written on receipt at Intermediate

  task "Action partner feedback on prototype".
Data Object "Prototype Handover Documentation" — written by Engineering task
  "Prepare prototype handover documentation".

Develop Prototype transforms the approved solution design into a testable,
physical or digital prototype by coordinating Engineering build work, Research
and Development design fidelity review, and external partner collaboration.
Integration issues are resolved through a structured loop, and partner
feedback is incorporated before the prototype is recorded in the Product
Lifecycle Management System. The subprocess hands a finalised, documented
prototype to Test with Users.
```

```text
  sign-off with Customer Experience"; read by Service task "Record
  sign-off in Requirements Management Tools".

Test with Users takes a prototype and its requirements baseline, runs
structured sessions with Beta Users, and consolidates feedback into a
validated set of findings. Where critical issues or coverage gaps arise,
additional testing rounds are triggered before sign-off. The confirmed
test findings and updated requirements baseline are handed to Validate
Commercial Model to underpin pricing and commercial decisions.
```

### V06.08 — Validate Commercial Model

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V06.08 Validate Commercial Model — subprocess within the Idea to
Market value chain, sitting between Test with Users and Prepare Launch.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Product Organisation" — the internal teams that validate pricing,

  Lanes (top to bottom):

  - Sales (product manager)
Pool "Customer" — external customers who provide buying signals and
  commercial feedback.

Pool "Investor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Investor
3. Product Organisation
4. CRM

4. Lane contents in flow order (Product Organisation)

Finance lane:

  User task "Review test results and commercial assumptions"

  User task "Build pricing model and revenue scenarios"
  User task "Prepare commercial model summary for investor review"

  - branch "No — revisions required":
      Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until Investor Approves" (standard loop)

        Send task "Resubmit commercial model to Investor",

      acceptable")

Sales lane:

  Intermediate message catch event "Customer buying signals and feedback
    received"
  User task "Analyse customer buying signals and willingness to pay"
  Exclusive gateway "Commercial assumptions validated?"
  - branch "No — assumptions weak":
      User task "Document gaps and recommended adjustments"

        to Finance for revision"
  - branch "Yes — assumptions confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Commercial assumptions
      validated")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Commercial assumptions validated"
  User task "Prepare sales readiness summary"
  End event "Commercial model validated — ready for Prepare Launch"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Revise Until
  Investor Approves" — label "Investor review deadline exceeded" —
  flow continues to End event "Investor approval timed out — escalate
  to product manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Finance lane on receipt of test
  results, moves through pricing model construction and investor
  engagement, including the revision loop if needed, then continues to
  finalise pricing tiers and record them in CRM. In parallel, the Sales
  lane runs customer segment identification and buying-signal collection,
  then analyses feedback at the "Commercial assumptions validated?"
  gateway; the "No" branch ends in its own escalation end event while
  the "Yes" branch merges and concludes with the sales readiness summary
  and the subprocess end event.

Message flows:
  Product Organisation (Send task "Send commercial model to Investor")
    → Investor (commercial model summary for review)

    catch event "Investor response received") (investor feedback and

  Product Organisation (Send task "Send commercial validation request

  Customer → Product Organisation (Sales lane, Intermediate message

    (buying signals, willingness-to-pay data, commercial feedback)
  CRM → Product Organisation (Finance lane, Service task "Retrieve
    customer and pipeline data from CRM") (customer data, pipeline
    status)
  Product Organisation (Service task "Record validated pricing data in
    CRM") → CRM (validated pricing tiers and discount policy)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Test Results" — read by User task "Review test results

Data Object "Commercial Assumptions" — read by User task "Review test

  pricing model and revenue scenarios".
Data Object "Pricing Model" — written by User task "Build pricing

Data Object "Commercial Model Summary" — written by User task "Prepare

Validate Commercial Model tests the product's revenue assumptions against
real investor scrutiny and customer buying behaviour. Finance builds and
iterates the pricing model until investors are satisfied, while Sales
gathers willingness-to-pay evidence from target customers. Once both
streams confirm the model is sound, validated pricing tiers are recorded
in CRM and a sales readiness summary is produced, handing a commercially
```

## V07 — Issue to Resolution

**Teams and roles involved.**
Issue to Resolution involves Customer Service, Technical Support, Service Operations, Complaints Management, Quality Assurance, Field Service, Product/Engineering, Legal, Risk, and sometimes Finance. Key roles include customer service agent, support analyst, complaints officer, case manager, service technician, product specialist, quality analyst, escalation manager, and customer experience manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Complainant, Customer, User, or Requester. The process is initiated when that participant raises an issue, complaint, defect, service request, warranty claim, incident, or query.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive issue, identify customer/user, classify issue, assess severity and entitlement, investigate, diagnose root cause, resolve or fulfil request, escalate if needed, communicate outcome, obtain confirmation, close case, and analyse trends.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, case management system, ticketing platform, customer portal, knowledge base, field service system, warranty system, product defect system, call centre/telephony platform, email management, workflow system, and analytics/BI.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include complaints handling policy, service-level agreement procedure, escalation procedure, warranty policy, refund/returns policy, privacy policy, customer communication standards, incident management procedure, root cause analysis procedure, and regulatory reporting requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer or complainant provides issue details, evidence, product/service information, impact description, contact details, and desired resolution. The process provides acknowledgement, case number, status updates, requests for further information, resolution advice, compensation/refund information, closure confirmation, and escalation outcomes.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates and updates cases, tickets, call logs, correspondence, issue categories, severity ratings, SLA timers, escalation records, knowledge articles, resolution codes, refund/credit requests, defect records, and trend reports. Systems provide customer history, product/service history, entitlement, prior issues, knowledge articles, SLA status, and reporting dashboards.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V07 - Issue to Resolution
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V07.01. Receive Issue
V07.02. Identify Customer / User
V07.03. Classify Issue
V07.04. Assess Severity & Entitlement
V07.05. Investigate
V07.06. Diagnose Root Cause
V07.07. Resolve or Fulfil Request
V07.08. Escalate if Needed
V07.09. Communicate Outcome
V07.10. Obtain Confirmation
V07.11. Close Case
V07.12. Analyse Trends

This is the customer-facing, issue-management end-to-end process: a raised
issue flows through intake, identification, classification, assessment,
investigation, diagnosis, resolution, escalation, communication,
confirmation, closure and trend analysis. The main external participant is
the Complainant / Customer / User; the process is triggered when that
participant raises an issue, complaint, defect, service request, warranty
claim, incident or query, and the external interaction begins the moment the
issue is received.
```

```text
1. Central system (process-system)
A single central process/system ellipse named "Service Company" representing
the whole organisation that runs the Issue to Resolution process. It is the
system in context: everything inside it — customer service, technical support,
service operations, complaints management, quality assurance, field service,
product / engineering, legal and risk and the supporting IT systems (CRM, case
management, ticketing, knowledge base, field service, warranty, product defect
and analytics) — is treated as one black box.

2. External entities (external-entity)
The parties OUTSIDE the company that exchange information with it, one
rectangle each:
- Complainant / Customer / User
- Field Service Partner
- Regulator

3. Layout
"Service Company" sits in the centre. The Complainant / Customer / User sits to
the LEFT (the demand side that raises the issue and receives the outcome).
Field Service Partner sits to the RIGHT (on-site fulfilment). Regulator sits to
the RIGHT (statutory reporting). The demand originates OUTSIDE the company (a
raised issue), so the customer sits on the left. Every external entity connects
directly to the central system with labelled information flows; entities never
connect to one another.

4. Information flows (each a labelled connector between an external entity and
   the central system; show both directions where information flows both ways)
- Complainant / Customer / User → Service Company: issue details, evidence,
  product / service information, impact description, contact details, desired
  resolution.
- Service Company → Complainant / Customer / User: acknowledgement, case
  number, status updates, requests for further information, resolution advice,

- Service Company → Field Service Partner: service request / work order, site
  and asset details, resolution instructions.
- Field Service Partner → Service Company: field diagnosis, completion report,
  parts used.
- Service Company → Regulator: regulatory notification / incident report.
- Regulator → Service Company: acknowledgement, directions, findings.

This Context Diagram frames the Service Company as a single system in context:
the Complainant / Customer / User raises the issue and receives the outcome, the
Field Service Partner performs on-site fulfilment, and the Regulator receives
statutory notifications and issues directions. The three external entities are
exactly the external actors of the Process Context diagram below, so the two
views stay consistent.
```

A single high-level ArchiMate view of the Issue to Resolution service area. It
shows the **Actors**, **Services**, **Processes**, **Interfaces** and

```text
ArchiMate: V07 — Issue to Resolution — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: show how the organisation provides the Issue Resolution Service and the
related services (to the Complainant / Customer / User and to the Field Service
Partner and Regulator) across the twelve V07 Issue to Resolution processes, and
the applications that support them. Lay it out in three horizontal bands, top to
bottom — BUSINESS SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS — with the
Complainant / Customer / User on the far left and the Field Service Partner /
Regulator on the far right. Read top-to-bottom as service → process →
application (ArchiMate service realisation).

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)
- Complainant / Customer / User — the external party the issue-resolution
  service is provided to (far left, the originator of every issue).
- Field Service Partner — the external party that performs on-site fulfilment
  (far right).
- Regulator — the external party that receives statutory notifications (far
  right).

2. Interfaces
- Business Interface "Customer Contact / Service Channel" — the channel the
  customer uses to raise the issue, receive updates and confirm the outcome.
  The Complainant / Customer / User ACCESSES this interface; the interface
  SERVES the business services below.
- Application Interfaces (optional, only the few the channel calls): "Portal
  API" on the Customer Portal, "Field Service API" on the Field Service System.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — the services provided, top band,
   left-to-right in resolution-journey order:
- Issue Intake Service — receive the issue and identify the customer.
- Triage & Assessment Service — classify, assess severity and entitlement.
- Investigation & Diagnosis Service — investigate and diagnose root cause.
- Resolution Service — resolve or fulfil the request.
- Escalation & Regulatory Service — escalate and notify where required.
- Customer Communication Service — communicate the outcome and obtain
  confirmation.
- Case Closure & Improvement Service — close the case and analyse trends.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — the twelve V07 processes, middle band
   in V07.01 → V07.12 order. Each REALISES the business service shown and is the
   link anchor to its BPMN diagram:
- V07.01 Receive Issue                    -> realises Issue Intake Service
- V07.02 Identify Customer / User         -> realises Issue Intake Service
- V07.03 Classify Issue                   -> realises Triage & Assessment Service
- V07.04 Assess Severity & Entitlement    -> realises Triage & Assessment Service
- V07.05 Investigate                      -> realises Investigation & Diagnosis Service
- V07.06 Diagnose Root Cause              -> realises Investigation & Diagnosis Service
- V07.07 Resolve or Fulfil Request        -> realises Resolution Service
- V07.08 Escalate if Needed               -> realises Escalation & Regulatory Service
- V07.09 Communicate Outcome              -> realises Customer Communication Service
- V07.10 Obtain Confirmation              -> realises Customer Communication Service
- V07.11 Close Case                       -> realises Case Closure & Improvement Service
- V07.12 Analyse Trends                   -> realises Case Closure & Improvement Service

5. Applications (Application Component) — the IT systems that support the
   processes, bottom band:
- Ticketing / Customer Contact Platform
- CRM System
- Case Management System
- Warranty / Entitlement System
- Knowledge Base
- Product Defect System
- Field Service System
- Workflow / Escalation System
- Email / Correspondence System
- Customer Portal
- Analytics / BI System

6. Relationships
- Complainant / Customer / User -accesses-> Customer Contact / Service Channel.
- Customer Contact / Service Channel -serving-> the Intake, Assessment,
  Communication and Confirmation services.
- Each Business Process -realisation-> its Business Service (section 4).
- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
  (serving, application -> process):
    V07.01 <- Ticketing / Customer Contact Platform; V07.02 <- CRM System;
    V07.03 <- Case Management System;      V07.04 <- Warranty / Entitlement System;
    V07.05 <- Knowledge Base;              V07.06 <- Product Defect System;
    V07.07 <- Field Service System;        V07.08 <- Workflow / Escalation System;
    V07.09 <- Email / Correspondence System; V07.10 <- Customer Portal;
    V07.11 <- Case Management System + CRM System; V07.12 <- Analytics / BI System.
- Field Service Partner -serving-> V07.07 Resolve or Fulfil Request.
- Regulator -serving-> V07.08 Escalate if Needed.

7. Intent
The Issue Resolution Service sits top-centre as the headline service. The twelve
Business Processes form the backbone in V07.01 -> V07.12 order so the reader can
trace the issue-resolution journey and drill from any process straight into its
detailed BPMN model. This one ArchiMate view therefore links to all twelve V07
BPMN process diagrams. The mapping of process -> actors/teams/applications is the
Process <-> Actors / Teams / IT Systems matrix above.
```
