**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V08):

- **External actors:** Asset Seller (V08.03); Supplier (V08.03, V08.04); Lessor (V08.03); Service Provider (V08.05); Maintenance Contractor (V08.06, V08.07); Insurer (V08.04, V08.09, V08.10); Buyer (V08.10).
- **Teams:** Operations (V08.01, V08.05, V08.06, V08.07); Asset Management (V08.01, V08.02, V08.04, V08.07, V08.09, V08.11); Investment Approver (V08.02); Finance (V08.02, V08.08, V08.09, V08.10, V08.11); Procurement (V08.03); Legal (V08.03, V08.10); Facilities / Receiving (V08.04); IT / Facilities (V08.05); Maintenance (V08.06); Risk (V08.09); Disposal Coordination (V08.10).
- **IT systems:** Enterprise Asset Management System (V08.01); Finance / General Ledger System (V08.02, V08.09, V08.11); Procurement System (V08.03); ERP Fixed Asset Register (V08.04, V08.08, V08.11); IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System (V08.05); Maintenance Management System (V08.06); Reporting / BI System (V08.07); Document Management System (V08.10).

**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

A single high-level ArchiMate view of the Acquire to Retire service area. It
shows the **Actors**, **Services**, **Processes**, **Interfaces** and
**Applications** that provide the Asset Lifecycle Service and the related
supplier-, contractor- and buyer-facing services across the eleven V08
processes. Each Business Process is a drill-down anchor: link it to the matching
V08.nn BPMN diagram and its marker turns green.

```text
ArchiMate: V08 — Acquire to Retire — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: show how the organisation provides the Asset Lifecycle Service and the
related services (to the internal asset owners and to the Asset Seller /
Supplier, Lessor, Service Provider, Maintenance Contractor, Insurer and Buyer)
across the eleven V08 Acquire to Retire processes, and the applications that
support them. Lay it out in three horizontal bands, top to bottom — BUSINESS
SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS — with the internal Operations /
Asset Management on the far left and the supply, service and disposal actors on
the far right. Read top-to-bottom as service → process → application (ArchiMate
service realisation).

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)
- Asset Management — the internal party the asset lifecycle service is provided
  to (far left, the owner of every asset need).
- Asset Seller, Supplier, Lessor — external parties that supply or lease the
  asset (far right, acquisition side).
- Service Provider, Maintenance Contractor, Insurer — external parties that
  install, maintain and insure the asset in life (far right).
- Buyer — the external party that receives the asset at disposal (far right,
  retirement side).

2. Interfaces
- Business Interface "Supplier & Contractor Portal / Asset Channel" — the
  channel the Supplier, Lessor, Service Provider, Maintenance Contractor,
  Insurer and Buyer use to quote, supply, service, insure and take title. Those
  actors ACCESS this interface; the interface SERVES the business services
  below.
- Application Interfaces (optional, only the few the portal calls): "Procurement
  API" on the Procurement System, "Work Order API" on the Maintenance
  Management System.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — the services provided, top band,
   left-to-right in asset-lifecycle order:
- Asset Planning & Approval Service — identify the need, approve the investment.
- Asset Acquisition Service — buy or lease the asset.
- Asset Onboarding Service — receive, register and deploy the asset.
- Asset Operation & Maintenance Service — maintain and monitor the asset in
  service.
- Asset Accounting Service — depreciate, impair and transfer the asset.
- Asset Retirement Service — dispose of the asset and close its record.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — the eleven V08 processes, middle band
   in V08.01 → V08.11 order. Each REALISES the business service shown and is the
   link anchor to its BPMN diagram:
- V08.01 Identify Asset Need                 -> realises Asset Planning & Approval Service
- V08.02 Approve Investment                  -> realises Asset Planning & Approval Service
- V08.03 Acquire or Lease Asset              -> realises Asset Acquisition Service
- V08.04 Receive and Register Asset          -> realises Asset Onboarding Service
- V08.05 Deploy Asset                        -> realises Asset Onboarding Service
- V08.06 Maintain Asset                      -> realises Asset Operation & Maintenance Service
- V08.07 Monitor Utilisation and Condition   -> realises Asset Operation & Maintenance Service
- V08.08 Account for Depreciation            -> realises Asset Accounting Service
- V08.09 Manage Impairments or Transfers     -> realises Asset Accounting Service
- V08.10 Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset    -> realises Asset Retirement Service
- V08.11 Close Asset Record                  -> realises Asset Retirement Service

5. Applications (Application Component) — the IT systems that support the
   processes, bottom band:
- Enterprise Asset Management System
- Finance / General Ledger System
- Procurement System
- ERP Fixed Asset Register
- IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System
- Maintenance Management System
- Reporting / BI System
- Document Management System

6. Relationships
- Asset Seller / Supplier, Lessor, Service Provider, Maintenance Contractor,
  Insurer and Buyer -accesses-> Supplier & Contractor Portal / Asset Channel.
- Supplier & Contractor Portal / Asset Channel -serving-> the Acquisition,
  Onboarding, Operation & Maintenance, Accounting and Retirement services.
- Each Business Process -realisation-> its Business Service (section 4).
- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
  (serving, application -> process):
    V08.01 <- Enterprise Asset Management System;  V08.02 <- Finance / General Ledger System;
    V08.03 <- Procurement System;                  V08.04 <- ERP Fixed Asset Register;
    V08.05 <- IT Asset Management / Facilities Mgmt System; V08.06 <- Maintenance Management System;
    V08.07 <- Reporting / BI System;               V08.08 <- ERP Fixed Asset Register;
    V08.09 <- Finance / General Ledger System;      V08.10 <- Document Management System;
    V08.11 <- ERP Fixed Asset Register + Finance / General Ledger System.
- Maintenance Contractor -serving-> V08.06 Maintain Asset and V08.07 Monitor
  Utilisation and Condition.
- Insurer -serving-> V08.04 Receive and Register Asset, V08.09 Manage
  Impairments or Transfers and V08.10 Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset.
- Buyer -serving-> V08.10 Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset.

7. Intent
The Asset Lifecycle Service sits top-centre as the headline service. The eleven
Business Processes form the backbone in V08.01 -> V08.11 order so the reader can
trace the asset's whole-of-life journey and drill from any process straight into
its detailed BPMN model. This one ArchiMate view therefore links to all eleven
V08 BPMN process diagrams. The mapping of process -> actors/teams/applications is
the Process <-> Actors / Teams / IT Systems matrix above.
```

### V08.01 — Identify Asset Need

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.01 Identify Asset Need — first subprocess of the Acquire to
Retire value chain, in which an operational need is identified, assessed,
and packaged as a capital request ready for investment approval.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the internal organisation running
the identification and assessment process, with lanes for Operations and
Asset Management.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management System" — the IT system used to record
asset needs and retrieve asset lifecycle data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management System": black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Management Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. Enterprise Asset Management System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Operations lane:
  None start event "Asset need identified by operations"
  User task "Document asset requirement"
  User task "Assess operational impact and urgency"
  Exclusive gateway "Is need clearly defined?"
    - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Requirement Defined"
      (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Clarify requirement
      with stakeholders", User task "Update requirement documentation"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Requirement
      defined")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Requirement defined"
  User task "Classify asset type and category"
  Send task "Submit asset need to Asset Management"

Asset Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Asset need received from Operations"
  User task "Review and validate asset need"
  Service task "Check existing asset register for alternatives"
  Exclusive gateway "Existing asset can fulfil need?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Recommend reallocation or reuse of existing
      asset"
      End event "Need resolved by reallocation — no capital request raised"
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "New asset
      required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "New asset required"
  User task "Confirm strategic alignment with asset plan"
  User task "Prepare capital request documentation"
  Service task "Record capital request in Enterprise Asset Management
  System"
  End event "Capital request complete — ready for Approve Investment"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Operations lane where the need is
identified, documented, assessed, and then passed through the "Is need
clearly defined?" gateway; the standard-loop subprocess fires if the
requirement is incomplete, otherwise the branch merges at "Requirement
defined" and the task "Classify asset type and category" follows before
the send task hands off to the Asset Management lane. In Asset Management
the message is caught, the register is checked, and the "Existing asset
can fulfil need?" gateway splits: the "Yes" branch ends without a capital
request; the "No" branch merges at "New asset required" and continues to
strategic alignment, documentation, and system recording before the end
event.

Message flows:
Enterprise Asset Management System → Service task "Check existing asset
register for alternatives" (existing asset and lifecycle data)
Service task "Record capital request in Enterprise Asset Management
System" → Enterprise Asset Management System (capital request record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Asset Requirement Document" — written by User task "Document
asset requirement"; read by User task "Review and validate asset need".
Data Object "Capital Request" — written by User task "Prepare capital
request documentation"; read by Service task "Record capital request in
Enterprise Asset Management System".

This subprocess captures and validates an internal operational need,
confirms that no existing asset can satisfy it, aligns the need with the
asset plan, and produces a formal capital request recorded in the
Enterprise Asset Management System. It hands a completed capital request
to Approve Investment, where budget holders and finance will assess and
authorise the expenditure.
```

### V08.02 — Approve Investment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.02 Approve Investment — second subprocess in the Acquire to
Retire value chain, receiving a validated asset need from Identify Asset
Need and passing an approved capital request to Acquire or Lease Asset.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation running the
approval process, containing all internal teams involved.
  Lane "Asset Management" — asset manager prepares and submits the
  capital request.
  Lane "Investment Approver" — budget holder reviews and decides on the
  investment.
  Lane "Finance" — finance accountant validates financial impact and
  records the approved request.
Pool "Finance / General Ledger System" — IT system that stores approved
capital requests and provides budget and financial data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Finance / General Ledger System": black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Management Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom:
   Asset Management, Investment Approver, Finance)
2. Finance / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Asset Management lane:
  Message start event "Asset need identified — received from Identify
  Asset Need"
  User task "Prepare capital expenditure request"
  User task "Attach supporting documentation and cost estimates"
  Send task "Submit capital request for approval"
  Intermediate message catch event "Decision received from Investment
  Approver"
  Exclusive gateway "Investment approved?"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Investment approved?")
  - branch "Rejected with revision required": User task "Revise capital
    request based on feedback"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Investment approved?")
  - branch "Rejected — not proceeding": End event "Capital request
    rejected — investment not authorised"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Investment approved?"
  Send task "Forward approved request to Finance for validation"

Investment Approver lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Capital request received for review"
  User task "Review capital expenditure request against policy and
  budget"
  User task "Assess alignment with capital expenditure policy and
  delegation of authority"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision outcome?"
  - branch "Approve": Send task "Issue approval decision"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision outcome?")
  - branch "Return for revision": User task "Record revision
    requirements and feedback"
    Send task "Return request with feedback"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision outcome?")
  - branch "Reject — not proceeding": Send task "Issue rejection
    notification"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision outcome?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision outcome?"

Finance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Approved capital request received
  from Asset Management"
  User task "Validate financial impact and budget availability"
  Service task "Record approved capital request in Finance / General
  Ledger System"
  User task "Confirm budget commitment and update capital plan"
  End event "Investment approved and recorded — ready for Acquire or
  Lease Asset"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Review capital expenditure
request against policy and budget" — label "Review deadline exceeded"
— triggers Send task "Issue escalation notification to senior
approver".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Asset Management lane with the
start event, proceeds through request preparation and submission,
then pauses for a message catch event awaiting the decision. The
exclusive gateway branches on the decision: the approved branch and
the revision branch rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway, after
which the approved request is forwarded to Finance; the rejection
branch ends at its own end event. In the Investment Approver lane,
the incoming message catch event triggers review tasks and a decision
gateway whose three branches — approve, return for revision, and
reject — all rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway in that lane. In
the Finance lane, the incoming message catch event triggers financial
validation, recording in the system, and budget confirmation,
concluding at the end event.

Message flows:
Asset Management lane "Submit capital request for approval" →
Investment Approver lane "Capital request received for review"
(capital expenditure request with supporting documentation and cost
estimates).
Investment Approver lane "Issue approval decision" → Asset Management
lane "Decision received from Investment Approver" (approval
decision).
Investment Approver lane "Return request with feedback" → Asset
Management lane "Decision received from Investment Approver" (revision
requirements and feedback).
Investment Approver lane "Issue rejection notification" → Asset
Management lane "Decision received from Investment Approver"
(rejection notification).
Asset Management lane "Forward approved request to Finance for
validation" → Finance lane "Approved capital request received from
Asset Management" (approved capital request).
Finance lane "Record approved capital request in Finance / General
Ledger System" → Finance / General Ledger System (approved capital
request record and budget commitment entry).
Finance / General Ledger System → Finance lane "Validate financial
impact and budget availability" (budget availability data and current
capital plan).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Capital Expenditure Request" — written by "Prepare
capital expenditure request"; read by "Review capital expenditure
request against policy and budget"; read by "Validate financial
impact and budget availability".
Data Object "Supporting Documentation and Cost Estimates" — written
by "Attach supporting documentation and cost estimates"; read by
"Review capital expenditure request against policy and budget".
Data Object "Revision Requirements and Feedback" — written by
"Record revision requirements and feedback"; read by "Revise capital
request based on feedback".
Data Object "Approved Capital Request" — written by "Record approved
capital request in Finance / General Ledger System"; read by
"Confirm budget commitment and update capital plan".

This subprocess takes a validated asset need and carries it through
formal capital expenditure approval, ensuring the investment is
assessed against policy, budget, and delegation of authority before
any commitment is made. It produces an approved, financially
validated capital request with a confirmed budget commitment, which
the next subprocess — Acquire or Lease Asset — uses as the
authorisation to engage suppliers, sellers, or lessors.
```

### V08.03 — Acquire or Lease Asset

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.03 Acquire or Lease Asset — the subprocess within Acquire to
Retire that executes the commercial transaction securing the asset, either
through outright purchase or a lease agreement, and hands a confirmed order
or signed lease to Receive and Register Asset.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation running the
acquisition or lease process, containing Procurement and Legal lanes.
Pool "Asset Seller" — external party offering assets for outright purchase.
Pool "Supplier" — external party supplying the asset under a purchase order.
Pool "Lessor" — external party providing the asset under a lease agreement.
Pool "Procurement System" — IT system supporting purchase orders, supplier
records, and contract management.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Asset Seller" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Lessor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Seller
2. Supplier
3. Lessor
4. Asset Management Organisation
5. Procurement System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Approved capital request received from Approve
    Investment"
  User task "Review approved capital request and confirm acquisition mode"
  Exclusive gateway "Acquire or Lease?"
  - branch "Acquire — purchase":
      User task "Identify and contact potential sellers and suppliers"
      Send task "Request quotes and specifications"
      Intermediate message catch event "Quotes and specifications received"
      User task "Evaluate quotes and select seller or supplier"
      User task "Raise purchase order"
      Service task "Record purchase order in Procurement System"
      Send task "Issue purchase order to Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Order acknowledgement received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acquisition mode resolved")
  - branch "Lease":
      User task "Identify potential lessors"
      Send task "Request lease terms and conditions"
      Intermediate message catch event "Lease terms received"
      User task "Evaluate lease terms and select Lessor"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acquisition mode resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acquisition mode resolved"
  User task "Prepare contract or lease agreement documentation"
  Send task "Send contract or agreement to Legal for review"

Legal lane:
  User task "Review contract or lease agreement"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract acceptable?"
  - branch "No — revisions required":
      User task "Document required amendments"
      Send task "Return contract with amendments to Procurement"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Contract Approved" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Revise contract or agreement",
        User task "Resubmit to Legal for review",
        User task "Review revised contract or agreement",
        Exclusive gateway "Revised contract acceptable?",
        - branch "No": (loop repeats)
        - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Yes — acceptable":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review resolved"
  User task "Obtain authorised signatures on contract or agreement"
  Send task "Return signed contract to Procurement"

Procurement lane:
  User task "File signed contract or agreement"
  Service task "Record contract or lease details in Procurement System"
  Exclusive gateway "Asset Seller involved?"
  - branch "Yes — purchase from Asset Seller":
      Send task "Notify Asset Seller of finalised purchase arrangement"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "External parties notified")
  - branch "No — Supplier or Lessor only":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "External parties notified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "External parties notified"
  End event "Purchase order confirmed or lease signed — ready for Receive
    and Register Asset"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Contract Approved" — label "Maximum negotiation period elapsed" — triggers
End event "Contract negotiation failed — escalate to Asset Management".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Procurement lane the flow passes from the start
event through the acquisition-mode gateway; the purchase branch runs through
seller and supplier contact, quote evaluation, purchase order creation, and
system recording before merging; the lease branch runs through lessor
identification, lease term request and evaluation before merging at the
exclusive merge gateway "Acquisition mode resolved"; the combined flow moves
to contract preparation and passes to the Legal lane; Legal reviews and
branches on acceptability, with the rejection branch entering the standard-
loop subprocess and the acceptance branch merging at "Legal review resolved";
after signatures the flow returns to the Procurement lane, files the
contract, records it in the system, resolves the Asset Seller notification
gateway, and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
  Procurement lane (Send task "Request quotes and specifications") →
    Asset Seller (quote and specification request)
  Asset Seller → Procurement lane (Intermediate message catch event
    "Quotes and specifications received") (quotes and specifications)
  Procurement lane (Send task "Request quotes and specifications") →
    Supplier (quote and specification request)
  Supplier → Procurement lane (Intermediate message catch event
    "Quotes and specifications received") (quotes and specifications)
  Procurement lane (Send task "Issue purchase order to Supplier") →
    Supplier (purchase order)
  Supplier → Procurement lane (Intermediate message catch event
    "Order acknowledgement received") (order acknowledgement)
  Procurement lane (Send task "Request lease terms and conditions") →
    Lessor (lease term request)
  Lessor → Procurement lane (Intermediate message catch event
    "Lease terms received") (lease terms and conditions)
  Procurement lane (Send task "Notify Asset Seller of finalised purchase
    arrangement") → Asset Seller (purchase confirmation)
  Legal lane (User task "Obtain authorised signatures on contract or
    agreement") → Lessor (signed lease agreement)
  Procurement lane (Service task "Record purchase order in Procurement
    System") → Procurement System (purchase order and contract data)
  Procurement lane (Service task "Record contract or lease details in
    Procurement System") → Procurement System (contract or lease record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Capital Request" — read by User task "Review approved
  capital request and confirm acquisition mode".
Data Object "Quotes and Specifications" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Quotes and specifications received"; read by User task
  "Evaluate quotes and select seller or supplier".
Data Object "Purchase Order" — written by User task "Raise purchase order";
  read by Service task "Record purchase order in Procurement System" and
  Send task "Issue purchase order to Supplier".
Data Object "Lease Terms" — written by Intermediate message catch event
  "Lease terms received"; read by User task "Evaluate lease terms and
  select Lessor".
Data Object "Contract or Lease Agreement" — written by User task "Prepare
  contract or lease agreement documentation"; read by User task "Review
  contract or lease agreement" and User task "Obtain authorised signatures
  on contract or agreement".
Data Object "Signed Contract or Lease Agreement" — written by User task
  "Obtain authorised signatures on contract or agreement"; read by User task
  "File signed contract or agreement" and Service task "Record contract or
  lease details in Procurement System".

This subprocess secures the legal and commercial basis for asset acquisition,
producing either a confirmed purchase order acknowledged by the Supplier or a
fully signed lease agreement with the Lessor, in both cases reviewed and
authorised by Legal. The signed contract or purchase-order confirmation, together
with the supplier or lessor details recorded in the Procurement System, is handed
to Receive and Register Asset so the incoming asset can be inspected, tagged,
and entered into the fixed asset register.
```

### V08.04 — Receive and Register Asset

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.04 Receive and Register Asset — the subprocess in which the
organisation physically receives a delivered asset, verifies it against the
purchase order, arranges insurance, and registers it in the fixed asset
register, handing a fully registered asset record to Deploy Asset.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation receiving and
registering the asset, with lanes for Facilities / Receiving and Asset
Management.
Pool "Supplier" — external party delivering the asset and providing
documentation.
Pool "Insurer" — external party providing insurance cover for the asset.
Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — IT system in which the asset master
record is created and maintained.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Asset Management Organisation
3. Insurer
4. ERP Fixed Asset Register

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Facilities / Receiving lane:
  Message start event "Asset delivery received from Supplier"
  User task "Check delivery against purchase order"
  Exclusive gateway "Delivery acceptable?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found": User task "Raise delivery
    discrepancy with Supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery acceptable?")
  - branch "Yes — delivery matches PO":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery acceptable?"
  User task "Affix asset tag and record serial number"
  User task "Capture physical condition and location details"
  Send task "Forward asset details and documentation to Asset
    Management"

Asset Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Asset details received from
    Facilities"
  User task "Review delivery documentation and warranties"
  User task "Initiate insurance cover for asset"
  Intermediate message catch event "Insurance confirmation received
    from Insurer"
  User task "Create asset master record in ERP Fixed Asset Register"
  Service task "Record asset capitalisation data, depreciation rules,
    and custodian in ERP"
  User task "File physical and digital asset documentation"
  End event "Asset registered — ready for Deploy Asset"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Raise delivery
discrepancy with Supplier" — label "Discrepancy unresolved after 5
business days" — flows to End event "Delivery rejected — supplier
escalation required".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Insurance confirmation received from Insurer" — label "Insurance
response not received within 3 business days" — flows to User task
"Chase insurer for confirmation" which then returns to Intermediate
message catch event "Insurance confirmation received from Insurer".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Facilities / Receiving lane with
the message start event, proceeds through delivery checking and the
"Delivery acceptable?" exclusive gateway; the discrepancy branch
raises the issue with the Supplier and waits for a response before
rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway "Delivery acceptable?"; the
acceptable branch joins at the same merge; flow continues through
asset tagging, condition capture, and handover to Asset Management;
in the Asset Management lane flow passes through documentation
review, insurance initiation, waiting for insurance confirmation,
asset master record creation, capitalisation data recording, and
documentation filing before reaching the end event.

Message flows:
Supplier → Facilities / Receiving lane (asset delivery, delivery
  documentation, warranties, and invoices)
Facilities / Receiving lane → Supplier (delivery discrepancy notice)
Supplier → Facilities / Receiving lane (supplier response to
  discrepancy)
Asset Management lane → Insurer (insurance cover request with asset
  details)
Insurer → Asset Management lane (insurance confirmation)
Asset Management lane → ERP Fixed Asset Register (asset master
  record creation request with capitalisation data, depreciation
  rules, serial number, location, and custodian)
ERP Fixed Asset Register → Asset Management lane (confirmation of
  asset record created)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Purchase Order" — read by User task "Check delivery
  against purchase order".
Data Object "Delivery Documentation" — read by User task "Review
  delivery documentation and warranties"; written by User task
  "Forward asset details and documentation to Asset Management".
Data Object "Asset Tag Record" — written by User task "Affix asset
  tag and record serial number"; read by User task "Create asset
  master record in ERP Fixed Asset Register".
Data Object "Condition and Location Record" — written by User task
  "Capture physical condition and location details"; read by User
  task "Create asset master record in ERP Fixed Asset Register".
Data Object "Insurance Certificate" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Insurance confirmation received from Insurer"; read by
  User task "File physical and digital asset documentation".
Data Object "Asset Master Record" — written by Service task "Record
  asset capitalisation data, depreciation rules, and custodian in
  ERP"; read by User task "File physical and digital asset
  documentation".

This subprocess takes a physically delivered asset through receiving
inspection, discrepancy resolution, asset tagging, and insurance
arrangement, culminating in creation of a complete asset master record
in the ERP Fixed Asset Register with depreciation rules, location, and
custodian assigned. It hands the registered asset record to Deploy
Asset, which will configure, locate, and commission the asset for
operational use.
```

### V08.05 — Deploy Asset

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.05 Deploy Asset — the fifth subprocess of the Acquire to Retire
value chain, covering the physical and logical deployment of a registered
asset into operational service.

1. Pools & Lanes

  - Operations (operations manager)

Pool "Service Provider" — external party supplying installation or
  configuration services.

  recording asset location, custodian, and deployment status.

Pool "Service Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System" — black-box,
  System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Service Provider
2. Asset Management Organisation (white-box, two lanes)
3. IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

IT / Facilities lane:
  Message start event "Registered asset received from Receive and Register
    Asset"
  User task "Plan deployment — confirm location, custodian, and
    configuration requirements"
  User task "Prepare deployment checklist and health and safety requirements"
  Send task "Issue deployment instructions to Service Provider"
  Intermediate message catch event "Deployment confirmation received from
    Service Provider"
  User task "Verify installation against deployment checklist"
  Exclusive gateway "Installation acceptable?"
  - branch "No — defects found": User task "Raise defect and instruct
      remediation"
    Send task "Send remediation request to Service Provider"
    Intermediate message catch event "Remediation confirmation received from
      Service Provider"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Installation acceptable")
  - branch "Yes — installation verified":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Installation acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Installation acceptable"
  User task "Assign asset tag, location, and custodian in system"
  Service task "Record deployment details in IT Asset Management System /
    Facilities Management System"
  User task "Complete handover documentation"

Operations lane:
  User task "Confirm operational readiness and acceptance of asset"
  Exclusive gateway "Asset accepted by Operations?"
  - branch "No — not ready": User task "Log outstanding items and return
      to IT / Facilities for resolution"
    End event "Deployment on hold — returned for IT / Facilities resolution"
  - branch "Yes — accepted":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Asset accepted by Operations")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Asset accepted by Operations"
  User task "Brief operations staff on asset use and maintenance schedule"
  End event "Asset deployed and in service — ready for Maintain Asset"

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Plan deployment — confirm location,

  planning delay to asset manager" in IT / Facilities lane, which rejoins
  the flow at "Prepare deployment checklist and health and safety
  requirements".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the IT / Facilities lane at the message start
event and progresses through planning, checklist preparation, and instruction
to the Service Provider. After the intermediate message catch event the
installation verification gateway branches to defect remediation (with its
own send task, intermediate message catch event, and return) or directly to
the merge. From the merge, asset tagging, system recording, and handover
documentation complete the IT / Facilities work, then flow passes to the
Operations lane for acceptance. The acceptance gateway branches to a terminal
end event for unresolved items or to the merge, after which staff briefing
leads to the final end event.

Message flows:

  Service Provider → IT / Facilities lane "Remediation confirmation received

  IT / Facilities lane "Record deployment details in IT Asset Management

    → IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System

  IT Asset Management System / Facilities Management System
    → IT / Facilities lane "Record deployment details in IT Asset Management
    System / Facilities Management System" (confirmation of recorded

7. Data objects

Data Object "Deployment Checklist" — written by "Prepare deployment checklist
  and health and safety requirements"; read by "Verify installation against

Data Object "Deployment Instructions" — written by "Plan deployment — confirm
  location, custodian, and configuration requirements"; read by "Issue
  deployment instructions to Service Provider".
Data Object "Defect Record" — written by "Raise defect and instruct
  remediation"; read by "Send remediation request to Service Provider".
Data Object "Handover Documentation" — written by "Complete handover
  documentation"; read by "Confirm operational readiness and acceptance of
  asset".
Data Object "Asset Deployment Record" — written by "Assign asset tag,
  location, and custodian in system"; read by "Record deployment details in

This subprocess takes a registered asset and moves it from the receiving dock
into live operational use. It coordinates physical or logical installation by
the Service Provider, verifies the outcome against a checklist, records the
deployment in the IT Asset Management System or Facilities Management System,
and obtains formal acceptance from Operations. Once the asset is confirmed in
```

### V08.06 — Maintain Asset

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
executed, and recorded, keeping the asset in operational condition.

   above Operations lane)
2. Maintenance Contractor
3. Maintenance Management System

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Deployed asset ready for maintenance — received

  - branch "No — work accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway

  Exclusive merge gateway "Report review complete"
  Service task "Record maintenance outcome in Maintenance Management

  User task "Update maintenance schedule and next service date"

Operations lane:

  - branch "No — asset not operational": User task "Escalate asset
    failure to Maintenance planner"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Operational check done")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Operational check done"

Flow note: The Maintenance lane drives the end-to-end sequence.
The Operations lane runs in parallel from the point of work-order
issuance: "Confirm asset availability for maintenance window"
follows "Issue work order to Maintenance Contractor" via a parallel
split gateway "Coordinate with Operations" in the Maintenance lane,
rejoining at a parallel merge gateway "Coordination complete" before
the intermediate message catch event "Inspection or repair report
received from Maintenance Contractor". The parallel split gateway
is named "Coordinate with Operations" and the parallel merge gateway
is named "Coordination complete". Operations lane tasks sit between
these two gateways.

Revised full Maintenance lane in flow order (incorporating parallel):

  Message start event "Deployed asset ready for maintenance — received
    from Deploy Asset"
  User task "Review maintenance schedule and asset condition"
  Exclusive gateway "Maintenance type?"
  - branch "Scheduled preventive maintenance": User task "Create

  - branch "Reactive or corrective maintenance": User task "Create

  Service task "Log work order in Maintenance Management System"
  Send task "Issue work order to Maintenance Contractor"
  Parallel split gateway "Coordinate with Operations"
  - branch "Maintenance track": Intermediate message catch event
    "Inspection or repair report received from Maintenance
    Contractor"
    (continues to parallel merge gateway "Coordination complete")
  - branch "Operations track": (flows to Operations lane — see
    Operations lane contents)
    (continues to parallel merge gateway "Coordination complete")
  Parallel merge gateway "Coordination complete"
  User task "Review inspection or repair report"
  Exclusive gateway "Further action required?"
  - branch "Yes — additional work needed": User task "Raise follow-on
    work order"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Report review complete")
  - branch "No — work accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Report review complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Report review complete"
  Service task "Record maintenance outcome in Maintenance Management
    System"
  User task "Update maintenance schedule and next service date"
  End event "Maintenance record updated — ready for Monitor
    Utilisation and Condition"

Operations lane (flows between the parallel gateways):
  User task "Confirm asset availability for maintenance window"
  Intermediate message catch event "Work order completion confirmed
    by Maintenance Contractor"
  User task "Inspect returned asset and confirm operational status"
  Exclusive gateway "Asset operational?"
  - branch "Yes — asset operational": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "Operational check done")
  - branch "No — asset not operational": User task "Escalate asset
    failure to Maintenance planner"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Operational check done")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Operational check done"
  (continues to parallel merge gateway "Coordination complete")

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Create preventive work order"
  — label "Schedule overdue", triggers End event "Maintenance
  overdue — escalate to asset manager".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess implied by
  the Maintenance Contractor turnaround — label "Contractor response
  deadline exceeded", attached to Send task "Issue work order to
  Maintenance Contractor", triggers User task "Chase Maintenance
  Contractor for response".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Maintenance lane with the message
start event, proceeds through schedule review and the exclusive
maintenance-type gateway (preventive or corrective branch), merges,
logs the work order, issues it to the contractor, then splits in
parallel — the Maintenance track waits for the contractor report
while the Operations track confirms availability, catches the
completion confirmation, and checks operational status, resolving
at the exclusive "Asset operational?" gateway before rejoining the
parallel merge. After the merge, the Maintenance lane reviews the
report, tests whether further action is needed (exclusive gateway,
follow-on work order branch or direct merge), records the outcome,
updates the schedule, and ends.

Message flows:
  Send task "Issue work order to Maintenance Contractor" →
    Maintenance Contractor (work order with scope, asset details,
    and service requirements)
  Maintenance Contractor → Intermediate message catch event
    "Inspection or repair report received from Maintenance
    Contractor" (inspection or repair report and condition
    assessment)
  Maintenance Contractor → Intermediate message catch event
    "Work order completion confirmed by Maintenance Contractor"
    (completion confirmation)
  Service task "Log work order in Maintenance Management System" →
    Maintenance Management System (work order data)
  Service task "Record maintenance outcome in Maintenance Management
    System" → Maintenance Management System (maintenance outcome,
    service records, condition data)
  Maintenance Management System → User task "Review maintenance
    schedule and asset condition" (existing maintenance schedule
    and asset history)

Data Object "Work Order" — written by "Create preventive work order"
  and "Create corrective work order"; read by "Issue work order to

  Management System".
Data Object "Inspection or Repair Report" — written by receipt at

  Contractor"; read by "Review inspection or repair report".
Data Object "Maintenance Record" — written by "Record maintenance
  outcome in Maintenance Management System"; read by "Update
  maintenance schedule and next service date".
Data Object "Maintenance Schedule" — read by "Review maintenance
  schedule and asset condition"; written by "Update maintenance
  schedule and next service date".

This subprocess keeps the asset in serviceable condition by translating
the maintenance schedule and any reactive triggers into formal work
orders, coordinating with the Maintenance Contractor for execution, and
capturing all inspection and repair outcomes in the Maintenance
Management System. It hands an up-to-date maintenance record and
revised service schedule to Monitor Utilisation and Condition, where
the asset's ongoing performance and health are tracked against
operational targets.
```

### V08.07 — Monitor Utilisation and Condition

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.07 Monitor Utilisation and Condition — subprocess within the
Acquire to Retire value chain, sitting between Maintain Asset and Account
for Depreciation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation running the
monitoring and condition assessment process, with lanes for Operations
and Asset Management.
Pool "Maintenance Contractor" — external contractor supplying inspection
reports and condition assessments.
Pool "Reporting / BI System" — IT system that stores and surfaces
utilisation data, condition data, and lifecycle reporting.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Maintenance Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Reporting / BI System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Maintenance Contractor
2. Asset Management Organisation
3. Reporting / BI System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Operations lane:
  Message start event "Utilisation and condition monitoring cycle
    triggered from Maintain Asset"
  User task "Collect asset utilisation data"
  Service task "Log utilisation data to Reporting / BI System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Condition assessment report received
    from Maintenance Contractor"
  User task "Review condition assessment against performance thresholds"
  Exclusive gateway "Condition within acceptable threshold?"
    - branch "Yes — condition acceptable":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Condition threshold
        outcome")
    - branch "No — condition below threshold":
        User task "Raise condition alert and document findings"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Condition threshold
        outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Condition threshold outcome"
  User task "Update asset condition status"
  Exclusive gateway "Utilisation trend concern?"
    - branch "No — utilisation normal":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Utilisation review
        outcome")
    - branch "Yes — underutilised or overloaded":
        User task "Document utilisation concern and recommend action"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Utilisation review
        outcome")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Utilisation review outcome"
  Send task "Submit utilisation and condition summary to Asset
    Management lane"

Asset Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Utilisation and condition summary
    received"
  User task "Assess overall asset health and lifecycle position"
  Exclusive gateway "Lifecycle or impairment action required?"
    - branch "No — continue monitoring":
        User task "Record monitoring outcome and schedule next review"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Action determination")
    - branch "Yes — escalate for further action":
        User task "Initiate escalation to impairment or transfer review"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Action determination")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Action determination"
  Service task "Store monitoring record in Reporting / BI System"
  End event "Monitoring cycle complete — asset health record ready
    for Account for Depreciation"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Collect asset
utilisation data", labelled "Data collection overdue — 5 days",
triggering User task "Escalate missing utilisation data to operations
supervisor"; flow rejoins after the boundary task by proceeding to the
intermediate message catch event "Condition assessment report received
from Maintenance Contractor".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Operations lane, passes through
utilisation collection, condition review with its two-branch exclusive
gateway merging at "Condition threshold outcome", then continues to
condition status update and the utilisation trend gateway merging at
"Utilisation review outcome", before a summary is sent to the Asset
Management lane; the Asset Management lane picks up the summary, runs the
lifecycle assessment and the two-branch "Lifecycle or impairment action
required?" gateway merging at "Action determination", then stores the
record and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
Maintenance Contractor → Operations lane, User task "Review condition
  assessment against performance thresholds" (condition assessment
  report and inspection findings).
Operations lane, Service task "Log utilisation data to Reporting / BI
  System" → Reporting / BI System (utilisation data submission).
Asset Management lane, Service task "Store monitoring record in
  Reporting / BI System" → Reporting / BI System (monitoring outcome
  record and asset health status).
Reporting / BI System → Operations lane, User task "Collect asset
  utilisation data" (current utilisation metrics and historical
  trend data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Asset Utilisation Data" — written by User task "Collect
  asset utilisation data"; read by Service task "Log utilisation data
  to Reporting / BI System".
Data Object "Condition Assessment Report" — read by User task "Review
  condition assessment against performance thresholds"; written by
  User task "Update asset condition status".
Data Object "Condition Alert Record" — written by User task "Raise
  condition alert and document findings"; read by User task "Update
  asset condition status".
Data Object "Utilisation Concern Record" — written by User task
  "Document utilisation concern and recommend action"; read by User
  task "Assess overall asset health and lifecycle position".
Data Object "Asset Health and Monitoring Summary" — written by User
  task "Assess overall asset health and lifecycle position"; read by
  Service task "Store monitoring record in Reporting / BI System".

This subprocess collects and evaluates asset utilisation metrics and
contractor-supplied condition assessments to form a current view of each
asset's health and lifecycle position. Where thresholds are breached or
utilisation trends are concerning, findings are flagged for escalation.
The completed monitoring record and asset health summary are handed to
Account for Depreciation, where current condition and usage inform
depreciation calculations and any adjustments required.
```

### V08.08 — Account for Depreciation

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.08 Account for Depreciation — the Finance subprocess that
periodically calculates, records, and reports asset depreciation within
the Acquire to Retire value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation running the
depreciation accounting process, with lanes for Finance.
Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — IT system holding asset master data,
depreciation rules, and accumulated depreciation balances.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Management Organisation
2. ERP Fixed Asset Register

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Finance lane:
Timer start event "Depreciation period opens (scheduled period-end)"
Service task "Retrieve asset register and depreciation rules"
User task "Review assets in scope for depreciation run"
Exclusive gateway "Assets correctly configured?"
- branch "No — configuration issues found": User task "Correct asset
  master data and depreciation rules"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assets correctly configured")
- branch "Yes — all assets in scope confirmed": (continues to exclusive
  merge gateway "Assets correctly configured")
Exclusive merge gateway "Assets correctly configured"
Service task "Run automated depreciation calculation"
Intermediate message catch event "Depreciation calculation results
received from ERP Fixed Asset Register"
User task "Review depreciation calculation output"
Exclusive gateway "Calculation output accepted?"
- branch "No — errors or anomalies identified": User task "Investigate
  and resolve depreciation discrepancies"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Calculation output accepted")
- branch "Yes — output accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Calculation output accepted")
Exclusive merge gateway "Calculation output accepted"
User task "Post depreciation journal entries to general ledger"
Service task "Update accumulated depreciation balances in asset register"
Intermediate message catch event "Posting confirmation received from
ERP Fixed Asset Register"
User task "Reconcile depreciation ledger to asset register"
Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation agreed?"
- branch "No — variances found": User task "Investigate and clear
  reconciling items"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed")
- branch "Yes — reconciliation agreed": (continues to exclusive merge
  gateway "Reconciliation agreed")
Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed"
User task "Prepare depreciation report for period"
End event "Depreciation accounted and reported — ready for Monitor
Utilisation and Condition or Manage Impairments or Transfers"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs entirely within the Finance lane from the
timer start event through asset retrieval, scope review, and the

received the "Calculation output accepted?" gateway routes any error
investigation back to its own merge, then continues through journal

"Reconciliation agreed?" gateway routes variance investigation back to

Message flows:
Service task "Retrieve asset register and depreciation rules" →
ERP Fixed Asset Register (request for asset master data and

ERP Fixed Asset Register → Intermediate message catch event
"Depreciation calculation results received from ERP Fixed Asset
Register" (calculated depreciation amounts per asset).
User task "Post depreciation journal entries to general ledger" →

ERP Fixed Asset Register → Intermediate message catch event "Posting

Data Object "Depreciation Rules" — read by "Retrieve asset register

Data Object "Depreciation Reconciliation" — written by "Reconcile
```
