```text
report for period".
Data Object "Depreciation Period Report" — written by "Prepare
depreciation report for period".

This subprocess takes registered assets with agreed depreciation rules
and produces fully posted, reconciled, and reported depreciation entries
for the accounting period. The Finance team retrieves asset data from
the ERP Fixed Asset Register, runs and validates the depreciation
calculation, posts the journal, and confirms balances agree before
issuing the period report. The verified depreciation position is then
available to support Monitor Utilisation and Condition reviews and any
impairment assessments carried out in Manage Impairments or Transfers.
```

### V08.09 — Manage Impairments or Transfers

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.09 Manage Impairments or Transfers — subprocess within the
Acquire to Retire value chain that identifies, assesses, and records asset
impairments or inter-unit transfers, updating financial records accordingly.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation running the process,
with lanes for Asset Management, Risk, Finance, and Legal (drawn from
V08.09 scope).
Pool "Insurer" — external party providing insurance assessments and
settlement information.
Pool "Finance / General Ledger System" — IT system recording impairment
entries and transfer accounting.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Finance / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Insurer
2. Asset Management Organisation
3. Finance / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Asset Management lane:
  Message start event "Impairment trigger or transfer request received
  from Monitor Utilisation and Condition"
  User task "Review asset condition or transfer request"
  Exclusive gateway "Trigger type?"
  - branch "Impairment": User task "Commission impairment assessment"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Trigger type resolved")
  - branch "Transfer": User task "Prepare inter-unit transfer proposal"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Trigger type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Trigger type resolved"
  User task "Compile assessment findings and supporting documentation"

Risk lane:
  User task "Review impairment or transfer risk assessment"
  Exclusive gateway "Assessment outcome acceptable?"
  - branch "No — rework required":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Assessment Approved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
      User task "Revise assessment findings",
      User task "Resubmit for risk review"
    (exits subprocess)
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assessment accepted")
  - branch "Yes — proceed":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assessment accepted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Assessment accepted"

Finance lane:
  User task "Determine impairment loss or transfer book value adjustment"
  Exclusive gateway "Insurer involvement required?"
  - branch "Yes — insurance claim applies":
    Send task "Send impairment details to Insurer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Insurance settlement received"
    User task "Record insurance settlement proceeds"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Insurance step complete")
  - branch "No — no insurance claim":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Insurance step complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Insurance step complete"
  Service task "Post impairment or transfer accounting entry to Finance /
  General Ledger System"
  User task "Update asset value and status in asset register"
  User task "Prepare impairment or transfer report"
  End event "Impairment or transfer recorded — ready for Close Asset Record"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Assessment Approved" — label "Assessment overdue (5 business days)" —
flows to End event "Assessment escalated — process suspended pending
management review".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom within the Asset Management
Organisation pool. The Asset Management lane opens with the start event,
handles initial review, splits on trigger type, merges, and compiles
documentation before handing to Risk. The Risk lane reviews, applies a
loop subprocess if rework is needed, and merges before passing to Finance.
The Finance lane determines the value adjustment, splits on insurer
involvement (merging after the insurance steps or bypassing), posts to the
general ledger system, updates the asset register, and closes with the
end event.

Message flows:
Asset Management lane "Commission impairment assessment" →
  Insurer (impairment assessment request).
Insurer → Finance lane "Insurance settlement received"
  (insurance settlement advice).
Finance lane "Send impairment details to Insurer" →
  Insurer (impairment claim details).
Finance lane "Post impairment or transfer accounting entry to Finance /
  General Ledger System" →
  Finance / General Ledger System (impairment or transfer journal entry).
Finance / General Ledger System → Finance lane "Update asset value and
  status in asset register" (confirmed posting acknowledgement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Impairment or Transfer Request" — written by Asset Management
  lane "Review asset condition or transfer request"; read by Risk lane
  "Review impairment or transfer risk assessment".
Data Object "Impairment Assessment Report" — written by Asset Management
  lane "Compile assessment findings and supporting documentation"; read by
  Finance lane "Determine impairment loss or transfer book value adjustment".
Data Object "Insurance Settlement Record" — written by Finance lane
  "Record insurance settlement proceeds"; read by Finance lane "Post
  impairment or transfer accounting entry to Finance / General Ledger System".
Data Object "Impairment or Transfer Accounting Entry" — written by Finance
  lane "Post impairment or transfer accounting entry to Finance / General
  Ledger System"; read by Finance lane "Prepare impairment or transfer report".

This subprocess receives a condition-based or administratively driven
trigger — an observed impairment or a request to relocate or transfer an
asset — and routes it through risk review and financial valuation before
posting the resulting accounting entry to the general ledger. Where
insurance applies, settlement proceeds are captured before the journal is
raised. The subprocess hands a fully reconciled, updated asset value and
status to Close Asset Record, or feeds back into ongoing monitoring when
the asset continues in service.
```

### V08.10 — Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.10 Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset — the subprocess in which
the organisation executes the controlled exit of an asset from service through
sale, write-off, or insurance claim, sitting between Manage Impairments or
Transfers and Close Asset Record in the Acquire to Retire value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the organisation executing the disposal
process, with lanes for Disposal Coordination, Legal, and Finance.
Pool "Buyer" — external party purchasing a disposed asset.
Pool "Insurer" — external party handling insurance-related disposal or
write-off claims.
Pool "Document Management System" — IT system storing disposal
documentation, sale agreements, and ownership transfer records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Buyer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Buyer
2. Insurer
3. Asset Management Organisation
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Disposal Coordination lane:
  Message start event "Disposal instruction received from Manage
  Impairments or Transfers"
  User task "Confirm asset disposal eligibility and method"
  Exclusive gateway "Disposal method?"
  - branch "Sale to buyer": User task "Prepare asset for sale and
    document condition"
    Send task "Issue asset details and sale terms to Buyer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Buyer offer received"
    Exclusive gateway "Offer acceptable?"
    - branch "No": User task "Negotiate revised terms with Buyer"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Offer acceptable?")
    - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Offer acceptable?")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Offer acceptable?"
    User task "Confirm sale and prepare transfer documentation"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposal method?")
  - branch "Write-off": User task "Document write-off justification
    and obtain disposal approval"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposal method?")
  - branch "Insurance claim": User task "Prepare insurance claim
    and supporting evidence"
    Send task "Submit insurance claim to Insurer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Insurer decision received"
    Exclusive gateway "Claim approved?"
    - branch "No": User task "Record claim rejection and escalate
      for write-off"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Claim approved?")
    - branch "Yes": User task "Record insurance proceeds and close
      claim"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Claim approved?")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Claim approved?"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposal method?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Disposal method?"
  Send task "Submit disposal documentation to Document Management
  System"

Legal lane:
  User task "Review and execute sale or transfer agreement"
  User task "Confirm legal title transfer and deregister asset"

Finance lane:
  User task "Record sale proceeds or write-off value in general
  ledger"
  User task "Raise disposal accounting entries and reconcile asset
  value"
  End event "Asset financially disposed — ready for Close Asset
  Record"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Confirm sale and prepare
transfer documentation" — label "Sale completion deadline exceeded"
— on trigger, flow continues to User task "Escalate delayed sale to
disposal coordinator manager" in Disposal Coordination lane, ending
at End event "Disposal escalated — process on hold".

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit insurance claim to
Insurer" — label "Claim response deadline exceeded" — on trigger,
flow continues to User task "Chase Insurer for outstanding decision"
in Disposal Coordination lane, returning to Intermediate message
catch event "Insurer decision received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Asset Management Organisation pool, flow
begins in the Disposal Coordination lane from the message start event
through eligibility confirmation, then branches at the "Disposal
method?" gateway into sale, write-off, and insurance claim paths.
The sale branch passes through the offer gateway and its merge before
joining; the insurance branch passes through the claim approved
gateway and its merge before joining; the write-off branch joins
directly. All three branches converge at the "Disposal method?" merge
gateway, then the disposal documentation send task passes to the Legal
lane for agreement review and title transfer, then to the Finance lane
for proceeds recording, accounting entries, and the end event.

Message flows:
Disposal Coordination — Send task "Issue asset details and sale terms
to Buyer" → Buyer (asset details, condition report, sale terms).
Buyer → Disposal Coordination — Intermediate message catch event
"Buyer offer received" (buyer offer and acceptance).
Disposal Coordination — Send task "Submit insurance claim to Insurer"
→ Insurer (claim form and supporting evidence).
Insurer → Disposal Coordination — Intermediate message catch event
"Insurer decision received" (claim decision and settlement amount).
Disposal Coordination — Send task "Submit disposal documentation to
Document Management System" → Document Management System (sale
agreement, transfer record, write-off or claim documentation).
Finance — User task "Record sale proceeds or write-off value in
general ledger" → Document Management System (disposal accounting
entries and reconciliation records).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disposal Eligibility Assessment" — written by
"Confirm asset disposal eligibility and method", read by "Prepare
asset for sale and document condition" and "Document write-off
justification and obtain disposal approval".
Data Object "Asset Condition Report" — written by "Prepare asset
for sale and document condition", read by "Issue asset details and
sale terms to Buyer".
Data Object "Sale Agreement" — written by "Confirm sale and prepare
transfer documentation", read by "Review and execute sale or transfer
agreement".
Data Object "Write-Off Justification" — written by "Document
write-off justification and obtain disposal approval", read by
"Record sale proceeds or write-off value in general ledger".
Data Object "Insurance Claim File" — written by "Prepare insurance
claim and supporting evidence", read by "Submit insurance claim to
Insurer" and "Record insurance proceeds and close claim".
Data Object "Disposal Accounting Entry" — written by "Raise disposal
accounting entries and reconcile asset value", read by "Submit
disposal documentation to Document Management System".

This subprocess takes an asset approved for exit and drives it through the
appropriate disposal route — sale, write-off, or insurance claim — securing
buyer agreement or insurer settlement, executing the legal title transfer, and
posting all resulting accounting entries. On completion it hands a fully
reconciled disposal record to Close Asset Record so the asset master data can
be closed and the fixed asset register updated.
```

### V08.11 — Close Asset Record

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V08.11 Close Asset Record — final subprocess of the Acquire to
Retire value chain, triggered when an asset disposal, write-off, or
transfer has been completed and all financial settlements received.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — the internal organisation
executing the close-down of the asset record across asset management
and finance teams.
  Lane "Asset Management" — asset manager who reviews the asset
  lifecycle history, confirms closure conditions are met, and
  authorises removal from the asset register.
  Lane "Finance" — finance accountant who clears any residual
  accounting balances, posts final journal entries, and confirms
  the general ledger is reconciled.

Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — system that holds the asset master
record and fixed asset register.

Pool "Finance / General Ledger System" — system in which final
accounting entries and reconciliations are posted.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Management Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "ERP Fixed Asset Register" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Finance / General Ledger System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Management Organisation
2. ERP Fixed Asset Register
3. Finance / General Ledger System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Management Organisation)

Asset Management lane:
  Message start event "Disposal, write-off, or transfer confirmed —
  received from Dispose / Sell / Write Off Asset"
  User task "Retrieve full asset lifecycle history"
  User task "Verify all closure conditions are met"
  Exclusive gateway "Closure conditions satisfied?"
  - branch "No — outstanding items remain": User task
    "Raise and resolve outstanding items"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Closure conditions
    satisfied")
  - branch "Yes — all conditions met":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Closure conditions
    satisfied")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Closure conditions satisfied"
  Service task "Mark asset as closed in ERP Fixed Asset Register"
  User task "Confirm asset tag and physical records are retired"
  Send task "Notify Finance of asset closure for final accounting"

Finance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Asset closure notification
  received"
  User task "Review residual book value and accumulated depreciation"
  Exclusive gateway "Residual balance requires clearing?"
  - branch "Yes — residual balance exists": User task
    "Post final journal entries to clear asset balance"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Residual balance
    resolved")
  - branch "No — balance already nil":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Residual balance
    resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Residual balance resolved"
  Service task "Record closure entries in Finance / General Ledger
  System"
  User task "Reconcile asset register to general ledger"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation agreed?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found": User task
    "Investigate and correct discrepancy"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed")
  - branch "Yes — registers agree":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation agreed"
  User task "Confirm final closure sign-off with Asset Management"
  Send task "Return closure confirmation to Asset Management"

Asset Management lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Final closure confirmation
  received from Finance"
  User task "Archive asset documentation in document management"
  User task "Produce asset lifecycle summary report"
  End event "Asset record fully closed — Acquire to Retire lifecycle
  complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Raise and resolve
outstanding items" — label "Resolution overdue (5 business days)" —
triggers escalation End event "Closure escalated to asset manager
for manual intervention".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Investigate and
correct discrepancy" — label "Discrepancy unresolved (3 business
days)" — triggers escalation End event "Reconciliation failure
escalated to Finance manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Asset Management lane with the
message start event and moves through lifecycle history retrieval,
closure-condition verification, and the exclusive gateway; the
outstanding-items branch loops via "Raise and resolve outstanding
items" and rejoins at the closure-conditions merge gateway; from
the merge gateway flow continues through asset marking closed and
tag retirement, then a send task hands off to the Finance lane; the
Finance lane processes residual balance clearing through its own
exclusive gateway and merge, posts to the general ledger, reconciles,
passes through the reconciliation gateway and merge, and returns a
confirmation send task to the Asset Management lane; the Asset
Management lane ends with archiving and a lifecycle summary report
before the end event.

Message flows:
  Service task "Mark asset as closed in ERP Fixed Asset Register" →
  ERP Fixed Asset Register (asset closure status update).
  ERP Fixed Asset Register → User task "Review residual book value
  and accumulated depreciation" (current book value and depreciation
  balance).
  Service task "Record closure entries in Finance / General Ledger
  System" → Finance / General Ledger System (final closure journal
  entries).
  Finance / General Ledger System → User task "Reconcile asset
  register to general ledger" (general ledger asset balance).
  Send task "Notify Finance of asset closure for final accounting" →
  Intermediate message catch event "Asset closure notification
  received" (asset closure notification).
  Send task "Return closure confirmation to Asset Management" →
  Intermediate message catch event "Final closure confirmation
  received from Finance" (final closure sign-off).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Asset Lifecycle History" — read by / written by
"Retrieve full asset lifecycle history".
Data Object "Closure Conditions Checklist" — read by / written by
"Verify all closure conditions are met".
Data Object "Final Journal Entry" — written by "Post final journal
entries to clear asset balance"; read by "Record closure entries in
Finance / General Ledger System".
Data Object "Reconciliation Report" — written by "Reconcile asset
register to general ledger"; read by "Confirm final closure sign-off
with Asset Management".
Data Object "Asset Lifecycle Summary Report" — written by "Produce
asset lifecycle summary report".

Close Asset Record completes the Acquire to Retire lifecycle by
confirming that all disposal, write-off, or transfer outcomes are
reflected in both the fixed asset register and the general ledger,
that residual balances are cleared and reconciled, and that full
asset documentation is archived. It produces no handoff to a further
subprocess; the asset record is permanently retired and the lifecycle
is closed.
```

## V09 — Source to Contract

**Teams and roles involved.**
Source to Contract involves Procurement, Category Management, Legal, Business Owners, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Vendor Management, and sometimes IT Security or Data Protection. Key roles include category manager, sourcing specialist, procurement manager, contract manager, legal counsel, business owner, risk officer, vendor manager, and commercial analyst.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Prospective Supplier, Vendor, Seller, or Service Provider. The process is usually initiated by a sourcing need, renewal requirement, market engagement, or strategic category plan. Suppliers participate through RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, negotiations, due diligence, and contract agreement.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: define sourcing need, analyse spend/category, identify supplier market, issue RFI/RFP/RFQ, evaluate responses, shortlist suppliers, conduct due diligence, negotiate commercial terms, draft contract, approve contract, execute contract, and hand over to supplier management or Procure to Pay.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include sourcing platform, supplier relationship management system, contract lifecycle management system, procurement/ERP system, eTendering platform, risk management system, document management, eSignature platform, supplier portal, and analytics/BI tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key policies include sourcing policy, procurement thresholds, tendering procedure, supplier due diligence policy, conflict of interest policy, delegation of authority, contract approval policy, data protection/security requirements, modern slavery or ESG policy, anti-bribery policy, and contract management procedure.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Suppliers receive market engagement documents, tender packs, specifications, evaluation criteria, contract terms, clarification questions, and award/decline notices. Suppliers provide capability statements, proposals, pricing, compliance responses, risk attestations, insurance details, financial information, and negotiated contract positions.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process records sourcing events, supplier lists, requirements, tender documents, supplier responses, evaluation scores, risk assessments, negotiation records, approvals, contract drafts, executed contracts, obligations, pricing, and supplier master data. Systems provide spend analysis, supplier performance history, contract templates, approval workflows, risk alerts, and contract repository access.

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V09 - Source to Contract (S2C)
Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages
(chevrons), one chevron per stage, in this order:

V09.01. Define Sourcing Need
V09.02. Analyse Spend / Category
V09.03. Identify Supplier Market
V09.04. Issue RFI / RFP / RFQ
V09.05. Evaluate Responses
V09.06. Shortlist Suppliers
V09.07. Conduct Due Diligence
V09.08. Negotiate Commercial Terms
V09.09. Draft Contract
V09.10. Approve Contract
V09.11. Execute Contract
V09.12. Hand Over to Supplier Management / Procure to Pay

This is the demand-side, supplier-selection end-to-end process: a sourcing
need flows through spend analysis, market identification, tendering,
evaluation, due diligence, negotiation and contracting to an executed,
handed-over agreement. The main external participant is the Prospective
Supplier (Vendor / Seller / Service Provider), who takes part through the
RFI / RFP / RFQ, due diligence, negotiation and contract agreement; the
process is triggered by a sourcing need, a renewal requirement or a
strategic category plan. Source to Contract is the sister chain to V02
Procure to Pay and feeds it: the executed contract it produces becomes the
approved supplier and contract pricing that Procure to Pay draws on.
```

**Context diagram prompt.**

```text
Context Diagram: V09 — Source to Contract (S2C).

1. Central system (process-system)
A single central process/system ellipse named "Sourcing Company"
representing the whole organisation that runs the Source to Contract
process. It is the system in context: everything inside it — business
owners, category management, procurement, legal, finance, risk, compliance,
vendor management and the supporting IT systems (sourcing platform,
eTendering, supplier relationship management, contract lifecycle management,
risk and analytics) — is treated as one black box.

2. External entities (external-entity)
The parties OUTSIDE the company that exchange information with it, one
rectangle each:
- Prospective Supplier
- Due Diligence / Reference Agency
- eSignature Provider

3. Layout
"Sourcing Company" sits in the centre. The Prospective Supplier sits to the
RIGHT (the supply side that responds to tenders, is assessed, negotiates and
signs). The Due Diligence / Reference Agency sits to the RIGHT (checks). The
eSignature Provider sits to the RIGHT (signing). The demand originates INSIDE
the company (a sourcing need, renewal or category plan), so no external
demand actor sits on the left. Every external entity connects directly to the
central system with labelled information flows; entities never connect to one
another.

4. Information flows (each a labelled connector between an external entity and
   the central system; show both directions where information flows both ways)
- Sourcing Company → Prospective Supplier: market engagement documents,
  tender pack (RFI / RFP / RFQ), specifications, evaluation criteria,
  clarification questions, contract terms, award / decline notice.
- Prospective Supplier → Sourcing Company: capability statement, proposal,
  pricing, compliance responses, risk attestations, insurance & financial
  information, negotiated contract positions, signed contract.
- Sourcing Company → Due Diligence / Reference Agency: due-diligence check
  request (supplier identity & scope).
- Due Diligence / Reference Agency → Sourcing Company: credit report,
  sanctions / adverse-media results, financial standing.
- Sourcing Company → eSignature Provider: contract for signature / signing
  request.
- eSignature Provider → Sourcing Company: counter-signature & completion
  certificate.

This Context Diagram frames the Sourcing Company as a single system in
context: an internal sourcing need drives the Source to Contract process, the
Prospective Supplier responds to the tender, is assessed, negotiates and
signs, the Due Diligence / Reference Agency provides the checks, and the
eSignature Provider completes execution. The three external entities are
exactly the external actors of the Process Context diagram below, so the two
views stay consistent.
```
