```text
  and Procure to Pay.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — the twelve V09 processes, middle
   band in V09.01 → V09.12 order. Each REALISES the business service shown and
   is the link anchor to its BPMN diagram:
- V09.01 Define Sourcing Need           -> realises Sourcing Strategy Service
- V09.02 Analyse Spend / Category        -> realises Sourcing Strategy Service
- V09.03 Identify Supplier Market        -> realises Sourcing Strategy Service
- V09.04 Issue RFI / RFP / RFQ           -> realises Tendering Service
- V09.05 Evaluate Responses              -> realises Tendering Service
- V09.06 Shortlist Suppliers             -> realises Tendering Service
- V09.07 Conduct Due Diligence           -> realises Supplier Assurance Service
- V09.08 Negotiate Commercial Terms      -> realises Negotiation Service
- V09.09 Draft Contract                  -> realises Contracting Service
- V09.10 Approve Contract                -> realises Contracting Service
- V09.11 Execute Contract                -> realises Contracting Service
- V09.12 Hand Over to Supplier Mgmt / P2P -> realises Supplier Onboarding & Handover Service

5. Applications (Application Component) — the IT systems that support the
   processes, bottom band:
- Sourcing Platform
- Analytics / BI Tools
- Supplier Relationship Management System
- eTendering Platform
- Risk Management System
- Contract Lifecycle Management System
- eSignature Platform
- Procurement / ERP System

6. Relationships
- Prospective Supplier -accesses-> Supplier Portal / Sourcing Channel.
- Supplier Portal / Sourcing Channel -serving-> the Tendering, Assurance,
  Negotiation and Contracting services.
- Each Business Process -realisation-> its Business Service (section 4).
- Each Business Process -served by-> its supporting Application Component
  (serving, application -> process):
    V09.01 <- Sourcing Platform;            V09.02 <- Analytics / BI Tools;
    V09.03 <- Supplier Relationship Mgmt;   V09.04 <- eTendering Platform;
    V09.05 <- Sourcing Platform;            V09.06 <- Sourcing Platform;
    V09.07 <- Risk Management System;       V09.08 <- Sourcing Platform;
    V09.09 <- Contract Lifecycle Mgmt;      V09.10 <- Contract Lifecycle Mgmt;
    V09.11 <- eSignature Platform;          V09.12 <- Supplier Relationship Mgmt + Procurement / ERP System.
- Due Diligence / Reference Agency -serving-> V09.07 Conduct Due Diligence.
- eSignature Provider -serving-> V09.11 Execute Contract.

7. Intent
The Sourcing Service sits top-centre as the headline service. The twelve
Business Processes form the backbone in V09.01 -> V09.12 order so the reader
can trace the sourcing journey and drill from any process straight into its
detailed BPMN model. This one ArchiMate view therefore links to all twelve V09
BPMN process diagrams. The mapping of process -> actors/teams/applications is
the Process <-> Actors / Teams / IT Systems matrix above.
```

### V09.01 — Define Sourcing Need

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.01 Define Sourcing Need — the opening subprocess of the
Source to Contract value chain, in which a sourcing need is identified,
documented, and formally approved before category analysis begins.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal organisation running the
  Define Sourcing Need process, with lanes for the teams involved.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Business Owner
  - Category Management

Pool "Sourcing Platform" — IT system that stores sourcing requests and
  requirement records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, contains all flow)
2. Sourcing Platform (black-box, IT system at the bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Business Owner lane:
  None start event "Sourcing need, renewal trigger, or strategic
    category plan arises"
  User task "Identify and describe sourcing need"
  User task "Complete sourcing request form"
  User task "Obtain initial business owner sign-off"
  Send task "Submit sourcing request to Category Management"

Category Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Sourcing request received from
    Business Owner"
  User task "Review and validate sourcing request"
  Exclusive gateway "Request sufficient and justified?"
    - branch "No — information incomplete": User task "Request
      clarification or additional information from Business Owner"
      Intermediate message catch event "Clarification received from
        Business Owner"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request sufficient
        and justified")
    - branch "Yes — proceed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Request sufficient and justified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Request sufficient and justified"
  User task "Classify sourcing category and assign priority"
  User task "Determine sourcing route and procurement threshold"
  Exclusive gateway "Approval required above threshold?"
    - branch "Yes — above threshold": User task "Escalate for
      procurement manager approval"
      Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received"
      Exclusive gateway "Approved?"
        - branch "Rejected — revise": User task "Return request to
          Business Owner with feedback"
          Intermediate message catch event "Revised request received
            from Business Owner"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approved")
        - branch "Approved — continue": (continues to exclusive
            merge gateway "Approved")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Approved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approval required
        above threshold")
    - branch "No — within threshold": (continues to exclusive merge
        gateway "Approval required above threshold")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approval required above threshold"
  Service task "Record confirmed sourcing need in Sourcing Platform"
  End event "Sourcing need defined and recorded — ready for Analyse
    Spend / Category"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Business Owner lane with the none
start event, moves through identification and submission tasks, then
crosses to the Category Management lane on receipt of the sourcing
request message. The validation gateway loops back through the
clarification catch event until the request is sufficient, then
merges. After classification and routing, the threshold gateway
branches to an escalation path (including an inner approval gateway
that loops if rejected) or passes through directly; both branches
rejoin at the threshold merge gateway before the final service task
and end event.

Message flows:
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Submit sourcing request to Category
  Management") → Sourcing Platform (sourcing request submitted for
  record)
Sourcing Platform → Sourcing Organisation (Service task "Record
  confirmed sourcing need in Sourcing Platform") (confirmed sourcing
  need record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Sourcing Request Form" — written by "Complete sourcing
  request form"; read by "Review and validate sourcing request".
Data Object "Sourcing Need Record" — written by "Record confirmed
  sourcing need in Sourcing Platform"; read by "Classify sourcing
  category and assign priority".
Data Object "Procurement Threshold Assessment" — written by
  "Determine sourcing route and procurement threshold"; read by
  "Escalate for procurement manager approval".

This subprocess establishes the formal basis for a new sourcing event
by capturing the business need, validating it against procurement
policy, confirming the appropriate sourcing route, and obtaining any
required threshold approvals. The confirmed and recorded sourcing need
is then handed to the Analyse Spend / Category subprocess, which will
examine historic expenditure and category dynamics before market
engagement begins.
```

### V09.02 — Analyse Spend / Category

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.02 Analyse Spend / Category — second subprocess in the Source
to Contract value chain, converting raw spend data and category intelligence
into a structured sourcing strategy that guides supplier market identification.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams performing spend and
category analysis.
  Lane "Category Management" — category manager leading the analysis.
  Lane "Procurement" — commercial analyst supporting data and strategy work.
Pool "Analytics / BI Tools" — analytics and business intelligence platform
providing spend data, reports, and category insights.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Analytics / BI Tools" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, contains Category Management and
   Procurement lanes)
2. Analytics / BI Tools (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Category Management lane:
  Message start event "Sourcing need confirmed — received from Define
    Sourcing Need"
  User task "Review sourcing need and confirm category scope"
  Service task "Request spend data and category reports from Analytics /
    BI Tools"
  Intermediate message catch event "Spend data and category reports
    received"
  User task "Analyse historical spend by category and supplier"
  User task "Identify spend patterns, maverick spend, and consolidation
    opportunities"
  User task "Assess category complexity and strategic importance"
  Exclusive gateway "Is sufficient data available to proceed?"
    - branch "Data gaps identified": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Data Sufficient" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Document data gaps and request supplementary data",
      Service task "Request additional spend data from Analytics /
      BI Tools",
      Intermediate message catch event "Additional data received",
      User task "Review supplementary data for completeness"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Data sufficient":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Is sufficient data
      available to proceed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Is sufficient data available to proceed?"
  User task "Develop category strategy and sourcing options"
  User task "Document spend analysis findings and category strategy"
  Send task "Share category strategy with Procurement for review"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Review category strategy and validate commercial
    assumptions"
  Exclusive gateway "Strategy approved?"
    - branch "Revisions required": User task "Provide feedback and
      return to category manager"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Strategy approved?")
    - branch "Approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Strategy approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy approved?"
  User task "Finalise spend analysis report and sourcing strategy
    document"
  End event "Spend analysis and category strategy complete — ready for
    Identify Supplier Market"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Data Sufficient" — labelled "Data request deadline exceeded (5 days)" —
flow continues to End event "Analysis stalled — insufficient data,
escalate to procurement manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Category Management lane with the
message start event, moves through scope review, data request, and spend
analysis tasks, reaches the "Is sufficient data available to proceed?"
gateway; the "Data gaps identified" branch enters the standard-loop
subprocess and exits to the merge gateway; the "Data sufficient" branch
joins at the same merge gateway; flow continues through category strategy
development and documentation, then a send task passes the strategy to
the Procurement lane; Procurement reviews and reaches the "Strategy
approved?" gateway; the "Revisions required" branch returns feedback and
rejoins at the merge gateway; the "Approved" branch also rejoins; flow
then moves to finalise the report and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
Analytics / BI Tools → Category Management lane (spend data and
category reports, in response to service task "Request spend data and
category reports from Analytics / BI Tools")
Analytics / BI Tools → Category Management lane (additional spend data,
in response to service task "Request additional spend data from
Analytics / BI Tools" inside the loop subprocess)
Category Management lane → Analytics / BI Tools (spend data request
initiated by service task "Request spend data and category reports from
Analytics / BI Tools")
Category Management lane → Analytics / BI Tools (supplementary data
request initiated by service task "Request additional spend data from
Analytics / BI Tools")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Sourcing Need Record" — read by User task "Review sourcing
need and confirm category scope".
Data Object "Spend Data Report" — written by Service task "Request spend
data and category reports from Analytics / BI Tools"; read by User task
"Analyse historical spend by category and supplier".
Data Object "Supplementary Data Report" — written by Service task
"Request additional spend data from Analytics / BI Tools"; read by User
task "Review supplementary data for completeness".
Data Object "Spend Analysis Findings" — written by User task "Document
spend analysis findings and category strategy"; read by User task "Review
category strategy and validate commercial assumptions".
Data Object "Category Strategy Document" — written by User task "Develop
category strategy and sourcing options"; read by User task "Finalise
spend analysis report and sourcing strategy document".

This subprocess converts the confirmed sourcing need into an evidence-based
category strategy by extracting and analysing historical spend from the
Analytics / BI Tools platform, identifying patterns and consolidation
opportunities, and developing sourcing options. The validated spend analysis
report and category strategy document are handed to Identify Supplier Market,
where the category manager uses them to map potential suppliers and assess
market conditions.
```

### V09.03 — Identify Supplier Market

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.03 Identify Supplier Market — the third subprocess in the
Source to Contract value chain, in which Category Management and
Procurement map the supplier landscape for the sourcing need confirmed
in Analyse Spend / Category.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams that research and
document the supplier market.
  Lane "Category Management" — category manager leads market
  identification and landscape assessment.
  Lane "Procurement" — sourcing specialist supports supplier research,
  maintains supplier lists, and records findings.
Pool "Supplier Relationship Management System" — SRM platform that
holds supplier master data, performance history, and market lists.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier Relationship Management System" — black-box,
System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. Supplier Relationship Management System (IT system, black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Category Management lane:
  Start event "Spend and category analysis received from
  Analyse Spend / Category"
  User task "Define supplier market scope and boundaries"
  User task "Conduct market research and landscape assessment"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient market data available?"
    - branch "No — data gaps exist": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      Market Data Is Sufficient" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify additional data sources",
      User task "Gather supplementary market intelligence"
      (exits subprocess when data is sufficient)
    - branch "Yes — data adequate": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Sufficient market data available")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient market data available"
  User task "Segment and classify supplier market"
  User task "Identify potential suppliers and initial long-list"

Procurement lane:
  Service task "Query SRM system for known suppliers and
  performance history"
  User task "Research new and emerging suppliers"
  User task "Compile and validate long-list of potential suppliers"
  Exclusive gateway "Long-list meets sourcing requirements?"
    - branch "No — further research needed": User task "Expand supplier
      search criteria"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Long-list meets sourcing
      requirements")
    - branch "Yes — long-list accepted": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Long-list meets sourcing requirements")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Long-list meets sourcing requirements"
  Service task "Record supplier long-list and market findings in
  SRM system"
  User task "Prepare supplier market report"
  End event "Supplier market identified — ready for Issue
  RFI / RFP / RFQ"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Category Management lane at the
start event and moves through market scope definition, market research,
and the data-sufficiency gateway. The "No" branch enters the standard-
loop subprocess and returns to the merge gateway on exit; the "Yes"
branch goes directly to the merge gateway. After the merge, control
passes to supplier segmentation and long-listing. Flow then crosses
to the Procurement lane, where the SRM system is queried, new
suppliers are researched, and the long-list is compiled and validated.
The long-list gateway splits on "No — further research needed" to
expand search criteria, returning to the merge gateway, and on
"Yes — long-list accepted" directly to the merge gateway. After the
merge, findings are recorded in the SRM system, the market report is
prepared, and the process closes at the end event.

Message flows:
Service task "Query SRM system for known suppliers and performance
history" → Supplier Relationship Management System (supplier query
request).
Supplier Relationship Management System → Service task "Query SRM
system for known suppliers and performance history" (supplier master
data, performance history, existing market lists).
Service task "Record supplier long-list and market findings in SRM
system" → Supplier Relationship Management System (validated supplier
long-list and market intelligence records).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Category Analysis Output" — read by User task "Define
supplier market scope and boundaries".
Data Object "Market Research Findings" — written by User task "Conduct
market research and landscape assessment"; read by User task "Segment
and classify supplier market".
Data Object "Supplier Long-List" — written by User task "Compile and
validate long-list of potential suppliers"; read by Service task
"Record supplier long-list and market findings in SRM system".
Data Object "Supplier Market Report" — written by User task "Prepare
supplier market report".

This subprocess produces a validated long-list of potential suppliers
and a documented supplier market report, drawing on SRM system data
and fresh market research. It gives Category Management and Procurement
a clear picture of who could compete for the opportunity and how the
market is structured. The confirmed long-list and market report are
handed to Issue RFI / RFP / RFQ, where Procurement and Legal will
package and dispatch the appropriate market engagement documents.
```

### V09.04 — Issue RFI / RFP / RFQ

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.04 Issue RFI / RFP / RFQ — the subprocess that prepares,
publishes, and manages tender documents to the supplier market, sitting
between Identify Supplier Market and Evaluate Responses in the Source to
Contract value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams preparing and issuing
tender documents.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Procurement (sourcing specialist)
  - Legal (legal counsel)

Pool "Prospective Supplier" — external supplier receiving and responding
to tender documents.

Pool "eTendering Platform" — system publishing tender events, receiving
supplier responses, and managing the tender inbox.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "eTendering Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospective Supplier
2. Sourcing Organisation
3. eTendering Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Shortlisted supplier market received from
    Identify Supplier Market"
  User task "Determine tender type (RFI / RFP / RFQ)"
  User task "Prepare tender pack and specifications"
  Exclusive gateway "Legal review required?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review
      complete")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review
      complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review complete"
  User task "Finalise tender documents and evaluation criteria"
  Service task "Publish tender event on eTendering Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier questions received"
  User task "Collate and review clarification questions"
  User task "Prepare clarification responses"
  Service task "Issue clarification responses via eTendering Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Further clarification needed?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Clarification
      cycle complete")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Clarification
      cycle complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Clarification cycle complete"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Tender submission deadline reached"
  Service task "Close tender event and retrieve responses"
  User task "Confirm receipt of all supplier submissions"
  Exclusive gateway "Minimum valid responses received?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Response
      threshold check complete")
    - branch "No — extend or re-issue": User task "Extend deadline or
      re-issue tender"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Response threshold check
      complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response threshold check complete"
  End event "Supplier responses received — ready for Evaluate Responses"

Legal lane:
  User task "Review tender pack for legal and compliance requirements"
  User task "Advise on terms, IP, and confidentiality obligations"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Publish tender event on eTendering
  Platform" — label "Platform publication timeout" — triggers User task
  "Escalate platform issue to eTendering Platform support" in Procurement
  lane, ending at End event "Publication failure escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Procurement lane with the start event,
moves through tender type determination and pack preparation, then
branches at "Legal review required?" — the Yes branch moves to the Legal
lane where legal counsel reviews and advises before returning to the
Procurement lane at the merge gateway; the No branch bypasses the Legal
lane and rejoins at the same merge. Flow continues through finalisation,
publication, the clarification cycle gateway (looping through question
collation and response issuance on the Yes branch, bypassing on No, both
rejoining the clarification merge), then through the deadline timer, close
and retrieval, and the threshold gateway (the No branch re-issues before
rejoining the threshold merge). Flow ends at the end event in the
Procurement lane.

Message flows:
  eTendering Platform → Prospective Supplier (tender pack, specifications,
    and evaluation criteria published on portal)
  Prospective Supplier → eTendering Platform (clarification questions
    submitted)
  eTendering Platform → Sourcing Organisation / Procurement lane
    (clarification questions forwarded to sourcing specialist)
  Sourcing Organisation / Procurement lane → eTendering Platform
    (clarification responses issued for broadcast)
  eTendering Platform → Prospective Supplier (clarification responses
    distributed)
  Prospective Supplier → eTendering Platform (tender submission / proposal
    response submitted)
  eTendering Platform → Sourcing Organisation / Procurement lane
    (supplier submissions retrieved on deadline)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Tender Pack" — written by "Prepare tender pack and
  specifications"; read by "Review tender pack for legal and compliance
  requirements"; read by "Finalise tender documents and evaluation
  criteria".
Data Object "Evaluation Criteria" — written by "Finalise tender documents
  and evaluation criteria"; read by "Confirm receipt of all supplier
  submissions".
Data Object "Clarification Log" — written by "Collate and review
  clarification questions"; read by "Prepare clarification responses";
  read by "Issue clarification responses via eTendering Platform".
Data Object "Supplier Submissions" — written by "Close tender event and
  retrieve responses"; read by "Confirm receipt of all supplier
  submissions".

This subprocess takes the shortlisted supplier market from Identify
Supplier Market and produces a complete, legally reviewed tender event —
covering RFI, RFP, or RFQ as appropriate — that has been published,
clarified, and closed with a validated set of supplier submissions in
hand. Those submissions are handed to Evaluate Responses, where they will
be scored against the published evaluation criteria.
```

### V09.05 — Evaluate Responses

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.05 Evaluate Responses — evaluates supplier tender responses
against defined criteria within the Source to Contract value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams that score, review, and
  record the evaluation of supplier responses.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Procurement (commercial analyst)
  - Business Owner (business owner)
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — external suppliers who submitted responses
  and may answer clarification questions.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — IT system that stores evaluation scorecards,
  response documents, and scoring results.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospective Supplier
2. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, process flow here)
3. Sourcing Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Procurement (commercial analyst) lane:
  Message start event "Supplier responses received from Issue RFI / RFP /
    RFQ"
  User task "Register and log all supplier responses"
  Service task "Retrieve response documents from Sourcing Platform"
  User task "Distribute evaluation packs to evaluation panel"
  User task "Review commercial and pricing submissions"
  User task "Score commercial responses against evaluation criteria"
  Intermediate message catch event "Clarification answer received from
    Prospective Supplier"
  User task "Record clarification answers in evaluation record"
  User task "Consolidate evaluation scores from all panel members"
  Exclusive gateway "Scores complete and agreed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scores complete
      and agreed")
  - branch "No — scores missing or disputed": User task "Chase missing
      scores and resolve scoring disputes"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scores complete and agreed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scores complete and agreed"
  User task "Prepare evaluation summary report"
  Service task "Upload evaluation summary to Sourcing Platform"
  End event "Evaluation report complete — ready for Shortlist Suppliers"

Business Owner (business owner) lane:
  User task "Review technical and requirement-fit submissions"
  User task "Score responses against business requirements criteria"
  Send task "Send clarification questions to Prospective Supplier"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Chase missing scores and
  resolve scoring disputes" — labelled "Scoring deadline exceeded" —
  triggers End event "Evaluation stalled — escalate to Procurement
  Manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Procurement lane with the message start
event, passes through response registration, document retrieval, and pack
distribution; control then moves to the Business Owner lane for technical
review and scoring in parallel with the Procurement lane's commercial
review and scoring; the Business Owner lane issues clarification questions
via send task, and the Procurement lane catches the reply via the
intermediate message catch event before recording answers; both scoring
streams rejoin at the Procurement lane's consolidation step, which leads
to the exclusive gateway "Scores complete and agreed?", whose No branch
passes through the chase-and-resolve task and the Yes branch proceeds
directly, both merging at the exclusive merge gateway "Scores complete and
agreed" before the summary report is prepared, uploaded, and the end
event is reached.

Message flows:
Prospective Supplier → Procurement (commercial analyst) lane (supplier
  tender responses — proposals, pricing, compliance documents)
Business Owner (business owner) lane → Prospective Supplier (clarification
  questions)
Prospective Supplier → Procurement (commercial analyst) lane (clarification
  answers)
Procurement (commercial analyst) lane → Sourcing Platform (register
  responses — log of received submissions)
Sourcing Platform → Procurement (commercial analyst) lane (response
  documents retrieved for distribution)
Procurement (commercial analyst) lane → Sourcing Platform (evaluation
  summary report uploaded)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Supplier Response Pack" — written by User task "Register and
  log all supplier responses"; read by User task "Distribute evaluation
  packs to evaluation panel".
Data Object "Evaluation Scorecard" — written by User task "Score commercial
  responses against evaluation criteria" and User task "Score responses
  against business requirements criteria"; read by User task "Consolidate
  evaluation scores from all panel members".
Data Object "Clarification Record" — written by User task "Record
  clarification answers in evaluation record"; read by User task
  "Consolidate evaluation scores from all panel members".
Data Object "Evaluation Summary Report" — written by User task "Prepare
  evaluation summary report"; read by Service task "Upload evaluation
  summary to Sourcing Platform".

V09.05 Evaluate Responses takes the supplier submissions received from the
RFI/RFP/RFQ stage and puts them through a structured scoring process
covering both commercial and business-requirements dimensions, resolving
any clarifications with suppliers along the way. Scores are consolidated,
disputed, and agreed before a final evaluation summary report is produced
and stored on the Sourcing Platform. That report hands a ranked, evidenced
view of all respondents to the Shortlist Suppliers subprocess.
```

### V09.06 — Shortlist Suppliers

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.06 Shortlist Suppliers — sits within the Source to Contract
value chain, receiving evaluated supplier responses and producing a confirmed
shortlist for due diligence.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal organisation running the
shortlisting process, containing Procurement, Category Management, and
Business Owner lanes.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — IT system supporting shortlisting decisions,
scoring, and shortlist recording.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, spanning all lanes)
2. Sourcing Platform (black-box, bottom)

Lane order within Sourcing Organisation, top to bottom:
- Procurement (procurement manager)
- Category Management (category manager)
- Business Owner (business owner)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Evaluated supplier scores received from
    Evaluate Responses"
  User task "Review evaluation scores and ranking"
  User task "Apply minimum threshold criteria to evaluation results"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient suppliers meet threshold?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Sufficient suppliers meet threshold")
  - branch "No, threshold too high": User task "Adjust threshold
      criteria with justification"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient suppliers meet
      threshold")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient suppliers meet threshold"
  Send task "Circulate ranked evaluation summary to Category
    Management and Business Owner"

Category Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Ranked evaluation summary received"
  User task "Review category strategy alignment of ranked suppliers"
  User task "Propose shortlist candidates based on category plan"
  Send task "Submit category shortlist proposal to Procurement"

Business Owner lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Ranked evaluation summary received"
  User task "Assess fit of ranked suppliers against business
    requirements"
  User task "Submit business owner shortlist preferences to Procurement"

Procurement lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Category shortlist proposal and
    business owner preferences received"
  User task "Consolidate inputs into draft shortlist"
  Exclusive gateway "Agreement on shortlist reached?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Agreement
      on shortlist reached")
  - branch "No, objections raised": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
      Until Shortlist Agreed" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Facilitate shortlist review meeting with Category
        Management and Business Owner",
      User task "Revise draft shortlist based on meeting outcome",
      User task "Circulate revised shortlist for sign-off"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Agreement on shortlist
      reached")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Agreement on shortlist reached"
  User task "Record approved shortlist in Sourcing Platform"
  Service task "Retrieve confirmation of shortlist saved"
  User task "Notify shortlisted suppliers of selection"
  User task "Notify unsuccessful suppliers at this stage"
  Exclusive gateway "Shortlist requires Risk or Compliance review?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate shortlist to Risk and
      Compliance for pre-due-diligence check"
    Intermediate message catch event "Risk and Compliance
      pre-check outcome received"
    Exclusive gateway "Pre-check passed?"
    - branch "Passed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Pre-check passed")
    - branch "Failed — supplier removed": User task "Remove
        supplier from shortlist and notify"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pre-check passed")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Pre-check passed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Shortlist requires Risk
      or Compliance review")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Shortlist
      requires Risk or Compliance review")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Shortlist requires Risk or Compliance review"
  End event "Approved shortlist confirmed — ready for Conduct Due
    Diligence"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
Until Shortlist Agreed" — label "72-hour review deadline exceeded" —
triggers End event "Shortlist escalated to procurement manager for
decision".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs from Procurement start through threshold
review and the "Sufficient suppliers meet threshold" gateway; after
merging, the ranked summary is sent simultaneously to Category
Management and Business Owner lanes via send and message catch
events; both lanes return proposals to Procurement via send and
message catch events; Procurement consolidates and passes through
the "Agreement on shortlist reached" gateway, looping through the
expanded subprocess when objections arise and merging on agreement;
flow continues through shortlist recording, supplier notification,
and the "Shortlist requires Risk or Compliance review" gateway, with
both branches merging before the end event.

Message flows:
Sourcing Organisation (User task "Record approved shortlist in
  Sourcing Platform") → Sourcing Platform (shortlist data submitted
  for storage)
Sourcing Platform → Sourcing Organisation (Service task "Retrieve
  confirmation of shortlist saved") (confirmation of record saved)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Evaluation Score Summary" — read by User task "Review
  evaluation scores and ranking".
Data Object "Threshold Criteria" — read by / written by User task
  "Apply minimum threshold criteria to evaluation results"; written
  by User task "Adjust threshold criteria with justification".
Data Object "Category Shortlist Proposal" — written by User task
  "Propose shortlist candidates based on category plan"; read by
  User task "Consolidate inputs into draft shortlist".
Data Object "Business Owner Shortlist Preferences" — written by
  User task "Submit business owner shortlist preferences to
  Procurement"; read by User task "Consolidate inputs into draft
  shortlist".
Data Object "Draft Shortlist" — written by User task "Consolidate
  inputs into draft shortlist"; read by User task "Facilitate
  shortlist review meeting with Category Management and Business
  Owner".
Data Object "Approved Shortlist" — written by User task "Record
  approved shortlist in Sourcing Platform"; read by User task
  "Notify shortlisted suppliers of selection".

V09.06 Shortlist Suppliers takes the scored, ranked supplier
responses from the evaluation subprocess and, through a structured
review involving Procurement, Category Management, and Business
Owner, produces a formally agreed and recorded shortlist. Threshold
criteria are applied, inputs are consolidated, and any objections
are resolved through a time-boxed loop. Where required, a risk and
compliance pre-check further refines the list. The confirmed
shortlist is then handed to Conduct Due Diligence, where shortlisted
suppliers are subjected to detailed scrutiny before commercial terms
are negotiated.
```

### V09.07 — Conduct Due Diligence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.07 Conduct Due Diligence — the seventh subprocess in the
Source to Contract value chain, in which Risk, Compliance, and IT
Security / Data Protection assess shortlisted suppliers against
regulatory, financial, ethical, and security requirements before
commercial negotiations begin.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the buying organisation conducting due
diligence across risk, compliance, and security disciplines.
  Lane "Risk" — risk officer leads financial, legal, and operational
  risk assessment.
  Lane "Compliance" — compliance officer checks regulatory, ESG,
  anti-bribery, and modern slavery requirements.
  Lane "IT Security / Data Protection" — security lead assesses
  information security and data protection posture.

Pool "Prospective Supplier" — the shortlisted supplier(s) responding
to due diligence requests.

Pool "Due Diligence / Reference Agency" — external agency providing
verification, reference checks, or financial screening data.

Pool "Risk Management System" — IT system recording risk assessments,
compliance findings, and due diligence outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Due Diligence / Reference Agency" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Risk Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospective Supplier
2. Due Diligence / Reference Agency
3. Sourcing Organisation
4. Risk Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Risk lane:
  Message start event "Shortlisted suppliers received from Shortlist
  Suppliers"
  User task "Define due diligence scope and criteria"
  Service task "Initiate supplier due diligence record in Risk
  Management System"
  Send task "Issue due diligence questionnaire to supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier due diligence response
  received"
  Send task "Request third-party verification from Due Diligence /
  Reference Agency"
  Intermediate message catch event "Third-party verification report
  received"
  User task "Assess financial and operational risk"
  Parallel gateway "Begin specialist assessments"
    - branch "Compliance assessment": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Specialist assessments complete")
    - branch "IT security assessment": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Specialist assessments complete")
    - branch "Risk assessment continues": User task "Assess legal and
      reputational risk" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Specialist assessments complete")
  Parallel merge gateway "Specialist assessments complete"
  User task "Consolidate due diligence findings"
  Exclusive gateway "All suppliers assessed?"
    - branch "No — more suppliers pending": (loop repeats)
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All
      suppliers assessed")
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Suppliers Assessed" (standard
  loop) containing, in order: User task "Select next shortlisted
  supplier", User task "Assess financial and operational risk",
  Send task "Issue due diligence questionnaire to supplier",
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier due diligence response
  received"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All suppliers assessed"
  User task "Compile overall due diligence summary report"
  Exclusive gateway "Any supplier fails due diligence?"
    - branch "Yes — supplier rejected": Send task "Issue decline
      notice to rejected supplier"
      End event "Supplier rejected — due diligence complete"
    - branch "No — all pass": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Due diligence outcome determined")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Due diligence outcome determined"
  End event "Due diligence passed — ready for Negotiate Commercial
  Terms"

Compliance lane:
  User task "Check regulatory, ESG, anti-bribery and modern slavery
  compliance"
  User task "Record compliance findings"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Specialist assessments
  complete")

IT Security / Data Protection lane:
  User task "Assess information security and data protection posture"
  User task "Record security and data protection findings"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Specialist assessments
  complete")

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Repeat Until All Suppliers
Assessed" subprocess — label "Due diligence deadline exceeded" —
triggers End event "Due diligence timed out — escalation required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Risk lane with the message start
event, moves through scope definition, record initiation, and
questionnaire dispatch, then waits for supplier and agency responses
before the parallel gateway splits work across the Risk, Compliance,
and IT Security / Data Protection lanes simultaneously; all three
branches rejoin at the parallel merge gateway "Specialist assessments
complete"; consolidated findings feed the loop subprocess for
remaining suppliers, then proceed to summary report and the exclusive
gateway on pass/fail outcome, with the rejection branch ending locally
and the pass branch ending at the handover end event.

Message flows:
  Send task "Issue due diligence questionnaire to supplier" →
  Prospective Supplier (due diligence questionnaire and document
  request)
  Prospective Supplier → Intermediate message catch event "Supplier
  due diligence response received" (capability statements, compliance
  responses, risk attestations, insurance and financial information)
  Send task "Request third-party verification from Due Diligence /
  Reference Agency" → Due Diligence / Reference Agency (verification
  and reference check request)
  Due Diligence / Reference Agency → Intermediate message catch event
  "Third-party verification report received" (financial screening,
  reference checks, and verification report)
  Send task "Issue decline notice to rejected supplier" → Prospective
  Supplier (decline notice)
  Service task "Initiate supplier due diligence record in Risk
  Management System" → Risk Management System (new due diligence
  record)
  User task "Record compliance findings" → Risk Management System
  (compliance assessment data)
  User task "Record security and data protection findings" → Risk
  Management System (security and data protection assessment data)
  User task "Consolidate due diligence findings" → Risk Management
  System (consolidated findings)
  Risk Management System → User task "Assess financial and operational
  risk" (supplier performance history and prior risk alerts)
  User task "Compile overall due diligence summary report" → Risk
  Management System (final due diligence summary report)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Due Diligence Questionnaire" — written by Send task
"Issue due diligence questionnaire to supplier"; read by User task
"Assess financial and operational risk".
Data Object "Supplier Due Diligence Response" — written by
Intermediate message catch event "Supplier due diligence response
received"; read by User task "Assess financial and operational risk",
User task "Check regulatory, ESG, anti-bribery and modern slavery
compliance", User task "Assess information security and data
protection posture".
Data Object "Third-Party Verification Report" — written by
Intermediate message catch event "Third-party verification report
received"; read by User task "Assess financial and operational risk",
User task "Record compliance findings".
Data Object "Due Diligence Summary Report" — written by User task
"Compile overall due diligence summary report"; read by Exclusive
gateway "Any supplier fails due diligence?".

Conduct Due Diligence takes the shortlist produced by Shortlist
Suppliers and subjects each candidate to coordinated risk, compliance,
and IT security assessment, drawing on supplier-supplied evidence and
independent third-party verification. Findings are consolidated into a
due diligence summary report held in the Risk Management System.
Suppliers that fail are formally declined; those that pass are cleared
for commercial engagement and handed to Negotiate Commercial Terms
with their assessment record attached.
```

### V09.08 — Negotiate Commercial Terms

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.08 Negotiate Commercial Terms — the subprocess in which
Procurement, Category Management, and Finance engage the Prospective
Supplier to reach agreed commercial positions, forming the basis for
contract drafting.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams conducting the
negotiation.
  Lane "Procurement" — procurement manager leading the negotiation.
  Lane "Category Management" — category manager providing category
  strategy and commercial insight.
  Lane "Finance" — commercial analyst validating financial positions
  and approvals.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — the external supplier participating in
negotiation exchanges.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — IT system recording negotiation events,
positions, and agreed terms.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Sourcing Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospective Supplier
2. Sourcing Organisation
3. Sourcing Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Procurement lane:
  Message start event "Shortlisted supplier received from Shortlist
  Suppliers"
  User task "Review shortlist and confirm negotiation scope"
  User task "Prepare negotiation strategy and opening position"
  Send task "Issue opening commercial position to supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier counter-position received"
  User task "Assess supplier counter-position"
  Exclusive gateway "Counter-position acceptable?"
    - branch "Yes — position accepted": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Counter-position acceptable?")
    - branch "No — further negotiation required":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Position Agreed" (standard loop)
      containing, in order:
        User task "Prepare revised negotiation position",
        Send task "Issue revised position to supplier",
        Intermediate message catch event "Supplier revised response
        received",
        User task "Review revised supplier response"
      (exits subprocess)
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Counter-position
      acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Counter-position acceptable?"
  User task "Record agreed commercial terms"
  Send task "Send agreed terms summary to supplier for confirmation"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier confirmation received"
  Exclusive gateway "Supplier confirms terms?"
    - branch "Confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Supplier confirms terms?")
    - branch "Not confirmed — further clarification needed":
      User task "Resolve outstanding points with supplier"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier confirms terms?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier confirms terms?"
  User task "Compile negotiation record and handover pack"
  End event "Commercial terms agreed — ready for Draft Contract"

Category Management lane:
  User task "Contribute category strategy inputs to negotiation
  position"
  User task "Review counter-position against category plan"

Finance lane:
  User task "Validate financial parameters and pricing model"
  User task "Confirm approved financial position"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Position Agreed", labelled "Negotiation deadline exceeded", leading to:
End event "Negotiation failed — escalate to procurement manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow begins in the Procurement lane with the
message start event, passes through negotiation preparation and the
opening position send task, then waits for the supplier counter. The
exclusive gateway "Counter-position acceptable?" branches to immediate
merge on acceptance, or to the standard-loop subprocess on rejection,
both rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway. After terms are recorded
and the supplier confirms, the final compile task closes in the
Procurement lane. Category Management contributes inputs during
position preparation and counter-position review; Finance validates
pricing before the opening position is issued and confirms the approved
financial position before terms are recorded. All branches of both
gateways rejoin their respective merge gateways before flow continues.

Message flows:
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Issue opening commercial position to
supplier") → Prospective Supplier (opening commercial position
document).
Prospective Supplier → Sourcing Organisation (Intermediate message
catch event "Supplier counter-position received") (supplier
counter-position).
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Issue revised position to supplier")
→ Prospective Supplier (revised negotiation position).
Prospective Supplier → Sourcing Organisation (Intermediate message
catch event "Supplier revised response received") (supplier revised
response).
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Send agreed terms summary to supplier
for confirmation") → Prospective Supplier (agreed terms summary).
Prospective Supplier → Sourcing Organisation (Intermediate message
catch event "Supplier confirmation received") (supplier confirmation).
Sourcing Organisation (User task "Record agreed commercial terms") →
Sourcing Platform (negotiation record and agreed commercial terms).
Sourcing Organisation (User task "Compile negotiation record and
handover pack") → Sourcing Platform (completed negotiation record and
handover pack).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Negotiation Strategy Document" — written by User task
"Prepare negotiation strategy and opening position"; read by User task
"Contribute category strategy inputs to negotiation position".
Data Object "Supplier Counter-Position" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Supplier counter-position received"; read by User
task "Assess supplier counter-position".
Data Object "Revised Supplier Response" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Supplier revised response received"; read by User
task "Review revised supplier response".
Data Object "Agreed Commercial Terms Summary" — written by User task
"Record agreed commercial terms"; read by Send task "Send agreed terms
summary to supplier for confirmation" and User task "Compile
negotiation record and handover pack".
Data Object "Negotiation Record and Handover Pack" — written by User
task "Compile negotiation record and handover pack"; read by End event
"Commercial terms agreed — ready for Draft Contract".

This subprocess takes a shortlisted supplier through structured
commercial negotiation, iterating on positions until both parties reach
agreement on pricing, terms, and conditions. The standard-loop
subprocess manages repeated exchanges, bounded by a deadline that
triggers escalation if no agreement is reached in time. On successful
conclusion, the agreed terms summary and negotiation record are logged
in the Sourcing Platform and handed to Draft Contract, where Legal and
Contract Management will translate the agreed positions into a formal
contract document.
```

### V09.09 — Draft Contract

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.09 Draft Contract — the ninth subprocess in the Source to
Contract value chain, in which Legal and Contract Management convert
agreed commercial terms into a complete, reviewed, and supplier-accepted

1. Pools & Lanes

  process, containing Legal and Contract Management lanes.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Legal (legal counsel)
  - Contract Management (contract manager)
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — the external supplier who receives, reviews,
  and returns a marked-up draft contract.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management System" — the CLM platform used to
  store templates, manage draft versions, and record the agreed draft.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospective Supplier
2. Sourcing Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Legal above Contract
   Management)
3. Contract Lifecycle Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Negotiated commercial terms received from
    Negotiate Commercial Terms"
  Service task "Retrieve contract template from CLM system"
  User task "Populate template with agreed commercial terms"
  User task "Incorporate legal clauses and jurisdiction requirements"
  User task "Internal legal review of draft"

  - branch "No — amendments required":
      User task "Revise draft to address legal review comments"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review passed")
  - branch "Yes — draft approved internally":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review passed"
  Service task "Upload approved internal draft to CLM system"
  Send task "Issue draft contract to Prospective Supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Supplier accepts draft?"
  - branch "No — supplier returns marked-up draft":
      User task "Review supplier redlines and proposed amendments"
      Exclusive gateway "Redlines acceptable?"
      - branch "No — escalation required":
          User task "Escalate unresolved redlines to procurement and
            category management"
          Intermediate message catch event "Escalation decision received"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Redlines acceptable")
      - branch "Yes — incorporate changes":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Redlines acceptable")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Redlines acceptable"
      User task "Revise draft to reflect accepted redlines"
      Service task "Upload revised draft to CLM system"
      Send task "Reissue revised draft to Prospective Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts draft")
  - branch "Yes — supplier accepts":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts draft")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts draft"

Contract Management lane:
  User task "Confirm final draft is complete and all schedules attached"
  User task "Record agreed draft in CLM system"
  End event "Agreed contract draft recorded — ready for Approve Contract"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Internal legal review of
  draft" — label "Review overdue (5 business days)" — on trigger,
  escalates to a User task "Notify legal counsel manager of overdue
  review" in the Legal lane, then flow rejoins after the review task.
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Supplier response received" (first instance, after draft issued) —

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with the message start
  event, proceeds through template retrieval, population, and legal

Message flows:

  Legal lane Service task "Upload revised draft to CLM system" →

  Contract Management lane User task "Record agreed draft in CLM system"
    → Contract Lifecycle Management System (agreed final draft record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Contract Template" — read by "Retrieve contract template

  system".
Data Object "Draft Contract" — written by "Populate template with agreed

  redlines and proposed amendments".
Data Object "Agreed Contract Draft" — written by "Confirm final draft is
  complete and all schedules attached"; read by "Record agreed draft in

V09.09 Draft Contract converts the negotiated commercial terms into a
legally reviewed and supplier-agreed contract document. Legal retrieves
a CLM template, populates and reviews it internally, issues it to the
supplier, and iterates on any redlines until the supplier accepts. Contract
Management then confirms completeness and records the agreed draft in the
CLM system, handing a complete, versioned contract document to V09.10
Approve Contract for formal internal authorisation.
```

### V09.10 — Approve Contract

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.10 Approve Contract — the contract approval subprocess within

1. Pools & Lanes

approval process, containing the Procurement, Business Owner, and
Finance lanes.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management System" — the CLM system that
hosts approval workflows, contract drafts, and the contract repository.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation (white-box)
2. Contract Lifecycle Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Procurement lane (procurement manager):
  Message start event "Contract draft received from Draft Contract"

    "Draft acceptable for approval routing")

  - branch "No — approval rejected or escalation raised":

        Legal for redraft"

    - branch "Yes — resolve and resubmit": (continues to exclusive
        merge gateway "Can issues be resolved without redraft")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Can issues be resolved without redraft"
    User task "Address comments and update approval record in CLM"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All required approvals
    obtained")
  - branch "Yes — all approvals obtained": (continues to exclusive
    merge gateway "All required approvals obtained")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All required approvals obtained"
  Service task "Record final approval in CLM system"
  User task "Confirm delegation of authority compliance"
  Send task "Notify stakeholders of contract approval"
  End event "Contract approved — ready for Execute Contract"

Business Owner lane (business owner):
  User task "Review contract terms against business requirements"
  Exclusive gateway "Business Owner approves?"
  - branch "No — conditions or rejection": User task "Record objection
    and required changes"
    Send task "Send rejection response to Procurement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Business Owner approves")
  - branch "Yes — approved": User task "Submit approval in CLM system"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Business Owner approves")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Business Owner approves"

Finance lane (finance controller):
  User task "Review contract for financial exposure and budget
    alignment"
  Exclusive gateway "Finance approves?"
  - branch "No — conditions or rejection": User task "Record financial
    concern and required changes"
    Send task "Send rejection response to Procurement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance approves")
  - branch "Yes — approved": User task "Submit approval in CLM system"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Finance approves")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Finance approves"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Assign approvers and
set delegation of authority level" — label "Approval deadline
exceeded" — triggers Send task "Escalate overdue approval to
procurement manager", then flow rejoins at Exclusive gateway "All
required approvals obtained?" on the No branch.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Procurement lane with the message
start event, passes through the commercial review gateway — the No
branch ends with its own End event returning to Draft Contract; the
Yes branch merges and continues to CLM workflow initiation. After
approvers are assigned, the process waits via two intermediate message
catch events for the Business Owner and Finance responses, which are
generated in their respective lanes following internal gateway
branches that each resolve at their own merge gateways before sending

whose resolve branch merges and loops back to the all-approvals
```
