```text
Message flows:
Contract Lifecycle Management System → Procurement lane "Initiate
  approval workflow in CLM system" (approval workflow trigger and
  contract draft loaded for review).
Procurement lane "Initiate approval workflow in CLM system" →
  Contract Lifecycle Management System (approval workflow initiation
  request).
Business Owner lane "Submit approval in CLM system" →
  Contract Lifecycle Management System (business owner approval
  record).
Finance lane "Submit approval in CLM system" →
  Contract Lifecycle Management System (finance approval record).
Business Owner lane "Send rejection response to Procurement" →
  Procurement lane intermediate message catch event "Business Owner
  approval response received" (rejection or conditional approval
  response).
Finance lane "Send rejection response to Procurement" →
  Procurement lane intermediate message catch event "Finance approval
  response received" (rejection or conditional approval response).
Business Owner lane "Submit approval in CLM system" →
  Procurement lane intermediate message catch event "Business Owner
  approval response received" (positive approval response).
Finance lane "Submit approval in CLM system" →
  Procurement lane intermediate message catch event "Finance approval
  response received" (positive approval response).
Procurement lane "Record final approval in CLM system" →
  Contract Lifecycle Management System (final approved contract
  record).
Contract Lifecycle Management System → Procurement lane "Record final
  approval in CLM system" (contract repository confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Contract Draft" — read by User task "Review contract
  draft for commercial completeness"; read by User task "Review
  contract terms against business requirements"; read by User task
  "Review contract for financial exposure and budget alignment".
Data Object "Approval Record" — written by User task "Submit approval
  in CLM system" (Business Owner lane); written by User task "Submit
  approval in CLM system" (Finance lane); written by Service task
  "Record final approval in CLM system"; read by User task "Confirm
  delegation of authority compliance".
Data Object "Revision Notes" — written by Send task "Return draft to
  Legal with revision notes"; written by User task "Address comments
  and update approval record in CLM".
Data Object "Delegation of Authority Register" — read by User task
  "Assign approvers and set delegation of authority level"; read by
  User task "Confirm delegation of authority compliance".

Approve Contract receives the completed contract draft from the Draft
Contract subprocess and routes it through a structured, multi-lane
approval cycle governed by delegation-of-authority policy. Procurement
confirms commercial completeness, Business Owner validates business fit,
and Finance confirms budget alignment and financial exposure, all recorded
in the Contract Lifecycle Management System. Once all required approvals
are secured and compliance confirmed, the fully approved contract is handed
to Execute Contract for signature.
```

### V09.11 — Execute Contract

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.11 Execute Contract — the subprocess in which the finalised,
approved contract is formally signed by all parties and recorded, handing
an executed agreement to supplier management and Procure to Pay.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams that manage contract
execution.
  Lane "Contract Management" — contract manager who coordinates execution.
  Lane "Legal" — legal counsel who performs final review before signing.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — the external supplier who countersigns the
contract.
Pool "eSignature Platform" — the electronic signature system that routes
and captures signatures.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospective Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "eSignature Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Prospective Supplier" — top.
Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — middle (white-box).
Pool "eSignature Platform" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Contract Management lane:
  Message start event "Approved contract received from Approve Contract"
  User task "Prepare contract execution pack"
  User task "Confirm signatory authorities and delegation of authority"
  Exclusive gateway "Correct signatories confirmed?"
  - branch "No": User task "Escalate and resolve signatory issue"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Correct signatories confirmed")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Correct signatories
    confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Correct signatories confirmed"
  Send task "Initiate eSignature workflow"
  Intermediate message catch event "eSignature workflow accepted by platform"
  User task "Monitor signature progress"
  Intermediate message catch event "All signatures received"
  User task "Retrieve fully executed contract from eSignature Platform"
  User task "Register executed contract in Contract Lifecycle Management
    System"
  Send task "Notify Prospective Supplier of executed contract"
  End event "Executed contract registered — ready for Hand Over to Supplier
    Management / Procure to Pay"

Legal lane:
  User task "Perform final legal review of execution pack"
  User task "Confirm internal organisation signature applied"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Monitor signature progress"
  — label "Signature deadline exceeded" — triggers User task "Chase
  outstanding signatures" in the Contract Management lane, which loops back
  to the Monitor signature progress task until all signatures are received.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The flow begins in the Contract Management lane with the
start event, moves through preparation and signatory confirmation, then
passes to the Legal lane for final review and internal signing before
returning to Contract Management for eSignature initiation. The signatory
gateway has a "No" branch to the escalation task and a "Yes" branch, both
rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway before continuing. After all
signatures are received the flow continues through retrieval, registration,
and supplier notification to the end event.

Message flows:
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Initiate eSignature workflow") →
  eSignature Platform (contract execution pack with signature request).
eSignature Platform → Sourcing Organisation (Contract Management, message
  catch event "eSignature workflow accepted by platform") (platform
  acceptance confirmation).
eSignature Platform → Sourcing Organisation (Contract Management, message
  catch event "All signatures received") (fully signed contract document).
Sourcing Organisation (User task "Retrieve fully executed contract from
  eSignature Platform") → eSignature Platform (retrieval request).
eSignature Platform → Sourcing Organisation (executed contract file
  returned).
Sourcing Organisation (Send task "Notify Prospective Supplier of executed
  contract") → Prospective Supplier (executed contract notification).
Prospective Supplier → eSignature Platform (countersignature applied via
  supplier portal).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Contract Execution Pack" — written by User task "Prepare
  contract execution pack"; read by User task "Perform final legal review
  of execution pack" and Send task "Initiate eSignature workflow".
Data Object "Delegation of Authority Record" — read by User task "Confirm
  signatory authorities and delegation of authority".
Data Object "Executed Contract" — written by User task "Retrieve fully
  executed contract from eSignature Platform"; read by User task "Register
  executed contract in Contract Lifecycle Management System" and Send task
  "Notify Prospective Supplier of executed contract".

This subprocess takes the approved contract from the approval stage,
confirms and coordinates the required signatories, routes the document
through the eSignature Platform for internal and supplier countersignature,
and registers the fully executed contract on record. It hands a legally
binding, signed agreement to the Hand Over to Supplier Management /
Procure to Pay subprocess so that obligations, performance management, and
purchasing activity can commence.
```

### V09.12 — Hand Over to Supplier Management / Procure to Pay

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V09.12 Hand Over to Supplier Management / Procure to Pay —
the final subprocess of Source to Contract, transferring the executed
contract and all sourcing records to Vendor Management and Procure to Pay
so that ongoing supplier relationships and purchasing transactions can begin.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — the internal teams that carry out the
handover, represented as a white-box pool with lanes for Contract
Management, Vendor Management, and any cross-functional coordination.
- Lane "Contract Management" (contract manager)
- Lane "Vendor Management" (vendor manager)
Pool "Supplier Relationship Management System" — SRM system that stores
supplier master data, onboarding records, and relationship history.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — ERP or procurement system that receives
supplier and contract data to enable purchasing transactions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Sourcing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier Relationship Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Sourcing Organisation
2. Supplier Relationship Management System
3. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Sourcing Organisation)

Contract Management lane:
  Message start event "Executed contract received from Execute Contract"
  User task "Compile handover package"
  User task "Brief vendor manager on contract obligations and key terms"
  Send task "Transmit contract and sourcing records to Vendor Management"
  User task "Register contract in supplier relationship management system"
  Service task "Send contract data and obligations to SRM System"
  User task "Confirm supplier master record is complete"
  Exclusive gateway "Supplier master record complete?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier master
    record complete")
  - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Master Record Complete"
    (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Identify missing
    supplier master data fields", User task "Request and capture missing
    data"
    (exits subprocess, continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier master
    record complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier master record complete"
  Service task "Create or update supplier in Procurement / ERP System"
  Send task "Notify Vendor Management that supplier is active in ERP"

Vendor Management lane:
  User task "Receive and review handover package"
  User task "Accept ownership of supplier relationship"
  User task "Set up supplier governance and review schedule"
  User task "Confirm handover complete to Contract Management"
  End event "Supplier handed over — supplier management and Procure to Pay
  operational"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Master Record Complete" — label "Master data overdue (5 business days)" —
flow continues to End event "Handover blocked — master data incomplete;
escalated to procurement manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Contract Management lane with the
message start event, moves through package compilation, briefing, and
transmission to Vendor Management; the SRM registration and gateway
resolve whether the supplier master record is complete, looping through
the expanded subprocess if not; once complete, the ERP creation task
fires and a notification is sent to Vendor Management. Flow crosses to the
Vendor Management lane where the package is reviewed, ownership accepted,
governance scheduled, and confirmation returned to Contract Management
before the end event.

Message flows:
Contract Management → Supplier Relationship Management System (executed
contract, obligations, and sourcing records sent for registration and
storage).
Supplier Relationship Management System → Contract Management (supplier
master record data and confirmation returned).
Contract Management → Procurement / ERP System (supplier master data,
contract reference, and pricing sent to create or update supplier record).
Procurement / ERP System → Contract Management (confirmation that supplier
record is active in ERP).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Handover Package" — written by User task "Compile handover
package"; read by User task "Receive and review handover package" and User
task "Brief vendor manager on contract obligations and key terms".
Data Object "Executed Contract" — read by User task "Compile handover
package" and Service task "Send contract data and obligations to SRM
System".
Data Object "Supplier Master Record" — written by Service task "Create or
update supplier in Procurement / ERP System"; read by User task "Confirm
supplier master record is complete".
Data Object "Governance and Review Schedule" — written by User task "Set
up supplier governance and review schedule"; read by User task "Confirm
handover complete to Contract Management".

V09.12 packages the executed contract, all sourcing records, and key
commercial obligations into a structured handover that transfers ownership
from Contract Management to Vendor Management. The supplier master record
is verified and created in both the SRM System and the Procurement / ERP
System, making the supplier ready for purchasing transactions. Completing
this subprocess closes the Source to Contract value chain and opens the
Supplier Management and Procure to Pay operations.
```

## V10 — Market to Lead

**Teams and roles involved.**
Market to Lead usually involves Marketing, Digital/Campaign Marketing, Content, Events, Marketing Operations, Sales Development, and Sales, with support from Data/Analytics and sometimes Legal or Privacy for consent handling. Key roles include marketing manager, campaign manager, content producer, digital/paid media specialist, events coordinator, marketing operations analyst, lead qualification specialist, sales development representative, and data privacy officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Prospect — an individual or organisation not yet known to the business. The process is normally initiated by the organisation itself rather than by the customer: a campaign launches, content is published, or an event opens for registration. Other external parties include media and advertising platforms, list and data providers, event venues and partners, agencies, and marketing automation vendors.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: plan campaign, define audience and segments, produce content and assets, launch campaign across channels, capture responses and enquiries, enrich and score the response, qualify the lead, route the qualified lead to sales, nurture the unqualified response, and measure campaign performance.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include marketing automation, CRM, content management system, web analytics, advertising and social platforms, event management platform, data enrichment services, consent and preference management, customer data platform, and business intelligence/reporting tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include brand and messaging guidelines, marketing approval procedure, privacy and consent policy (opt-in, unsubscribe, retention), data sourcing and list acquisition policy, lead scoring and qualification criteria, service-level agreements between Marketing and Sales on lead follow-up, advertising spend approval, and campaign measurement standards.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The prospect provides enquiry details, registration and download information, consent and channel preferences, and engagement signals such as page visits, opens and clicks. The process provides the prospect with campaign messages, content and offers, event invitations and confirmations, follow-up communication, and preference and unsubscribe confirmations.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates campaign definitions, audience segments, content assets, response records, lead records, scores, consent records, and attribution data. IT systems provide audience data, delivery and engagement metrics, duplicate and enrichment matches, existing customer and account context, suppression lists, and campaign performance reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Marketing Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V10.01** Plan Campaign | — | Marketing (campaign manager), Marketing Operations (marketing operations analyst) | Marketing Automation Platform |
| **V10.02** Define Audience & Segments | Data Provider | Marketing Operations (marketing operations analyst), Data & Analytics (data analyst) | Customer Data Platform (CDP) |
| **V10.03** Produce Content & Assets | Agency | Content (content producer), Marketing (campaign manager) | Content Management System (CMS) |
| **V10.04** Obtain Approvals | — | Marketing (marketing manager), Legal / Privacy (data privacy officer) | Marketing Automation Platform |
| **V10.05** Launch Campaign | Prospect, Advertising Platform | Digital Marketing (digital media specialist), Marketing Operations (marketing operations analyst) | Marketing Automation Platform, Advertising Platform |
| **V10.06** Capture Response | Prospect | Marketing Operations (marketing operations analyst) | Marketing Automation Platform, Web Analytics System |
| **V10.07** Enrich & Score Response | Data Provider | Marketing Operations (marketing operations analyst), Data & Analytics (data analyst) | Data Enrichment Service, Customer Data Platform (CDP) |
| **V10.08** Qualify Lead | Prospect | Sales Development (sales development representative) | CRM System |
| **V10.09** Route Qualified Lead to Sales | — | Sales Development (sales development representative), Sales (account manager) | CRM System |
| **V10.10** Nurture Unqualified Response | Prospect | Marketing (campaign manager) | Marketing Automation Platform |
| **V10.11** Measure Campaign Performance | — | Marketing (marketing manager), Data & Analytics (data analyst) | Business Intelligence Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V10):

- **External actors:** Prospect (V10.05, V10.06, V10.08, V10.10); Data Provider (V10.02, V10.07); Advertising Platform (V10.05); Agency (V10.03).
- **Teams:** Marketing (V10.01, V10.03, V10.04, V10.10, V10.11); Marketing Operations (V10.01, V10.02, V10.05–V10.07); Content (V10.03); Legal / Privacy (V10.04); Digital Marketing (V10.05); Data & Analytics (V10.02, V10.07, V10.11); Sales Development (V10.08, V10.09); Sales (V10.09).
- **IT systems:** Marketing Automation Platform (V10.01, V10.04–V10.06, V10.10); Customer Data Platform / CDP (V10.02, V10.07); Content Management System / CMS (V10.03); Advertising Platform (V10.05); Web Analytics System (V10.06); Data Enrichment Service (V10.07); CRM System (V10.08, V10.09); Business Intelligence Platform (V10.11).

**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V10 — Market to Lead — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Market to Lead value chain, from initial campaign planning through to
qualified lead handoff and performance measurement. The diagram is arranged in
three horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES
→ APPLICATIONS. The Prospect and external supply-side actors (Data Provider,
Agency, Advertising Platform) sit on the far left as demand and input parties;
Sales sits on the far right as the delivery and handoff actor. The view is read
top-to-bottom as service → process → application, expressing ArchiMate service
realisation across the full chain.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Prospect — far left; initiates or receives campaign contact and supplies
  response and consent signals across V10.05, V10.06, V10.08, and V10.10.
- Data Provider — far left; supplies audience list and enrichment data for
  V10.02 and V10.07.
- Agency — far left; supplies creative and content assets consumed in V10.03.
- Advertising Platform — far left; delivers paid media impressions and
  click-through data in V10.05.
- Sales — far right; receives qualified leads handed off in V10.09.

2. Interfaces

- Campaign Intake Interface — accessed by Marketing team; serves the Campaign
  Planning Service and the Approval Service.
- Prospect Engagement Interface — accessed by Prospect; serves the Campaign
  Delivery Service and the Response Capture Service.
- Lead Handoff Interface — accessed by Sales Development and Sales; serves the
  Lead Qualification and Routing Service.
- Data Supply Interface — accessed by Data Provider; serves the Audience
  Definition Service and the Enrichment and Scoring Service.
- Creative Supply Interface — accessed by Agency; serves the Content and Asset
  Production Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Campaign Planning Service — provides structured campaign definition,
  objectives, budget, and schedule to internal teams.
- Audience Definition Service — provides validated, consented audience
  segments for targeting.
- Content and Asset Production Service — provides approved creative content
  and campaign assets ready for use.
- Approval Service — provides brand, legal, and privacy sign-off on campaigns
  and assets before launch.
- Campaign Delivery Service — provides multi-channel campaign execution and
  message distribution to prospects.
- Response Capture Service — provides recording and deduplication of inbound
  prospect responses and engagement signals.
- Enrichment and Scoring Service — provides enriched, scored prospect records
  ranked by fit and intent.
- Lead Qualification Service — provides assessed and qualified lead records
  meeting agreed scoring criteria.
- Lead Routing Service — provides timely, attributed lead assignment to the
  correct sales owner.
- Nurture Service — provides ongoing communication sequences to unqualified
  responses until ready to re-qualify.
- Campaign Performance Service — provides attribution, KPI, and ROI reporting
  across all campaign activity.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V10.01 Plan Campaign — sets campaign strategy, budget, channel mix, and
  schedule.
- V10.02 Define Audience & Segments — builds and validates targetable audience
  segments using first- and third-party data.
- V10.03 Produce Content & Assets — creates and stores all creative and
  content assets for the campaign.
- V10.04 Obtain Approvals — routes campaign plan and assets through brand,
  legal, and privacy review.
- V10.05 Launch Campaign — activates the campaign across email, paid, web, and
  event channels.
- V10.06 Capture Response — ingests and records prospect responses,
  registrations, and engagement events.
- V10.07 Enrich & Score Response — appends third-party firmographic data and
  calculates lead scores.
- V10.08 Qualify Lead — reviews scored records against qualification criteria
  and designates marketing-qualified leads.
- V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales — assigns accepted leads to sales owners
  and logs them in CRM with SLA timestamp.
- V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response — enrols disqualified or early-stage
  responses in automated nurture tracks.
- V10.11 Measure Campaign Performance — aggregates delivery, response, and
  pipeline data into performance reports.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Marketing Automation Platform — supports campaign definition, email and
  nurture execution, response capture, and approval workflow.
- Customer Data Platform (CDP) — supports audience segment creation and
  enriched prospect record management.
- Content Management System (CMS) — supports storage, versioning, and
  retrieval of content and creative assets.
- Advertising Platform — supports paid media campaign activation and delivery
  reporting.
- Web Analytics System — supports capture and analysis of on-site prospect
  engagement and conversion events.
- Data Enrichment Service — supports automated appending of firmographic and
  intent data to prospect records.
- CRM System — supports lead qualification records, ownership assignment,
  SLA tracking, and sales pipeline.
- Business Intelligence Platform — supports aggregated campaign performance
  dashboards and attribution reporting.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Marketing Automation Platform SERVES V10.01 Plan Campaign.
- Marketing Automation Platform SERVES V10.04 Obtain Approvals.
- Marketing Automation Platform SERVES V10.05 Launch Campaign.
- Marketing Automation Platform SERVES V10.06 Capture Response.
- Marketing Automation Platform SERVES V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response.
- Customer Data Platform (CDP) SERVES V10.02 Define Audience & Segments.
- Customer Data Platform (CDP) SERVES V10.07 Enrich & Score Response.
- Content Management System (CMS) SERVES V10.03 Produce Content & Assets.
- Advertising Platform SERVES V10.05 Launch Campaign.
- Web Analytics System SERVES V10.06 Capture Response.
- Data Enrichment Service SERVES V10.07 Enrich & Score Response.
- CRM System SERVES V10.08 Qualify Lead.
- CRM System SERVES V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales.
- Business Intelligence Platform SERVES V10.11 Measure Campaign Performance.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V10.01 Plan Campaign REALISES Campaign Planning Service.
- V10.02 Define Audience & Segments REALISES Audience Definition Service.
- V10.03 Produce Content & Assets REALISES Content and Asset Production
  Service.
- V10.04 Obtain Approvals REALISES Approval Service.
- V10.05 Launch Campaign REALISES Campaign Delivery Service.
- V10.06 Capture Response REALISES Response Capture Service.
- V10.07 Enrich & Score Response REALISES Enrichment and Scoring Service.
- V10.08 Qualify Lead REALISES Lead Qualification Service.
- V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales REALISES Lead Routing Service.
- V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response REALISES Nurture Service.
- V10.11 Measure Campaign Performance REALISES Campaign Performance Service.

ASSIGNMENT (actor assigned to interface):
- Prospect ASSIGNED TO Prospect Engagement Interface.
- Data Provider ASSIGNED TO Data Supply Interface.
- Agency ASSIGNED TO Creative Supply Interface.
- Advertising Platform ASSIGNED TO Prospect Engagement Interface.
- Sales ASSIGNED TO Lead Handoff Interface.
- Marketing team ASSIGNED TO Campaign Intake Interface.
- Sales Development ASSIGNED TO Lead Handoff Interface.

ACCESS (interface serves service):
- Campaign Intake Interface SERVES Campaign Planning Service.
- Campaign Intake Interface SERVES Approval Service.
- Prospect Engagement Interface SERVES Campaign Delivery Service.
- Prospect Engagement Interface SERVES Response Capture Service.
- Lead Handoff Interface SERVES Lead Qualification Service.
- Lead Handoff Interface SERVES Lead Routing Service.
- Data Supply Interface SERVES Audience Definition Service.
- Data Supply Interface SERVES Enrichment and Scoring Service.
- Creative Supply Interface SERVES Content and Asset Production Service.
```

```text
V10.11 Measure Campaign Performance.

Sales Development receives enriched and scored response records from
V10.07 Enrich & Score Response and performs qualification in
V10.08 Qualify Lead.
Sales Development routes qualified lead records and handoff details to
V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales.

Sales receives qualified lead assignments and supporting context from
V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales.

The boundary "V10 — Market to Lead" contains all eleven subprocesses that
take an organisation-initiated campaign from planning through audience
definition, content production, approval, launch, response capture,
enrichment and scoring, lead qualification, sales routing, unqualified
nurture, and performance measurement. It serves external actors — the
Prospect, Data Providers, the Advertising Platform, and the Agency — as
well as the internal teams of Marketing, Marketing Operations, Content,
Legal / Privacy, Digital Marketing, Data & Analytics, Sales Development,
and Sales.
```


**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V10 - Market to Lead

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages rendered
as chevrons, one chevron per stage, in the order listed below. Each chevron
label must use exactly the stage name given. No stage may be omitted, and no
stage not listed may be added.

V10.01. Plan Campaign
V10.02. Define Audience & Segments
V10.03. Produce Content & Assets
V10.04. Obtain Approvals
V10.05. Launch Campaign
V10.06. Capture Response
V10.07. Enrich & Score Response
V10.08. Qualify Lead
V10.09. Route Qualified Lead to Sales
V10.10. Nurture Unqualified Response
V10.11. Measure Campaign Performance

This chain converts market investment into qualified sales leads. It is
triggered by the organisation itself — through a campaign launch, content
publication, or event opening — rather than by an inbound request. The main
external participant is the Prospect, who receives campaign messages and
offers and whose responses, registrations, and engagement signals flow back
into the process. The chain ends when a qualified lead is routed to Sales for
follow-up or an unqualified response is returned to nurture, with campaign
performance measured throughout.
```

```text
    Automation Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Duplicate detected?"
  - branch "Yes — duplicate":
      User task "Merge or discard duplicate record"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Duplicate detected")
  - branch "No — new record":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Duplicate detected")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Duplicate detected"
  Service task "Apply consent and suppression check against Marketing
    Automation Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Consent valid and not suppressed?"
  - branch "No — suppressed or no consent":
      Service task "Flag record as suppressed and log reason"
      End event "Response suppressed — no further processing"
  - branch "Yes — consent confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Consent valid and not
        suppressed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Consent valid and not suppressed"
  User task "Classify response type and assign initial channel attribution"
  Service task "Write confirmed response record to Marketing Automation
    Platform"
  Service task "Log web engagement data to Web Analytics System"
  End event "Response record confirmed — ready for Enrich and Score
    Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Receive and log response event
  from Marketing Automation Platform" — label "Response not received
  within 24 hours" — triggers End event "Response capture timed out —
  no action taken".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Marketing Operations lane at the
message start event, proceeds through channel identification, where four
branches diverge and all rejoin at the "Response channel identified"
merge gateway; flow continues through duplicate check, where the
duplicate branch loops through a merge task before rejoining; flow
then passes through consent and suppression check, where the suppressed
branch ends independently and the valid-consent branch rejoins; flow
closes with classification, writing to systems, and the end event.

Message flows:
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Operations lane "Receive and
  log response event from Marketing Automation Platform" (response event
  record — form submission, email engagement, event registration).
Marketing Operations lane "Retrieve engagement signal from Marketing
  Automation Platform" → Marketing Automation Platform (request for
  email open/click signal).
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Operations lane "Retrieve
  engagement signal from Marketing Automation Platform" (email
  engagement signal data).
Web Analytics System → Marketing Operations lane "Retrieve page-visit
  data from Web Analytics System" (web visit and page-level engagement
  data).
Marketing Operations lane "Log web engagement data to Web Analytics
  System" → Web Analytics System (confirmed engagement record for
  attribution).
Marketing Operations lane "Apply consent and suppression check against
  Marketing Automation Platform" → Marketing Automation Platform
  (suppression and consent status lookup request).
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Operations lane "Apply consent
  and suppression check against Marketing Automation Platform"
  (suppression list and consent status).
Marketing Operations lane "Write confirmed response record to Marketing
  Automation Platform" → Marketing Automation Platform (validated
  response record with channel attribution).
Prospect → Marketing Organisation (enquiry details, form submission,
  registration data, email engagement, page visit signals).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Response Event Record" — written by "Receive and log
  response event from Marketing Automation Platform"; read by "Check
  for duplicate response record in Marketing Automation Platform".
Data Object "Validated Response Record" — written by "Review and
  validate submission details" and "Review and validate registration
  details"; read by "Apply consent and suppression check against
  Marketing Automation Platform".
Data Object "Consent and Suppression Status" — written by "Apply
  consent and suppression check against Marketing Automation Platform";
  read by "Classify response type and assign initial channel
  attribution".
Data Object "Channel Attribution Record" — written by "Classify
  response type and assign initial channel attribution"; read by
  "Write confirmed response record to Marketing Automation Platform".

This subprocess receives engagement signals and enquiry details from
prospects across all campaign channels — form submissions, email
interactions, event registrations, and web visits — and validates,
deduplicates, and consent-checks each one before writing a confirmed
response record. It hands a clean, attributed response record to
V10.07 Enrich and Score Response, where the record will be augmented
with third-party data and assigned a lead score.
```


### V10.07 — Enrich & Score Response

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.07 Enrich & Score Response — sits within the Market to Lead
value chain, receiving raw response records from Capture Response and
handing enriched, scored leads to Qualify Lead.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the internal team running the enrichment
and scoring process, with lanes for Marketing Operations and Data &
Analytics.
Pool "Data Provider" — external supplier of firmographic and demographic
enrichment data.
Pool "Data Enrichment Service" — IT system that performs automated data
matching and enrichment.
Pool "Customer Data Platform (CDP)" — IT system that holds unified
prospect and customer records and applies lead scoring.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Enrichment Service" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Customer Data Platform (CDP)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Data Provider" — top.
Pool "Marketing Organisation" — second (white-box process pool).
Pool "Data Enrichment Service" — third.
Pool "Customer Data Platform (CDP)" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing Operations lane:
  Message start event "Enriched response records ready from Capture
    Response"
  User task "Review and prepare response records for enrichment"
  Service task "Submit response records to Data Enrichment Service"
  Intermediate message catch event "Enrichment data returned"
  User task "Review enrichment results and flag exceptions"
  Exclusive gateway "Enrichment sufficient?"
  - branch "No — data gaps remain":
      User task "Request supplementary data from Data Provider"
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary data received from
        Data Provider"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Enrichment sufficient")
  - branch "Yes — proceed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Enrichment sufficient")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Enrichment sufficient"
  Service task "Push enriched record to Customer Data Platform (CDP)"
  Intermediate message catch event "Score assigned by CDP"
  User task "Review scored records and apply manual adjustments"
  Exclusive gateway "Score threshold met?"
  - branch "Yes — qualified for review":
      Service task "Mark record as scored and ready for qualification"
      End event "Enriched and scored lead ready for Qualify Lead"
  - branch "No — below threshold":
      Service task "Tag record for nurture stream"
      End event "Below-threshold record ready for Nurture Unqualified
        Response"

Data & Analytics lane:
  User task "Define and maintain lead scoring model"
  User task "Validate scoring output against model criteria"
  User task "Produce enrichment and scoring summary report"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Request supplementary
data from Data Provider" — label "48-hour data request timeout" —
if no supplementary data is received within 48 hours, flow exits to
Service task "Tag record for nurture stream" in the Marketing Operations
lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Marketing Operations lane with the
message start event, passes through record preparation and submission to
the Data Enrichment Service, catches the enrichment reply, reviews
results, and reaches the "Enrichment sufficient?" gateway. The "No"
branch loops through the Data Provider request and the intermediate
message catch event before rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway;
the "Yes" branch rejoins directly. After the merge, flow passes through
CDP push, score receipt, manual review, and the "Score threshold met?"
gateway, whose "Yes" branch ends at the qualified-lead end event and
whose "No" branch ends at the nurture end event. The Data & Analytics
lane tasks run in support: scoring model definition precedes the CDP
push, scoring validation follows score receipt and precedes manual
review, and the summary report follows manual review and runs in
parallel with the gateway decision.

Message flows:
Data Enrichment Service → Marketing Operations lane (enrichment results
  returned for matched response records)
Marketing Operations lane → Data Enrichment Service (response records
  submitted for matching and enrichment)
Data Provider → Marketing Operations lane (supplementary firmographic
  or demographic data in response to manual request)
Marketing Operations lane → Data Provider (request for supplementary
  enrichment data)
Marketing Operations lane → Customer Data Platform (CDP) (enriched
  response records pushed for unified profile update and scoring)
Customer Data Platform (CDP) → Marketing Operations lane (lead score
  assigned to each enriched record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Raw Response Record" — read by User task "Review and
  prepare response records for enrichment"; written by Message start
  event "Enriched response records ready from Capture Response".
Data Object "Enrichment Request Package" — written by User task
  "Review and prepare response records for enrichment"; read by
  Service task "Submit response records to Data Enrichment Service".
Data Object "Enrichment Results" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Enrichment data returned"; read by User task "Review
  enrichment results and flag exceptions".
Data Object "Supplementary Data" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Supplementary data received from Data Provider"; read by
  Exclusive merge gateway "Enrichment sufficient".
Data Object "Enriched Response Record" — written by Service task "Push
  enriched record to Customer Data Platform (CDP)"; read by Intermediate
  message catch event "Score assigned by CDP".
Data Object "Lead Score" — written by Intermediate message catch event
  "Score assigned by CDP"; read by User task "Review scored records and
  apply manual adjustments" and by User task "Validate scoring output
  against model criteria".
Data Object "Scoring Model Definition" — written by User task "Define
  and maintain lead scoring model"; read by User task "Validate scoring
  output against model criteria".
Data Object "Enrichment and Scoring Summary Report" — written by User
  task "Produce enrichment and scoring summary report"; read by User task
  "Review scored records and apply manual adjustments".

This subprocess takes raw response records from Capture Response,
enriches them with external firmographic and demographic data via the
Data Enrichment Service and, where necessary, direct requests to the Data
Provider, then pushes unified records into the Customer Data Platform for
automated lead scoring. Records meeting the score threshold are marked
ready for Qualify Lead; those falling below are tagged for the Nurture
Unqualified Response stream.
```


### V10.08 — Qualify Lead

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.08 Qualify Lead — subprocess in the Market to Lead value
chain where the Sales Development team assesses each enriched and scored
response against qualification criteria and determines whether it meets
the threshold to be passed to Sales.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the organisation running the
qualification process, containing the Sales Development lane.
Pool "Prospect" — the individual or organisation whose response is
being qualified.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for lead and contact data used
during qualification.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospect" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospect
2. Marketing Organisation
3. CRM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Sales Development lane:
  Message start event "Enriched and scored lead received from
    Enrich & Score Response"
  Service task "Retrieve lead record from CRM"
  User task "Review lead score and enrichment data"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead meets minimum score threshold?"
    - branch "No — below threshold":
        User task "Mark lead as unqualified in CRM"
        End event "Lead unqualified — handed to Nurture Unqualified
          Response"
    - branch "Yes — at or above threshold":
        User task "Review lead details against qualification criteria"
        Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information available to qualify?"
          - branch "No — information gaps":
              User task "Prepare qualification questions for prospect"
              Send task "Send qualification questions to prospect"
              Intermediate message catch event "Prospect response
                received"
              User task "Capture prospect responses in CRM"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
                information available to qualify")
          - branch "Yes — information complete":
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
                information available to qualify")
        Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information available to
          qualify"
        User task "Apply qualification framework to lead record"
        Exclusive gateway "Lead qualifies?"
          - branch "No — does not qualify":
              User task "Mark lead as unqualified in CRM"
              End event "Lead unqualified — handed to Nurture
                Unqualified Response"
          - branch "Yes — qualifies":
              User task "Set lead status to Qualified in CRM"
              End event "Lead qualified — ready for Route Qualified
                Lead to Sales"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Lead meets minimum score threshold"

Note: the "No — below threshold" branch from the first gateway ends at
its own End event and does not rejoin the merge gateway. The merge
gateway resolves only the "Yes — at or above threshold" branch, which
arrives after the lead qualifies or does not qualify sub-path
completes; in practice the merge sits after the score-threshold check
so that the "Yes" branch continues to the review step. Treat the
merge as placed immediately after the score-threshold gateway to
close the "Yes" branch cleanly into the review step that follows.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Sales Development lane at the
message start event, proceeds through CRM retrieval and score review
to the score-threshold gateway. The "No — below threshold" branch
leads to marking the lead unqualified and terminates. The "Yes"
branch continues to the qualification-criteria review and then the
information-availability gateway. The "No — information gaps" branch
triggers question preparation, dispatch, an intermediate message catch
event awaiting prospect response, and response capture, then rejoins
at the exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information available to
qualify". The "Yes — information complete" branch rejoins the same
merge directly. After the merge, the qualification framework is
applied and a second gateway tests whether the lead qualifies; the
"No" branch marks the lead unqualified and ends; the "Yes" branch
sets lead status to Qualified and ends.

Message flows:
Prospect → Sales Development lane (prospect response to qualification
  questions)
Sales Development lane → Prospect (qualification questions sent)
Sales Development lane → CRM System (retrieve lead record; update
  lead status — unqualified or qualified; capture prospect responses)
CRM System → Sales Development lane (lead record, score and
  enrichment data returned)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Enriched Lead Record" — read by "Review lead score and
  enrichment data"; read by "Review lead details against qualification
  criteria".
Data Object "Qualification Questions" — written by "Prepare
  qualification questions for prospect"; read by "Send qualification
  questions to prospect".
Data Object "Prospect Qualification Responses" — written by "Capture
  prospect responses in CRM"; read by "Apply qualification framework
  to lead record".
Data Object "Qualified Lead Record" — written by "Set lead status to
  Qualified in CRM".

This subprocess takes each enriched and scored lead and subjects it to
a structured qualification check against the organisation's lead
scoring and qualification criteria. Where information is missing, the
sales development representative contacts the prospect directly to
close the gap before a final determination is made. Leads that meet
the criteria are marked Qualified in the CRM and handed to Route
Qualified Lead to Sales; those that do not are marked Unqualified and
handed to Nurture Unqualified Response.
```


### V10.09 — Route Qualified Lead to Sales

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.09 Route Qualified Lead to Sales — the subprocess that hands a
scored, qualified lead from Sales Development to the appropriate Sales owner
and confirms acceptance, sitting between Qualify Lead and Measure Campaign
Performance in the Market to Lead value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the internal organisation running the routing
and acceptance process, with two lanes.
  Lane "Sales Development" — sales development representative who routes the
  qualified lead.
  Lane "Sales" — account manager who receives, reviews, and accepts the lead.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for lead and opportunity data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Marketing Organisation (white-box, contains Sales Development lane above
   Sales lane)
2. CRM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Sales Development lane:
  Message start event "Qualified lead received from Qualify Lead"
  User task "Review lead record and assign Sales owner"
  Service task "Update lead record with routing details in CRM"
  Send task "Notify assigned account manager of new lead"
  Intermediate message catch event "Lead acceptance confirmed by Sales"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead accepted within SLA?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Lead accepted
      within SLA")
    - branch "No — SLA breached": User task "Escalate unaccepted lead to
      Sales manager"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Lead accepted within SLA")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Lead accepted within SLA"
  Service task "Record routing outcome and timestamp in CRM"
  End event "Lead routed and accepted — ready for Measure Campaign
  Performance"

Sales lane:
  User task "Review lead details and context"
  Exclusive gateway "Lead suitable for Sales pursuit?"
    - branch "Yes — accept": User task "Accept lead and create opportunity
      in CRM"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Lead suitable for Sales
      pursuit")
    - branch "No — return": User task "Reject lead with reason and return
      to Sales Development"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Lead suitable for Sales
      pursuit")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Lead suitable for Sales pursuit"
  Send task "Confirm lead decision to Sales Development"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Escalate unaccepted lead to
Sales manager" — label "SLA reminder period elapsed" — if the escalation
itself receives no response within a further defined period, flow exits to
End event "Lead escalation unresolved — routed for review".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Sales Development lane, flow runs from the message
start event through review and assignment, CRM update, notification, and the
intermediate message catch event, then into the SLA gateway; the "Yes" branch
and the escalation branch rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Lead accepted
within SLA", after which flow continues to record the outcome and reach the
end event. Within the Sales lane, flow runs from review of lead details into
the suitability gateway; the "accept" branch passes through opportunity
creation and the "return" branch passes through rejection, both rejoining at
the exclusive merge gateway "Lead suitable for Sales pursuit", then reaching
the confirmation send task. The Send task "Confirm lead decision to Sales
Development" triggers the intermediate message catch event in the Sales
Development lane, closing the loop.

Message flows:
CRM System → Sales Development lane: "Qualified lead record with score and
segment data" (read at User task "Review lead record and assign Sales owner")
Sales Development lane → CRM System: lead routing details and owner
assignment (written by Service task "Update lead record with routing details
in CRM")
Sales Development lane → Sales lane: new lead notification (carried by Send
task "Notify assigned account manager of new lead")
Sales lane → CRM System: opportunity record (written by User task "Accept
lead and create opportunity in CRM")
Sales lane → Sales Development lane: lead decision confirmation (carried by
Send task "Confirm lead decision to Sales Development")
Sales Development lane → CRM System: routing outcome and timestamp (written
by Service task "Record routing outcome and timestamp in CRM")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Qualified Lead Record" — read by User task "Review lead record
and assign Sales owner"; written by Service task "Update lead record with
routing details in CRM".
Data Object "Lead Routing Assignment" — written by User task "Review lead
record and assign Sales owner"; read by User task "Review lead details and
context".
Data Object "Lead Decision Notice" — written by User task "Accept lead and
create opportunity in CRM" and by User task "Reject lead with reason and
return to Sales Development"; read by Service task "Record routing outcome and
timestamp in CRM".
Data Object "Opportunity Record" — written by User task "Accept lead and
create opportunity in CRM"; read by Service task "Record routing outcome and
timestamp in CRM".

This subprocess takes a validated, scored lead from Sales Development,
assigns it to the correct Sales owner in the CRM, and manages the acceptance
handshake within the agreed SLA. It produces a confirmed opportunity record
and a routing-outcome timestamp that feed directly into campaign attribution
reporting in Measure Campaign Performance.
```


### V10.10 — Nurture Unqualified Response

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.10 Nurture Unqualified Response — the subprocess that re-engages
prospects who did not qualify as sales-ready leads, maintaining contact through
targeted nurture programmes until they either become qualified or are retired
from the active pipeline.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the internal team running the nurture programme.
  Lane "Marketing" (campaign manager) — designs and manages the nurture track.
  Lane "Marketing Operations" (marketing operations analyst) — configures and
    monitors nurture automation.
Pool "Prospect" — the external individual or organisation receiving nurture
  communications.
Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — executes nurture sequences, tracks
  engagement, and surfaces re-engagement signals.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Prospect" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Marketing Automation Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Prospect
2. Marketing Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Marketing,
   Marketing Operations)
3. Marketing Automation Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing lane:
  Message start event "Unqualified response received from Qualify Lead"
  User task "Review unqualified response record"
  User task "Select nurture track"
  User task "Define nurture content and cadence"
  Exclusive gateway "Nurture track approved?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Nurture track
    approved")
  - branch "No": User task "Revise nurture track definition"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Nurture track approved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Nurture track approved"
  User task "Confirm nurture track handoff to Marketing Operations"
  Intermediate message catch event "Re-engagement signal received"
  Exclusive gateway "Prospect re-qualifies?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate re-qualified prospect for lead
    qualification"
    End event "Prospect re-qualified — ready for Qualify Lead"
  - branch "No, nurture cycle exhausted": User task "Mark prospect as
    inactive and retire from nurture"
    End event "Prospect retired from nurture programme"
  - branch "No, continue nurturing": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Prospect re-qualifies")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Prospect re-qualifies"

Marketing Operations lane:
  User task "Configure nurture sequence in Marketing Automation Platform"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Nurture Cycle Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: Service task "Trigger scheduled nurture message",
    Intermediate timer catch event "Next message interval elapsed",
    Service task "Retrieve engagement metrics from Marketing Automation
    Platform", User task "Review engagement data and flag anomalies"
  Service task "Signal re-engagement event to Marketing lane"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Nurture
  Cycle Complete" — label "Maximum nurture duration reached" — triggers User
  task "Mark prospect as inactive and retire from nurture" in the Marketing
  lane via an escalation to the Marketing lane end path.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Marketing lane with the start event, passes
through record review, track selection, content definition, the approval
gateway (with the revision branch looping back to the merge), and the handoff
task, then crosses to the Marketing Operations lane for sequence configuration
and the nurture loop subprocess, which signals re-engagement back to the
Marketing lane; the Marketing lane gateway then branches to re-qualification
escalation (ending at the re-qualified end event), continued nurturing (looping
back through the merge to await the next re-engagement signal), or retirement
(ending at the retired end event).

Message flows:
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Operations lane, Service task
  "Retrieve engagement metrics from Marketing Automation Platform"
  (engagement and delivery metrics per nurture message).
Marketing Operations lane, Service task "Trigger scheduled nurture message"
  → Marketing Automation Platform (nurture sequence trigger and content
  payload).
Marketing Automation Platform → Prospect (nurture emails, content offers,
  and invitations).
Prospect → Marketing Automation Platform (opens, clicks, form fills, and
  other engagement signals).
Marketing Automation Platform → Marketing Operations lane, Service task
  "Signal re-engagement event to Marketing lane" (re-engagement threshold
  alert).
Marketing lane, User task "Escalate re-qualified prospect for lead
  qualification" → CRM System implied by downstream; message shown as:
  Marketing lane → Marketing Automation Platform (re-qualification flag
  and updated prospect record).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Unqualified Response Record" — read by User task "Review
  unqualified response record"; written by Message start event "Unqualified
  response received from Qualify Lead".
Data Object "Nurture Track Definition" — written by User task "Define nurture
  content and cadence"; read by User task "Configure nurture sequence in
  Marketing Automation Platform".
Data Object "Nurture Engagement Report" — written by Service task "Retrieve
  engagement metrics from Marketing Automation Platform"; read by User task
  "Review engagement data and flag anomalies".
Data Object "Re-engagement Signal" — written by Service task "Signal
  re-engagement event to Marketing lane"; read by Intermediate message catch
  event "Re-engagement signal received".
Data Object "Prospect Disposition Record" — written by User task "Mark
  prospect as inactive and retire from nurture"; read by End event "Prospect
  retired from nurture programme".

This subprocess takes prospects deemed not yet sales-ready from the Qualify
Lead subprocess and places them into structured, automated nurture tracks
managed by Marketing. It monitors engagement signals through the Marketing
Automation Platform over a defined cycle, escalating any prospect who crosses
the re-qualification threshold back into Qualify Lead, and retiring those who
remain unresponsive after the maximum nurture duration. The outcome feeds
Measure Campaign Performance with disposition data and, where re-qualification
occurs, restarts the qualification flow.
```


### V10.11 — Measure Campaign Performance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V10.11 Measure Campaign Performance — closes the Market to Lead
value chain by aggregating, analysing, and reporting on campaign results
after all responses have been captured, enriched, and routed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — the organisation running the measurement
process, containing all internal teams involved.
  Lane "Marketing" — marketing manager reviews and signs off on performance
  reports.
  Lane "Data & Analytics" — data analyst extracts, consolidates, and analyses
  campaign data and produces reports.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — BI system that stores and serves
campaign metrics and dashboards.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Marketing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Marketing Organisation (white-box, with Marketing lane above Data &
   Analytics lane)
2. Business Intelligence Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Marketing Organisation)

Marketing lane:
  Start event "Campaign cycle complete — received from Route Qualified
  Lead to Sales and Nurture Unqualified Response"
  User task "Define measurement scope and KPIs"
  Send task "Request consolidated campaign data"

Data & Analytics lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Consolidated data received from
  Business Intelligence Platform"
  User task "Validate and reconcile campaign data"
  Exclusive gateway "Data complete and consistent?"
  - branch "No — gaps or discrepancies found":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Data Is Reconciled"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
        User task "Identify data gaps or discrepancies",
        Send task "Request corrected or missing data",
        Intermediate message catch event "Corrected data received from
        Business Intelligence Platform",
        User task "Re-validate data"
      (exits subprocess)
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Data complete and consistent")
  - branch "Yes — data is complete":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Data complete and consistent")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Data complete and consistent"
  User task "Analyse campaign performance against KPIs"
  User task "Calculate channel attribution and ROI"
  Service task "Publish performance dashboard to Business Intelligence
  Platform"
  User task "Produce campaign performance report"

Marketing lane (continued):
  User task "Review campaign performance report"
  Exclusive gateway "Report accepted?"
  - branch "No — revisions required":
      User task "Record revision feedback"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Report accepted")
  - branch "Yes — accepted":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Report accepted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Report accepted"
  User task "Capture lessons learned and recommendations"
  User task "Archive campaign record"
  End event "Campaign performance reported and record archived"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Data Is Reconciled" — label "Data reconciliation deadline exceeded" —
on trigger, flow continues to End event "Data reconciliation failed —
campaign measurement incomplete".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Marketing lane with the start event,
moves to "Define measurement scope and KPIs" and then "Request
consolidated campaign data", then crosses to the Data & Analytics lane
at the intermediate message catch event. Work proceeds through
validation, the exclusive gateway (with the loop subprocess on the
"No" branch and the direct path on the "Yes" branch, both merging at
"Data complete and consistent"), then through analysis, attribution,
dashboard publication, and report production. Flow returns to the
Marketing lane for review, passes through the "Report accepted?"
gateway (revision feedback on the "No" branch, direct pass on the
"Yes" branch, both merging at "Report accepted"), then through lessons
learned, archiving, and the end event.

Message flows:
Send task "Request consolidated campaign data" → Business Intelligence
Platform (data extract request).
Business Intelligence Platform → Intermediate message catch event
"Consolidated data received from Business Intelligence Platform"
(consolidated campaign metrics and engagement data).
Send task "Request corrected or missing data" (inside loop subprocess)
→ Business Intelligence Platform (corrected data request).
Business Intelligence Platform → Intermediate message catch event
"Corrected data received from Business Intelligence Platform" (corrected
or supplemented metrics).
Service task "Publish performance dashboard to Business Intelligence
Platform" → Business Intelligence Platform (performance dashboard and
attribution data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Measurement Scope and KPI Definition" — written by
"Define measurement scope and KPIs"; read by "Analyse campaign
performance against KPIs".
Data Object "Consolidated Campaign Dataset" — written by "Validate and
reconcile campaign data"; read by "Analyse campaign performance against
KPIs" and "Calculate channel attribution and ROI".
Data Object "Campaign Performance Report" — written by "Produce campaign
performance report"; read by "Review campaign performance report".
Data Object "Lessons Learned and Recommendations" — written by "Capture
lessons learned and recommendations"; read by "Archive campaign record".

This subprocess closes the Market to Lead chain by drawing together all
engagement, response, conversion, and spend data into a coherent
performance picture. The marketing manager and data analyst validate the
data, measure results against planned KPIs, calculate attribution and
ROI by channel, and produce a signed-off report. The archived campaign
record and lessons learned feed directly into the next planning cycle,
making the output of V10.11 the primary input for a future V10.01 Plan
Campaign.
```


## V11 — Sign to Onboard

**Teams and roles involved.**
Sign to Onboard usually involves Sales, Customer Success, Onboarding/Implementation, Service Delivery, Finance/Billing, IT or Provisioning, Legal or Contracts, and Support. Key roles include account manager, onboarding manager, implementation consultant, solution architect, data migration specialist, trainer, billing officer, provisioning engineer, and customer success manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the New Customer, represented by a sponsor, project contact and end users. The process is initiated when a contract is signed or an order for a new service is accepted. Other external parties include the customer's own IT provider, third-party implementation partners, integration vendors, and sometimes regulators where the service is licensed.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: accept signed contract, confirm scope and entitlements, assign the onboarding team, run kick-off, collect customer requirements and data, configure and provision the service, migrate data, test and validate with the customer, train users, obtain go-live acceptance, activate billing, and hand over to business as usual.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, contract lifecycle management, project or onboarding management tooling, provisioning and identity systems, the product or service platform itself, data migration tooling, billing and subscription management, knowledge base and learning management, and customer support/ticketing.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include contract acceptance and handover procedure, entitlement and scope-change rules, customer data handling and privacy policy, migration and cut-over procedure, acceptance and sign-off criteria, training standards, billing activation rules, and escalation paths where onboarding is delayed.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides contacts and authorised signatories, configuration requirements, existing data for migration, environment and access details, testing feedback, and formal acceptance. The process provides the customer with an onboarding plan and schedule, configuration and readiness updates, migration reports, training materials and sessions, go-live confirmation, and the first invoice and support arrangements.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates customer accounts, entitlements and licences, provisioned environments, user identities and roles, migrated records, onboarding tasks and milestones, and billing schedules. IT systems provide contract and order terms, provisioning status, migration validation results, usage and readiness telemetry, and support-case history.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Service Provider" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are
the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V11.01** Accept Signed Contract | New Customer | Sales (account manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V11.02** Confirm Scope & Entitlements | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Sales (account manager) | CRM System |
| **V11.03** Assign Onboarding Team | — | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Service Delivery (implementation consultant) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.04** Run Kick-off | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager), Service Delivery (solution architect) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.05** Collect Requirements & Data | New Customer | Service Delivery (implementation consultant) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.06** Configure & Provision Service | — | Service Delivery (implementation consultant), IT / Provisioning (provisioning engineer) | Provisioning & Identity System, Product Platform |
| **V11.07** Migrate Data | New Customer, Implementation Partner | Service Delivery (data migration specialist) | Data Migration Tooling, Product Platform |
| **V11.08** Test & Validate with Customer | New Customer | Service Delivery (implementation consultant), Onboarding (onboarding manager) | Product Platform |
| **V11.09** Train Users | New Customer | Onboarding (trainer) | Learning Management System (LMS) |
| **V11.10** Obtain Go-Live Acceptance | New Customer | Onboarding (onboarding manager) | Onboarding / Project Management System |
| **V11.11** Activate Billing | New Customer | Finance / Billing (billing officer) | Billing & Subscription System |
| **V11.12** Hand Over to Business as Usual | New Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Support (support lead) | CRM System, Support / Ticketing System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V11):

- **External actors:** New Customer (V11.01, V11.02, V11.04, V11.05, V11.07–V11.12); Implementation Partner (V11.07).
- **Teams:** Sales (V11.01, V11.02); Legal / Contracts (V11.01); Onboarding (V11.02–V11.05, V11.08–V11.10); Service Delivery (V11.03–V11.08); IT / Provisioning (V11.06); Finance / Billing (V11.11); Customer Success (V11.12); Support (V11.12).
- **IT systems:** Contract Lifecycle Management / CLM (V11.01); CRM System (V11.02, V11.12); Onboarding / Project Management System (V11.03–V11.05, V11.10); Provisioning & Identity System (V11.06); Product Platform (V11.06–V11.08); Data Migration Tooling (V11.07); Learning Management System / LMS (V11.09); Billing & Subscription System (V11.11); Support / Ticketing System (V11.12).

```text
(Implementation Partner) sit on the far right. Each band reads left to right
in the order the customer encounters the services.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- New Customer: demand-side actor, placed on the far left, present across

  training, go-live, billing, and handover.
- Implementation Partner: delivery-side actor, placed on the far right,
  engaged during data migration.

2. Interfaces

- Contract Submission Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Contract

- Scope Confirmation Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Scope and
  Entitlements Service; serves V11.02.
- Kick-off Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Onboarding
  Engagement Service; serves V11.04.
- Requirements Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Requirements

- Migration Collaboration Interface: used by New Customer and Implementation
  Partner to ACCESS the Data Migration Service; serves V11.07.
- Testing Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Test and Validation

- Training Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the User Training
  Service; serves V11.09.
- Acceptance Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Go-Live Acceptance
  Service; serves V11.10.
- Billing Notification Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Billing
  Activation Service; serves V11.11.
- Handover Interface: used by New Customer to ACCESS the Business-as-Usual
  Handover Service; serves V11.12.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Contract Acceptance Service: receives and validates the signed contract or
  accepted order from the customer.
- Scope and Entitlements Service: confirms agreed scope, licences, and
  entitlements with the customer.
- Onboarding Team Assignment Service: assigns the dedicated onboarding and
  implementation team.
- Onboarding Engagement Service: delivers the kick-off meeting and onboarding
  plan to the customer.
- Requirements Collection Service: gathers customer configuration requirements
  and existing data.
- Configuration and Provisioning Service: configures and provisions the
  product environment and user identities.
- Data Migration Service: migrates customer data into the provisioned
  environment.
- Test and Validation Service: supports joint testing and validation of the
  provisioned service.
- User Training Service: delivers training to customer end users.
- Go-Live Acceptance Service: obtains formal customer sign-off to proceed to
  live.
- Billing Activation Service: activates billing and issues the first invoice.
- Business-as-Usual Handover Service: transitions the customer to ongoing
  support and customer success.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V11.01 Accept Signed Contract: receives the executed contract, logs it, and
  triggers the onboarding workflow.
- V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements: reconciles order terms, entitlements,
  and licences against the contract.
- V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team: selects and assigns onboarding manager,
  implementation consultant, and solution architect.
- V11.04 Run Kick-off: conducts the kick-off meeting, shares the onboarding
  plan, and aligns stakeholders.
- V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data: elicits configuration requirements,
  environment details, and data for migration.
- V11.06 Configure & Provision Service: provisions environments, configures
  the product platform, and creates user identities.
- V11.07 Migrate Data: extracts, transforms, loads, and validates customer
  data in the product platform.
- V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer: runs structured testing cycles with
  the customer and resolves issues.
- V11.09 Train Users: delivers product training to customer end users using
  learning materials.
- V11.10 Obtain Go-Live Acceptance: collects formal acceptance sign-off and
  records the go-live decision.
- V11.11 Activate Billing: sets up billing schedules and subscription records
  and issues the first invoice.
- V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual: completes onboarding, transfers the
  account to customer success, and opens support arrangements.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band, left to right

- Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM): manages contract storage, status, and
  handover; used in V11.01.
- CRM System: holds customer account, contact, and entitlement records; used
  in V11.02 and V11.12.
- Onboarding / Project Management System: tracks onboarding tasks, milestones,
  team assignments, and schedules; used in V11.03, V11.04, V11.05, V11.10.
- Provisioning & Identity System: provisions environments and manages user
  identities and roles; used in V11.06.
- Product Platform: the live service platform used across provisioning,
  migration, and testing; used in V11.06, V11.07, V11.08.
- Data Migration Tooling: extracts, transforms, and loads customer data into
  the product platform; used in V11.07.
- Learning Management System (LMS): hosts training content and delivers user
  training sessions; used in V11.09.
- Billing & Subscription System: manages billing schedules, subscription
  records, and invoice generation; used in V11.11.
- Support / Ticketing System: manages support cases and customer-facing support
  arrangements post-handover; used in V11.12.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
```
