### V11.01 — Accept Signed Contract

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.01 Accept Signed Contract — opens the Sign to Onboard value
chain by receiving and formally accepting a signed customer contract,
readying it for scope confirmation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the acceptance process,
with lanes for Sales and Legal / Contracts.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer who has signed and submits
the contract.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — the CLM system that stores
and validates contract records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Sales lane:
  Message start event "Signed contract received from New Customer"
  User task "Log contract receipt and assign reference number"
  User task "Perform initial completeness check"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract complete?"
  - branch "Incomplete": Send task "Request missing information from
    customer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides missing
    information"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract complete")
  - branch "Complete": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Contract complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Contract complete"
  User task "Record contract in CLM"
  Intermediate message catch event "CLM confirmation received"
  User task "Notify Legal / Contracts for review"

Legal / Contracts lane:
  User task "Review contract terms and authorised signatories"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract accepted?"
  - branch "Issues found": User task "Raise contract query with Sales"
    Intermediate message catch event "Sales responds to query"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract accepted")
  - branch "Accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Contract accepted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Contract accepted"
  User task "Record formal acceptance and countersignature"
  Service task "Update CLM with accepted status"
  Send task "Send acceptance confirmation to New Customer"
  End event "Contract accepted — ready for Confirm Scope and Entitlements"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Perform initial
completeness check" — label "Completeness check overdue (2 business
days)" — triggers Send task "Escalate overdue check to Sales manager",
which ends in a local End event "Escalation raised".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review contract terms
and authorised signatories" — label "Legal review overdue (3 business
days)" — triggers Send task "Escalate overdue review to Legal manager",
which ends in a local End event "Legal escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Sales lane with the message start
event, moves through completeness check and the "Contract complete?"
gateway — incomplete branch loops via customer response back to the
merge, complete branch passes straight through — then continues to CLM
recording and legal notification. Flow crosses to the Legal / Contracts
lane for review and the "Contract accepted?" gateway — issues branch
loops via Sales query and response back to the merge, accepted branch
passes straight through — then ends with formal acceptance recording,
CLM status update, and customer confirmation.

Message flows:
New Customer → Sales lane "Signed contract received" (signed contract
document).
Sales lane "Request missing information from customer" → New Customer
(request for missing contract information).
New Customer → Sales lane "Customer provides missing information"
(supplementary contract information).
Sales lane "Record contract in CLM" → Contract Lifecycle Management
(CLM) (new contract record).
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Sales lane "CLM confirmation
received" (contract record confirmation and reference).
Legal / Contracts lane "Update CLM with accepted status" → Contract
Lifecycle Management (CLM) (accepted status and countersignature
record).
Legal / Contracts lane "Send acceptance confirmation to New Customer"
→ New Customer (formal acceptance confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Signed Contract Document" — read by User task "Perform
initial completeness check"; read by User task "Review contract terms
and authorised signatories".
Data Object "Contract Receipt Record" — written by User task "Log
contract receipt and assign reference number"; read by User task
"Record contract in CLM".
Data Object "CLM Contract Entry" — written by User task "Record
contract in CLM"; written by Service task "Update CLM with accepted
status"; read by User task "Record formal acceptance and
countersignature".
Data Object "Acceptance Confirmation" — written by User task "Record
formal acceptance and countersignature"; read by Send task "Send
acceptance confirmation to New Customer".

This subprocess receives the signed contract from the New Customer,
checks it for completeness, records it formally in the CLM system, and
puts it through a Legal / Contracts review that ends in countersignature
and formal acceptance. The confirmed, accepted contract record is then
handed to Confirm Scope and Entitlements, where the agreed service
scope and customer entitlements are validated in detail.
```


### V11.02 — Confirm Scope & Entitlements

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.02 Confirm Scope & Entitlements — second subprocess in the
Sign to Onboard value chain, occurring after the signed contract has been
accepted and before the onboarding team is assigned.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
with lanes for the teams involved in confirming scope and entitlements.
  Lane "Onboarding" — onboarding manager reviews and confirms scope.
  Lane "Sales" — account manager supplies deal context and entitlement
  details from the original sale.
Pool "New Customer" — customer sponsor or project contact who reviews and
approves the confirmed scope.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for customer account, deal, and
entitlement data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. CRM System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Sales lane:
  Message start event "Accepted contract handed over from Accept Signed
  Contract"
  User task "Retrieve deal and entitlement details"
  Service task "Pull entitlement and order data from CRM System"
  User task "Prepare scope summary"
  Send task "Send scope summary to Onboarding for review"

Onboarding lane:
  User task "Review scope summary against contract terms"
  Exclusive gateway "Scope summary complete and consistent?"
  - branch "No — gaps or inconsistencies found": User task "Request
    clarification from Sales"
    Intermediate message catch event "Clarification received from Sales"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scope summary complete and
    consistent")
  - branch "Yes — scope confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Scope summary complete and consistent")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scope summary complete and consistent"
  User task "Draft entitlement schedule"
  Send task "Send entitlement schedule to New Customer for approval"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer approves entitlement schedule?"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer
    approves entitlement schedule")
  - branch "Disputed — amendments requested": User task "Log dispute and
    assess requested amendments"
    Exclusive gateway "Amendment within original contract scope?"
    - branch "Yes — minor adjustment": User task "Update entitlement
      schedule"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Amendment within original
      contract scope")
    - branch "No — requires scope-change process": Send task "Notify Sales
      of out-of-scope request"
      End event "Scope change escalated to Sales — out-of-scope request
      cannot be resolved within this subprocess"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Amendment within original contract scope"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer approves entitlement
    schedule")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer approves entitlement schedule"
  Service task "Update confirmed entitlements in CRM System"
  User task "Record scope confirmation and close review"
  End event "Scope and entitlements confirmed — ready for Assign Onboarding
  Team"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
Customer response received" — label "Customer response overdue (5 business
days)" — triggers Send task "Send reminder to New Customer"; flow returns to
the intermediate message catch event to continue waiting.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Sales lane, moves to the Onboarding lane
after the scope summary is prepared. Within the Onboarding lane the flow
passes through the completeness gateway (with its clarification branch looping
back to merge), then through drafting and customer approval. The approval
gateway branches to merge on approval or routes through the amendment
sub-decision, which either rejoins the approval merge or exits via its own end
event for out-of-scope cases.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider Onboarding lane (customer approval or dispute
response to entitlement schedule)
Service Provider Onboarding lane → New Customer (entitlement schedule sent for
approval; reminder if overdue)
Service Provider Sales lane → CRM System (query for entitlement and order
data)
CRM System → Service Provider Sales lane (entitlement and order data returned)
Service Provider Onboarding lane → CRM System (confirmed entitlement update
written back)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Scope Summary" — written by User task "Prepare scope summary";
read by User task "Review scope summary against contract terms".
Data Object "Entitlement Schedule" — written by User task "Draft entitlement
schedule"; read by User task "Log dispute and assess requested amendments";
updated by User task "Update entitlement schedule".
Data Object "Entitlement and Order Data" — written by Service task "Pull
entitlement and order data from CRM System"; read by User task "Prepare scope
summary".

This subprocess takes the handed-over signed contract and produces a formally
agreed entitlement schedule, confirmed in writing by the customer and recorded
in the CRM System. Any out-of-scope requests are escalated to Sales before
they can disrupt delivery. The confirmed scope and entitlements are handed to
Assign Onboarding Team so that the right resources and workplan can be matched
to exactly what the customer has purchased.
```

```text
Onboarding lane:

  Service task "Create onboarding project record in system"

    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Onboarding
        manager assigned?")
    - branch "No": User task "Escalate resourcing gap to Onboarding
        leadership"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Onboarding manager
        assigned?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Onboarding manager assigned?"

    received"

Service Delivery lane:
  User task "Review scope for implementation and technical resource needs"
  User task "Identify and assign implementation consultant"
  Exclusive gateway "Implementation consultant available?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Implementation
        consultant available?")
    - branch "No": User task "Escalate resourcing gap to Service Delivery
        leadership"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Implementation consultant
        available?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Implementation consultant available?"
  Send task "Notify implementation consultant of assignment"

    received"
  User task "Record implementation consultant confirmation in project
    record"
  User task "Compile full team assignment summary"
  End event "Onboarding team assigned — ready for Run Kick-off"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Onboarding lane with the start event,
moves through scope review and onboarding manager identification, then
assignment and escalation if needed, merging at the exclusive merge gateway
before the send task and acceptance catch event. Concurrently, after the
project record is created, flow crosses to the Service Delivery lane, which
runs through consultant identification, the availability gateway and its
escalation branch, merging at the exclusive merge gateway before the send
task and acceptance catch event. Once both lanes have recorded their

Message flows:
Onboarding / Project Management System → Service Provider, Onboarding lane,
  "Create onboarding project record in system" (project record created and

Service Provider, Onboarding lane, "Record onboarding manager confirmation

7. Data objects

  confirmation in project record"; written by "Record implementation

Data Object "Team Assignment Summary" — written by "Compile full team

V11.03 Assign Onboarding Team takes the confirmed scope from V11.02 and
translates it into a named, committed onboarding team — pairing an onboarding
manager from the Onboarding lane with an implementation consultant from Service
Delivery, escalating any resourcing gaps, and recording all confirmations in the
project management system. The completed team assignment summary and live project
record are then handed to V11.04 Run Kick-off, where the full team meets the
customer for the first time.
```

### V11.04 — Run Kick-off

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.04 Run Kick-off — subprocess in the Sign to Onboard value
chain where the onboarding team convenes the new customer, confirms the
onboarding plan and schedule, and hands off to requirements collection.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the kick-off process,
  with lanes for Onboarding and Service Delivery.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer organisation attending and
  contributing to the kick-off.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — the project and task
  management platform used to record and distribute the onboarding plan.

2. Pool properties

Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:
  Message start event "Onboarding team assigned received from Assign
    Onboarding Team"

  Send task "Send kick-off invitation and agenda to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms kick-off attendance"
  User task "Prepare onboarding plan and schedule"
  Service task "Publish onboarding plan to project management system"
  User task "Facilitate kick-off meeting"
  User task "Capture meeting notes and action items"
  Service task "Record kick-off completion in project management system"

  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All required
      customer contacts confirmed")
  - branch "No": Send task "Request missing contact details from customer"

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All required customer contacts
      confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All required customer contacts confirmed"
  End event "Kick-off completed — ready for Collect Requirements & Data"

Service Delivery lane:
  User task "Present solution architecture and delivery approach"
  User task "Confirm roles, responsibilities and escalation paths"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  Customer confirms kick-off attendance" — label "Confirmation overdue
  (3 business days)" — triggers Send task "Send reminder to customer for
  kick-off confirmation", which rejoins the flow at the same message catch
  event (loop repeats).
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  Missing contact details received" — label "Contact details overdue
  (2 business days)" — triggers Send task "Chase customer for outstanding
  contacts", which rejoins the flow at the same message catch event
  (loop repeats).

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Onboarding lane at the message start
  event, proceeds through scheduling, invitation, attendance confirmation,
  plan preparation and publication, then into the kick-off meeting tasks;
  the Service Delivery lane tasks "Present solution architecture" and
  "Confirm roles" occur during the meeting and are sequenced between

  confirmed; the "No" branch sends a request and waits for a reply before
  merging; both branches rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway and the
  flow ends.

Message flows:

    customer") → New Customer (kick-off invitation and agenda).
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer confirms kick-off attendance") (attendance confirmation).
  Service Provider (Send task "Send reminder to customer for kick-off
    confirmation") → New Customer (attendance reminder).
  Service Provider (Send task "Request missing contact details from
    customer") → New Customer (request for missing contacts).

    "Missing contact details received") (missing contact details).
  Service Provider (Service task "Publish onboarding plan to project
    management system") → Onboarding / Project Management System
    (onboarding plan and schedule).
  Service Provider (Service task "Record kick-off completion in project
    management system") → Onboarding / Project Management System

  plan and schedule"; read by "Publish onboarding plan to project management

V11.04 Run Kick-off brings the service provider and the new customer together
to align on the onboarding plan, delivery approach, roles, and schedule. The
onboarding manager facilitates the meeting, the solution architect presents
the technical approach, and all action items and confirmed contacts are
recorded in the project management system. The completed kick-off record and
confirmed contact list are handed to V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data,
enabling the implementation consultant to begin structured requirements
gathering with the right customer representatives.
```

### V11.05 — Collect Requirements & Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.05 Collect Requirements & Data — subprocess in the Sign to
Onboard value chain, following Run Kick-off and preceding Configure &
Provision Service.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
with lanes for Service Delivery.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer supplying requirements and data.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — the tooling that records
requirements, data submissions, and onboarding tasks.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery lane:
Message start event "Kick-off completed — ready to collect requirements
and data"
User task "Prepare requirements and data collection templates"
Send task "Issue requirements questionnaire and data templates to customer"
Intermediate message catch event "Customer questionnaire and data
submission received"
User task "Review submitted requirements and data for completeness"
Exclusive gateway "Submission complete?"
- branch "Incomplete":
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Submission Complete" (standard loop)
  containing, in order: User task "Log gaps and clarify outstanding items
  with customer", Send task "Request supplementary information from
  customer", Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary information
  received", User task "Re-assess completeness of submission"
  (exits subprocess)
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Submission complete")
- branch "Complete":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Submission complete")
Exclusive merge gateway "Submission complete"
User task "Consolidate and document confirmed requirements"
Service task "Record requirements and data artefacts in Onboarding /
Project Management System"
User task "Obtain customer sign-off on documented requirements"
Exclusive gateway "Customer sign-off granted?"
- branch "Not approved — revisions requested":
  User task "Update requirements documentation per customer feedback"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer sign-off granted")
- branch "Approved":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer sign-off granted")
Exclusive merge gateway "Customer sign-off granted"
End event "Requirements and data confirmed — ready for Configure and
Provision Service"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Submission Complete" — label "Submission overdue (14 days)" — triggers
User task "Escalate delayed submission to onboarding manager", which flows
to an End event "Submission escalated — onboarding on hold".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Service Delivery lane the flow runs from the
message start event through template preparation, issuance, the message
catch event for customer submission, review, and the "Submission complete?"
gateway. The incomplete branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and
exits back to the merge gateway; the complete branch joins directly. After
the merge, the flow continues through consolidation, system recording,
sign-off request, and the "Customer sign-off granted?" gateway. The
revision branch loops back to the merge gateway after updating the
documentation; the approved branch joins at the same merge gateway, then
flows to the end event.

Message flows:
Send task "Issue requirements questionnaire and data templates to
customer" → New Customer (requirements questionnaire and data templates).
New Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Customer questionnaire
and data submission received" (completed questionnaire and data
submission).
Send task "Request supplementary information from customer" → New Customer
(request for supplementary information).
New Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary information
received" (supplementary information).
User task "Obtain customer sign-off on documented requirements" → New
Customer (requirements documentation for review and sign-off).
New Customer → Exclusive gateway "Customer sign-off granted?" (sign-off
decision).
Service task "Record requirements and data artefacts in Onboarding /
Project Management System" → Onboarding / Project Management System
(confirmed requirements and data artefacts).
Onboarding / Project Management System → Service task "Record requirements
and data artefacts in Onboarding / Project Management System"
(confirmation of recorded tasks and milestones).

and document confirmed requirements".
Data Object "Requirements Documentation" — written by User task
"Consolidate and document confirmed requirements"; read by User task
"Obtain customer sign-off on documented requirements"; read by Service
task "Record requirements and data artefacts in Onboarding / Project
Management System".

V11.05 captures, validates, and documents all customer requirements and
data needed to configure and provision the service. An iterative loop
ensures gaps are chased and resolved before the implementation consultant
consolidates everything into a signed-off requirements document. That
document, logged in the Onboarding / Project Management System, is the
direct input handed to Configure & Provision Service, giving the
provisioning and delivery teams a complete, agreed baseline to work from.
```

```text
    - branch "No": User task "Log configuration issues and revise

    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Readiness

    - branch "No": User task "Document readiness gaps and assign

  Exclusive merge gateway "Readiness review passed"
```

```text
  Intermediate message catch event "Migration job result received from
    Data Migration Tooling"
  Exclusive gateway "Migration successful?"
    - branch "No — migration errors":
        User task "Analyse migration errors and prepare remediation plan"
        Exclusive gateway "Errors remediable?"
          - branch "Yes — fix and retry":
              User task "Apply data fixes"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Errors remediable")
          - branch "No — escalate":
              User task "Escalate migration failure to onboarding manager"
              End event "Migration escalated — onboarding on hold"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Errors remediable"
        Service task "Resubmit corrected migration job to Data Migration
          Tooling"
        Intermediate message catch event "Resubmit job result received
          from Data Migration Tooling"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Migration successful")
    - branch "Yes — migration complete":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Migration successful")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Migration successful"
  Service task "Trigger post-migration validation in Product Platform"
  Intermediate message catch event "Validation result received from
    Product Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Validation passed?"
    - branch "No — validation failures":
        User task "Review validation failures and remediate records"
        Service task "Resubmit failed records to Data Migration Tooling"
        Intermediate message catch event "Resubmit validation result
          received from Data Migration Tooling"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed")
    - branch "Yes — all records valid":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Validation passed"
  User task "Produce migration report"
  Send task "Send migration report to New Customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer acknowledgement of migration
    report received"
  End event "Data migration complete — ready for Test & Validate with
    Customer"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Assess data quality and
  cleanse source data" — label "Data quality review overdue (48 h)" —
  triggers User task "Escalate data quality delay to onboarding manager",
  which leads to End event "Migration delayed — escalated".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Service task "Submit migration job
  to Data Migration Tooling" — label "Migration job timeout (4 h)" —
  triggers User task "Investigate migration job timeout and retry or
  escalate", which leads to End event "Migration timed out — escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Service Delivery lane with the message
  start event and proceeds through data mapping, extract requests, quality
  assessment, and the "Data quality acceptable?" gateway, with the
  correction branch looping back through corrected-data receipt to the
  merge; then through migration job submission, the "Migration successful?"
  gateway, with the error branch splitting again on remediability (the
  non-remediable branch ending in its own end event, the remediable branch
  resubmitting and rejoining the merge), then through post-migration
  validation, the "Validation passed?" gateway (the failure branch
  resubmitting failed records and rejoining), and finally through report
  production, customer send, acknowledgement catch, and the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Request source data extract and environment
    access") → New Customer (data extract and access request)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Source data extract received from New Customer") (source data extract)
  Implementation Partner → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch
    event "Implementation Partner data package received") (partner data
    package)
  Service Provider (Send task "Send correction request to customer and
    partner") → New Customer (data correction request)
  Service Provider (Send task "Send correction request to customer and
    partner") → Implementation Partner (data correction request)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Corrected data received") (corrected data)
  Service Provider (Service task "Submit migration job to Data Migration
    Tooling") → Data Migration Tooling (migration job submission)
  Data Migration Tooling → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch
    event "Migration job result received from Data Migration Tooling")
    (migration job result)
  Service Provider (Service task "Resubmit corrected migration job to
    Data Migration Tooling") → Data Migration Tooling (corrected
    migration job)
  Data Migration Tooling → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch
    event "Resubmit job result received from Data Migration Tooling")
    (resubmit job result)
  Service Provider (Service task "Trigger post-migration validation in
    Product Platform") → Product Platform (validation trigger)
  Product Platform → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Validation result received from Product Platform") (validation result)
  Service Provider (Service task "Resubmit failed records to Data
    Migration Tooling") → Data Migration Tooling (failed records for
    reprocessing)
  Data Migration Tooling → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch
    event "Resubmit validation result received from Data Migration
    Tooling") (resubmit validation result)
  Service Provider (Send task "Send migration report to New Customer")
    → New Customer (migration report)
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer acknowledgement of migration report received")
    (acknowledgement of migration report)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Data Mapping Specification" — written by User task "Define
  migration scope and data mapping"; read by Service task "Submit
  migration job to Data Migration Tooling".
Data Object "Source Data Extract" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Source data extract received from New Customer"; read by User
  task "Assess data quality and cleanse source data".
Data Object "Implementation Partner Data Package" — written by
  Intermediate message catch event "Implementation Partner data package
  received"; read by User task "Assess data quality and cleanse source
  data".
Data Object "Data Quality Assessment" — written by User task "Assess data
  quality and cleanse source data"; read by Exclusive gateway "Data
  quality acceptable?".
Data Object "Migration Job Result" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Migration job result received from Data Migration Tooling"; read
  by Exclusive gateway "Migration successful?".
Data Object "Validation Result" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Validation result received from Product Platform"; read by
  Exclusive gateway "Validation passed?".
Data Object "Migration Report" — written by User task "Produce migration
  report"; read by Send task "Send migration report to New Customer".

V11.07 Migrate Data takes the provisioned environment handed over from
Configure & Provision Service and moves the customer's existing records
into the product platform through a controlled cycle of extract, quality
assessment, job submission, and post-load validation. Every migration
error and quality failure is either remediated in-process or escalated,
ensuring only verified data enters the platform. A signed-off migration
report is sent to the customer, and the subprocess hands a validated,
populated environment to Test & Validate with Customer.
```


### V11.08 — Test & Validate with Customer

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer — subprocess in the Sign to
Onboard value chain where the configured and provisioned service is tested
against agreed acceptance criteria with the customer before go-live.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the test and validation
  process, with two lanes: Service Delivery and Onboarding.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer participating in testing and
  providing feedback.
Pool "Product Platform" — the product or service platform used to execute
  and observe test scenarios.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Product Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Product Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Service Delivery lane:
  Message start event "Provisioned service received from Configure &
    Provision Service"
  User task "Define test scenarios and acceptance criteria"
  Service task "Register test plan in Product Platform"
  Send task "Share test plan with customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms readiness to test"
  User task "Execute test scenarios"
  Service task "Retrieve test results from Product Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "All acceptance criteria met?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All acceptance
      criteria met")
    - branch "No": User task "Log defects and issues"
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Defects Resolved" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Coordinate defect resolution with
        provisioning team", Service task "Re-run failed test scenarios in
        Product Platform", Service task "Retrieve updated test results from
        Product Platform"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All acceptance criteria met")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All acceptance criteria met"
  User task "Compile test and validation summary report"

Onboarding lane:
  User task "Review test summary with customer"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer satisfied with results?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer
      satisfied with results")
    - branch "No": Send task "Issue issue-resolution notice to customer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides further feedback"
      User task "Update test summary incorporating feedback"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Customer satisfied with
      results")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Customer satisfied with results"
  User task "Obtain customer sign-off on test outcomes"
  End event "Testing validated — ready for Train Users"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Defects Resolved" — label "Defect resolution deadline exceeded" —
  flows to End event "Testing failed — escalation required".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Service Delivery lane with the message
  start event and proceeds through test planning, platform registration,
  sharing the plan, and awaiting customer readiness, then through test
  execution and result retrieval. The "All acceptance criteria met?"
  gateway splits: the "Yes" branch and the "No" branch (which passes
  through defect logging and the loop subprocess) both rejoin at the
  exclusive merge gateway "All acceptance criteria met". Flow then
  continues to report compilation before crossing to the Onboarding lane
  for customer review. The "Customer satisfied with results?" gateway
  splits: the "Yes" branch and the "No" branch (which issues a notice,
  awaits further feedback, and updates the summary) rejoin at the
  exclusive merge gateway "Customer satisfied with results". Flow then
  continues to sign-off and the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Share test plan with customer") →
    New Customer (test plan document).
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer confirms readiness to test") (readiness confirmation).
  Service Provider (Service task "Register test plan in Product Platform")
    → Product Platform (test plan registration).
  Service Provider (Service task "Retrieve test results from Product
    Platform") → Product Platform (test results request); reverse:
    Product Platform → Service Provider (test results data).
  Service Provider (Service task "Re-run failed test scenarios in Product
    Platform") → Product Platform (re-run request); reverse: Product
    Platform → Service Provider (updated test results).
  Service Provider (Send task "Issue issue-resolution notice to customer")
    → New Customer (issue-resolution notice).
  New Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer provides further feedback") (further feedback).
  New Customer → Service Provider (User task "Obtain customer sign-off on
    test outcomes") (signed test acceptance).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Test Plan" — written by User task "Define test scenarios and
  acceptance criteria"; read by Service task "Register test plan in
  Product Platform"; read by Send task "Share test plan with customer".
Data Object "Test Results" — written by Service task "Retrieve test
  results from Product Platform"; read by Exclusive gateway "All
  acceptance criteria met?".
Data Object "Defect Log" — written by User task "Log defects and issues";
  read by User task "Coordinate defect resolution with provisioning team".
Data Object "Updated Test Results" — written by Service task "Retrieve
  updated test results from Product Platform"; read by Exclusive merge
  gateway "All acceptance criteria met".
Data Object "Test and Validation Summary Report" — written by User task
  "Compile test and validation summary report"; read by User task "Review
  test summary with customer"; read by User task "Obtain customer sign-off
  on test outcomes".
Data Object "Customer Sign-off" — written by User task "Obtain customer
  sign-off on test outcomes".

V11.08 Test & Validate with Customer covers the end-to-end cycle of
defining test scenarios, executing them against the provisioned platform,
resolving any defects that emerge, and obtaining the customer's formal
sign-off on the outcomes. It confirms that the configured service meets
the agreed acceptance criteria and that the customer is satisfied before
any training or go-live activity proceeds. The signed test acceptance and
the validated test summary are handed to Train Users, which can then
proceed with confidence that the environment is stable and ready for
end-user training.
```


### V11.09 — Train Users

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.09 Train Users — subprocess in the Sign to Onboard value
chain in which the Onboarding team delivers training to New Customer
end users and records completion in the Learning Management System,
following tested and validated service and preceding go-live acceptance.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation delivering the onboarding,
  with lanes for the team involved in training.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
    - Onboarding (trainer)
Pool "New Customer" — the customer organisation receiving training,
  represented by end users and the project contact.
Pool "Learning Management System (LMS)" — the platform used to host
  and record training content and completions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Learning Management System (LMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. New Customer
  2. Service Provider
  3. Learning Management System (LMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding (trainer) lane:
  Message start event "Validated service received from Test & Validate
    with Customer"
  Task (user) "Review training needs and tailor training plan"
  Task (send) "Share training schedule and materials with customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer confirms readiness to
    train"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Sessions Delivered"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    Task (user) "Deliver training session to user group"
    Task (send) "Send session completion record to LMS"
    Intermediate message catch event "LMS confirms session recorded"
    Task (user) "Capture attendee feedback and queries"
    Exclusive gateway "Outstanding queries requiring follow-up?"
      - branch "Yes — follow-up needed":
          Task (user) "Resolve queries and provide supplementary
            materials"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Queries Resolved")
      - branch "No — no follow-up needed":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Queries Resolved")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Queries Resolved"
  Task (user) "Review overall training completion and attendance report"
  Exclusive gateway "All required users trained and quorum met?"
    - branch "Yes — training complete":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Training Sufficiency
          Confirmed")
    - branch "No — additional sessions needed":
        Task (user) "Schedule and arrange additional training sessions"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Training Sufficiency
          Confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Training Sufficiency Confirmed"
  Task (service) "Request training completion certificate from LMS"
  Intermediate message catch event "Training completion certificate
    received from LMS"
  Task (send) "Issue training completion summary to customer"
  End event "Training complete — ready for Obtain Go-Live Acceptance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until All Sessions Delivered" — label "Training window deadline
  exceeded" — triggers a Task (user) "Escalate delayed training to
  onboarding manager" followed by End event "Training escalated —
  onboarding manager notified".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Onboarding (trainer) lane at the
message start event, proceeds through training plan review and
schedule sharing, pauses at the customer-readiness catch event, then
enters the standard-loop subprocess where each session is delivered,
recorded, feedback captured, and the queries gateway branches either
to follow-up resolution or directly to the merge, before looping.
After the loop, the attendance-review task feeds the training-
sufficiency gateway, whose "No" branch routes through additional
session scheduling back to the merge, and whose "Yes" branch reaches
the merge directly; the certificate request and completion summary
tasks then lead to the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (send task "Share training schedule and materials
    with customer") → New Customer (training schedule and materials)
  New Customer → Service Provider (intermediate message catch event
    "Customer confirms readiness to train") (readiness confirmation)
  Service Provider (send task "Send session completion record to LMS")
    → Learning Management System (LMS) (session completion record)
  Learning Management System (LMS) → Service Provider (intermediate
    message catch event "LMS confirms session recorded") (session
    recording confirmation)
  Service Provider (service task "Request training completion
    certificate from LMS") → Learning Management System (LMS)
    (certificate request)
  Learning Management System (LMS) → Service Provider (intermediate
    message catch event "Training completion certificate received from
    LMS") (training completion certificate)
  Service Provider (send task "Issue training completion summary to

7. Data objects

Data Object "Training Plan" — written by "Review training needs and

  group".
Data Object "Training Schedule and Materials" — written by "Review
  training needs and tailor training plan"; read by "Share training
  schedule and materials with customer".
Data Object "Attendee Feedback Record" — written by "Capture attendee
  feedback and queries"; read by "Review overall training completion
  and attendance report".
Data Object "Training Completion Certificate" — written by Learning
  Management System (LMS) upon certificate request; read by "Issue
  training completion summary to customer".

This subprocess takes the tested and provisioned service and ensures
that all required end users are trained, their completion recorded in
the LMS, and any gaps addressed before go-live. It delivers a training
completion summary and certificate to the customer and hands a
confirmed-trained user base to Obtain Go-Live Acceptance, where the
customer formally signs off readiness to go live.
```


### V11.10 — Obtain Go-Live Acceptance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.10 Obtain Go-Live Acceptance — the subprocess in which the
Onboarding team formally seeks and records the customer's acceptance that
the service is ready to go live, sitting between Test & Validate with
Customer and Activate Billing in the Sign to Onboard value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the acceptance process,
containing the Onboarding team.
Pool "New Customer" — the external customer sponsor or project contact who
reviews and signs off go-live acceptance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — the system in which
acceptance tasks, milestones, and sign-off records are captured.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Onboarding / Project Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Onboarding / Project Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Onboarding lane:

Message start event "Validated service received from Test & Validate
with Customer"
User task "Prepare go-live acceptance pack"
Send task "Issue acceptance pack to customer"
Intermediate message catch event "Customer acceptance response received"
Exclusive gateway "Acceptance granted?"
- branch "Yes — accepted": User task "Record formal go-live acceptance"
  then Service task "Update milestone as accepted in project system"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance outcome resolved")
- branch "No — issues raised": User task "Log customer issues and
  determine remediation action"
  Exclusive gateway "Issues resolvable within onboarding scope?"
  - branch "Yes — resolvable": Send task "Notify customer of remediation
    plan"
    Intermediate timer catch event "Remediation period elapsed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance outcome resolved")
  - branch "No — escalate": Send task "Escalate to senior onboarding
    management"
    End event "Go-live acceptance blocked — escalated to senior management"
Exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance outcome resolved"
User task "Prepare go-live readiness summary"
Service task "Close acceptance milestone in project system"
End event "Go-live acceptance confirmed — ready for Activate Billing"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Prepare go-live
acceptance pack" — label "Acceptance pack overdue (2 business days)" —
triggers Send task "Send internal alert for delayed acceptance pack
preparation"; flow rejoins before Send task "Issue acceptance pack to
customer".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Customer acceptance response received" — label "No customer response
after 5 business days" — triggers User task "Chase customer for
acceptance response"; flow loops back to Intermediate message catch event
"Customer acceptance response received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the flow runs entirely within the Onboarding lane,
beginning at the message start event and progressing through pack
preparation, issuance, and the customer response wait; the Acceptance
granted gateway then splits into the accepted branch (record and update)
and the issues-raised branch (log and resolve or escalate); the resolvable
sub-branch rejoins the exclusive merge gateway "Acceptance outcome
resolved" together with the accepted branch; the escalation branch ends at
its own end event; after the merge gateway the flow passes through
readiness summary, project system closure, and the final end event.

Message flows:
Send task "Issue acceptance pack to customer" → New Customer (go-live
acceptance pack with sign-off request)
New Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Customer acceptance
response received" (acceptance decision or issues list)
Send task "Notify customer of remediation plan" → New Customer
(remediation plan and revised acceptance timeline)
Send task "Escalate to senior onboarding management" → New Customer
(escalation notification)
Service task "Update milestone as accepted in project system" →
Onboarding / Project Management System (accepted milestone record)
Service task "Close acceptance milestone in project system" →
Onboarding / Project Management System (closed acceptance milestone and
readiness summary)
Onboarding / Project Management System → User task "Prepare go-live
acceptance pack" (open milestone and test validation outcomes)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Go-Live Acceptance Pack" — written by User task "Prepare
go-live acceptance pack"; read by Send task "Issue acceptance pack to
customer".
Data Object "Customer Acceptance Response" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Customer acceptance response received"; read by
Exclusive gateway "Acceptance granted?".
Data Object "Issue and Remediation Log" — written by User task "Log
customer issues and determine remediation action"; read by Send task
"Notify customer of remediation plan".
Data Object "Go-Live Readiness Summary" — written by User task "Prepare
go-live readiness summary"; read by Service task "Close acceptance
milestone in project system".

This subprocess formalises the customer's sign-off that the configured and
tested service meets their requirements and is fit for live operation. It
captures acceptance or drives remediation of any outstanding issues, and
records the outcome as a closed milestone in the project system. On
successful completion it hands a confirmed go-live acceptance and readiness
summary to Activate Billing, enabling the billing officer to initiate the
customer's billing schedule with confidence that the service is live.
```


### V11.11 — Activate Billing

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.11 Activate Billing — subprocess within Sign to Onboard in
which the Finance / Billing team creates the billing schedule, issues the
first invoice, and confirms payment arrangements with the new customer.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the onboarding process,
  with Finance / Billing lane.
Pool "New Customer" — the customer receiving the first invoice and
  confirming payment arrangements.
Pool "Billing & Subscription System" — the billing and subscription
  management platform that holds the billing schedule and generates invoices.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing & Subscription System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Billing & Subscription System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Finance / Billing lane:
  Message start event "Go-live acceptance received from Obtain Go-Live
    Acceptance"
  User task "Retrieve contract billing terms"
  Service task "Create billing schedule in Billing & Subscription System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Billing schedule confirmed by system"
  User task "Review and approve billing schedule"
  Exclusive gateway "Schedule approved?"
    - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Schedule approved?")
    - branch "Needs correction": User task "Amend billing schedule",
        then Service task "Update billing schedule in Billing &
        Subscription System", then Intermediate message catch event
        "Updated schedule confirmed by system",
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved?"
  Service task "Generate first invoice in Billing & Subscription System"
  Intermediate message catch event "First invoice received from system"
  User task "Review first invoice for accuracy"
  Exclusive gateway "Invoice correct?"
    - branch "Correct": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Invoice correct?")
    - branch "Incorrect": User task "Correct invoice details",
        then Service task "Regenerate invoice in Billing &
        Subscription System",
        then Intermediate message catch event "Corrected invoice
        received from system",
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Invoice correct?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Invoice correct?"
  Send task "Issue first invoice to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer payment confirmation received"
  User task "Record payment arrangement in Billing & Subscription System"
  User task "Update customer billing status in CRM"
  End event "Billing activated — ready for Hand Over to Business as Usual"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review and approve billing
  schedule" — label "Approval overdue (2 business days)" — triggers
  Escalation end event "Escalate billing approval delay".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Customer payment confirmation received" — label "Payment confirmation
  not received (5 business days)" — triggers Escalation end event
  "Escalate outstanding payment confirmation".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Finance / Billing lane. From
  the start event the work proceeds through billing schedule creation and
  system confirmation to the approval gateway; the "Needs correction" branch
  loops through amend and update tasks before rejoining at the exclusive
  merge gateway "Schedule approved?". Flow then continues through invoice
  generation and review; the "Incorrect" branch loops through correction and
  regeneration before rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway "Invoice
  correct?". After invoice issue, flow waits for customer payment
  confirmation, then closes with recording and status update before the
  end event.

Message flows:
  Finance / Billing lane → Billing & Subscription System (create billing
    schedule request).
  Billing & Subscription System → Finance / Billing lane (billing schedule
    confirmed).
  Finance / Billing lane → Billing & Subscription System (update billing
    schedule request, on correction branch).
  Billing & Subscription System → Finance / Billing lane (updated schedule
    confirmed, on correction branch).
  Finance / Billing lane → Billing & Subscription System (generate first
    invoice request).
  Billing & Subscription System → Finance / Billing lane (first invoice
    document).
  Finance / Billing lane → Billing & Subscription System (regenerate
    invoice request, on correction branch).
  Billing & Subscription System → Finance / Billing lane (corrected invoice
    document, on correction branch).
  Finance / Billing lane → New Customer (first invoice issued).
  New Customer → Finance / Billing lane (payment confirmation).
  Finance / Billing lane → Billing & Subscription System (record payment
    arrangement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Contract Billing Terms" — read by User task "Retrieve contract
  billing terms"; read by User task "Review and approve billing schedule".
Data Object "Billing Schedule" — written by Service task "Create billing
  schedule in Billing & Subscription System"; read by User task "Review and
  approve billing schedule"; written by User task "Amend billing schedule".
Data Object "First Invoice" — written by Service task "Generate first
  invoice in Billing & Subscription System"; read by User task "Review first
  invoice for accuracy"; read by Send task "Issue first invoice to customer".
Data Object "Payment Confirmation" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Customer payment confirmation received"; read by User task "Record
  payment arrangement in Billing & Subscription System".

Activate Billing takes the go-live acceptance from Obtain Go-Live Acceptance
and converts it into a live billing relationship: the billing schedule is
created and approved, the first invoice is generated, reviewed and issued to
the customer, and payment arrangements are recorded in the Billing &
Subscription System. The subprocess hands a confirmed, active billing account
to Hand Over to Business as Usual.
```


### V11.12 — Hand Over to Business as Usual

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V11.12 Hand Over to Business as Usual — final subprocess of the
Sign to Onboard value chain, transferring the activated customer from the
onboarding programme to steady-state support and customer success.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the handover process,
with lanes for Customer Success and Support.
Pool "New Customer" — the customer's sponsor, project contact and end users
receiving the handover.
Pool "CRM System" — system of record for the customer account and
relationship data.
Pool "Support / Ticketing System" — system used to register the customer
for ongoing support and log the handover case.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "New Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Support / Ticketing System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. New Customer
2. Service Provider
3. CRM System
4. Support / Ticketing System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Customer Success lane (customer success manager):
  Message start event "Go-live acceptance confirmed — received from Obtain
    Go-Live Acceptance"
  User task "Review onboarding record and close onboarding project"
  Service task "Update customer account status to active in CRM System"
  User task "Prepare handover pack and transition summary"
  Send task "Send handover pack to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer acknowledges handover pack"
  User task "Introduce customer success manager to customer contacts"
  User task "Agree ongoing success cadence and escalation path"
  Service task "Record success plan in CRM System"
  Exclusive gateway "Support account ready?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Support account
    ready")
  - branch "No": User task "Coordinate support account setup with Support
    lane" (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Support account ready")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Support account ready"
  User task "Confirm support arrangements with customer"
  Send task "Send go-live confirmation and first-contact details to customer"
  End event "Customer handed over to Business as Usual"

Support lane (support lead):
  User task "Register customer in Support / Ticketing System"
  User task "Assign support tier and SLA profile"
  User task "Create welcome support case and log handover details"
  User task "Brief support team on customer background and known issues"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  Customer acknowledges handover pack" — if no acknowledgement is received
  within five business days, escalate to customer success manager: User task
  "Chase customer acknowledgement".
Non-interrupting escalation boundary event on User task "Coordinate support
  account setup with Support lane" — if Support lane setup is not confirmed
  within two business days, escalation boundary event labelled "Support
  setup overdue" triggers User task "Escalate support account delay to
  Support lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Customer Success lane at the message
start event and moves through account update, pack preparation, and
dispatch, pausing at the intermediate message catch event for customer
acknowledgement before the introduction and success-plan tasks. The gateway
"Support account ready?" branches to a merge point; the "No" branch passes
through the coordination task before rejoining. After the merge, the flow
continues through confirmation and the final send task to the end event.
The Support lane tasks form a self-contained sequence — register, assign
SLA, create case, brief team — triggered in parallel once the onboarding
record review is complete and feeding back readiness confirmation to the
Customer Success lane gateway.

Message flows:
New Customer → Service Provider Customer Success lane (go-live acceptance
  confirmation, triggering the start event)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → New Customer (handover pack and
  transition summary sent via Send task "Send handover pack to customer")
New Customer → Service Provider Customer Success lane (handover pack
  acknowledgement received at intermediate message catch event)
Service Provider Customer Success lane → New Customer (go-live confirmation
  and first-contact details sent via Send task "Send go-live confirmation
  and first-contact details to customer")
Service Provider Customer Success lane → CRM System (customer account
  status update via Service task "Update customer account status to active
  in CRM System")
Service Provider Customer Success lane → CRM System (success plan recorded
  via Service task "Record success plan in CRM System")
Service Provider Support lane → Support / Ticketing System (customer
  registration, SLA profile, and handover case created via User tasks
  "Register customer in Support / Ticketing System" and "Create welcome
  support case and log handover details")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Onboarding Record" — read by User task "Review onboarding
  record and close onboarding project".
Data Object "Handover Pack" — written by User task "Prepare handover pack
  and transition summary"; read by Send task "Send handover pack to
  customer".
Data Object "Success Plan" — written by User task "Agree ongoing success
  cadence and escalation path"; read by Service task "Record success plan
  in CRM System".
Data Object "Customer Support Profile" — written by User task "Assign
  support tier and SLA profile"; read by User task "Brief support team on
  customer background and known issues".

This subprocess completes the Sign to Onboard value chain by formally
closing the onboarding project, registering the customer for steady-state
support, and placing them under the care of the customer success manager.
It hands the customer a confirmed success plan, agreed escalation path, and
active support account, marking the transition to Business as Usual and
ending the onboarding programme.
```


## V12 — Renew to Retain

**Teams and roles involved.**
Renew to Retain usually involves Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, Renewals, Finance/Billing, Support, and Product, with Legal or Contracts involved where terms change. Key roles include customer success manager, renewals manager, account manager, support lead, billing officer, contracts administrator, and product or adoption analyst.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Existing Customer, usually represented by a commercial owner and a service owner. The process is initiated by an approaching contract end date, a usage or health trigger, or a customer-initiated cancellation or change request. Other external parties include resellers and channel partners, procurement teams acting for the customer, and payment providers.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: monitor account health and usage, identify the renewal opportunity, review service performance with the customer, assess risk of churn, prepare the renewal proposal, negotiate terms, handle cancellation or downgrade requests, execute the renewal, update entitlements and billing, and run win-back for lapsed customers.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include CRM, customer success platform, subscription and billing management, contract lifecycle management, product usage analytics, support/ticketing, survey and feedback tools, and business intelligence reporting.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include renewal notice periods and auto-renewal terms, discounting and approval authority, price-increase policy, cancellation and refund terms, customer health scoring definitions, escalation procedure for at-risk accounts, and retention offer approval rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides renewal intent, feedback on service performance, changes to required volumes or scope, cancellation or non-renewal notice, and purchase orders or signatures. The process provides the customer with renewal notices, service and value reviews, proposals and pricing, negotiated terms, confirmation of renewal or cancellation, and revised billing schedules.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates renewal opportunities, health scores and risk flags, proposals and quotes, amended contracts, entitlement changes, and billing schedules. IT systems provide contract dates and terms, usage and adoption data, support-case volumes and satisfaction scores, invoice and payment history, and churn and renewal-rate reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Service Provider" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are
the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V12.01** Monitor Account Health & Usage | — | Customer Success (customer success manager) | Customer Success Platform, Product Usage Analytics |
| **V12.02** Identify Renewal Opportunity | — | Renewals (renewals manager), Customer Success (customer success manager) | CRM System |
| **V12.03** Review Service Performance with Customer | Existing Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Support (support lead) | Customer Success Platform, Support / Ticketing System |
| **V12.04** Assess Churn Risk | — | Customer Success (customer success manager), Product (adoption analyst) | Product Usage Analytics, Business Intelligence Platform |
| **V12.05** Prepare Renewal Proposal | — | Renewals (renewals manager), Account Management (account manager) | CRM System |
| **V12.06** Negotiate Terms | Existing Customer, Channel Partner | Renewals (renewals manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V12.07** Handle Cancellation or Downgrade | Existing Customer | Customer Success (customer success manager), Renewals (renewals manager) | CRM System, Billing & Subscription System |
| **V12.08** Execute Renewal | Existing Customer | Renewals (renewals manager), Legal / Contracts (contracts administrator) | Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) |
| **V12.09** Update Entitlements & Billing | Payment Provider | Finance / Billing (billing officer) | Billing & Subscription System |
| **V12.10** Run Win-Back | Existing Customer | Account Management (account manager), Customer Success (customer success manager) | CRM System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V12):

- **External actors:** Existing Customer (V12.03, V12.06–V12.08, V12.10); Channel Partner (V12.06); Payment Provider (V12.09).
- **Teams:** Customer Success (V12.01–V12.04, V12.07, V12.10); Renewals (V12.02, V12.05–V12.08); Support (V12.03); Product (V12.04); Account Management (V12.05, V12.10); Legal / Contracts (V12.06, V12.08); Finance / Billing (V12.09).
- **IT systems:** Customer Success Platform (V12.01, V12.03); Product Usage Analytics (V12.01, V12.04); CRM System (V12.02, V12.05, V12.07, V12.10); Support / Ticketing System (V12.03); Business Intelligence Platform (V12.04); Contract Lifecycle Management / CLM (V12.06, V12.08); Billing & Subscription System (V12.07, V12.09).

### V12.01 — Monitor Account Health & Usage

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.01 Monitor Account Health & Usage — first subprocess of the
Renew to Retain value chain, establishing ongoing visibility of account
health before any renewal action is taken.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the monitoring process,
  containing the Customer Success team.
  Lane "Customer Success (customer success manager)" — monitors account
    health, reviews usage signals, and scores accounts.
Pool "Customer Success Platform" — SaaS platform providing health scores
  and engagement data.
Pool "Product Usage Analytics" — analytics system providing product
  adoption and usage metrics.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Success Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "Product Usage Analytics" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. Customer Success Platform
  2. Service Provider
  3. Product Usage Analytics

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Customer Success (customer success manager) lane:
  Timer start event "Scheduled monitoring cycle triggered"
  Service task "Pull usage and adoption metrics from Product Usage Analytics"
  Service task "Pull health scores and engagement data from Customer
    Success Platform"
  User task "Review combined health and usage data"
  Exclusive gateway "Health data complete and current?"
    - branch "No — data gaps identified": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
      Until Data Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify missing or stale data sources",
      Service task "Re-request data from relevant system"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Health data
      complete and current?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Health data complete and current?"
  User task "Assess account health score against thresholds"
  Exclusive gateway "Health threshold breached?"
    - branch "Yes — at risk": User task "Flag account as at-risk and
      record risk signal"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Health threshold breached?")
    - branch "No — healthy": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Health threshold breached?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Health threshold breached?"
  User task "Update account health record"
  Service task "Write health score and risk flags to Customer Success
    Platform"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Next monitoring cycle due"
  End event "Account health monitored — ready for Identify Renewal
    Opportunity"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs entirely within the Customer Success lane.
After the timer start, the two pull service tasks run in sequence, feeding
the review user task. The "Health data complete and current?" gateway
branches to the loop subprocess on the No path and rejoins at the merge
gateway; the Yes path goes directly to the merge gateway. From the merge,
assessment and the threshold gateway follow; both branches rejoin at the
"Health threshold breached?" merge gateway. The at-risk flag task sits on
the Yes branch before that merge. After the merge, the health record is
updated, scores are written back, and an intermediate timer catch event
holds the flow until the next cycle is due before reaching the end event.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Service task "Pull usage and adoption metrics from
    Product Usage Analytics") → Product Usage Analytics (usage and
    adoption metrics request).
  Product Usage Analytics → Service Provider (Service task "Pull usage
    and adoption metrics from Product Usage Analytics") (usage and
    adoption metrics data).
  Service Provider (Service task "Pull health scores and engagement data
    from Customer Success Platform") → Customer Success Platform (health
    score and engagement data request).
  Customer Success Platform → Service Provider (Service task "Pull health
    scores and engagement data from Customer Success Platform") (health
    scores and engagement data).
  Service Provider (Service task "Write health score and risk flags to
    Customer Success Platform") → Customer Success Platform (updated
    health score and risk flags).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Usage and Adoption Metrics" — written by "Pull usage and
  adoption metrics from Product Usage Analytics"; read by "Review
  combined health and usage data".
Data Object "Health Score and Engagement Data" — written by "Pull health
  scores and engagement data from Customer Success Platform"; read by
  "Review combined health and usage data".
Data Object "Account Health Record" — written by "Update account health
  record"; read by "Write health score and risk flags to Customer
  Success Platform".
Data Object "Risk Signal" — written by "Flag account as at-risk and
  record risk signal"; read by "Update account health record".

This subprocess establishes a repeating, data-driven view of every
account's health by combining product usage metrics with platform-held
engagement scores. At-risk accounts are flagged and health records are
kept current in the Customer Success Platform. The output — a scored,
up-to-date account health record with any risk flags set — is handed to
Identify Renewal Opportunity, which uses it to prioritise which accounts
need proactive renewal action.
```


### V12.02 — Identify Renewal Opportunity

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.02 Identify Renewal Opportunity — second subprocess in the
Renew to Retain value chain, triggered by health monitoring outputs and
responsible for surfacing upcoming renewals and assigning them for action.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the renewal process,
  containing the Renewals and Customer Success teams.
Pool "CRM System" — the CRM platform used to log and manage renewal
  opportunities.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider": white-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Service Provider (white-box)
2. CRM System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Renewals lane:
  Timer start event "Contract end date threshold reached or health trigger
    received from Monitor Account Health & Usage"
  User task "Review upcoming contract end dates and renewal list"
  User task "Qualify renewal opportunity"
  Exclusive gateway "Opportunity valid and within renewal window?"
    - branch "No — outside window or not yet actionable": End event
        "Opportunity deferred — no action required at this time"
    - branch "Yes — proceed": User task "Create or update renewal
        opportunity record in CRM"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity valid and within renewal window?"
  User task "Set renewal priority and target close date"
  Exclusive gateway "Account requires Customer Success involvement?"
    - branch "No — standard renewal": User task "Assign renewal to
        renewals manager"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Account requires Customer
        Success involvement?")
    - branch "Yes — at-risk or strategic account": User task "Flag account
        for joint ownership"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Account requires Customer
        Success involvement?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Account requires Customer Success involvement?"
  Send task "Notify assigned owner of renewal opportunity"

Customer Success lane:
  User task "Confirm account context and health summary"
  User task "Record ownership assignment and next-step actions"
  End event "Renewal opportunity identified and assigned — ready for
    Review Service Performance with Customer"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Renewals lane with the timer start event,
moving through contract-date review, qualification, and the first exclusive
gateway. The "No" branch ends at its own end event; the "Yes" branch continues
to create the CRM record and then merges. From the merge, flow continues
through priority-setting and the second exclusive gateway, whose "No" branch
assigns to the renewals manager and whose "Yes" branch flags for joint
ownership; both branches rejoin at the second merge gateway. The send task
notifying the assigned owner follows. Flow then crosses to the Customer Success
lane, where the account context is confirmed and ownership is recorded, ending
at the subprocess end event.

Message flows:
  "Service Provider — Renewals lane: User task 'Create or update renewal
    opportunity record in CRM'" → CRM System (renewal opportunity record
    created or updated).
  CRM System → "Service Provider — Renewals lane: User task 'Review
    upcoming contract end dates and renewal list'" (contract dates and
    existing account data).
  CRM System → "Service Provider — Customer Success lane: User task
    'Confirm account context and health summary'" (health score and
    account context data).
  "Service Provider — Customer Success lane: User task 'Record ownership
    assignment and next-step actions'" → CRM System (ownership assignment
    and next-step actions recorded).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Renewal Opportunity Record" — written by User task "Create or
  update renewal opportunity record in CRM"; read by User task "Set renewal
  priority and target close date" and User task "Confirm account context
  and health summary".
Data Object "Account Health Summary" — read by User task "Qualify renewal
  opportunity" and User task "Confirm account context and health summary".
Data Object "Ownership and Next-Step Actions" — written by User task
  "Record ownership assignment and next-step actions"; read by Send task
  "Notify assigned owner of renewal opportunity".

This subprocess scans the contract portfolio for accounts entering their
renewal window, qualifies each as actionable, and logs a formal renewal
opportunity in the CRM with a priority, target date, and named owner. Where
the account carries elevated risk or strategic value, Customer Success is
brought in alongside the renewals manager before the record is finalised.
The subprocess hands a fully assigned, context-enriched renewal opportunity
to Review Service Performance with Customer, which will engage the customer
directly.
```


### V12.03 — Review Service Performance with Customer

```text
V12.03 brings together usage data, support history, and direct customer
```

### V12.04 — Assess Churn Risk

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.04 Assess Churn Risk — the subprocess that synthesises usage,
adoption, and support signals into a churn risk rating and hands a scored
account to the Renewals team for proposal preparation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the renewal process,
  containing Customer Success and Product lanes.
Pool "Product Usage Analytics" — IT system providing usage and adoption data.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — IT system providing churn and

Top to bottom:
```
