```text
2. Product Usage Analytics
3. Business Intelligence Platform

Customer Success lane (customer success manager):

  User task "Record churn risk rating and risk flags on account record"

Product lane (adoption analyst):
```

### V12.05 — Prepare Renewal Proposal

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.05 Prepare Renewal Proposal — prepares a costed, approved renewal
proposal for the customer following churn-risk assessment, sitting between
Assess Churn Risk and Negotiate Terms in the Renew to Retain value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation preparing the renewal proposal,
  with lanes for Renewals and Account Management.
Pool "CRM System" — IT system holding renewal opportunities, quotes,
  and proposal records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "CRM System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Service Provider (white-box, contains all process flow)
2. CRM System (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Renewals lane:
  Message start event "Churn risk assessment received from Assess Churn Risk"
  User task "Review churn risk assessment and contract data"
  User task "Determine renewal scope and pricing parameters"
  Service task "Retrieve current contract terms and usage data from CRM System"
  User task "Draft renewal proposal"
  Service task "Record draft proposal in CRM System"
  Exclusive gateway "Discount required beyond standard authority?"
  - branch "No — standard discount": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Discount approval resolved")
  - branch "Yes — escalated discount needed": User task "Submit discount
    request for management approval"
    Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received"
    Exclusive gateway "Discount approved?"
    - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Discount approval resolved")
    - branch "Rejected": User task "Revise proposal within approved
      parameters"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discount approval resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Discount approval resolved"
  User task "Finalise renewal proposal document"
  Service task "Update proposal status in CRM System"
  Send task "Hand off proposal to Account Management for review"

Account Management lane:
  User task "Review proposal for account fit and relationship context"
  Exclusive gateway "Proposal accepted as ready?"
  - branch "Yes — ready to present": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Proposal readiness resolved")
  - branch "No — amendments needed": User task "Provide amendment
    instructions to Renewals"
    Intermediate message catch event "Amended proposal received from Renewals"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Proposal readiness resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Proposal readiness resolved"
  User task "Confirm proposal ready for negotiation"
  Service task "Record finalised proposal in CRM System"
  End event "Renewal proposal finalised — ready for Negotiate Terms"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Submit discount request for
  management approval" — label "Approval overdue — escalate" — on expiry,
  flow continues to User task "Escalate approval request to senior management"
  then rejoins at Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Renewals lane, progressing from risk
  review through pricing, drafting, and CRM recording to the discount gateway.
  The standard-discount branch and the approved or revised branches from the
  nested discount-approval gateway all merge at "Discount approval resolved"
  before the proposal is finalised and handed to Account Management. In the
  Account Management lane, the review gateway either passes the proposal
  directly or loops via an amendment instruction and a message catch before
  merging at "Proposal readiness resolved" and closing at the end event.

Message flows:
  CRM System → Service task "Retrieve current contract terms and usage data
    from CRM System" (contract terms, usage statistics, pricing history)
  Service task "Record draft proposal in CRM System" → CRM System
    (draft proposal record)
  Service task "Update proposal status in CRM System" → CRM System
    (updated proposal status)
  Service task "Record finalised proposal in CRM System" → CRM System
    (finalised proposal record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Churn Risk Assessment" — read by User task "Review churn risk
  assessment and contract data".
Data Object "Renewal Proposal" — written by User task "Draft renewal
  proposal"; read by User task "Review proposal for account fit and
  relationship context"; updated by User task "Finalise renewal proposal
  document".
Data Object "Discount Request" — written by User task "Submit discount
  request for management approval"; read by User task "Revise proposal
  within approved parameters".
Data Object "Amendment Instructions" — written by User task "Provide
  amendment instructions to Renewals"; read by Renewals lane following
  the intermediate message catch event.

V12.05 takes the churn risk output from Assess Churn Risk and transforms it
into a costed, scoped, and internally approved renewal proposal. Renewals
leads the pricing and drafting work, escalating discounts where needed, while
Account Management applies relationship context and confirms the proposal is
fit to present. The finalised proposal, recorded in the CRM System, is handed
to Negotiate Terms as the primary input for customer-facing commercial
discussions.
```


### V12.06 — Negotiate Terms

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.06 Negotiate Terms — the subprocess in which the Renewals and
Legal/Contracts teams work with the Existing Customer and Channel Partner
to agree final contract terms and an approved proposal before execution.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation running the negotiation process,
  with lanes for Renewals and Legal/Contracts.
Pool "Existing Customer" — the customer's commercial or procurement
  representative.
Pool "Channel Partner" — reseller or channel partner where the customer
  buys through an indirect route.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — the CLM system used to
  draft, redline, and store negotiated contracts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Existing Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Channel Partner" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Existing Customer
2. Channel Partner
3. Service Provider
4. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Renewals lane:
  Message start event "Renewal proposal received from Prepare Renewal
    Proposal"
  User task "Review proposal and set negotiation parameters"
  Send task "Issue proposal and opening terms to customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Response type?"
  - branch "Accepted without changes": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Response type resolved")
  - branch "Amendments or counter-terms requested": User task "Capture
      requested amendments"; (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Response type resolved")
  - branch "Rejected outright": End event "Negotiation failed — no
      agreement reached"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response type resolved"
  User task "Evaluate amendments against approved parameters"
  Exclusive gateway "Within renewals manager authority?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authority
      confirmed")
  - branch "No — escalation needed": User task "Escalate to senior
      approval"; Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision
      received"; (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authority
      confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Authority confirmed"
  User task "Prepare revised terms and updated pricing"
  Exclusive gateway "Further negotiation rounds needed?"
  - branch "Yes — continue negotiating": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
      Until Terms Agreed" (standard loop) containing, in order: Send
      task "Send revised terms to customer", Intermediate message catch
      event "Customer counter received", User task "Assess counter and
      update terms"
  - branch "No — terms agreed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Terms finalised")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Terms finalised"
  Send task "Confirm agreed terms to Legal/Contracts for drafting"

Legal / Contracts lane:
  User task "Draft or redline contract in CLM"
  User task "Conduct internal legal review"
  Exclusive gateway "Legal review outcome?"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal
      review resolved")
  - branch "Requires amendment": User task "Amend contract clauses";
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Legal review resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Legal review resolved"
  Send task "Issue contract to customer for signature"
  Intermediate message catch event "Signed contract received"
  User task "Record executed contract in CLM"
  End event "Terms agreed and contract signed — ready for Execute Renewal"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Terms Agreed", labelled "Negotiation deadline exceeded", triggers End
  event "Negotiation failed — deadline passed".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Customer response received" — not applicable; mount instead on User
  task "Issue proposal and opening terms to customer" — labelled
  "No response within notice period", triggers End event "Negotiation
  failed — customer non-responsive".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Service Provider pool, flow moves from the
  Renewals lane through proposal review, issuance, and response
  evaluation, branching at "Response type?", merging at "Response type
  resolved", continuing through authority check and multi-round loop,
  then passing to the Legal/Contracts lane for drafting, review, and
  signature, ending at the final end event. The "Rejected outright"
  branch and both timer-boundary paths terminate at their own end events
  without rejoining the main flow.

Message flows:
  Service Provider (Send task "Issue proposal and opening terms to
    customer") → Existing Customer (proposal and opening terms).
  Existing Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer response received") (customer response, counter-terms, or
    acceptance).
  Service Provider (Send task "Issue proposal and opening terms to
    customer") → Channel Partner (copy of proposal where indirect route
    applies).
  Channel Partner → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Customer response received") (partner-relayed response or
    amendments).
  Service Provider (Send task "Confirm agreed terms to Legal/Contracts
    for drafting") — internal sequence; CLM message flow below.
  Service Provider (User task "Draft or redline contract in CLM") →
    Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) (contract draft submitted for
    storage and redline tracking).
  Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Service Provider (User task
    "Record executed contract in CLM") (stored contract record
    returned for confirmation).
  Service Provider (Send task "Issue contract to customer for
    signature") → Existing Customer (contract document for signature).
  Existing Customer → Service Provider (Intermediate message catch event
    "Signed contract received") (executed signed contract).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Renewal Proposal" — read by User task "Review proposal and
  set negotiation parameters"; read by User task "Prepare revised terms
  and updated pricing".
Data Object "Negotiation Parameters" — written by User task "Review
  proposal and set negotiation parameters"; read by User task "Evaluate
  amendments against approved parameters".
Data Object "Customer Amendments" — written by User task "Capture
  requested amendments"; read by User task "Evaluate amendments against
  approved parameters".
Data Object "Revised Terms" — written by User task "Prepare revised
  terms and updated pricing"; read by User task "Draft or redline
  contract in CLM".
Data Object "Contract Draft" — written by User task "Draft or redline
  contract in CLM"; read by User task "Conduct internal legal review";
  read by User task "Amend contract clauses".
Data Object "Signed Contract" — written by User task "Record executed
  contract in CLM"; read by the end event as the handoff artefact.

V12.06 Negotiate Terms takes the renewal proposal from the previous
subprocess and manages every exchange with the Existing Customer and
Channel Partner until agreed pricing and scope are documented and
legally reviewed. It controls escalation of discounts or clause changes
beyond standard authority, drives iterative rounds of counter-proposal
through a standard-loop subprocess, and concludes only when a fully
executed and CLM-recorded contract exists. That signed contract is the
sole input handed to V12.08 Execute Renewal.
```

```text
  - branch "Downgrade": User task "Initiate downgrade assessment"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Request type resolved"
  User task "Review account history and identify retention levers"
  User task "Develop retention offer or downgrade configuration"
  Send task "Present retention offer or revised scope to Existing Customer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Customer response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Customer accepts retention offer?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Confirm retention outcome and update CRM
    System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Retention decision recorded")
  - branch "No, proceeds with downgrade": User task "Confirm downgrade
    scope and update CRM System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Retention decision recorded")
  - branch "No, proceeds with cancellation": User task "Confirm
    cancellation and update CRM System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Retention decision recorded")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Retention decision recorded"
  Exclusive gateway "Outcome requires billing change?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Trigger subscription change in Billing
    and Subscription System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Billing change handled")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Billing change
    handled")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Billing change handled"

Renewals lane:
  User task "Review escalation flag and authorise retention offer"
  Exclusive gateway "Retention offer approved?"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Offer
    approval resolved")
  - branch "Not approved — revise": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
    Offer Approved" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
    "Revise retention offer", User task "Resubmit for authorisation"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Offer approval resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Offer approval resolved"
  User task "Record final outcome in CRM System"
  Exclusive gateway "Final outcome?"
  - branch "Retained": End event "Customer retained — ready for
    Execute Renewal"
  - branch "Downgraded": End event "Downgrade confirmed — ready for
    Update Entitlements and Billing"
  - branch "Cancelled": End event "Cancellation confirmed — process
    concludes"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Repeat Until Offer Approved"
  subprocess, labelled "Authorisation deadline exceeded", leading to
  End event "Escalation to senior management — offer cycle timed out".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  context: mounted on User task "Present retention offer or revised scope
  to Existing Customer", labelled "No customer response within 5 business
  days", leading to User task "Chase customer for response" in Customer
  Success lane, then rejoins flow at Intermediate message catch event
  "Customer response received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Customer Success lane with the message
start event, proceeds through logging, classification, and the Request
type gateway whose branches (Cancellation, Downgrade) merge at "Request
type resolved" before continuing to history review, offer development,
and customer communication; after the message catch event the Customer
accepts gateway branches (retained, downgraded, cancelled) all merge at
"Retention decision recorded" before the billing-change gateway whose
branches merge at "Billing change handled"; control passes to the Renewals
lane for offer authorisation, the approval gateway resolving through the
loop subprocess or directly at "Offer approval resolved", then outcome
recording and the Final outcome gateway whose three branches end in their
own end events.

Message flows:
Existing Customer → Service Provider, Customer Success lane (cancellation
  or downgrade request).
Service Provider, Customer Success lane → Existing Customer (retention
  offer or revised scope presentation).
Existing Customer → Service Provider, Customer Success lane (customer
  response to retention offer).
Service Provider, Customer Success lane → CRM System (request log,
  account data retrieval, retention outcome update).
Service Provider, Renewals lane → CRM System (final outcome recorded).
Service Provider, Customer Success lane → Billing & Subscription System
  (subscription change instruction).
Billing & Subscription System → Service Provider, Customer Success lane
  (subscription change confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Cancellation or Downgrade Request" — written by User task
  "Log and acknowledge request"; read by User task "Classify request type".
Data Object "Account Health and Usage Summary" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve account health score and usage data from CRM System"; read by
  User task "Review account history and identify retention levers".
Data Object "Retention Offer" — written by User task "Develop retention
  offer or downgrade configuration"; read by User task "Review escalation
  flag and authorise retention offer"; read by Send task "Present retention
  offer or revised scope to Existing Customer".
Data Object "Outcome Record" — written by User task "Confirm retention
  outcome and update CRM System" or User task "Confirm downgrade scope and
  update CRM System" or User task "Confirm cancellation and update CRM
  System"; read by User task "Record final outcome in CRM System".

This subprocess receives a customer-initiated cancellation or downgrade
request, classifies it, assesses the account, and works through a
structured retention conversation with the customer. Approved retention
offers are presented and the customer response captured; the subscription
is adjusted in the Billing and Subscription System where required, and
the final outcome — retained, downgraded, or cancelled — is recorded in
the CRM System. The subprocess hands retained customers forward to Execute
Renewal, downgraded customers to Update Entitlements and Billing, and
records confirmed cancellations as a closed outcome.
```


### V12.08 — Execute Renewal

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.08 Execute Renewal — the subprocess in which the Renewals and
Legal / Contracts teams finalise and execute the agreed renewal contract,
collect the customer's signature, and confirm the renewal ahead of entitlement
and billing updates.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Service Provider" — the organisation executing the renewal, containing
all internal lanes.
  Lane "Renewals" — renewals manager coordinates finalisation and execution.
  Lane "Legal / Contracts" — contracts administrator prepares, issues, and
    archives the executed contract.
Pool "Existing Customer" — commercial or service owner who reviews and signs.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — system used to generate, send,
track, and store the contract.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Service Provider" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Existing Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Existing Customer
2. Service Provider
3. Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Service Provider)

Renewals lane:
  Message start event "Negotiated terms received from Negotiate Terms"
  User task "Confirm agreed terms and renewal scope"
  User task "Initiate contract generation request"
  Intermediate message catch event "Executed contract returned by customer"
  User task "Verify executed contract is complete and valid"
  Exclusive gateway "Contract valid?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract Valid")
  - branch "No — corrections needed": User task "Request corrections from
    customer"
    Send task "Return contract to customer for correction"
    Intermediate message catch event "Corrected contract received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contract Valid")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Contract Valid"
  User task "Confirm renewal execution and notify stakeholders"
  End event "Renewal executed — ready for Update Entitlements and Billing"

Legal / Contracts lane:
  User task "Prepare final contract from agreed terms"
  Service task "Upload contract to CLM"
  User task "Issue contract to customer for signature"
  User task "Archive executed contract in CLM"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
Executed contract returned by customer" — label "Signature deadline elapsed"
— triggers User task "Escalate overdue signature to account manager" in the
Renewals lane, followed by End event "Renewal stalled — escalated for manual
resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Renewals lane at the message start event,
then passes to "Confirm agreed terms and renewal scope" and on to "Initiate
contract generation request". Control passes to the Legal / Contracts lane
for "Prepare final contract from agreed terms", "Upload contract to CLM", and
"Issue contract to customer for signature". Control returns to the Renewals
lane at the intermediate message catch event "Executed contract returned by
customer". After verification the exclusive gateway "Contract valid?" branches:
the "Yes" branch and the correction loop branch (which passes through
"Request corrections from customer", "Return contract to customer for
correction", and "Corrected contract received") both rejoin at the exclusive
merge gateway "Contract Valid". Flow continues to the Legal / Contracts lane
for "Archive executed contract in CLM", then returns to the Renewals lane for
"Confirm renewal execution and notify stakeholders" and the end event.

Message flows:
Service Provider (Legal / Contracts — "Issue contract to customer for
  signature") → Existing Customer (contract document for signature)
Existing Customer → Service Provider (Renewals — "Executed contract returned
  by customer") (signed contract)
Service Provider (Renewals — "Return contract to customer for correction") →
  Existing Customer (contract correction request)
Existing Customer → Service Provider (Renewals — "Corrected contract
  received") (corrected signed contract)
Service Provider (Legal / Contracts — "Upload contract to CLM") →
  Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) (draft contract upload)
Service Provider (Legal / Contracts — "Archive executed contract in CLM") →
  Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) (executed contract for archiving)
Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) → Service Provider (Legal / Contracts —
  "Prepare final contract from agreed terms") (contract template and prior
  terms data)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Agreed Terms Record" — read by "Confirm agreed terms and
renewal scope"; read by "Prepare final contract from agreed terms".
Data Object "Renewal Contract Draft" — written by "Prepare final contract
from agreed terms"; read by "Upload contract to CLM"; read by "Issue contract
to customer for signature".
Data Object "Executed Contract" — written by "Verify executed contract is
complete and valid"; read by "Archive executed contract in CLM"; read by
"Confirm renewal execution and notify stakeholders".

V12.08 Execute Renewal takes the commercially agreed terms from V12.06
Negotiate Terms and converts them into a fully executed contract: Legal /
Contracts prepares and issues the document, the customer signs, and the
Renewals team validates and confirms execution. The archived, executed
contract and the renewal confirmation are then handed to V12.09 Update
Entitlements & Billing so that system access and charges reflect the new
agreement immediately.
```


### V12.09 — Update Entitlements & Billing

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V12.09 Update Entitlements & Billing — executes after renewal

Pool "Service Provider" — top (process owner, single white-box pool).
Pool "Payment Provider" — middle (external party that settles payment).
Pool "Billing & Subscription System" — bottom (IT system supporting

Finance / Billing lane:

  Exclusive merge gateway "Entitlement change type"

  User task "Validate revised billing schedule and amounts"

  - branch "No — amendments required":

  - branch "Yes — approved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Schedule approved")

  Intermediate message catch event "Payment authorisation response

  Exclusive gateway "Payment authorised?"

  - branch "Failed or declined":

      Intermediate message catch event "Customer payment response

      Service task "Resubmit payment request to Payment Provider"

  Exclusive merge gateway "Payment authorised"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until

6. Connectors

V12.09 Update Entitlements & Billing translates the executed renewal
```

## V13 — Return to Refund

**Teams and roles involved.**
Return to Refund usually involves Customer Service, Returns/Reverse Logistics, Warehouse, Quality, Repairs or Refurbishment, Finance/Accounts Receivable, and sometimes Supplier Management where the fault lies upstream. Key roles include customer service agent, returns coordinator, warehouse receiver, quality inspector, repair technician, disposition analyst, credit controller, and finance officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Customer returning goods. The process is initiated when the customer requests a return, reports a fault, exercises a right of withdrawal, or a recall is issued. Other external parties include freight carriers, third-party returns processors, suppliers and manufacturers, recyclers and disposal partners, and payment providers.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive return request, validate eligibility against policy, authorise the return and issue an RMA, arrange collection or return shipping, receive and inspect the goods, decide disposition (restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, return to supplier), process the refund or replacement, update inventory and financial records, recover cost from the supplier where applicable, and analyse return reasons.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include customer service/ticketing, order management, returns management, warehouse management, quality management, repair or field-service management, inventory and ERP, transport management, billing and accounts receivable, payment gateway, and reporting/analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include returns and refunds policy, statutory withdrawal and consumer-guarantee rights, warranty terms, restocking and shipping-cost rules, inspection and disposition criteria, hazardous or regulated goods handling, recall procedure, supplier recovery and warranty-claim terms, and refund authorisation limits.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The customer provides the return request and reason, order and product identifiers, condition and fault description, evidence such as photographs, and return shipment details. The process provides the customer with eligibility decisions, return authorisation and labels, collection arrangements, receipt and inspection outcomes, refund or replacement confirmation, and credit notes.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates return authorisations, inbound shipments, inspection results, disposition decisions, inventory adjustments, credit notes, refunds, and supplier claims. IT systems provide original order and payment details, product and warranty data, stock locations, carrier tracking, refund status, and return-reason analytics.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Retail Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V13.01** Receive Return Request | Customer | Customer Service (customer service agent) | Customer Service / Ticketing System |
| **V13.02** Validate Eligibility | Customer | Customer Service (customer service agent), Returns (returns coordinator) | Order Management System (OMS), Returns Management System |
| **V13.03** Authorise Return & Issue RMA | Customer | Returns (returns coordinator) | Returns Management System |
| **V13.04** Arrange Collection | Customer, Freight Carrier | Returns (returns coordinator), Logistics (logistics coordinator) | Transport Management System (TMS) |
| **V13.05** Receive & Inspect Goods | Freight Carrier | Warehouse (warehouse receiver), Quality (quality inspector) | Warehouse Management System (WMS), Quality Management System |
| **V13.06** Decide Disposition | — | Quality (disposition analyst), Repairs (repair technician) | Returns Management System, Inventory / ERP System |
| **V13.07** Process Refund or Replacement | Customer, Payment Provider | Finance (finance officer), Customer Service (customer service agent) | Billing / ERP System, Payment Gateway |
| **V13.08** Update Inventory & Financials | — | Warehouse (inventory controller), Finance (finance officer) | Inventory / ERP System |
| **V13.09** Recover Cost from Supplier | Supplier | Supplier Management (supplier manager), Finance (credit controller) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V13.10** Analyse Return Reasons | — | Quality (quality manager), Customer Service (service manager) | Business Intelligence Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V13):

- **External actors:** Customer (V13.01–V13.04, V13.07); Freight Carrier (V13.04, V13.05); Payment Provider (V13.07); Supplier (V13.09).
- **Teams:** Customer Service (V13.01, V13.02, V13.07, V13.10); Returns (V13.02–V13.04); Logistics (V13.04); Warehouse (V13.05, V13.08); Quality (V13.05, V13.06, V13.10); Repairs (V13.06); Finance (V13.07–V13.09); Supplier Management (V13.09).
- **IT systems:** Customer Service / Ticketing System (V13.01); Order Management System / OMS (V13.02); Returns Management System (V13.02, V13.03, V13.06); Transport Management System / TMS (V13.04); Warehouse Management System / WMS (V13.05); Quality Management System (V13.05); Inventory / ERP System (V13.06, V13.08); Billing / ERP System (V13.07); Payment Gateway (V13.07); Procurement / ERP System (V13.09); Business Intelligence Platform (V13.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V13 — Return to Refund — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Return to Refund value chain, from the moment a customer raises a
return request through to supplier cost recovery and return-reason analysis.
The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS
SERVICES (top), BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle), and APPLICATIONS (bottom).
The demand-side actor (Customer) sits on the far left; delivery and
settlement actors (Freight Carrier, Payment Provider, Supplier) sit on the
far right. The diagram is read top-to-bottom as service realisation:
business services are realised by business processes, which are supported
by application components below them.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Customer — far left; initiates the return and receives refund or
  replacement outcomes across V13.01 through V13.04 and V13.07.
- Freight Carrier — far right; participates in collection and inbound
  goods receipt in V13.04 and V13.05.
- Payment Provider — far right; processes refund disbursements in V13.07.
- Supplier — far right; receives cost-recovery claims and warranty
  submissions in V13.09.

2. Interfaces

- Customer Service Interface — accessed by Customer; serves the Return
  Request Handling service and the Refund or Replacement Confirmation
  service.
- Carrier Booking Interface — accessed by Freight Carrier; serves the
  Collection Arrangement service.
- Payment Gateway Interface — accessed by Payment Provider; serves the
  Refund Processing service.
- Supplier Claim Interface — accessed by Supplier; serves the Supplier
  Cost Recovery service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Return Request Handling — receives and acknowledges the customer's
  return request, reason, and supporting evidence.
- Eligibility Validation — assesses the request against returns policy,
  warranty terms, and statutory rights.
- Return Authorisation & RMA Issuance — grants authorisation and issues
  an RMA number and return label to the customer.
- Collection Arrangement — coordinates return shipping or carrier
  collection with the customer and freight carrier.
- Goods Receipt & Inspection — accepts inbound returned goods and
  records inspection and quality findings.
- Disposition Decision — determines the appropriate outcome for each
  returned item: restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, or return to
  supplier.
- Refund or Replacement Processing — executes the customer credit, refund
  payment, or replacement order.
- Inventory & Financial Update — adjusts stock records and posts
  financial entries for the completed return.
- Supplier Cost Recovery — raises and tracks warranty claims or cost
  recovery requests against the responsible supplier.
- Return Reason Analysis — aggregates and analyses return data to
  identify trends and drive improvement.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, chain order

- V13.01 Receive Return Request — captures the return request, reason,
  order identifiers, fault description, and any photographic evidence
  from the customer.
- V13.02 Validate Eligibility — checks the request against returns
  policy, withdrawal rights, and warranty terms using order and product
  data.
- V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA — approves the return, generates
  the RMA, and communicates authorisation and labels to the customer.
- V13.04 Arrange Collection — books freight carrier collection or
  generates a return-postage label and confirms arrangements with the
  customer.
- V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods — receives the inbound shipment,
  inspects condition, records quality findings, and confirms receipt.
- V13.06 Decide Disposition — evaluates inspection results and assigns
  each item a disposition: restock, repair, refurbish, scrap, or return
  to supplier.
- V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement — issues a credit note or refund
  via the payment provider, or initiates a replacement order.
- V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials — posts inventory adjustments,
  updates stock locations, and records financial entries in the ERP.
- V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier — raises warranty or fault claims,
  manages supplier correspondence, and tracks recovery amounts.
- V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons — extracts and analyses return-reason
  data to produce insights, trend reports, and improvement
  recommendations.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Customer Service / Ticketing System — supports return request intake
  and customer communication in V13.01, V13.02, V13.07, and V13.10.
- Order Management System (OMS) — provides original order and payment
  reference data used in V13.02.
- Returns Management System — manages return authorisations, RMA
  records, and disposition decisions in V13.02, V13.03, and V13.06.
- Transport Management System (TMS) — books carriers and tracks
  collection and inbound shipments in V13.04.
- Warehouse Management System (WMS) — records goods receipt, stock
  movements, and location updates in V13.05 and V13.08.
- Quality Management System — captures inspection results and quality
  findings in V13.05.
- Inventory / ERP System — maintains stock levels and supports
  disposition and inventory adjustment in V13.06 and V13.08.
- Billing / ERP System — generates credit notes and manages accounts
  receivable entries in V13.07.
- Payment Gateway — processes refund disbursements to the customer in
  V13.07.
- Procurement / ERP System — manages supplier claims and cost-recovery
  records in V13.09.
- Business Intelligence Platform — aggregates return-reason data and
  produces analytics and trend reports in V13.10.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.01 Receive Return
  Request.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or
  Replacement.
- Customer Service / Ticketing System SERVES V13.10 Analyse Return
  Reasons.
- Order Management System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.02 Validate Eligibility.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA.
- Returns Management System SERVES V13.06 Decide Disposition.
- Transport Management System SERVES V13.04 Arrange Collection.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory &
  Financials.
- Quality Management System SERVES V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V13.06 Decide Disposition.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials.
- Billing / ERP System SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement.
- Billing / ERP System SERVES V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials.
- Payment Gateway SERVES V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier.
- Business Intelligence Platform SERVES V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons.

SERVING (business service SERVES business actor):
- Return Request Handling SERVES Customer.
- Eligibility Validation SERVES Customer.
- Return Authorisation & RMA Issuance SERVES Customer.
- Collection Arrangement SERVES Customer.
- Collection Arrangement SERVES Freight Carrier.
- Goods Receipt & Inspection SERVES Freight Carrier.
- Refund or Replacement Processing SERVES Customer.
- Refund or Replacement Processing SERVES Payment Provider.
- Supplier Cost Recovery SERVES Supplier.

REALISATION (business process REALISES business service):
- V13.01 Receive Return Request REALISES Return Request Handling.
- V13.02 Validate Eligibility REALISES Eligibility Validation.
- V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA REALISES Return Authorisation &
  RMA Issuance.
- V13.04 Arrange Collection REALISES Collection Arrangement.
- V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods REALISES Goods Receipt & Inspection.
- V13.06 Decide Disposition REALISES Disposition Decision.
- V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement REALISES Refund or Replacement
  Processing.
- V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials REALISES Inventory & Financial
  Update.
- V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier REALISES Supplier Cost Recovery.
- V13.10 Analyse Return Reasons REALISES Return Reason Analysis.

ACCESS (business actor ACCESSES interface):
- Customer ACCESSES Customer Service Interface.
- Freight Carrier ACCESSES Carrier Booking Interface.
- Payment Provider ACCESSES Payment Gateway Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Supplier Claim Interface.

SERVING (interface SERVES business service):
- Customer Service Interface SERVES Return Request Handling.
- Customer Service Interface SERVES Refund or Replacement Processing.
- Carrier Booking Interface SERVES Collection Arrangement.
- Payment Gateway Interface SERVES Refund or Replacement Processing.
- Supplier Claim Interface SERVES Supplier Cost Recovery.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V13 - Return to Refund

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each represented as a chevron, in the order listed below. Each chevron
carries only the stage code and name. No swimlanes, no system icons, no
data flows — this is an overview diagram only.

V13.01. Receive Return Request
V13.02. Validate Eligibility
V13.03. Authorise Return & Issue RMA
V13.04. Arrange Collection
V13.05. Receive & Inspect Goods
V13.06. Decide Disposition
V13.07. Process Refund or Replacement
V13.08. Update Inventory & Financials
V13.09. Recover Cost from Supplier
V13.10. Analyse Return Reasons

This chain governs the end-to-end handling of a customer return, from the
moment the Customer submits a return request through eligibility checking,
physical collection, goods inspection, and disposition, to the settlement
of a refund or replacement, the correction of inventory and financial
records, the recovery of costs from a Supplier where fault lies upstream,
and the analysis of return reasons to drive continuous improvement. The
chain is triggered by the Customer requesting a return, reporting a fault,
exercising a statutory right of withdrawal, or by the issue of a product
recall.
```

### V13.01 — Receive Return Request

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.01 Receive Return Request — first subprocess in the Return to
Refund value chain, capturing the customer's return request and logging it
as a case before eligibility is checked.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company receiving and processing the
return request, with Customer Service as the acting lane.
- Lane "Customer Service" (customer service agent)

Pool "Customer" — the external party initiating the return.
Pool "Customer Service / Ticketing System" — the IT system that records
the return request as a support ticket or case.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer Service / Ticketing System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Customer Service / Ticketing System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Return request received from Customer"
  User task "Acknowledge return request"
  User task "Collect return details from customer"
  Exclusive gateway "All required details provided?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "All required details provided?")
  - branch "No":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: Send task "Request missing details from
    customer", Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides
    missing details", User task "Update return details"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All required details
    provided?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All required details provided?"
  Service task "Log return request in Customer Service / Ticketing System"
  User task "Assign case reference to return request"
  End event "Return request logged — ready for Validate Eligibility"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Details Complete", labelled "72-hour detail deadline exceeded", leading
to: End event "Return request closed — insufficient details provided"

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom within the Customer Service lane.
After "All required details provided?" the No branch enters the standard-
loop subprocess; on exit the loop continues to the exclusive merge
gateway. The Yes branch also continues to the exclusive merge gateway.
Both branches resolve there before the flow proceeds to logging and case
assignment. The timer boundary event on the loop subprocess diverts to a
separate terminating end event.

Message flows:
Customer → "Return request received from Customer" start event (return
  request, reason, order reference, product identifier, fault description,
  and any photographic evidence)
"Collect return details from customer" → Customer (request for order
  number, product details, fault description, and supporting evidence)
Send task "Request missing details from customer" → Customer (missing-
  detail request specifying what is still needed)
Customer → Intermediate message catch event "Customer provides missing
  details" (supplementary details and evidence)
Service task "Log return request in Customer Service / Ticketing System"
  → Customer Service / Ticketing System (full return request record)
Customer Service / Ticketing System → "Assign case reference to return
  request" (generated case or ticket reference number)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return Request" — written by "Collect return details from
customer"; updated by "Update return details"; read by "Log return
request in Customer Service / Ticketing System".
Data Object "Case Record" — written by "Log return request in Customer
Service / Ticketing System"; read by "Assign case reference to return
request".

This subprocess captures the customer's intent to return goods, gathers
all identifiers and supporting evidence, and persists the request as a
numbered case in the ticketing system. It hands a complete, reference-
stamped return request to Validate Eligibility, where the case will be
checked against returns policy, warranty terms, and the original order.
```


### V13.02 — Validate Eligibility

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.02 Validate Eligibility — second subprocess in the Return to
Refund value chain, following receipt of the return request and preceding
authorisation of the return and issuance of the RMA.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company processing the return eligibility
  check, with lanes for Customer Service and Returns.
Pool "Customer" — the external customer who submitted the return request.
Pool "Order Management System (OMS)" — IT system providing original order
  and product data.
Pool "Returns Management System" — IT system recording eligibility
  decisions and return policy data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Order Management System (OMS)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Returns Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Order Management System (OMS)
4. Returns Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Return request received from Receive Return Request"
  User task "Review return request and log details"
  Service task "Retrieve original order and product data from OMS"
  Exclusive gateway "Order and product data found?"
  - branch "No — order not found": Send task "Notify customer of
    unresolvable request"
    End event "Request closed — order data not found"
  - branch "Yes — data retrieved":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Order and product data found")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Order and product data found"
  User task "Check return reason against returns and refunds policy"
  User task "Verify warranty terms and statutory withdrawal rights"
  Exclusive gateway "Within return window and policy met?"
  - branch "No — outside window or policy breach":
    User task "Prepare ineligibility decision and reason"
    Send task "Communicate ineligibility to customer"
    End event "Return ineligible — customer notified"
  - branch "Yes — provisionally eligible":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Within return window and
    policy met")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Within return window and policy met"
  User task "Request supporting evidence from customer if required"
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence or confirmation received
    from customer"
  User task "Assess evidence and confirm eligibility decision"
  Exclusive gateway "Eligibility confirmed?"
  - branch "No — evidence insufficient or request rejected":
    User task "Record rejection decision"
    Send task "Notify customer of rejection"
    End event "Return rejected — customer notified"
  - branch "Yes — eligible":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility confirmed"
  Service task "Record validated eligibility decision in Returns
    Management System"

Returns lane:
  User task "Review eligibility decision and countersign if required"
  End event "Eligibility validated — ready for Authorise Return and
    Issue RMA"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request supporting evidence from
  customer if required" — label "Evidence deadline exceeded" — triggers
  a Send task "Notify customer of evidence deadline and close request"
  followed by End event "Request closed — evidence not received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Customer Service lane with the
message start event, progresses through order data retrieval, the
"Order and product data found?" gateway (No branch ends; Yes branch
merges), then policy and warranty checks, the "Within return window and
policy met?" gateway (No branch ends; Yes branch merges), then evidence
request, the intermediate message catch event awaiting customer
response, evidence assessment, the "Eligibility confirmed?" gateway
(No branch ends; Yes branch merges), recording in the Returns Management
System, and then passes to the Returns lane for countersign before
reaching the end event.

Message flows:
Customer → Retail Organisation, Customer Service lane (return request
  details and supporting evidence).
Retail Organisation, Customer Service lane → Customer (requests for
  evidence, ineligibility notifications, rejection notifications).
Retail Organisation, Customer Service lane → Order Management System
  (OMS) (query for original order and product data).
Order Management System (OMS) → Retail Organisation, Customer Service
  lane (order details, product identifiers, purchase date).
Retail Organisation, Customer Service lane → Returns Management System
  (validated eligibility decision and reason).
Returns Management System → Retail Organisation, Customer Service lane
  (returns policy rules and warranty data).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return Request" — read by "Review return request and log
  details" / written by "Review return request and log details".
Data Object "Order and Product Record" — read by "Check return reason
  against returns and refunds policy" / written by "Retrieve original
  order and product data from OMS".
Data Object "Eligibility Decision" — written by "Assess evidence and
  confirm eligibility decision" / read by "Record validated eligibility
  decision in Returns Management System" and "Review eligibility
  decision and countersign if required".
Data Object "Supporting Evidence" — written by the intermediate message
  catch event "Evidence or confirmation received from customer" / read
  by "Assess evidence and confirm eligibility decision".

This subprocess takes a logged return request, verifies it against
policy rules, warranty terms, and statutory rights using order data
from the OMS, collects any required evidence from the customer, and
produces a confirmed eligibility decision recorded in the Returns
Management System. An eligible, countersigned decision is handed to
Authorise Return and Issue RMA to proceed with the formal return
authorisation.
```


### V13.03 — Authorise Return & Issue RMA

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.03 Authorise Return & Issue RMA — third subprocess in the
Return to Refund value chain, triggered by a validated eligible return and
concluding when the customer holds an RMA and is ready for collection
arrangements.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the organisation processing the return
authorisation and issuing the RMA, with lanes for Returns.
Pool "Customer" — the customer who submitted the return request.
Pool "Returns Management System" — IT system that records and issues RMAs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer": black-box, single instance.
Pool "Returns Management System": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Returns Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Returns lane:
  Message start event "Eligible return received from Validate Eligibility"
  User task "Review validated return details"
  Exclusive gateway "Within returns coordinator authorisation limit?"
  - branch "Yes — within limit":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation resolved")
  - branch "No — exceeds limit":
      User task "Escalate to senior approver for authorisation"
      Intermediate message catch event "Senior approver decision received"
      Exclusive gateway "Authorisation granted?"
      - branch "Approved":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation resolved")
      - branch "Rejected":
          Send task "Notify customer of declined return"
          End event "Return declined — customer notified, process closed"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation resolved"
  Service task "Create RMA record in Returns Management System"
  User task "Generate RMA number and return shipping label"
  Send task "Issue RMA and return label to customer"
  End event "RMA issued — ready for Arrange Collection"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Escalate to senior approver for
authorisation" — label "Escalation unanswered after 48 hours" — triggers
Send task "Notify customer of processing delay" then flow rejoins at
Intermediate message catch event "Senior approver decision received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Returns lane at the message start event,
moves through the authorisation-limit gateway; the within-limit branch and
the approved branch of the nested authorisation gateway both converge at the
exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation resolved", then flow continues through
RMA creation, label generation, and dispatch to the customer before reaching
the end event; the rejected branch exits at its own end event without
rejoining.

Message flows:
Returns Management System → Returns lane, Service task "Create RMA record in
Returns Management System" (RMA record created and stored).
Returns Management System → Returns lane, User task "Generate RMA number and
return shipping label" (RMA number and label data retrieved).
Returns lane, Send task "Issue RMA and return label to customer" →
Customer (RMA authorisation letter and return shipping label).
Returns lane, Send task "Notify customer of declined return" →
Customer (decline notification).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Return Request" — read by "Review validated return
details".
Data Object "RMA Record" — written by "Create RMA record in Returns
Management System"; read by "Generate RMA number and return shipping label".
Data Object "Return Shipping Label" — written by "Generate RMA number and
return shipping label"; read by "Issue RMA and return label to customer".

This subprocess takes the validated, policy-compliant return from Validate
Eligibility, applies the organisation's authorisation rules, creates a formal
RMA record in the Returns Management System, and delivers the RMA number and
prepaid return label to the customer. Its output — a confirmed RMA with
shipping instructions — is the trigger that initiates Arrange Collection,
where the physical pickup or drop-off of the goods is coordinated.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.04 Arrange Collection — fourth subprocess in the Return to
Refund value chain, responsible for arranging the physical collection or
return shipment of goods from the customer following authorisation.

1. Pools & Lanes

collection, with lanes for Returns and Logistics.
Pool "Customer" — the customer from whom goods are being collected.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — the external carrier collecting or accepting
the return shipment.

track collection and return shipments.

Pool "Transport Management System (TMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Freight Carrier
4. Transport Management System (TMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Returns lane:
Message start event "Return authorised and RMA issued from Authorise
Return and Issue RMA"
User task "Confirm return method with customer"
Exclusive gateway "Return method?"
- branch "carrier collection": User task "Raise collection request"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Return method resolved")
- branch "customer drop-off": User task "Provide drop-off instructions
  to customer"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Return method resolved")
- branch "prepaid label": User task "Generate prepaid return label"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Return method resolved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Return method resolved"
User task "Record return shipment details in TMS"
Send task "Send collection confirmation and instructions to customer"
Intermediate message catch event "Carrier collection confirmed"

Logistics lane:
User task "Coordinate collection schedule with freight carrier"
User task "Verify carrier booking reference"
Exclusive gateway "Collection booking confirmed?"
- branch "yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Booking
  check resolved")
- branch "no": User task "Escalate booking failure and rebook"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Booking check resolved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Booking check resolved"
Intermediate timer catch event "Collection window elapsed"
User task "Confirm goods collected with carrier"
Exclusive gateway "Goods collected successfully?"
- branch "yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Collection
  outcome resolved")
- branch "no": User task "Rearrange collection with carrier"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Collection outcome resolved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Collection outcome resolved"
User task "Update collection status in TMS"
End event "Collection completed — ready for Receive and Inspect Goods"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Coordinate collection
schedule with freight carrier" — label "Scheduling deadline exceeded"
— triggers User task "Escalate booking failure and rebook" in the
Logistics lane, then continues to exclusive merge gateway "Booking
check resolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Returns lane with the message start
event, moves through return method confirmation and the three-branch
exclusive gateway, merges at "Return method resolved", then continues
to TMS recording and customer notification before passing to the
Logistics lane for carrier coordination, booking verification with its
yes/no gateway merging at "Booking check resolved", the timer catch
event representing the collection window, collection confirmation
with its yes/no gateway merging at "Collection outcome resolved",
TMS status update, and the end event.

Message flows:
Retail Organisation (Send task "Send collection confirmation and
instructions to customer") → Customer (collection instructions and
prepaid label or drop-off details).
Customer → Retail Organisation (Returns lane, User task "Confirm
return method with customer") (customer preference and availability).
Retail Organisation (Logistics lane, User task "Coordinate collection
schedule with freight carrier") → Freight Carrier (collection
request and scheduling details).
Freight Carrier → Retail Organisation (Logistics lane, Intermediate
message catch event "Carrier collection confirmed") (booking
confirmation and reference).
Retail Organisation (Logistics lane, User task "Confirm goods
collected with carrier") → Freight Carrier (collection verification
request).
Freight Carrier → Retail Organisation (Logistics lane, Exclusive

Retail Organisation (Returns lane, User task "Record return shipment
details in TMS") → Transport Management System (TMS) (inbound

Transport Management System (TMS) → Retail Organisation (Logistics
lane, User task "Update collection status in TMS") (carrier tracking

7. Data objects

Data Object "Collection Request" — written by User task "Raise

with freight carrier".
Data Object "Prepaid Return Label" — written by User task "Generate
prepaid return label"; read by Send task "Send collection confirmation
and instructions to customer".
Data Object "Return Shipment Record" — written by User task "Record
return shipment details in TMS"; read by User task "Update collection
status in TMS".
Data Object "Carrier Booking Reference" — written by User task "Verify
carrier booking reference"; read by User task "Confirm goods collected
with carrier".

This subprocess takes the authorised return and RMA from V13.03 and
arranges the physical movement of goods back to the warehouse, handling
carrier booking, scheduling, label or drop-off provision, and
confirmation of successful collection. It hands a completed, tracked
inbound shipment record to V13.05 Receive and Inspect Goods so the
warehouse knows to expect the goods and can initiate inspection on
```
