### V13.05 — Receive & Inspect Goods

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.05 Receive & Inspect Goods — the fifth subprocess in the
Return to Refund value chain, covering physical receipt of returned goods
from the freight carrier and quality inspection before disposition is
decided.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the organisation running the returns process,
containing the Warehouse and Quality lanes.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — external party delivering the returned goods.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — IT system recording inbound
shipment and stock movements.
Pool "Quality Management System" — IT system recording inspection results
and findings.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Freight Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Quality Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Freight Carrier
2. Retail Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)
4. Quality Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Warehouse lane:
Message start event "Returned goods arrived from freight carrier"
User task "Check delivery against RMA and collection booking"
Exclusive gateway "Delivery matches RMA?"
- branch "No — discrepancy found": User task "Record discrepancy and
  contact Returns coordinator"
  End event "Discrepancy escalated — returns coordinator to resolve"
- branch "Yes — matches RMA": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Delivery matches RMA")
Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery matches RMA"
Service task "Log inbound shipment in WMS"
User task "Unpack and count items against return manifest"
Exclusive gateway "Item count correct?"
- branch "No — quantity mismatch": User task "Record quantity discrepancy
  in WMS"
  End event "Quantity discrepancy escalated — returns coordinator
  to resolve"
- branch "Yes — count correct": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Item count correct")
Exclusive merge gateway "Item count correct"
User task "Label items with inspection reference and move to
inspection area"
Intermediate message catch event "Quality inspector confirms receipt
of items"

Quality lane:
User task "Review return reason, fault description, and product
documentation"
Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Items Inspected" (standard loop)
containing, in order: User task "Physically inspect item condition and
functionality", User task "Record inspection findings in Quality
Management System", Exclusive gateway "Further testing required?",
- branch "Yes": User task "Conduct additional technical or safety
  testing"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Further testing required")
- branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Further testing
  required")
Exclusive merge gateway "Further testing required"
User task "Assign preliminary condition grade to item"
Exclusive gateway "All items inspected?"
- branch "No": (loop repeats)
- branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
User task "Compile consolidated inspection report"
Exclusive gateway "Inspection report complete and consistent?"
- branch "No — gaps or conflicts": User task "Clarify findings with
  warehouse receiver and amend report"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection report complete
  and consistent")
- branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection report
  complete and consistent")
Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection report complete and consistent"
End event "Inspection report ready — ready for Decide Disposition"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Items Inspected", labelled "Inspection window exceeded (48 hours)",
leading to User task "Escalate overdue inspection to quality manager".
Interrupting error boundary event on Service task "Log inbound shipment
in WMS", labelled "WMS system error", leading to User task "Log
shipment manually and notify IT support".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Warehouse lane at the message start
event and passes through delivery checking, WMS logging, unpacking, and
labelling before crossing to the Quality lane via the intermediate
message catch event. In the Quality lane, flow continues through
document review, the standard-loop inspection subprocess, report
compilation, and the consistency gateway before reaching the end event.
The discrepancy and quantity-mismatch branches each terminate at their
own end events without rejoining. The timer boundary escalation task
completes and the flow ends there without rejoining the main path. The
error boundary task on WMS logging completes and ends there separately.

Message flows:
Freight Carrier → Retail Organisation / Warehouse lane (physical
delivery of returned goods and carrier handover documentation).
Retail Organisation / Warehouse lane → Warehouse Management System (WMS)
(inbound shipment record and item count data).
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Retail Organisation / Warehouse lane
(confirmation of logged inbound shipment and any WMS discrepancy
alerts).
Retail Organisation / Quality lane → Quality Management System
(inspection findings, condition grades, and test results per item).
Quality Management System → Retail Organisation / Quality lane
(stored inspection data confirmed and consolidated inspection report
reference).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return Manifest" — read by User task "Unpack and count
items against return manifest"; read by User task "Review return reason,
fault description, and product documentation".
Data Object "Inbound Shipment Record" — written by Service task "Log
inbound shipment in WMS"; read by User task "Label items with inspection
reference and move to inspection area".
Data Object "Inspection Findings" — written by User task "Record
inspection findings in Quality Management System"; read by User task
"Compile consolidated inspection report".
Data Object "Consolidated Inspection Report" — written by User task
"Compile consolidated inspection report"; read by Exclusive gateway
"Inspection report complete and consistent?".

This subprocess takes physical custody of the returned goods from the
freight carrier, verifies the delivery against the RMA and collection
booking, logs the inbound shipment in the WMS, and subjects every item
to a structured quality inspection with condition grading. It hands the
completed consolidated inspection report to the Decide Disposition
subprocess, giving the disposition analyst the evidence needed to route
each item to restock, repair, refurbishment, supplier return, or
disposal.
```


### V13.06 — Decide Disposition

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.06 Decide Disposition — sixth subprocess in the Return to Refund
value chain, sitting between Receive & Inspect Goods and Process Refund or
Replacement.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the organisation running the disposition
  decision process, with lanes for Quality and Repairs.
Pool "Returns Management System" — IT system holding the return
  authorisation and inspection results.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — IT system used to confirm stock positions
  and record disposition decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Returns Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Retail Organisation (white-box)
2. Returns Management System (black-box)
3. Inventory / ERP System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Quality lane:
  Message start event "Inspection outcome received from Receive &
    Inspect Goods"
  User task "Review inspection results and fault classification"
  Exclusive gateway "Disposition category?"
  - branch "Restock":
      Service task "Record restock decision in Returns Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved")
  - branch "Repair":
      Send task "Assign item to Repairs for assessment"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved")
  - branch "Refurbish":
      Send task "Assign item to Repairs for refurbishment"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved")
  - branch "Return to supplier":
      User task "Raise supplier return in Returns Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved")
  - branch "Scrap / recycle":
      User task "Record scrap or recycle disposition"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Disposition category resolved"
  Service task "Retrieve current stock position from Inventory / ERP
    System"
  User task "Confirm disposition decision and authorise"
  Exclusive gateway "Authorisation within analyst limit?"
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation complete")
  - branch "No — escalation required":
      User task "Escalate disposition for senior approval"
      Intermediate message catch event "Senior approval received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation complete"
  Service task "Write disposition decision to Returns Management System"
  Service task "Write inventory adjustment to Inventory / ERP System"
  End event "Disposition decision recorded — ready for Process Refund
    or Replacement"

Repairs lane:
  User task "Assess repairability or refurbishability"
  User task "Confirm repair or refurbishment feasibility and estimated
    cost"
  Send task "Return feasibility outcome to Quality"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Escalate disposition for senior
  approval" — label "Escalation deadline exceeded (48 hours)" — on
  expiry flow continues to User task "Override and apply default
  disposition ruling" in the Quality lane, which then continues to
  exclusive merge gateway "Authorisation complete".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Quality lane with the start event,
  proceeds through review and the five-branch disposition gateway,
  merging at "Disposition category resolved"; the Repair and Refurbish
  branches each trigger a send task that initiates the Repairs lane
  flow, with the feasibility outcome returned via a send task back to
  the Quality lane before the merge gateway is reached on those
  branches; after the merge the flow passes through stock retrieval,
  confirmation, the two-branch authorisation gateway merging at
  "Authorisation complete", and then the two write service tasks before
  the end event.

Message flows:
  Returns Management System → Quality lane "Review inspection results
    and fault classification" (inspection results and fault
    classification data)
  Quality lane "Record restock decision in Returns Management System"
    → Returns Management System (restock disposition record)
  Quality lane "Raise supplier return in Returns Management System"
    → Returns Management System (supplier return instruction)
  Quality lane "Write disposition decision to Returns Management System"
    → Returns Management System (authorised disposition decision)
  Inventory / ERP System → Quality lane "Retrieve current stock
    position from Inventory / ERP System" (current stock position and
    location data)
  Quality lane "Write inventory adjustment to Inventory / ERP System"
    → Inventory / ERP System (inventory adjustment instruction)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inspection Report" — read by "Review inspection results
  and fault classification".
Data Object "Disposition Decision Record" — written by "Confirm
  disposition decision and authorise"; read by "Write disposition
  decision to Returns Management System" and "Write inventory
  adjustment to Inventory / ERP System".
Data Object "Repair Feasibility Report" — written by "Confirm repair
  or refurbishment feasibility and estimated cost"; read by Quality
  lane after "Disposition category resolved" merge.

This subprocess takes the completed inspection outcome and translates it
into an authorised disposition decision — restock, repair, refurbish,
return to supplier, or scrap — confirmed against current stock positions
and approved within delegated limits. It hands a recorded, authorised
disposition decision and the corresponding inventory adjustment
instruction to Process Refund or Replacement, which uses the outcome to
determine whether the customer receives a refund, a credit note, or a
replacement item.
```


### V13.07 — Process Refund or Replacement

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.07 Process Refund or Replacement — the subprocess that issues a
refund or dispatches a replacement to the customer following disposition
decisions made in Decide Disposition, and hands confirmed outcomes to Update
Inventory & Financials.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the organisation executing the refund or
replacement process, with lanes for Finance and Customer Service.
Pool "Customer" — the customer receiving the refund or replacement.
Pool "Payment Provider" — the external payment provider that executes
the financial transaction.
Pool "Billing / ERP System" — the internal system used to raise credit
notes and record financial transactions.
Pool "Payment Gateway" — the IT system through which refund payments
are transmitted.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Customer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Payment Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Payment Gateway" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Customer
2. Retail Organisation
3. Payment Provider
4. Billing / ERP System
5. Payment Gateway

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Finance lane:
Message start event "Disposition decision received from Decide
  Disposition"
User task "Review disposition outcome and select resolution type"
Exclusive gateway "Resolution type?"
- branch "Refund": User task "Calculate refund amount and apply
  deductions"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type resolved")
- branch "Replacement": User task "Raise replacement order"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type resolved")
Exclusive merge gateway "Resolution type resolved"
Service task "Raise credit note or replacement record in Billing /
  ERP System"
Exclusive gateway "Refund or replacement?"
- branch "Refund": Service task "Submit refund instruction to Payment
  Gateway"
  Intermediate message catch event "Refund confirmation received"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transaction outcome received")
- branch "Replacement": Intermediate message catch event "Replacement
  dispatch confirmation received"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transaction outcome received")
Exclusive merge gateway "Transaction outcome received"
User task "Verify transaction outcome and record in Billing / ERP System"

Customer Service lane:
User task "Notify customer of refund or replacement decision"
Intermediate message catch event "Customer acknowledgement received"
User task "Confirm case closure with customer"
End event "Refund or replacement confirmed — ready for Update Inventory
  & Financials"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Raise replacement order" —
label "Replacement order timeout (24 h)" — triggers End event
"Replacement order failed — escalate to Finance".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit refund instruction to
Payment Gateway" — label "Refund submission timeout (48 h)" — triggers
End event "Refund submission failed — escalate to Finance".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Finance lane on receipt of the
disposition decision. After reviewing the outcome, an exclusive gateway
routes to either the refund calculation path or the replacement order
path; both branches rejoin at the "Resolution type resolved" merge
gateway. The Finance lane then raises the credit note or replacement
record, and a second exclusive gateway routes refund cases through the
Payment Gateway submission and its confirmation catch event, while
replacement cases wait on a dispatch confirmation catch event; both
rejoin at "Transaction outcome received". Finance verifies and records
the outcome, then flow passes to the Customer Service lane, which
notifies the customer, waits for acknowledgement, confirms closure,
and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
Billing / ERP System → Finance lane "Raise credit note or replacement
  record in Billing / ERP System" (credit note or replacement record
  confirmation).
Finance lane "Submit refund instruction to Payment Gateway" →
  Payment Gateway (refund instruction).
Payment Gateway → Finance lane "Refund confirmation received"
  (refund transaction confirmation).
Payment Provider → Finance lane "Refund confirmation received"
  (settlement confirmation from payment provider).
Finance lane "Raise replacement order" → Billing / ERP System
  (replacement order details).
Billing / ERP System → Finance lane "Replacement dispatch confirmation
  received" (dispatch confirmation).
Customer Service lane "Notify customer of refund or replacement
  decision" → Customer (refund or replacement notification and
  credit note or dispatch details).
Customer → Customer Service lane "Customer acknowledgement received"
  (customer acknowledgement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disposition Decision" — read by "Review disposition
  outcome and select resolution type".
Data Object "Credit Note" — written by "Raise credit note or
  replacement record in Billing / ERP System"; read by "Verify
  transaction outcome and record in Billing / ERP System".
Data Object "Refund Instruction" — written by "Calculate refund amount
  and apply deductions"; read by "Submit refund instruction to Payment
  Gateway".
Data Object "Replacement Order" — written by "Raise replacement order";
  read by "Verify transaction outcome and record in Billing / ERP
  System".
Data Object "Customer Notification" — written by "Notify customer of
  refund or replacement decision"; read by "Confirm case closure with
  customer".

This subprocess takes the confirmed disposition decision from V13.06 and
drives it to a financial and customer conclusion: calculating and issuing
refunds through the Payment Gateway, or raising and dispatching replacement
orders, then notifying and closing with the customer. On completion it hands
a verified transaction record and closed case to V13.08 Update Inventory &
Financials, which uses those outcomes to adjust stock levels and post the
corresponding accounting entries.
```


### V13.08 — Update Inventory & Financials

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials — fourth-to-last subprocess in

  - branch "Restock — item returned to saleable inventory":

  - branch "Quarantine — item held pending further action":

  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock update type"
  User task "Confirm inventory adjustment complete"

Finance lane:

    Inventory / ERP System"
  Exclusive gateway "Financial posting type?"
  - branch "Refund issued — credit to customer account":
      User task "Post customer credit note to accounts receivable"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Financial posting type")
  - branch "Replacement dispatched — no monetary refund":
      User task "Post replacement fulfilment journal entry"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Financial posting type")
  - branch "Stock write-off — asset reduction required":

  Exclusive merge gateway "Financial posting type"
  User task "Reconcile return transaction against original order"
  Exclusive gateway "Reconciliation outcome?"

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reconciliation outcome")
  - branch "Discrepancy found":

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Warehouse lane with the message start

merging at "Financial posting type"), reconciles, routes through the

Retail Organisation (Finance lane — "Post customer credit note to accounts
  receivable") → Inventory / ERP System (credit note posting).
Retail Organisation (Finance lane — "Post replacement fulfilment journal
  entry") → Inventory / ERP System (replacement journal entry).
Retail Organisation (Finance lane — "Post stock write-off to general

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disposition Decision" — read by "Review disposition outcome
  and stock condition".
Data Object "Inventory Adjustment Record" — written by "Record stock receipt
  and update bin location in Inventory / ERP System"; written by "Record item
  in quarantine location in Inventory / ERP System"; written by "Record stock
  write-off in Inventory / ERP System"; written by "Record outbound stock
  movement in Inventory / ERP System"; read by "Confirm inventory adjustment
  complete".
Data Object "Credit Note" — written by "Post customer credit note to
  accounts receivable"; read by "Reconcile return transaction against original
  order".
Data Object "Journal Entry" — written by "Post replacement fulfilment journal
  entry"; written by "Post stock write-off to general ledger"; read by
  "Reconcile return transaction against original order".
Data Object "Return Transaction Record" — written by "Close financial record
  for return transaction"; read by "Reconcile return transaction against
  original order".

V13.08 Update Inventory & Financials ensures that every physical and monetary
consequence of the return is formally recorded. The Warehouse lane adjusts
stock positions in the Inventory / ERP System according to the disposition
outcome, while the Finance lane posts the corresponding credit notes, journal
entries, and ledger adjustments and reconciles them against the original order.
The closed, reconciled return transaction record is then handed to V13.09
Recover Cost from Supplier, which uses it as the basis for any upstream
warranty or cost-recovery claim.
```


### V13.09 — Recover Cost from Supplier

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V13.09 Recover Cost from Supplier — subprocess within the Return to
Refund value chain in which Supplier Management and Finance recover the cost
of a faulty or recalled product from the responsible supplier.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Retail Organisation" — the company executing the supplier cost-recovery
process, with lanes for Supplier Management and Finance.
Pool "Supplier" — the external manufacturer or supplier liable for the
returned goods.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — IT system recording supplier claims,
purchase-order data, and financial settlements.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Retail Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Retail Organisation
3. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Retail Organisation)

Supplier Management lane:
  Message start event "Disposition decision received from Decide Disposition"
  User task "Review disposition record and assess supplier liability"
  Exclusive gateway "Supplier liable?"
  - branch "No": End event "No supplier recovery required — process closes"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Retrieve purchase order and warranty terms
    from Procurement / ERP System"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier liable?"
  User task "Prepare supplier recovery claim"
  Send task "Submit claim to supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
  Exclusive gateway "Supplier accepts claim?"
  - branch "Disputed": User task "Escalate and negotiate claim with supplier"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Claim Resolved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Exchange supporting evidence with
    supplier", Send task "Send updated claim or counter-offer to supplier",
    Intermediate message catch event "Supplier reply received", Exclusive
    gateway "Resolution reached?",
    - branch "No": (loop repeats)
    - branch "Yes": (exits subprocess)
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts claim?"
  User task "Record agreed recovery amount"

Finance lane:
  Service task "Raise supplier debit note in Procurement / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment or credit confirmation received
    from supplier"
  User task "Reconcile recovery against original cost"
  Service task "Post recovery to supplier ledger in Procurement / ERP System"
  End event "Supplier cost recovered — ready for Analyse Return Reasons"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Claim
Resolved", labelled "Negotiation deadline exceeded (30 days)", leading to
End event "Claim unresolved — escalated to legal or written off".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Supplier Management lane with the message
start event, flows through the liability gateway — the "No" branch ends
immediately; the "Yes" branch retrieves PO data then merges — then through
claim preparation, submission, and the response catch event. The "Disputed"
branch enters the loop subprocess; the timer boundary event exits to a
terminal end event if the deadline is exceeded. The "Accepted" branch and the
resolved loop both merge at the "Supplier accepts claim?" merge gateway, then
pass to "Record agreed recovery amount" before crossing into the Finance lane
for debit note issuance, payment confirmation, reconciliation, and posting,
ending at the final end event.

Message flows:
Retail Organisation (Send task "Submit claim to supplier") → Supplier
  (supplier recovery claim with supporting evidence).
Supplier → Retail Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Supplier
  response received") (claim acceptance, dispute, or counter-offer).
Retail Organisation (Send task "Send updated claim or counter-offer to
  supplier") → Supplier (revised claim or negotiation correspondence).
Supplier → Retail Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Supplier
  reply received") (negotiation reply).
Procurement / ERP System → Retail Organisation (Service task "Retrieve
  purchase order and warranty terms from Procurement / ERP System")
  (purchase order data and warranty terms).
Retail Organisation (Service task "Raise supplier debit note in Procurement
  / ERP System") → Procurement / ERP System (debit note record).
Supplier → Retail Organisation (Intermediate message catch event "Payment or
  credit confirmation received from supplier") (remittance or credit note).
Retail Organisation (Service task "Post recovery to supplier ledger in
  Procurement / ERP System") → Procurement / ERP System (ledger posting).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Disposition Record" — read by User task "Review disposition
record and assess supplier liability".
Data Object "Supplier Recovery Claim" — written by User task "Prepare
supplier recovery claim"; read by Send task "Submit claim to supplier".
Data Object "Purchase Order and Warranty Terms" — written by Service task
"Retrieve purchase order and warranty terms from Procurement / ERP System";
read by User task "Prepare supplier recovery claim".
Data Object "Debit Note" — written by Service task "Raise supplier debit
note in Procurement / ERP System"; read by User task "Reconcile recovery
against original cost".
Data Object "Remittance or Credit Confirmation" — written by Intermediate
message catch event "Payment or credit confirmation received from supplier";
read by User task "Reconcile recovery against original cost".

This subprocess establishes whether a supplier bears financial liability for
a returned item, prepares and submits a formal recovery claim, manages any
dispute through a timed negotiation loop, and concludes by posting the agreed
recovery to the supplier ledger. It hands a fully reconciled cost-recovery
record to the final subprocess, Analyse Return Reasons, where recovered costs
and return patterns feed into performance and quality reporting.
```

```text
2. Business Intelligence Platform (black-box)

  Service task "Extract return-reason data from Business Intelligence
    Platform"
  User task "Review aggregated return-reason report"
  User task "Identify top return-reason categories and trends"

  - branch "Yes — systemic issue":

  - branch "No — within acceptable range":

  - branch "No — no change required":

  Exclusive merge gateway "Update Resolved"
  User task "Record analysis cycle completion in ticketing system"
  End event "Return-reason analysis complete — value chain concluded"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Quality lane with the message start event,
progresses through data extraction, review, trend identification, and the
"Systemic Issue Detected?" gateway whose Yes branch (raise improvement action)
and No branch both rejoin at the "Systemic Issue Handled" merge gateway before
continuing to document findings and prepare the report; a send task passes the
report to the Customer Service lane, where an intermediate message catch event
receives it; flow continues through the policy-update gateway whose Yes branch
(update policy) and No branch rejoin at the "Update Resolved" merge gateway,
then through recording completion to the end event.

Message flows:
Business Intelligence Platform → Quality lane, Service task "Extract
  return-reason data from Business Intelligence Platform" (aggregated
  return-reason dataset including disposition outcomes, fault codes,
  and volume trends).
Quality lane, Send task "Send insights report to Customer Service manager"
  → Customer Service lane, Intermediate message catch event "Insights

7. Data objects

Data Object "Return-Reason Dataset" — written by Service task "Extract

This subprocess aggregates inspection, disposition, and fault data surfaced
by the Business Intelligence Platform into a structured analysis of return
```

## V14 — Dock to Stock

**Teams and roles involved.**
Dock to Stock usually involves Inbound Logistics, Warehouse Operations, Goods Receipt, Quality Assurance, Inventory Control, Procurement, and Accounts Payable. Key roles include inbound coordinator, dock supervisor, goods-receipt clerk, quality inspector, putaway operator, inventory controller, buyer, and accounts payable officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Supplier, together with the Carrier delivering the goods. The process is initiated when a shipment arrives at the receiving dock against a purchase order or transfer order. Other external parties include customs brokers and freight forwarders for imported goods, third-party logistics providers, and testing or certification bodies.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: schedule the inbound delivery, receive the shipment at the dock, verify against the purchase order and delivery documents, unload and count, inspect quality and record any damage, record the goods receipt, put stock away to its location, handle discrepancies and rejections, release stock as available to promise, and match the receipt to the supplier invoice.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include warehouse management, ERP and inventory, purchase order and procurement systems, transport and yard management, barcode or RFID scanning, quality management, customs and trade compliance systems, and accounts payable/invoice matching.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include receiving and inspection procedure, tolerance rules for over- and under-delivery, quality acceptance criteria and sampling plans, damage and discrepancy reporting, segregation of duties between ordering and receiving, dangerous-goods and cold-chain handling, customs and import compliance, stock valuation rules, and three-way matching before payment.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The supplier and carrier provide advance shipping notices, delivery dockets and packing lists, certificates of analysis or conformance, customs documentation, and proof of delivery. The process provides the supplier and carrier with delivery booking slots, receipt confirmations, discrepancy and damage notifications, rejection notices, and returns instructions.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates inbound delivery records, goods receipts, inspection results, stock quantities and locations, quarantine and hold flags, discrepancy records, and accounts-payable matching entries. IT systems provide open purchase orders and expected quantities, item master and storage rules, available locations, quality specifications, and stock-availability and receipt-performance reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Receiving Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V14.01** Schedule Inbound Delivery | Supplier, Carrier | Inbound Logistics (inbound coordinator) | Transport & Yard Management System |
| **V14.02** Receive Shipment at Dock | Carrier | Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.03** Verify Against Purchase Order | Supplier | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V14.04** Unload & Count | Carrier | Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.05** Inspect Quality | — | Quality Assurance (quality inspector) | Quality Management System |
| **V14.06** Record Goods Receipt | — | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) | Procurement / ERP System, Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.07** Put Stock Away | — | Warehouse Operations (putaway operator) | Warehouse Management System (WMS) |
| **V14.08** Handle Discrepancies | Supplier, Customs Broker | Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk), Procurement (buyer) | Procurement / ERP System |
| **V14.09** Release Stock as Available | — | Inventory Control (inventory controller) | Inventory / ERP System |
| **V14.10** Match Receipt to Invoice | Supplier | Accounts Payable (accounts payable officer) | Accounts Payable / ERP System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V14):

- **External actors:** Supplier (V14.01, V14.03, V14.08, V14.10); Carrier (V14.01, V14.02, V14.04); Customs Broker (V14.08).
- **Teams:** Inbound Logistics (V14.01); Warehouse Operations (V14.02, V14.04, V14.07); Goods Receipt (V14.03, V14.06, V14.08); Quality Assurance (V14.05); Procurement (V14.08); Inventory Control (V14.09); Accounts Payable (V14.10).
- **IT systems:** Transport & Yard Management System (V14.01); Warehouse Management System / WMS (V14.02, V14.04, V14.06, V14.07); Procurement / ERP System (V14.03, V14.06, V14.08); Quality Management System (V14.05); Inventory / ERP System (V14.09); Accounts Payable / ERP System (V14.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V14 — Dock to Stock — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Dock to Stock value chain, from the moment a supplier and carrier
initiate an inbound delivery to the point where a matched invoice is
ready for payment. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands
read top to bottom — BUSINESS SERVICES (top), BUSINESS PROCESSES
(middle), APPLICATIONS (bottom) — expressing ArchiMate service
realisation. Demand-side actors (Supplier, Carrier, Customs Broker)
sit on the far left; internal delivery teams occupy the centre; no
external settlement actor exists at the far right, so the rightmost
position is held by the Accounts Payable team completing invoice
matching.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Supplier: far left; initiates delivery booking, provides shipping
  documents and invoices, receives receipt confirmations and
  discrepancy notices.
- Carrier: far left, below Supplier; delivers goods to dock, provides
  proof of delivery, and participates in unloading.
- Customs Broker: far left, below Carrier; supports import compliance
  and discrepancy resolution for international shipments.
- Inbound Logistics team: centre-left; responsible for scheduling
  inbound deliveries (inbound coordinator).
- Warehouse Operations team: centre; responsible for dock receipt,
  unloading, counting, and putaway (dock supervisor, putaway operator).
- Goods Receipt team: centre; responsible for PO verification, goods
  receipt recording, and discrepancy handling (goods-receipt clerk).
- Quality Assurance team: centre; responsible for quality inspection
  (quality inspector).
- Procurement team: centre; supports discrepancy resolution and buyer
  decisions (buyer).
- Inventory Control team: centre-right; releases stock as available
  (inventory controller).
- Accounts Payable team: far right; performs invoice matching
  (accounts payable officer).

2. Interfaces

- Delivery Booking Interface: used by Supplier and Carrier to ACCESS
  the Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service; exposed by the Transport
  & Yard Management System.
- Shipping Document Interface: used by Supplier and Carrier to ACCESS
  the Shipment Receipt and PO Verification Services; carries advance
  shipping notices, packing lists, and delivery dockets.
- Discrepancy Notification Interface: used by Goods Receipt and
  Procurement teams to ACCESS the Discrepancy Handling Service and
  to inform the Supplier and Customs Broker of rejections or holds.
- Invoice Submission Interface: used by Supplier to ACCESS the Invoice
  Matching Service; carries supplier invoices for three-way matching.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service: provides delivery slot booking
  and advance shipment notice processing for inbound shipments.
- Shipment Receipt Service: provides dock-level acknowledgement of
  arriving carriers and goods.
- Purchase Order Verification Service: provides confirmation that
  arriving goods match an open purchase order and delivery documents.
- Unload & Count Service: provides supervised physical unloading and
  unit counting against expected quantities.
- Quality Inspection Service: provides inspection, sampling, and
  acceptance or rejection decisions against quality criteria.
- Goods Receipt Recording Service: provides formal recording of
  received quantities, storage locations, and valuation entries.
- Putaway Service: provides directed movement of stock to its
  designated warehouse location.
- Discrepancy Handling Service: provides investigation, reporting,
  and resolution of quantity, damage, or compliance discrepancies.
- Stock Release Service: provides updating of stock availability and
  release to available-to-promise for downstream demand.
- Invoice Matching Service: provides three-way matching of purchase
  order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice before payment approval.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band

- V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery: inbound coordinator books
  delivery slots and captures advance shipping notices.
- V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock: dock supervisor acknowledges
  carrier arrival and registers inbound delivery in WMS.
- V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order: goods-receipt clerk checks
  delivery documents against open purchase order lines.
- V14.04 Unload & Count: dock supervisor oversees physical unloading
  and unit count, recording variances.
- V14.05 Inspect Quality: quality inspector performs sampling and
  inspection, logging results and raising holds if required.
- V14.06 Record Goods Receipt: goods-receipt clerk posts the goods
  receipt, updating stock quantities and triggering valuation.
- V14.07 Put Stock Away: putaway operator moves stock to directed
  locations and confirms putaway in WMS.
- V14.08 Handle Discrepancies: goods-receipt clerk and buyer manage
  short deliveries, damages, rejections, and customs issues.
- V14.09 Release Stock as Available: inventory controller removes
  quarantine flags and releases stock to available inventory.
- V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice: accounts payable officer performs
  three-way match and approves invoice for payment.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Transport & Yard Management System: manages delivery scheduling,
  slot booking, yard movements, and carrier communications.
- Warehouse Management System (WMS): manages dock registration,
  unloading, goods receipt posting, putaway direction, and
  stock-location records.
- Procurement / ERP System: manages open purchase orders, goods
  receipt documents, discrepancy records, and supplier master data.
- Quality Management System: manages inspection plans, sampling
  rules, quality results, certificates, and quarantine flags.
- Inventory / ERP System: manages stock quantities, availability
  flags, valuation, and available-to-promise updates.
- Accounts Payable / ERP System: manages invoice capture, three-way
  matching rules, payment approval, and supplier ledger entries.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Transport & Yard Management System SERVES V14.01 Schedule
  Inbound Delivery.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.02 Receive Shipment
  at Dock.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.03 Verify Against
  Purchase Order.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.04 Unload & Count.
- Quality Management System SERVES V14.05 Inspect Quality.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Management System SERVES V14.07 Put Stock Away.
- Procurement / ERP System SERVES V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Inventory / ERP System SERVES V14.09 Release Stock as Available.
- Accounts Payable / ERP System SERVES V14.10 Match Receipt
  to Invoice.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery REALISES Inbound Delivery
  Scheduling Service.
- V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock REALISES Shipment Receipt Service.
- V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order REALISES Purchase Order
  Verification Service.
- V14.04 Unload & Count REALISES Unload & Count Service.
- V14.05 Inspect Quality REALISES Quality Inspection Service.
- V14.06 Record Goods Receipt REALISES Goods Receipt Recording
  Service.
- V14.07 Put Stock Away REALISES Putaway Service.
- V14.08 Handle Discrepancies REALISES Discrepancy Handling Service.
- V14.09 Release Stock as Available REALISES Stock Release Service.
- V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice REALISES Invoice Matching Service.

ASSIGNMENT (actor assigned to process):
- Inbound Logistics team ASSIGNED TO V14.01 Schedule Inbound
  Delivery.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.02 Receive Shipment
  at Dock.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.03 Verify Against Purchase
  Order.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.04 Unload & Count.
- Quality Assurance team ASSIGNED TO V14.05 Inspect Quality.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.06 Record Goods Receipt.
- Warehouse Operations team ASSIGNED TO V14.07 Put Stock Away.
- Goods Receipt team ASSIGNED TO V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Procurement team ASSIGNED TO V14.08 Handle Discrepancies.
- Inventory Control team ASSIGNED TO V14.09 Release Stock as
  Available.
- Accounts Payable team ASSIGNED TO V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice.

ACCESS (external actor accesses service via interface):
- Supplier ACCESSES Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service via
  Delivery Booking Interface.
- Carrier ACCESSES Inbound Delivery Scheduling Service via
  Delivery Booking Interface.
- Carrier ACCESSES Shipment Receipt Service via Shipping Document
  Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Purchase Order Verification Service via
  Shipping Document Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Discrepancy Handling Service via Discrepancy
  Notification Interface.
- Customs Broker ACCESSES Discrepancy Handling Service via
  Discrepancy Notification Interface.
- Supplier ACCESSES Invoice Matching Service via Invoice Submission
  Interface.
```

```text
external entity connects to any other external entity.

4. Information flows

Supplier → Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock: advance shipping
    notice, delivery dockets, packing lists, certificates of analysis
    or conformance, customs documentation, supplier invoice
Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock → Supplier: delivery booking
    slots, receipt confirmation, discrepancy and damage notification,
    rejection notice, returns instructions
Carrier → Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock: advance shipping
    notice, delivery dockets, packing lists, proof of delivery
Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock → Carrier: delivery booking
    slots, receipt confirmation, discrepancy and damage notification,
    rejection notice
Customs Broker → Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock: customs
    clearance documentation, import compliance certificates
Receiving Organisation — Dock to Stock → Customs Broker: shipment
    details, import declarations, trade compliance records
```


**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V14 - Dock to Stock

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron shape, one chevron per stage, in the order listed
below. The chevrons must flow continuously from left to right across the
diagram, each pointing into the next, with no branching or return paths.

V14.01. Schedule Inbound Delivery
V14.02. Receive Shipment at Dock
V14.03. Verify Against Purchase Order
V14.04. Unload & Count
V14.05. Inspect Quality
V14.06. Record Goods Receipt
V14.07. Put Stock Away
V14.08. Handle Discrepancies
V14.09. Release Stock as Available
V14.10. Match Receipt to Invoice

This chain governs the end-to-end movement of incoming goods from the moment
a shipment arrives at the receiving dock through to stock being available for
use and the supplier invoice being cleared for payment. It is triggered by a
Supplier and Carrier delivering goods against an open purchase order or
transfer order. The chain takes stock from physical arrival through
verification, counting, quality inspection, and putaway, resolving any
discrepancies along the way, before confirming inventory availability and
completing three-way invoice matching in Accounts Payable.
```
### V14.01 — Schedule Inbound Delivery

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery — opens the Dock to Stock value
chain by booking an inbound delivery slot before the shipment arrives at
the receiving dock.

1. Pools & Lanes

process, with internal lanes for Inbound Logistics.

delivery requests, books dock slots, and confirms bookings to the

providing advance shipping notices and documentation.

the confirmed slot and delivering against it.

yard capacity, available dock slots, and inbound delivery records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Carrier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Transport & Yard Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Carrier
4. Transport & Yard Management System

  requested date?")

- branch "No":

  - branch "Accepted":

    Send task "Send booking confirmation to Supplier"
    Send task "Send slot confirmation to Carrier"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts
    alternative slot?")
  - branch "Rejected":
    User task "Log failed booking attempt and notify buyer"
    End event "Booking failed — buyer notified, no delivery
    scheduled"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier accepts alternative slot?"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Slot available for
  requested date?")

Exclusive merge gateway "Slot available for requested date?"

User task "Verify advance shipping notice and packing list received"

Exclusive gateway "ASN and documents complete?"

- branch "Complete":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "ASN and documents
  complete?")

- branch "Incomplete":
  Send task "Request missing documents from Supplier"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier provides missing
  documents"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "ASN and documents
  complete?")

Exclusive merge gateway "ASN and documents complete?"

Service task "Update inbound delivery record with ASN details"

End event "Delivery scheduled and confirmed — ready for Receive
Shipment at Dock"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

'Supplier responds to alternative slot offer'" — label "Response
overdue (48 hours)" — if no response is received within 48 hours,

buyer", then to End event "Booking failed — buyer notified, no

exceeded (24 hours)" — if documents are not received within 24 hours,
flow continues to User task "Log failed booking attempt and notify
buyer", then to End event "Booking failed — buyer notified, no

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Inbound Logistics lane when the
booking request arrives, proceeds through slot-availability checking,
then down either the direct-assignment branch or the alternative-slot
negotiation branch, both merging at the "Slot available for requested
date?" merge gateway; flow then moves to document verification, with
an incomplete-documents branch looping back through the merge gateway
before the record is updated and the subprocess ends.

Message flows:
Supplier → User task "Review delivery booking request and purchase
order details" (delivery booking request with purchase order
reference)
Service task "Query available dock slots and yard capacity" →
Transport & Yard Management System (slot availability query)
Transport & Yard Management System → Service task "Query available
dock slots and yard capacity" (available slots and yard capacity
data)
Service task "Record inbound delivery booking" → Transport & Yard
Management System (inbound delivery booking record)
Send task "Send booking confirmation to Supplier" → Supplier
(booking confirmation with slot details)
Send task "Send slot confirmation to Carrier" → Carrier (confirmed
delivery slot and dock assignment)
Send task "Send alternative slot offer to Supplier" → Supplier
(alternative date and slot proposal)
Supplier → Intermediate message catch event "Supplier responds to

V14.01 Schedule Inbound Delivery captures the supplier's booking
request, checks yard capacity, negotiates a dock slot when the
preferred date is unavailable, and ensures the advance shipping notice
and packing list are on hand before the shipment moves. It hands a
```

### V14.02 — Receive Shipment at Dock

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.02 Receive Shipment at Dock — second subprocess in the Dock to
Stock value chain, covering the moment a carrier arrives at the receiving dock
through to confirmation that the shipment is ready for verification against the
purchase order.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the warehouse business running the inbound
receiving process.
  Lane "Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor)" — dock supervisor who manages
  arrival, checks in the carrier, assigns a dock door, and confirms readiness.
Pool "Carrier" — the external transport party delivering the shipment.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — IT system recording dock-door

Pool "Carrier" — black-box, single instance.

single instance.

Top to bottom:
1. Carrier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) lane:
  Message start event "Carrier arrives at dock with shipment"
  User task "Check carrier and vehicle details against booking"

      mismatch and request correction"
      Intermediate message catch event "Corrected details received from
      carrier"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Carrier and booking match")
    - branch "Yes — details confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Carrier and booking match")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Carrier and booking match"
  User task "Assign dock door and direct vehicle to bay"
  Service task "Register arrival and dock-door assignment in WMS"
  User task "Receive and review delivery docket and packing list from

    - branch "No — documents missing or illegible": User task "Request

    - branch "Yes — documents accepted":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Delivery documents present

  Exclusive merge gateway "Delivery documents present and legible"
  User task "Confirm shipment ready for unloading and PO verification"

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Check carrier and vehicle

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single lane flows from the message start event through
carrier-detail checking, into the "Carrier and booking match?" exclusive
gateway; the mismatch branch passes through the notification task and an
intermediate message catch event before rejoining at the merge gateway;
the match branch rejoins directly. Flow continues through dock-door
assignment, WMS registration, document review, into the "Delivery

branch passes through a request task and an intermediate message catch

Message flows:
Carrier → Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor)
lane, Message start event "Carrier arrives at dock with shipment"
(arrival notification).

User task "Notify carrier of mismatch and request correction" → Carrier

Carrier → Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor)

Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) lane,

Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations (dock supervisor) lane,

This subprocess takes the physical arrival of a carrier at the receiving
dock and converts it into a confirmed, documented check-in event: the
vehicle is verified against its booking, directed to an assigned bay, and
```

### V14.03 — Verify Against Purchase Order

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.03 Verify Against Purchase Order — third subprocess in the
Dock to Stock value chain, bridging dock receipt to unloading by confirming
delivery documents and quantities match the open purchase order.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the verification
  process, with lanes for the Goods Receipt team.
  Lane "Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk)"
Pool "Supplier" — external party that issued the purchase order and
  accompanying documentation.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — IT system holding open purchase orders,
  item master data, and tolerance rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt (goods-receipt clerk) lane:
  Message start event "Shipment received at dock — ready for
    Verify Against Purchase Order"
  User task "Collect delivery documents from carrier"
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "Match delivery docket and packing list to purchase order"
  Exclusive gateway "Documents present and legible?"
  - branch "No — documents missing or illegible": User task "Request
      corrected documents from supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Corrected documents received from
      supplier"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Documents present and legible?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Documents
      present and legible?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Documents present and legible?"
  User task "Check quantities against purchase order tolerances"
  Exclusive gateway "Quantities within tolerance?"
  - branch "Within tolerance": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Quantities within tolerance?")
  - branch "Outside tolerance": User task "Flag quantity discrepancy and
      note variance"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quantities within tolerance?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quantities within tolerance?"
  User task "Verify certificates of analysis or conformance where required"
  Exclusive gateway "Certificates acceptable?"
  - branch "Acceptable": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Certificates acceptable?")
  - branch "Not acceptable or missing": User task "Record certificate
      exception and notify supplier"
    Intermediate message catch event "Replacement certificates received
      from supplier"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Certificates acceptable?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Certificates acceptable?"
  Service task "Record verification outcome in Procurement / ERP System"
  Exclusive gateway "Verification passed?"
  - branch "Passed": End event "Verification complete — ready for
      Unload and Count"
  - branch "Failed — discrepancy unresolved": End event "Verification
      failed — referred to Handle Discrepancies"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Request corrected
  documents from supplier" — label "Supplier response overdue" — triggers
  User task "Escalate missing documents to buyer", which flows to an
  End event "Escalation raised — referred to Handle Discrepancies".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single lane runs from the message start event through
  document collection, PO retrieval, and document matching; the "Documents
  present and legible?" gateway branches to supplier-request or directly,
  both rejoining at the merge before quantity checking; the "Quantities
  within tolerance?" gateway branches to flag or pass, rejoining before
  certificate verification; the "Certificates acceptable?" gateway branches
  to exception-and-wait or pass, rejoining before the ERP record step;
  finally the "Verification passed?" gateway routes to one of two end
  events.

Message flows:
  Supplier → User task "Collect delivery documents from carrier" (delivery
    docket, packing list, certificates of analysis or conformance, customs
    documentation).
  User task "Request corrected documents from supplier" → Supplier
    (request for corrected or missing documents).
  Intermediate message catch event "Corrected documents received from
    supplier" ← Supplier (corrected delivery documents).
  User task "Record certificate exception and notify supplier" → Supplier
    (certificate exception notification).
  Intermediate message catch event "Replacement certificates received from
    supplier" ← Supplier (replacement certificates of analysis or
    conformance).
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP
    System" ← Procurement / ERP System (open purchase order, expected
    quantities, item master data, tolerance rules).
  Service task "Record verification outcome in Procurement / ERP System"
    → Procurement / ERP System (verification result, quantity variance,
    certificate status).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Delivery Docket and Packing List" — read by User task "Match
  delivery docket and packing list to purchase order" / written by User
  task "Collect delivery documents from carrier".
Data Object "Open Purchase Order" — read by User task "Match delivery
  docket and packing list to purchase order" / written by Service task
  "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System".
Data Object "Quantity Variance Record" — read by Service task "Record
  verification outcome in Procurement / ERP System" / written by User
  task "Flag quantity discrepancy and note variance".
Data Object "Certificate of Analysis or Conformance" — read by User task
  "Verify certificates of analysis or conformance where required" /
  written by User task "Collect delivery documents from carrier".
Data Object "Verification Outcome" — read by Exclusive gateway
  "Verification passed?" / written by Service task "Record verification
  outcome in Procurement / ERP System".

This subprocess confirms that the physical shipment arriving at the dock is
supported by complete, legible documentation and that stated quantities fall
within the purchase order tolerances before unloading begins. Any missing
documents or certificate shortfalls are resolved directly with the supplier,
with unresolved failures routed to Handle Discrepancies. A passed verification
outcome, recorded in the Procurement / ERP System, hands a clean authorisation
to the Unload and Count subprocess.
```

```text
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,

2. Receiving Organisation
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

- branch "Yes — quantities match": User task "Confirm count in WMS"

Sequence flows: The single Warehouse Operations lane carries the full
flow from the message start event through resource assignment, WMS
retrieval, unloading, sorting, and counting to the exclusive gateway

count in WMS" and rejoins at exclusive merge gateway "Count check
resolved". The No branch runs through "Record count variance" and
"Recount affected line items" to the nested exclusive gateway "Recount

that merge, flow continues through labelling and scanning to the WMS

Message flows:
Carrier → Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations lane (physical
vehicle and goods presented at dock — unload ready signal).
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Receiving Organisation, Warehouse
Operations lane, "Retrieve unload instructions from WMS" (unload
instructions, expected quantities, storage rules).
Receiving Organisation, Warehouse Operations lane, "Submit final unload

This subprocess takes physical control of the inbound shipment from the
carrier, unloads all goods at the dock, and produces a confirmed unit count
reconciled against purchase order expectations. Any unresolved variances are
flagged for downstream discrepancy handling, while matched lines are labelled
and recorded in the WMS. The confirmed count record is handed to Inspect
Quality so the quality inspector knows exactly what volume of goods to assess.
```

### V14.05 — Inspect Quality

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.05 Inspect Quality — subprocess within the Dock to Stock value
chain, executed after unloading and counting and before goods receipt is
recorded.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation conducting the quality
inspection of received goods.
  Lane "Quality Assurance" — quality inspector who performs sampling,
  inspection, and records results.
Pool "Quality Management System" — IT system that holds quality
specifications, sampling plans, and inspection results.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Quality Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation (white-box, single lane)
2. Quality Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Quality Assurance lane:
  Message start event "Unloaded and counted goods received from Unload
  and Count"
  Service task "Retrieve quality specifications and sampling plan"
  User task "Select sample from received goods"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Sample Inspection Complete"
  (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Inspect sample
  item", User task "Record inspection finding"
  Exclusive gateway "Inspection outcome?"
  - branch "All items pass": User task "Approve batch"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome")
  - branch "Minor defects within tolerance": User task "Approve batch
    with reservation and flag items"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome")
  - branch "Defects exceed tolerance or damage found": User task
    "Quarantine non-conforming goods", Send task "Notify discrepancy
    for handling"
    End event "Goods quarantined — routed to Handle Discrepancies"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome"
  Service task "Record inspection result in Quality Management System"
  End event "Inspection passed — ready for Record Goods Receipt"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Sample Inspection Complete" — label "Inspection time limit exceeded" —
flow continues to User task "Escalate overdue inspection to QA
supervisor".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins at the message start event in the Quality
Assurance lane and moves through sample retrieval, selection, the
standard-loop inspection subprocess, then the exclusive gateway "Inspection
outcome?" whose passing branches (pass and minor defects) rejoin at the
exclusive merge gateway "Inspection outcome" before the result is recorded
and the passing end event is reached; the failing branch diverges to
quarantine and the notify send task, terminating at its own end event
without rejoining; the timer boundary on the loop subprocess exits to the
escalation task, which then reaches the passing end event after supervisor
review.

Message flows:
Quality Management System → Quality Assurance lane, Service task "Retrieve
quality specifications and sampling plan" (quality specifications and
sampling plan).
Quality Assurance lane, Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Sample Inspection
Complete" → Quality Management System (interim inspection findings).
Quality Assurance lane, Service task "Record inspection result in Quality
Management System" → Quality Management System (final inspection result,
pass or fail flag).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Sampling Plan" — read by "Select sample from received goods".
Data Object "Inspection Record" — written by "Record inspection finding"
inside the loop subprocess; read by "Record inspection result in Quality
Management System".
Data Object "Quarantine Notice" — written by "Quarantine non-conforming
goods"; read by "Notify discrepancy for handling".

This subprocess takes the counted and unloaded goods and subjects them to a
structured quality inspection against the supplier's specifications and the
organisation's acceptance criteria. Batches that pass, or pass with minor
reservations within tolerance, are confirmed clean and handed to Record Goods
Receipt; any batch whose defects exceed tolerance is quarantined and a
discrepancy notification is sent directly to Handle Discrepancies, keeping
non-conforming stock from entering available inventory.
```


### V14.06 — Record Goods Receipt

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.06 Record Goods Receipt — the subprocess in which the Goods
Receipt team formally captures the goods-receipt transaction in the ERP and

Quality and Put Stock Away in the Dock to Stock value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the Dock to Stock
process, white-box, containing Goods Receipt and Warehouse Operations lanes.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — ERP and procurement system that holds open
```
