```text
2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation
2. Procurement / ERP System
3. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt lane:
  Message start event "Inspection outcome received from Inspect Quality"
  User task "Review inspection outcome and count results"
  Exclusive gateway "Goods accepted?"
  - branch "No — goods rejected or on hold": End event "Goods not accepted
    — routed to Handle Discrepancies"
  - branch "Yes — goods accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Goods accepted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Goods accepted"
  User task "Select and confirm purchase order line items"
  Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "Enter goods-receipt quantities against purchase order"
  Service task "Post goods receipt in Procurement / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Goods receipt confirmation received from
    Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "Review posted goods-receipt document"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Receipt Document Complete" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Correct or supplement
    goods-receipt data", Service task "Resubmit goods-receipt posting to
    Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "Record stock quantities and storage class in WMS"
  Service task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS"
  Intermediate message catch event "WMS stock update confirmed"
  User task "Apply quarantine or hold flag if partial acceptance"
  Service task "Set quarantine or hold flags in Procurement / ERP System"
  User task "File goods-receipt document and packing list"

Warehouse Operations lane:
  User task "Confirm physical count and location data with Goods Receipt"
  User task "Acknowledge stock update completion in WMS"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Receipt Document Complete" — label "Correction time limit exceeded" —
on trigger, flow continues to End event "Goods receipt posting failed —
escalated to Procurement".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Goods Receipt lane with the message
start event, moves through the inspection-outcome review and the
"Goods accepted?" gateway; the rejection branch ends immediately; the
accepted branch merges at the exclusive merge gateway and continues
through purchase-order selection, quantity entry, ERP posting, and the
message catch event confirming the posting. If the receipt document is
incomplete, the standard-loop subprocess repeats correction and
resubmission until the document is complete; a timer boundary event
exits to a failure end event if the limit is exceeded. Once the document
is complete, flow crosses to the Warehouse Operations lane for physical
count confirmation, then returns to Goods Receipt for WMS stock-quantity
update, the WMS confirmation catch event, quarantine-flag application,
and document filing. The Warehouse Operations lane also contains the WMS
acknowledgement task, sequenced after the WMS service task confirmation.

Message flows:
Service task "Retrieve open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System"
  → Pool "Procurement / ERP System" (open purchase order request)
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" → Service task "Post goods receipt in
  Procurement / ERP System" (purchase order line data returned)
Service task "Post goods receipt in Procurement / ERP System" → Pool
  "Procurement / ERP System" (goods-receipt posting)
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" → Intermediate message catch event
  "Goods receipt confirmation received from Procurement / ERP System"
  (goods-receipt confirmation)
Service task "Resubmit goods-receipt posting to Procurement / ERP System"
  → Pool "Procurement / ERP System" (corrected goods-receipt posting)
Service task "Set quarantine or hold flags in Procurement / ERP System"
  → Pool "Procurement / ERP System" (quarantine or hold flag instruction)
Service task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS" → Pool
  "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" (stock quantity and location update)
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" → Intermediate message catch
  event "WMS stock update confirmed" (stock update confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Inspection Outcome Report" — read by User task "Review
  inspection outcome and count results".
Data Object "Purchase Order Line Items" — read by User task "Select and
  confirm purchase order line items"; written by Service task "Retrieve
  open purchase order from Procurement / ERP System".
Data Object "Goods Receipt Document" — written by User task "Enter
  goods-receipt quantities against purchase order"; read by User task
  "Review posted goods-receipt document"; read by User task "File
  goods-receipt document and packing list".
Data Object "Packing List" — read by User task "File goods-receipt
  document and packing list".
Data Object "Stock Quantity and Location Record" — written by User task
  "Record stock quantities and storage class in WMS"; read by Service
  task "Update stock quantities and locations in WMS".
Data Object "Quarantine or Hold Flag" — written by User task "Apply
  quarantine or hold flag if partial acceptance"; read by Service task
  "Set quarantine or hold flags in Procurement / ERP System".

Record Goods Receipt formalises the transition from physical verification
to system-of-record. It posts a confirmed goods-receipt document against
the open purchase order in the ERP, updates stock quantities and storage
locations in the WMS, and applies any quarantine or hold flags arising
from partial acceptance. On completion, a clean, system-confirmed receipt
record is available for the Warehouse Operations team to act upon in the
Put Stock Away subprocess.
```


### V14.07 — Put Stock Away

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.07 Put Stock Away — the subprocess in which warehouse
operations moves counted and receipted stock from the receiving area
to its designated storage location, completing the physical inbound
movement before stock is released as available.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the warehouse business running the
putaway process, with lanes for Warehouse Operations.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — the IT system that
directs putaway tasks, assigns locations, and confirms stock
placement.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Warehouse Management System (WMS)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation
2. Warehouse Management System (WMS)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Warehouse Operations lane:
  Message start event "Goods receipt confirmed — received from
    Record Goods Receipt"
  User task "Review putaway task list"
  Service task "Request putaway location from WMS"
  Intermediate message catch event "Putaway location assigned by WMS"
  User task "Move stock to assigned location"
  User task "Scan stock into location"
  Service task "Confirm putaway in WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "Putaway confirmed by WMS?"
    - branch "Yes — location accepted":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Putaway confirmed
        by WMS")
    - branch "No — location conflict or error":
        User task "Resolve location conflict"
        Service task "Request alternative location from WMS"
        Intermediate message catch event "Alternative location
          assigned by WMS"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Putaway confirmed
        by WMS")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Putaway confirmed by WMS"
  Exclusive gateway "All lines putaway?"
    - branch "No — lines remain":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All lines putaway")
    - branch "Yes — all lines complete":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All lines putaway")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All lines putaway"
  User task "Close putaway task and update stock record"
  End event "Stock put away — ready for Release Stock as Available"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Move stock to assigned
location" — label "Putaway time limit exceeded" — triggers User task
"Escalate overdue putaway to dock supervisor", which flows to an
End event "Putaway escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Warehouse Operations lane with
the message start event and proceeds linearly through reviewing the
task list, requesting a location, and receiving the assignment. The
putaway operator moves and scans stock, then the system confirmation
gateway branches to either accept the location or loop through
conflict resolution and an alternative-location request before
merging. The all-lines gateway loops back through the move-and-scan
steps for any remaining lines, then merges and closes with the task
record update and end event.

Message flows:
Warehouse Operations "Request putaway location from WMS" →
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) (putaway location request)
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Warehouse Operations
  Intermediate message catch event "Putaway location assigned by WMS"
  (assigned storage location)
Warehouse Operations "Scan stock into location" →
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) (barcode or RFID scan data)
Warehouse Operations "Confirm putaway in WMS" →
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) (putaway confirmation)
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Warehouse Operations
  Exclusive gateway "Putaway confirmed by WMS?" (confirmation
  result — accepted or error)
Warehouse Operations "Request alternative location from WMS" →
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) (alternative location request)
Warehouse Management System (WMS) → Warehouse Operations
  Intermediate message catch event "Alternative location assigned
  by WMS" (alternative storage location)
Warehouse Operations "Close putaway task and update stock record" →
  Warehouse Management System (WMS) (final stock location and
  quantity update)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Putaway Task List" — written by Service task "Request
  putaway location from WMS"; read by User task "Review putaway task
  list".
Data Object "Assigned Location Record" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Putaway location assigned by WMS"; read by
  User task "Move stock to assigned location".
Data Object "Scan Confirmation" — written by User task "Scan stock
  into location"; read by Service task "Confirm putaway in WMS".
Data Object "Stock Location Record" — written by User task "Close
  putaway task and update stock record".

Put Stock Away physically moves receipted goods from the dock
receiving area to their designated warehouse locations, using
WMS-directed putaway tasks and barcode or RFID confirmation at
each location. Every stock line is scanned into place and confirmed
in the WMS before the task closes. The subprocess hands a fully
located and system-confirmed stock record to Release Stock as
Available, which will lift any holds and make the inventory visible
to order fulfilment.
```


### V14.08 — Handle Discrepancies

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.08 Handle Discrepancies — subprocess within the Dock to Stock
value chain that investigates and resolves quantity, damage, and
documentation discrepancies before stock is released or returned.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the
discrepancy-handling process, containing lanes for Goods Receipt and
Procurement.
Pool "Supplier" — external party notified of discrepancies and from whom
resolution decisions are sought.
Pool "Customs Broker" — external party engaged when import documentation
discrepancies arise.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — IT system used to record discrepancy
notices, update purchase orders, and log resolution outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Customs Broker" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Procurement / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Customs Broker
3. Receiving Organisation
4. Procurement / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Goods Receipt lane:
  Message start event "Discrepancy identified — received from Record
    Goods Receipt"
  User task "Review and classify discrepancy"
  Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy type?"
    - branch "Quantity or damage discrepancy":
        User task "Raise discrepancy notice"
        Send task "Notify supplier of discrepancy"
        Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
        Exclusive gateway "Supplier response acceptable?"
          - branch "Yes — credit or replacement agreed":
              User task "Record supplier resolution in system"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier response
                acceptable")
          - branch "No — dispute unresolved":
              User task "Escalate to buyer"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Supplier response
                acceptable")
        Exclusive merge gateway "Supplier response acceptable"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy type")
    - branch "Import documentation discrepancy":
        User task "Identify missing or incorrect customs documents"
        Send task "Contact customs broker for document correction"
        Intermediate message catch event "Corrected documents received"
        User task "Verify corrected customs documents"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy type")
    - branch "No discrepancy confirmed — recording error":
        User task "Correct goods receipt record"
        End event "Recording error resolved — no further action"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy type"
  User task "Update purchase order with discrepancy outcome"
  Service task "Post discrepancy record to Procurement / ERP System"
  Exclusive gateway "Stock disposition required?"
    - branch "Return to supplier":
        User task "Arrange return shipment and issue returns
          instructions"
        Send task "Send rejection notice and returns instructions to
          supplier"
        End event "Goods returned to supplier — discrepancy closed"
    - branch "Accept under tolerance":
        User task "Approve partial acceptance and adjust order quantity"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock disposition
          required")
    - branch "Quarantine pending further review":
        User task "Apply quarantine hold flag"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock disposition
          required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock disposition required"
  End event "Discrepancy resolved — ready for Release Stock as Available"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Escalate to buyer"
  - (This task receives flow from the Goods Receipt lane when a supplier
    dispute is unresolved; the buyer reviews the case and determines the
    resolution position before flow returns to the Goods Receipt lane at
    the exclusive merge gateway "Supplier response acceptable".)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Supplier response received" — label "Supplier response overdue
(72 hours)" — triggers User task "Escalate to buyer" in the Procurement
lane if no supplier response is received within 72 hours.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Goods Receipt lane at the message
start event, passes through classification and then the "Discrepancy
type" exclusive gateway whose three branches handle quantity/damage,
import documentation, and recording-error cases respectively; the
recording-error branch ends at its own end event; the other two branches
rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy type"; flow continues
through purchase-order update, ERP posting, and the "Stock disposition
required" exclusive gateway whose return and partial-acceptance and
quarantine branches resolve at the exclusive merge gateway "Stock
disposition required" before the final end event; the escalation task in
the Procurement lane is reached from the Goods Receipt lane when a
supplier dispute is unresolved and returns to the Goods Receipt lane at
the merge gateway.

Message flows:
Receiving Organisation (Send task "Notify supplier of discrepancy") →
  Supplier (discrepancy notice with quantities and damage evidence).
Supplier → Receiving Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
  "Supplier response received") (credit memo, replacement confirmation,
  or dispute).
Receiving Organisation (Send task "Contact customs broker for document
  correction") → Customs Broker (request for corrected import
  documentation).
Customs Broker → Receiving Organisation (Intermediate message catch
  event "Corrected documents received") (corrected customs documents).
Receiving Organisation (Send task "Send rejection notice and returns
  instructions to supplier") → Supplier (rejection notice and returns
  instructions).
Receiving Organisation (Service task "Post discrepancy record to
  Procurement / ERP System") → Procurement / ERP System (discrepancy
  record, updated purchase order quantities, and resolution outcome).
Procurement / ERP System → Receiving Organisation (User task "Update
  purchase order with discrepancy outcome") (open purchase order data
  and tolerance rules).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Discrepancy Notice" — written by User task "Raise
  discrepancy notice"; read by Send task "Notify supplier of
  discrepancy".
Data Object "Supplier Response" — written by Intermediate message catch
  event "Supplier response received"; read by Exclusive gateway
  "Supplier response acceptable?".
Data Object "Corrected Customs Documents" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Corrected documents received"; read by User task
  "Verify corrected customs documents".
Data Object "Discrepancy Record" — written by Service task "Post
  discrepancy record to Procurement / ERP System"; read by User task
  "Update purchase order with discrepancy outcome".
Data Object "Returns Instructions" — written by User task "Arrange
  return shipment and issue returns instructions"; read by Send task
  "Send rejection notice and returns instructions to supplier".

This subprocess takes discrepancies flagged during goods receipt —
covering quantity shortages or overages, physical damage, and import
documentation errors — and drives each to a documented resolution:
supplier credit, replacement, partial acceptance within tolerance,
quarantine, or physical return. Every outcome is posted to the
Procurement / ERP System so that purchase orders reflect actuality. The
subprocess hands a fully resolved and correctly recorded stock position
to Release Stock as Available, ensuring that only accepted goods proceed
into available inventory.
```


### V14.09 — Release Stock as Available

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.09 Release Stock as Available — the subprocess that lifts
quarantine and hold flags, confirms stock quantities and locations, and
makes goods available to promise following successful goods receipt and
putaway in the Dock to Stock value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the
release-to-available process, containing the Inventory Control team.
- Lane "Inventory Control (inventory controller)"

Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — the system that holds stock quantities,
availability flags, and stock-performance records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Inventory / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Receiving Organisation
2. Inventory / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Inventory Control (inventory controller) lane:
  Message start event "Putaway confirmed — received from Put Stock Away"
  User task "Review putaway confirmation and stock record"
  Service task "Retrieve current stock status from Inventory / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Stock status data received"
  Exclusive gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine?"
  - branch "Yes — hold or quarantine flag active":
    User task "Investigate reason for hold or quarantine flag"
    Exclusive gateway "Hold reason resolved?"
    - branch "No — hold cannot be resolved":
      End event "Stock retained on hold — escalated to Handle
      Discrepancies"
    - branch "Yes — hold resolved":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Hold reason resolved")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Hold reason resolved"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine")
  - branch "No — no active hold or quarantine":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Stock on hold or in quarantine"
  User task "Confirm quantity and location accuracy"
  Exclusive gateway "Quantity and location confirmed?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found":
    User task "Raise location or quantity correction"
    Service task "Submit correction to Inventory / ERP System"
    Intermediate message catch event "Correction acknowledgement received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quantity and location confirmed")
  - branch "Yes — confirmed":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quantity and location confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quantity and location confirmed"
  Service task "Set stock availability flag to Available in Inventory /
  ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Availability flag confirmation received"
  User task "Record stock release and update availability log"
  Service task "Trigger stock-availability and receipt-performance
  reporting in Inventory / ERP System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Reporting acknowledgement received"
  End event "Stock released as available — ready for Match Receipt
  to Invoice"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Investigate reason for hold or
quarantine flag" — label "Hold investigation deadline exceeded" — flow
continues to End event "Stock retained on hold — escalated to Handle
Discrepancies".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow runs entirely within the Inventory Control lane,
starting at the message start event and progressing through review,
status retrieval, and the hold-or-quarantine gateway. The hold branch
leads to investigation and a nested resolution gateway whose unresolved
branch ends in a hold-retained end event and whose resolved branch
merges back; the no-hold branch bypasses this. Both branches rejoin at
the "Stock on hold or in quarantine" merge gateway, continuing to
quantity and location confirmation. The discrepancy branch raises a
correction, submits it, and awaits acknowledgement before rejoining the
confirmed branch at the "Quantity and location confirmed" merge gateway.
Flow then proceeds through the availability-flag service task,
confirmation catch event, log update, and reporting service task before
reaching the end event.

Message flows:
Inventory / ERP System → "Retrieve current stock status from Inventory /
ERP System" (current stock status and hold or quarantine flags).
"Submit correction to Inventory / ERP System" → Inventory / ERP System
(location or quantity correction request).
Inventory / ERP System → "Correction acknowledgement received"
(correction acknowledgement).
"Set stock availability flag to Available in Inventory / ERP System" →
Inventory / ERP System (availability flag update).
Inventory / ERP System → "Availability flag confirmation received"
(flag-set confirmation).
"Trigger stock-availability and receipt-performance reporting in
Inventory / ERP System" → Inventory / ERP System (reporting trigger).
Inventory / ERP System → "Reporting acknowledgement received"
(reporting acknowledgement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Putaway Confirmation" — read by "Review putaway
confirmation and stock record".
Data Object "Stock Status Record" — read by "Confirm quantity and
location accuracy"; written by "Retrieve current stock status from
Inventory / ERP System".
Data Object "Location or Quantity Correction" — written by "Raise
location or quantity correction"; read by "Submit correction to
Inventory / ERP System".
Data Object "Stock Availability Log" — written by "Record stock release
and update availability log".

This subprocess takes the putaway confirmation handed off by Put Stock
Away and lifts any outstanding hold or quarantine flags, verifies that
quantities and locations are accurate, and writes the availability flag
to the Inventory / ERP System so that stock becomes visible as available
to promise. Any unresolvable hold is escalated back to Handle
Discrepancies rather than released. The confirmed, flagged, and logged
availability record is then handed to Match Receipt to Invoice, which
uses it as part of the three-way matching process before authorising
supplier payment.
```


### V14.10 — Match Receipt to Invoice

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V14.10 Match Receipt to Invoice — the final subprocess of the
Dock to Stock value chain, reconciling the supplier invoice against the
goods receipt and purchase order before authorising payment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — the organisation running the matching
and payment-authorisation process, with lanes for Accounts Payable and
Procurement.
Pool "Supplier" — the external supplier who raises and corrects invoices.
Pool "Accounts Payable / ERP System" — the IT system that holds
invoice records, purchase orders, goods receipts, and matching entries.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Receiving Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Accounts Payable / ERP System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Supplier
2. Receiving Organisation
3. Accounts Payable / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Receiving Organisation)

Accounts Payable lane:
  Message start event "Stock released — ready to match receipt to
    invoice"
  Task "Retrieve open purchase order and goods receipt record"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supplier invoice received"
  Service task "Load invoice into Accounts Payable / ERP System"
  Service task "Run three-way match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice"
  Exclusive gateway "Match result?"
  - branch "Matched within tolerance":
      User task "Approve matched invoice for payment"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Match result")
  - branch "Price or quantity discrepancy":
      User task "Flag discrepancy and place invoice on hold"
      Send task "Send discrepancy notification to Supplier"
      Intermediate message catch event "Supplier response received"
      Exclusive gateway "Discrepancy resolved?"
      - branch "Supplier issues credit note or corrected invoice":
          Service task "Load corrected invoice or credit note into
            Accounts Payable / ERP System"
          User task "Re-run three-way match on corrected documents"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolved")
      - branch "Dispute escalated to Procurement":
          User task "Escalate dispute to Procurement buyer for
            resolution"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolved")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Discrepancy resolved"
      User task "Confirm invoice disposition after resolution"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Match result")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Match result"
  Service task "Post matching entry to Accounts Payable / ERP System"
  User task "Schedule payment run"
  Send task "Send payment confirmation to Supplier"
  End event "Invoice matched and payment authorised — Dock to Stock
    complete"

Procurement lane:
  User task "Review escalated dispute and negotiate with Supplier"
  Send task "Return resolution outcome to Accounts Payable"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  Supplier response received" — label "Response overdue (5 business
  days)" — on expiry, flow moves to user task "Escalate dispute to
  Procurement buyer for resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the Accounts Payable lane carries the main flow from
the start event through retrieval, invoice load, and three-way match,
then branches at the "Match result?" gateway. The matched branch
approves and rejoins at the "Match result" merge. The discrepancy branch
places a hold, notifies the supplier, waits for a response, then splits
at "Discrepancy resolved?": the corrected-documents branch reloads and
re-runs the match, the escalation branch passes to the Procurement lane
where the buyer negotiates and returns the outcome; both rejoin at
"Discrepancy resolved" merge, then confirm disposition before rejoining
"Match result" merge. After the merge, the flow posts the matching
entry, schedules payment, sends confirmation, and ends.

Message flows:
  Supplier → Accounts Payable lane (supplier invoice)
  Accounts Payable lane → Supplier (discrepancy notification via send
    task "Send discrepancy notification to Supplier")
  Supplier → Accounts Payable lane (corrected invoice or credit note)
  Accounts Payable lane → Supplier (payment confirmation via send task
    "Send payment confirmation to Supplier")
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (invoice
    load via service task "Load invoice into Accounts Payable / ERP
    System")
  Accounts Payable / ERP System → Accounts Payable lane (purchase
    order and goods receipt data via task "Retrieve open purchase order
    and goods receipt record")
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (three-way
    match request via service task "Run three-way match — PO, goods
    receipt, and invoice")
  Accounts Payable / ERP System → Accounts Payable lane (match result
    returned to "Run three-way match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice")
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (corrected
    document load via service task "Load corrected invoice or credit
    note into Accounts Payable / ERP System")
  Accounts Payable lane → Accounts Payable / ERP System (matching
    entry posted via service task "Post matching entry to Accounts
    Payable / ERP System")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Supplier Invoice" — written by service task "Load invoice
  into Accounts Payable / ERP System"; read by service task "Run
  three-way match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice".
Data Object "Purchase Order" — read by task "Retrieve open purchase
  order and goods receipt record"; read by service task "Run three-way
  match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice".
Data Object "Goods Receipt Record" — read by task "Retrieve open
  purchase order and goods receipt record"; read by service task "Run
  three-way match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice".
Data Object "Three-Way Match Result" — written by service task "Run
  three-way match — PO, goods receipt, and invoice"; read by exclusive
  gateway "Match result?".
Data Object "Discrepancy Record" — written by user task "Flag
  discrepancy and place invoice on hold"; read by user task "Confirm
  invoice disposition after resolution".
Data Object "Corrected Invoice / Credit Note" — written by service
  task "Load corrected invoice or credit note into Accounts Payable /
  ERP System"; read by user task "Re-run three-way match on corrected
  documents".
Data Object "Payment Schedule Entry" — written by user task "Schedule
  payment run"; read by send task "Send payment confirmation to
  Supplier".

This subprocess takes the released stock from Release Stock as Available
and closes the financial loop by performing three-way matching of the
purchase order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice. Discrepancies are
resolved through supplier correction or Procurement escalation before
the invoice is approved. Once matched and posted, a payment run is
scheduled and the supplier is notified, concluding the entire Dock to
Stock value chain.
```


## V15 — Detect to Repair

**Teams and roles involved.**
Detect to Repair usually involves Maintenance, Reliability Engineering, Operations, Field Service, Planning and Scheduling, Spare Parts/Stores, Health and Safety, and Finance for cost capture. Key roles include maintenance planner, reliability engineer, condition-monitoring analyst, maintenance technician, field service engineer, scheduler, storeperson, safety officer, and asset manager.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Equipment Owner or Operator who reports the fault, and specialist Service Contractors or the Original Equipment Manufacturer where work is outsourced. The process is initiated by a fault report, an alarm or condition-monitoring exception, an inspection finding, or a preventive maintenance schedule falling due. Other external parties include parts suppliers, calibration and testing services, and regulators for safety-critical assets.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: detect the fault or condition exception, raise and triage the notification, assess criticality and safety impact, diagnose the fault, plan the work and required parts, schedule the work and secure permits, execute the repair, test and return the asset to service, close the work order and capture costs, and analyse failure causes to prevent recurrence.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include enterprise asset management or computerised maintenance management, condition-monitoring and IoT/SCADA platforms, work-order and field-service management, spare-parts inventory, permit-to-work and safety systems, document management for drawings and manuals, procurement for contracted services, and reliability analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include asset criticality classification, maintenance strategy and preventive schedules, permit-to-work and isolation procedures, safety and lock-out/tag-out rules, spare-parts stocking policy, contractor approval and induction, warranty claim procedure, calibration and statutory inspection requirements, and cost capitalisation versus expense rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The operator or owner provides fault reports, symptoms and operating context, access windows, and confirmation that the asset can be taken offline. Contractors provide quotes, method statements, work completion reports and certificates. The process provides fault acknowledgements, expected downtime and schedules, work instructions and permits, completion and return-to-service notifications, and warranty or claim documentation.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates notifications, work orders, diagnoses, parts reservations and issues, labour and cost postings, permits, test results, and asset history. IT systems provide asset registers and hierarchies, condition and alarm data, maintenance history and failure codes, parts availability, technician skills and availability, and reliability and downtime reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Asset Owner Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT
systems are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V15.01** Detect Fault or Condition Exception | Equipment Operator | Reliability Engineering (condition-monitoring analyst) | Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform |
| **V15.02** Raise & Triage Notification | Equipment Operator | Maintenance (maintenance planner) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) |
| **V15.03** Assess Criticality & Safety Impact | — | Reliability Engineering (reliability engineer), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) |
| **V15.04** Diagnose Fault | Original Equipment Manufacturer | Maintenance (maintenance technician), Reliability Engineering (reliability engineer) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Document Management System |
| **V15.05** Plan Work & Parts | — | Maintenance (maintenance planner), Spare Parts (storeperson) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Spare Parts Inventory System |
| **V15.06** Schedule Work & Secure Permits | Service Contractor | Planning & Scheduling (scheduler), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Permit-to-Work System, Work Order Management System |
| **V15.07** Execute Repair | Service Contractor | Maintenance (maintenance technician), Field Service (field service engineer) | Work Order Management System |
| **V15.08** Test & Return to Service | Equipment Operator | Maintenance (maintenance technician), Operations (operations supervisor) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) |
| **V15.09** Close Work Order & Capture Costs | — | Maintenance (maintenance planner), Finance (asset accountant) | Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), Finance / ERP System |
| **V15.10** Analyse Failure Causes | — | Reliability Engineering (reliability engineer) | Reliability Analytics Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V15):

- **External actors:** Equipment Operator (V15.01, V15.02, V15.08); Original Equipment Manufacturer (V15.04); Service Contractor (V15.06, V15.07).
- **Teams:** Reliability Engineering (V15.01, V15.03, V15.04, V15.10); Maintenance (V15.02, V15.04, V15.05, V15.07–V15.09); Health & Safety (V15.03, V15.06); Spare Parts (V15.05); Planning & Scheduling (V15.06); Field Service (V15.07); Operations (V15.08); Finance (V15.09).
- **IT systems:** Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform (V15.01); Enterprise Asset Management / EAM (V15.02–V15.05, V15.08, V15.09); Document Management System (V15.04); Spare Parts Inventory System (V15.05); Permit-to-Work System (V15.06); Work Order Management System (V15.06, V15.07); Finance / ERP System (V15.09); Reliability Analytics Platform (V15.10).

```text
ArchiMate: V15 — Detect to Repair — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Detect to Repair value chain, from the moment a fault or condition
exception is detected through to failure-cause analysis and work-order
closure. The diagram is arranged in three horizontal bands, read top to
bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) → BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) →
APPLICATIONS (bottom band). The demand-side actor (Equipment Operator) sits
on the far left; delivery and settlement actors (Original Equipment
Manufacturer, Service Contractor) sit on the far right. Reading top-to-bottom
follows ArchiMate service realisation: each business service is realised by
one or more business processes, which are in turn supported by application
components below them.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Equipment Operator — far left; initiates fault reports, provides access
  windows, and confirms return to service.
- Original Equipment Manufacturer — far right; provides specialist
  diagnostic support for complex faults.
- Service Contractor — far right; executes outsourced repair work and
  supplies completion certificates.

2. Interfaces

- Fault Reporting Interface — used by Equipment Operator to ACCESS the
  Fault Detection & Notification Service; served by V15.01 and V15.02.
- Return-to-Service Confirmation Interface — used by Equipment Operator to
  ACCESS the Asset Return to Service; served by V15.08.
- Diagnostic Support Interface — used by Original Equipment Manufacturer
  to ACCESS the Fault Diagnosis Service; served by V15.04.
- Contractor Work Interface — used by Service Contractor to ACCESS the
  Work Execution & Permitting Service; served by V15.06 and V15.07.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Fault Detection & Notification Service — provides timely identification
  and acknowledgement of equipment faults and condition exceptions.
- Criticality & Safety Assessment Service — provides structured evaluation
  of asset criticality and safety impact before work begins.
- Fault Diagnosis Service — provides root-cause identification and
  technical advice to support repair planning.
- Work Planning & Parts Provision Service — provides complete work scope,
  bill of materials, and parts reservation for the repair.
- Work Scheduling & Permitting Service — provides confirmed work schedule,
  contractor co-ordination, and valid permits to work.
- Repair Execution Service — provides safe, controlled execution of the
  repair by qualified technicians or contractors.
- Asset Return to Service — provides tested confirmation that the asset
  meets required performance standards and is safe to operate.
- Work Order Closure & Cost Capture Service — provides accurate financial
  posting, work-order closure, and warranty documentation.
- Failure Analysis & Reliability Improvement Service — provides
  structured failure-cause analysis and improvement recommendations.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V15.01 Detect Fault or Condition Exception — monitors asset condition
  data and raises an initial alert or alarm.
- V15.02 Raise & Triage Notification — creates a formal notification,
  classifies the fault type, and assigns initial priority.
- V15.03 Assess Criticality & Safety Impact — evaluates asset criticality
  classification and any safety implications before progressing.
- V15.04 Diagnose Fault — investigates symptoms, reviews history, and
  establishes root cause with specialist support where needed.
- V15.05 Plan Work & Parts — defines work scope, identifies required
  parts, and reserves or procures materials.
- V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure Permits — confirms resource and time
  schedule, engages contractors, and issues permits to work.
- V15.07 Execute Repair — carries out the physical repair in line with
  work instructions, permits, and safety rules.
- V15.08 Test & Return to Service — tests repaired asset against
  acceptance criteria and obtains operational sign-off.
- V15.09 Close Work Order & Capture Costs — posts labour, parts and
  contractor costs, closes the work order, and records asset history.
- V15.10 Analyse Failure Causes — performs reliability analysis on failure
  data and recommends preventive or design improvements.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform — collects and streams real-time
  asset condition, alarm, and sensor data.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) — manages asset register, work
  orders, maintenance history, failure codes, and cost postings.
- Document Management System — stores and serves engineering drawings,
  maintenance manuals, and technical specifications.
- Spare Parts Inventory System — manages parts catalogue, stock levels,
  reservations, and issues.
- Permit-to-Work System — issues, controls, and closes permits to work
  and isolation certificates.
- Work Order Management System — manages field work-order assignment,
  progress tracking, and completion recording.
- Finance / ERP System — receives cost postings from EAM, manages
  capitalisation versus expense rules, and supports financial reporting.
- Reliability Analytics Platform — aggregates failure data, supports
  root-cause analysis, and produces reliability and downtime reports.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component SERVES business process):
- Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform SERVES V15.01 Detect Fault or
  Condition Exception.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.02 Raise & Triage
  Notification.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.03 Assess Criticality &
  Safety Impact.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.04 Diagnose Fault.
- Document Management System SERVES V15.04 Diagnose Fault.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.05 Plan Work & Parts.
- Spare Parts Inventory System SERVES V15.05 Plan Work & Parts.
- Permit-to-Work System SERVES V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure Permits.
- Work Order Management System SERVES V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure
  Permits.
- Work Order Management System SERVES V15.07 Execute Repair.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.08 Test & Return to
  Service.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) SERVES V15.09 Close Work Order &
  Capture Costs.
- Finance / ERP System SERVES V15.09 Close Work Order & Capture Costs.
- Reliability Analytics Platform SERVES V15.10 Analyse Failure Causes.

REALISATION (business process REALISES business service):
- V15.01 and V15.02 REALISE Fault Detection & Notification Service.
- V15.03 REALISES Criticality & Safety Assessment Service.
- V15.04 REALISES Fault Diagnosis Service.
- V15.05 REALISES Work Planning & Parts Provision Service.
- V15.06 REALISES Work Scheduling & Permitting Service.
- V15.07 REALISES Repair Execution Service.
- V15.08 REALISES Asset Return to Service.
- V15.09 REALISES Work Order Closure & Cost Capture Service.
- V15.10 REALISES Failure Analysis & Reliability Improvement Service.

ASSIGNMENT (business actor ASSIGNED TO interface):
- Equipment Operator ASSIGNED TO Fault Reporting Interface.
- Equipment Operator ASSIGNED TO Return-to-Service Confirmation
  Interface.
- Original Equipment Manufacturer ASSIGNED TO Diagnostic Support
  Interface.
- Service Contractor ASSIGNED TO Contractor Work Interface.

ACCESS (interface ACCESSES business service):
- Fault Reporting Interface ACCESSES Fault Detection & Notification
  Service.
- Return-to-Service Confirmation Interface ACCESSES Asset Return to
  Service.
- Diagnostic Support Interface ACCESSES Fault Diagnosis Service.
- Contractor Work Interface ACCESSES Work Scheduling & Permitting Service.
- Contractor Work Interface ACCESSES Repair Execution Service.
```

### V15.01 — Detect Fault or Condition Exception

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.01 Detect Fault or Condition Exception — first subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, covering every path by which a fault or
condition exception is identified and passed to triage.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation running the detection
process, with lanes for Reliability Engineering.
  Lane "Reliability Engineering (Condition-Monitoring Analyst)"
Pool "Equipment Operator" — external party who observes and reports a fault.
Pool "Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform" — IT system providing alarm
and sensor data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Reliability Engineering (Condition-Monitoring Analyst) lane:
  Multiple start event "Fault signal, alarm, inspection finding, or PM
    schedule received"
  Exclusive gateway "Detection source?"
  - branch "Operator fault report received":
      Message intermediate catch event "Operator fault report received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Detection source resolved")
  - branch "Condition monitoring or SCADA alarm":
      Message intermediate catch event "Alarm or exception data received
        from Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Detection source resolved")
  - branch "Scheduled inspection or PM trigger":
      User task "Review preventive maintenance schedule and confirm trigger"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Detection source resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Detection source resolved"
  User task "Log raw detection signal and initial symptoms"
  Service task "Retrieve asset register entry and condition history from
    Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform"
  User task "Review signal against asset criticality classification and
    alarm thresholds"
  Exclusive gateway "Is the signal a confirmed fault or condition
    exception?"
  - branch "No — signal within normal limits or false alarm":
      User task "Document false-alarm finding and close detection record"
      End event "False alarm closed — no further action"
  - branch "Yes — confirmed fault or condition exception":
      User task "Capture fault description, observed symptoms, and
        operating context"
      Service task "Record confirmed detection event in Condition
        Monitoring / SCADA Platform"
      End event "Detection confirmed — ready for Raise and Triage
        Notification"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins at the multiple start event in the Reliability
Engineering lane, passes through the Detection source gateway, each branch
rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway "Detection source resolved", then
continues through logging, retrieval, review, and the confirmation gateway.
The false-alarm branch ends at its own end event; the confirmed-fault
branch ends at the subprocess end event.

Message flows:
Equipment Operator → Reliability Engineering (Condition-Monitoring Analyst)
  (operator fault report containing symptoms and operating context)
Condition Monitoring / SCADA Platform → Reliability Engineering
  (Condition-Monitoring Analyst) (alarm trigger or condition-exception data)
Reliability Engineering (Condition-Monitoring Analyst) → Condition
  Monitoring / SCADA Platform (confirmed detection event record written
  back to platform)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Fault Detection Record" — written by "Log raw detection signal
  and initial symptoms"; read by "Review signal against asset criticality
  classification and alarm thresholds".
Data Object "Asset Condition History" — read by "Review signal against
  asset criticality classification and alarm thresholds"; written by
  "Record confirmed detection event in Condition Monitoring / SCADA
  Platform".
Data Object "Confirmed Fault Description" — written by "Capture fault
  description, observed symptoms, and operating context"; read by
  "Record confirmed detection event in Condition Monitoring / SCADA
  Platform".

This subprocess identifies every path by which a fault or condition
exception can enter the maintenance process — operator report, automated
alarm, or preventive schedule — and validates the signal against asset
criticality thresholds before confirming it. False alarms are closed
without escalation. A confirmed detection event, carrying a structured
fault description and operating context, is handed to Raise and Triage
Notification for work-order creation and prioritisation.
```


### V15.02 — Raise & Triage Notification

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.02 Raise & Triage Notification — second subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, converting an incoming fault signal into a
triaged, prioritised notification ready for criticality and safety assessment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation receiving, raising, and
triaging the notification; white-box pool containing all lanes.
  Lane "Maintenance" — maintenance planner who logs and triages the
  notification.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — external party who reported the fault or
condition exception.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — system of record for
notifications and work orders.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Fault signal or condition exception received from
  Detect Fault or Condition Exception"
  User task "Review incoming fault signal and operator report"
  User task "Create notification record in EAM"
  Service task "Retrieve asset register and maintenance history from EAM"
  User task "Classify notification type (fault report, alarm, inspection
  finding, PM schedule)"
  User task "Capture fault symptoms, operating context, and asset details"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to triage?"
    - branch "No — information incomplete":
        Send task "Request additional details from Equipment Operator"
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional details received from
        Equipment Operator"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to
        triage")
    - branch "Yes — information complete":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to
        triage")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to triage"
  User task "Assign initial priority and urgency category"
  User task "Allocate notification to responsible Maintenance team"
  Service task "Update notification status and priority in EAM"
  Exclusive gateway "Notification valid and actionable?"
    - branch "Invalid or duplicate — close notification":
        User task "Document reason and close notification in EAM"
        End event "Notification closed — no further action required"
    - branch "Valid — proceed to assessment":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Notification valid and
        actionable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Notification valid and actionable"
  End event "Triaged notification confirmed — ready for Assess Criticality
  and Safety Impact"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Create notification
record in EAM" — label "Acknowledgement overdue (target window elapsed)"
— triggers Send task "Send fault acknowledgement to Equipment Operator"
which flows to an End event "Acknowledgement sent — boundary path
complete".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Maintenance lane at the message start
event and flows through review, notification creation, asset data
retrieval, classification, symptom capture, and the "Sufficient
information" gateway. The incomplete branch sends a request to the
Equipment Operator and waits for a reply before rejoining at the merge
gateway. After the merge, priority assignment, team allocation, and EAM
status update lead to the "Notification valid and actionable" gateway. The
invalid branch closes the notification and ends; the valid branch rejoins
at its merge gateway and continues to the final end event.

Message flows:
Equipment Operator → Maintenance lane (fault signal, symptoms, and
operating context — arriving at message start event)
Maintenance lane → Equipment Operator (request for additional fault
details — from Send task "Request additional details from Equipment
Operator")
Equipment Operator → Maintenance lane (additional details reply —
arriving at intermediate message catch event "Additional details received
from Equipment Operator")
Maintenance lane → Equipment Operator (fault acknowledgement — from
boundary-triggered Send task "Send fault acknowledgement to Equipment
Operator")
Maintenance lane → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (create
notification record — from User task "Create notification record in EAM")
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Maintenance lane (asset register,
maintenance history — to Service task "Retrieve asset register and
maintenance history from EAM")
Maintenance lane → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (priority, status,
and team allocation update — from Service task "Update notification status
and priority in EAM")
Maintenance lane → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (notification
closure record — from User task "Document reason and close notification in
EAM")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Fault Signal / Condition Exception Report" — read by User
task "Review incoming fault signal and operator report"; written by
Message start event "Fault signal or condition exception received from
Detect Fault or Condition Exception".
Data Object "Notification Record" — written by User task "Create
notification record in EAM"; read by User task "Classify notification type
(fault report, alarm, inspection finding, PM schedule)".
Data Object "Asset Register and Maintenance History" — written by Service
task "Retrieve asset register and maintenance history from EAM"; read by
User task "Capture fault symptoms, operating context, and asset details".
Data Object "Triaged Notification" — written by Service task "Update
notification status and priority in EAM"; read by End event "Triaged
notification confirmed — ready for Assess Criticality and Safety Impact".

This subprocess converts a raw fault signal or operator report into a
structured, prioritised notification logged in the EAM system. The planner
gathers sufficient symptom and asset context, assigns an urgency category,
and allocates the work to the right Maintenance team, discarding any
invalid or duplicate entries. The output — a validated, triaged
notification with priority and team assignment — is handed to Assess
Criticality and Safety Impact for detailed risk evaluation.
```


### V15.03 — Assess Criticality & Safety Impact

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.03 Assess Criticality & Safety Impact — third subprocess in the
Detect to Repair value chain, receiving a triaged notification from Raise &
Triage Notification and handing a criticality-assessed work order to Diagnose
Fault.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation performing the assessment,
  with two lanes: Reliability Engineering and Health & Safety.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — the EAM system used to read asset
  data and record assessment outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Owner Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Reliability Engineering
   top, Health & Safety below)
2. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Reliability Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Triaged notification received from Raise & Triage
    Notification"
  Service task "Retrieve asset register and maintenance history"
  User task "Classify asset criticality"
  Exclusive gateway "Criticality level?"
  - branch "Safety-critical": Send task "Notify Health & Safety for safety
      impact review"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Criticality level?")
  - branch "Non-safety-critical": User task "Document criticality
      classification"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Criticality level?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Criticality level?"
  Intermediate message catch event "Safety impact review outcome received"
  User task "Review consolidated criticality and safety outcome"
  Exclusive gateway "Assessment outcome acceptable?"
  - branch "Rework required": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Assessment
      Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Revise
      criticality inputs", User task "Re-evaluate classification"
      (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Accepted": User task "Record final criticality rating and risk
      classification"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Assessment outcome acceptable?"
  Service task "Update work order with criticality rating in EAM"
  End event "Criticality and safety assessment complete — ready for
    Diagnose Fault"

Health & Safety lane:
  User task "Conduct safety impact review"
  User task "Apply permit-to-work and isolation requirements"
  User task "Record safety constraints and lock-out/tag-out requirements"
  Send task "Return safety impact review outcome to Reliability Engineering"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Assessment Complete" — label "Assessment deadline exceeded" — triggers
  End event "Assessment escalated — time limit reached".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Reliability Engineering lane with the
message start event, proceeds through asset retrieval and criticality
classification, then splits at the "Criticality level?" exclusive gateway;
the safety-critical branch sends a notification to Health & Safety and
continues to the merge gateway, while the non-safety-critical branch
documents the classification and also continues to the merge gateway; after
the merge, flow pauses at the intermediate message catch event awaiting the
Health & Safety outcome, then advances to review and the "Assessment outcome
acceptable?" gateway; the rework branch enters the standard-loop subprocess
and exits to the merge gateway, the accepted branch goes directly to the
merge gateway; flow then continues to EAM update and the end event. In the
Health & Safety lane, tasks run in sequence — safety review, permit
requirements, recording constraints, and returning the outcome — triggered
by the send task in Reliability Engineering.

Message flows:
  Reliability Engineering "Retrieve asset register and maintenance history"
    → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (asset register and maintenance
    history request)
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Reliability Engineering "Retrieve
    asset register and maintenance history" (asset record, hierarchy, and
    maintenance history data)
  Reliability Engineering "Update work order with criticality rating in EAM"
    → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (criticality rating, risk
    classification, safety constraints written to work order)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Triaged Notification" — read by "Classify asset criticality".
Data Object "Asset Criticality Classification" — written by "Classify asset
  criticality"; read by "Review consolidated criticality and safety outcome".
Data Object "Safety Impact Review Record" — written by "Record safety
  constraints and lock-out/tag-out requirements"; read by "Review
  consolidated criticality and safety outcome".
Data Object "Final Criticality and Risk Assessment" — written by "Record
  final criticality rating and risk classification"; read by "Update work
  order with criticality rating in EAM".

This subprocess takes the triaged notification produced by Raise & Triage
Notification and establishes the asset's criticality level and any safety
constraints that must govern subsequent work. Reliability Engineering
classifies the asset using the EAM register and maintenance history, while
Health & Safety reviews safety impact and sets permit-to-work and isolation
requirements. The agreed criticality rating and safety constraints are
written back to the work order in EAM, equipping the Diagnose Fault
subprocess with the risk context it needs to direct the right level of
diagnostic effort.
```


### V15.04 — Diagnose Fault

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.04 Diagnose Fault — fourth subprocess in the Detect to Repair
value chain, receiving a triaged and criticality-assessed notification and
producing a confirmed diagnosis ready for work planning.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the maintaining organisation running the
diagnosis process, with lanes for Maintenance and Reliability Engineering.
Pool "Original Equipment Manufacturer" — external specialist providing
remote or on-site diagnostic support.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — system of record for work
orders, asset history, failure codes, and diagnosis records.
Pool "Document Management System" — system holding drawings, manuals,
and technical specifications used during diagnosis.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Original Equipment Manufacturer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Original Equipment Manufacturer
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
4. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane (maintenance technician):

Message start event "Assessed notification received from Assess
Criticality & Safety Impact"
User task "Review asset history and prior fault records"
Service task "Retrieve maintenance history and failure codes from EAM"
User task "Inspect asset and gather fault symptoms"
Service task "Retrieve drawings and technical manuals"
Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to diagnose?"
- branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
  information to diagnose")
- branch "No — OEM input required": Send task "Request diagnostic
  support from OEM"
  Intermediate message catch event "OEM diagnostic response received"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to
  diagnose")
Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to diagnose"
User task "Formulate preliminary diagnosis"
Send task "Send preliminary diagnosis to Reliability Engineering for
review"

Reliability Engineering lane (reliability engineer):

Intermediate message catch event "Preliminary diagnosis received from
Maintenance"
User task "Review and validate preliminary diagnosis"
Exclusive gateway "Diagnosis confirmed?"
- branch "Confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Diagnosis
  confirmed")
- branch "Requires further investigation": User task "Conduct
  additional analysis and root-cause investigation"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Diagnosis confirmed")
Exclusive merge gateway "Diagnosis confirmed"
User task "Record confirmed diagnosis and failure codes in EAM"
User task "Classify fault type and failure mode"
End event "Confirmed diagnosis recorded — ready for Plan Work & Parts"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Inspect asset and
gather fault symptoms" — label "Inspection time limit exceeded" —
triggers Send task "Escalate inspection delay to asset manager";
flow ends at a standalone End event "Inspection escalated".
Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch
event "OEM diagnostic response received" — label "OEM response
overdue" — triggers User task "Chase OEM for diagnostic input";
flow rejoins at exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to
diagnose".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Maintenance lane with the message
start event, proceeds through asset-history retrieval, asset
inspection, and the gateway testing whether information is sufficient;
the OEM-input branch sends a request, awaits a reply, then rejoins the
merge gateway; both branches continue to preliminary diagnosis
formulation and dispatch to Reliability Engineering; the Reliability
Engineering lane picks up with validation, the confirmation gateway
branches to additional analysis or directly to the merge gateway, then
proceeds through EAM recording and fault classification to the end
event.

Message flows:
Asset Owner Organisation (Send task "Request diagnostic support from
OEM") → Original Equipment Manufacturer (diagnostic support request).
Original Equipment Manufacturer → Asset Owner Organisation
(Intermediate message catch event "OEM diagnostic response received")
(diagnostic findings and recommendations).
Asset Owner Organisation (Service task "Retrieve maintenance history
and failure codes from EAM") → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
(history and failure code query).
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Asset Owner Organisation (Service
task "Retrieve maintenance history and failure codes from EAM")
(asset maintenance history and failure codes).
Asset Owner Organisation (Service task "Retrieve drawings and technical
manuals") → Document Management System (drawings and manuals request).
Document Management System → Asset Owner Organisation (Service task
"Retrieve drawings and technical manuals") (technical drawings and
manuals).
Asset Owner Organisation (User task "Record confirmed diagnosis and
failure codes in EAM") → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (confirmed
diagnosis record and failure codes).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assessed Notification" — read by User task "Review asset
history and prior fault records".
Data Object "Maintenance History & Failure Codes" — written by Service
task "Retrieve maintenance history and failure codes from EAM"; read
by User task "Formulate preliminary diagnosis".
Data Object "Technical Drawings & Manuals" — written by Service task
"Retrieve drawings and technical manuals"; read by User task "Inspect
asset and gather fault symptoms".
Data Object "OEM Diagnostic Report" — written by Intermediate message
catch event "OEM diagnostic response received"; read by User task
"Formulate preliminary diagnosis".
Data Object "Preliminary Diagnosis" — written by User task "Formulate
preliminary diagnosis"; read by User task "Review and validate
preliminary diagnosis".
Data Object "Confirmed Diagnosis Record" — written by User task
"Record confirmed diagnosis and failure codes in EAM"; read by User
task "Classify fault type and failure mode".

This subprocess takes the assessed and prioritised notification from
Assess Criticality & Safety Impact, assembles asset history, technical
documentation, and where necessary OEM expertise, and produces a
validated diagnosis with failure codes recorded in EAM. The confirmed
diagnosis, fault type, and failure mode classification are handed to
Plan Work & Parts, enabling the maintenance planner and storeperson to
determine the scope of repair and the parts required.
```


### V15.05 — Plan Work & Parts

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.05 Plan Work & Parts — fifth subprocess in the Detect to
Repair value chain, receiving a diagnosed fault from Diagnose Fault and
handing a fully planned work package to Schedule Work & Secure Permits.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the internal teams that plan the repair
  work and arrange parts.
  Lane "Maintenance" — maintenance planner who owns the work plan.
  Lane "Spare Parts" — storeperson who checks and issues parts.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — system of record for work
  orders, asset data, and parts reservations.
Pool "Spare Parts Inventory System" — system that holds stock levels,
  reservations, and replenishment records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Spare Parts Inventory System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — top (white-box process pool).
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — below Asset Owner Organisation.
Pool "Spare Parts Inventory System" — below Enterprise Asset Management.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane:
  Message start event "Diagnosed fault received from Diagnose Fault"
  User task "Review diagnosis and define scope of work"
  User task "Select maintenance strategy and repair method"
  User task "Identify required parts, materials and special tools"
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and maintenance records from EAM"
  User task "Draft work plan with task sequence and labour estimate"
  Service task "Create or update work order in EAM"
  Exclusive gateway "Parts required?"
  - branch "No parts required": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Parts required?")
  - branch "Parts required": Send task "Request parts availability
    check" then flow continues to Spare Parts lane and returns;
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Parts required?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Parts required?"
  User task "Finalise work plan with resource and duration estimate"
  User task "Attach drawings, manuals and work instructions to work order"
  Service task "Update work order status to Planned in EAM"
  End event "Work plan complete — ready for Schedule Work & Secure Permits"

Spare Parts lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Parts availability check request
    received"
  Service task "Query parts stock levels and locations in Spare Parts
    Inventory System"
  Exclusive gateway "Parts in stock?"
  - branch "In stock": User task "Reserve required parts against work
    order"
    Service task "Record reservation in Spare Parts Inventory System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Parts in stock?")
  - branch "Not in stock": User task "Identify alternative source or
    raise replenishment or purchase request"
    Intermediate message catch event "Parts sourcing confirmed"
    Service task "Record expected availability in Spare Parts Inventory
      System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Parts in stock?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Parts in stock?"
  Send task "Send parts status and reservation confirmation to Maintenance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on "Draft work plan with task
  sequence and labour estimate" — label "Planning overdue (48 h)" —
  triggers escalation Send task "Notify asset manager of planning delay"
  which flows to an End event "Planning delay escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Maintenance lane at the message start
  event, proceeds through review, strategy selection, parts identification,
  asset history retrieval, work drafting, work order creation, then to
  the "Parts required?" gateway. The "No parts required" branch rejoins
  immediately at the merge. The "Parts required?" branch triggers the
  Send task whose message crosses to the Spare Parts lane; the Spare Parts
  lane processes the "Parts in stock?" gateway, with the "In stock" branch
  reserving stock and the "Not in stock" branch sourcing parts and awaiting
  confirmation, both rejoining at the "Parts in stock?" merge, then the
  Send task returns confirmation back to the Maintenance lane as a message
  caught by the Intermediate message catch event that allows the
  Maintenance lane to continue to the merge gateway "Parts required?".
  After the merge, Maintenance finalises the work plan, attaches
  documentation, updates EAM, and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and maintenance records from EAM"
    → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (asset history and maintenance
    record query).
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Service task "Retrieve asset history
    and maintenance records from EAM" (asset history, failure codes,
    maintenance records returned).
  Service task "Create or update work order in EAM" → Enterprise Asset
    Management (EAM) (new or updated work order data).
  Service task "Update work order status to Planned in EAM" →
    Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (work order status update to
    Planned).
  Service task "Query parts stock levels and locations in Spare Parts
    Inventory System" → Spare Parts Inventory System (stock query by
    part number and quantity).
  Spare Parts Inventory System → Service task "Query parts stock levels
    and locations in Spare Parts Inventory System" (stock levels and
    bin locations returned).
  Service task "Record reservation in Spare Parts Inventory System" →
    Spare Parts Inventory System (parts reservation record).
  Service task "Record expected availability in Spare Parts Inventory
    System" → Spare Parts Inventory System (expected availability and
    sourcing note).
  Send task "Request parts availability check" → Intermediate message
    catch event "Parts availability check request received" (parts
    availability check request).
  Send task "Send parts status and reservation confirmation to
    Maintenance" → Maintenance lane (parts status and reservation
    confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Diagnosed Fault Record" — read by User task "Review
  diagnosis and define scope of work".
Data Object "Work Plan" — written by User task "Draft work plan with
  task sequence and labour estimate"; read by User task "Finalise work
  plan with resource and duration estimate".
Data Object "Work Order" — written by Service task "Create or update
  work order in EAM"; read by Service task "Update work order status
  to Planned in EAM"; read by User task "Attach drawings, manuals and
  work instructions to work order".
Data Object "Parts Requirement List" — written by User task "Identify
  required parts, materials and special tools"; read by Send task
  "Request parts availability check".
Data Object "Parts Reservation Confirmation" — written by Send task
  "Send parts status and reservation confirmation to Maintenance"; read
  by User task "Finalise work plan with resource and duration estimate".

Plan Work & Parts converts the diagnosed fault into a fully scoped,
documented work order. It determines the repair method, identifies every
part and special tool needed, resolves stock availability through
reservation or sourcing, and attaches all technical references to the
work order. The completed, Planned-status work order is then handed to
Schedule Work & Secure Permits for resource booking and permit
authorisation.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.06 Schedule Work & Secure Permits — the subprocess that turns
an approved work plan into a confirmed schedule, contracted resources, and
valid permits, readying the repair team to execute work safely.

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation planning, scheduling,
  and permitting the repair work.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Planning & Scheduling (scheduler)

Pool "Service Contractor" — black-box, single instance.

Pool "Work Order Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Service Contractor
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Permit-to-Work System

Planning & Scheduling lane:
  Message start event "Approved work plan received from Plan Work & Parts"
  User task "Review work plan and resource requirements"
  Service task "Check technician and contractor availability"

  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Contractor Required")

  Send task "Notify Health and Safety of scheduled work and isolation needs"

Health & Safety lane:

  - branch "No — amendment needed":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Permit Acceptable" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Request permit amendment",
      Send task "Send amendment request to Permit-to-Work System",
      Intermediate message catch event "Amended permit received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Permit Acceptable")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Permit Acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Permit Acceptable"
  User task "Brief maintenance team and contractor on permit conditions"
  User task "Confirm permit activated and site ready"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Draft schedule and assign

This subprocess converts an approved work plan into a locked-in schedule
with confirmed contractor availability, updated work order assignments, and
```
