```text
event and flows through briefing, the contractor gateway and its merge,
isolation, the looping repair subprocess, reinstatement, the outcome
gateway and its merge, and cost posting; the Field Service lane runs
in parallel after the contractor arrival confirmation, from site
attendance through specialist activities to completion report
submission and the end event; the timer boundary escalation path
rejoins the main Maintenance flow before reinstatement.

Message flows:
  Maintenance lane "Issue work instructions and site access to
    contractor" → Service Contractor (work instructions and access
    details).
  Service Contractor → Maintenance lane "Contractor arrival
    confirmed" (arrival confirmation).
  Service Contractor → Field Service lane "Attend site and sign in
    under permit conditions" (contractor personnel on site).
  Field Service lane "Submit completion report and handover to
    Maintenance" → Service Contractor (completion report copy for
    contractor records).
  Maintenance lane "Update work order progress in Work Order
    Management System" → Work Order Management System (progress
    updates and step records).
  Maintenance lane "Post labour and material usage to Work Order
    Management System" → Work Order Management System (labour
    entries and material consumption).
  Work Order Management System → Maintenance lane "Retrieve work
    order and repair instructions" (work order details and repair
    instructions).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Work Order" — read by "Retrieve work order and repair
  instructions"; written by "Update work order progress in Work Order
  Management System"; written by "Post labour and material usage to
  Work Order Management System".
Data Object "Repair Instructions" — read by "Brief technicians and
  confirm materials available"; read by "Execute repair step per work
  instructions".
Data Object "Step Inspection Record" — written by "Inspect completed
  step and record findings"; read by "Post labour and material usage
  to Work Order Management System".
Data Object "Field Completion Report" — written by "Prepare field
  completion report"; read by "Post labour and material usage to
  Work Order Management System".

This subprocess mobilises in-house technicians and any approved
contractor, physically executes the repair under permit and lock-out/
tag-out controls, and records step-by-step progress and resource
consumption against the work order. On completion it hands a fully
updated work order and field completion report to Test & Return to
Service, giving that subprocess the evidence needed to verify asset
condition and authorise return to operation.
```


### V15.08 — Test & Return to Service

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.08 Test & Return to Service — the subprocess in which the
maintenance team verifies the repaired asset, obtains operational acceptance
from the equipment operator, and formally returns the asset to service within
the Detect to Repair value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation carrying out the test and
return-to-service activities, with lanes for Maintenance and Operations.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — the external party that confirms the asset is
ready to resume operation and accepts it back into service.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — the EAM system that records test
results, updates asset status, and closes out the return-to-service record.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Equipment Operator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Equipment Operator
2. Asset Owner Organisation
3. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane (maintenance technician):

Message start event "Repair completed — ready for Test & Return to Service"
User task "Review repair completion documentation"
User task "Prepare test plan and acceptance criteria"
Service task "Record test plan in EAM"
User task "Conduct post-repair functional tests"
Exclusive gateway "Tests passed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Tests passed")
  - branch "No": User task "Log test failure and identify remedial action"
    Exclusive gateway "Remedial action within maintenance scope?"
      - branch "Yes": Send task "Notify planner of rework requirement"
        End event "Rework required — return to Execute Repair"
      - branch "No": Send task "Escalate to reliability engineering"
        End event "Fault escalated — return to Diagnose Fault"
Exclusive merge gateway "Tests passed"
Service task "Update asset status to tested in EAM"
Send task "Notify Operations that asset is ready for operational acceptance"

Operations lane (operations supervisor):

Intermediate message catch event "Asset ready for operational acceptance"
User task "Review test results and asset condition"
User task "Conduct operational walkdown and sign-off"
Exclusive gateway "Operational acceptance granted?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Operational acceptance granted")
  - branch "No": User task "Document outstanding concerns"
    Send task "Return asset to Maintenance with concerns noted"
    Intermediate message catch event "Maintenance response received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Operational acceptance granted")
Exclusive merge gateway "Operational acceptance granted"
User task "Confirm access reinstatement and remove any isolation"
Send task "Issue return-to-service notification to Equipment Operator"
Service task "Post return-to-service record in EAM"
End event "Asset returned to service — ready for Close Work Order
& Capture Costs"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Conduct post-repair
functional tests", labelled "Test window exceeded", leading to User task
"Log test failure and identify remedial action" in the Maintenance lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Maintenance lane with the message start
event, proceeds through documentation review, test planning, and functional
testing. The "Tests passed?" gateway branches to either the merge gateway on
the yes path or to remedial action and escalation end events on the no paths.
On the yes path the merge gateway continues to asset status update and a
notify send task. Flow passes to the Operations lane via an intermediate
message catch event; the Operations lane runs through review, walkdown, and
the "Operational acceptance granted?" gateway, whose yes branch and the no
branch (after maintenance response) both rejoin at the acceptance merge
gateway. From that merge the flow continues through isolation reinstatement,
operator notification, EAM posting, and the end event.

Message flows:
Maintenance lane "Send task — Notify Operations that asset is ready for
operational acceptance" → Operations lane "Intermediate message catch event —
Asset ready for operational acceptance" (asset ready notification).
Operations lane "Send task — Return asset to Maintenance with concerns noted"
→ Maintenance lane "Intermediate message catch event — Maintenance response
received" (outstanding concerns and rework notes).
Operations lane "Send task — Issue return-to-service notification to Equipment
Operator" → Equipment Operator (return-to-service notification).
Equipment Operator → Operations lane "User task — Conduct operational walkdown
and sign-off" (operator access confirmation and operating context).
Service task "Record test plan in EAM" → Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
(test plan data).
Service task "Update asset status to tested in EAM" → Enterprise Asset
Management (EAM) (test result and status update).
Service task "Post return-to-service record in EAM" → Enterprise Asset
Management (EAM) (return-to-service record and asset history update).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Repair Completion Documentation" — read by "Review repair
completion documentation".
Data Object "Test Plan" — written by "Prepare test plan and acceptance
criteria"; read by "Conduct post-repair functional tests".
Data Object "Test Results Record" — written by "Conduct post-repair functional
tests"; read by "Review test results and asset condition".
Data Object "Operational Acceptance Sign-off" — written by "Conduct
operational walkdown and sign-off"; read by "Post return-to-service record
in EAM".
Data Object "Return-to-Service Notification" — written by "Issue
return-to-service notification to Equipment Operator".

This subprocess takes the completed repair from Execute Repair and puts the
asset through structured functional testing and operational acceptance checks.
Failures that cannot be resolved within scope are routed back to earlier
subprocesses, while successful acceptance produces a fully updated EAM record
and a formal return-to-service notification. The subprocess hands a confirmed,
in-service asset and its updated work-order record to Close Work Order &
Capture Costs.
```


### V15.09 — Close Work Order & Capture Costs

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V15.09 Close Work Order & Capture Costs — the ninth subprocess in
the Detect to Repair value chain, closing the work order and posting all
labour, materials, and contractor costs to the financial ledger.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — the organisation executing the close-out
and cost-capture process, containing the Maintenance and Finance lanes.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — the EAM system that holds the
work order, asset history, and failure codes.
Pool "Finance / ERP System" — the finance and ERP system that receives cost
postings and applies capitalisation or expense rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Asset Owner Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Finance / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Asset Owner Organisation (white-box)
2. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
3. Finance / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Asset Owner Organisation)

Maintenance lane (maintenance planner):
  Message start event "Repair completion confirmed — received from Test &
    Return to Service"
  User task "Review work order for completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Work order data complete?"
  - branch "No — data missing":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Work Order Complete" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Identify and fill data gaps",
        User task "Update work order in EAM"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Work order data complete")
  - branch "Yes — complete":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Work order data complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Work order data complete"
  User task "Record failure codes and fault description in EAM"
  User task "Confirm labour hours and materials consumed"
  User task "Attach completion documents and close work order in EAM"
  Intermediate message catch event "Cost posting confirmation received"

  Exclusive gateway "Costs within acceptable variance?"
  - branch "Yes — within tolerance":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Cost variance check")
  - branch "No — variance requires review":
      User task "Raise cost query and seek approval"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Cost variance check")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Cost variance check"
  User task "Finalise work order closure and notify stakeholders"
  End event "Work order closed and costs captured — ready for Analyse
    Failure Causes"

Finance lane (asset accountant):
  Intermediate message catch event "Work order cost data received from EAM"
  User task "Apply capitalisation versus expense classification rules"
  User task "Post labour, materials, and contractor costs to financial

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Work
Order Complete" — label "72-hour closure deadline exceeded" — triggers End
event "Work order escalated — closure overdue".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Maintenance lane, flow moves from the message
start event through the completeness review, the "Work order data complete?"
gateway (with its loop subprocess on the "No" branch and a direct path on
the "Yes" branch, both rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway), then
through failure-code recording, labour and materials confirmation, and work

until the Finance lane returns a cost posting confirmation; flow then
continues through cost review, the variance gateway (the "No" branch raising

posting, and the send task.

Message flows:
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Maintenance lane "Attach completion
  documents and close work order in EAM" (work order record updated and
  closure acknowledged).
Maintenance lane "Record failure codes and fault description in EAM" →
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (failure codes and fault description).
Maintenance lane "Confirm labour hours and materials consumed" →
  Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (labour hours and materials consumed).
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → Finance lane intermediate message
  catch event "Work order cost data received from EAM" (work order cost

Finance lane "Post labour, materials, and contractor costs to financial

Finance / ERP System → Finance lane "Post labour, materials, and contractor
  costs to financial ledger" (ledger confirmation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Work Order" — read by "Review work order for completeness";
written by "Attach completion documents and close work order in EAM".
Data Object "Failure Code Record" — written by "Record failure codes and
fault description in EAM"; read by "Finalise work order closure and notify
stakeholders".
Data Object "Labour and Materials Consumption Record" — written by "Confirm
labour hours and materials consumed"; read by "Post labour, materials, and
contractor costs to financial ledger".
Data Object "Cost Posting Report" — written by "Post labour, materials, and
contractor costs to financial ledger"; read by "Review posted costs against
work order estimate".
Data Object "Completion Documents" — read by "Attach completion documents
and close work order in EAM".

This subprocess closes the active work order by verifying data completeness,
recording failure codes, and confirming all resource consumption before
locking the order in EAM. The Finance lane applies capitalisation or expense
rules and posts all costs — labour, materials, and contractor charges — to
the financial ledger. A confirmed, costed, and closed work order is handed
to Analyse Failure Causes, giving the reliability team a complete record
from which to draw conclusions about failure modes and prevention.
```

### V15.10 — Analyse Failure Causes

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

1. Asset Owner Organisation
2. Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
3. Reliability Analytics Platform

Reliability Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Closed work order received from Close Work Order
  & Capture Costs"
  Service task "Retrieve asset history and failure codes from EAM"

    - branch "Yes — root cause identified":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "RCA outcome sufficient")

        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "RCA outcome sufficient")
  Exclusive merge gateway "RCA outcome sufficient"
  User task "Classify failure mode and assign failure code"
  Service task "Record failure classification in EAM"
  User task "Identify corrective and preventive actions"
  Exclusive gateway "Actions require management approval?"
    - branch "Yes":
        User task "Prepare RCA report and recommendations for
        management review"
        Intermediate message catch event "Management decision received"
        Exclusive gateway "Management approved?"
          - branch "Approved":
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Management approved")
          - branch "Rejected — revise":
              User task "Revise recommendations and resubmit"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Management approved")
        Exclusive merge gateway "Management approved"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Actions require
        management approval")
    - branch "No — analyst authority":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Actions require
        management approval")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Actions require management approval"
  Service task "Raise improvement actions and preventive maintenance
  updates in EAM"
  Service task "Update failure mode and reliability models in Reliability
  Analytics Platform"
  User task "Communicate findings to Maintenance and Operations"
  End event "Failure analysis complete — improvement actions issued and
  asset record updated"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Reliability Engineering
lane. After the start event, asset history is retrieved, data is
extracted, and evidence is reviewed before root-cause analysis begins.
The "RCA outcome sufficient?" gateway branches to either the loop
subprocess (insufficient data) or directly to the merge; both paths
rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway. Failure classification and EAM
recording follow, then corrective actions are identified. The "Actions
require management approval?" gateway branches to the approval path
(including the nested "Management approved?" gateway and its merge) or
directly to its merge; both paths continue to raising improvement
actions in EAM, updating the analytics platform, and communicating
findings before the end event.

Message flows:
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → "Retrieve asset history and failure
codes from EAM" (asset history, failure codes, closed work-order
records)
Reliability Analytics Platform → "Extract reliability and downtime data
from Reliability Analytics Platform" (reliability statistics, downtime
trends, FMEA data)
Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) → "Retrieve supplementary records
from EAM" (additional maintenance history, inspection records)
"Record failure classification in EAM" → Enterprise Asset Management
(EAM) (failure mode classification and updated failure code)
"Raise improvement actions and preventive maintenance updates in EAM"
→ Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) (corrective action records,
revised preventive maintenance schedule)
"Update failure mode and reliability models in Reliability Analytics
Platform" → Reliability Analytics Platform (updated failure mode
data, revised reliability model inputs)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Closed Work Order" — read by "Review failure codes and
symptom data".
Data Object "Root-Cause Analysis Report" — written by "Conduct
root-cause analysis"; read by "Prepare RCA report and recommendations
for management review"; read by "Communicate findings to Maintenance
and Operations".
Data Object "Corrective and Preventive Action Register" — written by
"Identify corrective and preventive actions"; read by "Raise improvement
actions and preventive maintenance updates in EAM".

This subprocess converts the closed work-order record into structured
reliability knowledge by performing root-cause analysis, classifying
the failure mode, and issuing corrective and preventive actions back
into the asset management system. It updates the reliability analytics
platform with refined failure models and communicates findings to
Maintenance and Operations. By closing the learning loop, it feeds
improved preventive maintenance schedules and failure-mode libraries
back into the front end of the Detect to Repair chain, reducing the
likelihood and impact of recurrence.
```


## V16 — Detect to Respond

**Teams and roles involved.**
Detect to Respond usually involves Security Operations, Incident Response, IT Operations, Privacy/Data Protection, Legal, Risk and Compliance, Communications, and Executive Management, with Engineering teams drawn in for remediation. Key roles include security analyst, incident manager, threat hunter, forensic investigator, privacy officer, legal counsel, communications lead, service owner, and the executive incident sponsor.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Regulator and the Affected Individuals or Customers who must be notified where a breach is confirmed. The process is initiated by an alert from monitoring tooling, a report from staff or a customer, a third-party or law-enforcement notification, or a threat-intelligence advisory. Other external parties include managed security providers, forensic specialists, cyber insurers, law enforcement, and affected suppliers or partners.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: detect the event, triage and validate it, declare and classify the incident, contain the threat, investigate and preserve evidence, assess data and privacy impact, notify regulators and affected parties, eradicate and recover, confirm service restoration, and conduct a post-incident review with remediation actions.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include SIEM and log aggregation, endpoint and network detection and response, vulnerability management, identity and access management, case and incident management, forensic tooling, threat intelligence platforms, IT service management, secure communications and war-room tooling, and GRC/risk registers.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the incident response plan and severity matrix, breach notification obligations and statutory timeframes, evidence handling and chain-of-custody procedure, containment authority and emergency change rules, privacy impact assessment procedure, communications and disclosure policy, third-party notification obligations, insurance notification terms, and post-incident review requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Regulators receive breach notifications, impact assessments and remediation plans, and provide directions or findings. Affected individuals receive notification of what happened, what data was involved, and what they should do. Third parties provide threat intelligence, forensic findings, and their own breach notifications. The process provides status updates to executives, customers and partners throughout.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates incident records, timelines, evidence artefacts, containment and remediation actions, impact assessments, notifications, and risk-register entries. IT systems provide alerts and correlated events, log and telemetry evidence, asset and data classification, identity and access history, vulnerability and patch state, and incident metrics for reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V16.01** Detect Event | Managed Security Provider | Security Operations (security analyst) | SIEM Platform, Endpoint Detection & Response |
| **V16.02** Triage & Validate | — | Security Operations (security analyst) | SIEM Platform, Case Management System |
| **V16.03** Declare & Classify Incident | — | Incident Response (incident manager), Executive Management (executive sponsor) | Case Management System |
| **V16.04** Contain Threat | — | Incident Response (incident manager), IT Operations (service owner) | Endpoint Detection & Response, Identity & Access Management |
| **V16.05** Investigate & Preserve Evidence | Forensic Specialist | Incident Response (forensic investigator) | Forensic Tooling, SIEM Platform |
| **V16.06** Assess Data & Privacy Impact | — | Privacy (privacy officer), Legal (legal counsel) | Case Management System, GRC Platform |
| **V16.07** Notify Regulators & Affected Parties | Regulator, Affected Individual | Legal (legal counsel), Communications (communications lead) | Case Management System |
| **V16.08** Eradicate & Recover | — | IT Operations (service owner), Incident Response (incident manager) | IT Service Management, Endpoint Detection & Response |
| **V16.09** Confirm Service Restoration | — | IT Operations (service owner), Security Operations (security analyst) | IT Service Management |
| **V16.10** Conduct Post-Incident Review | Cyber Insurer | Risk & Compliance (risk manager), Incident Response (incident manager) | GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V16):

- **External actors:** Managed Security Provider (V16.01); Forensic Specialist (V16.05); Regulator (V16.07); Affected Individual (V16.07); Cyber Insurer (V16.10).
- **Teams:** Security Operations (V16.01, V16.02, V16.09); Incident Response (V16.03–V16.05, V16.08, V16.10); Executive Management (V16.03); IT Operations (V16.04, V16.08, V16.09); Privacy (V16.06); Legal (V16.06, V16.07); Communications (V16.07); Risk & Compliance (V16.10).
- **IT systems:** SIEM Platform (V16.01, V16.02, V16.05); Endpoint Detection & Response (V16.01, V16.04, V16.08); Case Management System (V16.02, V16.03, V16.06, V16.07); Identity & Access Management (V16.04); Forensic Tooling (V16.05); GRC Platform (V16.06, V16.10); IT Service Management (V16.08, V16.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V16 — Detect to Respond — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Detect to Respond value chain, from initial event detection through
to post-incident review. The diagram is arranged in three horizontal bands,
top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES → BUSINESS PROCESSES → APPLICATIONS. The
demand-side actor (Managed Security Provider, plus staff and customer
report sources) sits on the far left; delivery and settlement actors
(Regulator, Affected Individual, Cyber Insurer, Forensic Specialist) sit
on the far right. The view is read top-to-bottom as service → process →
application, following ArchiMate service realisation conventions.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Managed Security Provider — far left; initiates detection by supplying
  alerts and threat intelligence into V16.01.
- Forensic Specialist — far right; engaged externally during V16.05 to
  supply forensic findings.
- Regulator — far right; receives breach notifications and issues
  directions in V16.07.
- Affected Individual — far right; receives breach notifications and
  guidance in V16.07.
- Cyber Insurer — far right; receives post-incident reporting and review
  outputs in V16.10.

2. Interfaces

- Security Alert Interface — ACCESSED by Managed Security Provider;
  SERVES the Event Detection Service and V16.01 Detect Event.
- Forensic Findings Interface — ACCESSED by Forensic Specialist; SERVES
  the Investigation & Evidence Service and V16.05.
- Breach Notification Interface — ACCESSED by Regulator and Affected
  Individual; SERVES the Notification Service and V16.07.
- Insurer Reporting Interface — ACCESSED by Cyber Insurer; SERVES the
  Post-Incident Review Service and V16.10.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Event Detection Service — provides continuous monitoring and alert
  ingestion, delivering confirmed candidate security events for triage.
- Triage & Validation Service — provides rapid assessment of candidate
  events to confirm or dismiss them as genuine incidents.
- Incident Declaration Service — provides formal classification and
  severity assignment, mobilising the incident response structure.
- Threat Containment Service — provides authorised containment actions
  to limit the spread and impact of a confirmed threat.
- Investigation & Evidence Service — provides forensic investigation,
  log analysis, and chain-of-custody evidence preservation.
- Data & Privacy Impact Service — provides structured assessment of data
  exposure and privacy-breach obligations.
- Regulatory & Party Notification Service — provides timely, compliant
  notification to regulators and affected individuals.
- Eradication & Recovery Service — provides removal of threat artefacts
  and restoration of affected systems and services.
- Service Restoration Confirmation Service — provides formal verification
  that systems are clean and operating normally before stand-down.
- Post-Incident Review Service — provides structured lessons-learned,
  remediation planning, and risk-register updates.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V16.01 Detect Event — security analyst ingests and correlates alerts
  from monitoring tooling, the managed security provider, staff reports,
  and threat-intelligence advisories.
- V16.02 Triage & Validate — security analyst validates the alert,
  enriches it with context, and determines whether a genuine incident
  exists.
- V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident — incident manager formally declares
  the incident, assigns severity, and notifies the executive sponsor.
- V16.04 Contain Threat — incident manager and service owner execute
  containment actions including isolation, access revocation, and
  emergency changes.
- V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence — forensic investigator and
  external forensic specialist collect logs, artefacts, and timeline
  evidence under chain-of-custody controls.
- V16.06 Assess Data & Privacy Impact — privacy officer and legal counsel
  assess what data was involved, classify the breach, and determine
  notification obligations.
- V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties — legal counsel and
  communications lead draft and dispatch notifications to the regulator
  and affected individuals within statutory timeframes.
- V16.08 Eradicate & Recover — service owner and incident manager remove
  malicious artefacts, patch vulnerabilities, rebuild systems, and restore
  services.
- V16.09 Confirm Service Restoration — service owner and security analyst
  verify system integrity, close containment measures, and formally
  confirm restoration.
- V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review — risk manager and incident manager
  lead the post-incident review, document lessons learned, update the risk
  register, and report to the cyber insurer.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- SIEM Platform — provides log aggregation, event correlation, and alert
  generation; used in V16.01, V16.02, V16.05.
- Endpoint Detection & Response — provides endpoint and network threat
  detection, isolation capability, and telemetry; used in V16.01,
  V16.04, V16.08.
- Case Management System — provides incident record creation, workflow,
  timeline tracking, and notification drafting; used in V16.02, V16.03,
  V16.06, V16.07.
- Identity & Access Management — provides access history, account
  suspension, and credential revocation; used in V16.04.
- Forensic Tooling — provides forensic image acquisition, artefact
  analysis, and evidence preservation; used in V16.05.
- GRC Platform — provides risk-register entries, privacy impact
  assessment records, and post-incident findings; used in V16.06,
  V16.10.

  tracking, and incident closure; used in V16.08, V16.09.

6. Relationships

service):

ASSIGNMENT (business actor ASSIGNED TO interface):
```

```text
threat and coordinates the recovery sequence.

Executive Management — V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident: provides
executive sponsorship and authority to declare a major incident.

IT Operations — V16.04 Contain Threat: implements technical containment
measures across infrastructure and services.

patching, and service recovery steps.

or findings in return.

notification of the breach, data involved, and recommended protective
actions.

Risk & Compliance — V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review: leads the
post-incident review, updates the risk register, and tracks compliance with
remediation commitments.

Cyber Insurer — V16.10 Conduct Post-Incident Review: receives incident
summary and supporting evidence; provides findings or settlement guidance in
return.

The boundary contains all ten subprocesses of the Detect to Respond value
chain, from initial event detection through triage, declaration, containment,
investigation, privacy assessment, regulatory notification, eradication,
service restoration, and post-incident review. It serves internal teams
spanning Security Operations, Incident Response, IT Operations, Privacy,
Legal, Communications, Executive Management, and Risk & Compliance, as well
as external actors including the Managed Security Provider, Forensic
Specialist, Regulator, Affected Individual, and Cyber Insurer.
```
