**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V16 - Detect to Respond

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, one chevron per stage, in the
order listed below. The chevrons should flow continuously from left to
right across the diagram with no gaps between them.

V16.01. Detect Event
V16.02. Triage & Validate
V16.03. Declare & Classify Incident
V16.04. Contain Threat
V16.05. Investigate & Preserve Evidence
V16.06. Assess Data & Privacy Impact
V16.07. Notify Regulators & Affected Parties
V16.08. Eradicate & Recover
V16.09. Confirm Service Restoration
V16.10. Conduct Post-Incident Review

This chain covers the end-to-end organisational response to a security
event, from the moment an alert or report is first detected through
containment, investigation, mandatory notification, recovery, and
structured review. The chain is triggered by an inbound signal — from
monitoring tooling, a staff or customer report, a third-party advisory,
or a law-enforcement notification. The primary external participants are
the Regulator and Affected Individuals, who must be formally notified
where a breach is confirmed, and whose directions and responses shape
the later stages of the chain.
```
### V16.01 — Detect Event

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.01 Detect Event — first subprocess in the Detect to Respond
value chain, capturing every alert and report that opens a potential
security incident.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that receive and record
detected events.
  Lane "Security Operations" — security analyst who receives, reviews,
  and logs all incoming signals.
Pool "Managed Security Provider" — external managed security provider
that forwards alerts to the organisation.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — log aggregation and correlation system that
generates and stores alerts.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — EDR tooling that raises
endpoint and network alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Managed Security Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Managed Security Provider
2. Organisation
3. SIEM Platform
4. Endpoint Detection & Response

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security Operations lane:
  Multiple start event "Alert or report received from external source
  or monitoring tooling"
  Exclusive gateway "Source of signal?"
  - branch "SIEM-correlated alert": Intermediate message catch event
    "Correlated alert received from SIEM Platform"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Source of signal resolved")
  - branch "EDR alert": Intermediate message catch event "Endpoint or
    network alert received from Endpoint Detection & Response"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Source of signal resolved")
  - branch "Managed provider notification": Intermediate message catch
    event "Alert notification received from Managed Security Provider"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Source of signal resolved")
  - branch "Staff or customer report": User task "Receive and record
    manual report"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Source of signal resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Source of signal resolved"
  User task "Review signal and initial context"
  Service task "Log event in SIEM Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to proceed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Information
    check resolved")
  - branch "No": User task "Request additional context or log data"
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional context received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Information check resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Information check resolved"
  User task "Assign preliminary priority and categorise signal"
  Service task "Create initial event record in SIEM Platform"
  End event "Event detected and recorded — ready for Triage &
  Validate"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Request additional context or
log data" — label "Context request timeout (24 hours)" — if no
response arrives within 24 hours, flow proceeds to an End event
"Event escalated without full context — ready for Triage & Validate".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all flow within the Security Operations lane; the
exclusive gateway "Source of signal?" fans out to four branches that
each end at an intermediate message catch event or a user task before
rejoining at the merge gateway "Source of signal resolved"; flow then
continues linearly through review, logging, and the information-check
gateway before reaching the second merge and the final two tasks and
end event.

Message flows:
SIEM Platform → Security Operations (correlated alert or event
  notification)
Endpoint Detection & Response → Security Operations (endpoint or
  network detection alert)
Managed Security Provider → Security Operations (managed provider
  alert notification)
Security Operations → SIEM Platform (log event; create initial event
  record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incoming Alert or Report" — written by "Receive and
record manual report"; read by "Review signal and initial context".
Data Object "Initial Event Record" — written by "Create initial event
record in SIEM Platform"; read by "Assign preliminary priority and
categorise signal".

This subprocess captures every signal that could indicate a security
incident — whether from automated tooling, a managed provider, or a
human report — and produces a categorised, prioritised event record
in the SIEM Platform. By the time the flow ends, the Security
Operations team has enough structured information to hand to Triage &
Validate, where the signal will be assessed for validity and severity.
```


### V16.02 — Triage & Validate

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.02 Triage & Validate — second subprocess in the Detect to
Respond value chain, receiving a candidate security event from Detect Event
and handing a validated or dismissed finding to Declare & Classify Incident.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the team running the triage and validation process,
  with lanes for Security Operations.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — log aggregation and event correlation system.
Pool "Case Management System" — incident and case tracking system.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box)
2. SIEM Platform (black-box)
3. Case Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security Operations lane:
  Message start event "Alert or candidate event received from Detect Event"
  User task "Review incoming alert and initial context"
  Service task "Query correlated events and logs from SIEM Platform"
  User task "Assess alert fidelity and rule out false positive"
  Exclusive gateway "False positive?"
  - branch "Yes — false positive confirmed":
      User task "Document dismissal rationale"
      Service task "Close alert record in Case Management System"
      End event "Alert dismissed — no further action"
  - branch "No — potential true positive":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "False Positive")
  Exclusive merge gateway "False Positive"
  User task "Gather additional evidence and contextual indicators"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Sufficient Evidence Collected"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Identify gaps in evidence",
    Service task "Pull additional telemetry from SIEM Platform",
    User task "Evaluate whether evidence is sufficient"
  User task "Validate event against threat intelligence and asset context"
  Exclusive gateway "Event validated as credible security incident?"
  - branch "Yes — validated":
      User task "Assign preliminary severity rating"
      Service task "Create or update triage record in Case Management System"
      End event "Validated incident ready for Declare & Classify Incident"
  - branch "No — insufficient evidence, escalate for further review":
      User task "Log inconclusive finding and escalate for senior analyst"
      Service task "Record inconclusive status in Case Management System"
      End event "Inconclusive — escalated for analyst review"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Event Validated"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Sufficient Evidence Collected", labelled "Evidence collection time limit
  reached (4 hours)", leading to User task "Log inconclusive finding and
  escalate for senior analyst".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all sequence flows run within the Security Operations lane.
  From the message start event the flow moves through alert review, SIEM
  query, and false-positive assessment. The "False positive?" gateway
  branches to the dismissal path (which ends) and the validated path
  (which rejoins at the "False Positive" merge gateway). After the merge
  the flow enters the evidence-collection loop subprocess, then proceeds
  to validation and the "Event validated?" gateway, whose "Yes" branch
  ends at the validated end event and whose "No" branch ends at the
  escalation end event; neither branch rejoins the "Event Validated"
  merge gateway because both end independently. The "Event Validated"
  merge gateway is therefore reached only by flows that do not take an
  early end event; include it as drawn but note it is the logical merge
  point for any future branches added to this gateway.

Message flows:
  Security Operations → SIEM Platform (request for correlated events and
    log data)
  SIEM Platform → Security Operations (correlated event records and
    telemetry returned)
  Security Operations → SIEM Platform (request for additional telemetry
    during evidence loop)
  SIEM Platform → Security Operations (additional telemetry records
    returned during evidence loop)
  Security Operations → Case Management System (alert dismissal record
    or triage record written)
  Case Management System → Security Operations (confirmation of record
    creation or update)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Alert Record" — read by User task "Review incoming alert
  and initial context"; written by Service task "Close alert record in
  Case Management System".
Data Object "Triage Record" — written by Service task "Create or update
  triage record in Case Management System"; read by User task "Assign
  preliminary severity rating".
Data Object "Evidence Package" — written by User task "Gather additional
  evidence and contextual indicators"; read by User task "Validate event
  against threat intelligence and asset context".

V16.02 Triage & Validate takes the raw alert or candidate event surfaced
by Detect Event and puts it through a structured fidelity check, evidence
gathering loop, and validation step. False positives are closed and
documented immediately, while credible events are assigned a preliminary
severity and recorded as a validated incident. The subprocess hands a
completed triage record and severity rating to Declare & Classify Incident
so that the formal incident lifecycle can begin.
```


### V16.03 — Declare & Classify Incident

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.03 Declare & Classify Incident — third subprocess in the
Detect to Respond value chain, receiving a validated event from Triage &
Validate and handing a declared, classified incident to Contain Threat.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that declare and classify the
incident, with lanes for Incident Response and Executive Management.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system that stores and tracks the
incident record throughout classification.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, subdivided into lanes)
2. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane (incident manager):
  Message start event "Validated event received from Triage & Validate"
  User task "Review validated event details"
  User task "Draft incident declaration"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to declare?"
    - branch "No": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete"
      (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Request additional
      information from analyst", Intermediate message catch event
      "Additional information received"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Sufficient information to declare")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to declare"
  Service task "Log incident record in Case Management System"
  User task "Apply severity matrix and assign classification"
  Exclusive gateway "Severity level?"
    - branch "Critical": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Severity level")
    - branch "High": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Severity level")
    - branch "Medium or Low": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Severity level")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Severity level"
  Exclusive gateway "Executive notification required?"
    - branch "Yes — Critical or High": User task
      "Prepare executive notification brief"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Executive notification required")
    - branch "No — Medium or Low": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Executive notification required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Executive notification required"
  User task "Assign incident manager and response team"
  Service task "Update incident record with classification and ownership"
  End event "Incident declared and classified — ready for Contain Threat"

Executive Management lane (executive sponsor):
  Intermediate message catch event "Executive notification brief received"
  User task "Acknowledge incident and confirm authority to respond"
  Send task "Return acknowledgement to incident manager"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Details Complete" — label "48-hour declaration deadline exceeded" —
triggers End event "Declaration timed out — escalate to incident manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Incident Response lane at the message
start event, progresses through review and drafting to the sufficiency
gateway; the "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and exits back
to the merge gateway; the "Yes" branch joins at the same merge. After
logging in Case Management System, severity classification is applied; all
three severity branches rejoin at the severity merge gateway. The executive
notification gateway follows; the "Yes" branch routes through preparation of
the brief, sends it to the Executive Management lane, and rejoins at the
notification merge gateway after acknowledgement is received back; the "No"
branch skips directly to the merge. Both lanes then continue to team
assignment and record update before the end event.

Message flows:
Case Management System → Incident Response lane, "Log incident record in
Case Management System" (incident record created).
Incident Response lane, "Update incident record with classification and
ownership" → Case Management System (classification and ownership written).
Incident Response lane, "Prepare executive notification brief" →
Executive Management lane, "Executive notification brief received"
(incident brief delivered).
Executive Management lane, "Return acknowledgement to incident manager" →
Incident Response lane, "Executive notification required" merge gateway
area (executive acknowledgement received).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Event Report" — read by "Review validated event
details".
Data Object "Incident Declaration" — written by "Draft incident declaration";
read by "Log incident record in Case Management System".
Data Object "Severity Classification" — written by "Apply severity matrix
and assign classification"; read by "Update incident record with
classification and ownership".
Data Object "Executive Notification Brief" — written by "Prepare executive
notification brief"; read by "Acknowledge incident and confirm authority to
respond".

This subprocess takes the validated security event produced by Triage &
Validate and formalises it as a declared incident with an assigned severity
level, a named incident manager, and an assembled response team. Where the
event is Critical or High severity, executive sponsorship is confirmed before
the record is finalised. The completed, classified incident record held in
the Case Management System is then handed to Contain Threat, which uses the
classification to determine the urgency and scope of containment actions.
```


### V16.04 — Contain Threat

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.04 Contain Threat — the fourth subprocess in the Detect to
Respond value chain, executed after the incident has been declared and
classified, responsible for isolating and neutralising the active threat
before investigation and eradication proceed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing containment actions.
  Lane "Incident Response" — incident manager coordinates and authorises
    containment.
  Lane "IT Operations" — service owner executes technical containment
    actions on systems and infrastructure.

Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — EDR platform used to isolate
  endpoints and push containment actions.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — IAM platform used to revoke or
  suspend credentials and block access.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Organisation" — top (holds the process flow).
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — below Organisation.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — below Endpoint Detection & Response.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane:
  Message start event "Classified incident record received from Declare
    & Classify Incident"
  User task "Review incident classification and containment authority"
  User task "Select containment strategy"
  Exclusive gateway "Containment strategy type?"
  - branch "Endpoint isolation required":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Containment strategy type")
  - branch "Credential revocation required":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Containment strategy type")
  - branch "Both required":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Containment strategy type")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Containment strategy type"
  User task "Authorise containment actions under emergency change rules"
  Intermediate message catch event "Containment action confirmation
    received"
  User task "Verify containment effectiveness"
  Exclusive gateway "Threat contained?"
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Threat contained")
  - branch "No — escalate":
      User task "Escalate containment failure to executive sponsor"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Threat contained")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Threat contained"
  User task "Update incident record with containment outcome"
  End event "Threat contained — ready for Investigate & Preserve Evidence"

IT Operations lane:
  User task "Execute endpoint isolation via EDR"
  Service task "Send isolation command to Endpoint Detection & Response"
  User task "Revoke or suspend compromised credentials via IAM"
  Service task "Send credential revocation to Identity & Access Management"
  User task "Apply network segmentation or firewall rules"
  User task "Confirm containment actions completed"
  Send task "Send containment action confirmation to Incident Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Authorise containment actions under
  emergency change rules" — label "Authorisation deadline exceeded" —
  triggers User task "Invoke standing emergency containment authority"
  which then rejoins the flow at "Verify containment effectiveness" after
  the Intermediate message catch event.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Incident Response lane, flow runs from the
  message start event through classification review, strategy selection,
  and the strategy gateway; all three branches (endpoint isolation,
  credential revocation, both required) converge at the exclusive merge
  gateway "Containment strategy type" before passing to authorisation.
  After the authorisation task, the timer boundary event may fire to
  invoke emergency authority, which rejoins ahead of the verification
  step. The intermediate message catch event holds the flow until IT
  Operations confirms; verification then drives the "Threat contained?"
  gateway, whose "No — escalate" branch executes escalation before
  converging with the "Yes" branch at the merge gateway, leading to
  record update and the end event. Within IT Operations, flow runs from
  endpoint isolation through EDR command, credential revocation through
  IAM command, network segmentation, confirmation, and send confirmation.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Send isolation command to Endpoint
    Detection & Response") → Endpoint Detection & Response (isolation
    command).
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation (IT Operations lane,
    User task "Execute endpoint isolation via EDR") (isolation result
    and status).
  Organisation (Service task "Send credential revocation to Identity &
    Access Management") → Identity & Access Management (credential
    revocation request).
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (IT Operations lane,
    User task "Revoke or suspend compromised credentials via IAM")
    (revocation confirmation).
  Organisation (Send task "Send containment action confirmation to
    Incident Response") → Organisation (Incident Response lane,
    Intermediate message catch event "Containment action confirmation
    received") (containment actions completed notification).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Classified Incident Record" — read by User task "Review
  incident classification and containment authority"; written by User task
  "Update incident record with containment outcome".
Data Object "Containment Strategy" — written by User task "Select
  containment strategy"; read by User task "Authorise containment actions
  under emergency change rules".
Data Object "Emergency Change Authorisation" — written by User task
  "Authorise containment actions under emergency change rules"; read by
  User task "Execute endpoint isolation via EDR" and User task "Revoke or
  suspend compromised credentials via IAM".
Data Object "Containment Action Log" — written by User task "Confirm
  containment actions completed"; read by User task "Verify containment
  effectiveness".

V16.04 Contain Threat isolates the active threat by directing IT
Operations to cut off compromised endpoints through the EDR platform and
revoke credentials through IAM, under formal authorisation governed by
emergency change rules. Once IT Operations confirms all actions, the
Incident Response manager verifies effectiveness and, if escalation is
needed, engages the executive sponsor before closing out the containment
phase. The confirmed containment outcome and updated incident record are
handed to Investigate & Preserve Evidence, where forensic work can now
proceed safely.
```


### V16.05 — Investigate & Preserve Evidence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.05 Investigate & Preserve Evidence — the fifth subprocess in the
Detect to Respond value chain, conducted after the threat is contained and
before the data and privacy impact is assessed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams conducting the forensic investigation
  and evidence preservation.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Incident Response (forensic investigator)
Pool "Forensic Specialist" — external forensic expert engaged to support the
  investigation.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — IT system providing correlated log and telemetry data.
Pool "Forensic Tooling" — IT system used to acquire, image and analyse
  digital evidence.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Forensic Specialist" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "SIEM Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Forensic Tooling" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Forensic Specialist
2. Organisation
3. SIEM Platform
4. Forensic Tooling

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane:
  Message start event "Contained incident handed off from Contain Threat"
  User task "Define investigation scope and objectives"
  Service task "Retrieve correlated events and logs from SIEM Platform"
  User task "Identify assets and data stores in scope"
  User task "Establish chain-of-custody register"
  User task "Brief Forensic Specialist and share scope"
  Intermediate message catch event "Forensic Specialist confirms engagement"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Collection Complete"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Acquire forensic images and memory captures"
    Service task "Ingest artefacts into Forensic Tooling"
    User task "Perform static and dynamic analysis of artefacts"
    User task "Review Forensic Tooling findings and analyst notes"
    User task "Assess whether evidence collection is sufficient"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence collection sufficient?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
      collection sufficient")
  - branch "No — gaps identified": User task "Document gaps and
      extend collection scope"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence collection sufficient")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence collection sufficient"
  User task "Compile investigation timeline and attack narrative"
  User task "Validate chain-of-custody documentation"
  Exclusive gateway "Chain of custody intact?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Chain of
      custody intact")
  - branch "No — breach in custody": User task "Record custody
      discrepancy and escalate to incident manager"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Chain of custody intact")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Chain of custody intact"
  User task "Package evidence artefacts and secure for preservation"
  User task "Produce investigation findings report"
  End event "Investigation findings and preserved evidence ready for
      Assess Data & Privacy Impact"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Evidence Collection Complete" — label "Maximum investigation window
  elapsed" — triggers User task "Record partial findings and escalate to
  incident manager", then flows to Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
  collection sufficient".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: All flow within the Incident Response lane in the order
  listed above. The loop subprocess iterates until evidence is deemed
  sufficient; the timer boundary event on that subprocess exits early if
  the investigation window is exceeded and joins at the merge gateway
  "Evidence collection sufficient". The "Evidence collection sufficient"
  exclusive gateway branches to the merge of the same name, and the
  "Chain of custody intact" exclusive gateway branches to the merge of
  the same name, before continuing to evidence packaging and report
  production.

Message flows:
  Organisation (User task "Brief Forensic Specialist and share scope") →
    Forensic Specialist (investigation scope and engagement brief).
  Forensic Specialist → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Forensic Specialist confirms engagement") (engagement confirmation).
  Forensic Specialist → Organisation (User task "Acquire forensic images
    and memory captures") (externally acquired forensic artefacts and
    specialist analysis notes).
  SIEM Platform → Organisation (Service task "Retrieve correlated events
    and logs from SIEM Platform") (correlated log and telemetry data).
  Organisation (Service task "Ingest artefacts into Forensic Tooling") →
    Forensic Tooling (evidence artefacts for processing).
  Forensic Tooling → Organisation (User task "Review Forensic Tooling
    findings and analyst notes") (analysis results and artefact report).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Investigation Scope Document" — written by User task "Define
  investigation scope and objectives"; read by User task "Brief Forensic
  Specialist and share scope".
Data Object "Correlated Event Log" — written by Service task "Retrieve
  correlated events and logs from SIEM Platform"; read by User task
  "Identify assets and data stores in scope".
Data Object "Chain-of-Custody Register" — written by User task "Establish
  chain-of-custody register"; read by User task "Validate
  chain-of-custody documentation".
Data Object "Forensic Evidence Artefacts" — written by User task "Acquire
  forensic images and memory captures"; read by Service task "Ingest
  artefacts into Forensic Tooling".
Data Object "Forensic Analysis Results" — written by User task "Review
  Forensic Tooling findings and analyst notes"; read by User task "Compile
  investigation timeline and attack narrative".
Data Object "Investigation Findings Report" — written by User task "Produce
  investigation findings report"; read by the end event and passed to the
  next subprocess.

This subprocess conducts a structured forensic investigation of the
contained incident, collecting and preserving digital evidence under a
documented chain of custody with the support of an external Forensic
Specialist. It produces a validated investigation findings report and a
secured evidence package, which the next subprocess — Assess Data &
Privacy Impact — uses to determine what data was exposed and whether
regulatory or individual notification obligations are triggered.
```


### V16.06 — Assess Data & Privacy Impact

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.06 Assess Data & Privacy Impact — the sixth subprocess in the
Detect to Respond value chain, carried out after threat containment and
before regulatory and individual notification.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation conducting the privacy impact
assessment, with Privacy and Legal teams as lanes.
  Lane "Privacy" — privacy officer who leads the data impact assessment.
  Lane "Legal" — legal counsel who reviews obligations and advises.
Pool "Case Management System" — system of record for incident and
assessment data.
Pool "GRC Platform" — governance, risk and compliance system holding
data classification and risk register.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, Privacy lane above Legal lane)
2. Case Management System
3. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Privacy lane:
  Message start event "Contained incident record received from
    Contain Threat"
  Service task "Retrieve incident record and containment details"
  Service task "Retrieve data classification and asset inventory"
  User task "Identify personal and sensitive data in scope"
  User task "Assess volume, nature and categories of data affected"
  Exclusive gateway "Personal data involved?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Determine likely harm to data subjects"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Personal data involved")
  - branch "No": User task "Document nil-breach finding"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Personal data involved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Personal data involved"
  User task "Complete privacy impact assessment record"
  User task "Assign preliminary breach severity rating"
  Intermediate message catch event "Legal review outcome received"
  Exclusive gateway "Breach notification required?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Flag notification obligation and
      record statutory deadline"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Breach notification
    required")
  - branch "No": User task "Record rationale for no notification"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Breach notification
    required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Breach notification required"
  User task "Update impact assessment in Case Management System"
  User task "Record risk entry in GRC Platform"
  End event "Impact assessment complete — ready for Notify
    Regulators & Affected Parties"

Legal lane:
  User task "Receive impact assessment for legal review"
  User task "Review breach notification obligations and
    statutory timeframes"
  User task "Review third-party and insurance notification terms"
  User task "Confirm or revise breach severity and notification
    determination"
  Send task "Return legal review outcome to Privacy"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Privacy lane, work moves from the start event
through data retrieval and scoping tasks to the "Personal data involved?"
gateway; the Yes branch leads to harm assessment and the No branch to the
nil-breach task, both rejoining at the exclusive merge gateway; flow
continues through completion and severity-rating tasks to the intermediate
message catch event awaiting Legal's review outcome; the "Breach
notification required?" gateway splits to flagging or rationale tasks,
both rejoining at the second merge gateway, after which the assessment
is updated and the risk entry recorded before the end event. Within the
Legal lane, tasks run in sequence and conclude with the send task that
returns the outcome to the Privacy lane. Sequence flows do not cross
pool boundaries.

Message flows:
Case Management System → Privacy lane, "Retrieve incident record and
  containment details" (contained incident record and timeline).
GRC Platform → Privacy lane, "Retrieve data classification and asset
  inventory" (data classification and asset inventory data).
Privacy lane, "Update impact assessment in Case Management System"
  → Case Management System (completed privacy impact assessment record).
Privacy lane, "Record risk entry in GRC Platform"
  → GRC Platform (breach severity rating and risk register entry).
Privacy lane, "Complete privacy impact assessment record"
  → Legal lane, "Receive impact assessment for legal review"
  (draft impact assessment for legal review).
Legal lane, "Return legal review outcome to Privacy"
  → Privacy lane, intermediate message catch event "Legal review
  outcome received" (legal determination on notification obligation).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Privacy Impact Assessment" — written by "Complete privacy
  impact assessment record"; read by "Receive impact assessment for
  legal review"; updated by "Update impact assessment in Case
  Management System".
Data Object "Breach Severity Rating" — written by "Assign preliminary
  breach severity rating"; read by "Confirm or revise breach severity
  and notification determination"; updated by "Record risk entry in
  GRC Platform".
Data Object "Legal Review Determination" — written by "Confirm or
  revise breach severity and notification determination"; read by the
  intermediate message catch event "Legal review outcome received" and
  by "Flag notification obligation and record statutory deadline".

This subprocess determines whether personal or sensitive data was
compromised, quantifies the harm to data subjects, and produces a
completed privacy impact assessment with a confirmed breach severity
rating and notification determination. It hands a finalised assessment
record and statutory deadline flag to the Notify Regulators & Affected
Parties subprocess, enabling that team to act within required timeframes.
```


### V16.07 — Notify Regulators & Affected Parties

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.07 Notify Regulators & Affected Parties — the subprocess in
which Legal and Communications prepare, dispatch, and confirm statutory
breach notifications to regulators and affected individuals, following
confirmed data and privacy impact assessment.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the Detect to Respond process,
with Legal and Communications teams executing the notification workflow.
  Lane "Legal (legal counsel)"
  Lane "Communications (communications lead)"
Pool "Regulator" — external authority receiving breach notification and
issuing directions or findings.
Pool "Affected Individual" — external data subjects receiving notification
of the breach, what data was involved, and what they should do.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system holding the incident record,
notification obligations, and communication log.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Affected Individual" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Organisation
3. Affected Individual
4. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Data and privacy impact assessment received from
    Assess Data and Privacy Impact"
  User task "Review notification obligations and statutory timeframes"
  User task "Determine notifiable jurisdictions and affected populations"
  Exclusive gateway "Regulator notification required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Submit breach notification to Regulator"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Regulator notification
      required")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Regulator
      notification required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Regulator notification required"
  Intermediate message catch event "Regulatory direction or finding received"
  User task "Review regulatory response and update legal obligations"
  User task "Approve individual notification content and channel"
  User task "Record all notifications and outcomes in incident record"
  End event "Notifications complete — ready for Eradicate and Recover"

Communications lane:
  User task "Draft individual notification content"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Notification Approved" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Revise notification draft",
    User task "Submit draft for legal approval"
  User task "Identify affected individuals and contact details"
  Send task "Dispatch notifications to affected individuals"
  Intermediate message catch event "Individual acknowledgement or response
    received"
  User task "Log notification delivery and individual responses"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Submit breach notification
to Regulator", labelled "Statutory notification deadline elapsed", leading
to an End event "Notification deadline breached — escalate to executive
sponsor".
Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Regulatory direction or finding received", labelled "Regulatory response
window expired", leading to User task "Chase regulatory acknowledgement".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The Legal lane opens with the message start event and moves
through obligation review, jurisdiction determination, and the "Regulator
notification required" exclusive gateway. The "Yes" branch sends the
regulatory notification and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway; the "No"
branch rejoins at the same merge. After the merge, a message catch event
waits for the regulatory response, followed by legal review and approval of
individual notification content. In parallel, the Communications lane
drafts the notification, iterates through the standard-loop subprocess
until Legal approves it, identifies affected individuals, dispatches
notifications, waits for individual responses via a message catch event,
and logs delivery. Legal then records all notifications in the incident
record and the process ends.

Message flows:
Organisation (Legal lane, Send task "Submit breach notification to
  Regulator") → Regulator (breach notification with impact summary and
  remediation plan).
Regulator → Organisation (Legal lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Regulatory direction or finding received") (regulatory direction or
  finding).
Organisation (Communications lane, Send task "Dispatch notifications to
  affected individuals") → Affected Individual (individual breach
  notification detailing data involved and recommended actions).
Affected Individual → Organisation (Communications lane, Intermediate
  message catch event "Individual acknowledgement or response received")
  (acknowledgement or query response).
Case Management System → Organisation (Legal lane, User task "Review
  notification obligations and statutory timeframes") (incident record,
  impact assessment, and obligation flags).
Organisation (Legal lane, User task "Record all notifications and outcomes
  in incident record") → Case Management System (notification log,
  regulatory correspondence, and individual contact records).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Breach Notification Package" — written by User task "Review
  notification obligations and statutory timeframes"; read by Send task
  "Submit breach notification to Regulator".
Data Object "Individual Notification Draft" — written by User task "Draft
  individual notification content"; read by User task "Submit draft for
  legal approval"; read by User task "Approve individual notification
  content and channel".
Data Object "Affected Individual Contact List" — written by User task
  "Identify affected individuals and contact details"; read by Send task
  "Dispatch notifications to affected individuals".
Data Object "Regulatory Response Record" — written by User task "Review
  regulatory response and update legal obligations"; read by User task
  "Approve individual notification content and channel".
Data Object "Notification Log" — written by User task "Log notification
  delivery and individual responses"; read by User task "Record all
  notifications and outcomes in incident record".

This subprocess ensures that all statutory breach notifications are
prepared with proper legal review, dispatched to regulators within
mandated timeframes, and communicated clearly to affected individuals.
It captures regulatory directions and individual responses, and closes
out the notification obligations by recording every action in the incident
record. On completion it hands a fully documented notification log to the
Eradicate and Recover subprocess.
```


### V16.08 — Eradicate & Recover

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.08 Eradicate & Recover — the subprocess in which IT Operations
and Incident Response systematically remove the threat, restore affected
systems and services, and hand a recovered environment to Confirm Service
Restoration.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing eradication and recovery.
  Lane "Incident Response" — incident manager coordinating eradication.
  Lane "IT Operations" — service owner executing remediation and recovery.
Pool "IT Service Management" — ITSM platform recording changes and tasks.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — EDR platform used to verify
  eradication and push remediation actions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Endpoint Detection & Response" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box)
2. IT Service Management
3. Endpoint Detection & Response

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response lane:
  Message start event "Eradication authorised — received from Contain Threat"
  User task "Define eradication scope and remediation plan"
  Send task "Issue remediation tasks to IT Operations"
  Intermediate message catch event "Eradication completion confirmed"
  User task "Review eradication results and approve recovery start"
  Exclusive gateway "Eradication complete and verified?"
  - branch "Yes — eradication confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eradication complete and
      verified")
  - branch "No — residual threat found":
      User task "Revise eradication scope and reissue tasks"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eradication complete and
      verified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Eradication complete and verified"
  User task "Authorise recovery and system rebuild sequence"
  Intermediate message catch event "Recovery actions completed"
  User task "Validate recovery against incident baseline"
  Exclusive gateway "Recovery validated?"
  - branch "Yes — all systems restored":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Recovery validated")
  - branch "No — issues remain":
      User task "Log recovery defects and escalate to IT Operations"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Recovery validated")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Recovery validated"
  User task "Update incident record with eradication and recovery
    outcome"
  End event "Eradication and recovery complete — ready for Confirm
    Service Restoration"

IT Operations lane:
  User task "Isolate and remove malicious artefacts and persistence
    mechanisms"
  User task "Apply patches, configuration fixes, and credential resets"
  User task "Rebuild or restore affected systems from known-good images"
  Send task "Confirm eradication completion to Incident Response"
  User task "Execute recovery and service restoration actions"
  Service task "Log all remediation and recovery changes in IT Service
    Management"
  Send task "Confirm recovery actions completed to Incident Response"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Define eradication scope
  and remediation plan" — label "Eradication planning overdue (4 hours)"
  — triggers End event "Eradication planning escalated — breach of
  response SLA".
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Rebuild or restore
  affected systems from known-good images" — label "Rebuild deadline
  exceeded (RTO threshold)" — triggers User task "Escalate RTO breach to
  incident manager" in IT Operations lane, followed by End event "RTO
  breach escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in Incident Response with the message start
  event, proceeds to define scope, then issues tasks to IT Operations.
  IT Operations lane runs in parallel: isolates and removes artefacts,
  applies patches and credential resets, rebuilds systems, then sends
  eradication confirmation back to Incident Response. Incident Response
  catches that confirmation, reviews results, and routes through the
  "Eradication complete and verified" exclusive gateway; the "No" branch
  passes through "Revise eradication scope" before rejoining the merge.
  After the merge, Incident Response authorises recovery; IT Operations
  executes recovery actions and logs them to IT Service Management, then
  confirms completion. Incident Response catches that confirmation,
  validates recovery, and routes through the "Recovery validated"
  exclusive gateway; the "No" branch logs defects before rejoining the
  merge. After the merge, the incident record is updated and the end
  event fires.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Send task "Issue remediation tasks to IT Operations") →
    IT Service Management (remediation task record created).
  IT Service Management → Organisation IT Operations lane (task
    assignments and change records returned).
  Organisation IT Operations (User task "Isolate and remove malicious
    artefacts") → Endpoint Detection & Response (eradication actions
    dispatched).
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation IT Operations lane
    (eradication status and telemetry confirmation returned).
  Organisation IT Operations (User task "Apply patches, configuration
    fixes, and credential resets") → Endpoint Detection & Response
    (patch and configuration push).
  Endpoint Detection & Response → Organisation IT Operations lane
    (patch deployment result returned).
  Organisation IT Operations (Service task "Log all remediation and
    recovery changes in IT Service Management") → IT Service Management
    (remediation and recovery change records written).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Remediation Plan" — written by User task "Define eradication
  scope and remediation plan"; read by User task "Isolate and remove
  malicious artefacts and persistence mechanisms".
Data Object "Eradication Results Report" — written by Send task "Confirm
  eradication completion to Incident Response"; read by User task "Review
  eradication results and approve recovery start".
Data Object "Recovery Action Log" — written by Service task "Log all
  remediation and recovery changes in IT Service Management"; read by
  User task "Validate recovery against incident baseline".
Data Object "Incident Record (Eradication and Recovery)" — written by
  User task "Update incident record with eradication and recovery
  outcome"; read by User task "Validate recovery against incident
  baseline".

This subprocess takes the contained threat environment handed over from
Contain Threat and drives it through systematic eradication of all
malicious artefacts, credential resets, patching, and system rebuilds,
followed by a structured recovery sequence. Incident Response governs
scope and sign-off while IT Operations executes, with EDR confirming
clean state and ITSM recording every change. On validated completion it
hands a restored environment to Confirm Service Restoration.
```


### V16.09 — Confirm Service Restoration

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V16.09 Confirm Service Restoration — the subprocess in which IT
Operations and Security Operations jointly verify that restored services
are functioning correctly and securely before formally closing the
recovery phase and handing the incident record to post-incident review.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out service restoration
confirmation.
  Lane "IT Operations" (service owner) — verifies functional recovery and
  updates ITSM records.
  Lane "Security Operations" (security analyst) — validates security
  posture and monitors for recurrence.

Pool "IT Service Management" — ITSM platform used to record recovery
verification, update change records, and close service tickets.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, with lanes IT Operations above Security
   Operations)
2. IT Service Management (bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Operations lane:
  Message start event "Recovery actions complete — received from Eradicate
  & Recover"
  User task "Review recovery scope and restoration checklist"
  Service task "Retrieve open incident and change records from IT Service
  Management"
  User task "Execute service verification tests"
  Exclusive gateway "Services verified as functional?"
  - branch "No — verification failed":
      User task "Log verification failure and escalate to service owner"
      End event "Verification failure escalated — returns to Eradicate &
      Recover"
  - branch "Yes — services functional":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Services verified as
      functional")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Services verified as functional"
  Service task "Update incident record with verification outcome in IT
  Service Management"
  User task "Confirm service restoration formally with stakeholders"

Security Operations lane:
  User task "Conduct security health check on restored systems"
  Service task "Query SIEM for anomalous activity on restored services"
  Exclusive gateway "Security posture acceptable?"
  - branch "No — anomalies detected":
      User task "Raise security concern and notify incident manager"
      End event "Security concern raised — returns to Eradicate & Recover"
  - branch "Yes — posture acceptable":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Security posture acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Security posture acceptable"
  User task "Confirm security sign-off on restored services"
  Service task "Close monitoring alert in IT Service Management"
  End event "Service restoration confirmed — ready for Conduct
  Post-Incident Review"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Execute service verification tests"
— label "Verification deadline exceeded (4 hours)" — triggers User task
"Escalate overdue verification to service owner", leading to End event
"Escalation raised — returns to Eradicate & Recover".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within IT Operations the flow runs from the start event
through review, record retrieval, verification tests, and the functional
gateway; the "Yes" branch merges at the merge gateway and continues to
record update and stakeholder confirmation. Within Security Operations the
flow runs from the health check through SIEM query, the security posture
gateway; the "Yes" branch merges at the security merge gateway and
continues to sign-off, alert closure, and the end event. The IT
Operations lane feeds into the Security Operations lane after stakeholder
confirmation, joining before the security sign-off task.

Message flows:
IT Service Management → Organisation / IT Operations lane (open incident
and change records retrieved for review)
Organisation / IT Operations lane → IT Service Management (verification
outcome written to incident and change records)
Organisation / Security Operations lane → IT Service Management
(monitoring alert closed on confirmed restoration)
IT Service Management → Organisation / Security Operations lane (current
alert and ticket status queried via SIEM integration)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Restoration Checklist" — written by "Review recovery scope
and restoration checklist"; read by "Execute service verification tests".
Data Object "Verification Outcome Report" — written by "Execute service
verification tests"; read by "Update incident record with verification
outcome in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Security Health Check Report" — written by "Conduct security
health check on restored systems"; read by "Confirm security sign-off on
restored services".

V16.09 Confirm Service Restoration ensures that both functional recovery
and security integrity are independently validated before the incident
is formally closed. IT Operations confirms that services perform as
expected and updates the ITSM record accordingly, while Security
Operations verifies that no residual threats or anomalies remain on
restored systems. A clean sign-off from both lanes produces the confirmed
restoration status that initiates the Conduct Post-Incident Review
subprocess.
```

```text
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Cyber Insurer
2. Organisation
3. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Incident Response (incident manager) lane:
  Message start event "Service restoration confirmed — ready for Conduct
  Post-Incident Review"
  User task "Compile incident timeline and artefacts"
  User task "Schedule and facilitate review session"
  User task "Capture lessons learned and action items"
  Send task "Submit claim documentation to Cyber Insurer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Insurer acknowledgement received"

  User task "Finalise remediation action plan"
  User task "Hand remediation actions to owners"

Risk & Compliance (risk manager) lane:
  User task "Conduct structured review meeting"
  User task "Record review findings in GRC Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Are all critical findings assigned?"
    - branch "No — findings unassigned": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
      All Findings Assigned" (standard loop) containing, in order: User task
      "Identify unassigned finding", User task "Assign finding to owner and
      set due date"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Yes — all assigned": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "All Critical Findings Assigned")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All Critical Findings Assigned"
  User task "Update risk register in GRC Platform"
  Service task "Close incident record in GRC Platform"
  End event "Post-incident review complete — incident closed"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
Findings Assigned" — label "Review deadline exceeded" — triggers End event
"Review closed with outstanding findings — escalated to Risk & Compliance
leadership".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Incident Response lane with compilation
and scheduling tasks, then crosses to the Risk & Compliance lane for the
structured review meeting and findings recording. The exclusive gateway
branches to the assignment loop (which exits back to the merge) or directly
to the merge when all findings are assigned. After the merge, the Risk &
Compliance lane updates the risk register, closes the incident record, and
reaches the end event. The send task and intermediate catch event in the
Incident Response lane run in parallel with the Risk & Compliance review
activities, with the finalised action plan feeding the hand-off task before
the end event.

Message flows:
  Send task "Submit claim documentation to Cyber Insurer" → Cyber Insurer
  (incident claim package and remediation evidence)
  Cyber Insurer → Intermediate message catch event "Insurer acknowledgement
  received" (acknowledgement of claim receipt)
  Service task "Close incident record in GRC Platform" → GRC Platform
  (closed incident record)
  User task "Record review findings in GRC Platform" → GRC Platform (review
  findings and lessons learned)
  User task "Update risk register in GRC Platform" → GRC Platform (updated
  risk register entries)
  GRC Platform → User task "Record review findings in GRC Platform"
  (existing incident record and prior risk entries)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incident Timeline and Artefacts" — written by "Compile incident
timeline and artefacts", read by "Conduct structured review meeting".
Data Object "Lessons Learned and Action Items" — written by "Capture lessons
learned and action items", read by "Record review findings in GRC Platform".
Data Object "Remediation Action Plan" — written by "Finalise remediation
action plan", read by "Hand remediation actions to owners".
Data Object "Claim Documentation Package" — written by "Submit claim
documentation to Cyber Insurer", read by "Respond to insurer queries".
Data Object "Review Findings Report" — written by "Record review findings in
GRC Platform", read by "Update risk register in GRC Platform".

This subprocess brings the Detect to Respond chain to a formal close. It
assembles the complete incident record, facilitates a structured review that
captures lessons learned and assigns every remediation finding to an owner,
updates the risk register, and provides the Cyber Insurer with claim evidence.
With the incident record closed in the GRC Platform and remediation actions
handed to their owners, the organisation exits the chain with accountability
for improvement embedded in its risk governance cycle.
```


## V17 — Audit to Action

**Teams and roles involved.**
Audit to Action usually involves Internal Audit, Risk and Compliance, the audited Business Units, Finance, IT, and the Audit and Risk Committee. Key roles include chief audit executive, audit manager, auditor, control owner, process owner, remediation owner, risk manager, and committee chair.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are External Auditors and Regulators, and in some sectors certification bodies. The process is initiated by the annual audit plan, a regulatory examination, a certification cycle, or a triggering event such as an incident or whistleblower report. Other external parties include co-sourced audit providers and specialist assessors.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: plan the audit and set scope, notify the auditee and agree logistics, gather evidence and test controls, evaluate findings and rate them, draft the audit report, agree management responses and owners, issue the final report, track remediation to completion, verify and close findings, and report status to the committee.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include audit management, GRC and risk registers, control libraries and testing workpapers, document and evidence repositories, issue and action tracking, data analytics tooling for full-population testing, and board reporting packs.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the internal audit charter and independence requirements, risk-based audit planning methodology, evidence sufficiency and workpaper standards, finding rating criteria, management response and escalation timeframes, overdue-action escalation, retest and closure evidence requirements, and committee reporting obligations.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
External auditors and regulators provide scope requests, information requests, findings and directions; the process provides evidence, management representations, remediation plans and progress reports. Auditees provide process documentation, system access, data extracts and explanations, and receive draft findings, agreed actions and closure confirmations.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates audit plans, engagements, test procedures and results, findings and ratings, management actions, and closure evidence. IT systems provide the control library and risk register, prior findings and their status, transaction and configuration data for testing, action due dates and overdue alerts, and assurance-coverage reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V17.01** Plan Audit & Set Scope | — | Internal Audit (chief audit executive), Risk & Compliance (risk manager) | Audit Management System, GRC Platform |
| **V17.02** Notify Auditee & Agree Logistics | — | Internal Audit (audit manager), Business Unit (process owner) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.03** Gather Evidence & Test Controls | External Auditor | Internal Audit (auditor), Business Unit (control owner) | Audit Management System, Evidence Repository |
| **V17.04** Evaluate & Rate Findings | — | Internal Audit (audit manager) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.05** Draft Audit Report | — | Internal Audit (audit manager) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.06** Agree Management Responses | — | Business Unit (process owner), Internal Audit (audit manager) | Issue & Action Tracking System |
| **V17.07** Issue Final Report | Regulator | Internal Audit (chief audit executive) | Audit Management System |
| **V17.08** Track Remediation | — | Risk & Compliance (risk manager), Business Unit (remediation owner) | Issue & Action Tracking System |
| **V17.09** Verify & Close Findings | — | Internal Audit (auditor) | Audit Management System, Evidence Repository |
| **V17.10** Report to Committee | Audit & Risk Committee | Internal Audit (chief audit executive) | Board Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V17):

- **External actors:** External Auditor (V17.03); Regulator (V17.07); Audit & Risk Committee (V17.10).
- **Teams:** Internal Audit (V17.01–V17.05, V17.07, V17.09, V17.10); Risk & Compliance (V17.01, V17.08); Business Unit (V17.02, V17.03, V17.06, V17.08).
- **IT systems:** Audit Management System (V17.01–V17.05, V17.07, V17.09); GRC Platform (V17.01); Evidence Repository (V17.03, V17.09); Issue & Action Tracking System (V17.06, V17.08); Board Reporting System (V17.10).

```text
ArchiMate: V17 — Audit to Action — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for

committee reporting. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands,

band) → APPLICATIONS (bottom band). The demand-side actor (Business Unit
as auditee) sits on the far left; delivery and oversight actors (External
Auditor, Regulator, Audit & Risk Committee) sit on the far right. The
diagram is read top-to-bottom as service → process → application,
expressing ArchiMate service realisation.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Business Unit — demand-side actor, far left; initiates audit engagement

- Internal Audit — central delivery actor; spans the full width of the
  middle band as the primary executing team.
- Risk & Compliance — central delivery actor; supports planning and
  remediation tracking.
- External Auditor — far right; participates in evidence gathering and
  provides scope requests and findings.
- Regulator — far right; receives the final report and may issue directions
  or examination scope.
- Audit & Risk Committee — far right; receives assurance reporting and
  committee packs.

2. Interfaces

- Audit Engagement Interface — accessed by Business Unit (auditee); serves
  the Audit Planning & Scoping Service and the Notification & Logistics
  Service.
- Evidence Submission Interface — accessed by Business Unit (control owner)
  and External Auditor; serves the Evidence & Testing Service.
- Management Response Interface — accessed by Business Unit (process owner);
  serves the Management Response & Action Service.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface — accessed by Regulator; serves the Final
  Report Issuance Service.
- Committee Reporting Interface — accessed by Audit & Risk Committee; serves
  the Committee Assurance Reporting Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Audit Planning & Scoping Service — provides a risk-based annual audit plan
  with defined scope, objectives, and resourcing for each engagement.
- Notification & Logistics Service — provides formal notice of audit, agreed
  timelines, and access arrangements to the auditee.
- Evidence & Testing Service — provides structured collection, validation,
  and testing of controls across the audit population.
- Finding Evaluation & Rating Service — provides assessed and rated findings
  against defined criteria for significance and risk impact.
- Audit Report Drafting Service — provides a structured draft audit report
  for internal review and auditee comment.
- Management Response & Action Service — provides agreed management
  responses, remediation owners, and due dates for each finding.
- Final Report Issuance Service — provides the authorised final audit report
  distributed to relevant stakeholders including the Regulator.
- Remediation Tracking Service — provides ongoing monitoring of action
  completion against agreed due dates with overdue escalation.
- Finding Verification & Closure Service — provides evidence-based
  confirmation that remediation is complete and findings are closed.
- Committee Assurance Reporting Service — provides consolidated assurance
  status and outstanding actions to the Audit & Risk Committee.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V17.01 Plan Audit & Set Scope — risk-based planning and scope definition
  led by Internal Audit with input from Risk & Compliance.
- V17.02 Notify Auditee & Agree Logistics — formal notification and
  scheduling led by Internal Audit with Business Unit coordination.
- V17.03 Gather Evidence & Test Controls — evidence collection and control

- V17.07 Issue Final Report — chief audit executive authorises and issues

- V17.08 Track Remediation — Risk & Compliance and Business Unit
  remediation owner monitor action progress and escalate overdue items.
- V17.09 Verify & Close Findings — Internal Audit auditor retests and
  confirms closure with supporting evidence.
- V17.10 Report to Committee — chief audit executive presents assurance
  status and outstanding actions to the Audit & Risk Committee.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Audit Management System — core system supporting engagement planning,
  workpapers, findings, ratings, and report production.
- GRC Platform — risk register and control library providing risk-based
  inputs to audit planning.
- Evidence Repository — document and evidence store for workpapers, data
  extracts, and closure evidence.
- Issue & Action Tracking System — records management responses, action
  owners, due dates, and overdue escalation alerts.
- Board Reporting System — produces and distributes committee reporting

6. Relationships
```

```text
the Audit and Risk Committee receives a consolidated status report
confirming remediation outcomes and residual risk positions.
```

```text
looping through revision before rejoining at the merge gateway; both branches

Compliance for review" → Risk & Compliance lane "Draft audit plan received

register and flag gaps or conflicts".

V17.01 establishes the risk-based foundation of the entire audit cycle: it
draws on the risk register, control library, and prior findings to select and
```
