```text
Exclusive merge gateway "Logistics agreed within required timeframe"
User task "Confirm audit commencement date and circulate schedule"
Service task "Update engagement status to Ready in Audit Management System"
End event "Logistics confirmed — ready for Gather Evidence & Test Controls"

Business Unit (Process Owner) lane:
Intermediate message catch event "Audit notification received"
User task "Review terms of reference and identify key contacts"
User task "Confirm availability and propose schedule"
Send task "Send acknowledgement and proposed logistics to Internal Audit"
Intermediate message catch event "Confirmed schedule received"
User task "Brief internal stakeholders on audit scope and timeline"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Agree audit schedule, access
requirements, and key contacts" — label "Acknowledgement overdue (5 business
days)" — flow leads to User task "Escalate scheduling conflict and renegotiate
timeline" in the Internal Audit (Audit Manager) lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Internal Audit (Audit Manager) lane with
notification preparation and engagement creation, then a send task triggers
the Business Unit lane; after acknowledgement is received back in the Audit
Manager lane, schedule and access requirements are agreed, logistics are
recorded, and the exclusive gateway tests whether agreement was reached in
time — the "No" branch passes through escalation and renegotiation before
rejoining the merge gateway; both branches converge at the merge gateway,
after which the audit manager confirms the commencement date and sets the
engagement to Ready.

Message flows:
Send task "Issue formal audit notification to Business Unit" →
  Intermediate message catch event "Audit notification received"
  (formal audit notification letter and terms of reference)
Send task "Send acknowledgement and proposed logistics to Internal Audit" →
  Intermediate message catch event "Business Unit acknowledgement received"
  (acknowledgement and proposed schedule)
Send task "Confirm audit commencement date and circulate schedule" →
  Intermediate message catch event "Confirmed schedule received"
  (confirmed schedule and access instructions)
Service task "Create engagement record in Audit Management System" →
  Audit Management System (new engagement record)
Service task "Record agreed logistics in Audit Management System" →
  Audit Management System (logistics and contact details)
Service task "Update engagement status to Ready in Audit Management System" →
  Audit Management System (status update: Ready)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Audit Notification and Terms of Reference" — written by User
task "Prepare audit notification and terms of reference"; read by User task
"Review terms of reference and identify key contacts".
Data Object "Agreed Audit Schedule" — written by User task "Agree audit
schedule, access requirements, and key contacts"; read by User task "Confirm
audit commencement date and circulate schedule" and by User task "Brief
internal stakeholders on audit scope and timeline".
Data Object "Engagement Record" — written by Service task "Create engagement
record in Audit Management System"; read by Service task "Record agreed
logistics in Audit Management System" and by Service task "Update engagement
status to Ready in Audit Management System".

This subprocess takes the approved audit plan from V17.01 and converts it
into a live, agreed engagement. The audit manager formally notifies the
relevant business unit, negotiates and records the schedule, access
arrangements, and key contacts, and updates the engagement record to Ready.
The confirmed logistics package — schedule, contacts, and commencement date —
is handed to V17.03 Gather Evidence & Test Controls as the authorisation to
begin fieldwork.
```


### V17.03 — Gather Evidence & Test Controls

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.03 Gather Evidence & Test Controls — third subprocess in the
Audit to Action value chain, sitting between Notify Auditee & Agree
Logistics and Evaluate & Rate Findings.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Internal Audit Organisation" — the organisation running the process,
with lanes for Internal Audit and Business Unit.
Pool "External Auditor" — external audit provider or specialist assessor
supplying additional evidence or co-sourced testing.
Pool "Audit Management System" — system of record for test procedures,
results, and findings.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — document and evidence store for workpapers
and supporting materials.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Internal Audit Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Auditor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "External Auditor" — top.
Pool "Internal Audit Organisation" — second (white-box, process flow here).
Pool "Audit Management System" — third.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Internal Audit Organisation)

Internal Audit lane:
  Message start event "Confirmed audit schedule received from Notify
    Auditee & Agree Logistics"
  Service task "Retrieve control library and prior findings"
  User task "Prepare evidence request list and test procedures"
  Send task "Issue evidence requests to Business Unit and External
    Auditor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence package received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Is Sufficient" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: User task "Assess completeness of
    evidence received", Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient?",
    - branch "yes": (exits subprocess)
    - branch "no": Send task "Request additional or clarified
      evidence", Intermediate message catch event "Supplementary
      evidence received" (loop repeats)
  User task "Execute control tests against test procedures"
  User task "Document test results in workpapers"
  Service task "Upload workpapers to Evidence Repository"
  Service task "Record test results in Audit Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Exceptions or control failures identified?"
  - branch "exceptions found": User task "Draft preliminary
      findings for each exception"
    Service task "Log preliminary findings in Audit Management
      System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exceptions check")
  - branch "no exceptions": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Exceptions check")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exceptions check"
  User task "Conduct auditor review of workpapers and findings"
  Exclusive gateway "Workpaper review passed?"
  - branch "rework required": User task "Revise workpapers and
      retest as needed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Workpaper review")
  - branch "passed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Workpaper review")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Workpaper review"
  End event "Evidence testing complete — ready for Evaluate & Rate
    Findings"

Business Unit lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Evidence requests received"
  User task "Compile process documentation, data extracts, and system
    access"
  Send task "Submit evidence package to Internal Audit"
  Intermediate message catch event "Request for additional evidence
    received"
  User task "Prepare supplementary evidence or explanations"
  Send task "Submit supplementary evidence to Internal Audit"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Evidence Is Sufficient" — label "Evidence collection deadline exceeded"
— on trigger, flow moves to End event "Evidence collection timed out —
escalate to audit manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Internal Audit lane the flow runs from the
message start event through control-library retrieval, test-procedure
preparation, and evidence requesting, then waits at the intermediate
message catch event before entering the sufficiency loop subprocess;
on exit from the subprocess testing, workpaper documentation, and
system recording follow; the exceptions gateway branches to preliminary
finding drafting and logging or passes through directly, both rejoining
at the exceptions merge gateway; workpaper review then branches to
rework or passes through, both rejoining at the workpaper review merge
gateway, ending at the end event. The Business Unit lane runs
independently from its message catch event through compilation and
submission, then loops on receipt of supplementary requests.

Message flows:
Internal Audit lane "Issue evidence requests to Business Unit and
  External Auditor" → Pool "External Auditor" (evidence request list
  and test procedure scope).
Pool "External Auditor" → Internal Audit lane "Evidence package
  received" (co-sourced testing results and specialist assessment
  evidence).
Internal Audit lane "Issue evidence requests to Business Unit and
  External Auditor" → Business Unit lane "Evidence requests received"
  (evidence request list).
Business Unit lane "Submit evidence package to Internal Audit" →
  Internal Audit lane "Evidence package received" (process
  documentation, data extracts, system access).
Internal Audit lane "Request additional or clarified evidence" →
  Business Unit lane "Request for additional evidence received"
  (follow-up evidence request).
Business Unit lane "Submit supplementary evidence to Internal Audit"
  → Internal Audit lane "Supplementary evidence received"
  (supplementary documentation and explanations).
Internal Audit lane "Upload workpapers to Evidence Repository" →
  Pool "Evidence Repository" (completed workpapers and supporting
  materials).
Internal Audit lane "Retrieve control library and prior findings" →
  Pool "Audit Management System" (request for control library and
  historical findings).
Pool "Audit Management System" → Internal Audit lane "Retrieve
  control library and prior findings" (control library entries and
  prior finding status).
Internal Audit lane "Record test results in Audit Management System"
  → Pool "Audit Management System" (test procedures and results
  records).
Internal Audit lane "Log preliminary findings in Audit Management
  System" → Pool "Audit Management System" (preliminary findings and
  exception records).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Evidence Request List" — written by User task "Prepare
  evidence request list and test procedures"; read by Send task "Issue
  evidence requests to Business Unit and External Auditor".
Data Object "Evidence Package" — written by Business Unit lane User
  task "Compile process documentation, data extracts, and system
  access"; read by Internal Audit lane User task "Assess completeness
  of evidence received".
Data Object "Test Workpapers" — written by User task "Document test
  results in workpapers"; read by Service task "Upload workpapers to
  Evidence Repository" and User task "Conduct auditor review of
  workpapers and findings".
Data Object "Preliminary Findings Record" — written by User task
  "Draft preliminary findings for each exception"; read by Service
  task "Log preliminary findings in Audit Management System".

This subprocess takes the confirmed audit schedule produced by Notify
Auditee & Agree Logistics and delivers a complete, reviewed set of
test workpapers and preliminary findings ready for rating. It collects
evidence from the Business Unit and any co-sourced External Auditor,
loops until that evidence is sufficient, executes control tests, and
logs all results and exceptions in the Audit Management System and
Evidence Repository. Its end state — tested controls and documented
preliminary findings — is the direct input to Evaluate & Rate Findings.
```


### V17.04 — Evaluate & Rate Findings

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.04 Evaluate & Rate Findings — the subprocess in which Internal
Audit reviews gathered evidence, evaluates control weaknesses, and assigns
official ratings to all findings before drafting the audit report.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Internal Audit" — the organisation running the evaluation and rating
process, containing all active lanes.
Lane "Auditor" — team member who organises and prepares raw findings for
review.
Lane "Audit Manager" — senior role who evaluates, rates, challenges, and
approves all findings.

Pool "Audit Management System" — system that stores engagements, findings,
ratings, and workpaper records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Internal Audit" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Internal Audit (white-box, two lanes: Auditor above, Audit Manager below)
2. Audit Management System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Internal Audit)

Auditor lane:
  Message start event "Evidence and test results received from Gather Evidence
  & Test Controls"
  Service task "Retrieve test results and workpapers from Audit Management
  System"
  User task "Compile preliminary list of potential findings"
  User task "Document root cause and control weakness for each finding"
  Send task "Submit findings package to Audit Manager for evaluation"

Audit Manager lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Findings package received from Auditor"
  User task "Review each finding against rating criteria"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Findings Rated" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Apply severity rating to finding",
    User task "Record supporting rationale in workpaper",
    User task "Confirm root cause and control gap alignment"
  Exclusive gateway "All findings adequately rated and evidenced?"
  - branch "Yes": continues to exclusive merge gateway "Rating review
    complete"
  - branch "No — gaps identified": User task "Return findings to Auditor
    with review notes", Intermediate message catch event "Revised findings
    package received", (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Rating review
    complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Rating review complete"
  User task "Consolidate rated findings into findings register"
  Service task "Record ratings and findings register in Audit Management
    System"
  User task "Prioritise findings by rating for report structure"
  End event "Rated findings register complete — ready for Draft Audit Report"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Auditor lane with the message start event,
proceeds through retrieval, compilation, and documentation tasks, then passes
via send task to the Audit Manager lane. The Audit Manager reviews, loops
through rating each finding in the standard-loop subprocess, then reaches the
exclusive gateway "All findings adequately rated and evidenced?". The "Yes"
branch and the "No" branch (after Auditor revises and resubmits) both converge
at the exclusive merge gateway "Rating review complete", after which the Audit
Manager consolidates, records, and prioritises findings before the end event.

Message flows:
Audit Management System → Auditor lane: Service task "Retrieve test results
and workpapers from Audit Management System" (test results, workpapers, prior
findings).
Audit Manager lane → Audit Management System: Service task "Record ratings
and findings register in Audit Management System" (rated findings, severity
ratings, workpaper rationale).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Test Results and Workpapers" — read by "Retrieve test results
and workpapers from Audit Management System", read by "Compile preliminary
list of potential findings".
Data Object "Preliminary Findings List" — written by "Compile preliminary
list of potential findings", read by "Document root cause and control weakness
for each finding".
Data Object "Findings Package" — written by "Document root cause and control
weakness for each finding", read by "Review each finding against rating
criteria".
Data Object "Rated Findings Register" — written by "Consolidate rated
findings into findings register", read by "Prioritise findings by rating for
report structure".

V17.04 takes the evidence and test results produced in V17.03 and converts
them into a formally rated, fully documented findings register. The Audit
Manager applies the organisation's severity-rating criteria to every finding,
loops back to the Auditor if gaps remain, and ultimately records an agreed
register in the Audit Management System. The prioritised, rated register is
handed directly to V17.05 Draft Audit Report as the authoritative input for
structuring and writing the report.
```

```text
    - branch "Yes":

Sequence flows: work proceeds top to bottom within the Internal Audit
(audit manager) lane, from the message start event through drafting tasks
to the first exclusive gateway; the "No" branch enters the standard-loop
subprocess and returns to the exclusive merge gateway; the "Yes" branch
passes directly to the same merge point; flow continues through the
quality-review gateway, whose "No" branch loops to address comments and

Message flows:

workpapers from Audit Management System" (rated findings, workpaper
content, prior findings status).
Service task "Upload final draft report to Audit Management System" →

7. Data objects

Data Object "Rated Findings Register" — read by "Retrieve rated findings

Data Object "Draft Audit Report" — written by "Draft executive summary and

This subprocess takes the rated and evidenced findings produced in Evaluate
& Rate Findings and converts them into a structured, quality-assured draft
audit report. The audit manager leads drafting of the executive summary,
findings, recommendations, and overall opinion, with a built-in revision
loop and a formal quality review against workpaper standards. On
completion, the versioned draft is locked in the Audit Management System
and handed to Agree Management Responses so that process owners can
provide formal replies and remediation commitments.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

2. Issue & Action Tracking System (black-box)

This subprocess takes every rated finding produced in V17.04 and converts it
into a documented, owner-assigned management response with an agreed due date.

distributed.
```

```text
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Report Approved

Sequence flows: work begins in the Audit Manager lane with the message

check gateway, and the standard-loop rework subprocess on the "No" branch
```

### V17.08 — Track Remediation

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.08 Track Remediation — monitors and escalates remediation
actions to completion within the Audit to Action value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams managing remediation tracking
and escalation, with lanes for Risk & Compliance and Business Unit.
Pool "Issue & Action Tracking System" — the IT system recording action
status, due dates, and overdue alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Issue & Action Tracking System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains all lanes)
2. Issue & Action Tracking System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message start event "Remediation plan received from Issue Final Report"
  Service task "Load agreed actions and due dates into tracker"
  User task "Set monitoring schedule and escalation thresholds"
  Intermediate timer catch event "Periodic review cycle due"
  User task "Pull overdue-action report"
  Exclusive gateway "Actions overdue?"
  - branch "No overdue actions": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Actions overdue?")
  - branch "Overdue actions identified": User task "Initiate escalation
    to remediation owner and risk manager", then (continues to exclusive
    merge gateway "Actions overdue?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Actions overdue?"
  Exclusive gateway "All actions complete?"
  - branch "No — actions outstanding": Intermediate timer catch event
    "Next review cycle due", then loops back via User task "Pull
    overdue-action report"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Actions Complete"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Pull overdue-action report",
      User task "Review action status with remediation owners",
      User task "Update action status in tracker",
      User task "Escalate overdue actions where threshold breached"
  - branch "Yes — all actions complete": (continues to exclusive merge
    gateway "All actions complete?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All actions complete?"
  User task "Confirm completion evidence received for each action"
  End event "All actions evidenced — ready for Verify & Close Findings"

Business Unit lane:
  User task "Review assigned remediation actions"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Action Closed" (standard loop)
  containing, in order:
    User task "Implement remediation action",
    User task "Submit progress update and supporting evidence"
  User task "Confirm action closed to Risk & Compliance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
All Actions Complete", label "Maximum remediation period exceeded",
leading to User task "Escalate overdue portfolio to chief audit
executive" in Risk & Compliance lane, then End event "Escalation
raised — remediation period breached".

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
Until Action Closed", label "Interim progress update due", leading to
User task "Submit interim progress update" in Business Unit lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Risk & Compliance lane with the
message start event, moves through loading actions and setting the
monitoring schedule, then enters the periodic review loop via the timer
catch event. The "Actions overdue?" gateway branches to escalation or
directly to the merge; both branches rejoin at the exclusive merge
gateway "Actions overdue?" before reaching "All actions complete?".
The outstanding branch re-enters the standard-loop subprocess and the
complete branch rejoins at exclusive merge gateway "All actions
complete?" before confirmation and the end event. In the Business Unit
lane, work flows from reviewing assigned actions through the loop
subprocess to the closure confirmation, which feeds back to the Risk &
Compliance lane confirmation task.

Message flows:
Issue & Action Tracking System → Risk & Compliance lane: User task
"Load agreed actions and due dates into tracker" (action register with
due dates and overdue alerts).
Risk & Compliance lane: User task "Update action status in tracker" →
Issue & Action Tracking System (updated action status and evidence
references).
Risk & Compliance lane: User task "Pull overdue-action report" →
Issue & Action Tracking System (overdue-action query).
Issue & Action Tracking System → Risk & Compliance lane: User task
"Pull overdue-action report" (overdue-action report).
Business Unit lane: User task "Submit progress update and supporting
evidence" → Issue & Action Tracking System (progress update and
evidence).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Agreed Actions Register" — written by User task "Load
agreed actions and due dates into tracker"; read by User task "Pull
overdue-action report".
Data Object "Overdue Action Report" — written by Issue & Action
Tracking System message flow; read by User task "Initiate escalation
to remediation owner and risk manager".
Data Object "Progress Update" — written by User task "Submit progress
update and supporting evidence"; read by User task "Update action
status in tracker".
Data Object "Completion Evidence Package" — written by User task
"Confirm action closed to Risk & Compliance"; read by User task
"Confirm completion evidence received for each action".

V17.08 Track Remediation governs the monitoring and escalation of every
remediation action from the point the final report issues until all
actions are evidenced as complete. Risk & Compliance runs periodic
reviews, triggers escalation when deadlines are breached, and confirms
closure evidence; the Business Unit implements actions and submits
supporting evidence through the Issue & Action Tracking System. The
subprocess hands a fully evidenced, closed action register to V17.09
Verify & Close Findings.
```


### V17.09 — Verify & Close Findings

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.09 Verify & Close Findings — the ninth subprocess in the
Audit to Action value chain, in which Internal Audit retests remediated
controls, judges whether each finding is sufficiently resolved, and formally
closes or re-opens findings before handing a consolidated closure status to
Report to Committee.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Internal Audit Organisation" — the organisation running the
verification and closure process, containing all active lanes.
  Lane "Internal Audit (auditor)" — plans and executes retesting, reviews
  closure evidence, rates sufficiency, and records outcomes.
Pool "Audit Management System" — system of record for findings, test
results, and closure status.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — stores and retrieves closure evidence
submitted by remediation owners.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Internal Audit Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Evidence Repository" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Internal Audit Organisation (white-box, process owner)
2. Audit Management System
3. Evidence Repository

4. Lane contents in flow order (Internal Audit Organisation)

Internal Audit (auditor) lane:
  Message start event "Remediation due date reached — findings ready for
  verification, received from Track Remediation"
  Service task "Retrieve open findings and remediation evidence"
  Intermediate message catch event "Closure evidence received from
  remediation owner"
  User task "Review closure evidence for sufficiency"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient?"
  - branch "Yes — evidence meets standards":
      User task "Perform retest of control"
      Exclusive gateway "Retest passed?"
      - branch "Yes — control operating effectively":
          Service task "Record finding as closed in Audit Management System"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Retest outcome resolved")
      - branch "No — control still failing":
          User task "Document retest failure and rationale"
          Service task "Re-open finding and update status in Audit
          Management System"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Retest outcome resolved")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Retest outcome resolved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence decision resolved")
  - branch "No — evidence insufficient or missing":
      User task "Request additional or corrected evidence from remediation
      owner"
      Intermediate timer catch event "Evidence resubmission deadline (5
      business days)"
      Exclusive gateway "Resubmission received?"
      - branch "Yes — resubmission received":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence decision resolved")
      - branch "No — still not received":
          Service task "Escalate overdue finding in Audit Management System"
          End event "Finding escalated — overdue closure notified"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Resubmission received?"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence decision resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence decision resolved"
  Exclusive gateway "All findings processed?"
  - branch "No — further findings remain":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All findings check")
  - branch "Yes — all findings reviewed":
      User task "Prepare consolidated findings closure summary"
      Service task "Update assurance-coverage record in Audit Management
      System"
      End event "Findings closure summary complete — ready for Report to
      Committee"
  Exclusive merge gateway "All findings check"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review closure evidence for
sufficiency" — label "Overall verification deadline exceeded" — triggers
Service task "Escalate overdue finding in Audit Management System" and
leads to End event "Finding escalated — overdue closure notified".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Internal Audit (auditor) lane.
After the start event the auditor retrieves open findings, then waits for
closure evidence. The evidence-sufficiency gateway splits into the
sufficient branch (retest performed, retest-outcome merge, then
evidence-decision merge) and the insufficient branch (additional evidence
requested, timer wait, resubmission gateway splitting to evidence-decision
merge or escalation end event, then resubmission merge joining the
evidence-decision merge). The evidence-decision merge leads to the
all-findings gateway, whose "No" branch loops to the all-findings check
merge and whose "Yes" branch continues to the closure summary tasks and
the final end event.

Message flows:
Audit Management System → Internal Audit (auditor) "Retrieve open findings
and remediation evidence" (open findings list with remediation status and
due dates).
Evidence Repository → Internal Audit (auditor) "Review closure evidence for
sufficiency" (closure evidence packages submitted by remediation owners).
Internal Audit (auditor) "Record finding as closed in Audit Management
System" → Audit Management System (closure status update).
Internal Audit (auditor) "Re-open finding and update status in Audit
Management System" → Audit Management System (re-opened finding record
with retest failure details).
Internal Audit (auditor) "Escalate overdue finding in Audit Management
System" → Audit Management System (overdue escalation flag and audit
trail).
Internal Audit (auditor) "Update assurance-coverage record in Audit
Management System" → Audit Management System (assurance-coverage report
updated with all closure outcomes).
Internal Audit (auditor) "Review closure evidence for sufficiency" →
Evidence Repository (read request for stored closure evidence).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Open Findings List" — read by "Retrieve open findings and
remediation evidence".
Data Object "Closure Evidence Package" — read by "Review closure evidence
for sufficiency"; read by "Perform retest of control".
Data Object "Retest Results Record" — written by "Perform retest of
control"; read by "Record finding as closed in Audit Management System";
read by "Document retest failure and rationale".
Data Object "Findings Closure Summary" — written by "Prepare consolidated
findings closure summary"; read by "Update assurance-coverage record in
Audit Management System".

V17.09 Verify & Close Findings takes each remediated finding from the
tracking subprocess and subjects it to evidence review and control retest.
Findings that pass are formally closed in the Audit Management System;
those that fail are re-opened and re-escalated; those lacking evidence
trigger a time-boxed resubmission cycle with automatic escalation on
expiry. The subprocess concludes by assembling a consolidated closure
summary and updated assurance-coverage record, which V17.10 Report to
Committee uses as the basis for its status presentation to the Audit and
Risk Committee.
```


### V17.10 — Report to Committee

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V17.10 Report to Committee — the closing subprocess of the Audit
to Action value chain, in which Internal Audit presents consolidated
assurance status and remediation progress to the Audit and Risk Committee,
and obtains formal acknowledgement.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that prepare and deliver the
committee report.
  Lane "Internal Audit" — chief audit executive who assembles, reviews,
  presents and closes out the reporting cycle.
Lane "Audit & Risk Committee" — the governing body that receives,
  deliberates on and formally acknowledges the report.
Pool "Board Reporting System" — IT system that stores and distributes
  board and committee reporting packs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Audit & Risk Committee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Board Reporting System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Audit & Risk Committee
2. Organisation (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Internal Audit,
   Audit & Risk Committee)
3. Board Reporting System

Note: the Audit & Risk Committee pool sits above the Organisation pool to
represent the external governing body that triggers the reporting
obligation and receives the final output. The lane named "Audit & Risk
Committee" inside the Organisation pool models the committee's internal
process steps; the external pool models the committee as a participant.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Internal Audit lane:
  Message start event "Final report issued — ready for Report to Committee"
  User task "Compile consolidated assurance and remediation status pack"
  Service task "Retrieve prior findings status and overdue-action alerts
    from Board Reporting System"
  User task "Prepare committee reporting pack"
  Service task "Publish committee pack to Board Reporting System"
  Send task "Distribute committee pack to Audit and Risk Committee"
  Intermediate message catch event "Committee meeting convened"
  User task "Present assurance report and findings status to committee"
  Exclusive gateway "Committee satisfied with report?"
    - branch "Yes — no further information required":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Committee satisfied")
    - branch "No — additional information requested":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Additional Information Provided"
          (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Note committee queries and additional information
            requested",
          User task "Prepare and submit supplementary information"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Committee satisfied")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Committee satisfied"
  User task "Record committee deliberations and directions"
  Service task "Update Board Reporting System with committee outcomes"
  User task "Distribute formal committee acknowledgement to stakeholders"
  End event "Committee reporting complete — assurance cycle closed"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Additional Information Provided" — label "Supplementary information
deadline exceeded" — triggers End event "Reporting cycle escalated —
deadline not met".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Internal Audit lane with the message
start event and flows through pack compilation, retrieval, preparation,
publication, distribution, and the intermediate message catch event
waiting for the meeting. The presentation task leads to the exclusive
gateway "Committee satisfied with report?"; the "Yes" branch and the
looping subprocess branch both converge at the exclusive merge gateway
"Committee satisfied", after which deliberation recording, system update,
and acknowledgement distribution lead to the end event. The timer boundary
event on the loop subprocess exits to its own end event without rejoining
the main flow.

Message flows:
Board Reporting System → Internal Audit lane: Service task "Retrieve
  prior findings status and overdue-action alerts from Board Reporting
  System" (prior findings status, overdue-action alerts).
Internal Audit lane → Board Reporting System: Service task "Publish
  committee pack to Board Reporting System" (committee reporting pack).
Internal Audit lane → Audit & Risk Committee (external pool): Send task
  "Distribute committee pack to Audit and Risk Committee" (committee
  reporting pack).
Audit & Risk Committee (external pool) → Internal Audit lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Committee meeting convened"
  (meeting confirmation).
Internal Audit lane → Board Reporting System: Service task "Update Board
  Reporting System with committee outcomes" (committee deliberations and
  directions).
Internal Audit lane → Audit & Risk Committee (external pool): User task
  "Distribute formal committee acknowledgement to stakeholders"
  (formal committee acknowledgement).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Consolidated Assurance and Remediation Status Pack" —
  written by "Compile consolidated assurance and remediation status pack";
  read by "Prepare committee reporting pack".
Data Object "Committee Reporting Pack" — written by "Prepare committee
  reporting pack"; read by "Publish committee pack to Board Reporting
  System" and "Distribute committee pack to Audit and Risk Committee".
Data Object "Supplementary Information" — written by "Prepare and submit
  supplementary information"; read by "Note committee queries and
  additional information requested".
Data Object "Committee Deliberations and Directions" — written by "Record
  committee deliberations and directions"; read by "Update Board Reporting
  System with committee outcomes" and "Distribute formal committee
  acknowledgement to stakeholders".

This subprocess brings the Audit to Action chain to its formal close.
Internal Audit assembles consolidated findings, remediation status, and
overdue-action alerts into a committee reporting pack, presents it to the
Audit and Risk Committee, and handles any requests for supplementary
information before recording the committee's deliberations and directions.
The formal acknowledgement issued at the end confirms that the governing
body has sighted the assurance position, completing the cycle and
resetting the baseline for the next planning round.
```


## V18 — Draft to Publish

**Teams and roles involved.**
Draft to Publish usually involves Policy Owners, Risk and Compliance, Legal, Subject-Matter Experts, Document Control, Communications, Learning and Development, and the approving Executive or Board Committee. Key roles include policy author, policy owner, compliance manager, legal reviewer, document controller, communications lead, training coordinator, and approving executive.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Regulators, whose requirements drive much of the content, and where relevant Industry Bodies and external counsel. The process is initiated by a new or changed regulatory obligation, a scheduled policy review date, an audit or incident finding, or an organisational change. Other external parties include external legal advisers, standards bodies, and consultation participants.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: identify the need or trigger, assign an owner and scope the change, draft or revise the document, consult stakeholders and subject-matter experts, obtain legal and compliance review, obtain formal approval, publish and version the document, communicate the change, deliver training and capture attestations, and schedule the next review.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include document management with version control, policy and GRC platforms, workflow and approval tooling, intranet or knowledge portal, learning management system for training and attestation, obligations registers, and reporting on currency and attestation coverage.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the policy framework and document hierarchy, mandatory review cycles, approval authority matrix, version control and change history requirements, consultation requirements, mandatory training and attestation rules, retention of superseded versions, and communication standards for material changes.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Regulators and industry bodies provide obligations, guidance, consultation papers and deadlines; the process provides submissions, attestations and evidence of compliance where required. Consultation participants provide comments and objections and receive dispositions and the final published document.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates drafts, review comments and dispositions, approval records, published versions and effective dates, superseded versions, communication records, and training and attestation records. IT systems provide the obligations register, current document inventory and review dates, approval routing and audit trails, distribution lists, and attestation completion reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V18.01** Identify Need or Trigger | Regulator | Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Obligations Register |
| **V18.02** Assign Owner & Scope Change | — | Risk & Compliance (compliance manager), Policy Owner (policy owner) | Policy / GRC Platform |
| **V18.03** Draft or Revise Document | — | Policy Owner (policy author), Subject-Matter Experts (subject-matter expert) | Document Management System |
| **V18.04** Consult Stakeholders | Industry Body | Policy Owner (policy author), Business Unit (stakeholder representative) | Document Management System |
| **V18.05** Obtain Legal & Compliance Review | External Counsel | Legal (legal reviewer), Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Policy / GRC Platform |
| **V18.06** Obtain Formal Approval | Board Committee | Executive Management (approving executive) | Workflow & Approval System |
| **V18.07** Publish & Version | — | Document Control (document controller) | Document Management System, Intranet / Knowledge Portal |
| **V18.08** Communicate Change | — | Communications (communications lead) | Intranet / Knowledge Portal |
| **V18.09** Deliver Training & Capture Attestations | — | Learning & Development (training coordinator) | Learning Management System (LMS) |
| **V18.10** Schedule Next Review | — | Document Control (document controller), Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) | Policy / GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V18):

- **External actors:** Regulator (V18.01); Industry Body (V18.04); External Counsel (V18.05); Board Committee (V18.06).
- **Teams:** Risk & Compliance (V18.01, V18.02, V18.05, V18.10); Policy Owner (V18.02–V18.04); Subject-Matter Experts (V18.03); Business Unit (V18.04); Legal (V18.05); Executive Management (V18.06); Document Control (V18.07, V18.10); Communications (V18.08); Learning & Development (V18.09).
- **IT systems:** Obligations Register (V18.01); Policy / GRC Platform (V18.02, V18.05, V18.10); Document Management System (V18.03, V18.04, V18.07); Workflow & Approval System (V18.06); Intranet / Knowledge Portal (V18.07, V18.08); Learning Management System / LMS (V18.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V18 — Draft to Publish — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Draft to Publish value chain, covering everything from initial
regulatory trigger through to scheduled review. The canvas is arranged in
three horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top), BUSINESS
PROCESSES (middle), and APPLICATIONS (bottom). The demand-side actors
(Regulator, Industry Body, External Counsel, Board Committee) sit on the
far left; internal delivery teams occupy the centre; Document Control and
Risk & Compliance as scheduling actors sit on the far right. The view is
read top-to-bottom as service → process → application, expressing
ArchiMate service realisation.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Regulator: demand-side external actor, far left; triggers obligations
  and receives attestation evidence.
- Industry Body: demand-side external actor, far left; provides guidance
  and consultation papers during stakeholder consultation.
- External Counsel: demand-side external actor, far left; provides legal
  advice during legal and compliance review.
- Board Committee: demand-side external actor, far left; acts as formal
  approval authority.
- Document Control: internal delivery actor, far right; owns publishing
  and review scheduling.
- Risk & Compliance: internal delivery actor, far right; owns compliance
  review and next-review scheduling.

2. Interfaces

- Regulatory Intake Interface: accessed by Regulator; serves the
  Identify Need or Trigger business service.
- Industry Consultation Interface: accessed by Industry Body; serves the
  Consult Stakeholders business service.
- External Legal Advisory Interface: accessed by External Counsel; serves
  the Legal & Compliance Review business service.
- Board Approval Interface: accessed by Board Committee; serves the
  Formal Approval business service.
- Document Publication Interface: used by Document Control; serves the
  Publish & Version business service and connects to the Document
  Management System.
- Attestation Reporting Interface: used by Risk & Compliance; serves the
  Schedule Next Review business service and connects to the Policy / GRC
  Platform.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Regulatory Trigger & Obligation Identification Service: provides
  identification of new or changed regulatory obligations, audit findings,
  or scheduled review dates that initiate the chain.
- Owner Assignment & Scoping Service: provides formal assignment of a
  policy owner and scoping of the required change.
- Document Drafting & Revision Service: provides authoring and revision
  of policy documents with subject-matter expert input.
- Stakeholder Consultation Service: provides structured consultation with
  internal stakeholders and external industry participants.
- Legal & Compliance Review Service: provides independent legal and
  compliance assessment of draft documents.
- Formal Approval Service: provides routing and capture of executive or
  board-level approval decisions.
- Publish & Version Control Service: provides controlled publication,
  version numbering, and archiving of superseded documents.
- Change Communication Service: provides notification and distribution
  of published policy changes to affected audiences.
- Training & Attestation Service: provides delivery of training on the
  new or revised policy and capture of staff attestations.
- Review Scheduling Service: provides scheduling and registration of the
  next mandatory policy review date.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger: recognises the regulatory, audit,
  incident, or calendar trigger that initiates the policy lifecycle.
- V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change: formalises ownership and defines
  the scope of the required policy change or new document.
- V18.03 Draft or Revise Document: authors or revises the policy document
  with input from subject-matter experts.
- V18.04 Consult Stakeholders: circulates the draft for comment to
  internal stakeholders, business units, and external industry bodies.
- V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review: routes the draft to Legal and
  Risk & Compliance, incorporating external counsel where required.
- V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval: routes the reviewed document through
  the approval authority matrix to the approving executive or board
  committee.
- V18.07 Publish & Version: document controller publishes the approved
  document, assigns the version number, and archives the superseded
  version.
- V18.08 Communicate Change: communications lead distributes notification
  of the policy change to all affected audiences.
- V18.09 Deliver Training & Capture Attestations: learning and
  development delivers training and records staff attestations of
  understanding.
- V18.10 Schedule Next Review: document controller and compliance manager
  register the next mandatory review date in the GRC platform.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Obligations Register: records and tracks regulatory obligations and
  triggers that initiate the chain.
- Policy / GRC Platform: supports owner assignment, scoping, compliance
  review, and review scheduling; maintains the obligations register
  linkage and attestation reporting.
- Document Management System: stores and versions all draft and
  published documents; supports drafting, consultation, and publication
  workflows.
- Workflow & Approval System: manages approval routing, authority matrix
  enforcement, and audit trail for formal approval decisions.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal: hosts the published policy library and
  distributes change communications to staff.
- Learning Management System (LMS): delivers training courses linked to
  new or revised policies and records staff attestation completion.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Obligations Register SERVES V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review.
- Policy / GRC Platform SERVES V18.10 Schedule Next Review.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.03 Draft or Revise Document.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.04 Consult Stakeholders.
- Document Management System SERVES V18.07 Publish & Version.
- Workflow & Approval System SERVES V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal SERVES V18.07 Publish & Version.
- Intranet / Knowledge Portal SERVES V18.08 Communicate Change.
- Learning Management System SERVES V18.09 Deliver Training &
  Capture Attestations.

SERVING (business service serves business actor):
- Regulatory Trigger & Obligation Identification Service SERVES
  Regulator.
- Stakeholder Consultation Service SERVES Industry Body.
- Legal & Compliance Review Service SERVES External Counsel.
- Formal Approval Service SERVES Board Committee.
- Publish & Version Control Service SERVES Document Control.
- Review Scheduling Service SERVES Risk & Compliance.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger REALISES Regulatory Trigger &
  Obligation Identification Service.
- V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change REALISES Owner Assignment &
  Scoping Service.
- V18.03 Draft or Revise Document REALISES Document Drafting &
  Revision Service.
- V18.04 Consult Stakeholders REALISES Stakeholder Consultation
  Service.
- V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review REALISES Legal & Compliance
  Review Service.
- V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval REALISES Formal Approval Service.
- V18.07 Publish & Version REALISES Publish & Version Control Service.
- V18.08 Communicate Change REALISES Change Communication Service.
- V18.09 Deliver Training & Capture Attestations REALISES Training &
  Attestation Service.
- V18.10 Schedule Next Review REALISES Review Scheduling Service.

ASSIGNMENT (interface assigned to actor):
- Regulatory Intake Interface ASSIGNED TO Regulator.
- Industry Consultation Interface ASSIGNED TO Industry Body.
- External Legal Advisory Interface ASSIGNED TO External Counsel.
- Board Approval Interface ASSIGNED TO Board Committee.
- Document Publication Interface ASSIGNED TO Document Control.
- Attestation Reporting Interface ASSIGNED TO Risk & Compliance.

ACCESS (process or actor accesses application component):
- V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger ACCESSES Obligations Register
  (read).
- V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change ACCESSES Policy / GRC Platform
  (read-write).
- V18.03 Draft or Revise Document ACCESSES Document Management System
  (read-write).
- V18.04 Consult Stakeholders ACCESSES Document Management System
  (read-write).
- V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review ACCESSES Policy / GRC
  Platform (read-write).
- V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval ACCESSES Workflow & Approval System
  (read-write).
- V18.07 Publish & Version ACCESSES Document Management System
  (read-write).
- V18.07 Publish & Version ACCESSES Intranet / Knowledge Portal
  (write).
- V18.08 Communicate Change ACCESSES Intranet / Knowledge Portal
  (read-write).
- V18.09 Deliver Training & Capture Attestations ACCESSES Learning
  Management System (read-write).
- V18.10 Schedule Next Review ACCESSES Policy / GRC Platform
  (read-write).
- Regulator ACCESSES Obligations Register (read).
- Board Committee ACCESSES Workflow & Approval System (read-write).
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V18 - Draft to Publish

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, one chevron per stage, in the
order listed below. No chevron may be omitted or reordered.

V18.01. Identify Need or Trigger
V18.02. Assign Owner & Scope Change
V18.03. Draft or Revise Document
V18.04. Consult Stakeholders
V18.05. Obtain Legal & Compliance Review
V18.06. Obtain Formal Approval
V18.07. Publish & Version
V18.08. Communicate Change
V18.09. Deliver Training & Capture Attestations
V18.10. Schedule Next Review

This chain governs the end-to-end lifecycle of an organisational policy or
controlled document, from the moment a need is recognised through to the
scheduling of its next mandatory review. It is triggered externally by
Regulators — through a new or changed obligation, a consultation paper, or
a compliance deadline — or internally by a scheduled review date, an audit
finding, an incident, or an organisational change. The chain ensures that
every document is correctly scoped, drafted with subject-matter input,
reviewed by Legal and Compliance, formally approved at the right authority
level, versioned and published, communicated to affected staff, supported
by training and attestation evidence, and registered for future review.
```
### V18.01 — Identify Need or Trigger

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.01 Identify Need or Trigger — opening subprocess of the Draft to
Publish value chain, in which the organisation receives or detects a trigger
that necessitates a new or revised policy document.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation receiving and evaluating the trigger,
  with one internal lane.
  Lane "Risk & Compliance" (compliance manager)
Pool "Regulator" — external body whose obligations, guidance, and consultation
  papers drive policy change.
Pool "Obligations Register" — IT system holding the obligations inventory and
  review dates.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Regulator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Obligations Register" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Regulator
2. Organisation
3. Obligations Register

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message start event "Regulatory obligation, guidance, or consultation paper
    received from Regulator"
  User task "Log and categorise incoming trigger"
  Service task "Retrieve current obligations and policy inventory from
    Obligations Register"
  User task "Assess trigger against existing obligations inventory"
  Exclusive gateway "Does an existing obligation or policy cover this trigger?"
  - branch "Yes — existing coverage":
      User task "Record trigger as possible revision to existing policy"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Coverage determination complete")
  - branch "No — new obligation or gap":
      User task "Record trigger as requirement for new policy or document"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Coverage determination complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Coverage determination complete"
  User task "Determine urgency and preliminary priority"
  Exclusive gateway "Is the trigger urgent or deadline-driven?"
  - branch "Yes — urgent":
      User task "Flag trigger for expedited handling and note deadline"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Urgency classification resolved")
  - branch "No — standard timeline":
      User task "Schedule trigger for routine planning cycle"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Urgency classification resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Urgency classification resolved"
  User task "Compile trigger record and confirm readiness to scope"
  End event "Trigger identified and recorded — ready for Assign Owner and
    Scope Change"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Risk & Compliance lane on receipt of the
  message start event and proceeds linearly through logging, retrieval,
  assessment, and the first exclusive gateway whose two branches — existing
  coverage and new obligation — rejoin at the merge gateway "Coverage
  determination complete"; flow then continues through priority determination
  and the second exclusive gateway whose two branches — urgent and standard —
  rejoin at the merge gateway "Urgency classification resolved"; flow ends at
  the end event after the trigger record is compiled.

Message flows:
  Regulator → Risk & Compliance lane, Message start event "Regulatory
    obligation, guidance, or consultation paper received from Regulator"
    (obligation notice, guidance document, or consultation paper).
  Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Retrieve current obligations and
    policy inventory from Obligations Register" → Obligations Register
    (query for matching obligations and policy inventory).
  Obligations Register → Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Retrieve
    current obligations and policy inventory from Obligations Register"
    (current obligations list, policy inventory, and scheduled review dates).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Trigger Record" — written by "Log and categorise incoming
  trigger"; read by "Assess trigger against existing obligations inventory";
  updated by "Record trigger as possible revision to existing policy" and
  "Record trigger as requirement for new policy or document"; read and
  finalised by "Compile trigger record and confirm readiness to scope".
Data Object "Obligations and Policy Inventory" — written by "Retrieve current
  obligations and policy inventory from Obligations Register"; read by
  "Assess trigger against existing obligations inventory".

This subprocess captures the originating signal — a regulatory obligation,
guidance document, consultation paper, audit finding, or scheduled review
date — and converts it into a structured trigger record that classifies
whether a new policy is needed or an existing one requires revision, and
flags urgency and deadline. The completed trigger record is handed to
Assign Owner and Scope Change, which will nominate a policy owner and
define the boundaries of the required change.
```


### V18.02 — Assign Owner & Scope Change

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.02 Assign Owner & Scope Change — second subprocess in the
Draft to Publish value chain, receiving a validated trigger from Identify
Need or Trigger and handing a scoped change brief to Draft or Revise
Document.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that assign ownership and scope
the required change.
  Lane "Risk & Compliance" — compliance manager who receives the trigger,
  assigns the policy owner, and confirms the scope record.
  Lane "Policy Owner" — policy owner who accepts the assignment, defines
  the scope, and signs off the scope brief.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — workflow and obligations register used to
record the assignment and scope.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Risk & Compliance,
   Policy Owner)
2. Policy / GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Message start event "Validated trigger received from Identify Need
    or Trigger"
  User task "Review trigger and determine policy area"
  Service task "Retrieve current policy record from Policy / GRC Platform"
  User task "Identify and nominate policy owner"
  Send task "Issue assignment notification to Policy Owner"
  Intermediate message catch event "Scope brief received from Policy Owner"
  User task "Review and confirm scope brief"
  Exclusive gateway "Scope acceptable?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Record confirmed scope in Policy /
      GRC Platform"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scope acceptable")
  - branch "No — revise": Send task "Return scope brief with comments
      to Policy Owner"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Scope acceptable")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scope acceptable"
  Exclusive gateway "Scope confirmed?"
  - branch "Confirmed": End event "Scope confirmed — ready for Draft
      or Revise Document"
  - branch "Awaiting revision": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Scope confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Scope confirmed"
  Intermediate message catch event "Revised scope brief received from
    Policy Owner"
  User task "Review revised scope brief"
  (continues to exclusive gateway "Scope acceptable?")

Policy Owner lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Assignment notification received"
  User task "Accept or decline assignment"
  Exclusive gateway "Assignment accepted?"
  - branch "Accepted": User task "Define scope of change"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assignment accepted")
  - branch "Declined — propose alternative": Send task "Notify Risk
      and Compliance of decline and propose alternative"
      End event "Assignment declined — returned to Risk and Compliance"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Assignment accepted"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Scope Brief Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: User task "Draft scope brief", User task
    "Self-review scope brief against trigger"
  Send task "Submit scope brief to Risk and Compliance"
  Intermediate message catch event "Scope feedback received from
    Risk and Compliance"
  User task "Revise scope brief per feedback"
  Send task "Resubmit revised scope brief to Risk and Compliance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Scope Brief Complete", labelled "Scope brief overdue (5 business days)",
  leading to End event "Scope brief timeout — escalated to Risk and
  Compliance".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Risk & Compliance lane the flow runs from the
message start event through trigger review, policy record retrieval,
owner nomination and assignment notification, then waits at the
intermediate catch event for the scope brief, proceeds through the
"Scope acceptable?" gateway — the "Yes" branch records the confirmed scope
and merges; the "No" branch returns comments and merges — then the
"Scope confirmed?" gateway tests for confirmation, with the confirmed
branch reaching the end event and the awaiting-revision branch merging
back after receiving the revised scope brief and re-entering review.
Within the Policy Owner lane the flow runs from the assignment catch
event through acceptance, the scope brief loop subprocess, submission,
feedback receipt, revision and resubmission, rejoining the Risk and
Compliance review path.

Message flows:
Policy / GRC Platform → Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Retrieve
  current policy record from Policy / GRC Platform" (current policy
  record and obligations data).
Risk & Compliance lane, Service task "Record confirmed scope in Policy /
  GRC Platform" → Policy / GRC Platform (confirmed scope brief and
  assignment record).
Risk & Compliance lane, Send task "Issue assignment notification to
  Policy Owner" → Policy Owner lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Assignment notification received" (assignment instruction).
Policy Owner lane, Send task "Submit scope brief to Risk and Compliance"
  → Risk & Compliance lane, Intermediate message catch event "Scope brief
  received from Policy Owner" (scope brief).
Risk & Compliance lane, Send task "Return scope brief with comments to
  Policy Owner" → Policy Owner lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Scope feedback received from Risk and Compliance" (review comments).
Policy Owner lane, Send task "Resubmit revised scope brief to Risk and
  Compliance" → Risk & Compliance lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Revised scope brief received from Policy Owner" (revised scope brief).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Trigger Record" — read by User task "Review trigger and
  determine policy area".
Data Object "Current Policy Record" — read by User task "Review trigger
  and determine policy area"; written by Service task "Retrieve current
  policy record from Policy / GRC Platform".
Data Object "Assignment Notification" — written by Send task "Issue
  assignment notification to Policy Owner"; read by Intermediate message
  catch event "Assignment notification received".
Data Object "Scope Brief" — written by Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Scope Brief Complete"; read by User task "Review and confirm scope brief".
Data Object "Confirmed Scope Record" — written by Service task "Record
  confirmed scope in Policy / GRC Platform".

V18.02 takes the validated trigger produced by Identify Need or Trigger
and ensures that a named policy owner is formally assigned and that the
required change is bounded by an agreed scope brief before any drafting
begins. The compliance manager nominates and notifies the owner, the owner
drafts and iterates the scope brief, and Risk and Compliance confirm it
against the original trigger before recording the outcome in the Policy /
GRC Platform. The confirmed scope record and assignment then pass to Draft
or Revise Document.
```


### V18.03 — Draft or Revise Document

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.03 Draft or Revise Document — the subprocess in which the
Policy Owner and Subject-Matter Experts produce or update a policy document,
iterating until the draft is complete and ready for stakeholder consultation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation authoring and managing the policy,
  containing the lanes for Policy Owner and Subject-Matter Experts.
  Lanes top to bottom:
  - Policy Owner (policy author)
  - Subject-Matter Experts (subject-matter expert)
Pool "Document Management System" — IT system storing drafts, version
  history, and document metadata.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box)
2. Document Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Policy Owner lane:
  Message start event "Scoped change record received from Assign Owner
    & Scope Change"
  Service task "Retrieve current document version and scope record"
  Exclusive gateway "New document or revision?"
  - branch "new document": User task "Create document structure from
      template"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Document or revision ready")
  - branch "revision": User task "Load existing document for revision"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Document or revision ready")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Document or revision ready"
  User task "Draft or revise document content"
  Send task "Share draft sections with Subject-Matter Experts"
  Intermediate message catch event "SME input received"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Draft Complete" (standard loop)
    containing, in order:
    User task "Review SME comments and proposed edits",
    User task "Incorporate accepted changes into draft",
    Exclusive gateway "Further SME input needed?"
    - branch "yes": Send task "Request further clarification from
        Subject-Matter Experts"
        (loop repeats)
    - branch "no": (exits subprocess)
  User task "Apply document formatting and version control metadata"
  Service task "Save draft to Document Management System"
  User task "Conduct internal quality check on draft"
  Exclusive gateway "Draft meets quality threshold?"
  - branch "no": User task "Log quality issues and return draft for
      rework"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quality check resolved")
  - branch "yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Quality check resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quality check resolved"
  End event "Completed draft ready for Consult Stakeholders"

Subject-Matter Experts lane:
  User task "Review assigned draft sections"
  User task "Provide subject-matter comments and proposed edits"
  Send task "Return input to Policy Owner"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Timer boundary event (interrupting) on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Draft Complete" — label "SME review deadline exceeded" — triggers User
  task "Escalate overdue review to compliance manager" in Policy Owner
  lane, leading to End event "Draft escalated — process paused pending
  resolution".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Policy Owner lane at the message start
  event, passes through retrieval and the new-or-revision gateway whose
  branches merge before drafting begins, then moves to sharing the draft
  with Subject-Matter Experts and awaiting their input; the standard-loop
  subprocess iterates until no further SME input is needed; flow continues
  through formatting, saving, and quality checking, whose two branches
  merge before reaching the end event. The Subject-Matter Experts lane
  sequence runs: review sections → provide comments → return input,
  connected internally in that lane.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Service task "Retrieve current document version and scope
    record") → Document Management System (current document and scope
    record requested).
  Document Management System → Organisation (Service task "Retrieve
    current document version and scope record") (current document version
    and scope record returned).
  Organisation (Service task "Save draft to Document Management System")
    → Document Management System (draft document with version metadata
    saved).
  Organisation (Policy Owner lane: Send task "Share draft sections with
    Subject-Matter Experts") → Organisation (Subject-Matter Experts lane:
    User task "Review assigned draft sections") (draft sections for
    review).
  Organisation (Subject-Matter Experts lane: Send task "Return input to
    Policy Owner") → Organisation (Policy Owner lane: Intermediate message
    catch event "SME input received") (subject-matter comments and edits).
  Organisation (Policy Owner lane: Send task "Request further
    clarification from Subject-Matter Experts") → Organisation
    (Subject-Matter Experts lane: User task "Review assigned draft
    sections") (clarification request).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Scoped Change Record" — read by User task "Draft or revise
  document content"; read by User task "Create document structure from
  template"; read by User task "Load existing document for revision".
Data Object "Policy Draft" — written by User task "Draft or revise
  document content"; written by User task "Incorporate accepted changes
  into draft"; written by User task "Apply document formatting and version
  control metadata"; read by Service task "Save draft to Document
  Management System"; read by User task "Conduct internal quality check
  on draft".
Data Object "SME Comments" — written by User task "Provide subject-matter
  comments and proposed edits"; read by User task "Review SME comments
  and proposed edits".
Data Object "Quality Check Log" — written by User task "Log quality
  issues and return draft for rework"; read by User task "Draft or revise
  document content".

V18.03 Draft or Revise Document takes the scoped change record produced
in V18.02 and produces a quality-checked, formatted policy draft saved
under version control in the Document Management System. The Policy Owner
drives the drafting cycle, iterating with Subject-Matter Experts until the
content is accurate and complete, then verifies it meets internal quality
standards. The finished draft is handed to V18.04 Consult Stakeholders
for broader review and comment.
```


### V18.04 — Consult Stakeholders

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.04 Consult Stakeholders — the fourth subprocess in the Draft to
Publish value chain, sitting between Draft or Revise Document and Obtain Legal
& Compliance Review.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation managing the consultation process,

Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Industry Body
2. Organisation (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Policy Owner, Business Unit)
3. Document Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Policy Owner lane:
  Message start event "Reviewed draft received from Draft or Revise Document"
  User task "Identify consultation scope and stakeholder list"
  User task "Prepare consultation package"

  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "External industry body

  Exclusive merge gateway "External industry body input required"

  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Material changes

  Exclusive merge gateway "Material changes required"

Business Unit lane:

  User task "Submit comments and objections"

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Policy Owner lane, flow runs start event to

  consultation package", then "Distribute consultation package to
  stakeholders", then the intermediate catch event "Stakeholder comments
  received", then "Collate and review all comments", then the exclusive
  gateway "External industry body input required?", branching to "Submit
  consultation request to Industry Body" (then "Industry Body response

  then "Record dispositions in Document Management System", then "Material
  changes required?", branching to "Return draft for revision to Policy
  Author" ending at the material-changes end event on Yes, or rejoining the

  consultation record to Document Management System", then the completion end
  event. Within the Business Unit lane, flow runs "Review consultation
  package" to "Submit comments and objections" to "Disposition of comments

Message flows:
  Organisation (Policy Owner — "Distribute consultation package to
    stakeholders") → Business Unit lane (triggers "Review consultation
    package") (consultation package).
  Business Unit lane ("Submit comments and objections") → Organisation
    (Policy Owner — feeds "Stakeholder comments received") (stakeholder
    comments and objections).
  Organisation (Policy Owner — "Assess and disposition all comments") →

  Organisation (Policy Owner — "Record dispositions in Document Management

  Organisation (Policy Owner — "Upload final consultation record to Document
    Management System") → Document Management System (final consultation

  Document Management System → Organisation (Policy Owner — "Prepare

7. Data objects

Data Object "Consultation Package" — written by "Prepare consultation
  package"; read by "Distribute consultation package to stakeholders"; read
  by "Review consultation package".
Data Object "Stakeholder Comment Register" — written by "Collate and review
  all comments"; written by "Submit comments and objections"; read by "Assess
  and disposition all comments".
Data Object "Comment Disposition Record" — written by "Assess and disposition
  all comments"; read by "Record dispositions in Document Management System";
  read by "Disposition of comments received".
Data Object "Final Consultation Record" — written by "Finalise consultation
  record"; read by "Upload final consultation record to Document Management
  System".

V18.04 Consult Stakeholders gathers structured input from internal business
units and, where relevant, external industry bodies on the current policy
draft, then assesses and dispositions every comment received. Where those
comments reveal material gaps or errors the draft is returned to the Policy
Owner for revision; otherwise a finalised consultation record is lodged in
the Document Management System. The subprocess hands a consultation-cleared
draft and its full disposition record to V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance
Review.
```


### V18.05 — Obtain Legal & Compliance Review

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.05 Obtain Legal & Compliance Review — sits between stakeholder
consultation and formal approval in the Draft to Publish value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes
```
