```text
  Legal (legal reviewer) and Risk & Compliance (compliance manager) lanes.
Pool "External Counsel" — external legal advisers engaged for specialist
  review.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — workflow and records system that routes review
  tasks and stores dispositions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Counsel" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "External Counsel" — top.
Pool "Organisation" — middle (white-box).
Pool "Policy / GRC Platform" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Consulted document received from Consult Stakeholders"
  Service task "Retrieve current document version from Policy / GRC Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "External counsel required?"
  - branch "Yes": Send task "Commission external counsel review"
    Intermediate message catch event "External counsel opinion received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "External counsel required")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "External counsel
    required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "External counsel required"
  User task "Conduct legal review and annotate document"
  User task "Record legal review outcome in Policy / GRC Platform"
  Send task "Send legal review package to Risk and Compliance lane"

Risk & Compliance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Legal review package received"
  User task "Conduct compliance review against obligations register"
  User task "Record compliance review outcome in Policy / GRC Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Issues identified?"
  - branch "No issues": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Issues
    identified")
  - branch "Issues identified": User task "Raise review findings and return
    document to policy author"
    End event "Document returned to author — exits to Draft or Revise Document"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Issues identified"
  User task "Prepare consolidated review disposition"
  End event "Legal and compliance clearance confirmed — ready for Obtain
    Formal Approval"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Conduct legal review and annotate
  document" — label "Legal review deadline exceeded" — triggers Send task
  "Issue review overdue escalation to compliance manager", then End event
  "Escalation raised".
Interrupting timer boundary event on "Conduct compliance review against
  obligations register" — label "Compliance review deadline exceeded" —
  triggers Send task "Issue compliance review overdue escalation", then End
  event "Escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with document retrieval, passes
  through the external-counsel gateway and its merge, then through legal review
  and recording, before crossing to the Risk & Compliance lane via a message
  catch event; the compliance review follows, reaching the issues gateway whose
  "no issues" branch merges and continues to disposition and the clearance end
  event, while the "issues identified" branch ends separately.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Legal lane, Send task "Commission external counsel review") →
    External Counsel (request for specialist legal opinion).
  External Counsel → Organisation (Legal lane, Intermediate message catch event
    "External counsel opinion received") (external counsel opinion).
  Policy / GRC Platform → Organisation (Legal lane, Service task "Retrieve
    current document version from Policy / GRC Platform") (current document
    version and review metadata).
  Organisation (Legal lane, User task "Record legal review outcome in Policy /
    GRC Platform") → Policy / GRC Platform (legal review outcome and

  Organisation (Risk & Compliance lane, User task "Record compliance review

7. Data objects

Data Object "Document Review Package" — written by "Conduct legal review and
  annotate document"; read by "Send legal review package to Risk and
  Compliance lane"; read by "Conduct compliance review against obligations

Data Object "External Counsel Opinion" — read by "Conduct legal review and
  annotate document".
Data Object "Consolidated Review Disposition" — written by "Prepare
  consolidated review disposition"; read by the clearance end event transition
  to Obtain Formal Approval.
Data Object "Review Findings Notice" — written by "Raise review findings and
  return document to policy author".

V18.05 coordinates the legal and compliance review of a consulted document,
routing it through external counsel where specialist opinion is needed, then
through internal legal annotation and compliance checking against the
obligations register. Issues that cannot be resolved in this subprocess return
the document to drafting; a clean disposition produces a consolidated clearance
record that is handed to Obtain Formal Approval as the confirmed basis for the
approving executive or Board Committee to act on.
```


### V18.06 — Obtain Formal Approval

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.06 Obtain Formal Approval — the subprocess in which the
approving executive and Board Committee formally review and approve or
reject the compliance-reviewed document before it is published.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that route, present and act on
  the approval decision.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Executive Management (approving executive)
  - Document Control (document controller)
Pool "Board Committee" — the governing body that makes the formal approval
  decision.
Pool "Workflow & Approval System" — the system that routes the approval
  package, records decisions and maintains the audit trail.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Board Committee" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Workflow & Approval System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Board Committee
2. Organisation (white-box; Executive Management lane above Document
   Control lane)
3. Workflow & Approval System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Executive Management lane:
  Message start event "Compliance-reviewed document received from Obtain
    Legal and Compliance Review"
  User task "Review compliance-reviewed document and prepare approval
    package"
  Service task "Submit approval package to Workflow and Approval System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received from Board
    Committee"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision?"
  - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision")
  - branch "Rejected with conditions": User task "Record conditions and
    return document for revision"
    End event "Document returned for revision — exits to Draft or Revise
      Document"
  - branch "Deferred": User task "Record deferral and schedule
    resubmission"
    Intermediate timer catch event "Resubmission date reached"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision"
  User task "Endorse approval record and confirm effective date"
  Send task "Notify Document Control of approval outcome"

Document Control lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Approval outcome received from
    Executive Management"
  Service task "Record approval decision and effective date in Workflow
    and Approval System"
  End event "Approval confirmed — ready for Publish and Version"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review
  compliance-reviewed document and prepare approval package", labelled
  "Preparation deadline exceeded", leading to End event "Escalation
  raised — exits subprocess for management attention".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Executive Management lane at the
  message start event, proceeds through document review and package
  submission, then waits at the intermediate message catch event for the
  Board Committee decision. The exclusive gateway "Decision?" branches
  to three paths: the approved branch and the deferred branch (after a
  timer catch event) both rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway
  "Decision"; the rejected-with-conditions branch ends in its own end
  event and does not rejoin. After the merge, the Executive Management
  lane ends with the endorsement task and send task, whose message
  triggers the Document Control lane, which records the outcome and
  reaches the subprocess end event.

Message flows:
  Service task "Submit approval package to Workflow and Approval System"
    → Workflow & Approval System (approval package for routing and
    audit trail)
  Workflow & Approval System → Board Committee (routed approval package
    for formal review)
  Board Committee → Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision
    received from Board Committee" (formal approval decision)
  Service task "Record approval decision and effective date in Workflow
    and Approval System" → Workflow & Approval System (approved

  Workflow & Approval System → Service task "Record approval decision
    and effective date in Workflow and Approval System" (confirmation

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approval Package" — written by User task "Review
  compliance-reviewed document and prepare approval package"; read by

Data Object "Deferral Notice" — written by User task "Record deferral
  and schedule resubmission"; read by Intermediate timer catch event
  "Resubmission date reached".
Data Object "Revision Instructions" — written by User task "Record
  conditions and return document for revision"; read at End event
  "Document returned for revision — exits to Draft or Revise Document".

This subprocess takes the compliance-reviewed document and routes it
through the organisation's formal approval authority, culminating in a
recorded Board Committee decision. An approved outcome, complete with
confirmed effective date and a full audit trail in the Workflow and
Approval System, is handed to Publish and Version so that the document
can be released. Rejections exit back to drafting with conditions
attached, and deferrals are held until a rescheduled resubmission date
before rejoining the approval flow.
```

### V18.07 — Publish & Version

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V18.07 Publish & Version — the subprocess in the Draft to Publish
value chain that takes an approved document, assigns it a version number,
publishes it to the intranet and document repository, and retires the
superseded version, handing a live, versioned document to the
Communicate Change subprocess.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the publish and version
process, containing Document Control.
- Lane "Document Control (document controller)"
Pool "Document Management System" — system of record for document
versions, history, and repository.
Pool "Intranet / Knowledge Portal" — internal publishing platform where
staff access current policies.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Document Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Intranet / Knowledge Portal" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation
2. Document Management System
3. Intranet / Knowledge Portal

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Document Control (document controller) lane:
  Message start event "Approved document received from Obtain Formal
    Approval"
  User task "Retrieve approved document and approval record"
  User task "Assign version number and update change history"
  Service task "Register new version in Document Management System"
  Service task "Retrieve current published version from Document
    Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Is a prior published version superseded?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Archive superseded version in Document
      Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Prior version handled")
    - branch "No — first issue": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Prior version handled")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Prior version handled"
  User task "Set effective date and document metadata"
  Service task "Publish document to Intranet / Knowledge Portal"
  User task "Confirm publication and record publish event"
  Exclusive gateway "Publication confirmed successfully?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Publication
      outcome resolved")
    - branch "No — error detected": User task "Investigate and
      resolve publication error"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Publication outcome
      resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Publication outcome resolved"
  End event "Document published and versioned — ready for
    Communicate Change"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Publish document to Intranet /
Knowledge Portal" — label "Publication overdue", triggered if
publication has not completed within the expected window; leads to
User task "Escalate publication delay to Document Control manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Document Control lane,
from the message start event through retrieval, versioning, and system
registration, then through the exclusive gateway "Is a prior published
version superseded?" whose "Yes" branch passes through archiving and
whose "No" branch bypasses it, both rejoining at the exclusive merge
gateway "Prior version handled"; flow continues through metadata
setting, portal publication, and confirmation, then through the
exclusive gateway "Publication confirmed successfully?" whose "Yes"
branch and "No — error detected" branch (via error resolution) both
rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Publication outcome resolved"
before the end event.

Message flows:
Document Management System → Organisation / Document Control
  (approved document and current version record retrieved at start)
Organisation / Document Control → Document Management System
  (new version number, change history entry, and archived superseded
  version written to repository)
Document Management System → Organisation / Document Control
  (confirmation of version registration and archive action)
Organisation / Document Control → Intranet / Knowledge Portal
  (published document with effective date and metadata)
Intranet / Knowledge Portal → Organisation / Document Control
  (publication confirmation or error notification)

Data Object "Approved Document" — read by "Retrieve approved document

Data Object "Version and Change History Record" — written by "Assign
  version number and update change history"; read by "Register new

  effective date and document metadata"; read by "Publish document to

This subprocess takes the formally approved document and gives it an
official version number, records its change history, retires the
superseded version to the archive, sets the effective date, and
publishes the live document to the Intranet / Knowledge Portal.
On completion it hands the published, versioned document to the
Communicate Change subprocess so that staff and stakeholders can be
notified of the new or revised policy.
```

## V19 — Request to Access

**Teams and roles involved.**
Request to Access usually involves IT Service Desk, Identity and Access Management, Application and System Owners, Line Managers, Security, HR, and Internal Audit for periodic review. Key roles include requester, approving line manager, application owner, access administrator, identity engineer, security officer, and access-review certifier.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Contractors, Partners and Vendors who need access to organisational systems, and the Auditor who tests the controls. The process is initiated by a joiner, mover or leaver event, a project or engagement starting, a privileged-access request, or a scheduled access recertification. Other external parties include managed service providers and identity federation partners.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: raise the access request, validate identity and employment or engagement status, determine the entitlements required, check for segregation-of-duties conflicts, obtain approvals, provision the access, notify and confirm with the requester, review access periodically, revoke on change or exit, and evidence the whole cycle for audit.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include identity and access management, single sign-on and directory services, privileged access management, IT service management for requests, HR systems as the source of truth for people, application-level entitlement stores, access-review/certification tooling, and logging for audit evidence.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the access control policy, least-privilege and need-to-know principles, role definitions and entitlement catalogues, segregation-of-duties matrix, approval authority, privileged access rules and time limits, joiner/mover/leaver procedure, periodic recertification frequency, and revocation timeframes on termination.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Contractors and partners provide identity evidence, engagement details and acceptance of acceptable-use terms, and receive credentials, access confirmations and revocation notices. Auditors receive access registers, approval evidence, recertification results and exception reports.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates access requests, approvals, entitlement grants and revocations, segregation-of-duties exceptions, recertification decisions, and audit evidence. IT systems provide employment and engagement status, the entitlement catalogue and role definitions, current access holdings, conflict detection results, provisioning status, and orphaned or dormant account reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V19.01** Raise Access Request | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.02** Validate Identity & Status | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent), Human Resources (HR officer) | HR System, Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.03** Determine Entitlements Required | — | Identity & Access Management (identity engineer), Application Owner (application owner) | Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.04** Check Segregation of Duties | — | Security (security officer) | Identity & Access Management, GRC Platform |
| **V19.05** Obtain Approvals | — | Line Management (approving line manager), Application Owner (application owner) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.06** Provision Access | — | Identity & Access Management (access administrator) | Identity & Access Management, Directory Services |
| **V19.07** Notify & Confirm with Requester | Contractor | IT Service Desk (service desk agent) | IT Service Management |
| **V19.08** Review Access Periodically | — | Application Owner (access-review certifier), Security (security officer) | Access Certification Platform |
| **V19.09** Revoke on Change or Exit | — | Human Resources (HR officer), Identity & Access Management (access administrator) | HR System, Identity & Access Management |
| **V19.10** Evidence for Audit | Auditor | Security (security officer), Internal Audit (auditor) | Access Certification Platform, GRC Platform |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V19):

- **External actors:** Contractor (V19.01, V19.02, V19.07); Auditor (V19.10).
- **Teams:** IT Service Desk (V19.01, V19.02, V19.07); Human Resources (V19.02, V19.09); Identity & Access Management (V19.03, V19.06, V19.09); Application Owner (V19.03, V19.05, V19.08); Security (V19.04, V19.08, V19.10); Line Management (V19.05); Internal Audit (V19.10).
- **IT systems:** IT Service Management (V19.01, V19.05, V19.07); HR System (V19.02, V19.09); Identity & Access Management (V19.02–V19.04, V19.06, V19.09); GRC Platform (V19.04, V19.10); Directory Services (V19.06); Access Certification Platform (V19.08, V19.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V19 — Request to Access — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Request to Access value chain, covering the full lifecycle from initial
access request through periodic review, revocation, and audit evidence. The
diagram is organised in three horizontal bands read top-to-bottom as service
realisation: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) expresses what the organisation
delivers to requesters and auditors; BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows
the ten subprocesses that realise those services; APPLICATIONS (bottom band)
shows the IT systems that support those processes. The Contractor sits on the
far left as the primary demand-side actor initiating access requests and
receiving confirmations; the Auditor sits on the far right as the external
assurance actor receiving audit evidence.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Contractor: demand-side actor, far left; initiates access requests, provides
  identity evidence, receives credentials and revocation notices.
- Auditor: assurance actor, far right; receives access registers, approval
  evidence, recertification results and exception reports.
- IT Service Desk: internal team, left of centre; handles request intake,
  identity validation and requester notification.
- Human Resources: internal team, left of centre; provides employment and
  engagement status; drives joiner/mover/leaver events.
- Identity & Access Management: internal team, centre; determines entitlements,
  provisions access, and executes revocations.
- Application Owner: internal team, centre; confirms entitlements required and
  certifies periodic access reviews.
- Security: internal team, centre-right; checks segregation of duties and
  participates in periodic review and audit evidence.
- Line Management: internal team, centre; provides approval authority for
  access grants.
- Internal Audit: internal team, far right; reviews audit evidence alongside the
  external Auditor.

2. Interfaces

- Access Request Interface: used by Contractor (ACCESSES) to submit access
  requests; serves the Access Request Handling service.
- Approval Interface: used by Line Management and Application Owner (ACCESSES)
  to submit and record approvals; serves the Access Approval service.
- Notification Interface: used by IT Service Desk (ACCESSES) to send
  credentials and confirmations to Contractor; serves the Requester
  Notification service.
- Audit Evidence Interface: used by Auditor and Internal Audit (ACCESSES) to
  retrieve access registers and recertification reports; serves the Audit
  Evidence service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Access Request Handling: provides a structured channel for requesters to
  raise and track access requests.
- Identity Validation: provides verification of requester identity, employment
  or engagement status against authoritative sources.
- Entitlement Determination: provides mapping of business role to the
  entitlements and permissions required.
- Segregation of Duties Checking: provides conflict detection against the
  segregation-of-duties matrix before access is granted.
- Access Approval: provides a governed approval workflow capturing line-manager
  and application-owner sign-off.
- Access Provisioning: provides automated or administered provisioning of
  approved entitlements to target systems and directories.
- Requester Notification: provides timely confirmation of access grant or
  rejection, including credential delivery.
- Access Recertification: provides periodic certification campaigns to confirm
  or revoke continuing access entitlements.
- Access Revocation: provides timely revocation of access on change-of-role or
  exit events.
- Audit Evidence: provides compiled access registers, approval logs,
  recertification results and exception reports for audit consumption.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, left to right

- V19.01 Raise Access Request: requester or IT Service Desk logs the access
  request in the service management tool.
- V19.02 Validate Identity & Status: IT Service Desk and HR verify identity
  evidence and confirm employment or engagement status.
- V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required: Identity & Access Management and
  Application Owner identify the specific entitlements needed.
- V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties: Security evaluates the request against
  the segregation-of-duties matrix and flags conflicts.
- V19.05 Obtain Approvals: Line Management and Application Owner formally
  approve or reject the access request.
- V19.06 Provision Access: Identity & Access Management administrator
  provisions approved entitlements to directory and target systems.
- V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester: IT Service Desk sends access
  confirmation, credentials or rejection notice to the requester.
- V19.08 Review Access Periodically: Application Owner and Security certify
  current access holdings and revoke where no longer justified.
- V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit: HR triggers and Identity & Access Management
  executes timely revocation of access on role change or termination.
- V19.10 Evidence for Audit: Security and Internal Audit compile and present
  access logs, approvals and recertification records to the Auditor.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band, left to right

- IT Service Management: records and tracks access requests, approvals and
  notifications throughout the request lifecycle.
- HR System: authoritative source of employment and engagement status; triggers
  joiner, mover and leaver events.
- Identity & Access Management: manages entitlement catalogue, role
  definitions, access grants, conflict detection and revocations.
- GRC Platform: hosts the segregation-of-duties matrix and stores audit
  evidence and exception records.
- Directory Services: stores and enforces provisioned entitlements and account
  credentials in target directories.
- Access Certification Platform: runs periodic recertification campaigns and
  records certifier decisions for audit.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application components serve business processes):
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.01 Raise Access Request
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- IT Service Management SERVES V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester
- HR System SERVES V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- HR System SERVES V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.06 Provision Access
- Identity & Access Management SERVES V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- GRC Platform SERVES V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- GRC Platform SERVES V19.10 Evidence for Audit
- Directory Services SERVES V19.06 Provision Access
- Access Certification Platform SERVES V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Access Certification Platform SERVES V19.10 Evidence for Audit

REALISATION (business processes realise business services):
- V19.01 Raise Access Request REALISES Access Request Handling
- V19.02 Validate Identity & Status REALISES Identity Validation
- V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required REALISES Entitlement Determination
- V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties REALISES Segregation of Duties Checking
- V19.05 Obtain Approvals REALISES Access Approval
- V19.06 Provision Access REALISES Access Provisioning
- V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester REALISES Requester Notification
- V19.08 Review Access Periodically REALISES Access Recertification
- V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit REALISES Access Revocation
- V19.10 Evidence for Audit REALISES Audit Evidence

ASSIGNMENT (actors assigned to processes):
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.01 Raise Access Request
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- IT Service Desk ASSIGNED TO V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester
- Human Resources ASSIGNED TO V19.02 Validate Identity & Status
- Human Resources ASSIGNED TO V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.06 Provision Access
- Identity & Access Management ASSIGNED TO V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.03 Determine Entitlements Required
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- Application Owner ASSIGNED TO V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.08 Review Access Periodically
- Security ASSIGNED TO V19.10 Evidence for Audit
- Line Management ASSIGNED TO V19.05 Obtain Approvals
- Internal Audit ASSIGNED TO V19.10 Evidence for Audit

ACCESS (external actors access interfaces and services):

- Contractor ACCESSES Notification Interface
- Access Request Interface SERVES Access Request Handling
- Notification Interface SERVES Requester Notification
- Auditor ACCESSES Audit Evidence Interface

- Approval Interface SERVES Access Approval
```

```text
Value Chain V19 - Request to Access

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of high-level process stages as

moment a joiner, mover, leaver, or engagement-start event triggers an
access request through to provisioning, periodic recertification, revocation,
and the production of audit evidence. The main external participants are
Contractors and Partners who initiate requests and receive credentials, and
the Auditor who tests controls against the evidence produced. The chain
closes when all access activity for a given identity has been evidenced and
confirmed fit for audit.
```

### V19.01 — Raise Access Request

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.01 Raise Access Request — the opening subprocess of the
Request to Access value chain, in which a contractor or internal joiner
submits an access request that is captured and validated for completeness
by the IT Service Desk before passing to identity validation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the organisation running the access request process,
  containing the IT Service Desk team.
  Lane "IT Service Desk (Service Desk Agent)" — receives, reviews and
  records the access request.
Pool "Contractor" — external party initiating the access request.
Pool "IT Service Management" — IT service management platform used to
  log and track access requests.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation
3. IT Service Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk (Service Desk Agent) lane:
  Message start event "Access request received from Contractor"
  User task "Review access request submission"
  Exclusive gateway "Request submission complete?"
  - branch "Incomplete": Send task "Request missing information from
    Contractor"
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received
    from Contractor"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request submission complete")
  - branch "Complete": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Request
    submission complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Request submission complete"
  User task "Classify request type and priority"
  User task "Check requester identity evidence provided"
  Exclusive gateway "Identity evidence provided?"
  - branch "Evidence missing": Send task "Notify Contractor to supply
    identity evidence"
    Intermediate message catch event "Identity evidence received from
    Contractor"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Identity evidence provided")
  - branch "Evidence present": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Identity evidence provided")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Identity evidence provided"
  Service task "Log access request in IT Service Management"
  User task "Confirm acceptable-use terms acknowledged by requester"
  Exclusive gateway "Acceptable-use terms accepted?"
  - branch "Not accepted": Send task "Send acceptable-use terms to
    Contractor for acceptance"
    Intermediate message catch event "Acceptable-use acceptance received
    from Contractor"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acceptable-use terms accepted")
  - branch "Accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Acceptable-use terms accepted")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acceptable-use terms accepted"
  Service task "Update request record with classification and evidence
    status in IT Service Management"
  End event "Access request raised and logged — ready for Validate
    Identity and Status"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins at the message start event in the IT Service
Desk lane and progresses through request review, the "Request submission
complete?" gateway whose incomplete branch sends a query to the Contractor
and waits for a reply before rejoining at the merge, then classification,
identity evidence check, the "Identity evidence provided?" gateway whose
missing-evidence branch sends a notice and waits before rejoining at the
merge, acceptable-use confirmation, the "Acceptable-use terms accepted?"
gateway whose not-accepted branch sends the terms and waits before
rejoining at the merge, and finally record update and the end event.

Message flows:
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk (access request submission
  including engagement details and purpose)
Organisation IT Service Desk → Contractor (request for missing
  information)
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk (additional information
  supplied)
Organisation IT Service Desk → Contractor (notification to supply
  identity evidence)
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk (identity evidence documents)
Organisation IT Service Desk → Contractor (acceptable-use terms for
  acknowledgement)
Contractor → Organisation IT Service Desk (signed acceptable-use
  acceptance)
Organisation IT Service Desk → IT Service Management (new access request
  record creation)
Organisation IT Service Desk → IT Service Management (updated request
  record with classification and evidence status)
IT Service Management → Organisation IT Service Desk (request reference
  number and current record state)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request Form" — written by User task "Review access
  request submission"; read by User task "Classify request type and
  priority".
Data Object "Identity Evidence Package" — written by User task "Check
  requester identity evidence provided"; read by Service task "Update
  request record with classification and evidence status in IT Service
  Management".
Data Object "Acceptable-Use Acknowledgement" — written by User task
  "Confirm acceptable-use terms acknowledged by requester"; read by
  Service task "Update request record with classification and evidence
  status in IT Service Management".
Data Object "Classified Access Request Record" — written by Service task
  "Update request record with classification and evidence status in IT
  Service Management"; read by End event "Access request raised and
  logged — ready for Validate Identity and Status".

V19.01 Raise Access Request opens the value chain by capturing and
structuring an incoming access request from a contractor or other
requester. The IT Service Desk collects the submission, chases any
missing information or identity evidence, confirms acceptance of
acceptable-use terms, and logs a complete, classified request record in
the IT Service Management platform. The fully formed and evidenced record
is then handed to V19.02 Validate Identity and Status for formal identity
and employment or engagement verification.
```


### V19.02 — Validate Identity & Status

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.02 Validate Identity & Status — second subprocess in the
Request to Access value chain, receiving a logged access request from
Raise Access Request and passing a validated identity record to
Determine Entitlements Required.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams performing identity and status
validation.
  Lane "IT Service Desk" — service desk agent triages the incoming request
  and liaises with the contractor.
  Lane "Human Resources" — HR officer confirms employment or engagement
  status against HR records.
Lane "Contractor" — external individual whose identity and engagement
status must be confirmed.
Pool "HR System" — system of record for employment and engagement status.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — IAM platform used to check for an
existing identity record and to create or update the identity profile.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "HR System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation (lanes: IT Service Desk, then Human Resources)
3. HR System
4. Identity & Access Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk lane:
  Message start event "Access request received from Raise Access Request"
  User task "Review logged access request"
  Send task "Request identity evidence from contractor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Identity evidence received from
  contractor"
  User task "Assess completeness of identity evidence"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence complete?"
  - branch "No": User task "Log evidence gap and request resubmission"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence complete?")
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
    complete?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence complete?"
  User task "Pass identity evidence to HR for status check"

Human Resources lane:
  User task "Verify employment or engagement status in HR System"
  Service task "Retrieve engagement record from HR System"
  Exclusive gateway "Status confirmed?"
  - branch "Not confirmed — no record found": User task "Raise status
    exception and notify IT Service Desk"
    End event "Validation failed — request halted pending HR resolution"
  - branch "Confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Status
    confirmed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Status confirmed?"
  User task "Confirm identity is active and in good standing"
  Service task "Check for existing identity record in IAM platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Identity record exists?"
  - branch "No": Service task "Create new identity profile in IAM platform"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Identity record exists?")
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Update identity profile in IAM platform"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Identity record exists?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Identity record exists?"
  User task "Mark identity as validated and record outcome"
  End event "Identity validated — ready for Determine Entitlements
  Required"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
'Identity evidence received from contractor'" — label "Evidence overdue
(3 business days)" — triggers User task "Escalate non-response to
service desk manager" in the IT Service Desk lane, followed by End event
"Validation stalled — escalated to service desk manager".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the IT Service Desk lane, moves to Human
Resources once evidence is assessed as complete, and ends in Human
Resources after the identity profile is confirmed in the IAM platform.
The "Evidence complete?" gateway loops back through the resubmission task
before merging; the "Status confirmed?" gateway has one branch ending in
a terminal End event and one merging forward; the "Identity record
exists?" gateway merges after either creating or updating the profile.

Message flows:
  Organisation (IT Service Desk — Send task "Request identity evidence
  from contractor") → Contractor (identity evidence request)
  Contractor → Organisation (IT Service Desk — Intermediate message catch
  event "Identity evidence received from contractor") (identity evidence
  documents)
  Organisation (Human Resources — Service task "Retrieve engagement
  record from HR System") → HR System (engagement record query)
  HR System → Organisation (Human Resources — Service task "Retrieve
  engagement record from HR System") (employment or engagement record)
  Organisation (Human Resources — Service task "Check for existing
  identity record in IAM platform") → Identity & Access Management
  (identity record lookup)
  Identity & Access Management → Organisation (Human Resources — Service
  task "Check for existing identity record in IAM platform") (existing
  identity record or not-found response)
  Organisation (Human Resources — Service task "Create new identity
  profile in IAM platform") → Identity & Access Management (new identity
  profile)
  Organisation (Human Resources — Service task "Update identity profile
  in IAM platform") → Identity & Access Management (updated identity
  profile)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request" — read by "Review logged access request";
read by "Pass identity evidence to HR for status check".
Data Object "Identity Evidence Package" — written by "Assess completeness
of identity evidence"; read by "Verify employment or engagement status
in HR System".
Data Object "Engagement Record" — written by "Retrieve engagement record
from HR System"; read by "Confirm identity is active and in good
standing".
Data Object "Validated Identity Record" — written by "Mark identity as
validated and record outcome"; read by the downstream Determine
Entitlements Required subprocess.

This subprocess establishes that the person requesting access is who they
claim to be and holds a current, legitimate engagement with the
organisation. It confirms or creates their identity profile in the IAM
platform and records the validation outcome. A clean validated identity
record is handed to Determine Entitlements Required, which uses it to
identify the specific access rights the individual should be granted.
```


### V19.03 — Determine Entitlements Required

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
producing a confirmed entitlement set ready for segregation-of-duties checking.

requester needs.

Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

2. Identity & Access Management System (black-box, bottom)

Identity & Access Management lane:

  - branch "Yes — standard role covers need":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Role determination resolved")
  - branch "No — bespoke or elevated entitlement needed":

    Intermediate message catch event "Application owner entitlement
    advice received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Role determination resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Role determination resolved"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings for requester"
  User task "Identify entitlements to add, remove or amend"
  Exclusive gateway "Entitlement set complete and agreed?"
  - branch "Yes":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entitlement set finalised")
  - branch "No — further clarification needed":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Entitlement Set Agreed"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Clarify requirements with application owner",
      User task "Revise proposed entitlement set"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entitlement set finalised")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Entitlement set finalised"
  Service task "Record confirmed entitlement set in IAM system"

  of Duties"

Application Owner lane:
  User task "Review proposed entitlements for owned applications"
  Exclusive gateway "Proposed entitlements acceptable?"
  - branch "Acceptable":
    Send task "Confirm entitlement selection"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Application owner response
    resolved")
  - branch "Needs adjustment":

    Send task "Return adjusted entitlement advice"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Application owner response
    resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Application owner response resolved"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Identity & Access Management lane, flow runs
from the message start event through catalogue retrieval, profile mapping,
and the "Standard role sufficient?" gateway; the "Yes" branch rejoins the
merge gateway directly while the "No" branch passes through the send task
and message catch event before rejoining; after the merge, flow continues
through current-holdings retrieval, entitlement identification, and the
"Entitlement set complete and agreed?" gateway; the "Yes" branch rejoins
the finalised merge gateway directly while the "No" branch passes through
the standard-loop subprocess before rejoining; after that merge, flow
continues through the service task recording the entitlement set and ends.
Within the Application Owner lane, flow runs from the review task through
the "Proposed entitlements acceptable?" gateway; the "Acceptable" branch
passes through the confirm send task and the "Needs adjustment" branch
passes through the adjustment user task and return send task, both rejoining
the "Application owner response resolved" merge gateway.

Message flows:
Identity & Access Management lane "Retrieve entitlement catalogue and
role definitions" → Identity & Access Management System (catalogue and
role definitions query)
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management lane
"Retrieve entitlement catalogue and role definitions" (entitlement
catalogue and role definitions)
Identity & Access Management lane "Retrieve current access holdings for
requester" → Identity & Access Management System (current holdings query)
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management lane
"Retrieve current access holdings for requester" (current access holdings
record)
Identity & Access Management lane "Record confirmed entitlement set in
IAM system" → Identity & Access Management System (confirmed entitlement
set write)
Identity & Access Management lane "Request application-specific
entitlement advice" → Application Owner lane "Review proposed
entitlements for owned applications" (proposed entitlement set for review)
Application Owner lane "Confirm entitlement selection" → Identity &
Access Management lane intermediate message catch event "Application

Access Management lane intermediate message catch event "Application

This subprocess takes the validated identity record produced by Validate
Identity & Status and maps the requester's profile against the entitlement
catalogue and role definitions held in the IAM system. It engages the
Application Owner to confirm or adjust proposed entitlements for their
systems, iterating until agreement is reached. The confirmed, reconciled
entitlement set is then written to the IAM system and handed to Check
Segregation of Duties for conflict analysis.
```

### V19.04 — Check Segregation of Duties

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.04 Check Segregation of Duties — checks the requested
entitlements against the segregation-of-duties matrix after entitlements
have been determined and before approvals are sought.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams carrying out the SoD check.
  Lane "Security" — security officer who runs and adjudicates the SoD
  check.
  Lane "Identity & Access Management" — identity engineer who provides
  current access holdings and acts on the conflict outcome.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — IAM platform that holds
current entitlements and runs conflict detection.
Pool "GRC Platform" — governance, risk and compliance platform that
records SoD exceptions and conflict results.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Security on top, Identity &
   Access Management below)
2. Identity & Access Management System
3. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security lane:
  Message start event "Determined entitlements received from Determine
  Entitlements Required"
  User task "Review entitlement set against SoD matrix"
  Service task "Trigger conflict detection in IAM system"
  Intermediate message catch event "Conflict detection results received"
  Exclusive gateway "SoD conflict detected?"
  - branch "No conflict": Service task "Record clean result in GRC
    Platform"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "SoD outcome resolved")
  - branch "Conflict identified": User task "Assess severity of SoD
    conflict"
    Exclusive gateway "Conflict acceptable with exception?"
    - branch "Exception approved": User task "Document SoD exception
      and compensating controls"
      Service task "Record exception in GRC Platform"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exception outcome resolved")
    - branch "Exception not approved": User task "Raise conflict
      rejection decision"
      Service task "Record rejection in GRC Platform"
      End event "SoD conflict rejected — request returned to Identity
      and Access Management for rework"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Exception outcome resolved"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "SoD outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "SoD outcome resolved"
  End event "SoD check complete — ready for Obtain Approvals"

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings for requester"
  Service task "Supply entitlement and access data to Security"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Security lane with the start event,
then moves to "Review entitlement set against SoD matrix" before
Security triggers conflict detection. Control passes to the Identity &
Access Management lane for "Retrieve current access holdings for
requester" and "Supply entitlement and access data to Security", whose
output feeds back to Security before the intermediate catch event
receives detection results. The exclusive gateway "SoD conflict
detected?" splits into the no-conflict branch, which records a clean
result and rejoins at merge gateway "SoD outcome resolved", and the
conflict branch, which passes through "Assess severity" to gateway
"Conflict acceptable with exception?". That gateway splits into the
exception branch, which documents and records the exception then rejoins
at merge gateway "Exception outcome resolved" before continuing to merge
gateway "SoD outcome resolved", and the rejection branch, which records
the rejection and ends at the rejection end event. The process
terminates at "SoD check complete — ready for Obtain Approvals".

Message flows:
  Security lane "Trigger conflict detection in IAM system" →
    Identity & Access Management System (conflict detection request with
    current entitlement set)
  Identity & Access Management System →
    Security lane intermediate message catch event "Conflict detection
    results received" (conflict detection results)
  Identity & Access Management lane "Retrieve current access holdings
    for requester" →
    Identity & Access Management System (request for current holdings)
  Identity & Access Management System →
    Identity & Access Management lane "Supply entitlement and access
    data to Security" (current access holdings)
  Security lane "Record clean result in GRC Platform" →
    GRC Platform (clean SoD result record)
  Security lane "Record exception in GRC Platform" →
    GRC Platform (SoD exception with compensating controls)
  Security lane "Record rejection in GRC Platform" →
    GRC Platform (conflict rejection record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Entitlement Set" — read by "Review entitlement set against
SoD matrix"; read by "Trigger conflict detection in IAM system".
Data Object "Current Access Holdings" — written by "Retrieve current
access holdings for requester"; read by "Supply entitlement and access
data to Security".
Data Object "Conflict Detection Results" — written by intermediate
message catch event "Conflict detection results received"; read by
"Assess severity of SoD conflict".
Data Object "SoD Exception Record" — written by "Document SoD exception
and compensating controls"; read by "Record exception in GRC Platform".
Data Object "SoD Check Outcome" — written by "Record clean result in
GRC Platform" or "Record rejection in GRC Platform"; read by the
respective end events.

V19.04 takes the determined entitlement set produced by V19.03 and
tests it against the segregation-of-duties matrix by querying current
access holdings in the IAM system and running automated conflict
detection. Where no conflict exists the result is logged as clean in the
GRC Platform; where a conflict exists the security officer assesses
severity and either approves an exception with compensating controls or
rejects the request and returns it for rework. A clean or excepted
outcome is then passed forward to V19.05 Obtain Approvals, while the
complete SoD evidence is retained in the GRC Platform for audit.
```


### V19.05 — Obtain Approvals

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.05 Obtain Approvals — sits within the Request to Access value
chain after segregation-of-duties checks have cleared and before access is
provisioned.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that manage the approval workflow.
  Lane "Line Management" — approving line manager reviews and approves the
    request on behalf of the requester.
  Lane "Application Owner" — application owner grants or refuses entitlement-
    level sign-off.
Pool "IT Service Management" — the IT service management platform that
  routes approval tasks and records decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Line Management on top, Application
   Owner beneath)
2. IT Service Management (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Line Management lane:
  Message start event "Approved SoD check received from Check Segregation
    of Duties"
  Service task "Retrieve approval request from ITSM"
  User task "Review access request and requester justification"
  Exclusive gateway "Line manager decision?"
    - branch "Rejected": Send task "Record rejection and notify requester"
        End event "Request rejected — approval process ends"
    - branch "More information needed": Send task "Request additional
        information from requester"
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Line manager decision")
    - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Line manager decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Line manager decision"
  Service task "Record line manager approval in ITSM"
  Send task "Forward approved request to Application Owner"

Application Owner lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Approved request received from Line
    Management"
  User task "Assess entitlement-level requirements and risks"
  Exclusive gateway "Application owner decision?"
    - branch "Rejected": Send task "Record application owner rejection in
        ITSM"
        End event "Request rejected at entitlement level — approval process
          ends"
    - branch "Escalate to Security": Send task "Escalate request to
        Security for privileged-access review"
        Intermediate message catch event "Security review outcome received"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Application owner decision")
    - branch "Approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Application owner decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Application owner decision"
  Service task "Record application owner approval in ITSM"
  End event "All approvals obtained — ready for Provision Access"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review access request and
  requester justification" — label "Approval deadline exceeded (line
  manager)" — triggers Send task "Send escalation notice to line manager's
  superior", then rejoins flow at exclusive merge gateway "Line manager
  decision".
Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Assess entitlement-level
  requirements and risks" — label "Approval deadline exceeded (application
  owner)" — triggers Send task "Send escalation notice to application
  owner's superior", then rejoins flow at exclusive merge gateway
  "Application owner decision".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs top to bottom through the Line Management lane
  from the message start event through retrieval, review, and the line
  manager gateway; the approved branch and the looping more-information
  branch both merge at the exclusive merge gateway "Line manager decision"
  before the approval is recorded and forwarded; the rejection branch ends
  at its own end event. Flow continues into the Application Owner lane via
  an intermediate message catch event, through the entitlement review and
  the application owner gateway; the escalation branch and the approved
  branch merge at the exclusive merge gateway "Application owner decision"
  before the final approval is recorded; the rejection branch ends at its
  own end event.

Message flows:
  IT Service Management → Line Management lane, Service task "Retrieve
    approval request from ITSM" (approval task payload, request details,
    entitlement list).
  Line Management lane, Service task "Record line manager approval in
    ITSM" → IT Service Management (line manager decision and timestamp).
  Line Management lane, Send task "Forward approved request to Application
    Owner" → Application Owner lane, Intermediate message catch event
    "Approved request received from Line Management" (forwarded approval
    request).
  Application Owner lane, Service task "Record application owner approval
    in ITSM" → IT Service Management (application owner decision,
    entitlement grant confirmation, and audit trail entry).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Access Request" — read by "Retrieve approval request from
  ITSM"; read by "Review access request and requester justification"; read
  by "Assess entitlement-level requirements and risks".
Data Object "Line Manager Approval Record" — written by "Record line
  manager approval in ITSM".
Data Object "Application Owner Approval Record" — written by "Record
  application owner approval in ITSM".
Data Object "Escalation Notice" — written by "Send escalation notice to
  line manager's superior"; written by "Send escalation notice to
  application owner's superior".

V19.05 Obtain Approvals gathers the mandatory sign-offs from the approving
line manager and the application owner in sequence, enforcing deadline
escalation where reviewers do not respond in time and halting the request
cleanly if either party refuses. Once both approvals are recorded in the
IT service management platform, the subprocess hands a fully authorised
access request to V19.06 Provision Access.
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text

  single instance.
Pool "Directory Services" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

Pool "Identity & Access Management (system)" — top.
Pool "Organisation" — middle (white-box).
Pool "Directory Services" — bottom.

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Message start event "Approved entitlement package received from
    Obtain Approvals"
  User task "Review approved entitlement package"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from IAM system"
  Exclusive gateway "Account already exists?"

  - branch "Yes — account exists":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Account ready")

  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Entitlements Provisioned"
    (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Select next entitlement from approved package",

    Service task "Activate group membership or role in Directory Services",
    User task "Mark entitlement as provisioned in service request"
  Service task "Retrieve provisioning confirmation from IAM system"

  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provisioning outcome resolved")
  - branch "No — errors detected":

      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provisioning outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Provisioning outcome resolved"

  - branch "Yes":
      User task "Apply privileged access time limit and controls"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privileged access handled")
  - branch "No":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privileged access handled")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Privileged access handled"
  User task "Update access record with grant details and timestamp"
  Service task "Log provisioning event to IAM system for audit evidence"
  End event "Access provisioned — ready for Notify & Confirm with Requester"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting error boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All

Sequence flows: the flow begins in the Identity & Access Management lane with
```

### V19.07 — Notify & Confirm with Requester

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester — the subprocess that
closes the access-provisioning loop by informing the requester that
access has been granted and confirming receipt, within the V19 Request
to Access value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that notify and confirm access
  with the requester.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - IT Service Desk (service desk agent)
Pool "Contractor" — external contractor or partner who submitted the
  access request and now receives notification.
Pool "IT Service Management" — ITSM platform that records the
  notification, tracks confirmation and closes the request ticket.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Contractor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "IT Service Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Contractor
2. Organisation (IT Service Desk lane)
3. IT Service Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

IT Service Desk lane:
  Message start event "Access provisioned — received from Provision
    Access"
  Service task "Retrieve provisioning details from ITSM ticket"
  User task "Prepare access notification"
  Send task "Send access notification to contractor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Contractor acknowledgement received"
  Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement confirmed?"
  - branch "Yes — acknowledged":
      User task "Record confirmation in ITSM ticket"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement confirmed")
  - branch "No — no response within deadline":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Acknowledgement Received"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
        Send task "Re-send access notification to contractor",
        Intermediate message catch event "Contractor acknowledgement
          received on retry"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement confirmed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement confirmed"
  Service task "Update ITSM ticket status to Resolved"
  End event "Notification confirmed — access request cycle complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Acknowledgement Received" — labelled "Maximum retry period elapsed";
  leads to End event "Notification unconfirmed — escalation raised".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the IT Service Desk lane runs from the message start
  event through retrieval, preparation and sending of the notification,
  then pauses at the intermediate message catch event awaiting the
  contractor's acknowledgement. The exclusive gateway splits into the
  confirmed branch and the no-response branch, both rejoining at the
  exclusive merge gateway before the ITSM update and end event. The
  no-response branch enters the standard-loop subprocess, which repeats
  re-sending and waiting; a timer boundary event on that subprocess
  exits to a separate end event if the retry period elapses without
  confirmation.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Send task "Send access notification to contractor") →

  Contractor → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Contractor acknowledgement received") (acknowledgement of receipt)

    Contractor (retry access notification)
  Contractor → Organisation (Intermediate message catch event

    on retry)
  Organisation (Service task "Retrieve provisioning details from ITSM

  IT Service Management → Organisation (Service task "Retrieve
    provisioning details from ITSM ticket") (ticket and provisioning

  Organisation (Service task "Update ITSM ticket status to Resolved") →

  contractor".

  "Record confirmation in ITSM ticket"; read by Service task "Update
  ITSM ticket status to Resolved".

V19.07 Notify & Confirm with Requester ensures that once access has
been provisioned, the contractor or partner is formally informed of
their credentials and access details, and that their receipt is
confirmed and recorded. The IT Service Desk orchestrates notification
via the ITSM platform and pursues acknowledgement through retries if
needed. On confirmed receipt the request ticket is closed, completing
the active provisioning cycle and making the closed record available
to V19.08 Review Access Periodically and V19.10 Evidence for Audit.
```
