```text
  End event "Recertification complete — access register updated, ready for
    Evidence for Audit"

Security lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Escalated entitlement received from
    Application Owner"
  User task "Assess escalated entitlement against least-privilege policy"
  Exclusive gateway "Escalation decision?"
    - branch "Retain access": Send task "Return retain decision to Application
      Owner" — End event "Escalation resolved — decision returned to
      Application Owner certifier"
    - branch "Revoke access": Send task "Return revoke decision to Application
      Owner" — End event "Escalation resolved — decision returned to
      Application Owner certifier"
  User task "Monitor review campaign progress and exception rate"
  User task "Flag unresponsive certifiers and enforce deadline"
  Service task "Record exceptions and overrides in Access Certification
    Platform"

Note: The Security lane monitoring tasks run in parallel with the Application
Owner certification work. The escalation path within Security begins on receipt
of the escalation message event and concludes before the certification decisions
are submitted.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Review and certify each entitlement" —
  label "Certifier response deadline exceeded" — triggers User task "Flag
  unresponsive certifiers and enforce deadline" in Security lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Application Owner lane at the timer start
  event, moves through retrieval of access holdings, then into the certify-
  entitlement loop. The "Entitlement certified?" exclusive gateway branches to
  confirm, revoke or escalate, all rejoining at the "Entitlement certified?"
  merge gateway. The outer "All entitlements reviewed?" gateway loops back
  until complete, then exits to the submit task, the intermediate message catch
  event for provisioning outcomes, and finally the end event. In the Security
  lane, the escalation message catch event leads to the assessment task and
  escalation-decision gateway whose two branches each end independently.
  Security monitoring tasks run concurrently alongside the main Application
  Owner flow.

Message flows:
  Access Certification Platform → Service task "Retrieve current access
    holdings from Access Certification Platform" (current entitlement holdings
    per user and application)
  Service task "Submit certification decisions to Access Certification Platform"
    → Access Certification Platform (certified, revoke and escalation decisions)
  Access Certification Platform → Intermediate message catch event "Provisioning
    and revocation outcomes received from Provision Access" (provisioning and
    revocation status)
  Service task "Record exceptions and overrides in Access Certification
    Platform" → Access Certification Platform (exception and override records)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Entitlement Holdings Report" — read by "Review and certify each
  entitlement"; written by "Retrieve current access holdings from Access
  Certification Platform".
Data Object "Certification Decision Record" — written by "Review and certify
  each entitlement" and "Mark entitlement for revocation"; read by "Submit
  certification decisions to Access Certification Platform".
Data Object "Escalation Record" — written by "Escalate entitlement to Security
  for decision"; read by "Assess escalated entitlement against least-privilege
  policy".
Data Object "Exception Report" — written by "Record exceptions and overrides in
  Access Certification Platform"; read by "Monitor review campaign progress and
  exception rate".

This subprocess carries out the periodic recertification of all standing access
entitlements, ensuring certifiers confirm or revoke each right against the
least-privilege policy, with Security governing the campaign and resolving
escalations. Exceptions and overrides are recorded in the Access Certification
Platform. On completion, the updated access register and the full set of
certification decisions, exceptions and revocation outcomes are handed to
Evidence for Audit for control testing and reporting.
```


### V19.09 — Revoke on Change or Exit

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.09 Revoke on Change or Exit — subprocess within the Request to
Access value chain that terminates access rights when a person changes role
or leaves the organisation.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing the revocation process.
  Lane "Human Resources" — HR officer who triggers and records the change or
    exit event.
  Lane "Identity & Access Management" — access administrator who executes
    access revocation.
Pool "HR System" — system of record for employment and engagement status.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — IAM platform used to locate
  and revoke entitlements.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "HR System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Identity & Access Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. HR System
2. Organisation (lanes: Human Resources, then Identity & Access Management)
3. Identity & Access Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Human Resources lane:
  Message start event "Joiner/mover/leaver event received from HR System"
  User task "Record change or exit event"
  Service task "Retrieve current access holdings from HR System"
  User task "Confirm scope of revocation required"
  Exclusive gateway "Full exit or role change?"
  - branch "Full exit": Send task "Raise full-revocation instruction"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Revocation scope resolved")
  - branch "Role change": Send task "Raise partial-revocation instruction"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Revocation scope resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Revocation scope resolved"
  User task "Log revocation request in HR System"

Identity & Access Management lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Revocation instruction received"
  Service task "Retrieve active entitlements from Identity & Access
    Management System"
  Expanded Subprocess "Revoke Until All Entitlements Removed" (standard
    loop) containing, in order: Service task "Disable or remove entitlement",
    Service task "Verify entitlement removed in Identity & Access Management
      System"
  Service task "Disable or lock account in Directory Services via Identity
    & Access Management System"
  User task "Check for orphaned or dormant accounts"
  Exclusive gateway "Orphaned accounts found?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Remediate orphaned accounts"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Orphan check resolved")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Orphan check
    resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Orphan check resolved"
  Service task "Record revocation completion in Identity & Access Management
    System"
  User task "Confirm revocation outcome to Human Resources lane"
  End event "Access revoked — ready for Evidence for Audit"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Revoke Until All
  Entitlements Removed" — label "Revocation deadline exceeded" — triggers
  User task "Escalate overdue revocation to Security officer" then End event
  "Escalation raised — ready for Evidence for Audit".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Human Resources lane at the message start
event, proceeds through recording and confirming the event, then branches at
the full-exit/role-change gateway before merging and logging the request;
a send task passes the instruction to the Identity & Access Management lane,
which proceeds through entitlement retrieval, the standard-loop revocation
subprocess, account disablement, orphan checking (branching yes/no and
merging), completion recording, and ends with confirmation back to Human
Resources before the end event.

Message flows:
HR System → Human Resources lane, "Record change or exit event" (joiner/
  mover/leaver trigger event).
Human Resources lane, "Retrieve current access holdings from HR System" →
  HR System (request for current access holdings).
HR System → Human Resources lane, "Retrieve current access holdings from
  HR System" (current access holdings response).
Human Resources lane, "Log revocation request in HR System" → HR System
  (revocation request record).
Identity & Access Management lane, "Retrieve active entitlements from
  Identity & Access Management System" → Identity & Access Management System
  (request for active entitlements).
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management lane,
  "Retrieve active entitlements from Identity & Access Management System"
  (active entitlement list).
Identity & Access Management lane, "Disable or remove entitlement" →
  Identity & Access Management System (entitlement removal instruction).
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management lane,
  "Verify entitlement removed in Identity & Access Management System"
  (removal confirmation).
Identity & Access Management lane, "Disable or lock account in Directory
  Services via Identity & Access Management System" → Identity & Access
  Management System (account disable instruction).
Identity & Access Management lane, "Record revocation completion in Identity
  & Access Management System" → Identity & Access Management System
  (revocation completion record).
Identity & Access Management System → Identity & Access Management lane,
  "Check for orphaned or dormant accounts" (orphaned and dormant account
  report).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Change or Exit Event Record" — written by "Record change or
  exit event"; read by "Confirm scope of revocation required".
Data Object "Active Entitlement List" — written by "Retrieve active
  entitlements from Identity & Access Management System"; read by "Disable
  or remove entitlement".
Data Object "Revocation Instruction" — written by "Raise full-revocation
  instruction" and "Raise partial-revocation instruction"; read by
  "Retrieve active entitlements from Identity & Access Management System".
Data Object "Revocation Completion Record" — written by "Record revocation
  completion in Identity & Access Management System"; read by "Confirm
  revocation outcome to Human Resources lane".

This subprocess ensures that when a person leaves or changes role, all
associated entitlements are identified, systematically removed, and accounts
disabled or locked within the required revocation timeframe. Orphaned and
dormant accounts are caught and remediated before the process closes. A
complete revocation completion record is produced and passed to Evidence for
Audit, where it forms part of the access-control audit trail.
```


### V19.10 — Evidence for Audit

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V19.10 Evidence for Audit — closes the Request to Access value chain
by assembling, reviewing and delivering audit evidence to the Auditor.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that compile and present audit
evidence.
  Lane "Security" — security officer who compiles evidence packages.
  Lane "Internal Audit" — internal auditor who reviews and certifies evidence.

Pool "Auditor" — external auditor who requests and receives audit evidence.

Pool "Access Certification Platform" — system holding recertification
decisions and results.

Pool "GRC Platform" — system holding SoD exceptions, approvals and
control evidence.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Auditor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Access Certification Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "GRC Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Auditor
2. Organisation
3. Access Certification Platform
4. GRC Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Security lane:
  Message start event "Audit evidence request received from Auditor"
  User task "Log audit evidence request in register"
  Service task "Extract access register from Identity & Access
    Management records"
  Service task "Retrieve recertification results from Access
    Certification Platform"
  Service task "Retrieve SoD exception and approval records from
    GRC Platform"
  User task "Compile audit evidence package"
  Exclusive gateway "Package complete and within scope?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Package
    complete and within scope")
  - branch "No — gaps identified":
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Package Complete"
      (standard loop) containing, in order:
      User task "Identify missing evidence items",
      User task "Gather missing records from source systems",
      User task "Update audit evidence package"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Package complete and
    within scope")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Package complete and within scope"
  User task "Quality-check evidence package for accuracy"
  Send task "Send audit evidence package to Internal Audit"

Internal Audit lane:
  User task "Review audit evidence package"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence sufficient and accurate?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence
    sufficient and accurate")
  - branch "No — queries raised":
    User task "Raise evidence queries with Security"
    Intermediate message catch event "Clarification response received"
    User task "Assess clarification response"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient and
    accurate")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence sufficient and accurate"
  User task "Record internal audit sign-off"
  Send task "Transmit final evidence package to Auditor"
  Intermediate message catch event "Auditor acknowledgement received"
  User task "Archive audit evidence and close audit request"
  End event "Audit evidence delivered and cycle evidenced — audit
    complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Evidence Package Complete", label "Evidence collection deadline
exceeded", leading to End event "Audit evidence request escalated —
deadline breached".

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review audit evidence
package", label "Internal review deadline exceeded", leading to User
task "Escalate review delay to Security Officer" then End event
"Internal audit review escalated — deadline breached".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Security lane, moves through
evidence extraction, compilation and quality-check before passing to
the Internal Audit lane for review, sign-off and transmission to the
Auditor; the "No — gaps identified" branch enters the standard-loop
subprocess before rejoining at the merge gateway; the "No — queries
raised" branch raises queries with Security, waits for a clarification
response and reassesses before rejoining at the merge gateway.

Message flows:
Auditor → Security lane, Message start event "Audit evidence request
  received from Auditor" (audit evidence request).
Access Certification Platform → Security lane, Service task "Retrieve
  recertification results from Access Certification Platform"
  (recertification results and decisions).
GRC Platform → Security lane, Service task "Retrieve SoD exception
  and approval records from GRC Platform" (SoD exception records and
  approval evidence).
Internal Audit lane, Send task "Transmit final evidence package to
  Auditor" → Auditor (final audit evidence package).
Auditor → Internal Audit lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Auditor acknowledgement received" (acknowledgement of receipt).
Security lane, Send task "Send audit evidence package to Internal
  Audit" → Internal Audit lane, User task "Review audit evidence
  package" (evidence package for internal review).
Internal Audit lane, User task "Raise evidence queries with Security"
  → Security lane (evidence queries).
Security lane → Internal Audit lane, Intermediate message catch event
  "Clarification response received" (clarification response).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Audit Evidence Request" — written by User task "Log
  audit evidence request in register"; read by User task "Compile
  audit evidence package".
Data Object "Access Register" — written by Service task "Extract
  access register from Identity & Access Management records"; read by
  User task "Compile audit evidence package".
Data Object "Recertification Results" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve recertification results from Access Certification
  Platform"; read by User task "Compile audit evidence package".
Data Object "SoD Exception and Approval Records" — written by Service
  task "Retrieve SoD exception and approval records from GRC Platform";
  read by User task "Compile audit evidence package".
Data Object "Audit Evidence Package" — written by User task "Compile
  audit evidence package"; read by User task "Quality-check evidence
  package for accuracy" and User task "Review audit evidence package".
Data Object "Internal Audit Sign-off Record" — written by User task
  "Record internal audit sign-off"; read by User task "Archive audit
  evidence and close audit request".

V19.10 Evidence for Audit assembles all records generated across the
Request to Access cycle — access registers, recertification decisions,
SoD exceptions and approval evidence — into a verified package that
satisfies external audit requirements. The Security officer compiles
and quality-checks the package, Internal Audit reviews and signs off,
and the final evidence is transmitted to the Auditor. Completion of
this subprocess closes the V19 value chain, confirming that access
controls have been operated, reviewed and evidenced in accordance with
policy.
```


## V20 — Matter to Resolution

**Teams and roles involved.**
Matter to Resolution usually involves Legal, Compliance, Risk, Company Secretariat, the affected Business Unit, Finance for provisioning, and Executive Management. Key roles include general counsel, legal counsel, paralegal, compliance manager, matter owner, external counsel liaison, finance business partner, and company secretary.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are the Counterparty — a claimant, litigant, complainant or regulator — and External Counsel engaged to act. The process is initiated by a claim, dispute, complaint escalation, regulatory notice, subpoena or litigation filing. Other external parties include courts and tribunals, mediators and arbitrators, insurers, expert witnesses, and opposing counsel.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive and register the matter, assess merits and exposure, assign internal and external counsel, issue legal hold and preserve evidence, develop the strategy, manage discovery and disclosure, negotiate or mediate, litigate or defend where required, settle or obtain judgment, and close the matter with lessons learned.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include matter management, e-discovery and legal hold tooling, document management, contract repositories, spend and e-billing management for external counsel, risk registers and provisioning in finance systems, and board and committee reporting.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include legal engagement and outside-counsel guidelines, delegation of authority for settlement, legal hold and document retention obligations, privilege protection procedures, conflict-of-interest checks, disclosure obligations to regulators and insurers, provisioning and materiality thresholds for financial reporting, and reporting obligations to the board.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The counterparty and courts provide claims, pleadings, notices, discovery requests and judgments; the process provides responses, disclosures, submissions and settlement offers. External counsel receive instructions, evidence and authority limits, and provide advice, drafts, appearances and invoices.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates matter records, exposure assessments, legal holds, evidence collections, strategy and privilege logs, external counsel budgets and invoices, settlement records, and provisions. IT systems provide contract and transaction evidence, custodian and data-source mapping for holds, spend against budget, provision and accrual postings, and matter status and exposure reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V20.01** Receive & Register Matter | Counterparty | Legal (paralegal) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.02** Assess Merits & Exposure | — | Legal (legal counsel), Risk (risk manager) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.03** Assign Internal & External Counsel | External Counsel | Legal (general counsel) | Matter Management System, Legal Spend Management |
| **V20.04** Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence | — | Legal (paralegal), Business Unit (matter owner) | Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform |
| **V20.05** Develop Strategy | External Counsel | Legal (legal counsel) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.06** Manage Discovery & Disclosure | Counterparty, Court | Legal (paralegal), Business Unit (matter owner) | Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform, Document Management System |
| **V20.07** Negotiate or Mediate | Counterparty, Mediator | Legal (legal counsel), Executive Management (delegated approver) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.08** Litigate or Defend | Court, External Counsel | Legal (legal counsel) | Matter Management System |
| **V20.09** Settle or Obtain Judgment | Counterparty, Insurer | Legal (general counsel), Finance (finance business partner) | Matter Management System, Finance / ERP System |
| **V20.10** Close Matter & Capture Lessons | — | Legal (legal counsel), Company Secretariat (company secretary) | Matter Management System, Board Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V20):

- **External actors:** Counterparty (V20.01, V20.06, V20.07, V20.09); External Counsel (V20.03, V20.05, V20.08); Court (V20.06, V20.08); Mediator (V20.07); Insurer (V20.09).
- **Teams:** Legal (V20.01–V20.10); Risk (V20.02); Business Unit (V20.04, V20.06); Executive Management (V20.07); Finance (V20.09); Company Secretariat (V20.10).
- **IT systems:** Matter Management System (V20.01–V20.03, V20.05, V20.07–V20.10); Legal Spend Management (V20.03); Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform (V20.04, V20.06); Document Management System (V20.06); Finance / ERP System (V20.09); Board Reporting System (V20.10).

```text
  acknowledgement.
Counterparty — V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure: provides and receives
  discovery requests, disclosures, and productions.
Counterparty — V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate: exchanges settlement offers,
  positions, and counter-proposals.
Counterparty — V20.09 Settle or Obtain Judgment: executes settlement
  agreement or receives judgment outcome.

External Counsel — V20.03 Assign Internal & External Counsel: receives
  engagement instructions, scope, and outside-counsel guidelines;
  confirms acceptance and conflict checks.
External Counsel — V20.05 Develop Strategy: receives evidence, privilege
  logs, and strategy brief; provides legal advice and strategy drafts.
External Counsel — V20.08 Litigate or Defend: receives authority limits
  and evidence; provides court appearances, submissions, and invoices.

Court — V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure: issues discovery orders and
  procedural directions; receives filed productions and submissions.
Court — V20.08 Litigate or Defend: issues rulings, procedural orders, and
  hearing dates; receives pleadings and legal submissions.

Mediator — V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate: facilitates mediation sessions;
  receives briefs and position statements from the process.

Insurer — V20.09 Settle or Obtain Judgment: receives disclosure of
  settlement terms and claim details; provides coverage confirmation
  and insurer approval.

Legal — V20.01 Receive & Register Matter: registers matter record, assigns
  matter number, and captures initial details.
Legal — V20.02 Assess Merits & Exposure: conducts legal merits review and
  prepares exposure assessment.
Legal — V20.03 Assign Internal & External Counsel: selects and engages
  internal and external counsel; issues instructions.
Legal — V20.04 Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence: issues legal hold
  notices and oversees evidence preservation.
Legal — V20.05 Develop Strategy: leads strategy development and maintains
  privilege log.
Legal — V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure: coordinates document review,
  disclosure obligations, and productions.
Legal — V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate: conducts negotiations and mediation
  with authority from delegation of authority policy.
Legal — V20.08 Litigate or Defend: manages litigation conduct and
  instructs external counsel on defence.
Legal — V20.09 Settle or Obtain Judgment: executes settlement within
  delegated authority or secures judgment.
Legal — V20.10 Close Matter & Capture Lessons: closes matter record and
  documents lessons learned.

Risk — V20.02 Assess Merits & Exposure: provides risk register input and
  validates exposure quantum and materiality thresholds.

Business Unit — V20.04 Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence: identifies
  custodians and data sources; complies with hold notices.
Business Unit — V20.06 Manage Discovery & Disclosure: locates and produces
  relevant documents and transaction records.

Executive Management — V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate: provides delegated
  settlement authority and approves negotiation parameters.

Finance — V20.09 Settle or Obtain Judgment: raises financial provisions,
  posts accruals, and processes settlement payments via ERP.

Company Secretariat — V20.10 Close Matter & Capture Lessons: prepares
  board and committee reporting on matter closure and lessons learned.

The boundary "V20 — Matter to Resolution" contains ten subprocesses covering
every stage from initial receipt of a claim through assessment, legal hold,
strategy, discovery, negotiation, litigation, and final settlement or
judgment, to matter closure and lessons learned. It serves five external
actors — Counterparty, External Counsel, Court, Mediator, and Insurer — and
six internal teams — Legal, Risk, Business Unit, Executive Management,
Finance, and Company Secretariat — whose interactions with the subprocesses
are shown by the connections above.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V20 - Matter to Resolution

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each rendered as a chevron pointing right, in the order listed below. One
chevron per stage, no chevrons omitted. The chevrons should be evenly spaced
and connected so that the point of each feeds directly into the tail of the
next.

V20.01. Receive & Register Matter
V20.02. Assess Merits & Exposure
V20.03. Assign Internal & External Counsel
V20.04. Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence
V20.05. Develop Strategy
V20.06. Manage Discovery & Disclosure
V20.07. Negotiate or Mediate
V20.08. Litigate or Defend
V20.09. Settle or Obtain Judgment
V20.10. Close Matter & Capture Lessons

This chain governs the end-to-end handling of a legal or regulatory matter
from first notification through to final closure. It is triggered when a
Counterparty — a claimant, litigant, complainant or regulator — raises a
claim, dispute, complaint, subpoena or regulatory notice against the
organisation. The chain coordinates Legal, Risk, Compliance, Finance,
Business Unit, Executive Management and Company Secretariat internally,
and External Counsel, courts, mediators and insurers externally, to
assess exposure, preserve evidence, pursue or defend proceedings, and
reach a settlement or judgment, before capturing lessons and closing
the matter.
```
### V20.01 — Receive & Register Matter

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.01 Receive & Register Matter — first subprocess in the Matter
to Resolution value chain, covering intake and registration of an
incoming legal matter.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal team receiving and registering the
matter, with lanes for Legal.
  Lane "Legal (Paralegal)"
Pool "Counterparty" — the external claimant, litigant, complainant
or regulator initiating the matter.
Pool "Matter Management System" — the IT system used to create and
store the matter record.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Counterparty" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Counterparty
2. Organisation
3. Matter Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (Paralegal) lane:
  Message start event "Claim, notice, complaint or filing received
    from Counterparty"
  User task "Log initial matter details"
  User task "Classify matter type and jurisdiction"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to proceed?"
    - branch "No — information missing":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
          Send task "Request additional information from
            Counterparty",
          Intermediate message catch event "Additional information
            received from Counterparty",
          User task "Review supplementary information"
        (exits subprocess)
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
        information to proceed")
    - branch "Yes — information complete":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
        information to proceed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to proceed"
  User task "Conduct conflict-of-interest check"
  Exclusive gateway "Conflict identified?"
    - branch "Yes — conflict exists":
        User task "Escalate conflict to General Counsel"
        End event "Matter escalated — conflict requires resolution
          before proceeding"
    - branch "No — no conflict":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Conflict identified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Conflict identified"
  User task "Assign matter reference and priority rating"
  Service task "Create matter record in Matter Management System"
  User task "Notify relevant internal stakeholders of new matter"
  End event "Matter registered — ready for Assess Merits
    and Exposure"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Legal (Paralegal)
lane. After the message start event the paralegal logs and
classifies the matter, then reaches the "Sufficient information to
proceed?" gateway. The No branch enters the standard-loop
subprocess and rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient
information to proceed"; the Yes branch joins the same merge
gateway directly. Flow continues through the conflict-of-interest
check to the "Conflict identified?" gateway. The Yes branch leads
to escalation and terminates at its own end event; the No branch
rejoins at the exclusive merge gateway "Conflict identified". Flow
then proceeds through reference assignment, matter record creation,
and stakeholder notification to the final end event.

Message flows:
Counterparty → Legal (Paralegal) lane — "Claim, notice, complaint
  or filing" (triggers message start event).
Legal (Paralegal) lane → Counterparty — "Request for additional
  information" (sent from Send task inside loop subprocess).
Counterparty → Legal (Paralegal) lane — "Additional information"
  (received by intermediate message catch event inside loop
  subprocess).
Legal (Paralegal) lane → Matter Management System — "New matter
  record" (sent from Service task "Create matter record in Matter
  Management System").

7. Data objects

Data Object "Incoming Matter Document" — written by User task
  "Log initial matter details"; read by User task "Classify matter
  type and jurisdiction".
Data Object "Conflict-of-Interest Check Result" — written by User
  task "Conduct conflict-of-interest check"; read by Exclusive
  gateway "Conflict identified?".
Data Object "Matter Record" — written by Service task "Create
  matter record in Matter Management System"; read by User task
  "Notify relevant internal stakeholders of new matter".

This subprocess captures the first formal step in the Matter to
Resolution chain: receiving a claim, notice or complaint from a
counterparty, gathering enough information to proceed, verifying
there is no conflict of interest, and creating an official matter
record. It hands a fully registered matter with a reference number
and priority rating to the Assess Merits and Exposure subprocess.
```


### V20.02 — Assess Merits & Exposure

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.02 Assess Merits & Exposure — second subprocess in the Matter to
Resolution value chain, following receipt and registration of the matter.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal team and risk team assessing the registered
matter.
  Lane "Legal" — legal counsel reviewing the matter record and leading the
  merits assessment.
  Lane "Risk" — risk manager assessing financial exposure and provisioning
  need.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter data, exposure
assessments and risk register updates.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes: Legal on top, Risk below)
2. Matter Management System (black-box, bottom)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Registered matter received from Receive & Register
  Matter"
  Service task "Retrieve matter record and supporting documents"
  User task "Review claim, pleadings and applicable law"
  User task "Assess legal merits and identify key issues"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient information to assess?"
  - branch "No — information gaps identified": User task "Request additional
    information or documents"
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to assess")
  - branch "Yes — assessment can proceed":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to assess")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient information to assess"
  User task "Draft merits assessment and identify privilege considerations"
  User task "Determine litigation risk rating"
  Send task "Send merits assessment to Risk for exposure quantification"

Risk lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Merits assessment received from Legal"
  User task "Quantify financial exposure and worst-case liability"
  User task "Assess provisioning and materiality thresholds"
  Exclusive gateway "Provision required?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Raise or update provision in finance system"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provision required")
  - branch "No":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provision required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Provision required"
  User task "Record exposure assessment and risk rating"
  Send task "Return completed exposure assessment to Legal"

Legal lane (continued):
  Intermediate message catch event "Exposure assessment received from Risk"
  User task "Consolidate merits and exposure into matter assessment record"
  Service task "Update matter record in Matter Management System"
  End event "Matter assessment complete — ready for Assign Internal &
  External Counsel"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Within the Legal lane the flow runs from the message start
event through retrieval and review tasks to the gateway "Sufficient
information to assess?"; the No branch loops through request and catch before
rejoining at the merge gateway; the Yes branch rejoins directly at the same
merge gateway; flow then continues through drafting, risk rating and the send
task. In the Risk lane flow starts at the message catch event, runs through
exposure quantification and provisioning tasks to the gateway "Provision
required?"; the Yes branch adds a provision task before rejoining at the merge
gateway; the No branch rejoins directly; flow then continues through recording
and the send task. Control returns to the Legal lane via the message catch
event and ends after the system update.

Message flows:
Matter Management System → Legal lane "Retrieve matter record and supporting
documents" (registered matter record, claim documents and pleadings).
Legal lane "Send merits assessment to Risk for exposure quantification" →
Risk lane "Merits assessment received from Legal" (draft merits assessment
and risk rating).
Risk lane "Return completed exposure assessment to Legal" → Legal lane
"Exposure assessment received from Risk" (quantified exposure and
provisioning recommendation).
Legal lane "Update matter record in Matter Management System" →
Matter Management System (consolidated matter assessment record, exposure
figure and risk rating).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Matter Record" — read by "Retrieve matter record and supporting
documents"; updated by "Consolidate merits and exposure into matter assessment
record".
Data Object "Merits Assessment" — written by "Draft merits assessment and
identify privilege considerations"; read by "Consolidate merits and exposure
into matter assessment record".
Data Object "Exposure Assessment" — written by "Record exposure assessment
and risk rating"; read by "Consolidate merits and exposure into matter
assessment record".

V20.02 takes the registered matter handed over from V20.01 and produces a
consolidated assessment of legal merits, litigation risk rating and quantified
financial exposure. Legal counsel leads the legal analysis while the risk
manager calculates provisioning need and materiality. The completed matter
assessment record — covering merits, exposure, privilege considerations and
any provision raised — is stored in the Matter Management System and passed
to V20.03 to support the assignment of internal and external counsel.
```


### V20.03 — Assign Internal & External Counsel

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.03 Assign Internal & External Counsel — third subprocess in the
Matter to Resolution value chain, following Assess Merits & Exposure and
preceding Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal department and support functions carrying out
counsel assignment.
  Lane "Legal" — general counsel leads assignment decisions and engages
  external counsel.
Pool "External Counsel" — law firm or barrister engaged to act on the matter.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter and counsel
data.
Pool "Legal Spend Management" — system managing external counsel budgets,
engagement terms and billing.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "External Counsel" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Legal Spend Management" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Counsel
2. Organisation (white-box)
3. Matter Management System
4. Legal Spend Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Assessed matter received from Assess Merits & Exposure"
  User task "Review matter assessment and confirm scope of legal need"
  Exclusive gateway "External counsel required?"
  - branch "No — internal counsel sufficient":
      User task "Assign internal counsel and define responsibilities"
      Service task "Record internal counsel assignment in Matter Management
      System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Counsel assignment complete")
  - branch "Yes — external counsel needed":
      User task "Identify suitable external counsel and check conflicts of
      interest"
      Exclusive gateway "Conflict of interest found?"
      - branch "Yes — conflict exists":
          User task "Select alternative external counsel"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Conflict check passed")
      - branch "No — no conflict":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Conflict check passed")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Conflict check passed"
      User task "Prepare and issue letter of engagement and outside-counsel
      guidelines"
      Send task "Send engagement letter and guidelines to External Counsel"
      Intermediate message catch event "Engagement confirmed by External
      Counsel"
      User task "Establish external counsel budget and authority limits"
      Service task "Record external counsel engagement in Legal Spend
      Management"
      User task "Assign internal counsel liaison and link to external counsel"
      Service task "Record full counsel assignment in Matter Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Counsel assignment complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Counsel assignment complete"
  End event "Counsel assigned — ready for Issue Legal Hold & Preserve
  Evidence"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Prepare and issue letter
of engagement and outside-counsel guidelines" — label "Engagement letter
overdue (3 days)" — triggers Send task "Chase engagement confirmation from
External Counsel" which flows back to the intermediate message catch event
"Engagement confirmed by External Counsel".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane at the message start event and
proceeds through the conflict-check gateway; the "Yes — conflict exists"
branch leads to the alternative-selection task then rejoins at "Conflict check
passed"; the "No" branch rejoins the same merge gateway directly; both
branches of the outer "External counsel required?" gateway rejoin at "Counsel
assignment complete" before the end event.

Message flows:
  Legal lane "Send engagement letter and guidelines to External Counsel" →
  External Counsel (engagement letter and outside-counsel guidelines).
  External Counsel → Legal lane intermediate message catch event "Engagement
  confirmed by External Counsel" (signed engagement confirmation).
  Legal lane Service task "Record internal counsel assignment in Matter
  Management System" → Matter Management System (internal counsel assignment
  record).
  Legal lane Service task "Record full counsel assignment in Matter Management
  System" → Matter Management System (external and internal counsel assignment
  record).
  Matter Management System → Legal lane User task "Review matter assessment
  and confirm scope of legal need" (matter record and exposure assessment).
  Legal lane Service task "Record external counsel engagement in Legal Spend
  Management" → Legal Spend Management (counsel engagement, budget and
  authority limits).
  Legal Spend Management → Legal lane User task "Establish external counsel
  budget and authority limits" (budget templates and rate schedules).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Matter Assessment" — read by User task "Review matter assessment
and confirm scope of legal need".
Data Object "Conflict-of-Interest Check Record" — written by User task
"Identify suitable external counsel and check conflicts of interest"; read by
Exclusive gateway "Conflict of interest found?".
Data Object "Letter of Engagement" — written by User task "Prepare and issue
letter of engagement and outside-counsel guidelines"; read by Send task "Send
engagement letter and guidelines to External Counsel".
Data Object "Counsel Assignment Record" — written by Service task "Record
internal counsel assignment in Matter Management System" and by Service task
"Record full counsel assignment in Matter Management System".
Data Object "External Counsel Budget" — written by User task "Establish
external counsel budget and authority limits"; read by Service task "Record
external counsel engagement in Legal Spend Management".

This subprocess establishes who will conduct the legal defence or prosecution
of the matter, covering both the internal counsel liaison and any external law
firm engaged under formal outside-counsel guidelines. Conflict-of-interest
screening ensures independence, and budget authority limits are set before
any substantive legal work begins. The subprocess hands a fully assigned and
budgeted counsel team to Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence, which needs
identified custodians and a responsible counsel before holds can be issued.
```


### V20.04 — Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.04 Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Evidence — the fourth subprocess
in the Matter to Resolution value chain, triggered once counsel has been
assigned, covering the issuance of legal hold notices to custodians and the
systematic collection and preservation of evidence.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal department and business unit executing the
legal hold and evidence preservation process.
  Lane "Legal (Paralegal)" — paralegal who identifies custodians, issues hold
  notices, monitors compliance, and logs the hold.
  Lane "Business Unit (Matter Owner)" — matter owner who confirms custodians,
  locates and submits relevant evidence, and attests compliance.
Pool "Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform" — IT system that automates hold
notice distribution, tracks custodian responses, and collects evidence.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, containing Legal (Paralegal) lane above Business
   Unit (Matter Owner) lane)
2. Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (Paralegal) lane:
  Message start event "Counsel assignment confirmed — received from Assign
    Internal & External Counsel"
  User task "Identify custodians and data sources"
  Service task "Create legal hold order in platform"
  Send task "Issue legal hold notices to custodians"
  Intermediate message catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received"
  Exclusive gateway "All custodians acknowledged?"
    - branch "No — outstanding acknowledgements":
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All Custodians Acknowledge"
          (standard loop) containing, in order: User task "Chase
          non-responding custodians", Send task "Re-issue hold notice to
          non-responding custodians", Intermediate message catch event
          "Further acknowledgements received"
        (exits subprocess)
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All custodians acknowledged")
    - branch "Yes — all acknowledged":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All custodians acknowledged")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All custodians acknowledged"
  User task "Review collected evidence for completeness"
  Exclusive gateway "Evidence collection complete?"
    - branch "No — gaps identified":
        Send task "Request additional evidence from Business Unit"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence collection complete")
    - branch "Yes — collection sufficient":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Evidence collection complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Evidence collection complete"
  User task "Log hold and evidence index in platform"
  User task "Confirm privilege status and mark privileged materials"
  End event "Legal hold issued and evidence preserved — ready for Develop
    Strategy"

Business Unit (Matter Owner) lane:
  User task "Confirm custodian list and data locations"
  User task "Locate and submit relevant documents and records"
  User task "Attest hold compliance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until All
Custodians Acknowledge" — labelled "Escalation deadline reached (5 business
days)" — triggers Send task "Escalate unacknowledged hold to General Counsel"
in the Legal (Paralegal) lane, followed by End event "Hold compliance
escalated — awaiting General Counsel intervention".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Legal (Paralegal) lane with the start
event, then proceeds through custodian identification, hold creation, notice
issuance, acknowledgement waiting, and the loop subprocess where outstanding
acknowledgements are chased; both branches of "All custodians acknowledged?"
converge at the exclusive merge gateway; flow continues through evidence
review, the "Evidence collection complete?" gateway whose two branches
converge at its merge gateway, then through logging, privilege marking, and
the end event. The Business Unit (Matter Owner) lane tasks occur in parallel
following the issue of hold notices: "Confirm custodian list and data
locations" runs concurrently with custodian identification, "Locate and
submit relevant documents and records" runs concurrently with the
acknowledgement phase, and "Attest hold compliance" runs concurrently with
evidence review.

Message flows:
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): Service task "Create
  legal hold order in platform" (hold order confirmation)
Legal (Paralegal) → Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform: Send task "Issue
  legal hold notices to custodians" (hold notices for distribution)
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): Intermediate message
  catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received" (acknowledgement records)
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): Intermediate message
  catch event "Further acknowledgements received" (additional acknowledgement
  records)
Business Unit (Matter Owner) → Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform: User task
  "Locate and submit relevant documents and records" (evidence and documents)
Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform → Legal (Paralegal): User task "Review
  collected evidence for completeness" (collected evidence index)
Legal (Paralegal) → Legal Hold & e-Discovery Platform: User task "Log hold
  and evidence index in platform" (finalised hold record and evidence index)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Custodian and Data Source List" — written by User task
  "Identify custodians and data sources"; read by Service task "Create legal
  hold order in platform" and User task "Confirm custodian list and data
  locations".
Data Object "Legal Hold Notice" — written by Service task "Create legal hold
  order in platform"; read by Send task "Issue legal hold notices to
  custodians" and Send task "Re-issue hold notice to non-responding
  custodians".
Data Object "Custodian Acknowledgement Record" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Custodian acknowledgements received"; read by
  Exclusive gateway "All custodians acknowledged?".
Data Object "Evidence Collection" — written by User task "Locate and submit
  relevant documents and records"; read by User task "Review collected
  evidence for completeness".
Data Object "Evidence Index and Privilege Log" — written by User task "Log
  hold and evidence index in platform" and User task "Confirm privilege
  status and mark privileged materials"; read by End event "Legal hold issued
  and evidence preserved — ready for Develop Strategy".

This subprocess ensures that, once counsel is in place, all potential
custodians are formally notified of their preservation obligations, their
compliance is tracked and enforced, and relevant documents and data are
collected, indexed, and assessed for privilege. It hands the Develop Strategy
subprocess a complete legal hold record, an indexed evidence collection, and
a privilege log, giving the strategy team a secure and auditable evidential
foundation from which to plan the organisation's legal position.
```

```text
Pool "External Counsel" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. External Counsel
2. Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Legal (legal counsel))
3. Matter Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (legal counsel) lane:
  Message start event "Strategy brief received from Assign Internal &
  External Counsel"
  User task "Review matter record, exposure assessment, and counsel
  assignments"
  Service task "Retrieve matter record from Matter Management System"
  User task "Define litigation, negotiation, and settlement objectives"
  Send task "Issue strategy brief to External Counsel"
  Intermediate message catch event "Strategic advice received from

  User task "Draft legal strategy document"
  Exclusive gateway "Strategy document complete and privileged?"
    - branch "No — revisions required": Expanded Subprocess "Revise

      Intermediate message catch event "Revised advice received from

      User task "Incorporate revisions into strategy document"
      (exits subprocess)
    - branch "Yes — approved": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Strategy document complete and privileged?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Strategy document complete and privileged?"
  User task "Record privilege designation and access controls"
  Service task "Submit strategy document and privilege log to Matter
  Management System"
  End event "Strategy document approved — ready for Manage Discovery
  & Disclosure"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal (legal counsel) lane with the
message start event and proceeds linearly through matter review, objective
setting, and brief issue; after the intermediate catch event for strategic
advice the legal counsel drafts the strategy document and reaches the
exclusive gateway; the "No" branch enters the revision loop subprocess and
exits back to the exclusive merge gateway; the "Yes" branch continues
directly to the merge gateway; flow then continues through privilege
designation and system submission to the end event.

Message flows:
  Send task "Issue strategy brief to External Counsel" → External
  Counsel (strategy brief and instructions)
  External Counsel → Intermediate message catch event "Strategic advice
  received from External Counsel" (strategic advice and draft inputs)
  Send task "Request further input from External Counsel" → External
  Counsel (revision request)
  External Counsel → Intermediate message catch event "Revised advice
  received from External Counsel" (revised advice)
  Service task "Retrieve matter record from Matter Management System" →
  Matter Management System (matter record retrieval request)
  Matter Management System → Service task "Retrieve matter record from
  Matter Management System" (matter record and exposure assessment)
  Service task "Submit strategy document and privilege log to Matter
  Management System" → Matter Management System (strategy document and
  privilege log)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Strategy Brief" — written by Send task "Issue strategy brief
to External Counsel"; read by External Counsel.
Data Object "Strategic Advice" — written by External Counsel; read by
User task "Draft legal strategy document".
Data Object "Legal Strategy Document" — written by User task "Draft legal
strategy document"; read by User task "Record privilege designation and
access controls" and Service task "Submit strategy document and privilege
log to Matter Management System".
Data Object "Privilege Log" — written by User task "Record privilege
designation and access controls"; read by Service task "Submit strategy
document and privilege log to Matter Management System".

This subprocess transforms the counsel assignments and exposure assessment
from V20.04 into a privileged, access-controlled legal strategy document
that sets the objectives and approach for the matter. External counsel's
advice is solicited, incorporated, and iterated until the strategy is
complete, at which point the document and its privilege log are lodged in
the Matter Management System and passed to V20.06 Manage Discovery &
Disclosure as the authoritative guide for all subsequent steps.
```

```text
  Exclusive merge gateway "Production obligation determined"
```

### V20.07 — Negotiate or Mediate

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.07 Negotiate or Mediate — subprocess within the Matter to
Resolution value chain, receiving a negotiation-ready matter from Develop
Strategy and handing a resolved or unresolved matter to Litigate or Defend.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal function, executive management, and
supporting teams conducting negotiation or mediation.
  Lane "Legal" — legal counsel leading negotiation and mediation activity.
  Lane "Executive Management" — delegated approver authorising settlement
  authority and escalation decisions.
Pool "Counterparty" — claimant, litigant, complainant or opposing counsel
participating in negotiation or mediation.
Pool "Mediator" — neutral third-party mediator or arbitrator facilitating
structured mediation sessions.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter status,
negotiation positions, privilege logs and exposure updates.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Counterparty" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Mediator" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Counterparty
2. Mediator
3. Organisation (Legal lane above Executive Management lane)
4. Matter Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal lane:
  Message start event "Strategy approved — ready for Negotiate or Mediate"
  User task "Review negotiation position and settlement authority limits"
  Service task "Record negotiation position in matter record"
  Exclusive gateway "Negotiation approach?"
  - branch "Direct negotiation": User task "Prepare and send settlement
    offer to counterparty"
    Send task "Transmit settlement offer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty response received"
    Exclusive gateway "Counterparty response?"
    - branch "Offer accepted": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Counterparty response")
    - branch "Counteroffer received": User task "Evaluate counteroffer
      against authority limits"
      Exclusive gateway "Within authority?"
      - branch "Yes — proceed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Within authority")
      - branch "No — escalate": Send task "Escalate to Executive Management
        for authority increase"
        Intermediate message catch event "Executive Management decision
        received"
        Exclusive merge gateway "Within authority"
      User task "Revise settlement position"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Counterparty response")
    - branch "Offer rejected": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Counterparty response")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Counterparty response"
    Exclusive gateway "Settlement reached via direct negotiation?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Settlement
      reached?")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Settlement
      reached?")
  - branch "Mediation": Send task "Instruct mediator and share matter
    summary"
    Intermediate message catch event "Mediator session scheduled"
    User task "Prepare mediation brief and evidence bundle"
    User task "Attend and participate in mediation session"
    Intermediate message catch event "Mediation outcome received"
    Exclusive gateway "Mediation outcome?"
    - branch "Settlement agreed": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Mediation outcome")
    - branch "Impasse — no agreement": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Mediation outcome")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Mediation outcome"
    Exclusive gateway "Settlement reached via mediation?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Settlement
      reached?")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Settlement
      reached?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Negotiation approach"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Settlement reached?"
  Exclusive gateway "Matter resolved?"
  - branch "Yes — settlement agreed": User task "Document agreed settlement
    terms"
    Service task "Update matter record with settlement outcome"
    End event "Settlement agreed — ready for Settle or Obtain Judgment"
  - branch "No — negotiation exhausted": User task "Prepare negotiation
    summary and escalation note"
    Service task "Update matter record with failed negotiation outcome"
    End event "Negotiation exhausted — ready for Litigate or Defend"

Executive Management lane:
  User task "Review escalated position and determine revised authority"
  Send task "Communicate authority decision to Legal"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded — mounted on User task "Attend
and participate in mediation session", label "Mediation session time limit
reached", triggers Send task "Notify mediator of adjournment required" then
rejoins flow at Intermediate message catch event "Mediation outcome received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with the message start event,
proceeds through position review and recording, then splits at the "Negotiation
approach" gateway into the direct-negotiation branch or the mediation branch;
the direct-negotiation branch internally loops through offer, response, and
authority-escalation cycles before resolving at the "Settlement reached via
direct negotiation?" gateway; the mediation branch proceeds through instruction,
preparation and session attendance before resolving at "Settlement reached via
mediation?"; both branches merge at "Settlement reached?" and continue to the
"Matter resolved?" gateway, whose two branches end in their respective end
events. The Executive Management lane handles escalated authority decisions and
returns a decision message to the Legal lane.

Message flows:
Counterparty → Legal lane (counterparty response to settlement offer)
Legal lane → Counterparty (settlement offer transmitted)
Legal lane → Mediator (mediator instruction and matter summary)
Mediator → Legal lane (session schedule and mediation outcome)
Legal lane → Matter Management System (negotiation position and outcome
  recorded)
Matter Management System → Legal lane (current matter record, exposure
  figures and authority limits)
Executive Management lane → Legal lane (authority decision communicated)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Negotiation Position" — written by User task "Review negotiation
position and settlement authority limits"; read by User task "Prepare and
send settlement offer to counterparty".
Data Object "Settlement Offer" — written by User task "Prepare and send
settlement offer to counterparty"; read by Send task "Transmit settlement
offer".
Data Object "Counteroffer" — written by User task "Evaluate counteroffer
against authority limits"; read by User task "Revise settlement position".
Data Object "Mediation Brief" — written by User task "Prepare mediation brief
and evidence bundle"; read by User task "Attend and participate in mediation
session".
Data Object "Settlement Terms" — written by User task "Document agreed
settlement terms"; read by Service task "Update matter record with settlement
outcome".
Data Object "Negotiation Summary" — written by User task "Prepare negotiation
summary and escalation note"; read by Service task "Update matter record with
failed negotiation outcome".

This subprocess manages all direct negotiation and structured mediation
activity, cycling through offer, response, and authority-escalation steps
for direct negotiation or through brief preparation, session attendance, and
outcome capture for mediation. Where the parties reach a settlement, the
agreed terms are documented and the matter is handed to Settle or Obtain
Judgment for execution and financial closure. Where negotiation is fully
exhausted without agreement, a summary is recorded and the matter is passed
to Litigate or Defend.
```

### V20.09 — Settle or Obtain Judgment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V20.09 Settle or Obtain Judgment — the subprocess in which the
organisation resolves the matter either by negotiated settlement or by
court judgment, updates financial provisions, and notifies insurers,
handing a closed resolution record to Close Matter & Capture Lessons.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the legal, finance and general counsel teams
  executing the settlement or judgment process.
  Lanes (top to bottom):
  - Legal — General Counsel
  - Finance — Finance Business Partner
Pool "Counterparty" — the claimant, litigant, complainant or opposing
  party with whom settlement may be reached.
Pool "Insurer" — the insurer notified of the outcome and called on to
  contribute where applicable.
Pool "Matter Management System" — system of record for matter status,
  settlement records and exposure.
Pool "Finance / ERP System" — system recording provision adjustments,
  accrual postings and settlement payments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Counterparty" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Matter Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.
Pool "Finance / ERP System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Counterparty
2. Organisation (white-box, two lanes)
3. Insurer
4. Matter Management System
5. Finance / ERP System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal — General Counsel lane:
  Message start event "Strategy and authority limits received from
    Develop Strategy"
  User task "Review settlement authority and resolution options"
  Exclusive gateway "Resolution path?"
  - branch "Negotiate settlement":
      User task "Prepare and issue settlement offer to counterparty"
      Send task "Send settlement offer to counterparty"
      Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty response received"
      Exclusive gateway "Offer accepted?"
      - branch "Yes — settlement reached":
          User task "Finalise and execute settlement agreement"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Offer accepted?")
      - branch "No — counter-offer or rejection":
          Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Settlement Agreed or
            Abandoned" (standard loop) containing, in order:
            User task "Review counterparty position and revise offer",
            User task "Seek revised authority if limits exceeded",
            Send task "Send revised offer to counterparty",
            Intermediate message catch event "Counterparty response
              received"
          Exclusive gateway "Agreement reached after iteration?"
          - branch "Yes":
              User task "Finalise and execute settlement agreement"
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Agreement reached
                after iteration?")
          - branch "No — proceed to litigation judgment":
              (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path?
                merge")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Offer accepted?"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path? merge")
  - branch "Obtain court judgment":
      Intermediate message catch event "Court judgment received"
      User task "Review and record judgment terms"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path? merge")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Resolution path? merge"
  User task "Notify insurer of outcome and claim contribution"
  Send task "Send outcome notification to insurer"
  Intermediate message catch event "Insurer acknowledgement received"
  User task "Update matter record with resolution outcome"
  Service task "Record settlement or judgment in Matter Management
    System"
  End event "Resolution record complete — ready for Close Matter and
    Capture Lessons"

Finance — Finance Business Partner lane:
  User task "Review current financial provision against resolution
    amount"
  Exclusive gateway "Provision adjustment required?"
  - branch "Yes — adjust provision":
      User task "Prepare provision adjustment journal"
      Service task "Post provision adjustment to Finance / ERP System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provision adjustment
        required?")
  - branch "No — provision sufficient":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Provision adjustment
        required?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Provision adjustment required?"
  User task "Confirm payment or recovery instruction"
  Service task "Record settlement payment or receipt in Finance /
    ERP System"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Settlement Agreed or Abandoned", labelled "Maximum negotiation
  period elapsed", leading to End event "Negotiation time-out —
  escalate to litigation".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal — General Counsel lane with
  the message start event, moves through the resolution-path gateway
  whose "Negotiate settlement" branch drives the offer, catch, and
  acceptance gateway, with the "Yes" branch producing the settlement
  agreement and rejoining at the "Offer accepted?" merge, and the
  "No" branch entering the repeat subprocess before testing agreement
  again; both settlement and judgment branches converge at the
  "Resolution path? merge" gateway before flowing through insurer

  triggered in parallel after the resolution path merges, running

Message flows:

    counterparty") → Counterparty (settlement offer)

    event "Counterparty response received") (acceptance, rejection or

  Legal — General Counsel (Send task "Send revised offer to
    counterparty") → Counterparty (revised settlement offer, inside

    "Insurer acknowledgement received") (insurer acknowledgement)
  Legal — General Counsel (Service task "Record settlement or judgment
    in Matter Management System") → Matter Management System (resolution
    record update)
  Matter Management System → Legal — General Counsel (matter record
    confirmation)
  Finance — Finance Business Partner (Service task "Post provision
    adjustment to Finance / ERP System") → Finance / ERP System

  Finance / ERP System → Finance — Finance Business Partner (posting
    confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Settlement Offer" — written by User task "Prepare and

  settlement offer to counterparty".
Data Object "Settlement Agreement" — written by User task "Finalise
  and execute settlement agreement"; read by User task "Update matter
  record with resolution outcome".
Data Object "Court Judgment" — written by User task "Review and record
  judgment terms"; read by User task "Update matter record with
  resolution outcome".
Data Object "Provision Adjustment Journal" — written by User task
  "Prepare provision adjustment journal"; read by Service task "Post
  provision adjustment to Finance / ERP System".
Data Object "Insurer Notification" — written by User task "Notify
  insurer of outcome and claim contribution"; read by Send task "Send
  outcome notification to insurer".

This subprocess takes the authorised strategy and settlement limits from
Develop Strategy and drives the matter to a definitive resolution, either
by executed settlement agreement or by receipt and recording of a court
judgment. Financial provisions are adjusted and posted, the insurer is
notified and acknowledged, and the matter record is updated in the Matter
Management System. The completed resolution record then passes to Close
Matter and Capture Lessons for post-matter review, reporting and archiving.
```

```text
  matter closure and lessons-learned capture.

  closure data, and lessons learned.

  reporting on matter outcomes.

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.

1. Organisation
2. Matter Management System
3. Board Reporting System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Legal (legal counsel) lane:
  Message start event "Settlement, judgment, or withdrawal confirmed — received
    from Settle or Obtain Judgment"
  User task "Review matter outcome and confirm closure eligibility"
  Service task "Retrieve final matter record from Matter Management System"
  User task "Draft matter closure summary"
  Exclusive gateway "All obligations discharged?"
  - branch "No — outstanding obligations":
      User task "Resolve outstanding obligations"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All obligations discharged")
  - branch "Yes — obligations clear":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All obligations discharged")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All obligations discharged"
  User task "Conduct lessons-learned review"
  User task "Document lessons learned and recommended process improvements"
  Service task "Record closure and lessons learned in Matter Management System"
  Send task "Submit matter closure report to Company Secretariat"

Company Secretariat (company secretary) lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Matter closure report received"
  User task "Review closure report and confirm board reporting obligations"
  Exclusive gateway "Board or committee reporting required?"
  - branch "Yes — reporting required":
      User task "Prepare board or committee report on matter outcome"
      Service task "Publish report via Board Reporting System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Board reporting required")
  - branch "No — no board reporting":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Board reporting required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Board reporting required"
  User task "Archive matter record and confirm document retention compliance"
  Service task "Set matter status to Closed in Matter Management System"
  End event "Matter closed and lessons captured — value chain complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Resolve outstanding obligations" —
  label "Obligation resolution overdue (14 days)" — triggers User task
  "Escalate unresolved obligations to general counsel".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Legal lane with the message start event,
  proceeds through outcome review, closure eligibility check (with the
  outstanding-obligations branch looping through resolution before merging),
  then through lessons-learned drafting and recording, and closes with a
  send task passing the closure report to the Company Secretariat lane;
  the Company Secretariat lane resumes after the intermediate message catch
  event, checks board reporting obligation (yes branch through report
  preparation and publication, no branch bypassing both, merging before
  archiving), then archives the record and closes the matter.

Message flows:
  Service task "Retrieve final matter record from Matter Management System"
    → Matter Management System (request for final matter record).
  Matter Management System → Service task "Retrieve final matter record
    from Matter Management System" (final matter record returned).
  Service task "Record closure and lessons learned in Matter Management
```
