```text
This subprocess receives confirmation that a matter has been settled, judged,
or withdrawn and brings it to a formal close. Legal counsel reviews the
outcome, discharges any remaining obligations, and captures structured lessons
learned before Company Secretariat archives the record, fulfils any board
reporting obligation, and sets the matter status to Closed in the Matter
Management System, completing the Matter to Resolution value chain.
```


## V21 — Application to Decision

**Teams and roles involved.**
Application to Decision usually involves Intake or Contact Centre, Assessment/Underwriting, Credit or Eligibility Analysis, Verification, Risk, Fraud, Compliance, and Quality Assurance, with an Appeals or Review function for disputed outcomes. Key roles include intake officer, assessor, underwriter, credit analyst, verification officer, fraud analyst, delegated approver, quality reviewer, and appeals officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Applicant. The process is initiated when the applicant submits an application for credit, insurance cover, a grant, a licence, a benefit, admission or membership. Other external parties include credit bureaux and identity verification services, employers and referees, brokers or agents acting for the applicant, and regulators setting eligibility rules.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive the application, check completeness and request missing information, verify identity, gather supporting evidence and third-party data, assess eligibility against criteria, score and price the risk, refer to a delegated authority where limits are exceeded, decide approve, decline or approve with conditions, notify the applicant with reasons, and handle appeals or reviews.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include the application or origination platform, customer portal and document upload, identity verification and credit bureau interfaces, decision engines and scorecards, fraud detection, case management, document management, correspondence generation, and reporting for decision quality and turnaround.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include eligibility criteria and product rules, delegated authority and approval limits, identity verification and anti-money-laundering requirements, responsible lending or suitability obligations, adverse-action and reasons-for-decision requirements, privacy and data-minimisation rules, fraud referral procedures, quality assurance sampling, and appeal rights and timeframes.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The applicant provides the application, identity documents, supporting evidence, consents and declarations, and responses to requests for more information. The process provides the applicant with acknowledgement and reference, requests for further information, status updates, the decision with reasons and any conditions, and appeal rights. Third parties provide bureau reports, verification results and referee responses.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates application records, verification outcomes, evidence documents, scores and decision rationale, referrals and approvals, correspondence, and appeal records. IT systems provide product and eligibility rules, bureau and verification responses, fraud signals, decision-engine outputs, delegated authority limits, and turnaround, approval-rate and quality reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Assessing Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V21.01** Receive Application | Applicant, Broker | Intake (intake officer) | Application / Origination Platform, Customer Portal |
| **V21.02** Check Completeness | Applicant | Intake (intake officer) | Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.03** Verify Identity | Applicant, Identity Verification Service | Verification (verification officer) | Identity Verification Service, Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.04** Gather Supporting Evidence | Applicant, Credit Bureau | Verification (verification officer) | Credit Bureau Interface, Document Management System |
| **V21.05** Assess Eligibility | — | Assessment (assessor) | Decision Engine, Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.06** Score & Price Risk | — | Assessment (underwriter), Risk (credit analyst) | Decision Engine |
| **V21.07** Refer to Delegated Authority | — | Assessment (delegated approver) | Case Management System |
| **V21.08** Decide Outcome | — | Assessment (underwriter), Compliance (compliance officer) | Application / Origination Platform |
| **V21.09** Notify Applicant with Reasons | Applicant | Intake (intake officer) | Correspondence System, Customer Portal |
| **V21.10** Handle Appeal or Review | Applicant | Appeals (appeals officer), Quality Assurance (quality reviewer) | Case Management System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V21):

- **External actors:** Applicant (V21.01–V21.04, V21.09, V21.10); Broker (V21.01); Identity Verification Service (V21.03); Credit Bureau (V21.04).
- **Teams:** Intake (V21.01, V21.02, V21.09); Verification (V21.03, V21.04); Assessment (V21.05–V21.08); Risk (V21.06); Compliance (V21.08); Appeals (V21.10); Quality Assurance (V21.10).
- **IT systems:** Application / Origination Platform (V21.01–V21.03, V21.05, V21.08); Customer Portal (V21.01, V21.09); Identity Verification Service (V21.03); Credit Bureau Interface (V21.04); Document Management System (V21.04); Decision Engine (V21.05, V21.06); Case Management System (V21.07, V21.10); Correspondence System (V21.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V21 — Application to Decision — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Application to Decision value chain, from first receipt of an application
through to appeal or review. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands
read top-to-bottom as service realisation: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) shows
what the assessing organisation offers to external participants;
BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows the ten subprocesses that realise those
services; APPLICATIONS (bottom band) shows the IT systems that support the
processes. The Applicant and Broker sit on the far left as demand-side actors;
the Identity Verification Service and Credit Bureau sit on the far right as
external delivery and data-provision actors.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Applicant — far left; initiates the chain and receives decisions and
  notifications throughout.
- Broker — far left, below Applicant; acts on behalf of the applicant at
  intake.
- Identity Verification Service — far right; provides identity verification
  results to the process.
- Credit Bureau — far right, below Identity Verification Service; provides
  bureau reports and credit data.

2. Interfaces

- Applicant Portal Interface — accessed by Applicant and Broker; serves the
  Application Submission Service and the Notification and Decision Service.
- Broker Submission Interface — accessed by Broker; serves the Application
  Submission Service.
- Identity Verification Interface — accessed by Identity Verification Service;
  serves the Identity and Evidence Verification Service.
- Credit Bureau Interface — accessed by Credit Bureau; serves the Identity and
  Evidence Verification Service.
- Appeal Lodgement Interface — accessed by Applicant; serves the Appeal and
  Review Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Application Submission Service — accepts applications and supporting
  documents from the applicant or broker and issues an acknowledgement and
  reference.
- Completeness and Information Request Service — checks applications for
  missing information and requests any outstanding items from the applicant.
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service — verifies applicant identity and
  gathers third-party supporting evidence including bureau and referee data.
- Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service — assesses eligibility against
  product rules and scores and prices the risk of the application.
- Delegated Authority Referral Service — routes cases that exceed assessment
  limits to an appropriately authorised approver.
- Decision and Outcome Service — records the approve, decline, or
  conditional-approval decision with full reasons and conditions.
- Notification and Decision Service — communicates the decision, reasons, and
  any conditions to the applicant.
- Appeal and Review Service — accepts and manages appeals or review requests
  from applicants and returns a reviewed outcome.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V21.01 Receive Application — intake officer receives the application from
  the applicant or broker and creates the application record.
- V21.02 Check Completeness — intake officer checks the application for
  completeness and requests missing information from the applicant.
- V21.03 Verify Identity — verification officer confirms applicant identity
  using the identity verification service.
- V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence — verification officer collects bureau
  reports, employer or referee responses, and other third-party data.
- V21.05 Assess Eligibility — assessor evaluates the application against
  eligibility criteria and product rules.
- V21.06 Score & Price Risk — underwriter and credit analyst score and price
  the risk of the application using scorecards.
- V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority — delegated approver receives and acts
  on referrals where approval limits are exceeded.
- V21.08 Decide Outcome — underwriter and compliance officer record the final
  approve, decline, or conditional decision.
- V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons — intake officer generates and sends
  the decision notice with reasons and appeal rights to the applicant.
- V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review — appeals officer and quality reviewer
  manage the appeal or review and communicate the reviewed outcome.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Application / Origination Platform — core platform for application record
  creation, completeness checking, eligibility assessment, and decision
  recording.
- Customer Portal — self-service channel for application submission, document
  upload, status updates, and receipt of decision notices.
- Identity Verification Service (system) — interface and processing layer for
  real-time identity verification checks.
- Credit Bureau Interface — integration layer for retrieving bureau reports
  and credit data from external bureaux.
- Document Management System — stores and manages identity documents,
  evidence files, and supporting materials.
- Decision Engine — applies product eligibility rules, scorecards, and
  pricing models to produce decision-engine outputs.
- Case Management System — manages referral workflows for delegated authority
  and tracks appeal and review cases.
- Correspondence System — generates and distributes decision letters,
  information-request notices, and appeal-rights communications.

6. Relationships

SERVING
- Application Submission Service SERVES Applicant.
- Application Submission Service SERVES Broker.
- Completeness and Information Request Service SERVES Applicant.
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service SERVES Identity Verification
  Service (actor).
- Identity and Evidence Verification Service SERVES Credit Bureau (actor).
- Notification and Decision Service SERVES Applicant.
- Appeal and Review Service SERVES Applicant.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.01 Receive Application.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.02 Check Completeness.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.03 Verify Identity.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.05 Assess Eligibility.
- Application / Origination Platform SERVES V21.08 Decide Outcome.
- Customer Portal SERVES V21.01 Receive Application.
- Customer Portal SERVES V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons.
- Identity Verification Service (system) SERVES V21.03 Verify Identity.
- Credit Bureau Interface SERVES V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence.
- Document Management System SERVES V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence.
- Decision Engine SERVES V21.05 Assess Eligibility.
- Decision Engine SERVES V21.06 Score & Price Risk.
- Case Management System SERVES V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority.
- Case Management System SERVES V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review.
- Correspondence System SERVES V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons.

REALISATION
- V21.01 Receive Application REALISES Application Submission Service.
- V21.02 Check Completeness REALISES Completeness and Information Request
  Service.
- V21.03 Verify Identity REALISES Identity and Evidence Verification Service.
- V21.04 Gather Supporting Evidence REALISES Identity and Evidence
  Verification Service.
- V21.05 Assess Eligibility REALISES Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service.
- V21.06 Score & Price Risk REALISES Eligibility and Risk Assessment Service.
- V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority REALISES Delegated Authority Referral
  Service.
- V21.08 Decide Outcome REALISES Decision and Outcome Service.
- V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons REALISES Notification and Decision
  Service.
- V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review REALISES Appeal and Review Service.

ASSIGNMENT
- Applicant Portal Interface ASSIGNED TO Customer Portal.
- Broker Submission Interface ASSIGNED TO Application / Origination Platform.
- Identity Verification Interface ASSIGNED TO Identity Verification Service
  (system).
- Credit Bureau Interface (interface) ASSIGNED TO Credit Bureau Interface
  (system).
- Appeal Lodgement Interface ASSIGNED TO Case Management System.

ACCESS
- Applicant ACCESSES Applicant Portal Interface.
- Broker ACCESSES Applicant Portal Interface.
- Broker ACCESSES Broker Submission Interface.
- Identity Verification Service (actor) ACCESSES Identity Verification
  Interface.
- Credit Bureau (actor) ACCESSES Credit Bureau Interface (interface).
- Applicant ACCESSES Appeal Lodgement Interface.
```

```text
This subprocess captures every inbound application, regardless of whether it
arrives directly from the applicant via the customer portal or through a
broker. It assigns a unique reference, opens a case in the origination
platform, and sends the applicant an acknowledgement. The verified application
record is then handed to Check Completeness, which confirms that all required
fields and documents are present before assessment begins.
```

```text
        Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Application Complete"
        (standard loop) containing, in order:
          User task "Identify missing or deficient items"
          Send task "Request missing information from applicant"
          Intermediate message catch event "Applicant response received"
          User task "Review applicant response and update checklist"
        (exits subprocess)
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Application complete?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Application complete?"
  Service task "Record completeness confirmation in platform"
  End event "Application confirmed complete — ready for Verify Identity"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Application Complete", labelled "Maximum information-request period
elapsed", leading to: End event "Application abandoned — incomplete
after time limit".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow proceeds through the Intake lane from the message
start event to retrieve the record, then to the completeness check, then
to the "Application complete?" gateway. The "Yes" branch and the exit of
the loop subprocess both rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Application
complete?", continuing to record confirmation and the end event. The
loop subprocess internally sequences identify missing items, send request,
catch the applicant response, and review the response, repeating until
the checklist is satisfied. The timer boundary on the subprocess
interrupts and routes to the abandonment end event.

Message flows:
Application / Origination Platform → Intake "Retrieve application record
and completeness checklist" (application record and checklist).
Intake "Record completeness confirmation in platform" →
Application / Origination Platform (completeness status update).
Intake "Request missing information from applicant" → Applicant
(request for missing or deficient items).
Applicant → Intake "Applicant response received" (additional
information or documents submitted by applicant).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Completeness Checklist" — written by "Check application
against completeness checklist"; read by "Identify missing or deficient
items"; read by "Review applicant response and update checklist".
Data Object "Information Request" — written by "Identify missing or
deficient items"; read by "Request missing information from applicant".
Data Object "Applicant Response" — written by (message received at)
"Applicant response received"; read by "Review applicant response and
update checklist".

This subprocess ensures that only fully documented applications proceed
further. The intake officer works through a structured checklist, loops
requesting and reviewing information from the applicant until every
required item is present, then records the confirmed completeness status
in the Application / Origination Platform. A timer boundary protects
throughput by abandoning applications that remain incomplete beyond the
permitted period. A complete, confirmed application is handed to Verify
Identity for the next stage of processing.
```


### V21.03 — Verify Identity

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.03 Verify Identity — third subprocess of the Application to
Decision value chain, sitting between Check Completeness and Gather Supporting
Evidence.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation running the identity
verification work, with lanes for Verification.
  Lane "Verification" — verification officer who drives the checks,
  updates records, and resolves any identity issues.

Pool "Applicant" — external individual or entity whose identity is
being verified.

that performs automated identity and document checks.

for application data and verification outcomes.

routes requests and responses between the process and the external
Identity Verification Service.

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Identity Verification Service" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Identity Verification Service (IT)" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Identity Verification Service
3. Assessing Organisation
4. Identity Verification Service (IT)
5. Application / Origination Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Verification lane:
  Message start event "Completed application received from Check
    Completeness"
  Service task "Retrieve application and identity documents from
    platform"
  User task "Review identity documents submitted by applicant"
  Exclusive gateway "Documents sufficient to attempt verification?"
  - branch "No — documents missing or illegible": Send task "Request
    additional identity documents from applicant"
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional identity documents
      received from applicant"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Documents sufficient to
      attempt verification?")
  - branch "Yes — documents in hand": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Documents sufficient to attempt verification?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Documents sufficient to attempt
    verification?"
  Service task "Submit identity check request to verification service"
  Intermediate message catch event "Verification result received from
    Identity Verification Service"
  Exclusive gateway "Automated check passed?"
  - branch "Yes — identity confirmed": (continues to exclusive merge
      gateway "Automated check passed?")
  - branch "No — check inconclusive or failed": User task "Review
    failed verification result and determine next action"
    Exclusive gateway "Manual resolution possible?"
    - branch "Yes — override with evidence": User task "Record manual
      identity confirmation with supporting rationale"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Manual resolution
        possible?")
    - branch "No — identity cannot be confirmed": Service task
      "Flag application as identity failure on platform"
      End event "Identity verification failed — application halted
        before Gather Supporting Evidence"
    Exclusive merge gateway "Manual resolution possible?"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Automated check passed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Automated check passed?"
  Service task "Record verified identity outcome on platform"
  User task "Confirm AML and identity check compliance requirements
    met"
  End event "Identity verified — ready for Gather Supporting Evidence"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Send task "Request additional
identity documents from applicant" — label "Identity document
deadline exceeded" — triggers Service task "Flag application as
identity failure on platform" leading to End event "Identity
verification failed — application halted before Gather Supporting
Evidence".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Verification lane runs from the message
start event through document review, the "Documents sufficient?"
gateway (with its missing-documents branch looping via the
intermediate message catch event and rejoining at the merge), on
to the verification service submission and result catch event, then
the "Automated check passed?" gateway (with the manual-review
sub-branch either rejoining at the "Manual resolution possible?"
merge or ending at the failure end event, then rejoining the main
gateway merge), concluding with the platform record task, AML
confirmation, and the success end event.

Message flows:
  Applicant → Verification lane, Message start event (completed
    application with identity documents)
  Verification lane, Send task "Request additional identity documents
    from applicant" → Applicant (request for further documents)
  Applicant → Verification lane, Intermediate message catch event
    "Additional identity documents received from applicant"
    (additional documents)
  Verification lane, Service task "Submit identity check request to
    verification service" → Identity Verification Service (IT)
    (identity check request)
  Identity Verification Service (IT) → Identity Verification Service
    (identity check request forwarded)
  Identity Verification Service → Identity Verification Service (IT)
    (verification result)
  Identity Verification Service (IT) → Verification lane,
    Intermediate message catch event "Verification result received
    from Identity Verification Service" (verification result)
  Verification lane, Service task "Retrieve application and identity
    documents from platform" → Application / Origination Platform
    (document retrieval request)
  Application / Origination Platform → Verification lane, Service
    task "Retrieve application and identity documents from platform"
    (application record and identity documents)
  Verification lane, Service task "Record verified identity outcome
    on platform" → Application / Origination Platform (verified
    identity outcome)
  Verification lane, Service task "Flag application as identity
    failure on platform" → Application / Origination Platform
    (identity failure flag)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Identity Documents" — read by User task "Review identity
  documents submitted by applicant"; written by Message start event
  "Completed application received from Check Completeness".
Data Object "Verification Request" — written by Service task "Submit
  identity check request to verification service"; read by
  Identity Verification Service (IT).
Data Object "Verification Result" — written by Intermediate message
  catch event "Verification result received from Identity
  Verification Service"; read by Exclusive gateway "Automated check
  passed?".
Data Object "Identity Verification Outcome Record" — written by
  Service task "Record verified identity outcome on platform";
  read by User task "Confirm AML and identity check compliance
  requirements met".
Data Object "Manual Confirmation Rationale" — written by User task
  "Record manual identity confirmation with supporting rationale";
  read by Service task "Record verified identity outcome on
  platform".

V21.03 Verify Identity takes the complete, validated application from
Check Completeness and subjects the applicant to automated identity
and document checks routed through the Identity Verification Service,
with a manual review path for inconclusive results and an AML
compliance confirmation before closure. A clean verified-identity
outcome and an updated application record are handed to Gather
Supporting Evidence, while any irresolvable identity failure halts
the application and flags it on the platform before that stage is
reached.
```

### V21.05 — Assess Eligibility

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.05 Assess Eligibility — the fifth subprocess in the Application
to Decision value chain, in which the Assessment team evaluates the verified
application against product eligibility criteria and rules, producing an
eligibility outcome that feeds into scoring and pricing.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation conducting the eligibility
  assessment, containing Assessment team lanes.
Pool "Decision Engine" — the rules and decision engine system that evaluates
  eligibility criteria and returns outputs.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — the platform holding the
  application record and product rules.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Decision Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — top (process owner).
Pool "Decision Engine" — below Assessing Organisation.
Pool "Application / Origination Platform" — bottom.

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane:
  Message start event "Verified application received from Verify Identity"
  Service task "Retrieve application record and product rules"
  Service task "Submit application to Decision Engine for eligibility check"
  Intermediate message catch event "Eligibility result received from
    Decision Engine"
  Exclusive gateway "Eligibility result?"
  - branch "Eligible": User task "Review eligibility confirmation and
      record outcome"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility result")
  - branch "Ineligible": User task "Review ineligibility flags and
      record reasons"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility result")
  - branch "Refer for manual review": User task "Conduct manual
      eligibility review against criteria"
      Exclusive gateway "Manual review outcome?"
      - branch "Eligible after review": User task "Record manual
          eligibility approval"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Manual review outcome")
      - branch "Ineligible after review": User task "Record manual
          ineligibility with reasons"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Manual review outcome")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Manual review outcome"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility result")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility result"
  Service task "Update application record with eligibility outcome"
  End event "Eligibility assessed — ready for Score and Price Risk"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Assessment lane with retrieval of the
  application record, proceeds to submission to the Decision Engine, and
  pauses at the intermediate message catch event awaiting the eligibility
  result. The exclusive gateway "Eligibility result?" splits into three
  branches: the eligible branch leads to recording confirmation; the
  ineligible branch leads to recording reasons; the refer-for-manual-review
  branch leads to a manual review task followed by a nested exclusive
  gateway "Manual review outcome?" splitting into eligible-after-review and
  ineligible-after-review branches, both rejoining at exclusive merge gateway
  "Manual review outcome", which then continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Eligibility result". All branches from "Eligibility result?" rejoin at
  exclusive merge gateway "Eligibility result", after which the application
  record is updated and the end event is reached.

Message flows:
  Assessment lane "Submit application to Decision Engine for eligibility
    check" → Decision Engine (application data and criteria request).
  Decision Engine → Assessment lane intermediate message catch event
    "Eligibility result received from Decision Engine" (eligibility result
    and rule outputs).
  Assessment lane "Retrieve application record and product rules" →
    Application / Origination Platform (application record and rules
    request).
  Application / Origination Platform → Assessment lane "Retrieve
    application record and product rules" (application record and product
    eligibility rules).
  Assessment lane "Update application record with eligibility outcome" →
    Application / Origination Platform (eligibility outcome and reasons).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Application Record" — read by "Retrieve application record
  and product rules"; written by "Update application record with eligibility
  outcome".
Data Object "Eligibility Result" — written by "Conduct manual eligibility
  review against criteria"; read by "Record manual eligibility approval"
  and "Record manual ineligibility with reasons".
Data Object "Eligibility Outcome Record" — written by "Review eligibility
  confirmation and record outcome" and "Review ineligibility flags and
  record reasons"; read by "Update application record with eligibility
  outcome".

This subprocess takes the verified application from Verify Identity and
evaluates it against product rules and eligibility criteria, using the
Decision Engine for automated assessment and a manual review path for
borderline cases. It produces a definitive eligibility outcome — eligible,
ineligible, or eligible with notes — recorded on the application record and
handed to Score and Price Risk for the next stage of analysis.
```


### V21.06 — Score & Price Risk

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.06 Score & Price Risk — subprocess in the Application to
Decision value chain, receiving a verified and eligibility-assessed application
and producing a risk score and indicative price for referral or decision.

1. Pools & Lanes

pricing work, with lanes for Assessment and Risk.
Pool "Decision Engine" — the scoring and pricing system that runs
scorecards and returns risk scores and premium or rate outputs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation": white-box, single instance.
Pool "Decision Engine": black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation (white-box, two lanes)
2. Decision Engine (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane (underwriter):
  Message start event "Eligibility-assessed application received from
    Assess Eligibility"
  User task "Review eligibility outcome and prepare scoring inputs"
  Service task "Submit application data to Decision Engine for scoring"
  Intermediate message catch event "Risk score and pricing output
    received"
  User task "Review scorecard output and automated risk grade"
  Exclusive gateway "Score within automated acceptance band?"
    - branch "Yes — within band": User task "Confirm risk grade and
        indicative price"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Score band resolved")
    - branch "No — outside band": User task "Flag for manual risk
        review and refer to Risk"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Score band resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Score band resolved"
  User task "Record scoring result and pricing recommendation"
  End event "Risk scored and priced — ready for Refer to Delegated
    Authority"

Risk lane (credit analyst):
  User task "Conduct manual risk assessment and adjust risk grade"
  User task "Validate pricing against product risk appetite"

Note on flow: the "Flag for manual risk review and refer to Risk"
task in the Assessment lane hands control to the Risk lane tasks
above, which complete in order before returning to the exclusive
merge gateway "Score band resolved" in the Assessment lane.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Assessment lane with the message
start event, proceeds through input preparation and submission to the
Decision Engine, then pauses at the intermediate message catch event
until the scoring output arrives. The exclusive gateway "Score within
automated acceptance band?" splits into two branches: the "Yes" branch
returns directly to the merge gateway; the "No" branch routes first to
the Risk lane for manual review and pricing validation before rejoining
the merge gateway "Score band resolved". From the merge, flow returns
to the Assessment lane to record the outcome and reach the end event.

Message flows:
Decision Engine → Assessment lane, "Submit application data to Decision
  Engine for scoring" (application scoring request sent to engine)
Decision Engine → Assessment lane, intermediate message catch event
  "Risk score and pricing output received" (scorecard results,
  risk grade, and indicative rate or premium)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Scoring Input Pack" — written by "Review eligibility
  outcome and prepare scoring inputs"; read by "Submit application data
  to Decision Engine for scoring".
Data Object "Risk Score and Pricing Output" — written by intermediate
  message catch event "Risk score and pricing output received"; read by
  "Review scorecard output and automated risk grade" and "Conduct
  manual risk assessment and adjust risk grade".
Data Object "Pricing Recommendation" — written by "Confirm risk grade
  and indicative price" or "Validate pricing against product risk
  appetite"; read by "Record scoring result and pricing
  recommendation".

Score & Price Risk takes the eligibility-confirmed application, submits
it to the Decision Engine scorecard, and evaluates the returned risk
grade and indicative price. Applications falling inside the automated
acceptance band are confirmed directly by the underwriter; those
outside are escalated to the credit analyst for manual review and
appetite validation. The subprocess hands a risk grade and agreed
pricing recommendation to Refer to Delegated Authority.
```

### V21.07 — Refer to Delegated Authority

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority — subprocess within the

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the body receiving, assessing and deciding
  on applications; contains Assessment lane only.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system used to log, route and track
  referral records and approver responses.

Top to bottom:
1. Assessing Organisation (white-box)
2. Case Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Assessment lane:
  Message start event "Scored and priced application received from
    Score & Price Risk"
  User task "Confirm referral required against authority limits"
  Service task "Log referral in Case Management System"
  Exclusive gateway "Referral type?"
  - branch "standard referral": User task "Prepare referral pack"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Referral type resolved")
  - branch "complex or high-value referral": User task "Prepare extended
    referral pack with additional risk commentary"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Referral type resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Referral type resolved"
  Service task "Submit referral to delegated approver via Case Management
    System"

  Exclusive gateway "Approver decision received?"
  - branch "response received within deadline":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Response timing resolved")
  - branch "no response within deadline": User task "Escalate overdue
    referral to senior delegated approver"
    Intermediate message catch event "Senior approver response received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Response timing resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Response timing resolved"
  User task "Record approver decision and rationale in Case Management

  - branch "approved within delegated authority": User task "Confirm

    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approver outcome resolved")
  - branch "approved with conditions": User task "Document conditions
    imposed by approver and update application record"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approver outcome resolved")
  - branch "declined by approver": User task "Record decline rationale
    and update application record"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approver outcome resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approver outcome resolved"
  End event "Referral outcome recorded — ready for Decide Outcome"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on expanded subprocess — mounted on
  "Submit referral to delegated approver via Case Management System";

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Assessment lane, starting at

  rejoin at "Referral type resolved", then through submission and the
  intermediate message catch event to the "Approver decision received?"
  gateway whose branches — timely response and overdue escalation path
  (with its own intermediate message catch event) — rejoin at "Response
  timing resolved", then through the record task to the "Approver outcome?"
  gateway whose three branches — approved, approved with conditions,

  decision and rationale in Case Management System"; read by "Confirm
  approval and update application record", "Document conditions imposed
  by approver and update application record", and "Record decline
  rationale and update application record".

V21.07 Refer to Delegated Authority takes a fully scored and priced
application that exceeds the assessor's own authority limits and routes it
to the appropriate delegated approver, managing both standard and complex
escalation paths, enforcing a response deadline with senior-approver
escalation, and capturing the approver's reasoned decision — approved,
conditionally approved, or declined — in the Case Management System. The
recorded outcome and its rationale are then handed to Decide Outcome, where
the formal decision on the application is made.
```

```text
  Exclusive gateway "Draft outcome type?"
  - branch "Approve": User task "Prepare approval with any conditions"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Outcome prepared")
  - branch "Approve with conditions": User task "Document conditions and
    obligations"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Outcome prepared")
  - branch "Decline": User task "Document reasons for decline including
    adverse-action grounds"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Outcome prepared")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Outcome prepared"
  Service task "Submit outcome to Application / Origination Platform"

Compliance lane (compliance officer):
  User task "Review outcome for policy and regulatory compliance"
  Exclusive gateway "Compliance check passed?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Compliance
    resolved")
  - branch "No — issues found": User task "Return outcome to Assessment
    with compliance notes"
    End event "Outcome returned for rework — Assessment lane resumes at
    formulate draft outcome"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Compliance resolved"
  User task "Sign off outcome record"
  End event "Outcome decided and recorded — ready for Notify Applicant
    with Reasons"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Assessment lane with the message start
event, passes through the delegated authority check gateway and its merge,
then into formulating the draft outcome. The draft outcome gateway splits
into three branches — approve, approve with conditions, or decline — each
rejoining at the "Outcome prepared" merge gateway before the service task
submits to the platform. Control then passes to the Compliance lane, where
the compliance check gateway splits into a passing branch that continues to
the merge and a failing branch that ends with the outcome returned for
rework. The passing branch rejoins at the "Compliance resolved" merge,
proceeds to sign-off, and reaches the end event.

Message flows:
Application / Origination Platform → Assessment lane "Review scoring
  outcome" task (scoring outcome, delegated authority decision, and
  application record retrieved for review).
Assessment lane "Submit outcome to Application / Origination Platform"
  task → Application / Origination Platform (decision record — outcome
  type, reasons, and any conditions written to system).
Compliance lane "Sign off outcome record" task → Application /
  Origination Platform (compliance sign-off confirmation recorded).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Decision Package" — read by User task "Review scoring
  outcome and delegated authority decision".
Data Object "Draft Outcome Record" — written by User task "Formulate
  draft outcome and conditions"; read by User task "Review outcome for
  policy and regulatory compliance".
Data Object "Conditions and Obligations" — written by User task
  "Document conditions and obligations"; read by User task "Review
  outcome for policy and regulatory compliance".
Data Object "Adverse-Action Reasons" — written by User task "Document
  reasons for decline including adverse-action grounds"; read by User
  task "Review outcome for policy and regulatory compliance".
Data Object "Signed-Off Outcome Record" — written by User task "Sign
  off outcome record"; read by Service task "Submit outcome to
  Application / Origination Platform".

This subprocess takes the scored and authority-cleared decision package
and converts it into a formal, compliance-verified outcome — approved,
conditionally approved, or declined — recorded in the Application /
Origination Platform with full reasons and any conditions attached. The
signed-off outcome record is the authoritative input handed to Notify
Applicant with Reasons, which uses it to generate the decision
communication and present appeal rights to the applicant.
```


### V21.09 — Notify Applicant with Reasons

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons — the subprocess that
communicates the final decision, reasons, and any conditions or appeal
rights to the applicant, completing the outward-facing part of the
Application to Decision value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the body running the application process,
  with lanes for Intake and no other internal team in this subprocess.
Pool "Applicant" — the individual or entity that submitted the application.
Pool "Correspondence System" — generates and dispatches formal decision
  letters and electronic notifications.
Pool "Customer Portal" — the self-service channel through which the
  applicant views status updates and decision notices.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Correspondence System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Customer Portal" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Assessing Organisation
3. Correspondence System
4. Customer Portal

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Intake lane:
  Message start event "Decision outcome received from Decide Outcome"
  User task "Review decision package and prepare notification"
  Exclusive gateway "Decision type?"
  - branch "Approved": User task "Draft approval notice with conditions
    and next steps"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision type")
  - branch "Approved with conditions": User task "Draft conditional
    approval notice detailing conditions and compliance requirements"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision type")
  - branch "Declined": User task "Draft decline notice with reasons and
    adverse-action statement"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision type")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision type"
  User task "Include appeal rights and timeframes in notification"
  Service task "Generate formal correspondence via Correspondence System"
  Service task "Publish decision notice to Customer Portal"
  Intermediate message catch event "Applicant acknowledgement received"
  Exclusive gateway "Acknowledgement received within deadline?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement
    check")
  - branch "No": Send task "Send follow-up reminder to applicant"
    Intermediate timer catch event "Reminder period elapsed"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement check")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Acknowledgement check"
  User task "Record notification outcome in application record"
  End event "Applicant notified — notification complete, appeal window open"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Review decision package
and prepare notification" — label "Notification deadline exceeded" —
triggers Send task "Escalate notification delay to supervisor"; leads to
End event "Notification delay escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work proceeds top to bottom through the Intake lane;
after the start event the intake officer prepares the notification, then
the Decision type gateway splits into three branches — approved, approved
with conditions, and declined — each producing the appropriate draft
notice before rejoining at the Decision type merge gateway; the flow
continues to append appeal rights, generate correspondence, publish to
the portal, wait for acknowledgement, then branches at the
Acknowledgement check gateway between a direct path and a reminder path
before rejoining at the Acknowledgement check merge gateway; the flow
ends after recording the notification outcome.

Message flows:
  Assessing Organisation (Service task "Generate formal correspondence
    via Correspondence System") → Correspondence System (decision letter
    and adverse-action statement)
  Correspondence System → Applicant (formal decision notice with reasons,
    conditions, and appeal rights)
  Assessing Organisation (Service task "Publish decision notice to
    Customer Portal") → Customer Portal (decision notice and status
    update)
  Customer Portal → Applicant (portal notification of decision)
  Applicant → Assessing Organisation (Intermediate message catch event
    "Applicant acknowledgement received") (acknowledgement of receipt)
  Assessing Organisation (Send task "Send follow-up reminder to
    applicant") → Applicant (reminder to acknowledge decision notice)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Decision Package" — read by User task "Review decision
  package and prepare notification"; written by the preceding Decide
  Outcome subprocess.
Data Object "Approval Notice" — written by User task "Draft approval
  notice with conditions and next steps"; read by Service task "Generate
  formal correspondence via Correspondence System".
Data Object "Conditional Approval Notice" — written by User task "Draft
  conditional approval notice detailing conditions and compliance
  requirements"; read by Service task "Generate formal correspondence
  via Correspondence System".
Data Object "Decline Notice with Adverse-Action Statement" — written by
  User task "Draft decline notice with reasons and adverse-action
  statement"; read by Service task "Generate formal correspondence via
  Correspondence System".
Data Object "Notification Record" — written by User task "Record
  notification outcome in application record".

V21.09 Notify Applicant with Reasons takes the decided outcome from
V21.08 and ensures the applicant receives a clear, compliant communication
covering the decision, the reasons behind it, any conditions attached, and
their right of appeal. It waits for acknowledgement and follows up if
none arrives. On completion it hands an open appeal window to V21.10
Handle Appeal or Review, which activates only if the applicant chooses
to contest the outcome.
```


### V21.10 — Handle Appeal or Review

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V21.10 Handle Appeal or Review — final subprocess of the
Application to Decision value chain, handling disputed decisions through
a structured appeals and quality review process.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — the organisation processing the appeal,
  with Appeals and Quality Assurance lanes.
Pool "Applicant" — the external party lodging the appeal or review
  request.
Pool "Case Management System" — IT system supporting appeal case
  tracking, referrals, and outcomes.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Assessing Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Applicant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Case Management System" — black-box, System = true, single
  instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Applicant
2. Assessing Organisation
3. Case Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Assessing Organisation)

Appeals lane:
  Message start event "Appeal or review request received from Applicant"
  User task "Register appeal and assign reference"
  Service task "Open appeal case in Case Management System"
  User task "Acknowledge receipt and advise appeal rights to applicant"
  Send task "Send acknowledgement to Applicant"
  Intermediate message catch event "Supporting grounds and documents
    received from Applicant"
  User task "Review original decision and all case evidence"
  User task "Conduct appeal hearing or file-based review"
  Exclusive gateway "Additional information required?"
    - branch "Yes": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Information
      Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order:
        Send task "Request additional information from Applicant",
        Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received
          from Applicant",
        User task "Assess sufficiency of information received"
      (exits subprocess — continues to exclusive merge gateway
      "Additional information required?")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Additional
      information required?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Additional information required?"
  User task "Prepare appeal determination"
  Exclusive gateway "Fraud or compliance concern identified?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Escalate to Compliance for review"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fraud or compliance concern
      identified?")
    - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fraud or
      compliance concern identified?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Fraud or compliance concern identified?"
  Exclusive gateway "Appeal outcome decision"
    - branch "Upheld — original decision overturned": User task
      "Record upheld determination and update application record"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Appeal outcome decision")
    - branch "Partially upheld — conditions varied": User task
      "Record partial determination and amend conditions"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Appeal outcome decision")
    - branch "Dismissed — original decision confirmed": User task
      "Record dismissed determination"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Appeal outcome decision")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Appeal outcome decision"
  Service task "Update appeal case outcome in Case Management System"
  Send task "Send appeal determination and reasons to Applicant"

Quality Assurance lane:
  User task "Sample appeal file for quality review"
  User task "Record quality assurance findings"
  Service task "Log QA outcome in Case Management System"
  End event "Appeal determined and quality findings recorded — process
    complete"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Information Complete" — label "Information deadline elapsed" —
  on trigger, flow exits the subprocess and continues to an End event
  "Appeal closed — insufficient information provided".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Appeals lane with the message start
  event, proceeds through registration, acknowledgement, evidence
  receipt, review, and the "Additional information required?" gateway
  loop subprocess, then through the compliance escalation gateway to the
  three-branch appeal outcome gateway, merging before the case update
  and notification send task; flow then crosses to the Quality Assurance
  lane for sampling, findings, and the end event. The timer boundary
  event on the loop subprocess exits to a terminal end event in the
  Appeals lane without rejoining the main flow.

Message flows:
  Applicant → Appeals lane "Register appeal and assign reference"
    (appeal or review request with grounds and supporting documents)
  Appeals lane "Send acknowledgement to Applicant" → Applicant
    (acknowledgement letter with appeal reference and rights)
  Appeals lane "Request additional information from Applicant" →
    Applicant (request for further grounds or documents)
  Applicant → Appeals lane Intermediate message catch event "Additional
    information received from Applicant" (additional information and
    documents)
  Appeals lane "Send appeal determination and reasons to Applicant" →
    Applicant (determination letter with outcome and reasons)
  Appeals lane "Open appeal case in Case Management System" → Case
    Management System (new appeal case record)
  Case Management System → Appeals lane "Conduct appeal hearing or
    file-based review" (original case file and decision rationale)
  Appeals lane "Update appeal case outcome in Case Management System" →
    Case Management System (appeal determination and outcome record)
  Quality Assurance lane "Log QA outcome in Case Management System" →
    Case Management System (quality assurance findings and rating)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Appeal Request" — written by User task "Register appeal
  and assign reference"; read by User task "Review original decision
  and all case evidence".
Data Object "Appeal Case Record" — written by Service task "Open appeal
  case in Case Management System"; read by User task "Prepare appeal
  determination".
Data Object "Supporting Grounds and Documents" — written by
  Intermediate message catch event "Supporting grounds and documents
  received from Applicant"; read by User task "Review original decision
  and all case evidence".
Data Object "Appeal Determination" — written by User task "Prepare
  appeal determination"; read by Send task "Send appeal determination
  and reasons to Applicant".
Data Object "QA Findings Report" — written by User task "Record quality
  assurance findings"; read by Service task "Log QA outcome in Case
  Management System".

Handle Appeal or Review receives a formal dispute from the Applicant
against the outcome notified in Notify Applicant with Reasons. The
Appeals team registers the appeal, gathers grounds and evidence, and
conducts a structured review with a compliance escalation path where
needed. It issues a binding determination — uphold, partially uphold,
or dismiss — with written reasons to the Applicant, updates the Case
Management System, and submits the file to Quality Assurance for
sampling. This is the final subprocess in the Application to Decision
value chain; its end event closes the case.
```


## V22 — Claim to Settlement

**Teams and roles involved.**
Claim to Settlement usually involves Claims Intake, Claims Assessment, Investigation, Fraud, Supply Chain or Repair Networks, Finance/Payments, Recoveries, Complaints, and Actuarial or Reserving. Key roles include claims consultant, assessor, loss adjuster, investigator, fraud analyst, repairer or supplier coordinator, payments officer, recoveries officer, complaints officer, and reserving analyst.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Claimant — a policyholder, member, patient or beneficiary. The process is initiated when a loss or event is notified. Other external parties include loss adjusters and assessors, repairers and suppliers, medical or expert providers, third parties and their insurers, reinsurers, legal representatives, and ombudsman or dispute-resolution schemes.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: receive notification of the claim, register it and set an initial reserve, validate cover and eligibility, triage and assign, assess the loss and quantum, investigate where indicators warrant it, approve or decline the claim, arrange repair, service or payment, pursue recoveries and reinsurance, and close the claim with reserve release.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include the claims management platform, policy administration, customer and claims portals, fraud detection and analytics, supplier and repairer networks, payments and disbursement systems, document and image management, reserving and actuarial systems, complaints management, and reinsurance and recoveries systems.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include policy wordings and cover terms, claims handling standards and service timeframes, reserving policy, delegated authority for settlement amounts, fraud referral criteria, supplier panel and pricing agreements, recoveries and subrogation procedure, complaints and external dispute-resolution obligations, and regulatory claims-handling conduct requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The claimant provides notification, incident details, supporting evidence and quotes, bank details and declarations, and receives acknowledgement, cover decisions, assessment outcomes, settlement or repair arrangements, payment advice and complaint rights. Suppliers and experts provide assessments, quotes, reports and invoices; reinsurers and third-party insurers exchange recovery claims and settlements.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates claim records, reserves, cover decisions, assessments and quantum, supplier work orders, payments, recovery and reinsurance claims, and complaint records. IT systems provide policy and cover data, claims history, fraud scores and rules outcomes, supplier pricing and availability, payment status, and claims ratio, leakage and cycle-time reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Insurer" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V22.01** Receive Notification | Claimant | Claims Intake (claims consultant) | Claims Management Platform, Customer Portal |
| **V22.02** Register Claim & Set Reserve | — | Claims Intake (claims consultant), Actuarial (reserving analyst) | Claims Management Platform, Reserving System |
| **V22.03** Validate Cover & Eligibility | Claimant | Claims Assessment (claims consultant) | Policy Administration System |
| **V22.04** Triage & Assign | — | Claims Assessment (claims consultant) | Claims Management Platform |
| **V22.05** Assess Loss & Quantum | Loss Adjuster, Expert Provider | Claims Assessment (assessor) | Claims Management Platform, Document & Image Management |
| **V22.06** Investigate Where Warranted | Third Party | Investigation (investigator), Fraud (fraud analyst) | Fraud Detection Platform |
| **V22.07** Approve or Decline | — | Claims Assessment (assessor), Claims Management (delegated approver) | Claims Management Platform |
| **V22.08** Arrange Repair, Service or Payment | Claimant, Repairer | Supply Chain (repairer coordinator), Finance (payments officer) | Supplier Network System, Payments System |
| **V22.09** Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance | Third-Party Insurer, Reinsurer | Recoveries (recoveries officer) | Recoveries & Reinsurance System |
| **V22.10** Close Claim & Release Reserve | — | Claims Assessment (claims consultant), Actuarial (reserving analyst) | Claims Management Platform, Reserving System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V22):

- **External actors:** Claimant (V22.01, V22.03, V22.08); Loss Adjuster (V22.05); Expert Provider (V22.05); Third Party (V22.06); Repairer (V22.08); Third-Party Insurer (V22.09); Reinsurer (V22.09).
- **Teams:** Claims Intake (V22.01, V22.02); Actuarial (V22.02, V22.10); Claims Assessment (V22.03–V22.05, V22.07, V22.10); Investigation (V22.06); Fraud (V22.06); Claims Management (V22.07); Supply Chain (V22.08); Finance (V22.08); Recoveries (V22.09).
- **IT systems:** Claims Management Platform (V22.01, V22.02, V22.04, V22.05, V22.07, V22.10); Customer Portal (V22.01); Reserving System (V22.02, V22.10); Policy Administration System (V22.03); Document & Image Management (V22.05); Fraud Detection Platform (V22.06); Supplier Network System (V22.08); Payments System (V22.08); Recoveries & Reinsurance System (V22.09).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V22 — Claim to Settlement — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Claim to Settlement value chain. It is organised in three
horizontal bands read top-to-bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top) represent
what the chain delivers to external participants; BUSINESS PROCESSES
(middle) show the ten subprocesses that realise those services; and
APPLICATIONS (bottom) show the IT systems that support execution. The
Claimant sits on the far left as the primary demand-side actor; delivery
and settlement actors — Repairer, Loss Adjuster, Expert Provider, Third
Party, Third-Party Insurer, and Reinsurer — sit on the far right. The
view is read top-to-bottom as service realisation per ArchiMate
conventions.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Claimant: demand-side actor, far left; initiates notification, receives
  decisions, settlement and payment advice.
- Loss Adjuster: delivery-side actor, far right; engaged during loss
  assessment.
- Expert Provider: delivery-side actor, far right; supplies assessments,
  reports and quotes during loss assessment.
- Third Party: delivery-side actor, far right; involved during
  investigation where warranted.
- Repairer: delivery-side actor, far right; engaged during repair, service
  or payment arrangement.
- Third-Party Insurer: delivery-side actor, far right; counterpart in
  recoveries pursuit.
- Reinsurer: delivery-side actor, far right; counterpart in reinsurance
  recoveries pursuit.

2. Interfaces

- Claims Intake Interface: accessed by Claimant; serves the Claim
  Notification Reception Service and the Claim Registration Service.
- Customer Portal Interface: accessed by Claimant; serves the Claim
  Notification Reception Service and the Settlement & Payment Advice
  Service.
- Cover Validation Interface: accessed by Claimant; serves the Cover and
  Eligibility Validation Service.
- Supplier & Repairer Interface: accessed by Repairer; serves the Repair,
  Service and Payment Arrangement Service.
- Recoveries & Reinsurance Interface: accessed by Third-Party Insurer and
  Reinsurer; serves the Recoveries and Reinsurance Pursuit Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Claim Notification Reception Service: receives loss or event
  notification from the Claimant and issues acknowledgement.
- Claim Registration Service: registers the claim record and sets an
  initial reserve.
- Cover and Eligibility Validation Service: confirms or declines cover
  based on policy terms and eligibility criteria.
- Triage and Assignment Service: prioritises the claim and routes it to
  the appropriate team or handler.
- Loss Assessment and Quantum Service: assesses the nature, extent and
  quantum of the loss, engaging external experts where needed.
- Investigation Service: investigates the claim where fraud or
  irregularity indicators are present.
- Claim Decision Service: issues an approval or decline decision within
  delegated authority.
- Repair, Service and Payment Arrangement Service: arranges repair,
  alternative service or direct payment settlement to the Claimant.
- Recoveries and Reinsurance Pursuit Service: pursues subrogation,
  third-party recoveries and reinsurance recoveries.
- Claim Closure and Reserve Release Service: closes the claim file and
  releases or adjusts the outstanding reserve.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V22.01 Receive Notification: captures loss or event details notified by
  the Claimant across intake and portal channels.
- V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve: creates the claim record and
  establishes an initial case reserve.
- V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility: checks policy terms, conditions
  and member eligibility to confirm or deny cover.
- V22.04 Triage & Assign: assesses complexity and urgency, then assigns
  the claim to the appropriate handler or team.
- V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum: gathers evidence, obtains expert reports
  and quotes, and determines the loss quantum.
- V22.06 Investigate Where Warranted: conducts investigation and fraud
  analysis where referral criteria are met.
- V22.07 Approve or Decline: applies delegated authority to reach and
  communicate a claim decision.
- V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment: coordinates repairers or
  suppliers and executes settlement payment.
- V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance: lodges and manages recovery
  claims against third-party insurers and reinsurers.
- V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve: finalises the claim file, updates
  reporting, and releases the case reserve.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Claims Management Platform: central system for claim records, workflow,
  decisions and reporting.
- Customer Portal: self-service channel for claimant notification,
  tracking and communication.
- Policy Administration System: source of policy, cover and eligibility
  data.
- Reserving System: manages initial and revised reserve amounts and
  actuarial data.
- Document & Image Management: stores and retrieves claim documents,
  photos, reports and evidence.
- Fraud Detection Platform: applies fraud rules, scores and analytics to
  claim data.
- Supplier Network System: manages supplier and repairer panels, work
  orders and pricing.
- Payments System: executes and tracks settlement disbursements and
  payment advice.
- Recoveries & Reinsurance System: manages recovery claims, reinsurance
  bordereaux and settlement tracking.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.01 Receive Notification.
- Customer Portal SERVES V22.01 Receive Notification.
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve.
- Reserving System SERVES V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve.
- Policy Administration System SERVES V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility.
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.04 Triage & Assign.
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum.
- Document & Image Management SERVES V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum.
- Fraud Detection Platform SERVES V22.06 Investigate Where Warranted.
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.07 Approve or Decline.
- Supplier Network System SERVES V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or
  Payment.
- Payments System SERVES V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment.
- Recoveries & Reinsurance System SERVES
  V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance.
- Claims Management Platform SERVES V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve.
- Reserving System SERVES V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve.

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V22.01 Receive Notification REALISES Claim Notification Reception
  Service.
- V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve REALISES Claim Registration
  Service.
- V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility REALISES Cover and Eligibility
  Validation Service.
- V22.04 Triage & Assign REALISES Triage and Assignment Service.
- V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum REALISES Loss Assessment and Quantum
  Service.
- V22.06 Investigate Where Warranted REALISES Investigation Service.
- V22.07 Approve or Decline REALISES Claim Decision Service.
- V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment REALISES Repair, Service and
  Payment Arrangement Service.
- V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance REALISES Recoveries and
  Reinsurance Pursuit Service.
- V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve REALISES Claim Closure and Reserve
  Release Service.

SERVING (business service serves business actor):
- Claim Notification Reception Service SERVES Claimant.
- Cover and Eligibility Validation Service SERVES Claimant.
- Repair, Service and Payment Arrangement Service SERVES Claimant.
- Repair, Service and Payment Arrangement Service SERVES Repairer.
- Loss Assessment and Quantum Service SERVES Loss Adjuster.
- Loss Assessment and Quantum Service SERVES Expert Provider.
- Investigation Service SERVES Third Party.
- Recoveries and Reinsurance Pursuit Service SERVES Third-Party Insurer.
- Recoveries and Reinsurance Pursuit Service SERVES Reinsurer.

ASSIGNMENT (interface assigned to actor):
- Claims Intake Interface ASSIGNED TO Claimant.
- Customer Portal Interface ASSIGNED TO Claimant.
- Cover Validation Interface ASSIGNED TO Claimant.
- Supplier & Repairer Interface ASSIGNED TO Repairer.
- Recoveries & Reinsurance Interface ASSIGNED TO Third-Party Insurer.
- Recoveries & Reinsurance Interface ASSIGNED TO Reinsurer.

ACCESS (business process accesses application component):
- V22.01 Receive Notification ACCESSES Claims Management Platform
  (write: creates claim record).
- V22.01 Receive Notification ACCESSES Customer Portal (read: receives
  claimant notification).
- V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve ACCESSES Claims Management Platform
  (write: registers claim and initial reserve).
- V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve ACCESSES Reserving System
  (write: sets initial reserve).
- V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility ACCESSES Policy Administration
  System (read: retrieves policy and cover data).
- V22.04 Triage & Assign ACCESSES Claims Management Platform (write:
  records triage outcome and assignment).
- V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum ACCESSES Claims Management Platform
  (write: records assessment and quantum).
- V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum ACCESSES Document & Image Management
  (write: stores evidence, reports and photos).
- V22.06 Investigate Where Warranted ACCESSES Fraud Detection Platform
  (read/write: submits claim data, retrieves fraud scores and rules
  outcomes).
- V22.07 Approve or Decline ACCESSES Claims Management Platform (write:
  records claim decision).
- V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment ACCESSES Supplier Network
  System (write: raises work orders and supplier instructions).
- V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment ACCESSES Payments System
  (write: initiates settlement disbursement).
- V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance ACCESSES Recoveries &
  Reinsurance System (write: lodges and tracks recovery and reinsurance
  claims).
- V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve ACCESSES Claims Management
  Platform (write: closes claim file and updates reporting).
- V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve ACCESSES Reserving System (write:
  releases or adjusts reserve).
```

```text
The boundary contains all ten subprocesses of the Claim to Settlement
value chain, from first notification through to reserve release. It
serves the Claimant as the primary external recipient of cover
decisions, repair arrangements and settlement payments, and interacts
with Loss Adjusters, Expert Providers, Repairers, Third Parties,
Third-Party Insurers and Reinsurers at the stages where their
involvement is required.
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V22 - Claim to Settlement

Lay out a single left-to-right sequence of ten high-level process stages,
each represented as a chevron pointing right. Place the chevrons in the
order listed below, one chevron per stage, with no branches or return
paths. Use the stage names exactly as given.

V22.01. Receive Notification
V22.02. Register Claim & Set Reserve
V22.03. Validate Cover & Eligibility
V22.04. Triage & Assign
V22.05. Assess Loss & Quantum
V22.06. Investigate Where Warranted
V22.07. Approve or Decline
V22.08. Arrange Repair, Service or Payment
V22.09. Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance
V22.10. Close Claim & Release Reserve

This chain governs the end-to-end handling of an insurance claim from
first notice of loss through to final settlement and reserve release.
The primary external participant is the Claimant — a policyholder,
member, patient or beneficiary — whose notification of a loss or event
triggers the chain. The chain concludes when the claim is closed, the
reserve is released, and all recovery and reinsurance positions have
been pursued and reconciled.
```
