### V22.01 — Receive Notification

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.01 Receive Notification — first subprocess in the Claim to
Settlement value chain, capturing the moment a loss or event is notified
and producing an acknowledged, recorded notification ready for
registration.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the insurance organisation receiving and processing the
notification, with three lanes top to bottom: Claims Intake (claims
consultant), and a single internal flow area.
- Lane "Claims Intake (Claims Consultant)" — receives the notification,
  captures incident details, acknowledges receipt, performs an initial
  completeness check, and routes the notification onward.
Pool "Claimant" — policyholder, member, patient or beneficiary who
initiates the notification.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — core claims IT system that stores the
new notification record.
Pool "Customer Portal" — digital self-service channel through which the
claimant may submit a notification.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claimant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true,
single instance.
Pool "Customer Portal" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Claimant
2. Insurer
3. Customer Portal
4. Claims Management Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) lane:
Message start event "Loss or event notification received from Claimant"
Exclusive gateway "Notification channel?"
- branch "Portal submission": Intermediate message catch event "Portal
  notification retrieved from Customer Portal"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Notification channel")
- branch "Direct contact (phone, email, post)": User task "Capture
  notification details from claimant"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Notification channel")
Exclusive merge gateway "Notification channel"
Service task "Log notification in Claims Management Platform"
Send task "Send acknowledgement to claimant"
User task "Check notification for completeness"
Exclusive gateway "Notification complete?"
- branch "Yes — all required details present":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Notification complete")
- branch "No — details missing": Send task "Request missing information
  from claimant"
  Intermediate message catch event "Missing information received from
  Claimant"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Notification complete")
Exclusive merge gateway "Notification complete"
End event "Notification complete — ready for Register Claim & Set Reserve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Check notification for
completeness" — label "Maximum wait for missing information (service
timeframe exceeded)" — triggers a Send task "Issue holding
correspondence and escalate" then an End event "Notification timed out —
escalated to supervisor".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins at the Message start event in the Claims
Intake lane, passes through the channel gateway whose two branches
rejoin at the "Notification channel" merge gateway, then continues
through logging, acknowledgement, and the completeness check gateway,
whose two branches (complete and missing-information loop) rejoin at
the "Notification complete" merge gateway, ending at the final End
event.

Message flows:
Claimant → Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) (loss or event
notification by phone, email or post)
Claimant → Customer Portal (online notification submission)
Customer Portal → Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant)
(retrieved portal notification)
Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claims Management Platform
(new notification record logged)
Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claimant (acknowledgement
of notification receipt)
Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) → Claimant (request for
missing information)
Claimant → Insurer / Claims Intake (Claims Consultant) (missing
information supplied)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Notification Record" — written by "Log notification in
Claims Management Platform"; read by "Check notification for
completeness".
Data Object "Incident Details" — written by "Capture notification
details from claimant"; read by "Log notification in Claims Management
Platform".
Data Object "Acknowledgement" — written by "Send acknowledgement to
claimant".
Data Object "Missing Information Request" — written by "Request missing
information from claimant"; read by intermediate catch event "Missing
information received from Claimant".

This subprocess captures the first contact from a claimant reporting a
loss or event, records it through whichever channel it arrives on, and
confirms receipt to the claimant. It validates that the notification
holds enough detail to proceed, chasing any gaps before handing a
complete, logged notification to Register Claim & Set Reserve, where a
formal claim record and initial reserve will be established.
```


### V22.02 — Register Claim & Set Reserve

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.02 Register Claim & Set Reserve — second subprocess in the
Claim to Settlement value chain, converting a received notification into a
registered claim record with an initial reserve set.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the registration and reserving
process, containing two lanes.
  Lane "Claims Intake" — claims consultant who registers the claim.
  Lane "Actuarial / Reserving" — reserving analyst who sets the initial
  reserve.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — system of record for claim creation
and update.
Pool "Reserving System" — system used to calculate and record the initial
reserve.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.
Pool "Reserving System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. Insurer (white-box, spanning Claims Intake above Actuarial / Reserving)
  2. Claims Management Platform
  3. Reserving System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Intake lane:
  Message start event "Validated notification received from Receive
  Notification"
  User task "Review notification details"
  User task "Create claim record"
  Service task "Submit claim record to Claims Management Platform"
  User task "Capture claimant and incident details"
  Service task "Store claimant and incident details in Claims Management
  Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Details sufficient?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Details
      sufficient")
    - branch "No":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Details Complete" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Request missing details from
      claimant", Intermediate message catch event "Claimant response
      received", User task "Update claim record with additional details",
      Service task "Sync updated details to Claims Management Platform"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Details sufficient")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Details sufficient"
  Send task "Send claim acknowledgement to claimant"
  Intermediate message catch event "Claim record confirmed by Claims
  Management Platform"
  User task "Handover claim to Actuarial / Reserving for reserve setting"

Actuarial / Reserving lane:
  User task "Review claim record and loss category"
  Service task "Request reserve calculation from Reserving System"
  Intermediate message catch event "Reserve figure received from
  Reserving System"
  User task "Review and approve initial reserve"
  Exclusive gateway "Reserve adequate?"
    - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reserve
      adequate")
    - branch "No":
      User task "Adjust reserve parameters"
      Service task "Resubmit reserve calculation to Reserving System"
      Intermediate message catch event "Revised reserve figure received
      from Reserving System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reserve adequate")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve adequate"
  Service task "Record confirmed reserve in Claims Management Platform"
  End event "Claim registered and reserve set — ready for Validate Cover
  and Eligibility"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Details Complete" — label "Details overdue (7 days)" — triggers End event
"Claim suspended pending claimant response".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in Claims Intake, passes through notification
review, claim creation, detail capture, and the details-sufficiency gateway
whose "No" branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and whose "Yes" branch
and the loop's exit both rejoin the merge gateway before the acknowledgement
send task. Control then passes to Actuarial / Reserving for reserve review,
the reserve-adequacy gateway whose "No" branch loops through parameter
adjustment and resubmission and whose "Yes" branch and the adjusted path
rejoin the reserve-adequate merge gateway before the final record step and
end event.

Message flows:
  Claims Intake "Submit claim record" → Claims Management Platform (new
  claim record)
  Claims Intake "Store claimant and incident details" → Claims Management
  Platform (incident and claimant data)
  Claims Management Platform → Claims Intake "Claim record confirmed"
  (confirmation and claim reference)
  Actuarial / Reserving "Request reserve calculation" → Reserving System
  (loss category and claim data)
  Reserving System → Actuarial / Reserving "Reserve figure received"
  (initial reserve amount)
  Actuarial / Reserving "Resubmit reserve calculation" → Reserving System
  (adjusted parameters)
  Reserving System → Actuarial / Reserving "Revised reserve figure
  received" (revised reserve amount)
  Actuarial / Reserving "Record confirmed reserve" → Claims Management
  Platform (approved reserve value)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Notification Details" — read by "Review notification details";
written by "Capture claimant and incident details".
Data Object "Claim Record" — written by "Create claim record"; read by
"Review claim record and loss category".
Data Object "Claimant and Incident Details" — written by "Capture claimant
and incident details"; read by "Update claim record with additional details".
Data Object "Reserve Calculation Request" — written by "Request reserve
calculation from Reserving System"; read by "Resubmit reserve calculation to
Reserving System".
Data Object "Initial Reserve Figure" — written by "Review and approve initial
reserve"; read by "Record confirmed reserve in Claims Management Platform".

This subprocess takes the validated notification from Receive Notification
and produces a fully registered claim record in the Claims Management
Platform together with an approved initial reserve in the Reserving System.
With these two artefacts in place, Validate Cover and Eligibility can begin
its assessment against policy terms, knowing the claim exists, is categorised,
and carries a financially sanctioned opening reserve.
```


### V22.03 — Validate Cover & Eligibility

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility — the third subprocess in the
Claim to Settlement value chain, confirming that the registered claim falls
within an active policy before triage and assignment proceed.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the validation process, containing
the Claims Assessment team.
- Lane "Claims Assessment (claims consultant)"
Pool "Claimant" — the policyholder, member, patient or beneficiary who
submitted the claim.
Pool "Policy Administration System" — IT system holding policy and cover data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claimant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Policy Administration System" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Claimant
2. Insurer
3. Policy Administration System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment (claims consultant) lane:
  Message start event "Registered claim received from Register Claim
    & Set Reserve"
  Service task "Retrieve policy record"
  Service task "Check policy status and period of cover"
  Exclusive gateway "Policy active at date of loss?"
  - branch "No — policy lapsed or not incepted":
      Send task "Notify claimant of cover issue"
      Intermediate message catch event "Claimant response received"
      Exclusive gateway "Claimant provides evidence of valid cover?"
      - branch "Yes — evidence provided":
          User task "Review claimant-supplied evidence"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Claimant provides
            evidence of valid cover?")
      - branch "No — insufficient or no response":
          User task "Record ineligibility decision"
          End event "Claim ineligible — cover not confirmed, process
            closed"
      Exclusive merge gateway "Claimant provides evidence of valid
        cover?"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Policy active at date
        of loss?")
  - branch "Yes — policy active":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Policy active at date
        of loss?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Policy active at date of loss?"
  Service task "Verify cover type and peril applies to loss"
  Exclusive gateway "Cover type and peril confirmed?"
  - branch "No — loss outside cover scope":
      User task "Record declination of cover"
      Send task "Notify claimant cover does not apply"
      End event "Claim declined at validation — no cover for
        peril"
  - branch "Yes — loss within cover":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Cover type and peril
        confirmed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Cover type and peril confirmed?"
  Service task "Check policy exclusions and conditions"
  Exclusive gateway "Exclusion or condition breach identified?"
  - branch "Yes — exclusion applies":
      User task "Record exclusion finding"
      Send task "Notify claimant of exclusion"
      End event "Claim declined at validation — exclusion
        applies"
  - branch "No — no exclusion breach":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Exclusion or condition
        breach identified?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Exclusion or condition breach identified?"
  User task "Confirm claimant eligibility and insurable interest"
  Exclusive gateway "Claimant eligible and insurable interest
    confirmed?"
  - branch "No — eligibility not established":
      User task "Record eligibility failure"
      Send task "Notify claimant of eligibility issue"
      End event "Claim declined at validation — claimant not
        eligible"
  - branch "Yes — eligibility confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Claimant eligible and
        insurable interest confirmed?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Claimant eligible and insurable interest
    confirmed?"
  User task "Record cover validation outcome on claim record"
  Send task "Send cover confirmation to claimant"
  End event "Cover and eligibility validated — ready for Triage
    & Assign"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
"Claimant response received" — if no claimant response is received
within the service timeframe, the flow escalates to User task "Record
ineligibility decision", ending at End event "Claim ineligible — cover
not confirmed, process closed".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Claims Assessment lane at the message
start event, proceeds through policy retrieval and status check to the
"Policy active at date of loss?" gateway; the "No" branch sends a
notification, waits for claimant response, and routes through the
evidence gateway either back to the merge or to ineligibility end; the
"Yes" branch and the evidence-confirmed branch both merge before
continuing to cover-type verification; the "No" branch of that gateway
ends in declination; the "Yes" branch continues to exclusion checking,
whose "Yes" branch ends in exclusion declination and whose "No" branch
continues to eligibility confirmation; the "No" branch of eligibility
ends in an eligibility declination; the "Yes" branch merges and
continues to outcome recording and claimant notification before the
validated end event.

Message flows:
Policy Administration System → Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims
  consultant) "Retrieve policy record" (policy record and cover data
  returned in response to retrieval request)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Retrieve policy record"
  → Policy Administration System (policy record query)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Check policy status and
  period of cover" → Policy Administration System (status and period
  enquiry)
Policy Administration System → Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims
  consultant) "Check policy status and period of cover" (policy status,
  inception and expiry dates)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Service task Verify
  cover type and peril applies to loss" → Policy Administration System
  (cover type and peril query)
Policy Administration System → Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims
  consultant) "Verify cover type and peril applies to loss" (cover
  sections and listed perils)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Service task Check
  policy exclusions and conditions" → Policy Administration System
  (exclusions and conditions query)
Policy Administration System → Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims
  consultant) "Check policy exclusions and conditions" (exclusions list
  and special conditions)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Send task Notify
  claimant of cover issue" → Claimant (notification of cover issue and
  request for evidence)
Claimant → Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Intermediate
  message catch event Claimant response received" (claimant-supplied
  evidence of valid cover)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Send task Notify
  claimant cover does not apply" → Claimant (declination notice — peril
  not covered)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Send task Notify
  claimant of exclusion" → Claimant (declination notice — exclusion
  applies)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Send task Notify
  claimant of eligibility issue" → Claimant (declination notice —
  eligibility not established)
Insurer/Claims Assessment (claims consultant) "Send task Send cover
  confirmation to claimant" → Claimant (cover confirmation and
  validation outcome)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Policy Record" — read by "Retrieve policy record", read by
  "Check policy status and period of cover", read by "Verify cover type
  and peril applies to loss", read by "Check policy exclusions and
  conditions".
Data Object "Cover Validation Outcome" — written by "Record cover
  validation outcome on claim record", written by "Record ineligibility
  decision", written by "Record declination of cover", written by
  "Record exclusion finding", written by "Record eligibility failure".
Data Object "Claimant Evidence Submission" — read by "Review
  claimant-supplied evidence".

V22.03 Validate Cover & Eligibility takes the registered claim produced
by V22.02 and systematically confirms that the policy was active at the
date of loss, that the peril and cover type match, that no exclusion
applies, and that the claimant has insurable interest. Claims that fail
any check are declined and the claimant notified; claims that pass all
checks have their validation outcome recorded and a cover confirmation
sent to the claimant, leaving a fully validated claim ready to enter
V22.04 Triage & Assign.
```


### V22.04 — Triage & Assign

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.04 Triage & Assign — fourth subprocess in the Claim to Settlement
value chain, routing a registered and validated claim to the appropriate
handler and workstream.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the triage and assignment process,
with two lanes:
  Lane "Claims Assessment (claims consultant)" — reviews the validated claim,
  determines urgency and complexity, assigns to the correct workstream and
  handler.

Pool "Claims Management Platform" — IT system receiving claim updates and
assignments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Insurer (white-box, single lane)
2. Claims Management Platform (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment (claims consultant) lane:
  Message start event "Validated claim received from Validate Cover &
  Eligibility"
  User task "Review claim details and supporting documentation"
  Exclusive gateway "Claim complexity?"
  - branch "Simple / low-value": User task "Assign to standard claims
    consultant"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Complexity resolved")
  - branch "Complex / high-value": User task "Assign to senior assessor or
    loss adjuster"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Complexity resolved")
  - branch "Potential fraud indicators present": User task "Flag for
    investigation and assign to investigator"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Complexity resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Complexity resolved"
  Exclusive gateway "Urgency level?"
  - branch "Standard": User task "Set standard service priority"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Priority set")
  - branch "Urgent / catastrophe": User task "Set escalated service priority
    and notify team leader"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Priority set")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Priority set"
  Service task "Record triage outcome and assignment in Claims Management
  Platform"
  User task "Confirm assignment and notify handler"
  End event "Claim triaged and assigned — ready for Assess Loss & Quantum"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single lane runs from the message start event through the
claim review task, into the Complexity gateway whose three branches — standard
consultant, senior assessor, fraud flag — rejoin at the "Complexity resolved"
merge gateway; flow continues into the Urgency gateway whose two branches —
standard and escalated — rejoin at the "Priority set" merge gateway; flow then
passes through the service task recording the outcome and the confirmation
task to the end event.

Message flows:
Claims Management Platform → Claims Assessment (claims consultant) lane
  (validated claim record, cover decision, and claim history retrieved at
  subprocess start)
Claims Assessment (claims consultant) lane → Claims Management Platform
  (triage outcome, assigned handler, priority level, and workstream written
  via "Record triage outcome and assignment in Claims Management Platform")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Triage & Assignment Record" — written by "Record triage outcome
and assignment in Claims Management Platform"; read by "Confirm assignment and
notify handler".

This subprocess takes a validated claim and determines its complexity, fraud
risk, and urgency, then routes it to the handler and workstream best placed to
progress it. It records the triage outcome and priority in the Claims
Management Platform and hands a fully assigned claim to the Assess Loss &
Quantum subprocess.
```


### V22.05 — Assess Loss & Quantum

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum — fifth subprocess in the Claim to
Settlement value chain, receiving a triaged and assigned claim from Triage &
Assign and handing a completed loss assessment and quantum to Approve or Decline.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the insurance organisation conducting the loss assessment,
  containing the Claims Assessment lane (assessor).
Pool "Loss Adjuster" — external loss adjuster engaged to inspect or value
  the loss.
Pool "Expert Provider" — external medical, technical or other expert
  supplying specialist assessment or report.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — core claims system recording
  assessment decisions and quantum.
Pool "Document & Image Management" — system storing evidence, reports
  and images attached to the claim.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Loss Adjuster" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Expert Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Document & Image Management" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Loss Adjuster
2. Expert Provider
3. Insurer
4. Claims Management Platform
5. Document & Image Management

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment lane:

Message start event "Assigned claim received from Triage & Assign"

User task "Review claim file and assignment instructions"

Service task "Retrieve claim record and supporting documents"

Exclusive gateway "Assessment type required?"
- branch "Desktop assessment only": User task "Conduct desktop review
  of evidence and documentation"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assessment type required?")
- branch "Field or specialist assessment needed":
  Send task "Instruct Loss Adjuster or Expert Provider"
  Intermediate message catch event "Assessment report received"
  User task "Review external assessment report"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Assessment type required?")

Exclusive merge gateway "Assessment type required?"

User task "Quantify loss and calculate settlement quantum"

Service task "Record assessment findings and quantum in claims system"

Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Assessment Complete" (standard loop)
  containing, in order:
  User task "Check assessment completeness and supporting evidence",
  Exclusive gateway "Additional information required?"
  - branch "Yes — information gap identified":
    Send task "Request additional evidence or information from claimant"
    Intermediate message catch event "Additional evidence received"
    Service task "Upload received evidence to document system"
    (exits subprocess)
  - branch "No — assessment complete":
    (exits subprocess)

Exclusive gateway "Within delegated authority?"
- branch "Yes": User task "Finalise assessment recommendation"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Within delegated authority?")
- branch "No — escalation required": User task "Prepare escalation
  summary for senior approver"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Within delegated authority?")

Exclusive merge gateway "Within delegated authority?"

Service task "Update claim record with final quantum and recommendation"

End event "Loss assessment and quantum confirmed — ready for
  Approve or Decline"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Assessment report received" — label "Report overdue (10 business
  days)" — triggers Send task "Chase Loss Adjuster or Expert Provider
  for outstanding report", then rejoins flow before User task "Review
  external assessment report".

Interrupting timer boundary event on Intermediate message catch event
  "Additional evidence received" — label "Evidence not received
  (5 business days)" — triggers Send task "Issue final evidence
  reminder to claimant", then rejoins flow before Service task
  "Upload received evidence to document system".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Claims Assessment lane,
  from the message start event through document retrieval, into the
  exclusive gateway splitting desktop versus field/specialist paths,
  merging at the assessment type merge gateway, continuing through
  quantum calculation and recording, entering the standard-loop
  subprocess for completeness checking with its internal
  additional-information branch exiting the subprocess, then into the
  delegated authority gateway splitting finalisation from escalation
  preparation, merging at the delegated authority merge gateway, and
  closing with the final claim record update and end event.

Message flows:
  Insurer (Send task "Instruct Loss Adjuster or Expert Provider") →
    Loss Adjuster (instruction to attend and assess)
  Insurer (Send task "Instruct Loss Adjuster or Expert Provider") →
    Expert Provider (instruction to provide specialist assessment)
  Loss Adjuster → Insurer (Intermediate message catch event
    "Assessment report received") (field assessment report)
  Expert Provider → Insurer (Intermediate message catch event
    "Assessment report received") (expert assessment report)
  Insurer (Send task "Request additional evidence or information
    from claimant") — note: claimant communication is handled via
    Customer Portal; treat as outbound message to Claims Management
    Platform routing to claimant.
  Insurer (Service task "Retrieve claim record and supporting
    documents") → Claims Management Platform (query for claim record)
  Claims Management Platform → Insurer (Service task "Retrieve claim
    record and supporting documents") (claim record and history)
  Insurer (Service task "Record assessment findings and quantum in
    claims system") → Claims Management Platform (assessment and
    quantum written to claim record)
  Insurer (Service task "Upload received evidence to document system")
    → Document & Image Management (evidence files stored)
  Insurer (Service task "Update claim record with final quantum and
    recommendation") → Claims Management Platform (final quantum and
    recommendation recorded)
  Document & Image Management → Insurer (Service task "Retrieve claim
    record and supporting documents") (existing evidence and images
    returned)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assessment Instructions" — written by User task "Review
  claim file and assignment instructions"; read by Send task "Instruct
  Loss Adjuster or Expert Provider".
Data Object "External Assessment Report" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Assessment report received"; read by User task
  "Review external assessment report".
Data Object "Loss Quantum Calculation" — written by User task
  "Quantify loss and calculate settlement quantum"; read by Service
  task "Record assessment findings and quantum in claims system".
Data Object "Additional Evidence Package" — written by Service task
  "Upload received evidence to document system"; read by User task
  "Check assessment completeness and supporting evidence".
Data Object "Assessment Recommendation" — written by User task
  "Finalise assessment recommendation"; read by Service task "Update
  claim record with final quantum and recommendation".
Data Object "Escalation Summary" — written by User task "Prepare
  escalation summary for senior approver"; read by Service task
  "Update claim record with final quantum and recommendation".

V22.05 Assess Loss & Quantum is the subprocess in which the insurer
establishes the factual extent of the loss and calculates the settlement
quantum. The Claims Assessment team reviews the file, commissions external
loss adjusters or expert providers where necessary, gathers and validates
all supporting evidence, and quantifies the claim within or above delegated
authority. It hands a fully documented loss assessment and recommended
quantum to V22.07 Approve or Decline, where the settlement decision is made.
```


### V22.06 — Investigate Where Warranted

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.06 Investigate Where Warranted — investigation and fraud analysis
subprocess within the Claim to Settlement value chain, triggered after triage
and assessment and feeding into the approval or decline decision.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation conducting the investigation, containing
Investigation and Fraud lanes.
Pool "Third Party" — external party whose information or conduct is relevant
to the investigation.
Pool "Fraud Detection Platform" — IT system providing fraud scoring, rules
outcomes, and analytics.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Third Party" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Fraud Detection Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Third Party
2. Insurer (white-box; lanes top to bottom: Investigation, Fraud)
3. Fraud Detection Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Investigation lane:
  Message start event "Investigation referral received from Triage & Assign"
  User task "Review referral and plan investigation"
  Service task "Request fraud score and rules check"
  Intermediate message catch event "Fraud score and rules result received"
  User task "Gather evidence and obtain third-party information"
  Exclusive gateway "Sufficient evidence gathered?"
  - branch "No — further evidence needed":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Evidence Sufficient" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Identify evidence gaps",
      User task "Request additional information or documentation",
      Intermediate message catch event "Additional information received"
  - branch "Yes — evidence gathered":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient evidence gathered")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Sufficient evidence gathered"
  User task "Compile investigation file and findings"
  Send task "Refer findings to Fraud team for analysis"

Fraud lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Investigation file received from
  Investigation team"
  User task "Analyse findings against fraud indicators"
  Service task "Submit case for fraud platform assessment"
  Intermediate message catch event "Fraud platform assessment result received"
  Exclusive gateway "Fraud confirmed or suspected?"
  - branch "Fraud confirmed or strongly suspected":
      User task "Escalate to senior fraud analyst and flag claim"
      End event "Fraud confirmed — investigation closed, referral to
      Approve or Decline with fraud flag"
  - branch "Fraud not confirmed — inconclusive or clear":
      User task "Document fraud outcome on investigation file"
      End event "Investigation complete — ready for Approve or Decline"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
Evidence Sufficient", labelled "Evidence collection deadline exceeded",
leading to: User task "Escalate evidence shortfall and proceed with
available information", then continues to exclusive merge gateway
"Sufficient evidence gathered".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Investigation lane with the referral
start event, moves through planning, fraud score request, evidence
gathering, and the "Sufficient evidence gathered?" gateway. The "No"
branch enters the standard-loop subprocess and the timer boundary event
exits to the merge gateway; the "Yes" branch goes directly to the merge
gateway. After the merge, the investigation file is compiled and findings
are sent to the Fraud lane. In the Fraud lane, flow moves through analysis,
fraud platform assessment, and the "Fraud confirmed or suspected?" gateway,
whose branches each lead to their own end events.

Message flows:
Third Party → Insurer Investigation lane, User task "Gather evidence and
obtain third-party information" (statements, documents, and supporting
information).
Third Party → Insurer Investigation lane, Intermediate message catch event
"Additional information received" (additional evidence or documentation
supplied in response to request).
Insurer Investigation lane, Service task "Request fraud score and rules
check" → Fraud Detection Platform (claim data and referral details for
scoring).
Fraud Detection Platform → Insurer Investigation lane, Intermediate message
catch event "Fraud score and rules result received" (fraud score and rules
outcome).
Insurer Fraud lane, Service task "Submit case for fraud platform assessment"
→ Fraud Detection Platform (investigation file submitted for deep assessment).
Fraud Detection Platform → Insurer Fraud lane, Intermediate message catch
event "Fraud platform assessment result received" (detailed fraud platform
assessment result).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Investigation Referral" — read by User task "Review referral
and plan investigation".
Data Object "Fraud Score and Rules Result" — written by Service task
"Request fraud score and rules check"; read by User task "Gather evidence
and obtain third-party information".
Data Object "Evidence File" — written by User task "Gather evidence and
obtain third-party information"; read by User task "Compile investigation
file and findings".
Data Object "Investigation File" — written by User task "Compile
investigation file and findings"; read by User task "Analyse findings
against fraud indicators".
Data Object "Fraud Assessment Result" — written by Service task "Submit
case for fraud platform assessment"; read by User task "Analyse findings
against fraud indicators".
Data Object "Investigation Outcome Report" — written by User task "Document
fraud outcome on investigation file"; read by User task "Escalate to senior
fraud analyst and flag claim".

This subprocess receives the investigation referral from triage and
conducts a structured investigation combining third-party evidence
gathering, fraud scoring, and detailed fraud analysis. It produces a
completed investigation file and a clear fraud determination — either
flagging the claim for heightened scrutiny or clearing it — and hands
that outcome to Approve or Decline so the settlement decision is made on
a fully substantiated basis.
```


### V22.07 — Approve or Decline

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.07 Approve or Decline — the seventh subprocess of the Claim to
Settlement value chain, in which a settled assessment is reviewed against
delegated authority and either approved for settlement or declined, with
the outcome recorded in the claims management platform and communicated
for downstream action.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the approval and decline process,
containing the Claims Assessment and Claims Management lanes.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — IT system receiving and recording
approval and decline decisions.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true, single
instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Insurer (white-box)
2. Claims Management Platform (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment lane (assessor):
  Message start event "Assessed loss and quantum received from Assess
    Loss and Quantum"
  User task "Review assessment and quantum recommendation"
  Exclusive gateway "Within assessor delegated authority?"
  - branch "Yes — within authority":
      User task "Record assessment decision"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authority checked")
  - branch "No — exceeds authority":
      Send task "Escalate to delegated approver"
      Intermediate message catch event "Approval decision received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Authority checked")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Authority checked"
  Exclusive gateway "Approve or decline?"
  - branch "Approve":
      User task "Confirm approval and document rationale"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision resolved")
  - branch "Decline":
      User task "Document decline reasons and policy grounds"
      User task "Prepare decline notice and complaint rights statement"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Decision resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Decision resolved"
  Service task "Record final decision in Claims Management Platform"
  End event "Decision recorded — ready for Arrange Repair, Service or
    Payment"

Claims Management lane (delegated approver):
  Message start event "Escalation received from Claims Assessment"
  User task "Review escalated assessment against delegated authority
    schedule"
  Exclusive gateway "Grant or refuse approval?"
  - branch "Grant approval":
      User task "Authorise settlement within delegated limit"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approver decision made")
  - branch "Refuse approval":
      User task "Record refusal with reasons"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Approver decision made")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Approver decision made"
  Send task "Return approval decision to Claims Assessment"
  End event "Approval decision returned"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Intermediate message catch event
  Approval decision received" — label "Escalation response overdue
  (3 business days)" — triggers User task "Chase delegated approver for
  decision" which loops back to the intermediate catch event.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: within the Claims Assessment lane the flow runs from the
  start event through review and the authority gateway; the "within
  authority" branch continues directly to the merge; the "exceeds
  authority" branch passes through the send task and intermediate catch
  event before rejoining at the authority merge gateway; from the merge
  the flow enters the approve-or-decline gateway whose two branches
  rejoin at the decision-resolved merge gateway; the flow then passes to
  the service task and end event. Within the Claims Management lane the
  flow runs from the escalation start event through review and the
  grant-or-refuse gateway, whose branches rejoin at the approver-decision
  merge gateway, then to the send task and end event.

Message flows:
  Claims Assessment lane (Send task "Escalate to delegated approver") →
    Claims Management lane (Message start event "Escalation received from
    Claims Assessment") (escalation package with assessment and quantum
    recommendation)
  Claims Management lane (Send task "Return approval decision to Claims
    Assessment") → Claims Assessment lane (Intermediate message catch
    event "Approval decision received") (approval or refusal decision with
    reasons)
  Claims Assessment lane (Service task "Record final decision in Claims
    Management Platform") → Claims Management Platform (final approved or
    declined decision, rationale and policy grounds)
  Claims Management Platform → Claims Assessment lane (Service task
    "Record final decision in Claims Management Platform") (confirmation
    of record update and claim status)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Assessment and Quantum Report" — read by "Review assessment
  and quantum recommendation"; read by "Review escalated assessment
  against delegated authority schedule".
Data Object "Delegated Authority Schedule" — read by "Within assessor
  delegated authority?" gateway; read by "Review escalated assessment
  against delegated authority schedule".
Data Object "Approval Decision Record" — written by "Confirm approval and
  document rationale"; written by "Record refusal with reasons"; written
  by "Record assessment decision"; read by "Record final decision in
  Claims Management Platform".
Data Object "Decline Notice" — written by "Prepare decline notice and
  complaint rights statement"; read by "Record final decision in Claims
  Management Platform".

This subprocess takes the settled loss assessment from V22.05, applies
delegated authority controls to determine whether a claims assessor can
approve independently or must escalate, and produces a formally recorded
approval or decline decision with full rationale and, where declined, a
complaint rights statement. The recorded decision is handed to V22.08
Arrange Repair, Service or Payment for approved claims, enabling
settlement fulfilment to proceed.
```


### V22.08 — Arrange Repair, Service or Payment

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.08 Arrange Repair, Service or Payment — the subprocess within
Claim to Settlement that converts an approved claim decision into a
fulfilled repair, service or cash payment delivered to the claimant.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the repair, service and payment
  process, with lanes for Supply Chain and Finance.
Pool "Claimant" — the policyholder, member or beneficiary receiving the
  repair arrangement or payment.
Pool "Repairer" — the panel repairer or supplier fulfilling the repair or
  service work order.
Pool "Supplier Network System" — the IT platform managing supplier work
  orders, pricing and availability.
Pool "Payments System" — the IT platform processing and disbursing
  settlements and payments.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claimant" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Repairer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Supplier Network System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Payments System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Claimant
2. Insurer
3. Repairer
4. Supplier Network System
5. Payments System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Supply Chain lane:
  Message start event "Approved claim decision received from Approve
    or Decline"
  Exclusive gateway "Fulfilment method?"
  - branch "Repair or service":
      User task "Select panel repairer or supplier"
      Service task "Check repairer availability and pricing"
      User task "Issue work order to repairer"
      Intermediate message catch event "Repair completion confirmation
        received"
      User task "Verify repair quality and completion"
      Exclusive gateway "Repair accepted?"
      - branch "Yes" (continues to exclusive merge gateway
          "Repair accepted?")
      - branch "No":
          User task "Raise quality dispute with repairer"
          Intermediate message catch event "Repairer response received"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Repair accepted?")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Repair accepted?"
      Send task "Notify claimant of repair completion"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment method?")
  - branch "Cash payment":
      User task "Confirm claimant bank details and declaration"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment method?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Fulfilment method?"

Finance lane:
  User task "Validate payment amount against authorised settlement"
  Exclusive gateway "Payment amount within delegated authority?"
  - branch "Yes" (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount
      within delegated authority?")
  - branch "No":
      User task "Escalate to senior approver"
      Intermediate message catch event "Escalation approval received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount within
          delegated authority?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Payment amount within delegated authority?"
  Service task "Instruct payment disbursement"
  Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received"
  User task "Record payment advice and update claim record"
  End event "Payment fulfilled and claim record updated — ready for
    Pursue Recoveries and Reinsurance"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Issue work order to
  repairer" — label "Repairer acceptance deadline exceeded" — flow
  proceeds to User task "Select alternative repairer or supplier".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess — label
  "Payment instruction timeout" — mounted on Service task "Instruct
  payment disbursement" — flow proceeds to User task "Investigate
  payment failure with Payments System".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Supply Chain lane with the message
start event, then routes through the fulfilment method gateway; the
repair branch runs through repairer selection, work order issuance,
completion confirmation, quality check and the repair accepted gateway
before merging and notifying the claimant; the cash payment branch
confirms bank details before merging; both branches converge at the
fulfilment method merge gateway before passing to the Finance lane for
payment validation, delegated authority check (with escalation branch
merging back), payment instruction, confirmation and record update,
ending at the end event.

Message flows:
  Insurer (User task "Issue work order to repairer") → Repairer
    (work order)
  Repairer → Insurer (Intermediate message catch event "Repair
    completion confirmation received") (repair completion confirmation)
  Insurer (User task "Raise quality dispute with repairer") → Repairer
    (quality dispute notification)
  Repairer → Insurer (Intermediate message catch event "Repairer
    response received") (dispute response)
  Insurer (Send task "Notify claimant of repair completion") → Claimant
    (repair completion notice)
  Insurer (User task "Confirm claimant bank details and declaration")
    → Claimant (bank details and declaration request)
  Claimant → Insurer (User task "Confirm claimant bank details and
    declaration") (bank details and signed declaration)
  Insurer (Service task "Check repairer availability and pricing")
    → Supplier Network System (availability and pricing query)
  Supplier Network System → Insurer (Service task "Check repairer
    availability and pricing") (pricing and availability data)
  Insurer (Service task "Instruct payment disbursement") → Payments
    System (payment instruction)
  Payments System → Insurer (Intermediate message catch event "Payment
    confirmation received") (payment confirmation and reference)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Work Order" — written by User task "Issue work order to
  repairer"; read by User task "Verify repair quality and completion".
Data Object "Repair Completion Report" — written by Intermediate
  message catch event "Repair completion confirmation received"; read
  by User task "Verify repair quality and completion".
Data Object "Claimant Bank Details and Declaration" — written by
  User task "Confirm claimant bank details and declaration"; read by
  User task "Validate payment amount against authorised settlement".
Data Object "Payment Instruction" — written by Service task "Instruct
  payment disbursement"; read by Intermediate message catch event
  "Payment confirmation received".
Data Object "Payment Advice" — written by User task "Record payment
  advice and update claim record".

This subprocess converts the approved claim decision into a tangible
outcome — either a completed repair or service confirmed by the repairer,
or a cash settlement disbursed to the claimant — and records the result
in the claim record. It hands a fully settled and receipted claim to the
Pursue Recoveries and Reinsurance subprocess, which will seek to recover
costs from liable third parties or cede applicable losses to reinsurers.
```


### V22.09 — Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.09 Pursue Recoveries & Reinsurance — the subprocess that
identifies, lodges and settles recovery and reinsurance claims following
claim approval, sitting between Approve or Decline and Close Claim &
Release Reserve in the Claim to Settlement value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the recoveries and reinsurance
  process, with lanes for Recoveries.
  Lane "Recoveries (recoveries officer)" — identifies recovery and
    reinsurance opportunities, lodges claims, negotiates and records
    settlements.
Pool "Third-Party Insurer" — external insurer against whom a subrogation
  or contribution recovery is pursued.
Pool "Reinsurer" — external reinsurer to whom a reinsurance recovery
  claim is submitted.
Pool "Recoveries & Reinsurance System" — IT system that records recovery
  and reinsurance claim records, tracks correspondence and settlements.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Third-Party Insurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Reinsurer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Recoveries & Reinsurance System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Third-Party Insurer
2. Reinsurer
3. Insurer
4. Recoveries & Reinsurance System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Recoveries (recoveries officer) lane:
  Message start event "Approved claim received from Approve or Decline"
  User task "Review claim for recovery and reinsurance opportunities"
  Exclusive gateway "Recovery or reinsurance opportunity identified?"
  - branch "No opportunity": End event "No recovery pursued — claim
    passed to Close Claim & Release Reserve"
  - branch "Recovery opportunity identified":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity identified")
  - branch "Reinsurance recovery opportunity identified":
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity identified")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Opportunity identified"
  Exclusive gateway "Recovery type?"
  - branch "Third-party recovery (subrogation or contribution)":
    User task "Prepare and lodge recovery claim against third-party
      insurer"
    Send task "Submit recovery claim to Third-Party Insurer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Response received from
      Third-Party Insurer"
    Exclusive gateway "Third-party recovery agreed?"
    - branch "Disputed or no response":
      User task "Escalate or pursue via legal representatives"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Third-party outcome
        resolved")
    - branch "Settlement agreed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Third-party outcome
        resolved")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Third-party outcome resolved"
    User task "Record third-party recovery settlement"
    Service task "Update recovery record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
      System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All streams settled")
  - branch "Reinsurance recovery":
    User task "Prepare and lodge reinsurance recovery claim"
    Send task "Submit reinsurance claim to Reinsurer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Reinsurer response received"
    Exclusive gateway "Reinsurance claim agreed?"
    - branch "Disputed or queried":
      User task "Provide additional information and negotiate with
        Reinsurer"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reinsurance outcome
        resolved")
    - branch "Settlement agreed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reinsurance outcome
        resolved")
    Exclusive merge gateway "Reinsurance outcome resolved"
    User task "Record reinsurance settlement"
    Service task "Update reinsurance record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
      System"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All streams settled")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All streams settled"
  User task "Confirm total recoveries and net claim cost"
  End event "Recoveries and reinsurance settled — ready for Close Claim
    & Release Reserve"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Escalate or pursue via
  legal representatives" — label "Recovery negotiation deadline
  exceeded" — triggers End event "Recovery pursuit closed without
  settlement — passed to Close Claim & Release Reserve".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: the single Recoveries lane carries all flow. After the
start event, the recoveries officer reviews the claim and the first
exclusive gateway branches to either a no-opportunity end or the
opportunity-identified merge. From the merge, the recovery-type gateway
splits into a third-party branch and a reinsurance branch; each branch
processes independently through its own negotiation gateway and merge,
records the outcome in the system, then rejoins at the all-streams-
settled merge gateway, after which the officer confirms net recoveries
and the process ends.

Message flows:
  Send task "Submit recovery claim to Third-Party Insurer" →
    Third-Party Insurer (recovery claim document)
  Third-Party Insurer → Intermediate message catch event "Response
    received from Third-Party Insurer" (settlement response or
    repudiation)
  Send task "Submit reinsurance claim to Reinsurer" → Reinsurer
    (reinsurance recovery claim)
  Reinsurer → Intermediate message catch event "Reinsurer response
    received" (settlement acceptance or query)
  Service task "Update recovery record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
    System" → Recoveries & Reinsurance System (third-party recovery
    settlement record)
  Service task "Update reinsurance record in Recoveries & Reinsurance
    System" → Recoveries & Reinsurance System (reinsurance settlement
    record)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Approved Claim Record" — read by User task "Review claim
  for recovery and reinsurance opportunities".
Data Object "Recovery Claim Document" — written by User task "Prepare
  and lodge recovery claim against third-party insurer"; read by Send
  task "Submit recovery claim to Third-Party Insurer".
Data Object "Reinsurance Claim Document" — written by User task "Prepare
  and lodge reinsurance recovery claim"; read by Send task "Submit
  reinsurance claim to Reinsurer".
Data Object "Third-Party Settlement Record" — written by User task
  "Record third-party recovery settlement"; read by Service task
  "Update recovery record in Recoveries & Reinsurance System".
Data Object "Reinsurance Settlement Record" — written by User task
  "Record reinsurance settlement"; read by Service task "Update
  reinsurance record in Recoveries & Reinsurance System".
Data Object "Net Claim Cost Summary" — written by User task "Confirm
  total recoveries and net claim cost".

This subprocess identifies whether a settled claim gives rise to
subrogation, contribution or reinsurance recovery rights, then lodges,
negotiates and records those recoveries in the Recoveries & Reinsurance
System. Each recovery stream — third-party and reinsurance — runs
independently to resolution before the recoveries officer consolidates
the net claim cost. The confirmed recovery position and updated records
are then handed to Close Claim & Release Reserve to finalise the claim
and unwind the outstanding reserve.
```


### V22.10 — Close Claim & Release Reserve

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V22.10 Close Claim & Release Reserve — the final subprocess of the
Claim to Settlement value chain, confirming closure conditions, releasing the
reserve, updating all records, and formally closing the claim.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Insurer" — the organisation running the close-claim process, containing
  Claims Assessment lane and Actuarial lane.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — core claims system of record.
Pool "Reserving System" — actuarial reserving and reserve-release system.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Insurer" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Claims Management Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Reserving System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
  1. Claims Management Platform
  2. Insurer (Claims Assessment lane, then Actuarial lane)
  3. Reserving System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Insurer)

Claims Assessment lane:
  Message start event "Settlement or decline outcome received from Approve or
    Decline"
  User task "Review closure conditions and confirm all actions complete"
  Exclusive gateway "All actions complete?"
  - branch "No — outstanding actions":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Actions Complete" (standard loop)
        containing, in order: User task "Follow up outstanding action",
        Intermediate message catch event "Action confirmation received"
  - branch "Yes — closure confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "All actions complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "All actions complete"
  User task "Prepare closure summary and final claim record"
  Service task "Update claim status to closed in Claims Management Platform"
  Send task "Notify Claimant of claim closure and file retention rights"

Actuarial lane:
  User task "Receive closure notification and review reserve position"
  Exclusive gateway "Reserve fully expended or to be released?"
  - branch "Partial residual reserve":
      User task "Calculate and confirm reserve release amount"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reserve release determined")
  - branch "Reserve fully expended":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reserve release determined")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Reserve release determined"
  Service task "Post reserve release to Reserving System"
  User task "Confirm reserve release and update actuarial records"
  End event "Claim closed and reserve released — claim file archived"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Actions
  Complete" — label "Outstanding action deadline exceeded" — triggers an
  escalation path: End event "Closure escalated — outstanding action unresolved".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Work begins in the Claims Assessment lane with the message start
event, proceeds through the closure-condition review gateway, loops through the
outstanding-action subprocess until all actions are confirmed, then continues
to the closure summary task and the service task that marks the claim closed
in the Claims Management Platform, and the send task notifying the Claimant.
Control then passes to the Actuarial lane, which reviews the reserve, branches
on whether a residual reserve exists, merges at the reserve-release gateway,
posts the release to the Reserving System, and ends with the claim archived.

Message flows:
  Claims Management Platform → Claims Assessment lane, "Update claim status to
    closed in Claims Management Platform" (closed claim record written to
    platform)
  Claims Assessment lane → Claims Management Platform, "Update claim status to
    closed in Claims Management Platform" (closure status update)
  Claims Assessment lane → Claimant pool implied by send task — narrative names
    no Claimant pool for V22.10, so notification is an internal record only.
  Actuarial lane → Reserving System, "Post reserve release to Reserving System"
    (reserve release instruction)
  Reserving System → Actuarial lane, "Confirm reserve release and update
    actuarial records" (release confirmation and updated reserve balance)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Closure Summary" — written by "Prepare closure summary and final
  claim record", read by "Update claim status to closed in Claims Management
  Platform".
Data Object "Reserve Release Instruction" — written by "Calculate and confirm
  reserve release amount", read by "Post reserve release to Reserving System".
Data Object "Final Claim Record" — written by "Prepare closure summary and final
  claim record", read by "Confirm reserve release and update actuarial records".

This subprocess confirms that every settlement, repair, recovery and
communication action triggered by earlier subprocesses has been completed
before formally closing the claim. The Actuarial lane then calculates and
posts any residual reserve release, freeing capital back to the insurer's
balance sheet. With the reserve released and the claim record marked closed,
the value chain is complete and the claim file passes to archiving.
```


## V23 — Meter to Cash

**Teams and roles involved.**
Meter to Cash usually involves Metering and Field Operations, Meter Data Management, Billing, Revenue Assurance, Customer Service, Credit and Collections, and Finance. Key roles include meter reader or field technician, meter data analyst, billing officer, revenue assurance analyst, customer service agent, credit officer, collections officer, and hardship or concessions officer.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Consumer or Account Holder whose consumption is measured. The process is initiated on a billing cycle, or by a meter event such as a new connection, an exchange or a suspected fault. Other external parties include metering service providers, network or distribution operators, payment providers, regulators setting tariffs and hardship obligations, and debt collection agencies.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: acquire meter readings, validate and estimate missing or implausible data, apply tariffs and rate the consumption, generate and issue the bill, handle billing enquiries and disputes, receive and allocate payments, manage arrears and hardship arrangements, pursue collections, manage disconnection and reconnection, and perform revenue assurance and leakage analysis.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include meter data management and head-end systems for smart meters, field workforce management, the billing engine and rating tables, customer information and CRM, payment and direct-debit processing, collections and dispute management, general ledger, and revenue assurance analytics.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include metering and reading standards, validation/estimation/editing rules for missing data, tariff and pricing approval, billing accuracy and timeliness obligations, dispute and adjustment authority, hardship and payment-plan policy, disconnection rules and protected-customer exclusions, and regulatory reporting requirements.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The consumer provides meter access, self-reads where applicable, account and contact changes, payments, disputes and hardship applications. The process provides bills and statements, consumption and tariff information, estimated-read notices, reminders and arrears notices, payment plans, and disconnection or reconnection notifications. Network operators and metering providers exchange readings, service orders and outage data.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates meter reads and estimates, rated consumption, invoices and adjustments, payments and allocations, arrears and payment plans, service orders, and general-ledger postings. IT systems provide meter registers and interval data, tariff and calendar rules, account and contact data, payment confirmations, ageing and collections status, and unbilled-revenue and leakage reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Utility" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V23.01** Acquire Meter Readings | Consumer, Metering Service Provider | Metering & Field Operations (field technician) | Meter Data Management System |
| **V23.02** Validate & Estimate Data | — | Meter Data Management (meter data analyst) | Meter Data Management System |
| **V23.03** Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption | — | Billing (billing officer) | Billing Engine |
| **V23.04** Generate & Issue Bill | Consumer | Billing (billing officer) | Billing Engine, Customer Information System |
| **V23.05** Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes | Consumer | Customer Service (customer service agent) | Customer Information System, Dispute Management System |
| **V23.06** Receive & Allocate Payment | Consumer, Payment Provider | Finance (finance officer) | Payment Processing System, General Ledger |
| **V23.07** Manage Arrears & Hardship | Consumer | Credit & Collections (hardship officer) | Collections System |
| **V23.08** Pursue Collections | Consumer, Debt Collection Agency | Credit & Collections (collections officer) | Collections System |
| **V23.09** Manage Disconnection & Reconnection | Consumer, Network Operator | Metering & Field Operations (field technician), Credit & Collections (credit officer) | Field Workforce Management, Customer Information System |
| **V23.10** Perform Revenue Assurance | Regulator | Revenue Assurance (revenue assurance analyst) | Revenue Assurance Analytics |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V23):

- **External actors:** Consumer (V23.01, V23.04–V23.09); Metering Service Provider (V23.01); Payment Provider (V23.06); Debt Collection Agency (V23.08); Network Operator (V23.09); Regulator (V23.10).
- **Teams:** Metering & Field Operations (V23.01, V23.09); Meter Data Management (V23.02); Billing (V23.03, V23.04); Customer Service (V23.05); Finance (V23.06); Credit & Collections (V23.07–V23.09); Revenue Assurance (V23.10).
- **IT systems:** Meter Data Management System (V23.01, V23.02); Billing Engine (V23.03, V23.04); Customer Information System (V23.04, V23.05, V23.09); Dispute Management System (V23.05); Payment Processing System (V23.06); General Ledger (V23.06); Collections System (V23.07, V23.08); Field Workforce Management (V23.09); Revenue Assurance Analytics (V23.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V23 — Meter to Cash — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for the Meter to Cash value chain, from initial meter reading through to
revenue assurance. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, read
top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top band) shows what the chain delivers
to its participants; BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle band) shows the ten
subprocesses in chain order; APPLICATIONS (bottom band) shows the IT
systems that support them. The Consumer sits on the far left as the
primary demand-side actor; delivery and settlement actors — Metering
Service Provider, Payment Provider, Debt Collection Agency, Network
Operator, and Regulator — sit on the far right. The diagram reads
top-to-bottom as service realisation in ArchiMate terms: Business Service
→ Business Process → Application Component.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Consumer: demand-side actor, placed on the far left; participates in
  reading acquisition, bill receipt, enquiries, payments, arrears,
  collections, and disconnection.
- Metering Service Provider: delivery-side actor, far right; participates
  in meter reading acquisition.
- Payment Provider: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  payment receipt and allocation.
- Debt Collection Agency: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  collections pursuit.
- Network Operator: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in
  disconnection and reconnection.
- Regulator: delivery-side actor, far right; participates in revenue
  assurance and regulatory reporting.

2. Interfaces

- Meter Access Interface: used by Consumer and Metering Service Provider;
  serves the Meter Reading Acquisition Service.
- Billing & Statement Interface: used by Consumer; serves the Bill
  Generation & Issue Service and the Enquiry & Dispute Service.
- Payment Interface: used by Consumer and Payment Provider; serves the
  Payment Receipt & Allocation Service.
- Collections Interface: used by Debt Collection Agency; serves the
  Collections Pursuit Service.
- Field Order Interface: used by Network Operator; serves the
  Disconnection & Reconnection Service.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface: used by Regulator; serves the Revenue
  Assurance Service.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Meter Reading Acquisition Service: provides validated interval and
  register reads from meters to initiate billing.
- Data Validation & Estimation Service: provides complete, plausible
  consumption data by correcting or estimating missing reads.
- Tariff Rating Service: provides rated consumption figures by applying
  approved tariffs and pricing rules to metered usage.
- Bill Generation & Issue Service: provides accurate, timely bills and
  statements to the consumer.
- Enquiry & Dispute Service: provides resolution of billing questions,
  disputes and adjustments for the consumer.
- Payment Receipt & Allocation Service: provides receipt, matching and
  allocation of payments against account balances.
- Arrears & Hardship Service: provides payment plans and hardship
  arrangements for consumers in financial difficulty.
- Collections Pursuit Service: provides structured debt recovery action
  for overdue accounts.
- Disconnection & Reconnection Service: provides managed interruption and
  restoration of supply in line with policy rules.
- Revenue Assurance Service: provides leakage detection, unbilled-revenue
  identification and regulatory reporting.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings: collects meter data from smart head-end
  systems, metering service providers and field technicians.
- V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data: applies validation, estimation and
  editing rules to identify and correct implausible or missing reads.
- V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption: rates validated consumption
  against tariff and calendar rules to produce chargeable amounts.
- V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill: assembles rated charges, produces
  invoices and delivers bills to consumers by preferred channel.
- V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes: receives, investigates and
  resolves consumer queries, disputes and billing adjustments.
- V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment: processes incoming payments via all
  channels, matches them to accounts and posts to the ledger.
- V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship: identifies overdue accounts, offers
  payment plans and applies hardship concessions as required.
- V23.08 Pursue Collections: escalates unresolved arrears through
  internal and external collection action.
- V23.09 Manage Disconnection & Reconnection: issues field service orders
  for supply interruption and restoration per policy and exclusions.
- V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance: analyses unbilled usage, detects
  leakage, and produces regulatory and management reports.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Meter Data Management System: manages meter registers, interval data,
  head-end connectivity and estimation outputs.
- Billing Engine: holds rating tables, tariff rules and produces invoices
  and billing adjustments.
- Customer Information System: holds account, contact and service-point
  data; used across billing, disputes and field operations.
- Dispute Management System: records, tracks and resolves billing
  enquiries and formal disputes.
- Payment Processing System: processes payments, direct debits and
  payment-channel confirmations.
- General Ledger: receives and stores financial postings for payments,
  adjustments and write-offs.
- Collections System: manages arrears staging, payment plans, hardship
  arrangements and collection workflows.
- Field Workforce Management: schedules and dispatches field technicians
  for service orders including disconnection and reconnection.
- Revenue Assurance Analytics: analyses meter and billing data to
  identify unbilled revenue, leakage and regulatory exposures.

6. Relationships

SERVING (Application Component SERVES Business Process):
- Meter Data Management System serves V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings.
- Meter Data Management System serves V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data.
- Billing Engine serves V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption.
- Billing Engine serves V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill.
- Customer Information System serves V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill.
- Customer Information System serves V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries &
  Disputes.
- Customer Information System serves V23.09 Manage Disconnection &
  Reconnection.
- Dispute Management System serves V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries &
  Disputes.
- Payment Processing System serves V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment.
- General Ledger serves V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment.
- Collections System serves V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship.
- Collections System serves V23.08 Pursue Collections.
- Field Workforce Management serves V23.09 Manage Disconnection &
  Reconnection.
- Revenue Assurance Analytics serves V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance.

REALISATION (Business Process REALISES Business Service):
- V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings realises Meter Reading Acquisition
  Service.
- V23.02 Validate & Estimate Data realises Data Validation & Estimation
  Service.
- V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption realises Tariff Rating Service.
- V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill realises Bill Generation & Issue Service.
- V23.05 Handle Billing Enquiries & Disputes realises Enquiry & Dispute
  Service.
- V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment realises Payment Receipt &
  Allocation Service.
- V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship realises Arrears & Hardship Service.
- V23.08 Pursue Collections realises Collections Pursuit Service.
- V23.09 Manage Disconnection & Reconnection realises Disconnection &
  Reconnection Service.
- V23.10 Perform Revenue Assurance realises Revenue Assurance Service.

ASSIGNMENT (Business Interface ASSIGNED TO Business Actor):
- Meter Access Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Meter Access Interface assigned to Metering Service Provider.
- Billing & Statement Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Payment Interface assigned to Consumer.
- Payment Interface assigned to Payment Provider.
- Collections Interface assigned to Debt Collection Agency.
- Field Order Interface assigned to Network Operator.
- Regulatory Reporting Interface assigned to Regulator.

ACCESS (Business Actor ACCESSES Business Service via Interface):
- Consumer accesses Meter Reading Acquisition Service via Meter Access
  Interface.
- Metering Service Provider accesses Meter Reading Acquisition Service
  via Meter Access Interface.
- Consumer accesses Bill Generation & Issue Service via Billing &
  Statement Interface.
- Consumer accesses Enquiry & Dispute Service via Billing & Statement
  Interface.
- Consumer accesses Payment Receipt & Allocation Service via Payment
  Interface.
- Payment Provider accesses Payment Receipt & Allocation Service via
  Payment Interface.
- Debt Collection Agency accesses Collections Pursuit Service via
  Collections Interface.
- Network Operator accesses Disconnection & Reconnection Service via
  Field Order Interface.
- Regulator accesses Revenue Assurance Service via Regulatory Reporting
  Interface.
```

### V23.01 — Acquire Meter Readings

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.01 Acquire Meter Readings — first subprocess of the Meter to
Cash value chain, initiating the billing cycle by collecting consumption
data from meters and delivering validated reads to Meter Data Management.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the meter-to-cash process,
  with two lanes: Metering & Field Operations (field technician) and
  Meter Data Management (meter data analyst).
Pool "Consumer" — the account holder who provides meter access or
  submits a self-read.
Pool "Metering Service Provider" — external party that supplies
  automated or contracted meter reading services.
```
