```text
  that receives, stores and returns meter register and interval data.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Metering Service Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Metering Service Provider
3. Utility
4. Meter Data Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Metering & Field Operations lane:
  Timer start event "Billing cycle or meter event triggers read
    acquisition"
  Exclusive gateway "Read method?"
  - branch "Scheduled field read": User task "Schedule field meter
    read in workforce management"
    Service task "Dispatch field technician to meter site"
    User task "Capture meter read on site"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Read method")
  - branch "Smart meter automated read": Service task "Request
    interval and register data from head-end system"
    Intermediate message catch event "Meter data received from
      Metering Service Provider"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Read method")
  - branch "Consumer self-read": Send task "Send self-read request
    to Consumer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Self-read submitted by
      Consumer"
    User task "Record self-read received from Consumer"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Read method")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Read method"
  User task "Perform initial completeness check on read data"
  Exclusive gateway "Read data complete?"
  - branch "Incomplete — retry": Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
    Read Data Complete" (standard loop) containing, in order:
    User task "Log missing read and escalate to analyst",
    User task "Attempt supplementary read or contact Metering
      Service Provider"
    (exits subprocess)
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Read data complete")
  - branch "Complete": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Read data complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Read data complete"
  Send task "Submit reads to Meter Data Management System"

Meter Data Management lane:
  Service task "Receive and register reads in Meter Data Management
    System"
  User task "Review read register for anomalies"
  Exclusive gateway "Reads acceptable for downstream processing?"
  - branch "Yes": End event "Meter reads acquired — ready for
    Validate and Estimate Data"
  - branch "No — return for investigation": Send task "Return
    rejected reads to Metering and Field Operations for
    re-collection"
    End event "Re-collection initiated — loop back to field
      operations"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat
  Until Read Data Complete" — label "48-hour read deadline exceeded"
  — triggers Send task "Raise escalation notice to meter data
  analyst" and moves to Meter Data Management lane review step.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Metering & Field Operations lane
at the timer start event, fans out across the three read-method
branches of the exclusive gateway, merges at "Read method", continues
to the completeness check and its gateway, enters the standard-loop
subprocess on the incomplete branch or passes straight through on the
complete branch, merges at "Read data complete", then moves to the
Meter Data Management lane via the submit task, continuing through
review and the acceptability gateway to one of the two end events.
The rejected branch ends at its own end event without rejoining.

Message flows:
  Utility (Send task "Send self-read request to Consumer") →
    Consumer (self-read request notice)
  Consumer → Utility (Intermediate message catch event "Self-read
    submitted by Consumer") (consumer self-read data)
  Metering Service Provider → Utility (Intermediate message catch
    event "Meter data received from Metering Service Provider")
    (interval and register data)
  Utility (Service task "Request interval and register data from
    head-end system") → Meter Data Management System (data pull
    request)
  Meter Data Management System → Utility (Service task "Receive and
    register reads in Meter Data Management System") (stored meter
    register and interval data)
  Utility (Send task "Submit reads to Meter Data Management System")
    → Meter Data Management System (raw read submission)
  Utility (Send task "Attempt supplementary read or contact Metering
    Service Provider") → Metering Service Provider (supplementary
    read request)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Meter Read Record" — written by User task "Capture
  meter read on site"; written by User task "Record self-read
  received from Consumer"; read by User task "Perform initial
  completeness check on read data"; read by Service task "Submit
  reads to Meter Data Management System".
Data Object "Field Dispatch Order" — written by Service task
  "Dispatch field technician to meter site"; read by User task
  "Capture meter read on site".
Data Object "Read Anomaly Log" — written by User task "Review read
  register for anomalies"; read by Exclusive gateway "Reads
  acceptable for downstream processing?".

V23.01 collects consumption measurements from all read channels —
field technicians, smart-meter head-end polling, and consumer
self-reads — performs a first-pass completeness check, and registers
the results in the Meter Data Management System. Any gaps trigger a
time-boxed retry loop, and rejected reads are returned for
re-collection. Once the MDM analyst confirms the reads are
acceptable, the subprocess hands a complete set of raw meter reads
to V23.02 Validate and Estimate Data for quality assurance and gap
filling.
```

```text
Cash value chain, receiving raw meter reads from Acquire Meter Readings and
handing validated and estimated consumption data to Apply Tariffs & Rate
Consumption.

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the Meter to Cash process, containing
the Meter Data Management team.
Pool "Meter Data Management System" — IT system that holds meter registers,
interval data, and validation rule sets.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Meter Data Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Utility (white-box, one lane: Meter Data Management)
2. Meter Data Management System (black-box)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Meter Data Management lane:
Message start event "Raw meter reads received from Acquire Meter Readings"
Service task "Retrieve validation rules and register data"
Service task "Run automated validation checks"
Exclusive gateway "Reads pass validation?"
- branch "Yes — all reads valid":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reads pass validation")
- branch "No — reads fail validation":
  Exclusive gateway "Is estimation possible?"
  - branch "Yes — sufficient basis to estimate":
    Service task "Apply estimation algorithm"
    User task "Review and approve estimated reads"
    Exclusive gateway "Estimation accepted?"
    - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Estimation accepted")
    - branch "No — reject and escalate":

      End event "Read escalated — returned to Acquire Meter Readings for

    Exclusive merge gateway "Estimation accepted"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reads pass validation")
  - branch "No — insufficient basis":
    User task "Flag account for manual investigation"
    User task "Escalate unresolvable read to Metering & Field Operations"
    End event "Read escalated — returned to Acquire Meter Readings for re-read"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Is estimation possible"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Reads pass validation")
Exclusive merge gateway "Reads pass validation"
Service task "Validate interval data and profile consistency"
Exclusive gateway "Interval data consistent?"
- branch "Yes":
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Interval data consistent")
- branch "No — profile inconsistency detected":
  User task "Correct or substitute interval profile"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Interval data consistent")
Exclusive merge gateway "Interval data consistent"
Service task "Mark reads and estimates as validated in Meter Data Management
System"
User task "Review validation and estimation summary report"
Service task "Publish validated consumption data"
End event "Validated consumption data ready — ready for Apply Tariffs & Rate
Consumption"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Review and approve estimated reads" —
label "Approval overdue (24 hours)" — triggers User task "Escalate overdue
approval to Meter Data Management supervisor", which flows to End event "Read
escalated — returned to Acquire Meter Readings for re-read".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all sequence flows run within the Meter Data Management lane
in the Utility pool, proceeding from the message start event through automated
validation, the "Reads pass validation?" gateway with its two branches, the
nested "Is estimation possible?" gateway with escalation exits and the
"Estimation accepted?" gateway, merging at "Reads pass validation", continuing
through interval-profile checking with the "Interval data consistent?" gateway
and its merge, then to the final service and end event.

Message flows:
Meter Data Management System → Service task "Retrieve validation rules and
register data" (validation rule sets and meter register data)
Service task "Run automated validation checks" → Meter Data Management System
(validation results and flagged anomalies)
Service task "Apply estimation algorithm" → Meter Data Management System
(estimated read values)
Service task "Mark reads and estimates as validated in Meter Data Management
System" → Meter Data Management System (validated read and estimation records)
Service task "Publish validated consumption data" → Meter Data Management System
(finalised validated consumption dataset)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Raw Meter Reads" — read by "Run automated validation checks".
Data Object "Validation Rules" — read by "Retrieve validation rules and register
data".
Data Object "Estimated Reads" — written by "Apply estimation algorithm", read by
"Review and approve estimated reads".
Data Object "Interval Profile Data" — read by "Validate interval data and profile
consistency", written by "Correct or substitute interval profile".
Data Object "Validation and Estimation Summary Report" — written by "Mark reads
and estimates as validated in Meter Data Management System", read by "Review
validation and estimation summary report".
Data Object "Validated Consumption Data" — written by "Publish validated
consumption data".

This subprocess takes raw meter reads from Acquire Meter Readings and subjects
them to automated validation rules, applying approved estimation algorithms
wherever reads are missing or implausible and escalating any unresolvable cases
back upstream. Interval profile consistency is then confirmed, and the fully
validated and estimated consumption dataset is written to the Meter Data
Management System and published to Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption, which uses
it as the authoritative basis for rating.
```

### V23.03 — Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V23.03 Apply Tariffs & Rate Consumption — third subprocess in the
Meter to Cash value chain, converting validated consumption data into
rated charges ready for billing.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Utility" — the organisation running the rating process, with lanes
for the teams involved.
  Lane "Meter Data Management" — hands off validated reads to Billing.
  Lane "Billing" — billing officer applies tariffs and rates consumption.
Pool "Billing Engine" — IT system that holds tariff tables, rating logic,
and rated consumption records.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Billing Engine" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Utility (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Meter Data Management, Billing)
2. Billing Engine

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Meter Data Management lane:
  Message start event "Validated consumption data received from
    Validate & Estimate Data"
  Send task "Transfer validated reads to Billing"

Billing lane:
  Receive task "Accept validated reads"
  Service task "Retrieve tariff and rate tables from Billing Engine"
  Service task "Retrieve account and billing calendar from Billing Engine"
  Exclusive gateway "Account on standard or non-standard tariff?"
    - branch "standard tariff": User task "Apply standard tariff to
        consumption intervals"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Tariff applied")
    - branch "non-standard tariff": User task "Apply contract or
        time-of-use tariff to consumption intervals"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Tariff applied")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Tariff applied"
  Service task "Calculate charges and taxes for billing period"
  Exclusive gateway "Rating output valid?"
    - branch "yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
        "Rating check resolved")
    - branch "no — errors found": User task "Review and correct
        rating errors"
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Rating check resolved")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Rating check resolved"
  Service task "Write rated consumption and charges to Billing Engine"
  User task "Confirm rating run complete"
  End event "Rated consumption confirmed — ready for Generate & Issue Bill"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

None.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Meter Data Management lane with the
message start event, passes via the send task to the Billing lane where
it continues through retrieve, calculate, gateway, and write tasks in
order; the "Account on standard or non-standard tariff?" gateway splits
into two branches that rejoin at the exclusive merge gateway "Tariff
applied"; the "Rating output valid?" gateway splits into a pass-through
branch and an error-correction branch that rejoin at the exclusive merge
gateway "Rating check resolved"; flow then continues to the write task
and end event.

Message flows:
Billing Engine → Billing lane — "Retrieve tariff and rate tables from
  Billing Engine" (tariff rules and rate tables)
Billing Engine → Billing lane — "Retrieve account and billing calendar
  from Billing Engine" (account profile and billing calendar)
Billing lane → Billing Engine — "Write rated consumption and charges to
  Billing Engine" (rated consumption records and calculated charges)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Validated Consumption Data" — read by "Accept validated
  reads"; written by "Transfer validated reads to Billing".
Data Object "Tariff and Rate Tables" — read by "Apply standard tariff
  to consumption intervals" and "Apply contract or time-of-use tariff
  to consumption intervals"; written by "Retrieve tariff and rate tables
  from Billing Engine".
Data Object "Rated Consumption Record" — written by "Calculate charges
  and taxes for billing period"; read by "Write rated consumption and

This subprocess takes validated, estimated-complete consumption data from
V23.02 and, by retrieving current tariff rules and the account billing
calendar from the Billing Engine, produces a fully rated set of charges
and taxes for the period. Any rating errors are reviewed and corrected
before the run is confirmed. The rated consumption record is then passed
to V23.04 Generate & Issue Bill for invoice production.
```

```text
2. Utility

4. Customer Information System

retrieval to the "Delivery channel?" gateway, whose three branches
rejoin at "Delivery channel resolved"; flow then proceeds through bill
issuance recording, despatch confirmation, and the intermediate catch
event to the "Delivery confirmed?" gateway, whose branches rejoin at

This subprocess takes the rated consumption record produced by Apply
Tariffs & Rate Consumption and turns it into a formatted, delivered bill.
It handles generation errors, selects the consumer's preferred delivery

manages any queries or challenges the consumer raises against the bill.
```

```text
Pool "Dispute Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

1. Consumer
2. Utility (white-box)
3. Customer Information System
4. Dispute Management System

Customer Service lane:
  Message start event "Billing enquiry or dispute received from Consumer"

This subprocess captures every inbound billing contact from the Consumer,
separates simple enquiries from formal disputes, and drives each to a
```

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
to Cash value chain, receiving consumer payments and allocating them to

- Finance (finance officer)

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility
3. Payment Provider
4. Payment Processing System
5. General Ledger

Finance lane:
Message start event "Payment received from Consumer"
User task "Identify account and retrieve outstanding invoices"
Service task "Retrieve account balance and ageing from Payment
Processing System"
Exclusive gateway "Payment method identifiable?"
- branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment
  method identifiable")
- branch "No": User task "Contact consumer to clarify payment
  reference"
  Intermediate message catch event "Consumer provides payment
  reference"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Payment method
  identifiable")

Service task "Submit payment details to Payment Processing System"
Intermediate message catch event "Payment confirmation received
from Payment Processing System"
Exclusive gateway "Payment authorised?"
- branch "Declined": Send task "Notify consumer of failed payment"
  End event "Payment declined — consumer notified, no allocation
  made"
- branch "Authorised": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Payment authorised")
Exclusive merge gateway "Payment authorised"
User task "Allocate payment to outstanding invoices"
Exclusive gateway "Payment fully covers outstanding balance?"
- branch "Fully covers": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
  "Balance coverage assessed")
- branch "Partial payment": User task "Apply partial allocation and

  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Balance coverage assessed")
- branch "Overpayment": User task "Apply credit to account for
  excess amount"
  (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Balance coverage assessed")

- branch "Yes — arrears remain": Send task "Send payment receipt

Sequence flows: flow runs entirely within the Finance lane from the

three-way coverage gateway, and its merge, then to ledger posting and
status update, before splitting at the arrears gateway into two
terminal end events. The declined branch ends at its own end event
and does not rejoin.

Message flows:
Consumer → Utility Finance lane (payment instruction or remittance
advice)
Utility Finance lane → Payment Provider (payment submission request)

event "Payment received from Consumer"; read by User task "Identify
account and retrieve outstanding invoices".

"Retrieve account balance and ageing from Payment Processing System";
read by User task "Allocate payment to outstanding invoices".
Data Object "Payment Allocation Record" — written by User task
"Allocate payment to outstanding invoices"; read by Service task
"Post payment and allocation to General Ledger".
Data Object "Payment Receipt" — written by Send task "Send payment
receipt and arrears notification to consumer"; read by Send task
"Send payment receipt and account-clear confirmation to consumer".

V23.06 Receive & Allocate Payment governs the end-to-end handling of
an incoming payment: confirming its identity and authorisation through
the Payment Provider and Payment Processing System, allocating it
precisely against open invoices (handling partial payments and
overpayments as distinct cases), and posting the result to the General
Ledger. Where the allocation leaves a residual balance the subprocess
flags the account and hands it to V23.07 Manage Arrears and Hardship;
where the account is cleared it issues a receipt and closes the cycle
for that billing period.
```

```text
  hardship case records.

Pool "Utility" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Consumer" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Collections System" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Consumer
2. Utility
3. Collections System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Utility)

Credit & Collections lane:

Message start event "Overdue balance notification received from Generate &
  Issue Bill"
User task "Review account and arrears history"
Service task "Retrieve account and arrears data from Collections System"
Exclusive gateway "Is consumer eligible for hardship programme?"
- branch "Yes — hardship eligible":
    User task "Assess hardship application and supporting information"
    Exclusive gateway "Hardship application approved?"
    - branch "Yes — approved":
        User task "Establish payment plan and hardship arrangement"
        Service task "Record payment plan in Collections System"
        Send task "Send payment plan agreement to consumer"
        Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to payment plan"
        Exclusive gateway "Consumer accepts payment plan?"
        - branch "Accepted":
            Service task "Activate hardship arrangement in Collections System"
            User task "Schedule and monitor instalment due dates"
            Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Plan Completed or Breached"
              (standard loop) containing, in order:
              Intermediate timer catch event "Instalment due date reached",
              User task "Check instalment receipt",
              Exclusive gateway "Instalment received?",
              - branch "Yes": (loop repeats)
              - branch "No — missed": User task "Issue missed-payment reminder"
                (loop repeats)
            User task "Review plan outcome and update account status"
            Exclusive gateway "Plan completed or arrangement ended?"
            - branch "Completed — account current":
                End event "Hardship arrangement completed — account returned
                  to good standing"
            - branch "Breached — continued non-payment":
                End event "Hardship arrangement failed — referred to Pursue
                  Collections"
        - branch "Not accepted":
            End event "Consumer declined plan — referred to Pursue Collections"
    - branch "No — not approved":
        Send task "Send hardship application outcome to consumer"
        End event "Application declined — referred to Pursue Collections"
- branch "No — not hardship eligible":
    User task "Issue formal arrears notice and payment demand"
    Send task "Send arrears notice to consumer"
    Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to arrears notice"
    Exclusive gateway "Payment or arrangement made within notice period?"
    - branch "Yes — resolved":
        Service task "Update arrears status in Collections System"
        End event "Arrears resolved — account returned to good standing"
    - branch "No — unresolved":
        End event "Arrears unresolved — referred to Pursue Collections"

Finance lane:

User task "Post hardship adjustment or concession to account ledger"

Note: The Finance lane task is triggered after hardship arrangement is
activated; it occurs in parallel via a message flow from the Credit &
Collections lane following "Activate hardship arrangement in Collections
System", and posts any concession or fee waiver before monitoring begins.

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Plan
  Completed or Breached" — label "Maximum plan duration exceeded" — triggers
  End event "Plan duration expired — referred to Pursue Collections".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Credit & Collections lane with the message
start event, proceeds through account review and eligibility gateway, then
splits into hardship-eligible and non-eligible branches; the hardship branch
passes through approval, plan establishment, consumer acceptance, activation,
Finance lane posting, and the monitoring loop subprocess, then rejoins at the
plan-outcome gateway whose two branches each lead to their own end events; the
non-eligible branch passes through arrears notice, consumer response, and
resolution gateway whose two branches each lead to their own end events; no
branches rejoin across these two top-level paths.

Message flows:
Service task "Retrieve account and arrears data from Collections System" →
  Collections System (account and arrears data request).
Collections System → Service task "Retrieve account and arrears data from
  Collections System" (account history, ageing and arrears data).
Service task "Record payment plan in Collections System" → Collections System
  (payment plan record).
Service task "Activate hardship arrangement in Collections System" →
  Collections System (hardship arrangement activation).
Service task "Update arrears status in Collections System" → Collections
  System (arrears status update).
Collections System → User task "Schedule and monitor instalment due dates"
  (instalment schedule confirmation).
Send task "Send payment plan agreement to consumer" → Consumer (payment plan
  agreement document).
Consumer → Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to payment
  plan" (consumer acceptance or rejection).
Send task "Send arrears notice to consumer" → Consumer (formal arrears notice).
Consumer → Intermediate message catch event "Consumer responds to arrears
  notice" (payment or contact from consumer).
Send task "Send hardship application outcome to consumer" → Consumer
  (application outcome letter).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Arrears Account Record" — read by "Review account and arrears
  history"; written by "Update arrears status in Collections System".
Data Object "Hardship Application" — written by "Assess hardship application
  and supporting information"; read by "Establish payment plan and hardship
  arrangement".
Data Object "Payment Plan Agreement" — written by "Establish payment plan and
  hardship arrangement"; read by "Record payment plan in Collections System";
  read by "Send payment plan agreement to consumer".
Data Object "Instalment Schedule" — written by "Schedule and monitor
  instalment due dates"; read by "Check instalment receipt".
Data Object "Hardship Adjustment Record" — written by "Post hardship
  adjustment or concession to account ledger".

V23.07 Manage Arrears & Hardship picks up accounts flagged as overdue after
billing, assesses each consumer's eligibility for hardship support, and either
formalises a monitored payment plan with any applicable concessions posted to
the ledger, or issues a formal arrears demand where hardship does not apply.
Accounts that resolve through plan completion or direct payment are returned to
good standing; those that breach the plan or fail to respond within the notice
period are handed to V23.08 Pursue Collections for further action.
```

## V24 — Transaction to Return

**Teams and roles involved.**
Transaction to Return usually involves Tax, Finance/Accounting, Accounts Payable and Receivable, Treasury, Payroll, Legal, and external Tax Advisers, with Internal Audit providing assurance. Key roles include tax manager, tax accountant, financial accountant, indirect tax analyst, transfer pricing specialist, payroll manager, treasury analyst, and external tax adviser.

**External participants.**
The main external participant is the Tax Authority. The process is initiated by a statutory lodgement period ending, a transaction with tax consequences, or an authority query, ruling request or audit. Other external parties include external tax advisers and auditors, customs authorities for trade, and jurisdictions' revenue offices where the organisation operates across borders.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: capture transactions with tax attributes, determine the correct tax treatment, calculate liabilities and credits, reconcile tax accounts to the ledger, prepare the return and supporting workpapers, review and approve, lodge the return, pay or claim the balance, respond to authority queries and audits, and monitor legislative change.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include ERP and the general ledger, tax determination and calculation engines, indirect tax reporting tools, transfer pricing documentation systems, payroll systems, treasury and payment systems, e-filing gateways to revenue authorities, document management for workpapers, and tax provision and reporting tools.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include the tax governance framework and risk appetite, tax determination rules by jurisdiction and product, lodgement calendars and deadlines, review and approval authority for returns, documentation and record-retention requirements, transfer pricing policy, voluntary disclosure procedure, and escalation of uncertain tax positions.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
The tax authority provides legislation, rulings, assessments, queries and audit findings, and receives returns, payments, disclosures and supporting documentation. Advisers provide opinions and reviews; the process provides them with data and questions. Customers and suppliers exchange tax invoices and exemption certificates that evidence treatment.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates tax codes and determinations on transactions, calculated liabilities, reconciliations, workpapers, lodged returns, payments, and provisions. IT systems provide transaction detail with tax attributes, ledger balances, rate and rule tables, prior-period comparatives, lodgement confirmations and receipts, and tax position and effective-rate reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems are the
`System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V24.01** Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes | Customer, Supplier | Finance / Accounting (financial accountant) | ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.02** Determine Tax Treatment | — | Tax (indirect tax analyst) | Tax Determination Engine |
| **V24.03** Calculate Liabilities & Credits | — | Tax (tax accountant) | Tax Determination Engine, ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.04** Reconcile Tax Accounts | — | Finance / Accounting (financial accountant), Tax (tax accountant) | ERP / General Ledger |
| **V24.05** Prepare Return & Workpapers | External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax accountant) | Tax Reporting System, Document Management System |
| **V24.06** Review & Approve | — | Tax (tax manager) | Tax Reporting System |
| **V24.07** Lodge Return | Tax Authority | Tax (tax manager) | E-Filing Gateway |
| **V24.08** Pay or Claim Balance | Tax Authority | Treasury (treasury analyst) | Treasury & Payment System |
| **V24.09** Respond to Queries & Audits | Tax Authority, External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax manager), Legal (legal counsel) | Document Management System |
| **V24.10** Monitor Legislative Change | External Tax Adviser | Tax (tax manager) | Tax Reporting System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V24):

- **External actors:** Customer (V24.01); Supplier (V24.01); External Tax Adviser (V24.05, V24.09, V24.10); Tax Authority (V24.07–V24.09).
- **Teams:** Finance / Accounting (V24.01, V24.04); Tax (V24.02–V24.07, V24.09, V24.10); Treasury (V24.08); Legal (V24.09).
- **IT systems:** ERP / General Ledger (V24.01, V24.03, V24.04); Tax Determination Engine (V24.02, V24.03); Tax Reporting System (V24.05, V24.06, V24.10); Document Management System (V24.05, V24.09); E-Filing Gateway (V24.07); Treasury & Payment System (V24.08).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V24 — Transaction to Return — Service & Application Landscape
(high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape for
the Transaction to Return value chain, from the moment a taxable transaction
is captured through lodgement, payment, audit response, and legislative
monitoring. The canvas is organised in three horizontal bands, top to bottom:
BUSINESS SERVICES (top) → BUSINESS PROCESSES (middle) → APPLICATIONS
(bottom). The demand-side actors — Customer and Supplier — sit on the far
left; the delivery and settlement actors — Tax Authority, External Tax
Adviser — sit on the far right. The diagram is read top-to-bottom as service
realisation: each application component supports the business processes that,
in turn, realise the business services presented to actors.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Customer — demand-side actor, far left, initiates tax-relevant transactions
  by exchanging invoices and exemption certificates in V24.01.
- Supplier — demand-side actor, far left, exchanges tax invoices in V24.01.
- External Tax Adviser — delivery-side actor, far right, provides opinions and
  review in V24.05, V24.09, and V24.10.
- Tax Authority — settlement-side actor, far right, receives returns, payments,
  and disclosures; issues rulings, assessments, and audit findings in
  V24.07, V24.08, and V24.09.

2. Interfaces

- Transaction Intake Interface — Business Interface accessed by Customer and
  Supplier; serves the Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service (V24.01).
- Adviser Collaboration Interface — Business Interface accessed by External
  Tax Adviser; serves the Return Preparation Service (V24.05), the Audit
  Response Service (V24.09), and the Legislative Monitoring Service (V24.10).
- Lodgement & Payment Interface — Business Interface accessed by Tax
  Authority; serves the Return Lodgement Service (V24.07) and the Balance
  Settlement Service (V24.08).
- Authority Query Interface — Business Interface accessed by Tax Authority;
  serves the Query & Audit Response Service (V24.09).

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service — provides collection and coding
  of transactions with their tax attributes from customers and suppliers.
- Tax Treatment Determination Service — provides the correct tax treatment for
  each transaction by jurisdiction and product.
- Liability & Credit Calculation Service — provides computed tax liabilities
  and recoverable credits across all applicable taxes.
- Tax Account Reconciliation Service — provides reconciled tax accounts
  agreed to the general ledger balances.
- Return Preparation Service — provides completed return workpapers and
  supporting documentation ready for review.
- Return Review & Approval Service — provides authorised sign-off on returns
  against the approved authority matrix.
- Return Lodgement Service — provides timely, compliant lodgement of returns
  to the relevant revenue authority.
- Balance Settlement Service — provides payment of tax liabilities or receipt
  of refund claims from the authority.
- Query & Audit Response Service — provides structured responses to authority
  queries, assessments, and audit findings.
- Legislative Monitoring Service — provides ongoing tracking and assessment
  of legislative changes affecting tax positions.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes — Finance/Accounting and
  Tax teams record and code all transactions with relevant tax attributes.
- V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment — Tax team applies jurisdiction and product
  rules to assign the correct treatment to each transaction.
- V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits — Tax team computes gross
  liabilities and recoverable credits using determination outputs and
  ledger balances.
- V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts — Finance/Accounting and Tax teams reconcile
  calculated tax positions to general ledger balances.
- V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers — Tax team, with External Tax Adviser
  input, assembles the return and supporting workpaper package.
- V24.06 Review & Approve — Tax manager reviews and approves the return
  within the authorised approval authority matrix.
- V24.07 Lodge Return — Tax manager submits the approved return to the Tax
  Authority via the e-filing gateway.
- V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance — Treasury analyst initiates payment of
  assessed liability or processes a refund claim with the Tax Authority.
- V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits — Tax manager and Legal counsel manage
  authority queries and audit findings, supported by External Tax Adviser.
- V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change — Tax manager tracks legislative
  developments with External Tax Adviser and assesses impact on positions.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- ERP / General Ledger — core transactional and accounting system; captures
  transactions with tax attributes and holds ledger balances.
- Tax Determination Engine — applies rate and rule tables to transactions;
  supports treatment determination and liability calculation.
- Tax Reporting System — supports return preparation, review, approval, and
  legislative change monitoring.
- Document Management System — stores workpapers, supporting documentation,
  and audit correspondence.
- E-Filing Gateway — transmits lodged returns electronically to revenue
  authorities and receives lodgement confirmations.
- Treasury & Payment System — initiates tax liability payments and processes
  refund claims with the Tax Authority.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application component serves business process):
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.01 Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits
- ERP / General Ledger SERVES V24.04 Reconcile Tax Accounts
- Tax Determination Engine SERVES V24.02 Determine Tax Treatment
- Tax Determination Engine SERVES V24.03 Calculate Liabilities & Credits
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.06 Review & Approve
- Tax Reporting System SERVES V24.10 Monitor Legislative Change
- Document Management System SERVES V24.05 Prepare Return & Workpapers
- Document Management System SERVES V24.09 Respond to Queries & Audits
- E-Filing Gateway SERVES V24.07 Lodge Return
- Treasury & Payment System SERVES V24.08 Pay or Claim Balance

REALISATION (business process realises business service):
- V24.01 REALISES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
- V24.02 REALISES Tax Treatment Determination Service
- V24.03 REALISES Liability & Credit Calculation Service
- V24.04 REALISES Tax Account Reconciliation Service
- V24.05 REALISES Return Preparation Service
- V24.06 REALISES Return Review & Approval Service
- V24.07 REALISES Return Lodgement Service
- V24.08 REALISES Balance Settlement Service
- V24.09 REALISES Query & Audit Response Service
- V24.10 REALISES Legislative Monitoring Service

ASSIGNMENT (actor assigned to interface):
- Customer ASSIGNED TO Transaction Intake Interface
- Supplier ASSIGNED TO Transaction Intake Interface
- External Tax Adviser ASSIGNED TO Adviser Collaboration Interface
- Tax Authority ASSIGNED TO Lodgement & Payment Interface
- Tax Authority ASSIGNED TO Authority Query Interface

SERVING (interface serves business service):
- Transaction Intake Interface SERVES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture
  Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Return Preparation Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Query & Audit Response Service
- Adviser Collaboration Interface SERVES Legislative Monitoring Service
- Lodgement & Payment Interface SERVES Return Lodgement Service
- Lodgement & Payment Interface SERVES Balance Settlement Service
- Authority Query Interface SERVES Query & Audit Response Service

ACCESS (actor accesses service outcome):
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Return Lodgement Service
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Balance Settlement Service
- Tax Authority ACCESSES Query & Audit Response Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Return Preparation Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Query & Audit Response Service
- External Tax Adviser ACCESSES Legislative Monitoring Service
- Customer ACCESSES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
- Supplier ACCESSES Tax-Attributed Transaction Capture Service
```

```text
The boundary contains all ten subprocesses that take a transaction
from initial capture through tax determination, liability calculation,
```

**Value Chain diagram prompt.**

```text
Value Chain V24 - Transaction to Return

Draw a single left-to-right sequence of ten chevron shapes, one per
high-level process stage, in the order listed below. Each chevron must
display its stage code and name. No swimlanes, no data flows, and no
system icons appear in this diagram — only the ordered chevron sequence.

V24.01. Capture Transactions with Tax Attributes
V24.02. Determine Tax Treatment
V24.03. Calculate Liabilities & Credits
V24.04. Reconcile Tax Accounts
V24.05. Prepare Return & Workpapers
V24.06. Review & Approve
V24.07. Lodge Return
V24.08. Pay or Claim Balance
V24.09. Respond to Queries & Audits
V24.10. Monitor Legislative Change

This chain converts raw financial transactions into compliant tax
returns and settles the resulting obligations with the Tax Authority.
It is triggered by a statutory lodgement period ending, a transaction
with tax consequences, or a query or audit initiated by the Tax
Authority. Moving left to right, the chain progresses from capturing
taxable transactions through treatment determination, liability
calculation, account reconciliation, return preparation, internal
review, electronic lodgement, and payment or refund claim, closing
with ongoing responses to authority queries and surveillance of
legislative change that feeds back into future cycles.
```
