```text
BPMN: V25.02 Identify & Assess Sources — second subprocess in the Data to
Insight value chain, bridging the captured business question to the ingestion
of approved data sources.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the teams that identify, evaluate and approve data
sources for the analytics initiative.
  Lane "Data Engineering" — data engineer who discovers and assesses candidate
  sources.
  Lane "Data Governance" — data steward who evaluates compliance, ownership
  and fitness of each source.

Pool "Data Provider" — external third-party vendors, partners and public data
sources that supply feeds, extracts, schemas and licence terms.

Pool "Data Catalogue" — the IT system that holds existing source registrations,
metadata and lineage records, and receives new or updated source entries.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Catalogue" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Provider
2. Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Data Engineering, Data
   Governance)
3. Data Catalogue

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Scoped business question received from Capture Business
  Question"
  User task "Identify candidate data sources"
  Service task "Retrieve existing source metadata from Data Catalogue"
  User task "Request schemas, samples and licence terms from Data Provider"
  Intermediate message catch event "Schemas, samples and licence terms received"
  User task "Assess source coverage, volume and technical feasibility"
  User task "Document source assessment findings"
  Send task "Pass assessment findings to Data Governance"

Data Governance lane:
  User task "Review data classification and handling requirements"
  User task "Evaluate privacy and consent constraints"
  Exclusive gateway "Source compliant and fit for purpose?"
    - branch "Yes": User task "Approve source for use"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Source compliant and fit for
      purpose?")
    - branch "No — remediable": User task "Record remediation conditions and
      return to Data Engineering"
      End event "Source returned for remediation — assess revised source"
    - branch "No — rejected": User task "Record rejection rationale"
      End event "Source rejected — business sponsor notified"
  Exclusive merge gateway "Source compliant and fit for purpose?"
  User task "Register approved source in Data Catalogue"
  User task "Confirm data ownership and assign data steward"
  End event "Approved source catalogue entry ready — ready for Ingest Data"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Non-interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Request schemas, samples
and licence terms from Data Provider" — label "Provider response overdue
(5 business days)" — triggers Send task "Chase Data Provider for outstanding
materials"; flow rejoins before Intermediate message catch event "Schemas,
samples and licence terms received".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Data Engineering lane with the message
start event and proceeds through source identification, catalogue retrieval,
provider request and intermediate wait, then assessment and documentation,
before passing findings to Data Governance. In the Data Governance lane flow
moves through classification review and privacy evaluation to the exclusive
gateway. The "Yes" branch leads to source approval and rejoins at the merge
gateway; the "No — remediable" branch ends at its own end event; the "No —
rejected" branch ends at its own end event. From the merge gateway flow
continues through catalogue registration and steward assignment to the final
end event.

Message flows:
Data Engineering → Data Provider (request for schemas, samples and licence
terms)
Data Provider → Data Engineering (schemas, samples and licence terms supplied)
Data Catalogue → Data Engineering (existing source metadata returned)
Data Governance → Data Catalogue (approved source entry and steward
assignment written)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Source Assessment Report" — written by User task "Document source
assessment findings"; read by User task "Review data classification and
handling requirements".
Data Object "Source Registration Record" — written by User task "Register
approved source in Data Catalogue"; read by Service task "Retrieve existing
source metadata from Data Catalogue".
Data Object "Licence Terms" — read by User task "Evaluate privacy and consent
constraints"; written by User task "Request schemas, samples and licence terms
from Data Provider".

This subprocess identifies every candidate data source relevant to the scoped
business question, obtains schemas, samples and licence terms from external
Data Providers, and puts each source through a governance evaluation covering
data classification, privacy constraints and fitness for purpose. Sources that
clear the assessment are formally registered in the Data Catalogue with an
assigned data steward, producing the approved source catalogue entries that
the next subprocess, Ingest Data, will act on.
```


### V25.03 — Ingest Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.03 Ingest Data — third subprocess in the Data to Insight
value chain, receiving approved source definitions from Identify & Assess
Sources and delivering ingested raw datasets to Validate Quality & Profile.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing the ingestion subprocess.
  Lane "Data Engineering" — data engineer who configures, runs and monitors
  ingestion pipelines.
Pool "Data Provider" — external third-party data vendors, partners and public
  data sources supplying feeds and extracts.
Pool "Ingestion & Orchestration Platform" — pipeline scheduling and
  orchestration system.
Pool "Data Lake" — raw storage layer where ingested data lands.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Provider" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Ingestion & Orchestration Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Data Lake" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Provider
2. Organisation
3. Ingestion & Orchestration Platform
4. Data Lake

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Approved source definitions received from
    Identify & Assess Sources"
  User task "Review source definitions and access credentials"
  User task "Configure ingestion job and schedule"
  Service task "Register ingestion job in orchestration platform"
  Service task "Trigger ingestion pipeline run"
  Intermediate message catch event "Pipeline run status received"
  Exclusive gateway "Pipeline run successful?"
  - branch "Yes": Service task "Confirm raw data landed in data lake"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pipeline run successful?")
  - branch "No": User task "Diagnose pipeline failure"
    Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Ingestion Succeeds" (standard loop)
      containing, in order: User task "Apply fix to ingestion job",
      Service task "Retry ingestion pipeline run",
      Intermediate message catch event "Retry run status received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Pipeline run successful?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Pipeline run successful?"
  User task "Log ingestion run metadata and record volumes"
  End event "Raw datasets ingested — ready for Validate Quality & Profile"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Ingestion Succeeds" — label "Max retry window elapsed" — triggers End
  event "Ingestion failed — escalate to data engineer lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: Flow begins in the Data Engineering lane with the message
  start event and proceeds linearly through review, configuration,
  registration and triggering steps. After the intermediate catch event the
  exclusive gateway branches: the "Yes" branch goes to "Confirm raw data
  landed in data lake" and the "No" branch goes to "Diagnose pipeline
  failure" then into the standard-loop subprocess; both branches rejoin at
  the exclusive merge gateway "Pipeline run successful?". Flow then continues
  to "Log ingestion run metadata and record volumes" and the end event. The
  timer boundary event on the loop subprocess exits to its own failure end
  event without rejoining.

Message flows:
  Data Provider → Organisation / Data Engineering (source data feed or
    extract delivered to ingestion pipeline)
  Data Provider → Organisation / Data Engineering (source schema and
    licence terms supplied alongside feed)
  Organisation / Data Engineering → Ingestion & Orchestration Platform
    (ingestion job registration and schedule)
  Organisation / Data Engineering → Ingestion & Orchestration Platform
    (pipeline run trigger and retry trigger)
  Ingestion & Orchestration Platform → Organisation / Data Engineering
    (pipeline run status and failure detail)
  Ingestion & Orchestration Platform → Data Lake (pipeline writes raw
    data payload to lake storage)
  Data Lake → Organisation / Data Engineering (confirmation of data
    landed and volume metrics)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Source Definition" — read by "Review source definitions and
  access credentials"; read by "Configure ingestion job and schedule".
Data Object "Ingestion Job Configuration" — written by "Configure
  ingestion job and schedule"; read by "Register ingestion job in
  orchestration platform".
Data Object "Pipeline Run Log" — written by "Log ingestion run metadata
  and record volumes"; read by "Log ingestion run metadata and record
  volumes".
Data Object "Raw Dataset" — written by Ingestion & Orchestration Platform
  to Data Lake; read by "Confirm raw data landed in data lake".

This subprocess takes the approved source definitions and access credentials
produced by Identify & Assess Sources and turns them into running ingestion
pipelines that pull or receive data from external providers, land it in the
data lake, and record volumes and run metadata. It handles transient failures
through a bounded retry loop and escalates unrecoverable failures separately.
On successful completion it hands confirmed raw datasets and run logs to
Validate Quality & Profile, which will assess fitness for use before any
transformation begins.
```


### V25.04 — Validate Quality & Profile

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.04 Validate Quality & Profile — sits between Ingest Data and
Transform & Model Data in the Data to Insight value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing validation and profiling.
  Lane "Data Engineering" — data engineer running quality checks and profiling.
  Lane "Data Governance" — data steward reviewing results and governing
    remediation.

Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — IT system executing quality
  rules, profiling routines, and returning metric results.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, two lanes top to bottom: Data Engineering,
   Data Governance)
2. Data Quality & Observability Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Ingested dataset received from Ingest Data"
  User task "Define or confirm quality rules and thresholds"
  Service task "Submit dataset for profiling and quality assessment"
  Intermediate message catch event "Profiling and quality results received"
  User task "Review profiling summary and quality metrics"
  Exclusive gateway "Quality thresholds met?"
  - branch "Yes": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quality thresholds
    met")
  - branch "No": User task "Classify quality issues by severity"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quality thresholds met")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quality thresholds met"
  Exclusive gateway "Critical issues found?"
  - branch "No critical issues": (continues to exclusive merge gateway
    "Critical issues found")
  - branch "Critical issues present": Send task "Escalate critical issues
    to Data Governance"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Critical issues found")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Critical issues found"

Data Governance lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Critical issue escalation received"
  User task "Review critical quality issues and assess impact"
  Exclusive gateway "Remediation required?"
  - branch "Remediation required": User task "Raise remediation request
    with Data Engineering"
    Intermediate message catch event "Remediation outcome received"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Remediation required")
  - branch "Accept with caveats": User task "Record acceptance decision
    and caveats"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Remediation required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Remediation required"
  User task "Approve dataset for downstream use"
  Send task "Notify Data Engineering of governance decision"
  Intermediate message catch event "Governance decision received"
  (returns control to Data Engineering lane merge point)
  User task "Update quality status on dataset"
  Service task "Record profiling results and quality outcomes"
  End event "Dataset quality confirmed — ready for Transform & Model Data"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Submit dataset for profiling and
  quality assessment" — label "Profiling timeout (24 h)" — triggers a
  Send task "Alert platform engineer of profiling delay" then reaches
  End event "Profiling failed — notify Data Engineering".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Data Engineering lane with the start
  event leading through rule definition and profiling submission, then
  awaits results via a message catch event before the data engineer
  reviews metrics. The first exclusive gateway branches on whether
  thresholds are met (both paths merge); the second gateway branches on
  whether critical issues exist, with the escalation branch sending a
  message to the Data Governance lane. Data Governance handles review,
  the remediation gateway branches (both paths merge at the governance
  merge gateway), approval is recorded, and a notification is sent back
  to Data Engineering, where a message catch event resumes flow through
  status update, result recording, and the end event.

Message flows:
  Organisation (Data Engineering, "Submit dataset for profiling and
    quality assessment") → Data Quality & Observability Platform
    (dataset and quality rules submitted for profiling)
  Data Quality & Observability Platform → Organisation (Data
    Engineering, "Profiling and quality results received") (profiling
    summary and quality metrics returned)
  Organisation (Data Engineering, "Record profiling results and quality
    outcomes") → Data Quality & Observability Platform (confirmed
    quality outcomes and status written back)
  Organisation (Data Engineering, "Escalate critical issues to Data
    Governance") → Organisation (Data Governance, "Critical issue
    escalation received") (critical issue detail)
  Organisation (Data Governance, "Raise remediation request with Data
    Engineering") → Organisation (Data Engineering) (remediation
    request — internal message flow between lanes)
  Organisation (Data Governance, "Notify Data Engineering of governance
    decision") → Organisation (Data Engineering, "Governance decision
    received") (governance approval or acceptance-with-caveats decision)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Quality Rules & Thresholds" — written by "Define or confirm
  quality rules and thresholds"; read by "Submit dataset for profiling
  and quality assessment".
Data Object "Profiling & Quality Results" — written by the Data Quality
  & Observability Platform (received at "Profiling and quality results
  received"); read by "Review profiling summary and quality metrics" and
  "Review critical quality issues and assess impact".
Data Object "Quality Issue Log" — written by "Classify quality issues by
  severity"; read by "Escalate critical issues to Data Governance" and
  "Review critical quality issues and assess impact".
Data Object "Governance Decision Record" — written by "Approve dataset
  for downstream use" and "Record acceptance decision and caveats"; read
  by "Update quality status on dataset".

This subprocess takes the raw ingested dataset and subjects it to formal
profiling and rule-based quality assessment, routing critical issues
through a Data Governance review and remediation cycle before any
downstream transformation begins. It closes with a confirmed quality
status and recorded profiling outcomes, handing a governed, quality-
assessed dataset to Transform & Model Data.
```


### V25.05 — Transform & Model Data

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.05 Transform & Model Data — fifth subprocess in the Data to
Insight value chain, receiving validated and profiled data from Validate
Quality & Profile and handing transformed, modelled datasets to Catalogue
& Document Lineage.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the analytics engineering team executing
transformation and modelling work, with one lane.
- Lane: Analytics Engineering (analytics engineer)
Pool "Transformation Tooling" — tool that executes transformation logic
and manages pipeline runs.
Pool "Data Warehouse" — platform that stores curated, modelled datasets.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Transformation Tooling" — black-box, System = true, single instance.
Pool "Data Warehouse" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains the process flow)
2. Transformation Tooling (IT system)
3. Data Warehouse (IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics Engineering lane:
  Message start event "Validated profiled dataset received from Validate
    Quality & Profile"
  User task "Review data quality report and confirm readiness for
    transformation"
  Exclusive gateway "Data ready to transform?"
  - branch "No — quality issues outstanding":
      End event "Transformation halted — quality issues returned to
        Validate Quality & Profile"
  - branch "Yes — proceed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Data ready to transform")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Data ready to transform"
  User task "Define or update transformation logic and business rules"
  Service task "Submit transformation job to Transformation Tooling"
  Intermediate message catch event "Transformation job result received"
  Exclusive gateway "Transformation job succeeded?"
  - branch "Failed — job error":
      User task "Diagnose pipeline error and revise transformation logic"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job succeeded")
  - branch "Succeeded":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job succeeded")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job succeeded"
  Service task "Run data model build in Transformation Tooling"
  Intermediate message catch event "Model build result received"
  Exclusive gateway "Model build passed?"
  - branch "Failed — model errors":
      User task "Review model errors and correct modelling logic"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Model build passed")
  - branch "Passed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Model build passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Model build passed"
  Service task "Load modelled datasets to Data Warehouse"
  Intermediate message catch event "Load confirmation received from Data
    Warehouse"
  User task "Verify row counts, schema and grain of loaded datasets"
  Exclusive gateway "Verification passed?"
  - branch "No — discrepancy found":
      User task "Investigate and resolve load discrepancy"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Verification passed")
  - branch "Yes":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Verification passed")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Verification passed"
  User task "Document transformation logic, model definitions and
    decisions"
  End event "Transformed modelled datasets ready — hand to Catalogue
    & Document Lineage"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Service task "Submit transformation
job to Transformation Tooling" — label "Job timeout exceeded" — triggers
User task "Diagnose pipeline error and revise transformation logic", then
continues to exclusive merge gateway "Transformation job succeeded".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: all steps run within the Analytics Engineering lane in
the order listed above. The "Data ready to transform?" gateway splits on
readiness, with the No branch ending and the Yes branch rejoining at the
merge gateway. The "Transformation job succeeded?" gateway splits on job
outcome, with the Failed branch passing through the diagnose task and
both branches rejoining at their merge gateway. The "Model build passed?"
gateway splits on model build outcome, with the Failed branch passing
through the correct-logic task and both branches rejoining at their merge
gateway. The "Verification passed?" gateway splits on load verification,
with the No branch passing through the investigate task and both branches
rejoining at their merge gateway. The timer boundary on the submit task
feeds into the same Failed branch path.

Message flows:
Transformation Tooling → Analytics Engineering lane (transformation
  job result — success or failure status and run log)
Analytics Engineering lane → Transformation Tooling (transformation job
  submission — transformation logic and parameters)
Analytics Engineering lane → Transformation Tooling (model build
  instruction — dbt or equivalent model run command)
Transformation Tooling → Analytics Engineering lane (model build result —
  pass or fail with error detail)
Analytics Engineering lane → Data Warehouse (load instruction — modelled
  dataset write)
Data Warehouse → Analytics Engineering lane (load confirmation — row
  counts and schema acknowledgement)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Data Quality Report" — read by User task "Review data
  quality report and confirm readiness for transformation".
Data Object "Transformation Logic Definition" — written by User task
  "Define or update transformation logic and business rules"; read by
  Service task "Submit transformation job to Transformation Tooling".
Data Object "Pipeline Run Log" — read by User task "Diagnose pipeline
  error and revise transformation logic".
Data Object "Model Build Result" — read by User task "Review model errors
  and correct modelling logic".
Data Object "Modelled Dataset" — written by Service task "Load modelled
  datasets to Data Warehouse"; read by User task "Verify row counts,
  schema and grain of loaded datasets".
Data Object "Transformation Documentation" — written by User task
  "Document transformation logic, model definitions and decisions".

This subprocess takes validated, profiled source data and converts it
into clean, modelled datasets fit for analysis. Analytics engineers
define and execute transformation logic, build dimensional or metrics
models, load the results to the data warehouse, and verify correctness.
The documented, verified datasets and their transformation definitions
are then handed to Catalogue & Document Lineage for cataloguing and
full lineage recording.
```


### V25.06 — Catalogue & Document Lineage

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.06 Catalogue & Document Lineage — sits between Transform & Model
Data and Build Analysis, Model or Report in the Data to Insight value chain.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams executing cataloguing and lineage
documentation.
  Lane "Data Governance" — data steward registers datasets, documents lineage,
  applies classifications and publishes entries.
Pool "Data Catalogue" — the catalogue and lineage store system that receives
and serves catalogue entries and lineage graphs.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Catalogue" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Organisation (white-box, contains all lanes)
   - Data Governance lane
2. Data Catalogue (black-box, IT system)

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Governance lane:
  Message start event "Transformed dataset received from Transform & Model Data"
  User task "Review transformed dataset and confirm scope for cataloguing"
  User task "Register dataset in catalogue"
  Service task "Submit dataset metadata to Data Catalogue"
  Intermediate message catch event "Catalogue entry confirmation received"
  User task "Document data lineage end-to-end"
  Service task "Submit lineage graph to Data Catalogue"
  Intermediate message catch event "Lineage graph confirmation received"
  User task "Apply data classification and handling labels"
  Service task "Submit classification labels to Data Catalogue"
  Intermediate message catch event "Classification labels confirmed"
  Exclusive gateway "Classification requires privacy review?"
  - branch "Yes — sensitive or personal data identified":
      User task "Escalate classification to Privacy for review"
      Intermediate message catch event "Privacy review outcome received"
      Exclusive gateway "Privacy review passed?"
      - branch "Passed":
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privacy outcome resolved")
      - branch "Failed — reclassify or restrict":
          User task "Apply restriction or reclassification per privacy outcome"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privacy outcome resolved")
      Exclusive merge gateway "Privacy outcome resolved"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privacy review required")
  - branch "No — standard classification confirmed":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Privacy review required")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Privacy review required"
  User task "Verify completeness of catalogue entry and lineage"
  Exclusive gateway "Entry complete and accurate?"
  - branch "No — gaps or errors found":
      Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Entry Complete" (standard loop)
      containing, in order:
        User task "Identify and correct gaps or errors",
        User task "Resubmit corrected metadata or lineage to Data Catalogue",
        Intermediate message catch event "Resubmission confirmation received"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry validated")
  - branch "Yes — entry verified":
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Entry validated")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Entry validated"
  User task "Publish catalogue entry and mark dataset as available"
  Service task "Trigger availability notification in Data Catalogue"
  End event "Catalogue entry published — ready for Build Analysis, Model or
  Report"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Entry
Complete" — label "Correction deadline exceeded (48 hours)" — leads to End
event "Cataloguing failed — entry incomplete after deadline".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work proceeds top to bottom through the Data Governance lane.
After the classification gateway, both branches (privacy escalation path and
standard path) merge at "Privacy review required". After the completeness
gateway, the loop subprocess and the direct yes-branch both merge at "Entry
validated" before the final publish steps.

Message flows:
  Data Governance "Submit dataset metadata to Data Catalogue" →
    Data Catalogue (dataset metadata record)
  Data Catalogue → Data Governance "Catalogue entry confirmation received"
    (entry creation confirmation)
  Data Governance "Submit lineage graph to Data Catalogue" →
    Data Catalogue (lineage graph)
  Data Catalogue → Data Governance "Lineage graph confirmation received"
    (lineage graph confirmation)
  Data Governance "Submit classification labels to Data Catalogue" →
    Data Catalogue (classification and handling labels)
  Data Catalogue → Data Governance "Classification labels confirmed"
    (label application confirmation)
  Data Governance "Resubmit corrected metadata or lineage to Data Catalogue" →
    Data Catalogue (corrected metadata or lineage)
  Data Catalogue → Data Governance "Resubmission confirmation received"
    (correction confirmation)
  Data Governance "Trigger availability notification in Data Catalogue" →
    Data Catalogue (publish instruction)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Dataset Metadata Record" — written by "Register dataset in
catalogue"; read by "Submit dataset metadata to Data Catalogue".
Data Object "Lineage Graph" — written by "Document data lineage end-to-end";
read by "Submit lineage graph to Data Catalogue".
Data Object "Classification and Handling Labels" — written by "Apply data
classification and handling labels"; read by "Submit classification labels to
Data Catalogue".
Data Object "Privacy Review Outcome" — written by "Escalate classification to
Privacy for review"; read by "Apply restriction or reclassification per privacy
outcome".
Data Object "Catalogue Entry Completeness Report" — written by "Verify
completeness of catalogue entry and lineage"; read by "Identify and correct
gaps or errors".

This subprocess takes the transformed and modelled dataset produced by
Transform & Model Data and produces a complete, classified, lineage-documented
catalogue entry that is published in the Data Catalogue. It ensures every
dataset is traceable, correctly labelled for sensitivity, and discoverable
before any analytical work begins. The published entry is the prerequisite
handed to Build Analysis, Model or Report, which relies on knowing exactly
what data is available, how it was derived and how it may be used.
```

```text
  lane)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Review
Passed" — label "Peer review deadline exceeded" — triggers End event "Output
stalled at peer review — escalate to Analytics lead".
Interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Model
Acceptable" — label "Training iteration deadline exceeded" — triggers End event
"Model build stalled — escalate to Data Science lead".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Analytics lane with the message start event,
proceeds to output type agreement and the "Output type?" gateway. The
"Analysis or report" branch stays within Analytics through design, build and
formatting tasks before rejoining at "Output type resolved". The
"Machine-learning model" branch passes to the Data Science lane for model
definition, training submission, evaluation and registration before rejoining
"Output type resolved" in the Analytics lane. From that merge, the Analytics
lane carries peer review through the "Internal review passed?" gateway; the
"No" branch loops inside the expanded subprocess before exiting to "Internal
review outcome"; the "Yes" branch joins the same merge, leading to the end
event.

Message flows:
Business Intelligence Platform → Analytics lane, Service task "Retrieve
curated dataset from BI platform" (curated dataset delivered).
Analytics lane, Service task "Build analysis and draft report" → Business
Intelligence Platform (draft report submitted for render).
Business Intelligence Platform → Analytics lane, Intermediate message catch
event "Report render confirmed by BI platform" (render confirmation).
Data Science lane, Service task "Submit training job to ML platform" →
Machine Learning Platform (training job specification and feature data).
Machine Learning Platform → Data Science lane, Intermediate message catch
event "Training run completed by ML platform" (run results and metrics).
Data Science lane, Service task "Resubmit training job to ML platform" →
Machine Learning Platform (revised training job).
Machine Learning Platform → Data Science lane, Intermediate message catch
event "Retraining run completed" (retraining results and metrics).
Data Science lane, User task "Register model version and record experiment
metadata" → Machine Learning Platform (model artefact and metadata for
registry).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Business Question and Success Measures" — read by User task
"Review business question and agree output type".
Data Object "Report Structure Specification" — written by User task "Design
analysis or report structure"; read by User task "Build analysis and draft
report".
Data Object "Draft Report" — written by User task "Build analysis and draft
report"; read by User task "Apply formatting, filters and parameters".
Data Object "Formatted Report" — written by User task "Apply formatting,
filters and parameters"; read by User task "Conduct internal peer review of
output".
Data Object "Model Objective and Feature Specification" — written by User task
"Define model objective and feature requirements"; read by Service task "Submit
training job to ML platform".
Data Object "Model Performance Evaluation" — written by User task "Evaluate
model performance metrics"; read by Exclusive gateway "Model performance
acceptable?".
Data Object "Experiment Metadata Record" — written by User task "Register
model version and record experiment metadata".
Data Object "Peer Review Findings" — written by User task "Conduct internal
peer review of output"; read by Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Review
Passed".

This subprocess takes the curated, transformed data from the preceding
subprocess and produces either a formatted analysis or report rendered in the
BI platform, or a trained and registered machine-learning model in the ML
platform. Internal peer review ensures the output meets the original business
question before it is passed on. The internally approved output is handed to
Review & Validate Result, where the business sponsor and data governance owner
apply formal acceptance.
```


### V25.08 — Review & Validate Result

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.08 Review & Validate Result — the subprocess in which Analytics,
Data Governance, and the Business Sponsor inspect, challenge, and formally
accept or reject the analysis, model, or report before it is published.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the teams carrying out the review and validation.
  Lane "Analytics" — data analyst who presents the result and resolves
    feedback.
  Lane "Data Governance" — data owner who checks quality, governance, and
    fitness for purpose.
Pool "Business Sponsor" — external decision-maker who reviews and accepts or
  rejects the result.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — IT system used to share, view, and
  annotate the result.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Sponsor" — black-box, single instance.
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Business Sponsor
2. Organisation (white-box, lanes top to bottom: Analytics, Data Governance)
3. Business Intelligence Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Analytics lane:
  Message start event "Analysis, model or report received from Build
    Analysis, Model or Report"
  User task "Prepare result for review"
  Service task "Publish draft result to Business Intelligence Platform"
  Send task "Notify Business Sponsor that result is ready for review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Business Sponsor feedback received"
  Exclusive gateway "Feedback requires rework?"
    - branch "Yes — rework needed":
        Send task "Return result to Build Analysis, Model or Report
          for rework"
        End event "Result returned for rework — exits to Build Analysis,
          Model or Report"
    - branch "No — minor or no changes":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Feedback requires rework")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Feedback requires rework"
  User task "Apply or document minor revisions"

Data Governance lane:
  User task "Assess result against quality and governance standards"
  Exclusive gateway "Governance standards met?"
    - branch "No — standards not met":
        User task "Raise governance issue and record findings"
        Send task "Return result to Analytics for correction"
        End event "Result failed governance check — exits to Analytics
          for correction"
    - branch "Yes — standards met":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Governance standards met")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Governance standards met"
  User task "Record governance sign-off"

Analytics lane (continued):
  User task "Consolidate sponsor acceptance and governance sign-off"
  Exclusive gateway "Result accepted by all parties?"
    - branch "No — acceptance not reached":
        User task "Log outstanding objections and escalate"
        End event "Escalation raised — exits for resolution"
    - branch "Yes — fully accepted":
        (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Result accepted by all
          parties")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Result accepted by all parties"
  End event "Result validated and accepted — ready for Publish and
    Enable Access"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on User task "Prepare result for review"
  — label "Review preparation overdue (2 business days)" — triggers Send
  task "Alert Analytics lead of preparation delay" leading to End event
  "Preparation delay escalated".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: flow begins in the Analytics lane with the message start
event, proceeds through preparation and publication of the draft result,
then notification to the Business Sponsor. After the sponsor feedback
catch event, the exclusive gateway "Feedback requires rework?" branches:
the rework branch ends in its own End event; the no-rework branch merges
at "Feedback requires rework" and continues to "Apply or document minor
revisions". Control then passes to the Data Governance lane for the
governance assessment gateway "Governance standards met?": the failing
branch raises a governance issue and ends; the passing branch merges at
"Governance standards met" and records sign-off. Control returns to the
Analytics lane for consolidation, the "Result accepted by all parties?"
gateway, whose non-accepted branch ends in escalation and whose accepted
branch merges and reaches the final End event.

Message flows:
  Service task "Publish draft result to Business Intelligence Platform"
    → Business Intelligence Platform (draft result published for viewing).
  Business Intelligence Platform → Business Sponsor (result made available
    for review).
  Send task "Notify Business Sponsor that result is ready for review"
    → Business Sponsor (review notification).
  Business Sponsor → Intermediate message catch event "Business Sponsor
    feedback received" (review comments and acceptance or rejection
    decision).
  Business Intelligence Platform → User task "Assess result against quality
    and governance standards" (result content and metadata for governance
    check).
  User task "Record governance sign-off" → Business Intelligence Platform
    (governance sign-off status recorded against the result).

7. Data objects

Data Object "Review Feedback Record" — written by User task "Apply or
  document minor revisions"; read by User task "Consolidate sponsor
  acceptance and governance sign-off".
Data Object "Governance Assessment Report" — written by User task "Assess
  result against quality and governance standards"; read by User task
  "Record governance sign-off" and User task "Consolidate sponsor
  acceptance and governance sign-off".
Data Object "Validated Result Package" — written by User task "Consolidate
  sponsor acceptance and governance sign-off"; read by the final End event
  transition to Publish and Enable Access.

This subprocess ensures that every analysis, model, or report is inspected
by both the business sponsor and the data governance function before it
enters production. Sponsor feedback and governance findings are resolved or
escalated, and only a result that satisfies both parties advances. The
subprocess hands a fully signed-off, validated result package to Publish
and Enable Access, where it will be made available to its intended audience.
```


### V25.09 — Publish & Enable Access

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.09 Publish & Enable Access — the subprocess that publishes
validated results to the Business Intelligence Platform, enforces privacy and
access controls, and hands a governed, accessible insight product to
ongoing monitoring.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams that publish and enable access
  Lane "Data Platform" — platform engineer managing publication and access
  Lane "Privacy" — privacy officer reviewing consent and data-handling rules

Pool "Business Sponsor" — external requester who receives the published insight
Pool "Data Subject" — individual whose data may be in scope, exercising rights
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — BI and visualisation system
Pool "Access Management System" — system controlling access grants and roles

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance
Pool "Business Sponsor" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Data Subject" — black-box, single instance
Pool "Business Intelligence Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance
Pool "Access Management System" — black-box, System = true, single instance

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Business Sponsor
2. Data Subject
3. Organisation (Data Platform lane, then Privacy lane)
4. Business Intelligence Platform
5. Access Management System

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Platform lane:
  Message start event "Validated result received from Review & Validate Result"
  User task "Prepare publication package"
  User task "Define access scope and target audience"
  Send task "Request privacy review"
  Intermediate message catch event "Privacy clearance received"
  User task "Configure and publish asset to BI Platform"
  Service task "Record publication in BI Platform"
  Exclusive gateway "Access request type?"
  - branch "Role-based automatic grant":
      Service task "Provision role-based access in Access Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Access grant complete")
  - branch "Individual access request":
      User task "Review and approve individual access request"
      Service task "Provision individual access in Access Management System"
      (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Access grant complete")
  - branch "Data subject rights request":
      User task "Assess data subject rights request"
      Exclusive gateway "Rights action required?"
      - branch "Correction or deletion required":
          User task "Coordinate correction or deletion across platform"
          End event "Rights request fulfilled — no access granted"
      - branch "Access right — provide extract":
          User task "Prepare and send data extract to Data Subject"
          (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Access grant complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Access grant complete"
  User task "Notify Business Sponsor of availability"
  Send task "Send access confirmation and asset link"
  End event "Access enabled — ready for Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift"

Privacy lane:
  User task "Review privacy and consent constraints"
  User task "Confirm data classification and handling compliance"
  Exclusive gateway "Privacy clearance granted?"
  - branch "Cleared":
      Send task "Issue privacy clearance"
      (exits subprocess)
  - branch "Remediation required":
      User task "Request remediation of privacy issue"
      Intermediate message catch event "Remediation confirmed"
      Send task "Issue privacy clearance after remediation"
      (exits subprocess)

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Review and approve individual access
request" — label "Approval overdue (48 h)" — triggers End event "Access
request escalated — timed out".

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: work begins in the Data Platform lane with preparation and
audience definition, then a send task passes to the Privacy lane; after the
Privacy lane issues clearance, a message catch event in the Data Platform lane
resumes and drives publication and access provisioning through the exclusive
gateway "Access request type?", whose three branches — role-based grant,
individual request, and data subject rights — either rejoin the exclusive merge
gateway "Access grant complete" or end independently; the flow then closes with
notification and confirmation tasks before the end event.

Message flows:
  Data Platform "Send access confirmation and asset link" →
    Business Sponsor (published insight notification and access link)
  Data Platform "Prepare and send data extract to Data Subject" →
    Data Subject (personal data extract fulfilling rights request)
  Data Subject → Data Platform "Assess data subject rights request"
    (rights request: access, correction or deletion)
  Data Platform "Configure and publish asset to BI Platform" →
    Business Intelligence Platform (publication of dashboard, report or model)
  Business Intelligence Platform →
    Data Platform "Record publication in BI Platform"
    (publication confirmation and asset URL)
  Data Platform "Provision role-based access in Access Management System" →
    Access Management System (role-based access grant instruction)
  Data Platform "Provision individual access in Access Management System" →
    Access Management System (individual access grant instruction)
  Access Management System →
    Data Platform "Exclusive merge gateway Access grant complete"
    (access provisioning confirmation)

7. Data objects

Data Object "Publication Package" — written by "Prepare publication package";
  read by "Configure and publish asset to BI Platform".
Data Object "Access Scope Definition" — written by "Define access scope and
  target audience"; read by "Review and approve individual access request"
  and "Provision role-based access in Access Management System".
Data Object "Privacy Clearance Record" — written by "Issue privacy clearance";
  read by "Configure and publish asset to BI Platform".
Data Object "Data Subject Rights Request" — written by "Assess data subject
  rights request"; read by "Coordinate correction or deletion across platform"
  and "Prepare and send data extract to Data Subject".
Data Object "Access Grant Record" — written by
  "Provision role-based access in Access Management System" and
  "Provision individual access in Access Management System";
  read by "Notify Business Sponsor of availability".

V25.09 takes the reviewed and approved result from V25.08 and moves it into
production by publishing it to the Business Intelligence Platform under a
privacy clearance, provisioning the correct access rights for each recipient
type, and honouring any data subject rights requests that arise. The subprocess
closes by notifying the Business Sponsor that the insight is available,
and it hands an active, access-controlled asset to V25.10, which will
monitor its usage, accuracy and drift over time.
```


### V25.10 — Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift

**BPMN diagram prompt.**

```text
BPMN: V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift — the final subprocess of the
Data to Insight value chain, continuously watching published outputs for
declining engagement, data quality degradation and model drift.

1. Pools & Lanes

Pool "Organisation" — the internal teams operating the monitoring process.
  Lane "Data Platform" — platform engineers who oversee usage and cost signals.
  Lane "Data Science" — data scientists who track model accuracy and drift.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — monitors quality metrics and
  surfaces anomaly and drift signals.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — stores model versions, scores performance
  and emits drift alerts.

2. Pool properties

Pool "Organisation" — white-box, single instance.
Pool "Data Quality & Observability Platform" — black-box, System = true,
  single instance.
Pool "Machine Learning Platform" — black-box, System = true, single instance.

3. Layout

Top to bottom:
1. Data Quality & Observability Platform
2. Organisation (white-box, lanes: Data Platform, then Data Science)
3. Machine Learning Platform

4. Lane contents in flow order (Organisation)

Data Platform lane:
  Timer start event "Scheduled monitoring cycle begins"
  Service task "Retrieve usage and cost metrics from observability platform"
  Service task "Review dashboard adoption and query activity"
  Exclusive gateway "Usage or cost anomaly detected?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Investigate usage anomaly"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Usage anomaly resolved?")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Usage anomaly
    resolved?")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Usage anomaly resolved?"
  Intermediate message catch event "Data quality alert received"
  Service task "Review data quality and freshness report"
  Exclusive gateway "Quality threshold breached?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Raise data quality incident"
    Intermediate message catch event "Quality incident response received"
    User task "Confirm remediation and recheck thresholds"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quality threshold clear")
  - branch "No": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Quality threshold
    clear")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Quality threshold clear"
  Intermediate message catch event "Drift signal received from Data Science"
  Exclusive gateway "Action required on published output?"
  - branch "Republish or retrain": Send task "Trigger republish or retrain"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Output action complete")
  - branch "Suppress or retire": User task "Suppress or retire output"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Output action complete")
  - branch "No action": (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Output action
    complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Output action complete"
  User task "Update monitoring log and notify stakeholders"
  End event "Monitoring cycle complete — platform health confirmed"

Data Science lane:
  Intermediate message catch event "Model performance metrics available"
  Service task "Retrieve model performance scores from ML platform"
  Service task "Assess accuracy, bias and data drift indicators"
  Exclusive gateway "Drift or accuracy degradation confirmed?"
  - branch "Yes": User task "Document drift finding and recommend action"
    Send task "Send drift signal to Data Platform"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Drift assessment complete")
  - branch "No": User task "Record stable performance reading"
    (continues to exclusive merge gateway "Drift assessment complete")
  Exclusive merge gateway "Drift assessment complete"
  Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until Monitoring Period Ends" (standard loop)
    containing, in order: Service task "Poll ML platform for next performance
    batch", Service task "Assess updated scores and drift indicators"

5. Edge-mounted (boundary) events

Interrupting timer boundary event on "Raise data quality incident" —
  label "48-hour escalation deadline exceeded" — flow continues to User task
  "Escalate unresolved quality incident to Data Governance".
Non-interrupting timer boundary event on Expanded Subprocess "Repeat Until
  Monitoring Period Ends" — label "Monitoring window closed" — exits
  subprocess and flow rejoins at Intermediate message catch event "Drift
  signal received from Data Platform" in Data Platform lane.

6. Connectors

Sequence flows: The Data Platform lane opens with a timer start, proceeds
through usage review, then the anomaly gateway (merging both branches), waits
for a quality alert, reviews it, routes through the quality threshold gateway
(the breach branch loops through incident tasks before merging), waits for the
drift signal from Data Science, routes through the action gateway (all three
branches merging), then closes with notification and the end event. The Data
Science lane runs in parallel: it wakes on a performance-metrics message,
retrieves and assesses scores, routes through the degradation gateway (merging
both branches), and cycles in the standard-loop subprocess until the monitoring
window closes, at which point the drift signal send task fires to the Data
Platform lane.

Message flows:
Data Quality & Observability Platform → Organisation / Data Platform lane
  (usage metrics, cost data, freshness and quality reports, anomaly alerts)
Organisation / Data Platform lane → Data Quality & Observability Platform
  (quality incident confirmation, remediation acknowledgement)
Machine Learning Platform → Organisation / Data Science lane
  (model performance scores, accuracy metrics, drift indicators)
Organisation / Data Science lane → Machine Learning Platform
  (performance polling requests)
Organisation / Data Platform lane → Machine Learning Platform
  (retrain trigger when drift action is "Republish or retrain")

7. Data objects

Data Object "Usage and Cost Metrics Report" — written by Service task
  "Retrieve usage and cost metrics from observability platform"; read by
  User task "Investigate usage anomaly".
Data Object "Data Quality Report" — written by Service task "Review data
  quality and freshness report"; read by User task "Raise data quality
  incident".
Data Object "Drift Finding Record" — written by User task "Document drift
  finding and recommend action"; read by User task "Update monitoring log
  and notify stakeholders".
Data Object "Monitoring Log" — written by User task "Update monitoring log
  and notify stakeholders".

V25.10 Monitor Usage, Accuracy & Drift closes the Data to Insight chain by
running continuous, scheduled surveillance over every layer of the published
platform: dashboard engagement and cost, data quality and freshness, and model
accuracy and drift. Each layer can trigger its own investigation and remediation
path, including escalation for unresolved incidents and a retrain or republish
signal fed back to earlier subprocesses. The cycle ends only when the monitoring
window closes and platform health is confirmed, giving the organisation an
ongoing assurance loop rather than a one-off handoff.
```


## V26 — Concept to Commissioning

**Teams and roles involved.**
Concept to Commissioning usually involves Capital Planning, Project Management, Engineering and Design, Procurement, Construction or Delivery, Health and Safety, Quality, Commissioning, Operations and Maintenance, and Finance for capitalisation. Key roles include project sponsor, project manager, design engineer, cost estimator, procurement lead, construction manager, safety officer, quality inspector, commissioning engineer, operations representative, and asset accountant.

**External participants.**
The main external participants are Contractors and Consultants delivering the work, and the Regulator or Authority granting approvals and permits. The process is initiated by a capital proposal arising from growth, replacement, compliance or risk. Other external parties include equipment vendors, certifiers and testing authorities, landowners and community stakeholders, and financiers where the project is externally funded.

**High-level subprocesses.**
Typical subprocesses are: develop the concept and business case, obtain funding approval, perform detailed design, obtain permits and approvals, procure contractors and long-lead equipment, mobilise and construct or install, manage variations and progress claims, inspect and test, commission and hand over to operations, and capitalise the asset and close the project.

**Typical IT systems.**
Supporting systems include capital portfolio and project management, cost estimating and scheduling, engineering design and document control, procurement and contract management, site and safety management, quality and inspection test plans, commissioning and handover systems, enterprise asset management for the resulting asset register, and the fixed-asset ledger.

**Policies and procedures.**
Key controls include capital approval thresholds and stage gates, business case and benefits standards, design standards and review requirements, permit and environmental approval obligations, procurement and contracting policy, safety-in-design and site safety rules, variation and change control authority, inspection and test plan requirements, handover and acceptance criteria, and capitalisation versus expense rules.

**Information flow between external participants and process.**
Contractors and consultants provide tenders, designs, schedules, progress claims, variations, test results and as-built documentation, and receive scopes, drawings, instructions, approvals and payments. Regulators receive applications, impact assessments and compliance evidence, and provide permits, conditions and inspection outcomes. Community stakeholders provide submissions and receive consultation and notification.

**Information flow between process and IT systems.**
The process creates or updates business cases, approvals and stage gates, designs and drawings, contracts and purchase orders, schedules and progress, variations and claims, inspection and test records, commissioning evidence, asset records and capitalisation entries. IT systems provide budget and forecast positions, cost actuals against estimate, schedule status, document versions and approvals, permit status, and portfolio and benefits reporting.

**Process ↔ Actors / Teams / IT Systems association matrix.**

Each row matches the pools, lanes and roles of the corresponding BPMN process
prompt below — external actors are the non-organisation pools, teams are the
lanes of the "Project Organisation" pool (key role in brackets), and IT systems
are the `System = true` black-box pools.

| Process | External Actors | Teams (key role) | IT Systems |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **V26.01** Develop Concept & Business Case | — | Capital Planning (project sponsor), Engineering (cost estimator) | Capital Portfolio Management System |
| **V26.02** Obtain Funding Approval | Financier | Capital Planning (project sponsor), Finance (asset accountant) | Capital Portfolio Management System |
| **V26.03** Perform Detailed Design | Consultant | Engineering (design engineer) | Engineering Design & Document Control |
| **V26.04** Obtain Permits & Approvals | Regulator, Community Stakeholder | Project Management (project manager), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Document Management System |
| **V26.05** Procure Contractors & Equipment | Contractor, Equipment Vendor | Procurement (procurement lead) | Procurement & Contract Management |
| **V26.06** Mobilise & Construct | Contractor | Construction (construction manager), Health & Safety (safety officer) | Site & Safety Management System |
| **V26.07** Manage Variations & Claims | Contractor | Project Management (project manager), Finance (cost controller) | Procurement & Contract Management, Cost & Schedule System |
| **V26.08** Inspect & Test | Certifier | Quality (quality inspector) | Quality & Inspection Test Plan System |
| **V26.09** Commission & Hand Over | Contractor | Commissioning (commissioning engineer), Operations (operations representative) | Commissioning & Handover System, Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) |
| **V26.10** Capitalise Asset & Close Project | — | Finance (asset accountant), Project Management (project manager) | Fixed Asset Ledger, Capital Portfolio Management System |

**Actor / Team / System roll-up** (every distinct participant across V26):

- **External actors:** Financier (V26.02); Consultant (V26.03); Regulator (V26.04); Community Stakeholder (V26.04); Contractor (V26.05–V26.07, V26.09); Equipment Vendor (V26.05); Certifier (V26.08).
- **Teams:** Capital Planning (V26.01, V26.02); Engineering (V26.01, V26.03); Finance (V26.02, V26.07, V26.10); Project Management (V26.04, V26.07, V26.10); Health & Safety (V26.04, V26.06); Procurement (V26.05); Construction (V26.06); Quality (V26.08); Commissioning (V26.09); Operations (V26.09).
- **IT systems:** Capital Portfolio Management System (V26.01, V26.02, V26.10); Engineering Design & Document Control (V26.03); Document Management System (V26.04); Procurement & Contract Management (V26.05, V26.07); Site & Safety Management System (V26.06); Cost & Schedule System (V26.07); Quality & Inspection Test Plan System (V26.08); Commissioning & Handover System (V26.09); Enterprise Asset Management / EAM (V26.09); Fixed Asset Ledger (V26.10).



**ArchiMate diagram prompt.**

```text
ArchiMate: V26 — Concept to Commissioning — Service & Application Landscape (high level).

Purpose: This view shows the end-to-end service and application landscape
for V26 Concept to Commissioning, from capital proposal through to asset
capitalisation and project closure. The diagram is organised in three
horizontal bands, top to bottom: BUSINESS SERVICES (top), BUSINESS
PROCESSES (middle), and APPLICATIONS (bottom). Demand-side actors
(Financier, Consultant, Regulator, Community Stakeholder) sit on the far
left; delivery and settlement actors (Contractor, Equipment Vendor,
Certifier) sit on the far right. The view is read top-to-bottom as service
realisation: each business service is realised by one or more business
processes, which in turn are supported by application components below.

1. Business Actors (Business Actor)

- Financier — far left; provides external funding and approval for the
  capital project.
- Consultant — far left; delivers specialist design and advisory services
  to the project.
- Regulator — far left; grants permits, conditions and inspection outcomes.
- Community Stakeholder — far left; provides submissions and receives
  consultation and notification.
- Contractor — far right; delivers construction, installation and
  commissioning works and submits claims and variations.
- Equipment Vendor — far right; supplies long-lead and specialised
  equipment under purchase orders.
- Certifier — far right; performs independent inspection and issues
  certificates of compliance.

2. Interfaces

- Capital Proposal Interface — accessed by Capital Planning on the far
  left demand side; serves the Capital Investment Planning Service and
  feeds V26.01.
- Funding & Approval Interface — accessed by Financier; serves the Funding
  Approval & Stage Gate Service and feeds V26.02.
- Design Submission Interface — accessed by Consultant; serves the
  Engineering Design Service and feeds V26.03.
- Permit Application Interface — accessed by Regulator and Community
  Stakeholder; serves the Permitting & Compliance Service and feeds V26.04.
- Tender & Contract Interface — accessed by Contractor and Equipment
  Vendor; serves the Procurement & Contracting Service and feeds V26.05.
- Site & Claims Interface — accessed by Contractor; serves the Construction
  Delivery Service and the Variation & Claims Management Service, feeding
  V26.06 and V26.07.
- Inspection & Certification Interface — accessed by Certifier; serves the
  Quality & Testing Service and feeds V26.08.
- Handover Interface — accessed by Contractor; serves the Commissioning &
  Handover Service and feeds V26.09.

3. Business Services (Business Service) — top band, left to right

- Capital Investment Planning Service — provides structured concept
  development, options analysis and business case preparation for proposed
  capital investments.
- Funding Approval & Stage Gate Service — provides governance review,
  funding endorsement and stage-gate authorisation before project
  commitment.
- Engineering Design Service — provides detailed engineering, design
  documentation and drawing control for the project scope.
- Permitting & Compliance Service — provides management of permit
  applications, environmental approvals and regulatory obligations.
- Procurement & Contracting Service — provides sourcing, tendering,
  contract award and purchase-order management for contractors and
  equipment.
- Construction Delivery Service — provides site mobilisation, construction
  execution, and safety and progress management.
- Variation & Claims Management Service — provides controlled handling of
  scope changes, variations and progress payment claims.
- Quality & Testing Service — provides inspection, test plan execution and
  compliance verification against acceptance criteria.
- Commissioning & Handover Service — provides system commissioning,
  acceptance testing and formal handover to operations.
- Asset Capitalisation & Closure Service — provides capitalisation of
  completed assets into the asset register and formal project closure.

4. Business Processes (Business Process) — middle band, in chain order

- V26.01 Develop Concept & Business Case — defines the project need,
  options and business case for capital investment.
- V26.02 Obtain Funding Approval — submits the business case through
  governance and secures funding commitment.
- V26.03 Perform Detailed Design — develops engineering drawings,
  specifications and the document register.
- V26.04 Obtain Permits & Approvals — prepares and lodges permit
  applications and manages regulatory and community engagement.
- V26.05 Procure Contractors & Equipment — runs tendering, evaluates
  bids and awards contracts and purchase orders.
- V26.06 Mobilise & Construct — mobilises site resources, executes
  construction and manages safety and progress reporting.
- V26.07 Manage Variations & Claims — assesses and approves variations,
  processes progress claims and updates cost and schedule forecasts.
- V26.08 Inspect & Test — executes inspection and test plans, records
  results and manages non-conformances.
- V26.09 Commission & Hand Over — completes commissioning activities,
  obtains operations acceptance and transfers asset ownership.
- V26.10 Capitalise Asset & Close Project — records assets in the fixed
  asset ledger, raises capitalisation journals and formally closes the
  project.

5. Application Components (Application Component) — bottom band

- Capital Portfolio Management System — supports business case
  development, portfolio tracking, stage-gate approvals and project
  closure reporting.
- Engineering Design & Document Control — manages engineering drawings,
  design specifications, document versions and review workflows.
- Document Management System — manages permit applications, approval
  correspondence and regulatory compliance evidence.
- Procurement & Contract Management — manages tender processes, contract
  awards, purchase orders, variations and contract close-out.
- Site & Safety Management System — manages site mobilisation records,
  safety plans, incident reporting and progress data.
- Cost & Schedule System — manages project cost estimates, schedules,
  earned value and forecast-to-complete reporting.
- Quality & Inspection Test Plan System — manages inspection test plans,
  test records, non-conformance reports and quality certificates.
- Commissioning & Handover System — manages commissioning checklists,
  punch lists, acceptance records and handover documentation.
- Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) — receives the new or modified asset
  record and maintains the operational asset register.
- Fixed Asset Ledger — records capitalisation entries, asset values and
  depreciation commencement on project close.

6. Relationships

SERVING (application components serve business processes):
- Capital Portfolio Management System SERVES V26.01 Develop Concept &
  Business Case.
- Capital Portfolio Management System SERVES V26.02 Obtain Funding
  Approval.
- Capital Portfolio Management System SERVES V26.10 Capitalise Asset &
  Close Project.
- Engineering Design & Document Control SERVES V26.03 Perform Detailed
  Design.
- Document Management System SERVES V26.04 Obtain Permits & Approvals.
- Procurement & Contract Management SERVES V26.05 Procure Contractors &
  Equipment.
- Procurement & Contract Management SERVES V26.07 Manage Variations &
  Claims.
- Site & Safety Management System SERVES V26.06 Mobilise & Construct.
- Cost & Schedule System SERVES V26.07 Manage Variations & Claims.
- Quality & Inspection Test Plan System SERVES V26.08 Inspect & Test.
- Commissioning & Handover System SERVES V26.09 Commission & Hand Over.
- Enterprise Asset Management SERVES V26.09 Commission & Hand Over.
- Fixed Asset Ledger SERVES V26.10 Capitalise Asset & Close Project.

SERVING (business services serve business actors):
- Capital Investment Planning Service SERVES Capital Planning team (demand
  side).
- Funding Approval & Stage Gate Service SERVES Financier.
- Engineering Design Service SERVES Consultant.
- Permitting & Compliance Service SERVES Regulator.
- Permitting & Compliance Service SERVES Community Stakeholder.
- Procurement & Contracting Service SERVES Contractor.
- Procurement & Contracting Service SERVES Equipment Vendor.
- Construction Delivery Service SERVES Contractor.
- Variation & Claims Management Service SERVES Contractor.
- Quality & Testing Service SERVES Certifier.
- Commissioning & Handover Service SERVES Contractor.

REALISATION (business processes realise business services):
- V26.01 Develop Concept & Business Case REALISES Capital Investment
  Planning Service.
- V26.02 Obtain Funding Approval REALISES Funding Approval & Stage Gate

- V26.03 Perform Detailed Design REALISES Engineering Design Service.

- V26.09 Commission & Hand Over REALISES Commissioning & Handover Service.
- V26.10 Capitalise Asset & Close Project REALISES Asset Capitalisation &

ASSIGNMENT (interfaces assigned to actors):

- Funding & Approval Interface ASSIGNED TO Financier.

- Permit Application Interface ASSIGNED TO Regulator.
```
